scores.rationale: Product/tech investment has consistently produced new monetizable products (abSure online journey, OLX tech transfer, Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost, agentic AI on proprietary data), though revenue conversion at OLX is still slower than promised.
scores.quote: These are various AI initiatives which are using OLX core proprietary data to give you a better experience.

scores.rationale: The OLX India deal was large rather than a bolt-on and the acquiree was loss-making, but post-deal execution was strong — loss-makers shut, costs held flat, margins to 37% and PAT up 77% — and management showed discipline by walking away from CarDekho.
scores.quote: after studying it, at that point, decided to put it on hold... it is better to hold any inorganic opportunity at that point

scores.rationale: Cash has ballooned from ~INR750 crores to INR1,244 crores with roughly INR300 crores added last year alone, yet no dividend, buyback or stated distribution policy appears anywhere in the calls — capital is simply accumulating and depressing ROE.
scores.quote: we've now got INR1,244 crores of cash reserves. Last year, we added a cash balance of approximately INR300 crores

scores.rationale: The operating businesses are genuinely asset-light with 37–43% EBITDA margins and a traffic moat, but the huge idle cash pile drags reported capital efficiency — ROE only just crossed double digits after four years.
scores.quote: for the first time you can also see the return on equity reached double digits

scores.rationale: Consumer group grew 30–32% against a car industry growing 0–8%, and management explicitly attributes part of this to share capture from being the lowest-cost channel for dealers and OEMs.
scores.quote: We also gain market share because we're the most cost-effective way for a dealer, a manufacturer to sell a car.

scores.rationale: Expansion is purely domestic city-by-city (180 locations in FY23 to 350+ by FY24); there is no international footprint and the only cross-border angle raised is speculative EU-FTA import demand.
scores.quote: we have 180 locations, about 126 auto malls and the rest are abSure outlets

scores.rationale: Management explicitly names ARPU and mix — the shift to SUVs and to digital ad budgets — as growth drivers alongside industry volume, so growth is meaningfully price/mix led rather than purely volume.
scores.quote: We also benefit in car ARPU when prices go up in terms of ARPUs, which means people move towards a bigger vehicle like an SUV.

scores.rationale: The remarketing repossession cycle bottomed around FY24 after the COVID lending gap and has since recovered (FY26 revenue +22%, PAT +66%), and the car industry is in an upturn on GST cuts — though the company is now past the bottom rather than at it.
scores.quote: There was just a period in COVID when that went down for about a year and a half

scores.rationale: The core end-market is the permanent secular migration of auto marketing budgets from offline to digital plus growth in used-vehicle transactions, a shift management has ridden through both up and down industry cycles.
scores.quote: It is offline to digital spend... there's a big shift to spending on platforms like CarWale

scores.rationale: Zero debt throughout, self-funded growth, and explicit refusal of a large acquisition when organic returns looked better — offset only by the large OLX deal and the failure to deploy or return an idle INR1,244 crore cash pile.
scores.quote: the company is completely debt free and there is strong cash balance

scores.rationale: Founder-led management set out a margin-and-leverage thesis in 2022 and delivered it over 12 straight quarters — group margins from 9% to 33%, EBITDA CAGR ~98%, and a full OLX turnaround executed without external pressure.
scores.quote: Margins have now gone from 9% to 33%.

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently plain, numbers-first and free of celebrity positioning, run by the same small management team (Sanghi, Bhandary) for four years, though the FY26 deck's foregrounding of share-price CAGR is mildly promotional.
scores.quote: the share price is up 94% in the last 3 years during this phase

scores.rationale: A people/learning agenda was stated in 2022 and a management team was installed at OLX post-acquisition, but across 17 calls there is no systematic talent-pipeline evidence, and the CSO role now sits with a family member.
scores.quote: one of the goals we have taken this year is to create a really strong people and learning organization

scores.rationale: Management admits misses and discloses unflattering items — conceding they wrongly called the repo bottom, and voluntarily flagging expensed CarDekho diligence costs — though the relentless 'very optimistic' framing and repeatedly deferred OLX acceleration temper this.
scores.quote: we thought that last year and it still went down

scores.rationale: The results are real but a large share of the improvement came from an acquired asset's cost reset and a strong car-industry upcycle rather than pure operating skill, and management's own framing leans on share-price CAGR — so the record should be discounted for halo.
scores.quote: the car industry in the last seven months has had steep growth, including April as well

scores.rationale: Owning CarWale, BikeWale and OLX simultaneously gives a top-of-mind position in Indian auto classifieds, evidenced by 95% organic traffic and Google Trends dominance 'head and shoulders' over rivals.
scores.quote: It continues to demonstrate the dominance that we have as a brand

scores.rationale: Dealers are effectively captive — almost every Indian used-car dealer lists or buys on the platforms, and subscription plus inventory-liquidation tools like Super Dost raise switching friction — but the lock-in is behavioural, not contractual.
scores.quote: OLX and CarWale has almost all used car dealers in India listing or buying vehicles from the platform

scores.rationale: The market is a small set of scaled players (CarTrade, CarDekho, Cars24/Spinny) with CarTrade holding two of the major brands, but OEMs at 70% of consumer-group revenue are large, concentrated customers with real negotiating leverage.
scores.quote: it's about 70-30, OEM being 70 and dealer being 30 of our revenue

scores.rationale: 95% organic traffic and near-zero marketing spend is a formidable customer-acquisition barrier, and pricing has stayed rational — competitor marketing spend fell rather than escalating into a discount war.
scores.quote: when competition spends have come down the gaps between our brand or a digital brand and then becomes more stock

scores.rationale: Cash-strapped venture-funded rivals have been retrenching since 2022 (a competitor laying off 600 staff) and CarDekho was available for acquisition, indicating weakened players from whom share can be taken.
scores.quote: one of your competitors laying off 600 employees

scores.rationale: This is a listed, high-profile IPO name covered regularly by Citi, Nomura, Axis, JM and others, with management itself highlighting share-price performance — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Sachin Dixit from JM Financial.

scores.rationale: Brand recall drives 95% free traffic and translates into extremely high incremental margins (consumer group EBITDA margin 43%), the financial signature of intangible-led pricing power.
scores.quote: margins have gone from 40% to 43% sequentially. Over last year, margins has gone from 35% to 43%

scores.rationale: Trust and certainty are being explicitly productised — abSure certification and money-back guarantees early on, and Verification/Elite Buyer trust scoring later — indicating customers pay for reliability, though monetisation is still young.
scores.quote: a completely new product to further enhance customer experience on trust and safety on the platform

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine edge — 80+ million monthly users across platforms, 350+ physical touchpoints and now instant WhatsApp-rendered matchmaking that cuts dealer inventory holding from 60–90 days to days.
scores.quote: if a dealer keeps inventory for 60 to 90 days, how do you bring that inventory stock down to five days

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is correctly matched — retail consumers get brand, trust and convenience while OEM/dealer corporates are sold measurable cost-per-sale efficiency — but the 70% OEM revenue concentration is a structural dependency.
scores.quote: we're the most cost-effective way for a dealer, a manufacturer to sell a car

scores.rationale: A multi-product AI stack built on proprietary listing data — matchmaking, pricing, negotiation and image-based condition-check agents — is a credible edge, though it is recent and its customer-benefit superiority is not yet proven in revenue.
scores.quote: with photographic image recognition, we're able to judge condition

scores.rationale: A genuine two-sided marketplace where 2 million monthly used-vehicle buyers and sellers plus nearly all Indian dealers attract each other, producing 95% organic traffic and near-zero customer acquisition cost that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: the 2 million buyers and sellers are people who come every month to buy or sell cars on OLX or CarWale

scores.rationale: Reach is hard to replicate — 350+ physical auction/retail locations plus 1.9 million vehicles auctioned annually and 80 million monthly users across three brands — giving distribution rivals cannot easily match in a service-intensive category.
scores.quote: Vehicles auctioned at a rate of 1.9 million vehicles a year.

scores.rationale: Capex is low and flat (~INR130-150cr on INR5,722cr revenue) with management stating existing plants suffice for the next couple of years, so growth is funded through distribution/brand opex rather than rising growth capex, though the India Technology Center and solar/water projects show some forward investment.
scores.quote: we have three plants in India. We feel that at the moment we are adequately equipped to release capacity

scores.rationale: Sustained, large-scale A&P (Shah Rukh Khan EDGE campaign, MotoGP, T20 World Cup/Wimbledon, 300mn+ consumers reached) is explicitly credited with driving revenue and coincided with eight straight quarters of volume-led growth and market-share gains.
scores.quote: Our brand building initiatives reached an unprecedented scale, touching 300-plus million consumers and trade professionals

scores.rationale: A steady stream of commercialised products (EDGE variants, CRB TURBOMAX+ CK4, MAGNATEC upgrade, ~20 localised launches in 2025, RRBO engine oil, data-centre immersion fluids) plus a new India Technology Center, but the heavy R&D spend (£50mn battery centre) sits at the parent and core additives are bought from Lubrizol/Infineum/Afton/Chevron.
scores.quote: launched new products and localized close to 20 products across automotive, industrial and our specialty range

scores.rationale: The only deal cited is a small, complementary minority stake in Ki Mobility with TVS that feeds lubricant volume into a service network — bolt-on and strategic rather than transformational — but no quantified post-deal margin benefit is given.
scores.quote: our investment in Ki Mobility is a strategic investment. We're not a financial investor

scores.rationale: A consistent, rising dividend policy (interim INR3 in 2022, INR3.5 in 2024, total INR8.75 for FY25) framed as balanced against reinvestment, but no buybacks and dividends are declared regardless of valuation.
scores.quote: final dividend of INR5.25 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR8.75 per share

scores.rationale: Asset-light model — three plants and ~INR150cr capex supporting INR5,722cr revenue at 24% EBITDA margin with robust cash generation and a debt-free balance sheet, protected by brand and distribution.
scores.quote: we actually closed it right at the top of range, almost at the 24% mark

scores.rationale: Share was flat at ~20-22% for years (2022 and 2024 calls), but the 2025-26 calls show genuine capture with volume growing at 1.5-2x market and explicit share gains, and at ~20% there is ample runway.
scores.quote: eighth straight quarter of volume-led growth, closed the year with the highest ever revenue and gained market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-geographic rather than international — a deliberate, well-executed push into rural India (40,000+ rural outlets, 700 Rural Service Express, villages under 20,000 population) that is delivering double-digit growth; no cross-border expansion since the parent owns other markets.
scores.quote: we focused on expanding our reach directly into villages that have a population below 20,000

scores.rationale: Management deliberately shifted from realisation-led to volume-led growth, and mix is diluting margins as industrial grows, with EBITDA up only 5-5.5% against 8% volume — the opposite of pricing/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: As we grew volumes high single digits and EBITDA grew about 5%, 5.5%, there is a dilution

scores.rationale: Demand is steady rather than cyclical, and on the input-cost cycle the company is entering rather than exiting a headwind (crude, currency and additive costs rising into 2Q FY26), so there is no identifiable bottom-of-cycle positioning.
scores.quote: our main feedstock, which is crude has indeed shown huge increase in costs

scores.rationale: Consistently argued across all four years that low Indian car/bike penetration supports lubricant demand into the 2030s-2040s, reinforced by industrial/manufacturing and data-centre adjacencies, though EV transition is a long-dated structural offset.
scores.quote: low per capita penetration of cars and bikes should continue to support the core lubricant demand

scores.rationale: Organic focus, no large M&A, tight working capital, strong cash-generative debt-free balance sheet and continued brand/distribution investment through a volatile cost environment.
scores.quote: We managed costs and working capital tightly, which supported profitability even in a high-growth environment

scores.rationale: The rural/industrial/services strategy has been pursued consistently for several years and is now delivering 12 consecutive growth quarters, but independence and continuity are weak — an MNC subsidiary with a pending parent-level ownership change and repeated MD turnover ending in an interim CEO.
scores.quote: the deal is subject to closure after various approvals across the world are received

scores.rationale: Executives are consistently low-key on calls, declining to speculate on bonuses, battery manufacturing or data-centre revenue and deferring to the Board, with substance-over-hype framing.
scores.quote: I would not like to speculate... What may happen or not happen in future is pure speculation

scores.rationale: Weak internal pipeline evidenced by an outside lateral MD hire who exited within about a year, three MD changes in five years and a currently 'Interim' CEO, only partly offset by formalising 1,100 distributor sales staff and large-scale mechanic training.
scores.quote: for the first time that we have done a lateral hiring at the senior level, Mr. Kedar Lele

scores.rationale: Management gives an explicit EBITDA guidance band and reports against it, openly explains margin dilution, one-time labour-code costs and that data centres are immaterial today, though it has become less forthcoming on volume disclosure than in earlier years.
scores.quote: it is indeed very, very small for us right now. We are at a very early part of the journey

scores.rationale: Results are solid but much of the advantage is inherited — global brand, parent R&D and additive partners — and headline strength (record revenue) coexists with mid-single-digit EBITDA growth and margin dilution, so skill is hard to separate from franchise.
scores.quote: Being a part of the global Castrol, we do benefit from the research and development

scores.rationale: Castrol holds a strong top-of-mind position in the aftermarket but at ~20% share faces PSU and MNC rivals and admits many consumers delegate the choice to the workshop, so it is not monopoly-like in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: there's consumers who give this responsibility to the workshop owners

scores.rationale: Switching costs are minimal in the retail aftermarket — consumers downtrade or defer oil changes under price pressure and workshops can substitute brands — with no captive installed base lock-in.
scores.quote: some consumers would postpone the servicing of their vehicles. And some consumers would potentially look at cheaper options

scores.rationale: The Indian lubricant market is fragmented across PSUs, MNCs and commodity players with management repeatedly flagging persistent competitive intensity, and the company deliberately avoids the commoditised end.
scores.quote: As competitive intensity continues, raw material movement and currency volatility persisted through the year

scores.rationale: Brand and a 150,000-outlet distribution network are real barriers and pricing is managed to a stated premium strategy, but management still cites ongoing competitive pressure and had to launch cheaper 'ESSENTIAL' ranges to defend the mass segment.
scores.quote: we've also introduced products in lower segments, which cater to the mass segment

scores.rationale: Share is being taken in underserved mass and rural pockets and from a commoditised low end where weaker players operate, with volume growing at 1.5-2x an overall market growing only 3.5-4%.
scores.quote: we will hold on to our guidance of growing our volume at 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a mass-advertised consumer brand using celebrity endorsers and global sports sponsorships, widely covered by analysts, and its niche (data centres, EV fluids) is one every major player is chasing.
scores.quote: featuring Shah Rukh Khan... We sponsored the television broadcast of the ICC World Cup

scores.rationale: A stated premium-pricing strategy backed by brand image sustains ~24% EBITDA margins, but the premium is not absolute — downtrading occurs and the company added mass-segment ESSENTIAL variants.
scores.quote: We are a premium brand, and we want to maintain those premiums. So we operate a premium to market

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty of asset protection — '3x protection guaranteed', 100,000km OEM testing, reliability of supply through the Middle East disruption — with management stating customers pay a premium for that assurance.
scores.quote: if you give customers the assurance of a good product that protects their asset... Consumers are willing to pay a premium

scores.rationale: Exceptional accessibility built consistently over the period: 150,000+ outlets, 800 Castrol Auto Service points, 34,000 bike workshops, 13,000 car workshops, 40,000 rural outlets, plus a professionalised 1,100-person feet-on-street sales force.
scores.quote: Our distribution network now covers more than 150,000 outlets nationwide

scores.rationale: Benefit types are well matched — brand/image and advertising for retail two-wheeler and car consumers, and differentiated total-cost-of-operations value plus OEM co-engineering for industrial and commercial customers, with commoditised B2B deliberately avoided.
scores.quote: where we play is where we can offer differentiated value to our customers... and we'll use their cost of operations

scores.rationale: Credible product technology across ICE, hybrid, E20, EV fluids and immersion cooling, but it is largely licensed from the global parent and the majority of key additives are sourced from external suppliers, so the India entity's own tech edge is shallow.
scores.quote: a majority of that is something that we source from our strategic partners

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing two-sided network; the closest thing is reciprocal selling with Ki Mobility's workshop network, which is a commercial cross-sell rather than a network that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: We sell our lubricants into their network. They sell their spare parts into our IWS network

scores.rationale: The clearest durable advantage — a national footprint rivals cannot easily replicate, extended over the period from 135,000 to 150,000+ outlets with deep rural last-mile reach and an owned service ecosystem, in a category where workshop access decides the sale.
scores.quote: This scale gives us deep last-mile reach through which we can make our assortment available to rural consumers

scores.rationale: Investment is real and growth-directed (international offices, AI subsidiary, regulatory licences, platform build) and funded from low-leverage internal cash, but incremental returns are unproven — gross TPV/revenue doubled while net revenue grew only 6-15%.
scores.quote: This financial flexibility allows us to fund investments in AI and platform infrastructure and selectively invest in growth initiatives such as Rediff without stressing returns on or liquidity.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the excerpts.

A steady cadence of in-house product launches (TapPay pin-on-glass, CommerceAI, PayCentral.ai, a US patent filing) but no disclosed R&D spend and no demonstrated revenue conversion — the newest products are explicitly described as early-stage.
scores.quote: This is still an early-stage opportunity globally.

scores.rationale: Acquisitions are diversifying rather than bolt-on and the targets are weak — Rediff was bought for a majority stake despite ~INR36 crore revenue and a loss, alongside a media/live-events subsidiary buyout and minority stakes in NBFCs and Online PSB Loans.
scores.quote: It's INR360 million last year... It is a marginal loss. So it reported a INR4 crore -- INR4 crores to INR5 crores loss for last year.

scores.rationale: No mention of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy across the excerpts.

The model is genuinely asset-light — INR8,116 crore of FY26 revenue on a payments/software stack with low leverage and no lending balance sheet — though the protecting moat is thinner than the asset-lightness.
scores.quote: Importantly, our strategy remains asset-light and scalable. We are not looking to become a traditional balance sheet lender.

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of volume share capture with runway remaining — TPV and gross revenue more than doubled in FY26 on enterprise, utility, government and B2B merchant wins, from a non-dominant base.
scores.quote: revenue from operations for financial year '26 increased to INR8,116 crores compared to INR3,923 crores in FY '25, representing strong year-on-year growth of 103%

scores.rationale: Expansion is wide (UAE, Saudi, Oman, Australia, GIFT City, US ambitions) but the FY24 promise that international would reach 12-15% of net revenue within two years is still described only as a growing share with no number given by FY26.
scores.quote: We remain confident that the international markets will contribute a growing share of net payment revenue over the medium term.

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with adverse mix and falling realisation — Q3 FY26 gross revenue rose 122% while net revenue rose just 6%, and management has abandoned take rate as an objective.
scores.quote: we are concisely prioritizing volume-led growth and absolute profitability over headline take rates

scores.rationale: No cyclical positioning discussed; the end market is presented as secular rather than cyclical.
Indian digital payments is in durable secular expansion with regulatory tailwinds, a point sustained across all four years of calls.
scores.quote: Between 2021 and 2026, the industry is expected to grow in the range of 30% to 40% annually. The government and the regulator are also very supportive

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent and there is no balance-sheet lending risk, but stewardship is not organic-focused — a majority buy of loss-making Rediff, an AI subsidiary, an entertainment buyout, NBFC stakes and a corporate rebrand all inside two years.
scores.quote: Today, we also announced that the Board has approved an investment in Rediff.com for a majority stake.

scores.rationale: Genuine two-decade operating persistence and a self-funded regulatory stack, offset by a narrative that has been rewritten repeatedly (frictionless fintech, then AI-native infrastructure, then embedded lending) rather than one vision doggedly executed.
scores.quote: We are no longer a payment gateway company. We are building an AI-native transaction infrastructure platform

scores.rationale: Management renamed the listed company AvenuesAI at the peak of the AI cycle and speaks in grandiose flywheel/world-stage terms, the opposite of substance-over-celebrity.
scores.quote: Our vision is to build one of the world's most important AI-first fintech infrastructure companies emerging from India.

scores.rationale: Beyond one independent director appointment, there is no discussion of talent development or an internal leadership pipeline.

Disclosure is detailed but the goalposts move without acknowledgement — take rates were promised to keep rising and were the headline KPI in 2022-24, then dropped as a metric once they compressed, and the FY24 TPV run-rate target is never reconciled.
scores.quote: Our focus remains on absolute profitability and cash generation rather than headline take rate metrics.

scores.rationale: Headline results flatter the underlying business — profit is quoted on an 'adjusted' basis, a INR28 crore other-income boost came from Ind AS fair-value marks rather than operations, and 100%+ 'revenue' growth is gross pass-through volume.
scores.quote: This is an Ind AS impact, which is on account of changes in fair value in case of equity shares.

scores.rationale: CCAvenue is a long-established brand in Indian online payment acceptance but holds no monopoly-like position; management itself concedes many rivals offer comparable pricing.
scores.quote: you have a lot of companies offering similar competitive rates

scores.rationale: Real switching costs are being built where payments are embedded in merchant workflows — hotel central reservation systems certified with Opera/Micros-Fidelio and platform layers that lock merchants in beyond the gateway.
scores.quote: The switching cost moved beyond just contractual dependency and they become operationally existential.

scores.rationale: Indian payment aggregation is fragmented and price-competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, and merchants hold the pricing power — management repeatedly concedes intense competition and passes savings to merchants.
scores.quote: If you look at the competitive intensity, it is significant in this country.

scores.rationale: Regulation raises entry barriers (RBI payment aggregator, PPI, offline PA, IFSCA approvals) but pricing behaviour is irrational enough to compress net take rates toward volume-chasing, cancelling much of that benefit.
scores.quote: the digital payment industry in India is poised for growth, with strong entry barriers and strict compliance requirements

scores.rationale: No competitor is identified as weakening or ceding share in the excerpts.
The niche is the opposite of ignored — Indian digital payments is among the most capital- and competitor-saturated markets, and the company actively courts attention with an AI rebrand.
scores.quote: During the quarter, we completed our corporate rebranding to AvenuesAI Limited. This is not a cosmetic change.

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power; realisation on volume is falling and the mix shift to large-ticket enterprise work is explicitly lower-margin per transaction.
scores.quote: the quarter saw a higher share of credit card and enterprise-led volumes, which typically carry over -- carry lower take rates

scores.rationale: Merchants buy reliability and compliance — the value proposition rests on a licensed, auditable, fraud-managed rail, and management has built a deliberate regulatory stack around that promise.
scores.quote: the completion of a broad defensible regulatory stack

scores.rationale: Strong accessibility and merchant intimacy — very high daily onboarding, a single omnichannel dashboard, hardware-free acceptance and an agent-led rural bill-payment network.
scores.quote: this is the only omni channel solution across the country where you can process your online transactions, offline transactions and get reported into a single dashboard

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/merchant and the benefits offered match it — reliability, compliance and workflow integration that creates lock-in, rather than consumer-brand intangibles.
scores.quote: supported by strong demand from large enterprises, utilities, telecom, travel, hospitality

scores.rationale: A multi-product technology stack with some genuine firsts (India's first pin-on-glass TapPay, a US patent filing, agentic PayCentral layer), but the edge has not translated into pricing power.
scores.quote: TapPay, which is India's first pin on glass solution

scores.rationale: A closed-loop data flywheel is asserted but it is a scale/learning claim rather than a demonstrated two-sided network, and management concedes it has no consumer side of payments today.
scores.quote: It is not peer to peer, if that is a question. We don't have the consumer side of payments.

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is a real asset — millions of merchants, bank and cooperative-bank channels, 3,500+ hotel properties and agent-led semi-urban/rural bill payments.
scores.quote: consistent onboarding across SMEs and cooperative banking networks

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex — capacity from 38,500t toward 70,000t+, Vietnam FD and India F&B plants — but incremental returns lagged (debt tripled, PBT fell in FY24) before utilisation caught up at only 65-70% by FY26.
scores.quote: we are now increasing a capacity to more than 70,000 tons, so it is like doubling up capacity

scores.rationale: Deliberate reinvestment of domestic profits into brand-building has compounded into real equity — branded sales INR210cr (FY24) to INR440cr (FY26) with South urban share moving 4% to 6% — though margins are deliberately held at 5-6% to fund it.
scores.quote: the 5%, 6% EBITDA margins that we are running on this business, we will keep it at those lev

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or innovation efficiency discussed across the calls beyond incidental product reformulation for Percol.

Percol/Rocket Fuel was a small complementary bolt-on but the acquiree was weak (sub-1% UK share needing renegotiated listings, new packaging and reformulation), so it fails the 'already strong acquiree' test even if it stayed small.
scores.quote: Percol is very small in UK right now, probably less than 1% market share

scores.rationale: With FY27 free cash surging, management explicitly declined to commit to any distribution policy, preferring optionality between debt retirement and acquisitions; no buybacks discussed.
scores.quote: there is no commitment as of now, but things that you spoke about, most of the things we are thinking about

scores.rationale: Business is both capital-heavy (multi-year, INR650cr+ debt-funded plants) and working-capital heavy — 166 days even after an 80-day improvement — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: Working capital days have actually come down by 80 days to 166 days

scores.rationale: Consistent, quantified share capture from a small base across four years — South urban share from low single digits to over 6%, #3 nationally, double-digit share at Reliance and DMart — with plenty of runway left.
scores.quote: we have crossed 6% market share in South of India

scores.rationale: Credible multi-country build-out (Vietnam plants, UK via Percol, North America ground-up, India North/West rollout) that is executing, though the UK brand stumbled and needed a full relaunch.
scores.quote: we are increasing our business in North America through ground up

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led under a cost-plus model where price is pure green-coffee pass-through and EBITDA/kg is deliberately held flat, with only incremental mix help from freeze-dried and small packs.
scores.quote: the volatility in coffee prices does not affect our margins because... we are modeling as a cost-plus model

scores.rationale: Coffee prices ran from ~$2 to $4 and are now softening, but the cost-plus structure means the cycle drives optical revenue rather than earnings, so there is no identifiable cyclical upturn to capture.
scores.quote: it is only optical in nature as we have always maintained that our business works on per kilo EBITDA

scores.rationale: Domestic coffee consumption is in steady secular expansion and management describes demand as price-inelastic, plus a structural shift of global private-label sourcing toward India/Vietnam.
scores.quote: the coffee consumption has been pretty inelastic to the price changes

scores.rationale: Organic-growth focus with only tiny bolt-ons, and after letting debt peak near INR1,950cr they set a deleveraging plan and executed it to INR963cr without equity dilution, asset sales or pausing growth.
scores.quote: All this happened without dilution of equity, without sale of any non-core assets or without pausing the growth

scores.rationale: Promoter-led team took a multi-year contrarian capacity bet through a coffee-price spike and a debt overhang and saw it through to 65-70% utilisation and record cash flows.
scores.quote: Only after we got a lot of assurances and underwriting from some of our key clients... We went ahead and set up this plant

scores.rationale: Low-key Guntur-headquartered operator whose calls are plain operational updates, largely selling under other companies' private labels rather than courting profile.
scores.quote: No Unpublished Price Sensitive Information was discussed in the call

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or internal pipeline; the only signal is a CFO change from Lakshmi Narayana to Chaithanya Agasthyaraju with no context given.

Owned the FY24 guidance miss and named the causes (NCL breakdown, price volatility), told investors EBITDA/kg would not rise for two years, and refused to over-promise on FY27 despite a 20% Q1 — though they decline to disclose volume splits.
scores.quote: we could not make up for that volume that we lost in quarter 2, and that is the reason we could not achieve 18%, instead of which we achieved 14%

scores.rationale: Headline FY26 43% revenue growth is largely green-coffee inflation pass-through rather than skill, and management itself flags this, so results must be discounted to volume and EBITDA/kg to judge management ability.
scores.quote: if you take the 46% growth top line, it is a combination of 18%-20% volume growth and another 20%-25% of coffee prices increase

scores.rationale: Core business is contract/private-label instant coffee sold under customers' brands with no monopoly position in the end consumer's mind, and the own brand is only #3 domestically.
scores.quote: out of INR320 crores India sales, the brand sales is now at INR210 crores

scores.rationale: Some lock-in exists via long-term contracts and clients underwriting freeze-dried capacity, but customers openly go tentative and short-term when prices move, showing limited switching costs.
scores.quote: They don't want to go for long-term contracts. They are less committed

scores.rationale: Few global-scale private-label instant coffee suppliers, but the cost-plus pricing model and buyers' ability to defer contracts show the customer retains meaningful negotiating power.
scores.quote: at these kind of prices, the customers also become a little tentative

scores.rationale: High capital intensity and 1.5-2 year build lead times deter entrants, pricing is rational cost-plus rather than discount-driven, and promoter ownership has been stable throughout.
scores.quote: It does take 1.5 to 2 years to materialize the capex

scores.rationale: Brazilian suppliers have become uncompetitive in Europe on price and freight, handing accounts to CCL, while domestically the branded category grows slower than CCL, implying share is being taken from incumbents.
scores.quote: Brazil it has become a little non-competitive, especially in the European market... We have been able to win some of those accounts

scores.rationale: A quiet Guntur-based private-label instant coffee niche, largely invisible to consumers since output sells under clients' brands, with little competing capital chasing the segment.
scores.quote: so the generic products that we supply to some of our clients who use very generic products

scores.rationale: The dominant B2B business is explicitly cost-plus with a fixed EBITDA/kg and no pricing power, and consumers down-trade from freeze-dried to spray-dried when prices rise.
scores.quote: Margin story doesn't change, Shirish, because it is a cost-plus model

scores.rationale: Customers buy supply certainty and price protection — back-to-back green coffee buying, natural currency hedge, and forex policy insulate both sides — and clients pre-underwrite capacity before it is built.
scores.quote: the moment we do contract, we do back-to-back buying of green coffee, which means that we are guarded against any fluctuations

scores.rationale: Rapid build of domestic reach, with 20-25% of branded sales through online and strong positions on quick commerce and modern trade chains, plus aggressive distribution expansion South to North/West.
scores.quote: approximately 20% to 25% of our sales come form the online channel

scores.rationale: The benefit types are correctly matched — corporate private-label buyers get TCO/reliability under cost-plus contracts, while retail consumers are served through the Continental brand and premiumisation.
scores.quote: out of the INR650 crores that we did in the India business, INR440 crores were the retail business, the branded business

scores.rationale: Newer plants carry upgraded, more efficient technology and freeze-dried capability delivering ~20% ROE, but there is no evidence of high R&D intensity or a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: It would be an upgraded technology, which we are going to implement under the new facility

scores.rationale: Nothing in four years of calls indicates any self-reinforcing two-sided network; growth comes from capacity, contracts and distribution, not network scale.
Domestic distribution is improving quickly and D2C/modern trade positions are strong, but as the #3 player still expanding into North and West India it does not yet have reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: Now we are concentrating a lot on the North and West markets

scores.rationale: Technology capex is high, rising and explicitly pre-emptive capacity building ahead of demand (1.8cr to 18cr accounts in 6 years), but incremental returns have deteriorated sharply — 4x cost growth against 1.82x volume growth with FY26 consolidated PAT falling.
scores.quote: technology costs have increased by around 4x since FY '23, whereas during the same period, volume increase has been somewhere around 1.82x

scores.rationale: Spend is on investor education and brand visibility (YouTube, comics, symposium, CSR) which builds institutional trust but has no demonstrated link to sales, since demand is intermediated by depository participants and regulation.
scores.quote: we recently crossed a milestone of 100 million YouTube channel views on the CDSL account

scores.rationale: New products do emerge steadily (T+0, ASBA in secondary market, eCAS in 23 languages, demat portability, Form 121) but they are largely regulator-mandated rather than proprietary R&D, and revenue per rupee of tech spend has fallen.
scores.quote: T+0 has come in. That will need new processes and new in AIF processing has come in

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the five years — expansion into insurance repository, commodity repository, KRA and GIFT IFSC has been organic greenfield subsidiary creation, so there is no M&A track record to judge.

A coherent, regular dividend policy with a special 25th-anniversary payout, but no buyback despite a large cash balance and management declined to commit to any return-of-capital framework when asked.
scores.quote: a final dividend of INR19 per equity share, and a special dividend on account of our 25th year anniversary celebration of INR3 per equity share

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-light — c.335 CDSL employees and a software platform generate INR1,096 crores standalone income servicing 18 crore accounts, protected by a SEBI-licensed duopoly moat.
scores.quote: This year, we have closed at 335 accounts of CDSL. And last year, it was 279 employees.

scores.rationale: Demonstrated and sustained share capture (71% to 80%+ of BO accounts, 85-90% of incremental openings), but the runway is now narrow precisely because CDSL is already dominant in account share.
scores.quote: the market share of new account openings always in the range of 85% plus

scores.rationale: The only geographic move is a just-approved GIFT IFSC KYC unit — credible in direction but at the no-objection stage with no execution or revenue yet; domestic reach is already near-saturated at 98% of pin codes.
scores.quote: received SEBI's no objection to set up a separate business unit at GIFT IFSC

scores.rationale: Growth is almost entirely volume-led (accounts, folios, IPOs) with no pricing power — depository tariffs require SEBI approval and the issuer fee hike has been pending a decade, while the KYC subsidiary faces outright price competition.
scores.quote: we can ask for an issuer price hike, which is now pending for the last 10 years

scores.rationale: The company is roughly 1.5 years into a market-activity downcycle with turnover down year-on-year and revenue flat, while capacity has been built ahead — the classic pre-upturn position, though the timing of any upturn is unidentified.
scores.quote: around INR1 lakh crores, about 8.3% less than the average daily turnover during the same period of the previous year

scores.rationale: Demat penetration has risen from 7% to only 9-10% of the population against 40-50% in developed markets, with new structural sources (unlisted companies, insurance, commodities, newborn accounts) — a genuinely permanent secular expansion.
scores.quote: only 9% to 10% participation of the growing and young population. And this can easily grow to 25%, 30%

scores.rationale: Consistently organic growth, debt-free with a large cash pile, no acquisitions in five years, deliberate counter-cyclical investment during the current lean phase, and a stated refusal to chase adjacent businesses like listed-company RTA outside core competence.
scores.quote: we are continuing to build on our systems, whether we have a great period or a lean period

scores.rationale: The same technology-and-people investment thesis has been articulated and executed unchanged across all 17 calls, defended repeatedly against analyst pressure on costs, and delivered a 10x scale-up in accounts.
scores.quote: in September 2019, we were 1.8 crore demat accounts. Today, we are about 10x plus more in a short period of 6 years

scores.rationale: Operationally understated — no guidance, no promotional forecasts — but opening remarks have become increasingly award-heavy, including a personal CEO accolade highlighted by the MD himself.
scores.quote: Business Today recognized me, on behalf of the entire CDSL team and the ecosystem that has placed its trust in us... as India's Best CEO of 2026

scores.rationale: Evidence of an internal leadership pipeline — subsidiary CEOs (Alvares at CVL, Shetty at Centrico, Srivastava at Countrywide) presenting on calls — and deliberate compensation to retain scarce tech talent, though no formal development programme is described.
scores.quote: We have a full team now looking at our insurance repository... we have put in our people there, our technology there

scores.rationale: Financial disclosure is granular and unflattering facts are admitted (KYC price competition, mark-to-market hits, insurance market share still low), but repeated direct questions on the return from a 4x technology cost increase were answered with analogies rather than capex/opex numbers.
scores.quote: it's difficult for me to commit on what would be the constant at CDSL then

scores.rationale: The headline record years were driven by a market boom rather than managerial skill, and once turnover normalised revenue went flat and consolidated profit fell — so past results substantially overstate the operating skill component.
scores.quote: we experienced a 126% growth on the year-on-year equity turnover marking it as an exceptional quarter for the entire securities market

scores.rationale: CDSL holds a near-monopoly position in retail investors' minds (80%+ of accounts, 85-90% of new openings) and is the largest KRA, but it is a shared licence rather than a true monopoly and its pricing is capped by SEBI.
scores.quote: our wholly owned subsidiary and the first and largest KYC registration agency

scores.rationale: Deep API integration with depository participants and custody of investor holdings create real switching costs, though management itself has just automated demat account portability, which cuts the other way.
scores.quote: the entire account opening to transactions to pledging, etc. becomes extremely seamless when it's an API-based protocol

scores.rationale: A stable two-player, SEBI-licensed structure where end investors and issuers have no negotiating power, but it is a duopoly rather than a broader oligopoly and tariffs are set by the regulator, not the incumbents.
scores.quote: CDSL saw more than 75-+ lakh accounts opened during this quarter... maintaining our 80% share

scores.rationale: Entry requires a SEBI depository licence and none has been granted in 25 years, and regulated tariffs preclude discount wars in the core business — but the same regulation caps pricing, and the KYC arm does face price competition.
scores.quote: the pricing is approved by SEBI in case of depositories. So, it's taken on record

scores.rationale: NSDL has steadily donated retail account share to CDSL (64% to 80%+, with 85-90% of incremental accounts), and CVL argues KRA data quality keeps CKYC from taking share the other way.
scores.quote: a market share of CDSL at about 71% compared to 64% in Q1 of 2021-2022

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — a heavily analyst-covered listed company that publicises global awards, hosts a symposium attended by the SEBI Chairman and actively courts investor visibility.
scores.quote: two of the major global awards, including the Central Securities Depository of the Year 2025 by Asset Servicing Times

scores.rationale: Gross margins and demand stickiness are high through annuity issuer charges, but there is no image-driven pricing power — tariffs are regulator-approved and the KYC arm has already conceded price to competition.
scores.quote: There is pricing pressure because of the competition as well as lower fetches

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty and reliability — safekeeping of securities, uptime through volume surges, security and seamlessness — and price is genuinely secondary because it is regulated and identical across the industry.
scores.quote: In such periods, the role of trusted market infrastructure becomes even more important

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a core strength — near-universal pin-code reach through DP service locations, API-based access customised to DPs of every size, and free multilingual eCAS and investor services.
scores.quote: covers about 98% of the pin codes in India through over 20700 service locations

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is correctly matched — integration, scalability and reliability lock-in for corporate DPs and issuers, education and accessibility for retail investors — though corporate switching costs are moderated by regulated portability.
scores.quote: the value proposition for all these 3 components have to remain high for them to remain continuously invested and committed to the CDSL platform

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-product technology depth with tech spend now exceeding employee cost across infrastructure, application, security and network, but the edge over NSDL is one of execution and service rather than proprietary, defensible technology.
scores.quote: technology is the DNA of our business. It's kind of the Raw Material, Work in Progress, and Finished goods

scores.rationale: A real two-sided reinforcement exists — more DPs choosing CDSL brings more investors, which pulls issuers and sustains 85-90% incremental account share — but investors do not gain value from other investors, so the effect is distributional rather than classic.
scores.quote: there has been a consistent growth investor wanting to access the CDSL platform, the market share of new account openings always in the range of 85% plus

scores.rationale: The DP network and service reach are the decisive competitive asset — near-universal geographic coverage plus API connectivity tailored to fintech, mid-size and small DPs, converting into 85-90% of all new accounts.
scores.quote: maintaining our 80% plus market share with a consistently incremental market share of 85% to 90%, supported by the continuous trust of investors and depository participants

scores.rationale: Growth capex has scaled steadily from ~INR700cr (FY23) to ~INR1,076cr (FY26) and a guided INR1,300-1,400cr for FY27 plus a board-approved INR1,205cr 2-wheeler expansion, funded largely from internal accruals with utilisation at 85-95%, but returns are only 'double digit post tax ROCE' rather than exceptional.
scores.quote: our Board of Directors...approved a capex of about INR1,205 crores for setting up additional 53,000 2-wheeler tyres capacity

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P through IPL/WPL strategic timeout partnerships, brand ambassadors and digital lead-gen is showing measurable brand and sales payoff (top-10 Brand Finance ranking, +46% positive sentiment, 2x premium lead-gen sales).
scores.quote: Our premium sales through lead generation grew 2x in quarter 1 while overall 4-wheeler sale through lead generation grew 32%

scores.rationale: R&D output is consistent and commercially converted — 130+ new off-highway SKUs in FY26, Secura Lyfe 2-wheeler launch, premium low-TCO TBR, EV-specific OEM approvals and BEE 5-star ratings — though R&D intensity is never separately disclosed.
scores.quote: About 130-plus new off-highway SKUs were launched, which gives robustness to our product portfolio

scores.rationale: The CAMSO carve-out from Michelin is neither small nor simple: a 4-6 quarter transition with value chain control only by FY28, start-up costs, warehouse/hiring drag and Sri Lankan currency losses that pulled consolidated PAT to INR4cr versus INR98cr standalone in Q1 FY27.
scores.quote: higher costs in our CAMSO business arising from initial investments in new warehouses, new offices, start-up costs, new hirings there without commensurate growth in revenue

scores.rationale: Distribution is a plain, consistent dividend (120% final for FY23, dividend again recommended for FY26) with no buybacks and no articulated valuation-linked framework; cash is prioritised for capex.
scores.quote: Board in the meeting yesterday approved a final dividend of about 120% for the year

scores.rationale: Tyre manufacturing is structurally asset-heavy — INR1,000cr+ annual capex, INR3,011cr consolidated debt and rising depreciation from new plants against INR15,678cr revenue — and there is no moat protecting those assets from commodity-driven margin swings.
scores.quote: our capex was about INR1,076 crores in FY '26...Our consolidated debt stood at INR3,011 crores

scores.rationale: As a challenger brand with clear runway, CEAT has repeatedly converted it into measured share gains across categories in replacement and OEM over the period.
scores.quote: In PC UV about 0.5% up; in motorcycle, about 1% up...in truck bus radial also about 0.5% up in replacement

scores.rationale: Geographic build-out is credible and executed over years — US GTM, European entities in Germany/UK/France/Poland, new markets like Vietnam and Peru, IB growing ~30% — but the 26% saliency target promised for FY26 landed at ~23%.
scores.quote: We have set up overseas entities and branches in Germany, U.K., France and Poland to build a more permanent localized presence

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume-led with pricing acting only as lagging cost pass-through, which collapsed standalone EBITDA margin to 9.1% in Q1 FY27 when RM rose 16-18%.
scores.quote: 2/3rd of the stand-alone revenue growth came from volumes and balance 1/3rd of the growth came from price and mix

scores.rationale: The company is currently at a raw-material-driven cyclical trough — margins compressed from 14.6% to 9.1% on a 16-18% RM spike — with price hikes underway and a stated expectation of commodity stabilisation, implying an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: We expect the commodity prices to stabilize once the West Asia war comes to an end...hopefully, in the second half of the year

scores.rationale: End markets show secular drivers — premiumisation (17-inch+ replacement saliency guided from 13% to 30-40% over five years), EV fitments and post-GST consumption uplift — though the underlying tyre market remains GDP-and-cycle linked.
scores.quote: The market saliency is about 13%, and it will grow to 30-40% in the next 5 years

scores.rationale: Leverage has been managed prudently throughout (debt/EBITDA 2.1 in FY23 falling to 1.22 in FY25, 1.6 in Q1 FY27) and capex funded from accruals, but the sizeable CAMSO cross-border acquisition cuts against the organic-only, no-big-M&A criterion.
scores.quote: we have managed all our capital expenditure of about close to INR900 crores in the year only from our internal accruals

scores.rationale: The same four strategic pillars — electrification, international, premiumisation, digital — have been articulated and pursued unchanged across the entire 2023-2026 period, with multi-year projects like the US entry taken from plan to committed channel orders.
scores.quote: we are looking at electrification, international business, premiumization and digital and we talk about these 4 pillars in every analyst meet

scores.rationale: Commentary is substance-heavy and operationally detailed, but CEAT is a highly visible promoter-family (Goenka/RPG) brand that deliberately buys mass visibility via IPL/WPL sponsorships and celebrity ambassadors.
scores.quote: CEAT was proud to get associated with the first edition of Women's Premier League as strategic time out partner

scores.rationale: Leadership succession was internal — Arnab Banerjee elevated to MD & CEO after ~18 years inside CEAT — supported by workplace recognition and a rising employee happiness score.
scores.quote: Arnab has been associated with CEAT in multiple roles since 2005 and lastly, as the Chief Operating Officer

scores.rationale: Management gives granular forward RM and pricing guidance, openly admits when its own forecasts were wrong, and volunteers standalone-vs-consolidated bridges, VRS exceptional items and working-capital deteriorations rather than burying them.
scores.quote: international rubber price remaining at a level of $1,900-$2,000 was a surprise with respect to our own assessment

scores.rationale: Reported results track the raw-material cycle far more than managerial skill — EBITDA margin swung 12.9% (FY23) to 10.5% (Q3 FY25) to 14.6% (Q4 FY26) to 9.1% (Q1 FY27) largely on rubber and crude — so strong headline years should not be read as durable execution alpha.
scores.quote: The margin drop is primarily on account of the net increase in raw material prices, which we could not pass it on to customers

scores.rationale: CEAT is a challenger competing on share gains of half a percent at a time across categories, with no monopoly-like ownership of the customer's mind or of any aftermarket niche.
scores.quote: In PC UV about 0.5% up; in motorcycle, about 1% up

scores.rationale: Replacement tyres carry negligible switching costs and no captive aftermarket — CEAT must re-win the customer at every purchase and OEM fitments themselves shift with model production ramps.
scores.quote: we were slightly down in passenger car segment, less than about 1% down...these are minor adjustments in terms of models and production ramp-up

scores.rationale: The Indian tyre market behaves as a stable oligopoly where the industry moves price together during input inflation, indicating limited end-customer negotiating power.
scores.quote: the competition has been taking up price hikes in different measures, in different categories, a little bit here and there on dates, but the price table is moving up

scores.rationale: Capital intensity (INR1,200cr for one 2-wheeler capacity block) keeps new entrants out and pricing has broadly been rational through the cycle, though discounting does appear in soft demand periods.
scores.quote: There have been some minor discounting here and there, which is happening right through the year

scores.rationale: Consistent share capture in rural 2-wheeler, TBR and premium OEM fitments over multiple years implies weaker players are ceding ground, though no specific donating competitor is named.
scores.quote: The growth rate in rural market was almost 40%-50% higher than the growth rate in the urban market

scores.rationale: CEAT is a heavily covered large-cap with multiple broker-hosted calls, IPL-scale consumer advertising and dual credit-rating surveillance — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We remain associated with IPL as strategic timeout partner in the current edition as well

scores.rationale: Brand equity is real (top-10 Brand Finance, ~40% gross margin in good quarters) but it does not confer pricing power — a 16% RM spike forced a 575bps gross margin contraction before prices could catch up.
scores.quote: Q1 standalone gross margin witnessed a contraction of 575 basis points Q-o-Q

scores.rationale: Repeated OEM quality and service awards from Maruti, Mahindra, Renault-Nissan and Daimler, plus first-in-India EV CV tyre approval, show customers buying reliability and validation rather than price alone.
scores.quote: We also got recognition and awards from OEM such as Daimler for the service level and quality

scores.rationale: CEAT explicitly attributes outperformance to superior reach in under-served rural markets, supplemented by a growing direct D2C channel.
scores.quote: higher growth coming in from the rural market where we have a distribution advantage

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is sensibly matched — brand/image marketing and D2C for retail replacement buyers, and TCO/reliability plus indexed pricing contracts for OEM corporate customers.
scores.quote: we have launched a couple of absolutely top-of-the-line premium products, which gives a lower TCO to our customers

scores.rationale: There is genuine process and digital capability (two WEF Lighthouse plants, enterprise data lake, agentic AI, EV-specific approvals) but no deep proprietary product-technology edge versus global majors, and R&D sits inside routine capex.
scores.quote: our Chennai plant has been designated as a World Economic Forum Lighthouse. This is the second plant of CEAT which got this recognition

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.

Distribution is CEAT's most cited competitive edge — a rural reach rivals struggle to match domestically, now being replicated internationally through localised European entities and US regional distributors.
scores.quote: The initial set of regional distributors has been set up. Product feedback is good. And we have a visibility of commitments made by our channel partners

scores.rationale: Growth capex has been large and sustained (Rs 200cr glass plant, Rs 275cr FY25, Rs 219cr FY26 for steel bottle lines) but incremental returns have been poor — glassware sits at 60% utilisation at mere breakeven and FY27 capex is cut to ~Rs 100cr, mostly maintenance.
scores.quote: the business has reached breakeven and is contributing meaningfully to revenue. Profitability from glass will take some time to scale

scores.rationale: Management asserts "consistent spending towards brand building" but never quantifies A&P or links it to measurable sales/brand-equity outcomes, and demand-led discounting was used instead in weak quarters.
scores.quote: consistent spending towards brand building and a strategic expansion in our overall reach

scores.rationale: There is continuous new-product launch activity (premium pens, drinker collection, added stationery lines) but no R&D spend, capability or efficiency is ever discussed, and the steel-bottle capability had to be bought/built only after BIS blocked Chinese imports.
scores.quote: We continue to churn out new and innovative products every year

scores.rationale: Deals are small and complementary (Cello stationery brand buy-back, Wimplast merger) and lifted writing-instruments revenue 64%, but the acquired brand carried loss-making products needing rationalisation, the deal structure was opaque enough that analysts could not follow it, and consolidated margins fell rather than improved.
scores.quote: there were a lot of loss-making products in that particular portfolio

scores.rationale: An analyst directly asked how dividend payouts are balanced against capex funding and the CFO answered only on raw material pricing and capex, leaving no articulated distribution policy or buyback evidence on record.

The business is working-capital heavy (159 days working capital, receivables 111-124 days, inventory ~88-98 days) and increasingly capital-intensive with glass furnaces and steel lines running at 60% and partial utilisation, so asset turn is mediocre rather than asset-light.
scores.quote: trade receivables, which are about at 124 days in quarter 2 of '25 has now improved to about 111 days

scores.rationale: There is genuine runway (writing instruments cover only ~55% of India geography, small appliances base) but no demonstrated capture — growth fell from 30% pre-IPO to 4-9%, and steelware sales dropped 25% on self-inflicted stockouts.
scores.quote: we cover only 55% of India geography, so there is ample room for growth

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic tier-2/3 distribution plus an export book of only ~8-9% of sales that has been volatile (declines on shipping issues, later recovery), with no evidence of a premium brand travelling internationally.
scores.quote: we are getting now more into two and three tier cities also where we were not before

scores.rationale: Growth has been volume/capacity-led rather than price/mix-led: value growth trailed volume when polymer prices fell, discounts were passed on in weak demand, premiumisation is only 7-8% of mix, and the FY26 12-20% MRP hikes were cost pass-through, not pricing power.
scores.quote: there were some discounts that were passed on because due to weak demand conditions

scores.rationale: Management has positioned the company at a cyclical trough with an upturn ahead for three straight years (tax cuts, rate cuts, steel ramp, glass scaling) yet each promised rebound has been deferred, so the bottom is asserted rather than demonstrated.
scores.quote: financial year 26 represented a phase of temporary consolidation

scores.rationale: Core end-markets (consumerware, hydration, stationery, e-commerce/q-commerce now ~17% of sales) are structurally expanding with import substitution and formalisation tailwinds, though molded furniture is in structural decline.
scores.quote: These channels now account for nearly 17% of our overall revenue

scores.rationale: Leverage is negligible (debt-to-equity 0.01), expansion is organic and counter-cyclical (glass and steel plants built through a demand downturn), and acquisitions are confined to in-group bolt-ons rather than large outside M&A.
scores.quote: Debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.01%

scores.rationale: They explicitly accept multi-year losses on glassware for strategic reasons, backward-integrated into steel bottles rather than abandoning the category after BIS, and run a six-decade family franchise, though execution timing has repeatedly slipped.
scores.quote: glassware remains a long-term strategic growth business rather than a near-term profit maximization opportunity

scores.rationale: Calls are brief, factual and run by the JMD and CFO with no celebrity posturing or promotional flourish, and the promoter family stays behind the brand rather than in front of it.
scores.quote: we are only into the niche areas and we are only into kitchen appliances

scores.rationale: Across eleven calls there is no discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline; management commentary is confined to family directors and the CFO.

They do disclose bad news plainly (stockouts, 40% steel decline, gratuity one-off, glass at breakeven) but guidance has been serially cut from 20% to 12-14% to 8-10%, segment data is withheld on "confidentiality", and a capital-allocation question went unanswered.
scores.quote: we do not give out these numbers separately. This is basically together. This is more for our confidentiality

scores.rationale: Stripping the legacy-brand halo, the record is unimpressive — margins fell from 25% to 22.7%, growth halved, and shortfalls are consistently attributed to external causes (demand, China dumping, BIS, war) rather than to execution, including a self-caused steel stockout.
scores.quote: the macro scenario was so bad that probably just keeping our margins intact and growing at maybe a slightly slower pace

scores.rationale: Cello holds genuine mindshare in stationery and lunchboxes/casseroles among household buyers, but it is one of many brands in every category it plays in and has no aftermarket or services lock-in.
scores.quote: Cello being Cello as a brand is very, very strong in the stationery market

scores.rationale: These are low-ticket retail consumer goods with effectively zero switching costs — buyers moved away on discounts and the company lost steelware sales outright when product was unavailable.
scores.quote: we faced stockouts in insulated steel products, which led to an approximate 40% quarter-on-quarter decline

scores.rationale: The end markets are fragmented rather than oligopolistic — unorganised competition in molded furniture, new opalware capacity, Chinese dumping in glassware, and many players in appliances.
scores.quote: In the molded furniture vertical there is a lot of unorganized competition

scores.rationale: Capacity keeps entering (new opalware lines, Chinese glass dumping) and competitors respond to weak demand with discounting, indicating low barriers and imperfect pricing rationality.
scores.quote: there has been additional discounts rolled out by a lot of our competitors as well

scores.rationale: Weak unorganised players in molded furniture and struggling unlisted writing-instrument makers, plus import substitution in glassware, offer identifiable pools of share to take.
scores.quote: even in the unlisted space, people are struggling a little bit

scores.rationale: This is a well-covered post-IPO consumer name with ICICI-hosted calls and a stream of institutional analysts (IIFL, HDFC Life, Nuvama, Investec, PL, Anand Rathi), and new capital is actively entering its categories.
scores.quote: We are happy to witness a healthy response to our IPO

scores.rationale: Gross margins near 50-53% and strong household brand recall point to some intangible pull, but pricing follows raw material costs both ways and they could not raise steelware prices when input costs rose, so image-driven pricing power is limited.
scores.quote: we were buying from China before and then we had to switch to OEMs... but we couldn't increase our selling prices

scores.rationale: Long-standing household trust in the Cello name supports repeat purchase and BIS-compliant manufacturing adds reliability, but price clearly is not secondary — discounts and MRP resistance drove volumes both ways.
scores.quote: she's the decision maker. So, we are getting good response

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the company's clearest customer benefit — general trade is the backbone at ~75-79% of sales, complemented by modern trade, exports and a fast-scaling e-commerce/quick-commerce channel at ~17%.
scores.quote: general trade is the backbone of our distribution network and it is well complemented by modern trade, online and exports

scores.rationale: The customer base is correctly retail/middle-class where intangibles should dominate, but the intangible benefit delivered is thin — premiumisation is only 7-8% of mix against a 20% ambition and demand tracks discretionary spending closely.
scores.quote: the purchasing power of our largest customer segment, the middle class

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed beyond in-house moulds; the company imported steel bottles from China until regulation forced backward integration, and its new glass furnace took months to reach even 60% efficiency.
scores.quote: we have inhouse molds that we are able to work with. So, that differentiates us from the market a little bit

scores.rationale: A single-sided consumer-goods model with no platform, ecosystem or two-sided dynamic — nothing in eleven calls suggests value rises with user count.
scores.quote: All our businesses are consumer-facing

scores.rationale: A pan-India multi-channel network across 13 plants, general trade, modern trade and digital channels is a real asset rivals cannot quickly replicate, though management concedes retail reach in writing instruments is still small.
scores.quote: Our retail network is still very small compared to the size of the market

scores.rationale: Capex is rising (₹150-200cr FY25 → ₹260cr FY26 → ₹350-400cr guided FY27) and is partly growth-oriented (new TBMs for Pune/Delhi Metro, data-centre division) on a ₹10,061cr revenue base with EBITDA margin improving to 11.9%, though management itself labels much of it replacement/formwork spend.
scores.quote: Capex, INR260 crores... '27, it will be more. It will be around INR350 crores to INR400 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt — a B2B tender-driven contractor.
No R&D spend, product development or R&D efficiency is discussed across the 16 calls.
The company is the acquiree (parent stake sold to Adani) rather than an acquirer; apart from a 27% JV stake in Mor Sagar there is no bolt-on M&A programme to judge.

scores.rationale: Disclosure is granular on gas, brass, discounts and tier mix, but management deflected the decade-low 10.2% EBITDA quarter as a phasing 'one-off' and never explicitly owned the abandoned INR2,900 crore guidance when challenged.
scores.quote: it is a one -off kind of a thing and is not expected to continu e as a trend

scores.rationale: The dazzling FY23 numbers (77% revenue growth, 660bps margin expansion) reflected a COVID-depressed base plus industry-wide price hikes rather than durable skill, as the subsequent three years of flat sales and margin erosion to 10-15% demonstrate.
scores.quote: Revenues from operations in Q1 FY23 were Rs. 396 crore versus Rs. 223 crore in Q1FY22, an increase of 77.6%

scores.rationale: CERA has strong brand recall and leadership in sanitaryware, but it is one of several branded players with no monopoly position in the customer's mind and no aftermarket/service annuity.
scores.quote: the core Cera brand remains central to our growth strategy and continues to be the primary driver of volumes

scores.rationale: Bathware is a replacement/retail purchase with no switching costs or captive aftermarket — the company must defend position with trade discounts and loyalty schemes rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: the drop in margins, EBITDA margins by 3%, this was primarily driven by the increase in the trade discounts

scores.rationale: The industry is not a tight oligopoly: roughly 45% of both sanitaryware and faucetware is unorganised, and dealers/projects clearly extract discounts, indicating weak pricing control over the channel.
scores.quote: sanitaryware industry size of the organized sector would be INR 5,000 ... The unorganized for the sanitaryware industry would be something like INR 4,000 crore

scores.rationale: Barriers are low enough that pipe and adjacent building-material players keep entering bathware, and pricing has been irrational — rising trade discounts drove margins to a multi-decade-low 10.2%, with price hikes taken only reactively after a 30% brass cost surge.
scores.quote: the Pipe players are getting into bath ware and paints

scores.rationale: There is a large, visibly weakening unorganised cohort — Morbi players squeezed by pollution norms, brass costs and now gas-availability disruption — from which CERA, insulated by subsidised GAIL gas, is directly taking supply and share.
scores.quote: the industry has been witnessing disruptions in parts of the unorganized sector, particularly in Morbi , due to gas availability challenges ... Cera has remained relatively insulated

scores.rationale: CERA is a four-decade-old listed brand covered by multiple institutional analysts (ICICI, PL, 360 ONE, Yes Securities on the calls), so it is neither obscure nor ignored by capital, though it is a modest mid-cap in an unglamorous category.
scores.quote: We take the next question from the line of Arun Baid from ICICI Securities

scores.rationale: Brand strength was demonstrably real in FY22-23 when ~26-31% cumulative price hikes stuck with no sales dent, but pricing power has since eroded into discount-led competition and EBITDA margins fell to 10.2%.
scores.quote: last year we took 21% price hikes in Sanitaryware, 26% in Faucetware ... And you're seeing no dent on sales velocity.

scores.rationale: Customers and developers buy reliability from CERA — long-standing developer relationships enable participation in complex projects, and it maintained uninterrupted supply while competitors were disrupted by the Morbi gas crisis.
scores.quote: our strong brand equity, execution reliability and long -standing relationships with developers continue to enable participation in larger and more complex projects

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is a genuine strength: a retailer loyalty platform grown from 11,500 to over 28,000 enrolled retailers, a new dealer management system for secondary-sales visibility, and Tier-3 led geographic reach.
scores.quote: The company's retailer loyalty program with over 28,000 enrolled retailers

scores.rationale: The mix has drifted the wrong way for a retail-brand model — B2C fell from 68% in FY23 to a guided 60%, with projects rising to ~40% on discounted, price-locked orders that management itself blames for margin compression.
scores.quote: the proportion of retail and project should now remain stable at 60% for retail and 40% for the project business

scores.rationale: There is no disclosed R&D intensity or proprietary technology edge — differentiation is design/SKU refresh and automation of existing lines, and the company was still importing product from China as recently as FY25.
scores.quote: In Q1 FY 25, our imports from China totalled INR 7 crore , representing 2% of the sales.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the retailer app is a loyalty/data tool, not a network.

Distribution reach is the company's most defensible asset — a national dealer-retailer network skewed to Tier-3 (40% of sales), 40 Senator flagship stores, 102 Polipluz distributors and institutional franchise tie-ups built over four decades.
scores.quote: we have onboarded 102 distributors and 1,120 dealers during FY26, with a target to expand the network to 200 distributors and 2,000 dealers

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly growth-oriented — a gold-loan branch build from zero (INR560mn budgeted FY23, 750 branches in 15 months, 1,429 total by Q4FY26) that is now converting into rising incremental returns (branch productivity INR17cr, ROA 3.5%, ROE 16.5%).
scores.quote: Our total branch network expanded to 1,429 locations in Q4 FY '26 with a net addition of 98 branches during the quarter and 318 branches during the year

scores.rationale: A&P is mentioned only in passing as a cost driver and as 'brand visibility' from branch openings, with no evidence of durable brand equity or measurable sales lift from marketing spend.
scores.quote: majorly due to strategic investment in expanding our team and implementing impactful marketing initiative s

scores.rationale: Sustained technology 'R&D' (INR112cr in FY24 alone, in-house LOS/LMS, SPARK, Orion, Pegasus, and a proprietary small language model) has consistently yielded new capability and hard efficiency output — disbursements +83% on headcount +19% and cost-to-income from 60% to 49%.
scores.quote: our AUM grew 60% year-on-year. Disbursement grew by 83%, while headcount grew just by 19%

scores.rationale: No acquisition has been executed across the five years; management only notes it privately evaluates inorganic options, leaving nothing to judge.
scores.quote: we are open to exploring inorganic opportunities, but that is something we do not talk about openly

scores.rationale: The company is a net capital raiser (INR1,200cr rights issue, INR2,000cr equity infusion in Q1FY26) with only a token 15% dividend on INR1 face value and no buyback — a growth-funding policy rather than a disciplined distribution policy.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors approved dividend at the rate of 15 % per share on the face value of INR1 for FY24

scores.rationale: As a balance-sheet lender it is inherently asset-heavy, though co-lending at 21-23% of AUM and fee income at ~29-32% of net income add genuine capital-light elements; no protecting moat accompanies it.
scores.quote: This capital-efficient model continues to enhance ROE, diversify funding sources and scale fee-led income without incremental balance sheet strain

scores.rationale: A sub-scale player with enormous runway that is demonstrably capturing share — gold loan built from zero to INR16,965cr and consolidated AUM compounding to INR36,623cr at 60% YoY.
scores.quote: Gold loans grew an impressive 111% year -on-year and MSME grew at healthy 23% year -on-year, while housing loans rose 43%

scores.rationale: Credible, well-executed multi-state expansion into Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and UP with evidence of successful ramp — 90% of gold branches already above breakeven and UP MSME branches hitting run-rate targets.
scores.quote: 90% branches now operating above the breakeven threshold of INR5 crore s AUM per branch

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and branch-led rather than price-led — blended yield is essentially flat at 16.3-16.4% — with only modest mix help from higher-yield gold and a pivot to self-employed housing borrowers.
scores.quote: our blended yields and spreads on net advances remained healthy in the quarter at 16.3% and 7.1%

scores.rationale: The company is riding a favourable rather than a bottoming cycle — falling MCLR/cost of funds and rising gold prices are current tailwinds, not a trough position with an upturn still ahead.
