scores.quote: innovators are recalibrating volumes earlier than we had previously anticipated

scores.rationale: Regulatory and complex-chemistry barriers are meaningful (FDA audits, DMFs, ADC/oligo capability), but pricing rationality is absent where it matters — Chinese generic pressure and 4-5% price corrections show discounting in the commodity-exposed lines.
scores.quote: close to around 4% to 5%... the price correction has happened

scores.rationale: China Plus One and Biosecure dynamics create identifiable weak incumbents to take share from, and Western CDMOs are now outsourcing to Cohance's platforms rather than competing head-on.
scores.quote: we are expanding relationships with Western CDMOs that are seeking to leverage our technology platforms

scores.rationale: The portfolio is genuinely niche and small-volume, but the company is a widely-covered listed PE-backed platform courted by capital, not an ignored corner of the market.
scores.quote: the Cohance portfolio is a little curated and niche

scores.rationale: Gross margin is high at 70.8%, but this is contract manufacturing with no image- or taste-driven pricing power, and demand has proven anything but steady.
scores.quote: Gross margin was at 70.8%. This was supported by product mix, backward integration, cost actions

scores.rationale: Customers clearly buy reliability — 20+ audits and senior customer site visits, healthy OTIF, business continuity audits — although the Nacharam OAI-to-warning-letter sequence is a direct hit to exactly that assurance proposition.
scores.quote: Customer OTIF metrics remain healthy, and we are able to service customer demands effectively

scores.rationale: Customer-facing reach is being rebuilt rather than being an existing advantage — the BD organisation was only described as complete in December 2025, having previously been a recognised gap.
scores.quote: With the completeness of our business development team in December

scores.rationale: The benefit type is correctly matched to a corporate customer base — large innovators buying regulatory reliability, backward integration and TCO with validation-driven lock-in, not brand intangibles.
scores.quote: we are primarily with large Biopharmaceutical companies and we are with large innovative firms only

scores.rationale: The ADC payload-linker and oligonucleotide platforms are genuinely differentiated multi-product capabilities backed by 640 scientists and sustained filings, and are what draws large innovators despite weak financials.
scores.quote: capabilities such as ADCs and oligonucleotides, which are well-differentiated and hard to replicate

scores.rationale: The model is bilateral, project-by-project contract manufacturing across ~140 discrete programs with no two-sided network that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: we have more than 140 active projects across the Pharma CDMO standalone portfolio

scores.rationale: There is no distribution moat — reach is a directly-employed nine-person global BD team recently assembled, and formulation supply itself had to be rerouted to alternate sites during the Nacharam disruption.
scores.quote: we are also transferring select filings to alternate facilities to manage risk and ensure supply continuity

scores.rationale: No discussion of capital expenditure, capacity addition or incremental ROIC on plant appears anywhere in the seven calls.

scores.rationale: The end market is stable-to-slowly-growing (consumption ~24 million tons, flat YoY) but with genuine structural mix shifts Coromandel is levered to — NPK share rising to 60% of phosphatics, import substitution of 6-7 million tons of DAP, and biologicals adoption.
scores.quote: Consumption for the year was close to 24 million tons, more or less the same as the previous year, and the mix is favoring NPK ... The share of NPKs in the overall Phosphatics is currently at 60%.

scores.rationale: Net cash of INR 4,214 crores while self-funding a multi-thousand-crore capex programme, conservative FX hedging, AA+ rating, and a counter-cyclical call to moderate production and protect sourcing economics rather than chase volume.
scores.quote: the company took a conscious call to moderate phos acid production and ensure that the prices of sulphur reach a reasonable level to be competitive on sourcing

scores.rationale: A decade-long backward-integration thesis was stated in 2022 (Senegal rock stake, sulphuric acid) and delivered on schedule by 2026 — Senegal stake raised 45%→53.8%→71.5%, output above 3.5 lakh tons, Kakinada acid plants commissioned March 2026 as promised in 2024.
scores.quote: This project is likely to be commissioned by March '26 ... In March month, company successfully commissioned the 2,000 tons per day Sulphuric acid plant and 650 tons per day Phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and metric-dense with no promotional framing or personality-building, and management defers credit to functional teams rather than itself.
scores.quote: Commercial and sourcing teams did very well to ensure timely availability of raw material

scores.rationale: Safety and operational-excellence certifications suggest systematic capability building, but the excerpts say nothing about talent development or succession pipeline, and MD turnover has been high (Goel → Alagappan → Vellayan family → Sankarasubramanian, with two CFOs).
scores.quote: one of our largest fertilizer plant has been given British Safety Council Five-Star Rating

scores.rationale: Management volunteers bad news plainly — the Dhaksha drone impairment, the Q4 profit optics from the prior-year land sale, the Nano bans in UP and Maharashtra, and market share falling from 17.8% to 13.5% in 2022 — each with its reason stated.
scores.quote: the reported profit is modest at INR 115 crores due to this variation of almost INR 420 crores between the corresponding periods

scores.rationale: Much of the earnings swing is exogenous — monsoon quality, NBS subsidy rates and global commodity prices drive results as visibly as management action, so skill cannot be cleanly separated from a favourable multi-year agri cycle.
scores.quote: The decrease in revenues is mainly on account of drop-in subsidy rates in the fertilizer business

scores.rationale: Genuine niche near-monopolies exist — ~60% share in Nano DAP, market leadership in SSP and in neem-based biopesticides — though these are small relative to the core fertilizer business.
scores.quote: a market leadership position with nearly 60% of market share

scores.rationale: Strong regional entrenchment in the South backed by 1,200+ captive retail outlets creates local dominance and direct farmer capture, but fertilizer itself is a fungible commodity with negligible switching costs.
scores.quote: The business deepened its reach through additional 22 new stores, taking the network to over 1,200 outlets.

scores.rationale: Phosphatics is a concentrated industry with high capital and raw-material-linkage barriers where Coromandel is the largest player at 17.5% share, but pricing is set by government NBS rates rather than by industry structure.
scores.quote: making us the largest player with the highest market share of 17.5% in the phosphatic sector in the country

scores.rationale: Entry requires securing rock, acid and ammonia linkages that took Coromandel years and thousands of crores, and industry conduct is rational — coordinated via an empowered government-industry committee, with restrained price action rather than discounting.
scores.quote: An empowered committee comprising of government and industry officials have been working in close coordination for fertilizer production, planning and raw material sourcing.

scores.rationale: Coromandel is explicitly taking share from importers (6-7 million tons of imported DAP targeted for NPK substitution) and from weaker players hit by production outages, and NACL itself was a loss-making donator it acquired.
scores.quote: industry is still importing 6 to 7 million tons of DAP and NPKs ... And that is where Coromandel is looking to fill this and substitute the imported DAP with NPKs.

scores.rationale: This is a large, heavily analyst-covered listed fertilizer major hosting quarterly calls with multiple brokerages, operating in a politically salient, subsidy-driven sector — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Coromandel has reported highest ever revenue of INR 31,827 crores

scores.rationale: Gromor/GroPlus branding and unique grades earn some premium, but the core product is a subsidised commodity where farm-gate prices are administered and affordability, not image, governs demand.
scores.quote: these rates do not reflect the sharp increase in raw material prices ... Industry expects further support to address the affordability issue for the farming community.

scores.rationale: Reliable availability is the company's core promise to farmers and it was demonstrably delivered during the West Asia shortage when rivals cut production, backed by Responsible Care and British Safety Council certifications.
scores.quote: Commissioning of these plants has happened at a very opportune time, and this has ensured that we continue to produce and make phosphate fertilisers available to farmers when industry is facing shortage of key raw materials.

scores.rationale: Deep direct customer intimacy via 1,200+ own retail stores growing 85% YoY with 76% profitable, plus nutri clinics, drone spraying on 3 lakh acres, e-commerce and last-mile delivery — a reach management says outperforms the trade channel.
scores.quote: whatever new products we are introducing in various business segments, retail could scale up the volumes and go to market much better than the trade channel

scores.rationale: The customer is the retail farmer and the benefit stack is correctly matched — advisory, clinics, drone services, direct stores and last-mile delivery build stickiness where product intangibles alone would be weak.
scores.quote: The direct connect with customers is really helpful to understand the psych of the customer and ensure that we position the products well.

scores.rationale: Real but narrow tech edge — nanotechnology leadership, fluoro chemistry and CDMO capability build, fermentation/microbial platforms and a new IIT research centre — meaningful in the non-subsidy businesses but not the fertilizer core.
scores.quote: developing next-generation platform technologies in Nano, Biologicals and Advanced Chemistries

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts; the retail and dealer network is a distribution asset, not a self-reinforcing network.

A distribution moat rivals cannot easily replicate — 1,200+ owned rural stores, 1,000+ new dealers onboarded in FY26, drone spraying services and nutri clinics — in a business where last-mile availability during shortages is decisive.
scores.quote: In domestic market, we expanded our presence by introducing new territories, onboarding over 1000 new dealers

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-directed — 400mn tablet/capsule capacity commissioned Dec 2025, a 600-kg line adding ~40% capacity, a dedicated hormone plant due Q1/Q2 FY27 and a further plant planned for FY28-29 — funded internally at ROCE of 41-49%.
scores.quote: We are undertaking the expansion of our manufacturing capabilities through the addition of a new 600-kg line expansion, alongside the commissioning of our dedicated hormone manufacturing plant

scores.rationale: A&P plus sales promotion runs ~19% of sales (10% KOL consulting, 5% S&D promotion, 4% scientific conferences) and has demonstrably built brand equity — two brands now above INR 100 crore and 38 brands above INR 10 crore — though it is doctor-facing scientific spend rather than consumer brand-building.
scores.quote: 10% would be in the form of consulting… with the key opinion leaders, 5% would be in the form of S&D, promotion spend, and 4% in the form of scientific conferences

scores.rationale: R&D is deliberately kept below 2% of sales — lower than peers, as an analyst flagged — yet new-introduction growth of 6.4% was 2.6x the IPM's 2.5%, implying high efficiency per rupee spent rather than depth.
scores.quote: the percentage contribution to the R&D will remain less than 2%. And today about 100 plus scientists are working in R&D

scores.rationale: Deals are small complementary brand bolt-ons (seven Bayer-Zydus trademarks, Wokadine ranked #2 in povidone iodine) with a stated track record of scaling brands previously bought from GSK, Abbott and Sanofi, funded from cash with margins still expanding 80bps in FY26.
scores.quote: After acquiring brands from giants like GlaxoSmithKline, Abbott, Sanofi, etc., we have been successful in scaling those brands considerably

scores.rationale: A maiden 100% dividend of INR 10/share was declared in FY26 but there is no buyback, no stated payout policy and only one post-listing year of history to judge discipline against.
scores.quote: We are delighted to announce 100% dividend, which is equal to ₹10 per share for FY26

scores.rationale: Capital efficiency is exceptional — ROCE 41-49%, ROE ~29-31%, net working capital of 23 days and a net cash balance sheet — combined with a branded-prescription moat that protects those returns.
scores.quote: net working capital days stood at the best of the class at 23 days

scores.rationale: At only ~1.9% share of its covered market and rank 27 in IPM, the runway is large and share capture is documented — fastest-growing among the top 30 companies, up five ranks in three years, growing at nearly 2x IPM.
scores.quote: CORONA continues to be the fastest-growing pharmaceutical company among the top 30 companies in IPM. Our industry ranking has improved to 27th position, moving five spots in last three years

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is credible but early and deliberately small — EAEU GMP certification opens five Eurasian markets and international grew 29.5% in FY26, yet exports are only ~4% of revenue and management guides to a 90:10 India-international mix even long term.
scores.quote: this 3%-4% will go to 7%-8% and then further go to 8%-9% in the years to come

scores.rationale: Pricing is the single largest growth component at 7.8% (helped by a 92-93% non-NLEM portfolio allowing 10% annual hikes) and management calls it sustainable, but they repeatedly frame volume plus new introductions as their differentiating driver rather than price/mix.
scores.quote: the pricing growth as reported by PharmaTrac is around 7.8%… It is absolutely sustainable. The reason is only about our 93% portfolio of non-NELM

scores.rationale: The only cyclical signal is a mild IPM upturn — double-digit industry growth in the last five months versus 8.6% for FY26 — which is a modest tailwind, not a bottom-of-cycle position.
scores.quote: IPM, the industry has recorded double-digit growth over the past five months, which is an extremely positive development

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — a INR 2.32 lakh crore Indian pharma market compounding 8.5-10%, with the company's 72% chronic/semi-chronic mix plus new secular pockets in infertility, GLP-1 and biosimilars.
scores.quote: it's about INR 2,32,000 crores market growing at the speed of about 8.5% on year-on-year

scores.rationale: Net cash with no cash-credit utilisation (the INR 143 crore 'borrowing' is an overdraft against own FDs), growth funded from operating cash flow, and expansion confined to small brand bolt-ons rather than large M&A.
scores.quote: we don't have any single cash credit facility from any banks… INR 142.9 crores borrowings is only because of the overdraft on the basis of FDs which we have

scores.rationale: A 21-year build with a deliberate multi-year sequencing plan — unlocking one therapy at a time over 3-5 years, backward integrating into hormone API via La Chandra, and delivering 15%+ revenue and 20%+ PAT every year since FY22.
scores.quote: we will unlock each therapy at the right time, starting with the infertility in this year. Slowly and gradually, we will unlock each therapies in, next 3 to 4 to 5 years of time

scores.rationale: Humility is an explicit stated culture pillar and the company operated privately for 21 years before its Dec 2025 listing, though post-IPO commentary leans heavily on 'fastest growing' rankings and self-promotion.
scores.quote: We believe in internal promotion, adaptability and humbleness

scores.rationale: Internal promotion is a named culture pillar, employee training spend rose 50%, and 600 MRs were added over three years with a disclosed productivity ladder by tenure (INR 2.5 lakh at 0-3 years rising to INR 8 lakh at 6-9 years) — systematic, though the senior pipeline is largely asserted.
scores.quote: Investing in employee training increased by 50% and promoting gender equality

scores.rationale: Management quantified the Q4 margin miss line by line (INR 9 crore employee, INR 5 crore MR expenses, INR 1.6 crore BE/R&D), openly conceded lower-than-peer R&D and PCPM, explained the borrowings optically, and named accepting mistakes as a core value.
scores.quote: in the Q4, INR 9 crores was additionally spent in the form of the forming of two new divisions… and INR 1.6 crores relates to the BE cost, which is an R&D in nature

scores.rationale: Results are strong but the public record is only two quarters old, growth has been input-driven (600 MRs added, brands bought from MNCs) and EBITDA margins of ~21% still trail peers at 35%, so skill is not yet cleanly separable from spend and industry tailwind.
scores.quote: when it comes to margins we are still at around 22% to 24% kind of a range whereas similar business mix or product mix companies are also operating at 35% plus EBITDA margin

scores.rationale: Several brands hold a differentiated position in the prescriber's mind — B29 at INR 150 crore positioned specifically for diabetic neuropathy, two brands above INR 100 crore and many ranked top-five in category — but none is a true monopoly and overall share is only ~1.9%.
scores.quote: our number one brand B29, which is about INR 150 crores plus brand… it is the brand for neuro diabetic neuropathy management

scores.rationale: Switching costs come from prescription stickiness in a 72% chronic portfolio plus exclusive in-licensing from Ferring (one of only three Indian licensees), though these are contractual and habitual rather than a hard captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: CORONA is one of the only three Indian companies to have in-licensed any brand from Ferring

scores.rationale: The Indian pharma market is structurally fragmented rather than oligopolistic — the top 50 take 79% while the remainder is split across roughly 1,300-1,400 ranked companies, and CORONA itself is only rank 27.
scores.quote: about 79% of that market is being diversified from the top 50 company and the rest has been diversified between 51 to 1,300, 1,400 ranked company

scores.rationale: Management cites complex supply chain and brand management as the scale barrier, pricing is rational and regulated (non-NLEM 10% annual lever, no discount wars), and they explicitly refused to relax credit/discount hygiene to win institutional IVF business — but the long tail of 1,300+ competitors caps the score.
scores.quote: in this institute business we have decided not to give any leverage onto the fundamentals of CORONA

scores.rationale: Multinationals are actively donating share — brands acquired cheaply from GSK, Abbott, Sanofi and now Bayer-Zydus were under-promoted by their prior owners, giving CORONA ready-made share to reclaim.
scores.quote: The promotion has gone a little slow because of the priorities of the earlier company. But now we have gone and launched that brand in the Indian market

scores.rationale: The middle-of-pyramid and hormone niches are genuinely under-served, but after the December 2025 listing the company is already covered by Kotak, JM, IIFL, Ambit, InCred and multiple funds — it is no longer under the radar.
scores.quote: The theme for international market remain - think hormone, think CORONA. It's absolutely a niche in this segment

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 81.4% with sustainable 7.8% price growth and a deliberate branded-versus-generic positioning (management's own Colgate analogy) evidences pricing power from image and trust with steady chronic demand.
scores.quote: Brand gives a flavor, a quality adherence and the confidence in the set customer's mind

scores.rationale: The proposition is certainty — EU-GMP, WHO-GMP and EAEU-GMP accreditations under a 'one world, one quality' banner, QR-code anti-counterfeiting, and explicit reliance on 'quality trust' to relaunch the Bayer brands.
scores.quote: there is a legacy in the mind of the customer and the quality trust

scores.rationale: Direct customer intimacy is the core asset — 2,600+ medical representatives pan-India, a dedicated 46-person team covering 3,000 IVF centres, cold-chain capability, and AI-based sales force effectiveness lifting PCPM from INR 3.62 lakh to INR 4.11 lakh.
scores.quote: today we have a PCPM of INR 4.11 lakhs… which was last year about INR 3,62,000

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to channel — B2C branded intangibles and specialist relationships in India, B2B reliability-led supply in exports, and a refusal to trade discounts in the institutional IVF channel — though institutional lock-in is still unproven.
scores.quote: In B2B model, in India we are working on B2C model… when you are working on B2B model or international business, it's been a less gross margin and more EBITDA

scores.rationale: There is real process capability (EU-GMP hormone API backward integration, 100+ scientists, DSIR-approved centres, three biosimilar launches) but R&D is deliberately under 2% of sales and the differentiated technology is licensed in rather than owned.
scores.quote: the products are little unique, little different and the technology is of Bayer, so we will take the utmost advantage of it

scores.rationale: No discussion of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network across the three calls.
A 2,600-strong MR network with pan-India distributors, cold chain and specialist targeting is a genuine reach advantage in a service-vital market, but at rank 27 in IPM larger peers can match it.
scores.quote: today we are on a critical mark of around 2,600 plus medical representatives

scores.rationale: Capacity scaled 1.5m→1.9m→2.5m units/month within FY26 with new housing/enclosure, lens, Noida and Kadapa expansions funded from internal accruals, alongside EBITDA margin rising 6.9%→18% — clearly growth capex earning high incremental returns.
scores.quote: Our manufacturing capacity has now reached 2.5 million units... The project is fully funded through internal accruals.

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P — airport OOH, IFSEC, PACC and IPL Punjab Kings title sponsorships, Vijay Sethupathi/Prithviraj campaigns and 141 co-funded Galaxy stores — has built the only true consumer brand in a B2B category, coinciding with share moving from ~21% to ~45%.
scores.quote: the first player to create a true consumer brand in India's security and surveillance industry

scores.rationale: R&D footprint expanded from one Noida centre to Ahmedabad, Taiwan (wholly-owned subsidiary), and a planned Bangalore centre with DSIR-certified labs, and it converted directly into the largest STQC-certified portfolio plus Qualcomm and L&T Semiconductor programs.
scores.quote: We have also incorporated Aditya Infotech Taiwan Company Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary dedicated to global R&D

scores.rationale: The only real deal — buying Dixon's 50% of the existing manufacturing JV in Sept 2024 — was a small, complementary bolt-on of an already-working asset and is explicitly cited as a margin lever, though management now flags open-ended 'selective inorganic' intent.
scores.quote: we are now fully integrating AIL Dixon... this is also leading to efficiencies of scale that are coming in manufacturing

scores.rationale: Only a maiden INR1.6/share dividend post-IPO with no buyback and no articulated distribution policy; capital priority is stated as capex and inorganic growth, which is defensible but not a distribution track record.
scores.quote: We have announced a dividend of INR1.6 per equity share

scores.rationale: FY26 revenue of INR4,220 crores against a capex plan of only INR200-300 crores and a single Kadapa plant implies high asset turn, protected by brand and distribution, though outsourcing of HD analog to EMS is what keeps it light rather than a structural asset-light model.
scores.quote: HD analog job work is being planned to be moved to EMS players for further enhancing scalability

scores.rationale: Own-brand share went from ~25% at IPO to ~45.4% by Q3 FY26 versus a projected 36%, and with the remaining ~55% split among ~30 sub-scale brands the runway is still real.
scores.quote: our market share reached approximately 45.4%, establishing us as the clear market leader

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely within India (500+ cities, South/West traction, regional celebrity campaigns) with no export or overseas sales strategy disclosed; Taiwan is an R&D office, not a market entry.
scores.quote: revenue grew 35.6% year-on-year to INR4,220.8 crores, driven by market share gains across geographies

scores.rationale: FY27 guidance explicitly splits growth into 25-30% units and a 20-25% rise in per-unit realisation from staggered price hikes plus the HD-to-IP mix shift, and Q4 gross margin expanded ~900bps on that mix.
scores.quote: the average per unit camera recovery is expected to rise by 20% to 25%

scores.rationale: The regulatory reset is behind them and the memory/SoC cost cycle is near a peak with costs 'likely to continue rising until 2027', so the company sits after a favourable inflection rather than at the bottom of a cycle.
scores.quote: Industry trends indicate that costs are likely to continue rising until 2027

scores.rationale: India's video surveillance market is underpenetrated and forecast to compound 16.5% to FY30 with units nearly doubling from 39.7m to 75m, driven by urbanisation, safe-city spend and the analog-to-IP/AI shift.
scores.quote: growth is expected to continue at a CAGR of 16.5% annually until FY '30

scores.rationale: IPO proceeds cut gross debt 89% to INR48 crores, expansion is funded from internal accruals, and they invested counter-cyclically by pre-paying and forward-ordering chipsets three quarters ahead while smaller rivals froze.
scores.quote: This repayment has reduced our gross debt by 89%, bringing it down to just Rs. 48 crores

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-decade arc — distributor (1995) to own brand (2007) to Dixon JV (2017) to full manufacturing ownership (2024) to component backward integration and an FY28 2x-capacity vision — shows long-horizon execution independent of the easy distribution profit pool they walked away from.
scores.quote: our vision is to expand overall production capacity to 2x of the existing capacity, achieve complete backward integration

scores.rationale: The brand is loudly promoted but the promoters themselves are low-key operators who only began public disclosure with the Aug 2025 maiden call and speak in operational detail rather than self-promotion.
scores.quote: thank you for joining us today for this maiden Earnings Call

scores.rationale: They are scaling talent systematically — 4,100+ employees, a 50,000-participant Mission Tech skilling program with the Ministry of Skill Development, and hiring 20-year global R&D veterans — but senior additions (President Manufacturing, GM Credit) are lateral hires rather than evidence of an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: successfully engaged over 50,000 participants until now under our Mission Tech and other training programs

scores.rationale: Across four calls they repeatedly disclosed unflattering specifics — low-cost inventory now exhausted, profit growth will lag revenue, price-pass-through lag, a INR7.7 crore labour-code provision — and cut their own market-growth assumption from 20%+ to 15% rather than defending it.
scores.quote: the benefit of company's earlier low-cost inventory has now been exhausted... profitability growth may not mirror the pace of the revenue growth

scores.rationale: The spectacular FY26 numbers are substantially a regulatory windfall — the STQC mandate disqualified Chinese incumbents and handed over their share — so results overstate management skill even though the 2017 manufacturing bet and certification readiness were genuine preparation.
scores.quote: the neighboring country brands... will generate a vacuum in the market which is the opportunity for domestic brands

scores.rationale: CP PLUS occupies a category-defining position in the Indian customer's mind with a recall tagline and ~45% share, but the monopoly is brand-led rather than locked in via aftermarket or service annuity.
scores.quote: consumer brand that is literally synonymous with the category

scores.rationale: Competition is genuinely broken by certification and supply-chain exclusion of Chinese brands, and the new Nexivue brand creates city-level exclusive distribution rights, but end-customer switching costs on CCTV hardware remain low.
scores.quote: it's like a city-based exclusive kind-of-a model with the Nexivue brand

scores.rationale: The structure is a dominant leader plus a fragmented fringe of ~30 brands each roughly a tenth its size, not a stable oligopoly, and management itself cannot name a credible number two.
scores.quote: most of them are probably one tenth of our size at the moment or even lower

scores.rationale: STQC/BIS certification, semiconductor allocation and manufacturing scale form real barriers and the leader is setting orderly monthly price rises rather than discounting, but ~30 brands did clear certification and the company itself launched Eyra explicitly to fight on price at the bottom.
scores.quote: we have an option of playing price cards against the private Indian brands

scores.rationale: Two waves of donators exist — Chinese brands like Dahua/Hikvision disqualified by STQC (Dahua revenue collapsing to under INR100-150 crores) and the small domestic tail now unable to secure memory or SoCs.
scores.quote: the big get bigger and the smaller tail is the largely affected one

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a INR1,300 crore IPO, coverage by ICICI, Axis, Ambit and IIFL, celebrity and IPL sponsorships, and a sector now flagged as a national-policy priority.
scores.quote: our IPO successfully raised Rs. 1,300 crores

scores.rationale: Brand image supports real pricing power — a 6-8% January hike passed through plus monthly increases without volume loss — but gross margin at ~31.8% is respectable-for-hardware rather than a high-gross-margin consumer franchise.
scores.quote: We have also announced a price hike of 6% to 8%... which is already passed to the market

scores.rationale: The entire value proposition post-STQC is certified trust and cyber-security ('Trust Core'), with government, BFSI and enterprise buyers choosing compliance and supply reliability over the cheapest device.
scores.quote: largest portfolio of CP PLUS trusted-core cyber-secured products

scores.rationale: Access is the company's most tangible edge: 1,000+ distributors, 2,000+ system integrators across 500+ cities, 48 branch offices, 13 RMA centres and 141 exclusive Galaxy stores for touch-and-feel.
scores.quote: the largest distribution network, comprising over 1,000 plus distributors and 2,000 plus system integrators across more than 500 cities

scores.rationale: The benefit set is well matched by segment — brand and Galaxy stores for the 10% retail/home base, certification, TCO and service reach for the 90% SMB/enterprise/government base — with multi-brand launches added to defend depth-distribution customers.
scores.quote: Our largest pie comes from the SMB space, which constitutes 60% of our revenue

scores.rationale: There is real and rising engineering depth across AI analytics, firmware, multi-SoC architectures and DSIR-certified labs, but the core silicon and sensors are sourced from Qualcomm, Ambarella, Realtek, Sony and SmartSens, so the edge is integration and certification rather than proprietary technology.
scores.quote: we have built strong partnerships with six leading non-Chinese SoC companies

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network was discussed across the four calls; the cloud/OnVigil platform is described as a product feature, not a network.

Distribution and service reach that no rival can match is the durable moat — 500+ cities, 48 branches, 13 RMA service centres and 141 exclusive stores — and it is precisely what let the company absorb the vacated Chinese share fastest.
scores.quote: we are right now the only player who has the solid readiness with respect to all facets of business, be it the market reach coverage

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-led and rising (₹580cr FY24 to ~₹1,000-1,100cr FY26 across Kothavadi foundry, Bhiwadi, Shoolagiri alloy wheels), and is order-backed, but incremental returns have lagged with consolidated ROCE sliding from 22% to 16% and new plants running at sub-50% utilisation.
scores.quote: in the last many years, we have never cut back on capex

scores.rationale: As a B2B component maker there is effectively no brand-building A&P; the only promotional activity cited across five years is trade-show participation, which is customer-acquisition rather than durable brand equity.
scores.quote: We have participated in the EUROGUSS exhibition just two weeks ago in Nuremberg

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but sustained expensed product development for off-highway and stationary engines converted into a firm $100mn stationary-engine order book targeted for FY29/30, showing development spend does yield sticky new business.
scores.quote: these products are a long gestation for development itself

scores.rationale: Mixed record: DR Axion is a strong, well-performing acquisition (₹1,246cr revenue, ₹196cr EBIT), but Sunbeam was a weak asset needing multi-year restructuring (customer exits, price resets, still single-digit margins) and the deals were large enough to leverage the balance sheet rather than being small bolt-ons.
scores.quote: We are just lacking behind on the margin-wise with a single, still at single-digit

scores.rationale: No buyback or coherent distribution policy is discussed anywhere; the company instead sought an enabling resolution to raise equity from the public to de-leverage after heavy capex and acquisitions.
scores.quote: we have decided to de-leverage by reducing the amount of debt. So, we are raising funds via the public

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-heavy — foundries, die-casting and machining lines with very high depreciation and debt/EBITDA of 2.55 — so despite management framing replacement cost as a barrier, asset turn is low rather than asset-light.
scores.quote: The capex cost for anybody entering this business is very, very, very large

scores.rationale: Clear runway without dominance: #2 in static racking and top-two in automated storage, plus share capture from OEMs outsourcing in-house machining and from consolidating supplier bases in aluminium.
scores.quote: we are the second largest player in the country as far as the static racking

scores.rationale: Credible multi-year international build-out — Daimler Brazil cylinder blocks/heads, PV exports to Europe, Korea contracts, and the Fronberg Guss foundry in Germany — though execution has been uneven with exports repeatedly slipping and no premium brand travelling.
scores.quote: We are getting inquiries for 4-wheelers for export market. Both Europe and North America

scores.rationale: Headline revenue growth is largely volume plus commodity pass-through with no real price power, but management is deliberately driving mix — 95% machined content, exiting raw-casting and low-value customers, resetting legacy prices, higher-horsepower tractor parts.
scores.quote: It is a pass-through. So it will only optically increase the top line revenue

scores.rationale: Core CV market has been muted for roughly three years with tractors only now recovering and an identifiable upturn from higher-horsepower engine migration, placing the company nearer the bottom than the top of its cycle.
scores.quote: tractor is doing very well in this financial year and commercial vehicle is showing green shoots

scores.rationale: Genuine secular exposure via data-centre/AI-driven stationary engine castings ($100mn order book to FY29/30), windmill gearbox housings and China+1 localisation, though the largest segments remain cyclical auto.
scores.quote: the data center market or AI is booming all over the world

scores.rationale: Counter-cyclical investment discipline is real (never cut capex through the downturn), but stewardship is offset by three acquisitions and leverage that rose to 2.55x debt/EBITDA and forced an equity-raise resolution.
scores.quote: Debt to EBITDA on a consolidated level, we are at 2.55

scores.rationale: Promoter-led execution over long horizons is well evidenced: land bought in stages over years, stationary-engine capability seeded from 2021 and only invoicing from FY27-29, and the Kothavadi foundry built ahead of demand on customer commitments.
scores.quote: we had our investment done at starting from 2021 onwards itself in small steps

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key across 17 calls — no opening theatrics (straight to Q&A in recent years), refusal to name customers or tout order wins, and technical rather than promotional framing.
scores.quote: Pardon me, but I don't want to give exact customer wise sales

scores.rationale: The calls discuss manpower cost, automation-driven headcount reduction and team integration, but are genuinely silent on systematic talent development or a leadership pipeline.

Repeatedly owns shortfalls without spin — deferred maintenance during the post-COVID ramp, idle Stage-5 capacity from delayed regulation, capex overshooting guidance, Sunbeam still below target margins — and proactively warns that percentage margins mislead when aluminium prices move.
scores.quote: we didn't have some of the maintenance which we should have done

scores.rationale: The assessment holds up because management itself separates outcome from skill — attributing margin swings to commodity pass-through, inventory corrections and operating leverage rather than claiming credit — so results are not being flattered by a halo.
scores.quote: the scale has still not built up in the powertrain as we expected

scores.rationale: Niche near-monopoly positions in heavy 1-20 tonne critical castings and large-engine parts where domestic alternatives barely exist and the global end-customer set is tiny.
scores.quote: these products are not available for sourcing within India except one or two foundries

scores.rationale: Meaningful switching costs from multi-phase supplier validation, long development gestation and plants sited beside customers, which management describes as making the businesses sticky.
scores.quote: there is many -- a lot of validation required to onboard a supplier

scores.rationale: Storage solutions is a rational consolidating top-three oligopoly, but the far larger auto segments sell to powerful OEMs who dictate legacy pricing and pass-through terms, so the end customer retains negotiating power.
scores.quote: there's no need to undercut each other on this matter

scores.rationale: Replacement capex, imported machinery costs and rupee depreciation create a hard entry barrier, pricing behaviour in storage is rational with no discount war, and promoter ownership has been stable throughout.
scores.quote: The capex cost for anybody entering this business is very, very, very large

scores.rationale: Weak players are visibly ceding ground — storage competitors relegated to regional status, constrained European foundry capacity, and OEMs releasing in-house machining work to outsourced suppliers.
scores.quote: They have become regional players

scores.rationale: The most attractive niches — heavy multi-tonne castings and large stationary engine parts — are unglamorous, capital-hungry corners that few competitors or capital providers pursue.
scores.quote: hardly less than 10 companies all over the world

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; material cost is fully transparent to customers and passed through, leaving only the engineering value-add spread and no premium gross margin.
scores.quote: Aluminium is a calculated material cost, and that is it. And that is anybody can calculate it

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — critical machining tolerances, multi-phase qualification for engine parts, and reliability requirements that management says let it price new products properly.
scores.quote: new products call for also high reliability from the suppliers and high capability from the suppliers

scores.rationale: Deliberate proximity strategy with multiple plants sited near customer clusters nationally (Coimbatore, Bhiwadi, Faridabad, Shoolagiri, Gujarat, Ludhiana) plus in-house design, erection and service teams for storage.
scores.quote: we have seven, eight plants located across the country closer to the customer

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to a corporate customer base — reliability, TCO and validation-based lock-in with global OEMs rather than any consumer-intangible play.
scores.quote: These are very sticky businesses and these are all major companies, global companies

scores.rationale: Real process capability in critical machining, in-house special-purpose machine building and automation, but this is manufacturing know-how rather than a deep, high-R&D-intensity multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: we are using a mixture of our own equipment manufacturing for the special purpose machines

scores.rationale: The business model described across all calls is bilateral component supply to OEMs with no two-sided platform dynamic that strengthens with scale.

A hard-to-replicate footprint of plants near customers plus end-to-end design, erection and service capability in storage, extended internationally via Germany and Korea, though not decisively beyond rivals' reach.
scores.quote: this is marketing, the service and also erection, end-to-end design team

scores.rationale: Asset-light AMC reinvesting in branches (23→29), digital platforms, dedicated SIP sales teams across five locations and investment/research capability, i.e. genuine growth spend rather than maintenance, though magnitude is small and incremental returns are not yet visible in AUM.
scores.quote: we've grown our branch es to 29 branches from 23 of last year

scores.rationale: A&P appears only as episodic NFO-linked marketing flagged as a one-time cost spike, with no evidence of durable brand-equity building beyond inherited Canara Bank recall in the South.
scores.quote: we have a NFO in the last quarter... some of the expenses, advertisement and marketing expenses related to that NFO

scores.rationale: Only generic mention of investing in the investment team and research capability, with no demonstrated product/customer output from it — the MD himself says products are regulator-standardised and copyable.
scores.quote: investments in the investment team and research capability

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed or contemplated across any of the calls; nothing to judge.
No dividend, buyback or capital-return policy is discussed in any excerpt.

Genuinely capital-light with strong operating leverage (a fund manager runs Rs.1,000cr or Rs.10,000cr at the same cost, cost-to-income 38-42%), but the management itself concedes the business is commoditised so the moat protecting that turn is weak.
scores.quote: my fund manager can manage a Rs.1,000 crores or Rs.10,000 crores. It is the same cost structure

scores.rationale: Runway exists (~Rs.1.2 lakh cr vs Rs.82 lakh cr industry) but the trajectory is share loss, not capture: FY26 closing AUM +3.2% and Q1FY27 QAAUM +7% against industry growth of 21% and 10.5%, with management admitting share was merely maintained.
scores.quote: I think we have maintained more or less the same share as such.

scores.rationale: Credible domestic penetration — branches to 29, 56,890 empanelled partners, B-30 monthly AAUM up from Rs.261cr to Rs.288cr and B-30 now ~24% of AUM — but it is India-only with no premium brand travelling abroad and NRI/offshore ideas were deflected.
scores.quote: Approximately 24% of our AUM is from B30 locations

scores.rationale: Q1FY27 revenue grew 20% on just 7% QAAUM growth, so growth was led by yield/mix (equity yield 35.5→39-40bps) plus cost efficiency, though management attributes the yield lift to TER slab mechanics from a market fall rather than genuine pricing power.
scores.quote: the rest at the moment, as you can see, is improvement in yields... and cost efficiencies

scores.rationale: The equity-heavy book was hit by a ~15% Nifty correction in Q4FY26 and has begun recovering (+7% in Q1FY27), and the deliberately 91% equity mix is designed to outperform on the upturn.
scores.quote: periods where markets do well, we will do very well as compared to the industry

scores.rationale: The Indian MF end-market is in clear secular expansion — industry QAAUM +21% YoY to Rs.81.5 lakh cr, record monthly SIP flows above Rs.32,000 cr, SIP AUM Rs.50.1 lakh cr and rising B-30 penetration.
scores.quote: the industry continu es to exhibit strong structural flows, continued retail participation

scores.rationale: Consistently organic and unlevered: repeatedly declined to chase AIF/PMS/ETF/commodity/SIF diversification, no M&A, treasury mandated into liquid/overnight funds, and it kept adding branches and SIP sales teams through the FY26 drawdown.
scores.quote: We do not want to diversify in a big way and very quickly , because there are risks to be managed

scores.rationale: Strategy has been stated identically across all four calls and defended against peer pressure and analyst prodding, with an explicit long-horizon rationale, though the listed track record is only ~1 year and results have yet to validate it.
scores.quote: I also believe the re is no first -mover advantage in this industry

scores.rationale: Low-key, substance-over-celebrity tone throughout — plain operating detail, no self-promotion, and the MD routinely hands questions to Purohit, Turakhiya and Goyal rather than centring himself.
scores.quote: I don't have that number offhand with me, so I don't want to take a random guess on it

scores.rationale: Some pipeline signals — a 2% ESOP pool, growing headcount and Gaurav Goyal's internal elevation from Head of Sales to Chief Business Officer — but no systematic talent-development programme is described and the second ESOP round remains unlaunched.
scores.quote: the board of directors has approved an ESOP scheme f or staff. It is 2% that has been set aside

scores.rationale: Openly discusses uncomfortable facts — falling SIP accounts, ELSS tax-driven pressure, underperformance in down markets, and even admits not knowing why its own yields rose — while asking for patience rather than over-promising, but withholds flow data and dodged the quartile-performance question.
scores.quote: you're right that this quarter we saw an increase, while we are also still investigating the reasons for it

scores.rationale: The headline results flatter the skill: FY26 PAT grew only 7% and Q1FY27's 24% PAT growth rests on TER-slab-driven yield expansion and cost control while AUM badly trailed the industry, so profits reflect market beta and pricing mechanics more than franchise strength.
scores.quote: quarterly AUM growth has only grown by 7%, but operating revenue has grown by 20%

scores.rationale: Management explicitly denies any monopoly-like mindshare — regulator-mandated identical product categories across 52 AMCs, with only 'trust' offered as a differentiator.
scores.quote: ours is a commoditized business in more ways than one

scores.rationale: Switching costs are minimal (daily NAV transparency, free redemption) and the only regional edge is inherited brand recall in the South that management is actively trying to dilute into a pan-India identity.
scores.quote: we do have a higher brand recall in the South, and that's because of one of the shareholders

scores.rationale: A fragmented 52-player market where CRAMC holds ~1.5% share, and negotiating power sits with large distributors who can force yields down by ~2bps for a block of business.
scores.quote: there are around 52 AMC , so what exactly we are doing

scores.rationale: SEBI licensing and regulated telescopic TER slabs impose uniform pricing discipline across all AMCs (limiting discount wars), but entry is clearly open with 52 players and commission economics still get bid at the distributor level.
scores.quote: the te lescopic structure app lies to all AMCs in the industry

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified as donating share; on the contrary CRAMC is the one growing below industry and describes flows as concentrating into small/mid-cap and arbitrage categories where it is under-represented.
scores.quote: largely the industry growth has been very concentrated

scores.rationale: Modest scale and an unglamorous focused niche, but it listed in October 2025 and is now covered by Motilal Oswal, HDFC Securities, JM Financial, Equirus and others — the obscurity is gone.
scores.quote: it is our first analyst call post our listing on the 16 th of October

scores.rationale: Trust and a quality-stock investment image are claimed and equity yields have improved to 39-40bps, but yields still sit below larger AMCs and management explicitly deprioritises yield to win distributor blocks — limited real pricing power.
scores.quote: equity yields are slightly higher for the other AMCs

scores.rationale: The whole proposition is reliability rather than price — three-decade legacy, PSU bank plus Robeco parentage, and a stated quality-portfolio construct investors are asked to trust through cycles.
scores.quote: your true differentiator w ill be the trust you're able to build with your investors

scores.rationale: Reach is broad and deepening — 56,890 empanelled partners, 29 branches, digital platforms and newly dedicated SIP sales teams across five locations — though the distribution is third-party rather than owned.
scores.quote: we are planning to do is actually set up sales teams dedicated to SIPs. So , we are doing that across five locations

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to customer type: 86% individual retail base served with trust/performance intangibles and sticky SIPs (Rs.41,000 cr SIP AUM, ~one-third of assets), with only 14% institutional exposure.
scores.quote: Individual investors contributed 86% of our AUM

scores.rationale: Digital platform and regulatory-tech investments are recurring but described only as efficiency and compliance spend, with no multi-product technology edge or differentiated customer benefit claimed.
scores.quote: there are some , which are related to technology investments that w e've made to support the regulatory environment

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing network exists — distributors serve all AMCs on identical terms, so scale in the panel confers no compounding advantage to CRAMC.
scores.quote: their pricing is the same irrespective of which AMC they wo rk for

scores.rationale: Management concedes the manufacturer owns no distribution and depends on a shared partner fraternity that prices identically across AMCs, so reach is rentable rather than proprietary — and the falling SIP account book shows rivals can match it.
scores.quote: the manufacturer do es not have its own distribution

scores.rationale: Consistent growth-oriented branch and headcount build-out (1,681 branches in Jun-2022 to 2,276 by Jun-2026, 183 opened in FY26 alone) funded largely by internal accruals with high cross-cycle returns, though it is distribution build rather than high-ROIC fixed capex.
scores.quote: We opened 183 branches to close with 2,236 branches by March 2026

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.

Technology investment (business rule engine, Grameen Mahi app, AI in credit decisioning) has demonstrably produced new products and customers — retail finance from 5.9% to 20.6% of AUM and 15.4 Lakh app users — though this is IT spend rather than classical R&D.
scores.quote: Our customer app, Grameen Mahi, onboarded 8.4 Lakh borrowers in FY26

scores.rationale: The Madura Microfinance bolt-on was small and complementary and was integrated onto the CA Grameen platform, but the acquiree was weaker on asset quality (91-93% collection efficiency vs 97%) so the deal diluted rather than improved operating quality initially.
scores.quote: at MMFL, collection efficiency excluding arrears improved from 91% in Q4 to 93%

scores.rationale: Capital is fully retained to fund growth (86% of net-worth build from internal accruals) — a coherent stance for a compounding lender, but no buyback or dividend policy is articulated anywhere.
scores.quote: compounding at 20% CAGR, of which 86% increase came just through internal accruals

scores.rationale: As a balance-sheet lender the model is inherently asset-heavy (AUM INR 30,319 Crore on INR 8,347 Crore net worth, 3.0x debt/equity), the opposite of the asset-light profile this parameter rewards, even though yields and ROA are strong.
scores.quote: debt equity ratio at a conservative 3.0x

scores.rationale: Long runway with sustained share capture — 28.6% AUM CAGR over FY17-26 and 9.8 Lakh borrowers added in FY26 — in a fragmented market where it is a leader but far from dominant.
scores.quote: FY17 to FY26, we have compounded AUM at 28.6% per annum

scores.rationale: Credible, sustained district expansion from the Karnataka core (388 districts in Jun-2024 to 457 in Jun-2026, majority of new borrowers outside top-3 states), though execution outside core markets showed materially higher delinquency.
scores.quote: 56% of our new borrower addition on a consolidated basis came outside of the top 3 states

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/borrower-led while pricing is deliberately the lowest in the industry and actively being cut, with mix shift to retail finance offering similar or lower yields.
scores.quote: probably can look at a 50 bps price cut if we are able to hold the asset quality

scores.rationale: The company is clearly emerging from the trough of the MFI credit cycle with an identifiable upturn — credit cost falling from 6.74% to a guided 3-4%, PAT up 720% YoY and management describing a structurally strong up-cycle ahead.
scores.quote: Q4 FY26 marks a decisive inflection in our performance trajectory

scores.rationale: Rural/semi-urban micro-retail credit is structurally under-penetrated and growing double-digit, but the repeated disruptions (demonetization, COVID, MFI cycle) show the end market expands cyclically rather than smoothly.
scores.quote: the vast and underpenetrated opportunity of serving the 23.5 Crore low-to-middle income households by 2030

scores.rationale: Organic focus since the Madura bolt-on, conservative 3.0x leverage and 24.9% CRAR, growth funded from accruals, and counter-cyclical sequencing of collections before growth through the downturn.
scores.quote: We prioritized collections first, then portfolio maintenance and only then growth

scores.rationale: Ten-year compounding through three external shocks and a persistent multi-year lifecycle-finance strategy demonstrate tenacity, tempered by heavy chairman/MD churn across FY21-FY26.
scores.quote: Through 3 major external disruptions... the cross-cycle ROA stands at 3.4% and ROE at 13.9%

scores.rationale: Calls are dense, metric-driven and free of personality promotion, with the MD crediting field staff and lenders rather than himself.
scores.quote: A special note of gratitude to our employees, particularly our field teams

scores.rationale: Clear internal pipeline (Ganesh Narayanan CEO to MD, Nilesh Dalvi IR head to CFO) plus systematic training and sharply moderating attrition from 33.5% to 20.6%.
scores.quote: employee attrition continued to moderate meaningfully, standing at 20.6% as of Q1 FY27 against 25.8%

scores.rationale: Management explicitly owned the FY26 guidance miss (6.74% credit cost vs 5.5-6.0% guided) and named the difficulty, though in Jul-2024 it repeatedly framed building stress as 'transitory' and reiterated guidance that later broke.
scores.quote: our credit cost ended at 6.74% as against the guidance of 5.5% to 6.0%

scores.rationale: The assessment survives halo scrutiny because the FY25-26 downturn separated skill from luck — reported ROE fell to 10.7% yet the recovery playbook and cross-cycle ratios beat the COVID cycle, showing capability not just favourable conditions.
scores.quote: our return ratio through this MFI credit cycle were meaningfully higher than what we delivered through the COVID crisis

scores.rationale: Deep community trust and 6-8 year customer vintages give a privileged position in the borrower's mind, but microfinance customers routinely borrow from multiple lenders so there is no monopoly-like hold.
scores.quote: our Unnati loan customers carry an average vintage of 7.7 years

scores.rationale: Some lock-in via graduation of vintage customers into retail products (Unnati 100% internally sourced), offset by low switching costs — only ~46% of group-loan AUM is unique borrowers.
scores.quote: AUM share of unique group loan borrowers stands at 46.1%

scores.rationale: Microfinance is a fragmented, RBI-regulated market with banks, SFBs and many NBFC-MFIs competing for the same borrower, evidenced by borrowers historically carrying more than three lenders.
scores.quote: AUM share of GL borrowers with greater than three lenders has declined from 25.3% in August 2024

scores.rationale: Industry-body guardrails and RBI norms now impose lending discipline, but the very need for them confirms the prior cycle's irrational over-lending, so rationality is regulator-imposed rather than structural.
scores.quote: guidelines implemented by the industry body, MFIN... imposing a cap on microfinance limit to INR 2 Lakh, number of lenders to 4

scores.rationale: The credit cycle weakened smaller MFI competitors while CAGL kept the lowest cost of borrowing and strongest capital, positioning it to absorb share as the industry rationalises.
scores.quote: the industry has rationalized to a good extent

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar — calls are hosted by ICICI Securities and covered by CLSA, HSBC, Citi, Motilal Oswal, YES and Equirus, with explicit guidance sought every quarter.
scores.quote: MODERATOR: MR. CHINTAN SHAH – ICICI SECURITIES

scores.rationale: No image-driven pricing power: the company deliberately runs the lowest yield in the industry and passes rating and funding gains back to borrowers rather than capturing them.
scores.quote: Our portfolio yield at 21% continues to remain the lowest in the microfinance industry

scores.rationale: Borrowers buy reliable, responsibly-priced access and a Gold Standard client-protection record, with brand trust explicitly cited as the basis for graduating customers into new products.
scores.quote: leveraging the trust our brand has built on the ground

scores.rationale: Doorstep centre-meeting model backed by 2,276 branches, ~22,000 field staff and a vernacular app gives accessibility and customer intimacy rivals struggle to match.
scores.quote: vast distribution reach, dedicated foot on the street, localized intelligence, strong customer references

scores.rationale: Retail rural households are served with the right benefit set — convenience, trust and relationship depth — and lock-in is built through vintage-based graduation rather than intangibles.
scores.quote: We are building the capability to be the financial life cycle partner of the entire household

scores.rationale: A genuine operating tech stack (business rule engine for district- and cohort-level credit policy, 30 Lakh transactions/day, AI in credit decisioning) supports multiple products, but it is an efficiency edge rather than a defensible multi-product technology moat.
scores.quote: with the BRE in place now, we are able to control our credit policy at product level, at customer level and at geography level

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists; the JLG group model provides peer discipline but collections and sourcing scale linearly with branches and staff, not self-reinforcingly.
scores.quote: more than 99% of regular collections still happening there

scores.rationale: Distribution is the core moat — 2,276 branches across 457 districts with deep rural penetration and relationship-based servicing that competitors cannot replicate quickly in the same geographies.
scores.quote: we opened 42 new branches during the quarter, taking our total network to 2,276 branches... spread across 457 districts

scores.rationale: Capex is intangible-heavy (digital infrastructure, cloud, information security, Gen-AI, talent) and is described as sustained and growth-oriented across all four calls, with FY26 margins expanding to 22.7% from 18.3% suggesting good incremental returns, but no quantified growth-capex disclosure.
scores.quote: We continue to make significant investments in digital infrastructure, information security, and building a future-ready talent pool.

scores.rationale: Brand spend is real and durable — a full rebrand in Jan 2025, franchise events (India Outlook Conclave, Infrastructure Conclave), and leading media share of voice among CRAs — but it is thought-leadership marketing rather than measurable brand-equity capex.
scores.quote: we rolled out a new brand identity, positioning our businesses under a cohesive brand identity

scores.rationale: R&D consistently converts into launched, revenue-bearing products across the period — Q Square, Phoenix, Fulcrum, Quantix in 2023 to GenEye Credit, DeepMind, i360, ICON and Myron AI by 2026 — though R&D spend and its efficiency are never quantified.
scores.quote: In 2025, we launched several pioneering Gen-AI products.

scores.rationale: Both deals in the window are small, complementary bolt-ons in adjacent niches (Peter Lee Associates in Australia for benchmarking, PriceMetrix in Toronto for wealth management), and the acquiring segment's margin rose to 22.7% from 18.3% post-deal.
scores.quote: completed the acquisition of PriceMetrix to deepen our presence in the wealth management space

scores.rationale: A coherent, steadily rising interim dividend policy (INR7 to INR8 to INR9 across the years) is evident, but there is no buyback and no discussion of distributing at low valuations.
scores.quote: the Board declared an interim dividend of INR9 per share in quarter 1 FY26 compared to INR8 per share in the same quarter last year

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-light — its stated main asset is people and IP, not plant — combined with a protective ratings franchise, though asset turnover itself is never discussed.
scores.quote: Ours is a people business. Our main IP is people.

scores.rationale: Wallet-share gains are evidenced with global CIBs, asset managers and rising S&P delegation to GAC (segment +32.5% in Q1 2025, +20.2% in Q1 2026), but CRISIL is already the domestic ratings leader, limiting runway on its core.
scores.quote: Our wallet share has grown across key clients in global CIBs and asset managers

scores.rationale: Well-executed and widening footprint over the period — from 12 countries of operation in 2023 to 11,400+ clients in 40 countries by 2026, adding Canada via PriceMetrix, West Asia client growth and regional banks across Europe/Middle East/Asia.
scores.quote: looking at the geographic expansion, we've added a new geography, Canada, followed by our acquisition of PriceMetrix

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly attributes profit growth to product mix and margin discipline rather than pure volume, though the top line is still driven mostly by new mandates, acquisitions and delegated volumes.
scores.quote: growing approximately 16% on year, on the back of changing product mix and continued focus on margins

scores.rationale: The bond-issuance cycle is depressed rather than clearly bottoming — flat in CY2025 and down 12% in Q1 2026 on hardened yields and West Asia conflict — while bank credit is already recovering, so no identifiable near-term upturn is established.
scores.quote: In Q1 2026, the bond issuances declined by 12% on Y-o-Y basis.

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion across all four calls — financialization of savings with mutual fund AUM rising from INR55 lakh crore to INR83 lakh crore, bond-market deepening, private markets, sustainability and Gen-AI-driven analytics demand.
scores.quote: The industry AUM increased from INR55 lakh crores in Q1 2024 to about INR83 lakh crores in Q4 2026

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly organic with only tiny bolt-ons, no leverage discussed, and management kept investing in Gen-AI and talent through the weak 2024 discretionary-spend downturn while holding margins.
scores.quote: disciplined cost management alongside continuing to invest in our growth agenda

scores.rationale: Multi-year ambitions stated at the AGM were subsequently delivered (GAC scaling with S&P), showing tenacity, but a large and growing share of growth depends on parent S&P Global, which limits true independence.
scores.quote: we had at the last AGM mentioned about the potential to grow business with S&P Global

scores.rationale: Communication is substance-heavy and deliberately unpromotional — the company explicitly refuses quantitative guidance and calls are handed to business heads rather than a celebrity CEO — though the CRISIL brand itself courts visibility via awards and media share of voice.
scores.quote: As a policy, company refrains from giving specific quantitative guidance on its future performance.

scores.rationale: Systematic talent development is a consistent theme with an internal leadership pipeline visibly working (Chhatwal from Ratings MD to COO, Rai succeeding at Ratings, Arora moving from CSO to business head) plus layered AI upskilling for the whole workforce.
scores.quote: We have been investing heavily in AI literacy through a layered training approach

scores.rationale: Management proactively strips out flattering one-offs — FX swings, the INR29.4 crore Argentine Peso gain, and the USD4.5 million pull-forward it says will normalize — and openly explained the muted 2024, though it rarely owns strategic mistakes.
scores.quote: this is largely a timing effect, and we expect this to normalize over the course of the rest of the year

scores.rationale: Headline Q1 FY26 growth (revenue +30.1%, PAT +45.9%) is materially flattered by an FX swing, the PriceMetrix consolidation and pulled-forward renewals, so reported results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: Quarter 1 FY26 includes a foreign exchange gain of INR14.4 crores compared to a loss of INR5.2 crores

scores.rationale: CRISIL holds a mind-share monopoly in Indian corporate ratings, cited in every call as the reason for winning new business, backed by the lowest and most stable default rates versus peers and an annuity-like surveillance aftermarket.
scores.quote: The growth in new rating revenues is aided by continued investor preference for Crisil Ratings.

scores.rationale: Switching costs are visible through recurring surveillance fees, strong research renewal rates and multi-year benchmarking contracts, but there is no true regional monopoly and issuers can and do switch agencies.
scores.quote: having secured more multi-year contracts through 2025

scores.rationale: The Indian credit-rating industry is a SEBI-registered, stable few-player oligopoly explicitly compared agency-by-agency in the disclosures, and Coalition Greenwich occupies a near-unique global benchmarking niche.
scores.quote: This slide shows the one-year investment grade default rate averaged over the last 10 years for CRISIL Ratings, as well as some of the other credit rating agencies.

scores.rationale: Regulatory registration and a decade-long default-rate track record are high entry barriers with no new entrants mentioned across four years, but the real competitive pressure comes from banks pricing loans against bonds rather than rational intra-industry pricing.
scores.quote: banks offered lucrative rates to large corporates, leading to a substitution of corporate bonds with bank loans

scores.rationale: Weaker rating agencies with worse default and stability records are implicitly identified as the pool from which CRISIL takes share, and its new-rating wins are attributed to investor preference over them.
scores.quote: We have consistently displayed one of the best default rates and stability rates in the domestic credit rating agency space.

scores.rationale: CRISIL is the opposite of under-the-radar — it actively cultivates visibility through iconic-brand awards, conclaves, 26 industry recognitions and leading media share of voice.
scores.quote: we have been recognized as an iconic brand at the fifth edition of the Times Iconic Brand Conclave 2022

scores.rationale: Pricing power rests on reputational standing rather than taste or image, and margins are healthy (segment margin 22.7%), but the customers are institutions and the intangible is credibility, not consumer brand affinity.
scores.quote: maintained its leadership in corporate bond ratings, given investor preference for best-in-class ratings

scores.rationale: The core proposition across all four calls is certainty and credibility, with demand explicitly counter-cyclical to uncertainty and reliability, not price, framed as the buying criterion.
scores.quote: uncertain environments typically increase demand for credible risk opinions and insights

scores.rationale: There is genuine customer intimacy and reach — 11,400+ clients in 40 countries with repeated client-engagement initiatives and offshore delivery convenience for mid-sized banks — but accessibility is not a primary differentiator.
scores.quote: We serve 11,400-plus clients in 40 countries globally

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/institutional and CRISIL matches it correctly with reliability and TCO-driven offshoring lock-in rather than retail intangibles, though switching-cost depth varies by business line.
scores.quote: increased traction in midsized banks for their offshoring solutions options to manage costs more effectively

scores.rationale: A structured four-lever Gen-AI strategy has produced multiple proprietary products validated by 26 external AI recognitions, but the durable edge is proprietary data and domain expertise with technology as an amplifier rather than a deep standalone moat.
scores.quote: We've had 26 independent AI-related recognitions, including 20 from Chartis Research.

scores.rationale: The Coalition Greenwich benchmarking franchise has a genuine data-pooling network property — more participating banks make the benchmarks more valuable — and ratings link issuers to investors, but no self-reinforcing scale dynamic is explicitly claimed.
scores.quote: combined data sets from Coalition and Greenwich

scores.rationale: The Global Analytical Center's delivery scale for S&P and a 5,000-strong multi-country analyst base give reach rivals would struggle to replicate, but management never positions distribution or service reach as the competitive advantage.
scores.quote: robust surveillance work delegation from S&P Global Rating Services

scores.rationale: Asset-light model requires almost no growth capex — management says new destinations need no incremental platform spend — so high ROIC is real but there is no rising growth-capex engine to fund.
scores.quote: In our existing tech platform, we have that capability to add any new institution without any additional cost.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

Tech investment is modest and late — AI barely deployed in Aug 2025 and the flagship EduMentor commitment is only USD 2.5mn spread over five years with benefits described as future, so no track record of R&D yielding products yet.
scores.quote: We haven't used too much of AI as of today... committed USD 2.5 million over five years roadmap to the EduMentor project

scores.rationale: Four small complementary bolt-ons in FY26 (StudiesPlanet LATAM, 51% of an established Global Tree at ~50% margins, EduMentor, Medway NZ team) with group EBITDA margin still expanding 172bps, though integration and returns are unproven and deal costs already inflated other expenses.
scores.quote: In January 2026, we acquired a 51% stake in Global Tree Careers Private Limited, a well-established B2C counseling and immigration service.

scores.rationale: Coherent and improving distribution — first special interim dividend in Q3 followed by Rs.8/share taking FY26 payout to ~64% versus a committed 40%, funded from net cash, though there are no buybacks.
scores.quote: the board declared a dividend of Rs. 8 per equity share in Q4 FY26, representing a dividend payout of approximately 64% which is higher than our committed 40%

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light commission model with ROCE 48.6% and ROE 37.2% on a debt-free balance sheet, but the protecting moat is only partial since universities work with multiple competing platforms.
scores.quote: ROE of 37.2% and ROCE of 48.6% for FY26, reflecting the asset-light nature of our operating model

scores.rationale: Sub-1% global share leaves a very long runway and share capture is visible in the numbers — applications +43% and active agents +36% in FY26, with no agent attrition claimed.
scores.quote: our market share, if you look at across the globe of the students we send to our partner universities, it's less than 1%

scores.rationale: Source-market diversification is executing well (85+ countries, India now below 50%, Ireland ~10% share), but destination expansion lags badly with UK still ~97% and Australia repeatedly promised and still not cracked across all four calls.
scores.quote: getting contracts from universities is our biggest challenge or the blocker... for us to get these contracts secured from Australia University is not that easy

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led rather than price/mix-led, and mix is turning adverse — applications grew 43% while enrolments grew only 14%, and new geographies are explicitly lower-margin at entry.
scores.quote: it will be lower at the initial period, but with scale of volume should become same as the existing one

scores.rationale: The cycle is policy-driven and two-sided rather than clearly near a bottom — US/Canada tightening redirects flow to Crizac's UK base while the Middle East pipeline is simultaneously damaged by conflict.
scores.quote: Because of the current war situation, Middle East pipeline seems a bit damaged

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion — 80 lakh global student mobility versus Crizac's tiny share, with the UK government targeting GBP40bn of education exports by 2030.
scores.quote: target to boost its international education exports to GBP40 billion sterling a year by 2030

scores.rationale: Leverage discipline is exemplary — debt-free, self-funded for 15 years, Rs.467cr net cash — but the organic-focus criterion is contradicted by four acquisitions in one year and a deliberately 'highly active' inorganic pipeline.
scores.quote: Crizac is still entirely debt-free and fully self-funded. Every ounce of growth that we've achieved over 15 years has come from internal cash generation.

scores.rationale: Founder-led since 2011, funded entirely from internal accruals, and tenacious in pursuing hard destination contracts (Ireland cracked to ~10% share, New Zealand operationalized), though execution timelines slip.
scores.quote: Ireland, we have already cracked and we are doing a good number for Ireland with a market share of almost closer to 10%

scores.rationale: Promoter family is low-profile and Kolkata-based, but post-IPO commentary has become notably promotional with self-declared moats and network effects rather than plain substance.
scores.quote: These are classic platform network effects, and they create increasing stickiness and switching costs on both sides of the marketplace

scores.rationale: Some capability-building via lift-outs and named hires (Medway team, EduMentor's leader, an IR advisor) on a 350-person base, but no evidence of systematic talent development or an internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we operationalized our new New Zealand business at scale through onboarding of the entire Medway Educational Consultant Team

scores.rationale: Repeatedly withholds core operating metrics as 'sensitive data' and over-promised on growth — 30%+ was guided in Aug 2025 and reiterated, while FY26 revenue grew 22.7%, with a Rs.55cr termination fee disclosed without explanation.
scores.quote: We normally don't prefer giving a realisation per student, because it's a sensitive data, which might affect the business continuity.

scores.rationale: Headline ROCE and growth are hard to separate from an exogenous tailwind — US/Canada visa tightening redirecting students to Crizac's ~97% UK destination base, with top-10 universities at 66% of revenue.
scores.quote: Our top 10 university partners account for 66% of our revenue

scores.rationale: No monopoly position in the customer's mind — management concedes universities run multiple competing recruitment platforms alongside Crizac.
scores.quote: most of the universities work with multiple platforms like ours

scores.rationale: Some real stickiness — zero claimed agent attrition and 5+ year tenure with top-30 universities — but both agents and universities multi-home, so switching costs are soft rather than captive.
scores.quote: the traditional pool of old agents are with us. I don't think anybody has left us

scores.rationale: Market is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly (IDP, ApplyBoard, Krishna Consultants and thousands of agents), and the paying customer is concentrated with negotiating power — top 10 universities are 66% of revenue.
scores.quote: our peers would be ApplyBoard, Krishna Consultants

scores.rationale: Regulation is actively raising entry barriers — the UK Agent Quality Framework is described as burdensome enough that only mature platforms can comply at scale, entrenching incumbents.
scores.quote: It's quite a burdensome, heavy regulatory regime. And this means that only mature, sophisticated platforms are in a position to comply with it and operate at large scale.

scores.rationale: Weaker sub-scale agents and lighter-touch platforms that cannot bear compliance or on-ground presence are identified share donators, with wallet-share gain from other players cited as a growth source.
scores.quote: our agent network spanning more than 85 source countries with an on-ground presence in 11 of those gives us early cycle visibility... in a way that purely digital or lighter touch platforms cannot replicate

scores.rationale: The B2B education-agent niche is genuinely unglamorous, but Crizac is now listed, analyst-covered and openly touting its scale, so it is no longer under the radar of capital.
scores.quote: this was a validation of not just our business model but also everything that we've been building since our founding in 2011
