scores.quote: Now I'll talk about what did not go well in the quarter. The first quarter disbursement was quite low. April, in particular, was really bad.

scores.rationale: Leadership succession happened (Jagadesh replacing Rohit Phadke on assets, new treasury head, Balaji elevated to Executive Director) suggesting a bench, but no systematic talent-development programme is ever described.
scores.quote: MR. JAGADESH J. -- HEAD OF ASSETS – EQUITAS SMALL FINANCE BANK LIMITED

scores.rationale: Management routinely leads with what went wrong, refuses to guide when it cannot see clearly, and quantifies bad news precisely (slippages above comfort level, one-time PCR correction, labour-code hit).
scores.quote: Our slippages during the quarter were 4.49%, which is above the comfort level of 4%... on microfinance is something that we have to really wait and watch

scores.rationale: The FY26 recovery is materially attributable to industry-wide factors — MFIN guardrails and a falling rate cycle repricing deposits — as much as to management skill, so results should not be read as pure execution alpha.
scores.quote: combined with improved lending discipline in the industry and the strict implementation of MFIN guardrails by all the players have resulted in significant improvement

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold in the customer's mind; the bank explicitly wins deposits on rate and admits it is only now trying to shift to a value proposition.
scores.quote: we want to move from only rate-conscious approach to value proposition

scores.rationale: No captive aftermarket or switching-cost lock-in — borrowers and depositors are rate-mobile, and the bank must migrate customers with pricing incentives (444-day to 888-day products).
scores.quote: shifting the consumer from 444 to 888. Last quarter, we did close to 110,000 customers

scores.rationale: Small finance banking is fragmented and contested by banks, NBFCs and MFIs, with end customers holding real negotiating power on deposit rates — the bank had to raise TD and SA rates in March '26.
scores.quote: we have increased our interest rate on TD and SA during March '26, and this is expected to increase the cost of funds going forward

scores.rationale: RBI licensing is a genuine entry barrier and MFIN guardrails restored lending rationality, but deposit pricing remains competitive and the bank is a rate-taker on both sides.
scores.quote: strict implementation of MFIN guardrails by all the players have resulted in significant improvement in performance of this book

scores.rationale: Post-MFI-crisis weak lenders have retreated, leaving room for a capitalised player to take secured-lending share — evidenced by record secured disbursements up 49% YoY.
scores.quote: our secured book, we also delivered our highest ever quarterly disbursements of INR5,835 crores, up 49 percentage year-on-year

scores.rationale: The informal-segment niche is genuinely unglamorous, but the bank is listed, widely covered by analysts on every call and openly targeting a universal bank licence.
scores.quote: the new guidelines that RBI has come out with in the month of April for SFBs to convert into universal banks

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; the stated deposit proposition is to pay above-market rates, and lending yields are set by segment risk not brand.
scores.quote: building a retail bank that offers relatively attractive rates of interest to depositors

scores.rationale: Deposit gathering has been rate-led rather than trust-led — deposit growth fell to 7-8% precisely when rates were tweaked down, showing price, not certainty, drives the customer.
scores.quote: Last quarter, we did rate tweaking strategically... we ended up with just 7% growth in deposit in Q3

scores.rationale: Genuine accessibility and customer intimacy through branch banking, a dedicated RM structure, doorstep informal-segment lending and adopted digital apps (Selfie loan app, 6 lakh mobile downloads).
scores.quote: Our Selfie Loan app for borrowers is seeing strong adoption with about 1.5 lakh downloads in the last quarter

scores.rationale: Benefit types are deliberately matched to customer tiers — segmented retail propositions (ARTHA/Elite Lite/Elite, family banking) on liabilities and cash-flow-based informal lending on assets.
scores.quote: we have 3 different categories within the HNI, one for Mass Affluent, one for Affluent and third for HNI, which we call it as ARTHA, Elite Lite and Elite

scores.rationale: Technology is bought-in and catch-up in nature (Microsoft Dynamics CRM, new LOS, standard apps) rather than a proprietary multi-product edge, and it has weighed on cost-to-income without a visible customer-benefit moat.
scores.quote: our new CRM app being built on the Microsoft Dynamics platform

scores.rationale: No two-sided network is described anywhere; growth comes from branch/RM-driven customer acquisition and cross-sell, which does not strengthen with scale in a self-reinforcing way.
Distribution is decent and multi-channel (branches, RMs, business correspondents, digital, sound box/QR/POS for current accounts) but is a work-in-progress rather than reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: we have now got our sound box, our POS and QR ready operational in the market... And current account last quarter showed a reasonable growth, but to sustain that, we need this proposition

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-oriented (Bhopal insulin fill-finish, GLP-1/Semaglutide, third injectable unit) at ~INR 200-300 cr/yr within a front-loaded INR 750 cr 3-year plan, but returns have been delayed by regulatory slippage that cost ~INR 50 cr of insulin sales two years running.
scores.quote: CapEx for the financial year came close to INR 300 crores, largely on Biologics and Sterile Injectables

scores.rationale: Promotion is field-force-and-launch-expense driven (Semaglutide prelaunch spend, new cosmetology division) rather than a discussed brand-equity A&P program, so there is spend but no evidence of durable brand-building returns from A&P per se.
scores.quote: Q4 DBF EBITDA was at INR 246 crores... slightly depressed because of the Semaglutide prelaunch expenses

scores.rationale: In-house R&D has repeatedly produced approvals and launches (Dapagliflozin combinations, first-in-India Esaxerenone developed and trialled by their own team, Semaglutide internalisation, Aspart/Degludec pipeline), though several FY26 launches slipped on regulatory delays.
scores.quote: This has been successfully formulated by our own R&D team... We were the first company to develop this in India

scores.rationale: Deals are complementary and post-deal OPM improvement is exceptional (Oaknet 10%→36-38%, Biocon-1 19%→39% in 2-3 quarters), but they are large and debt-funded and the stated thesis is buying sub-optimally run assets rather than already-strong ones.
scores.quote: The Q1 EBITDA margin for this piece was at 39% versus 19% at the time of acquisition

scores.rationale: No buyback and no articulated distribution policy across the period; dividend questions were deflected and all capital is directed to debt reduction and capex.
scores.quote: Right now, we would like to focus more about Dermatology and Oaknet.

scores.rationale: The core branded model is high-gross-margin and was historically asset-light, but the balance sheet has become materially heavier — INR 2,255 cr net debt, large acquired intangibles, rising manufacturing capex and receivables jumping from INR 458 cr to INR 680 cr with OCF/EBITDA halving to 50%.
scores.quote: OCF to EBITDA ratio came in at close to 50% for the financial year versus 105% for the last financial year

scores.rationale: Consistent, quantified share capture across years — IPM rank 29 to top 20, RHI cartridge share 8%→26%, RHI+Glargine 9%→16%, Derma to #3, and #1 by volume in injectable Semaglutide in the first full month.
scores.quote: we have tripled its market share in less than 2 years since, which is the highest ever gain seen in the Insulin segment by any player

scores.rationale: Credible international build-out via Swiss Parenterals with a >INR 1,000 cr EU CDMO order book and a 2029-30 INR 1,000 cr aspiration, but FY26 execution missed (INR 348 cr vs INR 375 cr guided) and an EU GMP inspection returned non-compliance observations.
scores.quote: we have a list of noncompliance observations, which we need to remediate

scores.rationale: Growth is led by volume and share capture rather than price/mix — mix has shifted toward lower-margin insulins/injectables (consolidated GM fell ~800 bps), and Semaglutide was deliberately launched below competitor pricing.
scores.quote: Our products are priced lower than competition.

scores.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of cyclical positioning or an identifiable cycle upturn for the business.

End markets are secularly expanding — 85%+ chronic/sub-chronic mix, super-specialty segments growing 10%+ in volume, plus the structurally new GLP-1/diabesity market layered on India's diabetes and CVD burden.
scores.quote: despite nearly doubling in size, this is still predominantly a Chronic / Sub-chronic business for more than 85% of the turnover

scores.rationale: Stewardship has been acquisition-led and leverage-heavy rather than organic and prudent — net debt peaked above INR 2,700 cr, breaching their own stated 2x internal ceiling, with deleveraging still incomplete at 2x by FY26.
scores.quote: The banks require you to stick to 3 times. So, we will be comfortable holding the 2x mark.

scores.rationale: A multi-year, independently pursued vision — building a biologics platform from insulin acquisition to in-house fill-finish to GLP-1 — has been pursued tenaciously and largely delivered on share gains, though timelines have repeatedly slipped.
scores.quote: this site is a key stepping stone to realize our Biotech vision

scores.rationale: Communication is operational and metric-driven with no promotional or celebrity framing; presentations lead with covered-market comparisons and misses rather than self-congratulation.
scores.quote: Looking back at the key hits and misses during the year

scores.rationale: Evidence of deliberate internal talent deployment and cultural retention — half the new cosmetology division staffed internally, acquired Biocon/Oaknet teams integrated and retained, and the flagship GLP launch staffed with long-tenured people for cultural alignment.
scores.quote: we wanted to take the people who have been with the company for a longer period of time... alignment with the company, with the product, with the culture takes time

scores.rationale: Management explicitly quantifies its own failures (INR 55-60 cr of abandoned/delayed launches, INR 50 cr insulin sales lost to Bhopal delay two years running, critical care not taking off) and openly concedes the OAD portfolio will lag the market for several more quarters.
scores.quote: Thirdly, our critical care business did not take off as expected.

scores.rationale: Genuine operating skill is visible in acquired-asset margin uplift and insulin share, but headline results are flattered by acquisitions, a one-off INR 150 cr deferred-tax gain and financial leverage, so results should not be read straight through to skill.
scores.quote: This is because of a one-off upside of INR 150 crores from a deferred tax adjustment.

scores.rationale: The company holds brand-level leadership positions in defined niches (five brands above INR 100 cr, six of nine acquired derma brands with top-3/top-5 ranks) which confer prescriber mindshare, but nothing approaching a true monopoly.
scores.quote: three of these brands are ranked among the top three in their respective segments

scores.rationale: Chronic prescription stickiness, cold-chain capability and a patient-care platform create real switching frictions in insulin/diabetes, though not a regional or captive-aftermarket monopoly.
scores.quote: our Patient Care platform, which is focused on developing and nurturing long-term relationships with patients

scores.rationale: Indian branded formulations is fragmented and contested — the company is only ~#20 with 6% share in its largest segment, and loss of exclusivity immediately invites multiple competitors as seen in Semaglutide.
scores.quote: Oral Anti-Diabetes market share inched towards 6%

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is not rational — genericisation destroyed the Zayo brand (INR 5 cr/month to INR 1.5 cr), regulatory FDC bans wiped out INR 30 cr brands, and the Semaglutide launch involved undercutting competitors on price.
scores.quote: reflection of Zayo now is more like Rs. 1.5 crores per month from a peak of Rs. 5 crores

scores.rationale: The strategy is explicitly built on weak donators — non-core brands divested by Dr. Reddy's, Glenmark and Biocon, plus innovator exits in RHI cartridges and an innovator-dominated INR 1,800 cr analogue market ripe for attack.
scores.quote: the presence of arbitrage opportunities by way of fundamentally good businesses which are sub-optimally run

scores.rationale: Certain niches it entered (RHI cartridges, EU CDMO injectables) were under-contested, but the company itself is now a top-20 listed player with heavy analyst coverage in the most crowded therapy areas in India.
scores.quote: Eris now ranks among the Top 20 companies in the market

scores.rationale: High and defended gross margins in the base branded business (86%, derma at 80%) evidence brand-derived pricing power, though mix into insulins and price-led Semaglutide entry dilutes this at the consolidated level.
scores.quote: The gross margin in Q1 was 86%, which is up by nearly 300 basis points on a year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: The insulin and GLP franchises sell reliability — cold chain competence, physician hand-holding and patient support are cited as the reason for share gains, but repeated supply failures (Zayo stockout, Bhopal delay) have undercut that assurance.
scores.quote: our long-standing experience of handling cold chain products

scores.rationale: A 3,700+ medical-representative field force plus a direct patient-services platform gives unusually intimate access to both prescriber and patient, and is credited with driving the difficult vial-first Semaglutide launch.
scores.quote: our DBF MR strength is close to 3,700-plus now

scores.rationale: The benefit set is correctly matched to a prescriber/retail-patient customer — brand image plus service intimacy rather than tender-driven TCO — although the newer hospital/injectable business has weaker economics and worse receivables.
scores.quote: now we have a lot of Injectables, Insulins, Hospital supplies and all those things

scores.rationale: Technical capability is real but shallow relative to a true tech moat — FDC/formulation R&D, a first-in-India Esaxerenone, and biosimilar fill-finish acquired rather than built, with the flagship Semaglutide molecule sourced from a partner.
scores.quote: our partner, Natco, has received CDSCO approval for Generic Semaglutide

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network is discussed anywhere in the calls.

Distribution reach is the company's clearest structural advantage — a ~3,700-rep force across seven to eight diabetes/metabolic teams plus cold-chain and patient-service infrastructure, which directly converted into a #1 volume rank on Semaglutide within one month of launch.
scores.quote: we already have around seven to eight teams doing Diabetes and Metabolics... we have added two teams for Insulin

scores.rationale: Genuine growth capex is being deployed (58,000 sq ft Kubota export hub, captive finance NBFC, a greenfield tractor plant for localization), but the greenfield has slipped repeatedly — Rajasthan abandoned over water, UP land still unsigned in Nov-2024 — so incremental ROIC remains unproven.
scores.quote: we have submitted an expression of interest to the UP government now with the Rajasthan government was not able to give us the assurance for the water supplies... our original plan of FY '27, '28 remains there

scores.rationale: A&P is never quantified across 11 calls; the only spend discussed is ground-level dealer activation and seasonal festive discounting, which supports volume rather than durable brand equity.
scores.quote: lot of activations, lot of activities, lot of key dealer focus, focus on key segments and products have happened to drive the retail growth

scores.rationale: R&D is producing a visible product cadence (PROMAXX, Worldmaxx, Kubota U22-6 mini-excavator, KA6/KA8 transplanters, Hydra-72) and PROMAXX demand now exceeds supply, but management concedes persistent portfolio gaps and a Powertrac series slip, so efficiency is only moderate.
scores.quote: The Promaxx series continue to gain traction with the order inflow now exceeding current supply level... In the coming next six-eight months, we will be launching new models and upgrades across all brands to address key product gaps

scores.rationale: The EKI/KAI amalgamation was neither small nor already strong — roughly INR 2,000 crores of breakeven revenue that diluted group margin 1.5–2% and requires 2–3 years of localization to fix, the opposite of a bolt-on where OPM improves post-deal.
scores.quote: these 2 JVs are combined levels were more or less breakeven operation, and they had about INR 2,000 crores of sales as a top line with very nominal operating margin. So that is why we had syndicated this will lead to about 1.5% to 2% dilution

scores.rationale: Distribution has been coherent and event-linked — a 16.3% capital reduction in FY24 and a one-time special dividend of INR 18/share paid out of the railway divestment proceeds — though these are structural/parent-driven actions rather than opportunistic buybacks at low valuations.
scores.quote: The board of directors has declared a one-time special dividend of Rs.18.0 per equity share of face value Rs.10 on completion of the railway business divestment.

scores.rationale: This is a capital-heavy manufacturer adding a greenfield plant and carrying a large idle cash/treasury book, with segment revenue of roughly INR 2,400–2,800 crores a quarter against rising fixed assets — asset-heavy, not asset-light with a protecting moat.
scores.quote: the localization will do a large extent, depend on the greenfield plant going live and kicking

scores.rationale: Trajectory is share loss, not capture: after gaining to 9.7% in FY24, share slid through FY26 and in the strongest industry quarter (Q3 FY26) EKL grew 12% against industry growth of 23.2%, with management only claiming to have arrested the decline.
scores.quote: Overall, the market share has not grown, but the continuous decline has been able -- we have been able to arrest that in quarter 2.

scores.rationale: Exports collapsed for two years (down 38% in Q1 FY24, Europe recession in FY25) and Brazil/US remain deferred to the greenfield plant, but FY26 shows real execution with exports up 26% and 63% YoY and Kubota-network sales rising from 20% to 68% of exports.
scores.quote: Our export volume was at 1,582 tractors, up by approximately 63%... sales to Kubota Global Network account for approximately 68% of the total export.

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and policy-led rather than price-led: the GST 2.0 cut lowered tractor prices, no portfolio-level price action was taken even into commodity inflation, and only the HP mix shift is favourable.
scores.quote: post the reduction of GST on tractors, the liquidity with the farmer has actually increased... in a INR7 lakh product, it's a straight INR50,000 reduction

scores.rationale: The company is at the top of the tractor cycle, not the bottom — the industry is heading to a record ~11.5 lakh units on GST cuts, subsidies and good monsoon, and management refuses to rule out an FY27 reversal.
scores.quote: Domestic tractor industry is likely to reach a new peak of around 11.5 lakh units this fiscal year

scores.rationale: Indian farm mechanization is a genuine secular market and EKL is broadening into it via non-tractor verticals (implements, harvesters, transplanters, engines, spares) now at 17–21% of agri revenue versus 10–12% pre-merger, though the core tractor demand remains monsoon- and subsidy-cyclical.
scores.quote: non tractor revenue now counts for around 17% to 19% of our overall agri machinery revenue as compared to 10% to 12% pre-merger

scores.rationale: Stewardship is prudent — consistently net-debt-free, INR 347 crores of amalgamated-company debt repaid on merger, non-core railway divested via a competitive process to reallocate capital to agri and CE, and no large external acquisitions.
scores.quote: we have made the decision to divest our railway equipment business to Sona Comstar, the purpose of this sale is to streamline our operations, reallocate capital and enhance the scale and efficiency of our core businesses

scores.rationale: A stated midterm plan has been ground out over years — NCLT merger completed, captive-finance NBFC licensed, export hub built, railway exited — but independence is limited by Kubota parentage and several milestones (greenfield land, Powertrac series, US/Brazil entry) have slipped repeatedly.
scores.quote: sharing key milestone that we have achieved in the current financial year that are aligned to our midterm business plan shared with you all earlier

scores.rationale: Calls across all 11 quarters are run by professional divisional heads and the CFO with no promoter/Chairman showmanship, and commentary stays on operating detail rather than personality.
scores.quote: MR. BHARAT MADAN – WHOLE-TIME DIRECTOR AND CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER... MR. NEERAJ MEHRA – CHIEF OFFICER, TRACTOR BUSINESS DIVISION

scores.rationale: The excerpts contain no discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline beyond changes in who appears on the call roster, so there is no basis to judge.

Management repeatedly volunteers bad news with specifics — post-merger margin dilution, market-share decline, product gaps and model unavailability, the Powertrac launch slip, the abandoned Rajasthan site and the labour-code hit — rather than burying it.
scores.quote: Post-merger margin dilution impact is there as the merged entity are currently not as profitable as EKL was premerger... our domestic performance was moderated by regional disparity... limited availability of key models impacted our sales momentum

scores.rationale: Stripping the halo off record FY26 profits, the earnings surge is driven by exogenous factors — GST 2.0, state subsidies, monsoon/reservoirs and commodity deflation — while the company-controlled metric, market share, went backwards.
scores.quote: This momentum was supported by favorable government policies, lower GST rate, healthy agriculture conditions including adequate water reservoir levels and state-level subsidiary programs

scores.rationale: EKL holds roughly 11% domestic tractor share as a distant number-three player with no monopoly position in the customer's mind, and its aftermarket verticals (spares, engines) were flat over the last six months.
scores.quote: Total share at the end of Q2 FY '26 stand at 11.28%... only the other 2 business on engine and spare parts were more or less flattish in this 6 months

scores.rationale: Its historic regional stronghold in North/Central India is eroding precisely as those markets underperform, and there is no evidence of switching costs — farmers move on price, GST and subsidy availability.
scores.quote: The North and Central markets continued to underperform as compared to the other regions, Other regions grew by 34.2%

scores.rationale: The Indian tractor market is a stable multi-player oligopoly (EKL, M&M, TAFE, Sonalika, John Deere) facing a fragmented farmer base with no negotiating power, though seasonal discounting by all manufacturers tempers the structure.
scores.quote: whenever it's peak festive time, all the manufacturers, including us, give certain shops, certain discounts. And those are actually withdrawn once the season gets over

scores.rationale: No new entrants are cited and cost inflation is generally passed through industry-wide, but pricing is followership-dependent rather than independently rational, and CE price increases failed to stick when demand was weak.
scores.quote: It will also depend on how the competition actually responds to that. So, based on that, we will take a call.

scores.rationale: EKL is the donator rather than the taker — competitors in the fast-growing South and West are taking share from it, and it is waiting on future product launches simply to stop the bleeding.
scores.quote: Yes, the industry growth in -- substantial industry growth in the Western part and South is actually impacting us.

scores.rationale: This is a high-profile, heavily covered large-cap — every call is hosted by a major broker with Bank of America, HSBC, Kotak, Nuvama and mutual funds on the line — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Gunjan Prithyani from Bank of America

scores.rationale: Demand responds directly to price, GST and subsidy rather than brand image, EBITDA margins sit in the 10–13.5% range, and no portfolio price increase was taken even into commodity inflation — evidence of weak pricing power.
scores.quote: with the reduction in the tractor prices, this buoyancy has actually increased... So, no price action taken so far, right? ... No, it is not on our overall portfolio level.

scores.rationale: The Kubota association supplies a genuine reliability/engineering promise on newer products, but the customer base still buys on affordability and subsidy, so trust does not yet outrank price.
scores.quote: the Next-Gen of Rice Transplanters, KA6 and KA8 models engineered in Japan for precision, efficiency and comfort

scores.rationale: Access has been steadily deepened — exclusive dealer count grew from ~1,240 to ~1,500, white-space channel expansion continued, and a captive finance NBFC was licensed to fund customers directly.
scores.quote: We have currently around 1,500 exclusive dealers for our Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac brand... We obtained the certificate of registration from RBI for Escorts Kubota Finance Limited

scores.rationale: The customer is retail (farmers), and EKL matches it with finance and dealer intimacy rather than with the intangible brand pull the framework prefers for retail buyers, leaving it exposed to subsidy and GST swings.
scores.quote: Our recent product introduction, strengthening financial partnership and deeper dealer engagement help maintain healthy market share

scores.rationale: EKL has privileged access to Kubota's Japanese engineering across tractors, engines and implements, but the technology is licensed rather than owned — key content is still imported pending localization — and no meaningful R&D intensity is disclosed.
scores.quote: the contribution with the material cost levels are high. The reason is because many products are still getting imported from outside

scores.rationale: Across all 11 calls there is no discussion of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network — the business is discussed purely as manufacturing, dealers and products — so there is no evidence to score.

Distribution is a relative weakness rather than an advantage: ~1,500 dealers against far larger rivals, a footprint skewed to the underperforming North/Central belt, and admitted model unavailability at the point of sale during the industry's best quarter.
scores.quote: limited availability of key models impacted our sales momentum

scores.rationale: Growth capex is high and rising — dark stores scaling toward 3,000 with ~INR 700cr capex in a single quarter and larger stores/warehousing — and management says these investments are already lifting margins (QC guidance raised to ~6%), though returns are still thin and unproven at scale.
scores.quote: over time, we have increased the capex per store in our business and some of these investments are leading to increase in efficiency in the business

scores.rationale: A&P is deployed opportunistically and counter-cyclically for customer acquisition at low CAC rather than as sustained discounting, but it builds users more than durable brand equity and management refuses to break it out by business.
scores.quote: We feel a lot of our competitors in the market have pulled back on this so we're seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition

scores.rationale: No discussion of R&D spend, intensity or product-innovation output anywhere in the excerpts.

The one major deal (Blinkit) was large and loss-making at acquisition — the opposite of a small bolt-on of an already-strong asset — but management budgeted it tightly, cut the guided investment from $400m to $320m, and it has since become the group's growth and profit engine.
scores.quote: we wanted to now update that overall budget and guidance from $400 million down to about $320 million

scores.rationale: Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are never mentioned across the excerpts; all capital is being reinvested.

Food delivery remains asset-light with a strong position, but the mix has shifted decisively toward capital-heavy quick commerce — 17 million sq ft of warehousing, ~INR 2.5cr capex per store — so group asset intensity is rising, not falling.
scores.quote: a large part of the capex is in warehousing and that investment is lumpy

scores.rationale: Consistent evidence of share capture from offline/modern retail and e-commerce, and a pivot from being #3-4 in southern markets to leading by NOV in most of them.
scores.quote: Now, we are the leading player by NOV in most of these markets

scores.rationale: Well-executed expansion beyond NCR into new cities and faster-growing non-metros, but this is domestic city-by-city rollout, not a premium brand travelling internationally.
scores.quote: the non-metro cities are obviously growing faster because they're also growing off a smaller base

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume- and frequency-led while AOV/NAOV is flat-to-declining under competitive price-matching, with only take-rate/platform-fee increases offsetting.
scores.quote: directionally, most of it is frequency growth... NAOV stabilizes. It grows but only slightly

scores.rationale: Management identifies Q1FY27 as the peak of competitive intensity with subsidy-led competition seen as unsustainable, implying the margin cycle is near its trough with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: First quarter, so far, was the peak of competitive intensity that we have seen till date

scores.rationale: Both end markets are in secular expansion — food delivery compounding ~20-30% for years and quick commerce guided at 60% CAGR over three years with no user saturation seen.
scores.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR

scores.rationale: Organic focus with no new large M&A, explicit refusal of unhealthy discount-led growth, and counter-cyclical marketing investment precisely when competitors retreat.
scores.quote: you can always make the argument that we can grow a lot faster by opting for unhealthy growth right now. We just don't think that that is the right thing to do

scores.rationale: Multi-year independence of thought — abandoned discount-led playbook for infrastructure building in the South and won, and declined to copy Swiggy's Toing without a clear thesis.
scores.quote: we don't have any plans to do what Swiggy is doing with Toing. We're not clear on what problem it solves

scores.rationale: The founder-CEO is a high-profile media figure whose interviews were themselves used as guidance benchmarks by analysts, the opposite of a low-profile management style.
scores.quote: there was a media interview of Deepinder, I think, last month where I think the guidance was of a slightly higher annual number

scores.rationale: Evidence of a real internal pipeline: Blinkit's founder-CEO Albinder Dhindsa was elevated to group CEO of Eternal, and store operations are systematically handed to local partner-operators.
scores.quote: Our attempt is to make sure that every new store that we open is eventually run by a local partner.

scores.rationale: Candid about failures and about what they will not forecast, and gives falsifiable guidance they later revisit openly, though they withhold a lot of operating detail on competitive grounds.
scores.quote: That didn't work for us initially in some markets in the south

scores.rationale: Results survive a skill test rather than resting on tailwinds — the South turnaround, NCR's proven 5-6% cohort margin and rising per-store capex efficiency show operating skill, though thin QC margins and heavy capital mean the record is not yet fully seasoned.
scores.quote: in NCR, you're doing 5-6% margin which would imply that contribution there is 8-9%

scores.rationale: Holds a mind-share-like position in dense markets — dominant in NCR where rivals struggle to convert its users, and leader by NOV in most markets — but this is leadership, not an unassailable monopoly.
scores.quote: You are clearly in a dominant position in an area like NCR, and competitors often struggle to get any consumers from you

scores.rationale: Local density gives regional strength, but customers multi-home and switching costs are low — management doesn't even track platform overlap, and price-sensitive cohorts must be won with targeted subsidies.
scores.quote: It's not something that we actively track.

scores.rationale: Food delivery is a stable duopoly with pricing power (rising platform fees), but quick commerce has many well-capitalized players and the end customer holds real power via subsidy-hopping.
scores.quote: there are like a few well-capitalized players in the market

scores.rationale: Supply-chain and store infrastructure is a genuine barrier, but pricing is plainly irrational — competition is running as broad grocery and delivery-fee subsidies that force Eternal to price match.
scores.quote: most of the competition is coming in the form of subsidies to customers on products and on delivery fees

scores.rationale: Ample weak donators exist — mid-tier modern retail, e-commerce and kirana are ceding share, and subsidy-funded QC rivals are described as being in a trap they cannot exit — though those rivals remain well-funded for now.
scores.quote: We don't see a recovery for platforms from this trap if they are acquiring customers by giving a lot of subsidies

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar: a heavily covered listed company fielding questions from JP Morgan, Goldman, Jefferies, Citi, Morgan Stanley and CLSA in a sector attracting maximal capital and competitive attention.
scores.quote: competitive intensity remains high

scores.rationale: Some pricing power exists in food delivery via repeated platform-fee increases, but quick commerce has little image-based pricing power — prices are being cut to match rivals and NAOV is drifting down.
scores.quote: Some of it can also just be related to lower product prices because there is a lot of competitive intensity, which also forces us to price match

scores.rationale: The stated wedge is reliability — consistency of service and availability of assortment — with customers choosing certainty over price and even tolerating split orders to get it.
scores.quote: Customers value the availability of products more than split orders.

scores.rationale: Convenience is the core product — a dense dark-store and delivery network delivering in minutes, with expansion justified by superior service levels where incumbents cannot match consistency.
scores.quote: the service level, both in terms of the selection available to customers and the consistency of service, is not at the same level that we provide

scores.rationale: Correctly matches retail consumers with convenience and reliability while monetising corporate customers (restaurants, FMCG brands) through ads and take rate, but consumer lock-in remains weak.
scores.quote: it's the gross margins, the delivery fee, and ad income

scores.rationale: The stated advantage is physical supply-chain and store infrastructure rather than a deep multi-product technology edge, and R&D intensity is never discussed.
scores.quote: Eventually, what worked was working on the infrastructure growth

scores.rationale: Real but moderate two-sided effects — restaurant supply sufficiency drives customer growth, and the Zomato app's traffic is reused to launch Blinkit and District at low CAC — yet consumers multi-home freely.
scores.quote: making sure that we keep our cost of customer acquisition lower using the traffic that we have on the Zomato app

scores.rationale: The clearest moat: a company-funded, high-quality dark-store network heading to 3,000 stores with ~17 million sq ft of warehousing and a national delivery fleet that rivals cannot replicate quickly.
scores.quote: our policy now is that we actually take the upfront cost of the capex because we find that we are able to do a higher quality capex

scores.rationale: Growth capex is high and rising — 12 stores for Rs 35 crore in H1 FY25, 14 boutiques in FY25, the 22,000 sq ft City of Time flagship and a path to 100+ boutiques — but incremental returns are unproven as EBITDA margin slipped and inventory ballooned from Rs 440 cr to Rs 593 cr.
scores.quote: we have successfully opened 12 stores with a total capital outlay of Rs. 35 crores

scores.rationale: Marketing is referenced as a differentiator (social following, website traffic, brand visibility) but no A&P quantum, efficiency or brand-equity payback is ever discussed across the eleven calls.
scores.quote: we've got a very potent and significant marketing muscle which operates only if you have got scale

scores.rationale: Ethos is a luxury retailer and no R&D spend, programme or output is mentioned anywhere in the excerpts.

No corporate M&A by the listed entity — the Favre Leuba brand was bought by the promoter group with Ethos taking only a long-term exclusive retail agreement, and the UAE subsidiary is a small greenfield step, so there is little post-deal OPM evidence either way.
scores.quote: Favre Leuba, the Swiss watch brand that our group has invested in

scores.rationale: The trajectory is repeated dilution rather than distribution — a Rs 175 crore QIP raised while roughly Rs 90 crore of IPO proceeds were still unutilised, with no buyback or dividend policy articulated.
scores.quote: still Rs 90 Crores are pending to utilize again you came out with the QIP to raise Rs 150 Crores recently

scores.rationale: The model is structurally asset- and working-capital-heavy, with inventory days worsening from 154 (Jun-22) to 159 (Sep-23) to 177 (Sep-24) and inventory up 35% in FY25, so turns are low despite the brand moat.
scores.quote: Inventory days, as on 30th September stood at 177 days

scores.rationale: Clear runway and evidence of capture — exclusive brand share rose from 24% pre-COVID to 31%, brands like Ulysse Nardin defected to Ethos after two decades in India, and same-store growth was 15.5% — though management admits it cannot quantify its share.
scores.quote: Ulysee Nardin is also well known in India where it has been present for nearly two decades and has now decided to work exclusively with Ethos

scores.rationale: Well-executed domestic geographic spread from ~50 to 73 boutiques across 26 cities with a deliberate Tier-2/Tier-3 push, plus an early exploratory UAE subsidiary; execution slipped versus the 20-store FY25 target.
scores.quote: it is important to establish a greater spread of physical stores into Tier-2, Tier-3 cities

scores.rationale: Growth has been decisively mix-led — ASP rose from Rs 84,000 to Rs 2.16 lakh in a few years by exiting low price points — although FY25 rebalanced toward volume (15.5% volume vs 7.4% ASP).
scores.quote: we are continuing to get out of lower price points and into brands at a higher price point

scores.rationale: The company is riding a strong upcycle rather than sitting at a cyclical bottom, with near-term headwinds (a possible GST hike to 28%, forex, weak H1 FY25 walk-ins) rather than an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: The first half of FY25 was marked by several challenges

scores.rationale: The Indian luxury end-market is in genuine secular expansion, with management citing a fivefold expansion over a decade driven by a multiplying affluent base extending beyond metros.
scores.quote: the luxury market in India will expand fivefold over the next decade

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with negligible debt (gross debt Rs 6.9 crore) and a stated aversion to leverage, but discipline is qualified by pre-emptive equity raises before prior proceeds were deployed.
scores.quote: we have always been very prudent about the kind of debt levels we keep

scores.rationale: A consistent, repeatedly reiterated ten-year 10x vision plus decade-long brand relationship-building and long-lease flagship investment show long-term orientation, though the goal remains largely unproven.
scores.quote: I would like to reiterate our long-term vision, which was stated when we went public to grow our revenue 10x over 10 years

scores.rationale: Family management is not celebrity-driven, but the commentary is notably promotional and self-congratulatory rather than understated.
scores.quote: this will be a Swiss watch brand that will achieve Himalayan heights in the years to come

scores.rationale: There is some professionalisation — a COO elevated to Executive Director and manpower build-out for new stores — but leadership succession is family (Pranav Saboo CEO to MD) and CFO turnover was high (three CFOs in four years), with no systematic talent pipeline described.
scores.quote: I am going to ask Mukul, our Chief Operating Officer to be able to answer that question

scores.rationale: Management quantifies misses and separates them (forex loss of Rs 4.65 crore split by line, 14 boutiques against a 20-plus target with GRAP IV explained, and an honest "I have no factual data" on market share), though H1 FY25 leaned on a long list of external excuses.
scores.quote: Several boutique openings were delayed due to unforeseen challenges, including the implementation of GRAP IV restrictions

scores.rationale: Much of the reported record performance reflects a post-COVID luxury boom, falling brand discounting and favourable brand allocation to India rather than demonstrable operator skill, so results should not be read as pure management alpha.
scores.quote: the demand for these iconic and luxury brands... has been steadily going up as they have become collectibles

scores.rationale: Exclusive retail rights over a large independent-brand portfolio (35 brands in 2022 growing to ~60, over 30% of revenue) plus a nationwide authorised service network create a monopoly-like position for those brands in India.
scores.quote: now 35 of the biggest watch brands are available exclusively at Ethos

scores.rationale: Authorised status and captive after-sales servicing create real switching frictions for both brands and customers, and the exclusivity is effectively a national monopoly on specific brands, though consumers can still buy competing brands elsewhere.
scores.quote: he can walk into any of our stores with any of the brands we represent and get servicing done across the country

scores.rationale: Organised Indian luxury watch retail is concentrated among few credible players with brand allocation acting as a gatekeeper, and buyers show low price sensitivity as discounts recede.
scores.quote: we do see a steady reduction in discounts... that's one of the reasons why you will see the margin improvement

scores.rationale: Entry requires multi-year brand relationships that are hard to replicate and pricing has grown more rational as discounting fell, though management gave little colour on brands opening their own boutiques.
scores.quote: Relationships with luxury brands and their owners typically take many years to develop and are difficult to replicate

scores.rationale: Grey-market and unauthorised/unorganised sellers plus fragmented small retailers are the clear donors, with Ethos's authorised status and scale marketing cited as the wedge.
scores.quote: I think we are authorized and they are not authorized

scores.rationale: The opposite is true — Ethos is a listed, heavily covered story (Emkay, JM Financial, Abakkus, EFG, multiple family offices on calls) that has already attracted institutional capital via a QIP.
scores.quote: The QIP of Rs.175 Crores was backed by leading institutional investors

scores.rationale: The category carries strong image-driven, inelastic demand (status symbol and store of wealth) but Ethos is a retailer whose MRPs are set by the brands, capping its own pricing power at ~30-32% gross margin.
scores.quote: Luxury watches are functional and serve as a status symbol and a store of wealth

scores.rationale: Trust and authenticity are the core purchase driver — authorised status, nationwide servicing and compliance processes are what let the pre-owned business grow 25-34% a year in an otherwise grey market.
scores.quote: Customers increasingly recognize the value of purchasing from an organized and trusted source

scores.rationale: A genuine omnichannel advantage — 73 boutiques across 26 cities, roughly a third of billings digital, specialist watch consultants, concierge and home/office delivery — that no rival matches in India.
scores.quote: nearly one-third of our business is now coming through digital medium

scores.rationale: The benefit set is correctly matched to an affluent retail HNI customer — image, assurance of authenticity and service — with a large HNI database and consultative selling, rather than corporate TCO arguments.
scores.quote: a large database of HNI customers, and an active program of a home and office delivery of luxury products

scores.rationale: The digital platform is a real capability contributing about a third of billings, but it is a retail channel rather than a defensible multi-product technology edge, and there is no R&D intensity.
scores.quote: Our digital platform has created a niche in the online luxury watch market

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts.

Distribution is the central moat — the largest authorised pan-India boutique and after-sales network, an exclusive brand portfolio rivals cannot stock, and brands now choose Ethos as their India entry route.
scores.quote: Ethos has become the preferred partner for many international brands looking to establish a foothold in India

scores.rationale: Capex is modest but deliberately rising for growth — from INR 55 cr (FY25) to INR 84 cr (FY26) — while still generating FCF at 148% of PAT and margins expanding from 6.3% to 12.2%, implying high incremental returns.
scores.quote: This is despite a step-up in capex from INR 55 crores in FY25 to INR 84 crores in FY26

scores.rationale: A&SP has been consistently stepped up (+40% in Q2FY25, +23.3% in Q3FY26, +13.2% for FY26) and demonstrably converted into category creation, share gain and margin expansion at the same time.
scores.quote: we delivered a 57 basis points margin expansion despite increasing our A&SP spends by 23% year-on-year

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or intensity is disclosed, but a steady cadence of premium innovations (under-the-counter, instant hot, Aquaguard Arctic Blaze at INR 79,999, robotics, softeners, air) has repeatedly driven ASP and new-category growth.
scores.quote: we also launched a new premium product, the Aquaguard Arctic Blaze, at a price point of INR 79,999, the highest in the category

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in the period — the record is of divesting non-core lines (Health Conditioners, Coronaguard, securities, B2B Forbes cleaning services), with inorganic optionality only flagged prospectively against the net cash pile.
scores.quote: net cash surplus of INR 443 crores today, giving us strategic flexibility, including for inorganic growth opportunities as and when they arise

scores.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy — cash has been directed to debt reduction and growth investment.

Business is asset-light (INR 2,710 cr revenue on INR 84 cr capex, FCF 148% of PAT, net cash INR 443 cr) and protected by the Aquaguard brand and nationwide service network, though the moat is being tested by new entrants.
scores.quote: we generated a free cash flow of INR 237 crores, representing 148% of reported PAT

scores.rationale: Repeated, explicit share gains (retail share up in Q2FY25; water purifiers ahead of category sequentially and YoY in Q3FY26) against a 5%-penetrated category, tempered by the fact that EFL is already the category pioneer/leader.
scores.quote: Our Water Purifiers performed ahead of the category, leading to market share gain both sequentially and year-on-year

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely within India — broad-based regional growth and air purifiers spreading beyond North markets — with no evidence of international or premium-brand-travel expansion.
scores.quote: we see this demand staying strong and becoming more geographically broad-based beyond the North markets

scores.rationale: Growth is a volume-plus-mix story with management explicitly disclaiming pricing-led growth until the cost-driven 6-7% April 2026 increase, so mix/premiumization contributes but pricing is not the engine.
scores.quote: in neither of the categories, was there a pricing led growth. We did not take pricing; it was on the back of both volumes and ASP

scores.rationale: The business is not cycle-positioned; the only cyclicality cited is a transient post-festive demand and channel-inventory slowdown in Q3FY26 that normalised within a quarter, not a bottom-of-cycle setup.
scores.quote: the growth slowdown in the quarter was a one-off aberration, which came on account of very temporary channel-specific issues

scores.rationale: End markets are in clear secular expansion — 5% water purifier penetration (3% rural), worsening national air quality, rising health awareness and BIS regulation formalising the category.
scores.quote: Water purifiers in India have a very low penetration of only 5%

scores.rationale: Purely organic execution with portfolio pruning, a swing from INR 193 cr net debt (Jun-22) to INR 443 cr net cash, and counter-cyclical A&SP step-ups sustained through the demand slowdown.
scores.quote: we have moved from a net debt of INR 193 crores in June 2022 to a net cash surplus of INR 443 crores today

scores.rationale: Project Udaan has been executed consistently across the full three-year window — margins 6.3% (FY23) to 12.2% (FY26), three years of teens product growth — with an explicit FY30 ambition and willingness to accept slow-burn payoffs like filters.
scores.quote: This marks a third consecutive year of margin expansion from 6.3% in FY23 to 12.2% in FY26

scores.rationale: Communication is process- and metric-led with no personality promotion across all thirteen calls, though the company runs Investor Days and heavy consumer/influencer marketing so it is not obscure.
scores.quote: our army of proud, passionate and committed Euro champs will be the sixth and the most critical pillar

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building is evident (leadership hiring, ESOP programs, technician training and revised incentives, digital tools for the service network), but the pipeline has been built largely by external hiring and the board/chairman roster has churned heavily.
scores.quote: We have strengthened the leadership team by hiring at various levels across functions and across the organization

scores.rationale: Management explicitly owned the missed Q3FY26 forecast, and proactively disclosed unflattering details such as AMC ASP dilution, coming FY27 gross-margin headwinds, and that the filters push will take years to change behaviour.
scores.quote: With the benefit of hindsight, it is now clear that the Q3 sell-out growth was not in line with our earlier projections and the post-festive slowdown was not anticipated

scores.rationale: The results survive skeptical decomposition — margin gains trace to identifiable, named programs (COGS program, cost/leakage control, operating leverage on employee cost) rather than to a favourable cycle, though category tailwinds and a very low FY23 base flatter the delta.
scores.quote: our COGS program is now well institutionalized and is helping create the headroom for growth investments

scores.rationale: Aquaguard holds a near-generic position in the Indian consumer's mind after 40+ years with an 8 mn customer base, but the aftermarket leg of the monopoly is leaky and being contested.
scores.quote: In Aquaguard, we have a power brand that enjoys tremendous consumer trust and acceptance

scores.rationale: Switching-cost lock-in is being deliberately built via multi-year AMC mix on the installed base, but management concedes the captive filter aftermarket was never captured and is held by gray-market operators and independent technicians.
scores.quote: our business model for the longest time has been AMC centric, and we were foregoing and not tapping into the large market for filters

scores.rationale: The structure is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly, with an unorganized/gray segment plus fresh aggressive entrants questioned by analysts in Q3FY26.
scores.quote: have we seen any impact from the 2 new players which are kind of showing aggression in this category?

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low and pricing behaviour is promotional — new entrants, aggressive buyback/discount schemes that compressed gross margin 111 bps, and entry price points cut to INR 6,499; BIS norms are the only prospective barrier.
scores.quote: Our Q2 gross margins at 56.3% were 111 basis points lower versus previous year. This was driven by a combination of buyback offers and channel mix

scores.rationale: There is a clear pool of weak donors — unorganized/gray-market players that BIS implementation should disadvantage, plus competitor installed bases converting via buyback schemes.
scores.quote: as BIS guidelines get accepted and get implemented, this will help drive the organized sector more favorably

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed consumer name — Kotak, Nomura, ICICI, HDFC, IIFL and Birla MF all on the calls — running mass-media and influencer campaigns, the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we launched major influencer-led marketing campaign that has already generated over 1 billion views

scores.rationale: Gross margins are structurally high and stable at 58-60% with a brand supporting a INR 79,999 flagship, but the portfolio also leans on an economy segment and buyback discounts, capping true image-led pricing power.
scores.quote: our gross margins have remained range bound at 58% to around 60% over the last 3 years now

scores.rationale: The category sells health certainty and reliability — service KPIs at all-time highs, a genuine-filters education campaign, and demand framed around contamination risk — though affordability and price points still feature heavily in the growth pitch.
scores.quote: We are investing in customer education, highlighting the importance of genuine filters

scores.rationale: Convenience is the sharpest customer benefit: direct sales force plus nationwide service network, 80% of interactions digital, a 24-hour TAT tightened to a 2-hour slot promise with a 4-hour model in pilot.
scores.quote: Earlier, our delivery promise was a 24-hour TAT... We've now moved that to a specific 2-hour slot promise

scores.rationale: The benefit set is correctly matched to a retail customer base — D2C strategy, brand/convenience-led benefits, and deliberate exit from the B2B cleaning services portfolio.
scores.quote: transforming into a vibrant D2C health and hygiene leader

scores.rationale: Innovation is product/feature-level (robotics, under-counter, instant hot, softeners) with no disclosed R&D intensity or proprietary technology edge; the stated differentiator is digital operations, not product technology.
scores.quote: being digital first is our fifth strategic pillar

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls; the installed base is a cross-sell asset, not a network.
The nationwide service network plus direct sales and full omnichannel reach is the company's hardest-to-replicate asset in a category where installation and after-sales service are essential.
scores.quote: Our omnichannel presence, including a direct sales network and a nationwide service network, give us unique advantages

scores.rationale: Very large and sustained growth capex — ~Rs.4,802 crore equity into the lithium-ion cell plant by FY26 plus Rs.400-500 crore/yr brownfield core capex — but incremental ROIC is still entirely unproven with SOP slipping from 2024 to trials only in May 2026.
scores.quote: total equity investment made in Exide Energy, our subsidiary till date, stands at Rs. 4,802 crores

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-building budget or promotional efficiency is discussed anywhere in the calls beyond generic references to brand recall.

Consistent flow of new products across the period — AGM batteries for premium PVs, Ultra/PowerBox inverter range, front-access data-centre batteries, premium export SKUs — though no R&D spend or efficiency is disclosed and the lithium cell technology is licensed from SVOLT.
scores.quote: this quarter, we have just launched AGM batteries for premium passenger vehicles

scores.rationale: Only M&A evident is taking Nexcharge to a 100% subsidiary — small and complementary, but management itself says it cannot be leveraged until own cells are made, and no post-deal margin improvement is shown.
scores.quote: that unit has become 100% subsidiary of Exide now

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or a distribution policy in any excerpt; the HDFC Life stake monetisation question was deflected without a policy framework.

Core lead-acid runs 85-90% utilisation behind a real brand/distribution moat, but the business is capital-heavy and a Rs.4,800 crore lithium asset base sits on the balance sheet generating zero revenue after four years, depressing group asset turn.
scores.quote: Capacity, we are clocking anything between 85% to 90% at this point in time

scores.rationale: Management claims share gains against both unorganised and organised rivals in 2022, and by FY26 cites 100% supplier status on new Tata Sierra and Kia Seltos SKUs plus mid-teens replacement growth, though headline FY26 growth of 4.1% tempers the claim.
scores.quote: Exide has been gaining share rapidly in the market, not only against unorganized players, but also against organized players in almost all segments

scores.rationale: Exports were promised as a major growth driver from Nov 2024 with new premium products for US/Europe, but instead shrank from 8% to 5-6% of revenue by FY26 with the recovery still deferred to the next fiscal — a clear delivery shortfall versus repeated promises.
scores.quote: Exports was already 8% of our revenue a couple of years back. So, we came down to 5%

scores.rationale: Pricing actions are defensive commodity pass-throughs taken with a lag (5-6% over three tranches plus 3% in April) rather than pricing power, though mix does help via a rising replacement share and premium AGM/front-access products.
scores.quote: we have taken increases which maybe amounts to about, let's say, about 5% to 6%

scores.rationale: Several verticals are visibly bottoming with identifiable upturns — exports on a low base, auto OEM up 25% for two consecutive quarters post-GST 2.0, and late-cycle industrial infra order flow picking up in railways, motive power and data-centre UPS.
scores.quote: But now it has bottomed out, I would like to feel so

scores.rationale: Genuine secular tailwinds in solar (crossed Rs.1,000 crore), data centres and motive power are offset by permanent structural erosion of the lead-acid base as telecom and e-rickshaw migrate to lithium-ion.
scores.quote: Telecom and E-Rickshaw continue to see shifts towards lithium-ion technology

scores.rationale: Organic focus and a historically zero-debt balance sheet are genuine positives, but the scale of the Rs.6,000+ crore single bet on an unproven lithium business, part-funded by bridge loans, is not obviously prudent stewardship.
scores.quote: We continue to maintain a very strong balance sheet with zero debt:equity and a high liquidity position

scores.rationale: Four years of consistent, independently funded pursuit of the lithium project — explicitly refusing PE or strategic partners and continuing to invest through weak quarters — shows tenacity, discounted by repeated timeline slippage from SOP 2024 to trials in 2026.
scores.quote: we are quite confident enough of managing this investment and we do not anticipate any such equity partnership as of now

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently factual and operational with no promotional framing or celebrity positioning; management repeatedly declines to speculate publicly on pricing, customers and capacity fungibility.
scores.quote: we would refrain from a comment. For us, it is more of a hypothetical question

scores.rationale: There is a deliberate organisation realignment and leadership build-out, but the pipeline looks externally sourced and unstable — MD, CFO and the Exide Energy CEO all changed within the four-year window (Chakraborty to Roy, Mukherjee to Agarwal, Deo to Saraf).
scores.quote: this resulted in some top leadership hiring who are being onboarded now

scores.rationale: Disclosure is unusually granular and self-critical — quantifying the two-thirds/one-third split of growing versus declining businesses, naming the Q2 GST washout, and giving specific commodity moves (antimony $11,000 to $66,000, sulphuric acid Rs.15 to Rs.74/kg).
scores.quote: we almost had a washout because there was no offtake from our distribution network

scores.rationale: Stripping the strong brand halo leaves a mixed delivery record — the 2022 promise to return to 14-15% margins once input prices stabilised is still unmet at 11.7% in FY26, and the lithium SOP has slipped roughly two years.
scores.quote: Once the prices stabilize, it will take about three to six months... And from then on, the earlier margin should be possible

scores.rationale: Exide holds a top-of-mind position in Indian batteries with strong brand recall and a captive replacement aftermarket pulled through by OEM fitment, though it shares the space with a comparable organised rival rather than owning it.
scores.quote: Exide, with its advanced product portfolio, pan-India distribution network and strong brand recall

scores.rationale: OEM fitment wins (100% supplier on Tata Sierra petrol and new Kia Seltos) and long B2B approval cycles create real aftermarket lock-in, but switching costs in retail replacement batteries remain modest.
scores.quote: this data center business has a long gestation period because these have so many approval processes

scores.rationale: The Indian organised lead-acid market is a stable two-player structure with a fading unorganised tail, though large auto OEM customers clearly retain negotiating power over pricing with a quarter-long pass-through lag.
scores.quote: we have been able to make our OEM customers agree to a certain amount of price increases

scores.rationale: No new entrants appear across four years of calls and pricing behaviour is rational — repeated industry-wide price corrections rather than discount wars, with stable promoter ownership throughout.
scores.quote: from January onwards, we could not sustain the cost inflation of material. Therefore, we started taking price increases stage-by-stage

scores.rationale: Explicit and continuing share capture from unorganised players in a consolidating market provides a clear donor pool, reinforced by the organised sector's rising salience.
scores.quote: The organized sector, I would imagine we have gained share

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a 75-year-old listed leader whose calls are attended by JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Nomura, Nuvama and Avendus, and whose lithium project is a nationally visible capital magnet.
scores.quote: we would be one of the first players to kick start a multi-gigawatt hour, lithium-ion facility in the country

scores.rationale: Brand recall supports a premium and enables staged price increases across trade channels, but gross margin around 30-31% and heavy commodity sensitivity show the intangible pull is real yet not dominant.
scores.quote: in Q3, it was 31.6 and in Q4, in the last quarter, it was 30.1

scores.rationale: Core B2B demand is reliability-driven — railways now replace batteries on a fixed overhaul cadence regardless of remaining life because the equipment is mission-critical, and data-centre UPS buyers run multi-consultant approval processes.
scores.quote: they change the battery because it's such a critical equipment for their vehicle

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a stated core strength — a pan-India network continuously augmented with new channel partners and digitalised sales/customer-service processes deepening dealer intimacy.
scores.quote: we have additionally augmented our go-to-market and finding out new channel networks

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched to customer type — brand and distribution reach for retail replacement/inverter buyers, and reliability plus homologation-based lock-in for OEM, railway and data-centre corporates.
scores.quote: we have a very strong strategy in place. Now we have additionally augmented our go-to-market

scores.rationale: The flagship lithium technology is licensed from an external partner (SVOLT) with cells and raw materials imported from China, and yields, chemistry choice and process knowledge all depend on that partner rather than on proprietary depth.
scores.quote: we have very good technology support from SVOLT

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.

The pan-India distribution and service network is the single most consistently cited competitive asset across all four years, is what management leans on to launch new verticals like solar (Rs.1,000+ crore) and to defend share, and is not replicable by rivals in a category where service and availability decide the sale.
scores.quote: Exide, with its advanced product portfolio, pan-India distribution network, and a strong brand recall, will continue to benefit from growth opportunities

scores.rationale: Sustained growth investment in branch network and new business lines (65 branches in H1FY24, 39 in Q4FY26) alongside ROA rising from 0.7% to 1.24%, though the FY26 approach is deliberately calibrated rather than aggressive.
scores.quote: we expanded our physical presence by adding 39 new branches, staying consistent with our calibrated and like Manian mentioned, data-driven approach to network expansion

scores.rationale: A brand refresh with a celebrity ambassador was launched only in FY26, so brand-equity payback is unproven despite coinciding CASA acceleration.
scores.quote: we took on board Vidya Balan as Brand Ambassador and launched a media campaign Savings ki Vidya

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or product-development pipeline is discussed; only passing references to technology and AI use.
scores.quote: our influence of technology, use of AI

scores.rationale: Only small complementary bolt-ons — raising the Ageas Federal Life stake from 26% to 30% and listing the Fedfina subsidiary — with no large or transformative acquisitions.
scores.quote: we increased our stake in our associate company, Ageas Federal Life Insurance, from 26% to 30%

scores.rationale: No buyback or distribution policy is articulated anywhere; the recurring capital theme is dilution — the FY23-24 raise and now the Blackstone infusion.
scores.quote: we received board and shareholder approval through an AGM for the proposed strategic investment by Blackstone

scores.rationale: A bank is structurally asset-heavy and Federal's returns are modest — ROA 1.24% and ROE 12.47% even at a record quarter, with management conceding it has never been a high-margin bank.
scores.quote: We have not been a very high margin bank. But our ROA from 0.7% to 1.4% has come in five financial years

scores.rationale: Long runway from a ~1.2-1.3% national credit share with incremental share running higher and NR share rising, though FY26 headline loan/deposit growth actually lagged the system by choice.
scores.quote: We are at about 1.2% share of the credit, but incremental credit our share of gains. I mean, our share of market is closer to 2%

scores.rationale: Steady pan-India branch build-out plus a dominant Gulf-corridor NRI franchise crossing INR1 lakh crore with rising market share, executed consistently across the period.
scores.quote: NRI deposits have now crossed INR1 lakh crore, alongside a continued increase in market share

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly mix-led — shifting to mid-yield assets and CASA-heavy liabilities — which defended NIM to within 2bps despite 125bps of rate cuts.
scores.quote: our NIM expansion... is not only a deposit repricing story... It is a mix story on the asset side, medium yield assets versus low-yield assets

scores.rationale: Positioned past the trough of the rate and MFI credit cycle, with deposit repricing benefits still ahead and MFI credit costs declining each quarter.
scores.quote: there is still scope for deposit repricing... There is some -- still some deposit repricing potential that is possible from here

scores.rationale: Indian banking credit is in secular expansion with a visible shift of intermediation toward banks, and management repeatedly cites broad-based demand.
scores.quote: there is an inherent shift to banks as lenders has increased visibly combined with, I think the demand for credit

scores.rationale: Consistently organic and counter-cyclical — refusing to chase volume or flex credit standards, deliberately shrinking wholesale deposits and corporate book for quality, with no large M&A.
scores.quote: our focus is deliberate consistency over volatility, quality over headline growth

scores.rationale: A multi-year, independently held plan delivered across two CEOs — ROA compounded from 0.7% to 1.4%, new businesses seeded pre-COVID matured on schedule, and the FY26 mix shift is framed as a medium-term journey.
scores.quote: This is inherently a medium-term journey, and we are encouraged by the traction seen across most of our identified focus segments

scores.rationale: Management is understated and process-focused on calls, deflecting macro punditry and letting numbers speak, though the FY26 brand campaign adds some external visibility.
scores.quote: I don't have any unique commentary differently from the market gurus who have a better view

scores.rationale: Strong internal pipeline evidenced by Harsh Dugar's rise from Group President to ED and Manikandan's internal elevation to CFO, though the MD role was filled externally.
scores.quote: congratulating my colleague, Manikandan, for becoming the CFO of the bank

scores.rationale: Unusually candid across years — admitting fallibility, disclosing account-opening wastage and fraud filtering, flagging MFI is not fully recovered, and refusing to pretend margins are a single-lever story.
scores.quote: Mahrukh, I've been wrong before. I'm this calm because I think these are moving parts

scores.rationale: Results survive the halo test reasonably well — NIM and ROA improved through a 125bps easing cycle rather than because of it — and management itself concedes it is a small player vulnerable to larger banks' choices.
scores.quote: despite the 125-bps rate cut from last year December to this year December, our margins have expanded

scores.rationale: The NRI remittance franchise is a genuine mind-share position, explicitly called a moat, with ~7-7.5% of India's NR deposit pool from a bank with only ~1.3% credit share.
scores.quote: Our NRE deposit, which is our moat, reached a significant milestone crossing the INR 1 lakh crore mark

scores.rationale: A regional stronghold in Kerala and the Gulf corridor built over a 90-year legacy gives sticky, relationship-based deposits, though banking switching costs are otherwise low.
scores.quote: Pride in a 90-year legacy while actively shaping the next chapter

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented and fiercely contested rather than a stable oligopoly, with customers holding real pricing power on both deposits and loans.
scores.quote: a market where we have seen intense and sometimes irrational rate competition

scores.rationale: Despite licensing barriers, pricing behaviour is explicitly irrational and competitive intensity is described as elevated throughout.
scores.quote: While competitive intensity remains elevated

scores.rationale: Weaker public-sector and smaller lenders plus the shift of borrowing from markets to banks give Federal identifiable share to take, which it has been capturing on an incremental basis.
scores.quote: Our share gain is visible. Outreach has improved quite substantially

scores.rationale: Far from under the radar — heavily covered by sell-side analysts on every call and now the target of a headline Blackstone strategic investment.
scores.quote: This is a strong validation of our strategy, governance framework, and execution capabilities

scores.rationale: Deposits and loans are price-sensitive commodities with no image-driven pricing power — margins sit near 3.2% and management admits it cannot price out of the market.
scores.quote: You cannot play price out of the market with our risk appetite

scores.rationale: The NRI and retail deposit franchise is built on trust and reliability rather than rate, evidenced by 21% CASA growth while wholesale deposits were deliberately shrunk.
scores.quote: This represents a robust 13.2% Y-o-Y increase, underscoring the deepening trust and strong engagement

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a deliberate build — data-driven branch expansion, fintech partnership-led account sourcing, and a new wealth business to deepen customer intimacy.
scores.quote: we also launched our wealth management business. This is an important step in building a stronger mass affluent franchise

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched — trust and convenience for granular retail/NRI depositors, and selectivity plus pricing discipline with high-rated corporates.
scores.quote: we have prioritized portfolio quality and pricing discipline over headline volume. With exposures within high-rated counterparties

scores.rationale: Digital partnerships, AI use and partnership-led onboarding are real but presented as operational learning rather than a deep multi-product tech edge over larger private peers.
scores.quote: We were at some stage doing maybe 13,000, 14,000 accounts a day on the savings side. We've brought it down to 4,000, 5,000

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is evident; growth comes from branch reach, partnerships and pricing, not from scale-driven network economics.
scores.quote: we are expanding in segments that deliver superior risk-adjusted returns

scores.rationale: The Kerala branch density plus Gulf remittance corridor and fintech sourcing give reach rivals struggle to replicate in that niche, though not a nationwide distribution advantage.
scores.quote: Our NRI franchise remains a key differentiator, and we have further strengthened our leadership position in this segment

scores.rationale: Sustained growth investment in physical distribution — 148 new gold branches in FY26 plus doorstep infrastructure — with AUM per branch still rising (Rs 12.1cr → 16.5cr → 17.7cr) and new branches reportedly profitable within a year, though ROE only reached the mid-teens.
scores.quote: we have opened 34 new gold branches this quarter, bringing our total to 148 new branches this year... our AUM per branch has reached INR16.5 crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the calls despite a CMO on the management roster.
No R&D function or spend is discussed; IT work described (Salesforce, BRE) is operational systems implementation, not product R&D.
No acquisitions are discussed anywhere in the excerpts; the only portfolio action is divestment/assignment of the unsecured book, not M&A.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed; capital actions are all inbound (IPO proceeds, Rs 450cr sub-debt, $250mn ECB) to fund growth.
As a balance-sheet NBFC the model is inherently asset-heavy and getting more levered, with debt/equity rising from 3.98 to 4.89 and capital adequacy needing constant relief via DA/co-lending.
scores.quote: leverage going up from 4.6 to 4.89

scores.rationale: Small base in a vastly under-served market with clear share capture — AUM up 27% to Rs 20,153cr, gold AUM +76% YoY and doorstep gold +108% — though ST LAP share was surrendered for two years during the credit repair.
scores.quote: Gold reached INR10,352 crores, an AUM growth of 76%

scores.rationale: Steady, well-executed domestic branch/state expansion (17th state in 2023, 607 branches then, 750+ now with 148 added in FY26), but it is purely within-India footprint growth, not a premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: We forayed into the state of Uttarakhand, which is our 17th state

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and collateral-price-driven, not pricing/mix-led: yields fell 12bps YoY as mix shifted to lower-yield gold and MT LAP, and management concedes it gives away basis points to push disbursals.
scores.quote: Our yields reduced 12 bps year-on-year due to a never before growth in the gold loan book

scores.rationale: Mixed cyclical position — the company is emerging from the bottom of its own credit cycle (credit cost 1.8% FY25 → 0.8% FY26) but rode gold prices at the top, which then fell 15% between Jan and Jun 2026.
scores.quote: head-winds of declining domestic prices of 15% between Jan 31st to June 30th

scores.rationale: The small self-employed/MSME secured-credit and formalised gold-loan market is a genuine secular under-penetrated end market, with management citing that only a fifth of demand is served.
scores.quote: it's estimated that only 20% of the demand is actually catered to

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with a deliberate exit from unsecured lending to a 99.5% secured book and capital conserved via DA/co-lending, though leverage has crept up to 4.89x and capital adequacy fell to 20.71%.
scores.quote: we 100% assigned our business loan portfolio of INR886 crores... ensures that we maintain a secured on-book ratio exceeding 99.5%

scores.rationale: The Mulla team has held the same stated priorities for five consecutive quarters and tenaciously rebuilt ST LAP and collections over two years, delivering PAT +52.5% and ROE 15.4% by Q1 FY27.
scores.quote: For the last five quarters, we have articulated the same set of priorities, and they remain unchanged

scores.rationale: Communication is largely operational and low-key, but the calls carry some self-congratulatory framing ('century', 'psychological milestone') and there is no evidence either way on public profile.
scores.quote: We crossed the psychological milestone of INR 100 crores of PAT
