scores.quote: We have seen the market leader become a bit more aggressive past few months

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs or captive aftermarket — management itself notes consumers face abundant choice and shelf presence alone confers no right to win.
scores.quote: Just today's consumer has got multiple sort of choices in every category

scores.rationale: BPC is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly, with legacy FMCG players plus a wave of digital-first brands, and platform/retail customers (quick commerce, modern trade) hold real negotiating power.
scores.quote: a lot of folks restructured and clearly announced their focus to build this and also have used multiple levers, including deep discounting

scores.rationale: Entry barriers in digital-first BPC are minimal and pricing is irrational, with competitors using deep discounting to buy online growth for six-plus quarters.
scores.quote: this focus change and aggression has been there for now, 6 plus quarters

scores.rationale: Slow-moving legacy multi-decade brands are the clear donators, from whom Honasa has visibly taken share in sunscreen, face wash and shampoo.
scores.quote: Derma Co is now the number one Sunscreen brand in the country, ahead of the legacy brands

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — a listed, heavily covered company in the most capital-attracting and most contested corner of FMCG, with incumbents explicitly restructuring to attack it.
scores.quote: there is a renewed focus and impetus to drive growth in online

scores.rationale: Sustained ~70–71% gross margins with rising Kantar brand power and purpose-led positioning indicate real image-based pricing power, but growth being volume- rather than price-led caps the score.
scores.quote: 71.4% gross margin, which has expanded by 70 basis points Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: The core proposition is safety and efficacy assurance — toxin-free/clean-label for Mamaearth and clinically framed actives with blind-test-verified formulations for Derma Co — rather than price.
scores.quote: a clean-label, toxin-free, natural, personal care brand

scores.rationale: Genuine omnichannel accessibility built from scratch — 80% direct distribution, ~200k outlets, EBOs, modern trade and the fastest-growing quick-commerce channel — gives strong customer reach and intimacy.
scores.quote: Our direct distribution contribution has expanded to almost 80% revenue contribution now

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail consumers and the benefit type is correctly matched — image, purpose and cohort-specific brand propositions rather than TCO arguments.
scores.quote: different brands which have and stand for different kind of sharp propositions

scores.rationale: R&D is credible formulation and ingredient work with real product wins, but it is applied cosmetic science that competitors can replicate, not a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: Our Sunscreen formulation has become even better with new generation filters like Tinosorb M

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network exists; the business relies on brand pull and third-party platforms whose scale benefits the platform rather than Honasa.
scores.quote: brands are built in the minds of consumers and purchased on platforms

scores.rationale: Distribution has improved dramatically from a low base and is now a functioning direct system, but at ~200k outlets versus legacy FMCG reach it is a catch-up asset rather than one rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: now we have more catch-up job to do on our distribution front

scores.rationale: Direct shareholder questions on FY25–27 capex plans, plant utilisation and 'Make-in-India' expansion went unanswered in the AGM, while the manufactured-goods share fell as traded (imported) goods rose from ~12% to 19% of topline — the opposite of growth capex.
scores.quote: on the capital expenditure part if you could provide what is the CapEx plans over the next three years from FY 25 to FY27

scores.rationale: Neither AGM makes any reference to advertising, promotion or brand-building spend.

The same shareholder asked in both FY23 and FY24 AGMs what share of revenue comes from products launched in the last five years and how innovation is tracked, and management never gave a number — HAIL explicitly excludes the underlying technology ('molecular') development, which sits with the parent.
scores.quote: What percentage of our revenue from the products for the last 5 years and how do we track the innovation business?

scores.rationale: No acquisitions, bolt-ons or inorganic activity are mentioned in either AGM.

Dividend raised from ₹95 to ₹100 per share with an explicitly rising payout ratio and a stated policy of consistent improvement, though there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution discipline.
scores.quote: The final dividend of ₹100 per equity share was recommended... which in the previous years was ₹95. Consistently improving the dividend payout is a goal

scores.rationale: Asset-light system-integration model — revenue grew to ₹4,582cr with profit growth (15%) outpacing revenue growth (11%) via fixed-cost leverage and a headcount roughly flat since FY16 — but the moat protecting it is only partial given margin erosion.
scores.quote: we have been able to generate that profit by leveraging the fixed cost

scores.rationale: Management could not quantify market share when asked, FY24 order growth of 11% lagged listed automation peers, and domestic revenue had barely grown from FY19 — evidence of share loss rather than capture.
scores.quote: our overall order growth was 11%, which seems slightly lower than the other listed automation peers

scores.rationale: HAIL's geography is capped at India plus captive exports to Honeywell subsidiaries, and management conceded the Middle East capex opportunity will largely be booked by other Honeywell entities, with exports declining from ~45% to 40% of sales.
scores.quote: a large chunk of that growth in those markets will go to the Honeywell entities in those respective markets

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/project-led with an actively deteriorating mix — traded goods rose from ~12% to 19% of sales and lumpy domestic projects diluted margins, leaving EBITDA margins well below FY19–20 peaks despite record revenue.
scores.quote: our margin rates are not steady given the both, the mix between domestic project business and domestic service

scores.rationale: The company is levered to an early-stage Indian private and government capex upcycle — infrastructure, manufacturing PLI, airports, giga-factories — with management rebuilding a pandemic-depleted project backlog.
scores.quote: capital investments, both in government as well as private sector in India is pretty optimistic and hence we participate in that upcycle

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — automation, digitalisation, energy transition (green hydrogen, BESS, CBG, ethanol), data centres and life-sciences facilities — all named as multi-year growth vectors with concrete FY24 wins in each.
scores.quote: The company's business is well aligned with the mega trend of automation underpinned by digitalization and sustainability

scores.rationale: Explicitly organic strategy with no M&A, no leverage discussed, working capital self-funded from operating cash (80% conversion) and net worth up 13%.
scores.quote: strategic priorities are broadly driving and focusing on organic growth

scores.rationale: As a 75%-owned Honeywell subsidiary HAIL's portfolio, geography and even growth opportunities are set by the parent — it holds only a 'small portfolio of global Honeywell' and cedes adjacent opportunities to sister entities — so long-term vision is executed with little independence.
scores.quote: first of all our portfolio is a very small portfolio of global Honeywell

scores.rationale: Management is genuinely low-profile and substance-oriented — no analyst meets, no quarterly calls, no press releases, engaging investors only at the annual AGM — though this is under-communication rather than deliberate modesty.
scores.quote: the Company hosts at least one analyst meet, which is a regular practice now by every listed entity

scores.rationale: Orderly internal succession — Atul Pai, a 23-year company veteran with multiple global Honeywell roles, replaced Ashish Gaikwad as MD — plus repeated emphasis on a stable, deep talent pool as a competitive asset.
scores.quote: I started nearly 23 years ago in this company and had the privilege of taking multiple roles across Honeywell Group globally

scores.rationale: Persistent opacity across both years — absolute order book withheld (and dropped from the FY24 annual report), no segment margins, innovation and market-share questions unanswered, and a shareholder publicly complaining that 20 minutes went to CSR versus 10 to financials — only partly offset by the FY24 admission on data centres.
scores.quote: we did not do a good job in explaining how important data centre markets are for us

scores.rationale: The headline 17–18% revenue records look strong but reflect a post-COVID backlog rebuild and India's GDP tailwind on a depressed base — five-year sales CAGR to FY23 was only ~2% and margins remain ~3% below peak — so results are cycle-driven rather than proof of managerial skill.
scores.quote: the HAIL sales growth for the last 5 years, it's merely grown at about 2% CAGR

scores.rationale: The stated strategy is a razor/razor-blade installed base that yields captive lifecycle service annuity for the life of the asset — a quasi-monopoly in the aftermarket of each site it automates.
scores.quote: very similar to the theory of razor and razor blade. The moment you win the install base, you are able to get annuity or life cycle services for the life of the entire asset

scores.rationale: Distributed control and building management systems create high switching costs once installed, giving HAIL a captive aftermarket at each refinery, plant or building, which management explicitly frames as total cost of ownership over the asset life.
scores.quote: you are able to get annuity or life cycle services for the life of the entire asset which is the total cost of ownership

scores.rationale: Process/building automation in India is a global oligopoly, but management dodged the competition-intensity question and its customers are large industrial and government buyers of lumpy projects who clearly hold negotiating power, as evidenced by sustained margin compression.
scores.quote: if you could talk about the competition intensity in the market currently happening

scores.rationale: A shareholder flagged many new competitors entering automation and sensing, HAIL's order growth trailed peers, and margins have stayed ~3% below pre-COVID peaks — signs of price competition rather than rational, protected pricing, despite stable parent ownership.
scores.quote: we are seeing many competitors coming in the space of automation and sensing

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified; on the contrary HAIL's domestic revenue was flat from FY19 and its order growth lagged listed peers, positioning it closer to the donator than the taker.
scores.quote: our domestic business has not grown from FY19, which is very unlike other capital goods

scores.rationale: Far from ignored by capital — the AGM speaker list alone includes Aditya Birla, ENAM, LIC, Kotak, Invesco, SBI, Helios and Nippon, and management notes the stock is in essentially every Indian index.
scores.quote: Honeywell Automation is a fairly large company and we are a part of every index now in India

scores.rationale: This is a B2B system-integration business with no image- or taste-driven pricing power; gross margins are materially below FY19–20 levels and the mix is shifting toward low-margin traded goods.
scores.quote: our gross margins have materially been lower compared to our FY19, FY20 levels

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — zero total-case incident rate over three years, customer and Microsoft recognitions for safe execution on hazardous and data-centre sites, and solutions specified for redundancy and resiliency in life-sciences and LNG applications where failure is catastrophic.
scores.quote: it needs to be a very highly controlled system because it is hazardous to handle such a gas which is highly inflammable

scores.rationale: There is a nationwide field presence at refineries, airports, metros and plants plus a distribution arm for BMS and sensing, but no evidence of superior accessibility or customer intimacy versus rivals — indeed disclosure gaps on customer requirements went unanswered.
scores.quote: The HAIL portfolio consists of System Integration in Process and Building Solution plus distribution of specific Building Management Systems

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to corporate/industrial buyers — the pitch is total cost of ownership and lifecycle annuity from an installed base rather than brand intangibles, which is the right benefit type for this customer set.
scores.quote: you are able to get annuity or life cycle services for the life of the entire asset which is the total cost of ownership

scores.rationale: HAIL accesses Honeywell's deep multi-product automation technology but explicitly does not own the underlying process technology and discloses no R&D intensity of its own, with rising traded-goods imports suggesting integration rather than a proprietary tech edge.
scores.quote: not the molecular part of process technology but the automation part of that technology is something that Honeywell Automation would participate as a leading system integrator

scores.rationale: The business model is project-based system integration with an installed-base annuity tail; nothing in either AGM indicates a two-sided or self-reinforcing network.

HAIL has a service and engineering footprint across Indian industrial and infrastructure sites plus a stable talent pool, but competitors match this reach and export distribution is limited to intra-group subcontracting rather than owned channels.
scores.quote: we have a very particular advantage with respect to the skills and the capabilities that we have because our industrialization has been pretty diverse

scores.rationale: Sustained, self-funded growth capex across specialty carbon black (60k→130k MTPA), pitch debottlenecking (500k→600k), anthraquinone/carbazole, LFP CAM, anode, CNT (₹70cr) and super-speciality CB (₹170cr), with ROCE held at 32-34%.
scores.quote: The capex program is thoughtfully structured to balance scale with efficiency. It is entirely self-funded and deliberately calibrated between brownfield expansions... and greenfield investments

scores.rationale: Brand activity exists (Durofresh retail naphthalene balls, Birla Tyres 'brand repositioning') but no A&P spend, efficiency or brand-equity evidence is disclosed in any call.
scores.quote: our recently launched branded naphthalene ball brand, Durofresh, has received an encouraging response in the retail market

scores.rationale: ₹120cr FY26 R&D, 180 scientists/28 PhDs, and a repeated record of converting research into commercial products — in-house anode technology, indigenous CNT, anthraquinone/carbazole, 70+ specialty CB grades.
scores.quote: the entire technology platform from raw material processing to finished anode active material has been developed fully in-house without reliance on external or licensed technologies

scores.rationale: Birla Tyres was a distressed insolvency asset in an unrelated, competitive industry requiring multi-year revival and further capex — the opposite of a small bolt-on that is already strong — alongside multiple venture-style stakes (Sicona, IBC, Invati).
scores.quote: This transition, along with modernization initiatives, will be supported by additional capital expenditure and expected to be executed over the next 3 years

scores.rationale: No buybacks; a token dividend of 60% of ₹1 face value while capital is raised from promoters via ₹316 warrant conversion — capital flows in, not out, with no articulated distribution policy.
scores.quote: the promoters have further strengthened their stake in Himadri to conversion of one crore warrants into equity. The warrant are acquired at a total price of INR316 per warrant

scores.rationale: ROCE is high at 32% and the moat (65%+ pitch share, integration) is real, but the business is capital-intensive with revenue of ~₹4,661cr against continuous heavy greenfield/brownfield capex — high returns come from margin, not asset-light turnover.
scores.quote: Our return on capital employed has also shown a steady upward trajectory, reaching 32% in FY26

scores.rationale: Already dominant domestically in the core (over 65% pitch share, limiting runway there), but with genuine share-gain runway and evidence in specialty CB (now top-5 globally), exports and import-substitution products.
scores.quote: Our domestic market share continues to be over 65%

scores.rationale: Credible, executed expansion — products in 56 countries, two liquid pitch export terminals (Haldia, Mangalore) with a first 3,600 MT Middle East shipment, and Birla Tyres into Asia/Middle East/Africa — though it is cost-led rather than a premium brand travelling.
scores.quote: commissioning of a Mangalore port terminal, successfully delivering 3,600 metric tons of liquid coal tar pitch to the Middle East. This establishes our second export corridor

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly mix-led, not volume-led: 9M FY26 volumes up only 3% while EBITDA/ton rose 15% and PAT 41%, with management deliberately trading volume for value addition.
scores.quote: EBITDA per metric ton stood at INR 16,934 in 9 months FY '26 compared to INR 14,707... driven by product mix that remains increasingly focused on high value-added offerings

scores.rationale: End markets (aluminium, graphite, tyres) are cyclical and management notes raw-material and geopolitical volatility, but there is no evidence of the company being positioned at a cycle bottom with an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: recent geopolitical developments in West Asia have introduced volatility in energy prices and logistics. However, our business remains structurally insulated

scores.rationale: Core new-growth vector sits in a secularly expanding end market — global lithium-ion demand projected from ~1.6 TWh (2025) to ~6.8 TWh (2035) — plus EV/ESS and import-substitution chemicals.
scores.quote: Global lithium-ion battery demand is projected to rise from around 1.6 terawatt hours in 2025 to nearly 6.8 terawatt hours by 2035

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage (net cash, self-funded capex) and mostly organic expansion, offset by a large unrelated diversification into tyre manufacturing plus several external technology stakes.
scores.quote: we hold a net positive cash balance of INR 121 crores, which gives us ample flexibilities to pursue growth opportunities while maintaining a prudent approach to capital allocation

scores.rationale: A decade of patient in-house lithium-ion research culminated in a self-developed, unlicensed anode plant, and the FY25 three-year PAT-doubling promise was delivered in two years — long-horizon vision executed independently.
scores.quote: last time when we told it will be done, it was done in 2 years instead of 3 years

scores.rationale: Communication is highly promotional — recitation of awards, superlatives ('world's largest', 'first globally outside China') and grand transformation narrative dominate the opening remarks each call.
scores.quote: Himadri was conferred with Company of the Year among the listed companies at India Chem 2024... we were also awarded with the DET Hurun Award

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building in technical talent — 180 scientists including 28 PhDs recruited globally and a Great Place to Work certification — though senior leadership remains family-held (Chairman/MD both Choudhary) with repeated CFO churn.
scores.quote: a team of over 180 scientists, technologists and subject matter experts, including 28 PhDs

scores.rationale: Management explicitly scorecards prior commitments against delivery and gives direct explanations for soft metrics (volume decline from value-added shift, deferred shipment, mining licence), though it declines technical/customer specifics and rarely owns an outright mistake.
scores.quote: When we stood before you twelve months ago, we made clear commitments, and I am pleased to say that we delivered on all of them

scores.rationale: Results are verifiably strong in the legacy business (EBITDA/ton, ROCE 32%), but the bull case leans heavily on unproven new-energy ventures still at sampling/200 MTPA scale, so skill cannot yet be separated from narrative there.
scores.quote: our demo plant is under construction... post that, we will be sending sample 'B' to our customers. There are a series of samples will need to be approved by the customers

scores.rationale: Monopoly-like positions: over 65% domestic coal tar pitch share from the world's largest single-location integrated carbon complex, India's first anthraquinone/carbazole plant and first indigenous CNT.
scores.quote: We operate the world's largest single location fully integrated carbon complex, with 600,000 MTPA of coal tar distillation capacity

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real — grades are tailor-made and customer-qualified through multi-stage sample approvals, which management describes as producing stickiness, and backward integration into feedstock reinforces it.
scores.quote: our speciality offering... which provide us customer stickiness and greater value realization

scores.rationale: Concentrated global structure in its niches (top-5 globally in specialty carbon black, 'only a few companies in the world' in CNT), though end customers are large industrial buyers (aluminium, tyre, cell makers) with real negotiating power.
scores.quote: there are only a few companies in the world who are doing this. And we are the first in India

scores.rationale: High barriers from feedstock integration, proprietary process know-how and customer qualification cycles, with stable promoter ownership rising to 52.5%; pricing rhetoric is cost-leadership rather than premium discipline.
scores.quote: we are not dependent on that region for our core feedstock... Promoter shareholding now stands at 52.5%

scores.rationale: Clear weak-holder targets — imports currently supply anthraquinone/carbazole and Chinese suppliers dominate LFP, both of which Himadri is set up to displace.
scores.quote: These products are currently largely imported in India, and our objective is clear: To substitute imports with world-class domestic manufacturing

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — awards-heavy positioning, extensive sell-side coverage on calls and headline-grabbing entries into EV battery materials place it squarely in the spotlight.
scores.quote: I saw some headlines that you are in talks with some large players

scores.rationale: Demand is steady and margins healthy (22% EBITDA margin), but pricing power derives from specification and cost economics in a B2B industrial setting rather than image or taste; the only retail brand (Durofresh) is immaterial.
scores.quote: we supply high-quality tailor-made coal package to our customers at most economical cost globally

scores.rationale: Customers buy consistency and qualified performance — quality, consistency and multi-stage approvals are the stated selling proposition, plus EcoVadis Platinum as a commercial prerequisite — though management also leads with lowest cost.
scores.quote: Increasingly, such credentials are not merely accolades, but important commercial prerequisites in global value chain

scores.rationale: Accessibility has been deliberately built — dedicated liquid pitch terminals at Haldia and Mangalore for direct global supply, and a tyre channel expanded to 49 distributors and 1,000+ dealers.
scores.quote: the distribution network spans 49 distributors and over 1,000 dealers

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to a corporate customer base: TCO savings, reliability and qualification-driven lock-in for aluminium/graphite/tyre/cell makers, with retail exposure kept marginal.
scores.quote: Our commitment to delivering the highest standards of quality results in sustainable economic savings for our customers, thereby strengthening our collaboration

scores.rationale: Deep multi-product technology edge developed in-house — anode platform, indigenous CNT, LFP cathode, 70+ specialty CB grades — backed by ₹120cr R&D and a lab-first commercialization discipline.
scores.quote: Our approach remains lab-first, plant-later, and shows that capacity expansion is always backed by validated applications

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in any of the calls; the model is industrial manufacturing and supply.

Logistics reach is a genuine differentiator in liquid pitch — two dedicated export terminals enabling supply to 56 countries — but the tyre dealer network is still being built and is not one rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: the commissioning of liquid Coal Tar Pitch terminal at Haldia and Mangalore has strengthened our ability to serve global markets

scores.rationale: As a lender HUDCO takes no physical capex, but its capital deployment (loan book INR80,000cr FY23 to INR1.55 lakh cr by FY26, ROE 11%→14.28%) is growth-oriented, though incremental returns are diluted by NIM slipping from ~3.3% to 2.88%.
scores.quote: We directly don't take any capex. Basically, we do a lending for the state government entities who do the capex

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotion spend in any of the calls.
No R&D discussion whatsoever across the seven calls.
No acquisitions discussed; MOUs with states are lending agreements, not M&A.
Only a single passing reference to a modest dividend increase, with no buybacks and no articulated distribution policy over the period.
scores.quote: We had raised our dividend bar from 38.5% to 41.5%.

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy balance-sheet lender with rising leverage (debt/equity 4x to 5.93x) earning a thin ~2% spread, the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: If you see our debt equity ratio, it is only 5.93x.

scores.rationale: Sanctions rose from INR25,000cr (FY23) to INR1.27 lakh cr (FY25) and the book grew ~30% off a small base in a vast infra-financing market, evidencing real share capture with runway.
scores.quote: if you see our loan book, it is not so -- the volumes are not so high, and there are ample opportunities to fund big projects

scores.rationale: Credible domestic state-by-state expansion — intensively active in 12-13 states with new INR1 lakh cr+ MOUs signed with Gujarat and Bihar and outreach into the Northeast — though it is purely within India.
scores.quote: Presently, we are more intensively working in around 12, 13 states, and some of the states were not in that kind of bigger capital-intensive projects.

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely volume/balance-sheet led while pricing deteriorated — NIM fell from 3.3% guidance to 2.88% in 9M FY26 and spread is capped at ~2% with competitors cutting rates.
scores.quote: We have seen them falling to around 2.88% in 9 months of FY '26

scores.rationale: Positioned into a favourable turn — RBI cut 100bps lowering funding cost to 6.32%, and state allocations rose ~33% to INR2 lakh crore, both cyclical tailwinds ahead.
scores.quote: we had borrowed around INR20,000 Crore at around 6.32%... thanks to the RBI for reducing this 100 basis points

scores.rationale: End market is in clear secular expansion — Indian urban population projected to double over 20 years with dedicated central programmes (Urban Challenge Fund, SASCI, AMRUT 2.0) funding it.
scores.quote: presently, if it is 40 crores of the urban population, it will be doubled in the next 20 years

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with no M&A and conservative asset quality, but leverage climbed from ~4x to ~6x and an out-of-policy FCNR/CHF exposure produced a INR470cr mark-to-market loss, denting the stewardship record.
scores.quote: The total loss on FCNR for 9 months is INR470 crores.

scores.rationale: Multi-year targets set in 2024 were largely delivered — the INR1.5 lakh cr FY26 book guidance was beaten — and the INR3 lakh cr by 2030 goal has been held consistently, though direction is heavily set by its administrative ministry.
scores.quote: you had guided for INR1,50,000 crores by FY '26, but you've crossed INR1,55,000 crores already

scores.rationale: Typical PSU management style, but commentary leans promotional with repeated emphasis on Navratna/Maharatna status and 'outperforming expectations' rather than pure substance.
scores.quote: we are continually outperforming the expectations of our investors and their stakeholders

scores.rationale: No talent-development or succession discussion in any call, and the five-year history shows four chairmen exiting between FY21 and FY24 under government rotation, indicating no controllable internal pipeline.
scores.quote: Chairman: Kuldip Narayan (FY2023–FY2024, exited)

scores.rationale: Owned the forex mistake explicitly and quantified it, corrected an analyst's understated loss figure upward, and gave specific numeric guidance rather than deflecting.
scores.quote: now we have learned our lessons... Actually, it is not INR360 crores, it is INR470 crores.

scores.rationale: Strong headline growth is hard to separate from the policy tailwind — sanctions surge, sovereign-guaranteed borrowers and RBI rate cuts drive results more than demonstrable managerial skill, and margins actually compressed.
scores.quote: All these things are happening, one, because of the opportunity which is available in the market.

scores.rationale: Holds a defensible niche in counterpart funding of central schemes that banks avoid, plus a 55-year consultancy-plus-lending relationship with states that competitors do not replicate.
scores.quote: There are some forte where only HUDCO can fund... Generally, these kind of products didn't work well with the bankers.

scores.rationale: State borrowers face negligible switching costs and openly shop between lenders, with no captive aftermarket or regional exclusivity.
scores.quote: there's a steep competition for financing state like Bihar from NABARD, NaBFID, Commercial Banks and the rate of interest has also gone down so much

scores.rationale: Not a stable oligopoly — it competes with banks, NaBFID and NABARD for the same state projects, and the end customer (state governments) clearly holds the negotiating power on rates.
scores.quote: you are entering a space crowded by aggressive commercial banks and other NBFCs

scores.rationale: Low barriers with a new state-backed entrant (NaBFID) and visible rate-based competition compressing pricing to a ~2% spread ceiling.
scores.quote: our spreads will remain around 2% and our NIMs will be around 3%

scores.rationale: The named competitors are strong, well-capitalised institutions rather than weak share donators, and management frames the dynamic as collaboration rather than displacing weak rivals.
scores.quote: we are working with the banks... it is not like that there is only the completion. It is the collaboration also.

scores.rationale: It does occupy a niche banks ignore (scheme counterpart funding), but it is a listed Navratna PSU with regular broker-hosted calls and open Maharatna ambitions — not under the radar.
scores.quote: recently we had been conferred with the Navratna. This is one of the most prestigious status

scores.rationale: Sells an undifferentiated commodity (money) at an administered ~2% spread with no image- or taste-driven pricing power, and yields fell as competitors cut rates.
scores.quote: the rate of interest has also gone down so much

scores.rationale: Borrowers accept HUDCO's spread on the strength of its 55-year track record and 360-degree project support rather than on price alone.
scores.quote: 2% is the spread, which is well acknowledged by our borrowers

scores.rationale: Genuine accessibility edge — regional offices originating projects directly with ULBs and states, plus the 'urban invest window' one-stop platform spanning project creation, bankability, financial closure and lending.
scores.quote: we have launched a very big platform... urban invest window, which will become a one-stop solution for -- from creation of the projects to make it bankable, financial closures

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely institutional (state governments, ULBs) and HUDCO matches this with reliability and policy-alignment benefits, but without the switching-cost lock-in that would make the corporate match strong.
scores.quote: over 70% of our book is either guaranteed by state or through budget provisions

scores.rationale: No technology capability or R&D intensity discussed anywhere in the calls.
The urban invest window is a service aggregation platform, not a self-reinforcing two-sided network; nothing strengthens with scale in a compounding way.
scores.quote: urban invest window, which will become a one-stop solution

scores.rationale: Management cites state-wide regional office reach and depth of policy understanding as the reason it wins business banks cannot, and it converts MOUs into sanctions through those offices.
scores.quote: because of our reach and penetration across the states and the understanding of their policies

scores.rationale: Sustained, rising growth capex — Pune plant acquired and commissioned, phased expansion to 320k units and >1.1mn total by 2030, with FY27 capex guided at a record INR 7,500 crores.
scores.quote: Our growth ambition plans will be fuelled by aggressive investments of approximately INR 7,500 crores in fiscal '27, marking the highest ever capex in recent years.

scores.rationale: A&P is purposeful rather than discount-led — ICC partnership plus targeted rural marketing drove record rural penetration, while promotional discounts were deliberately restrained at 3.2% of ASP.
scores.quote: Hyundai's partnership with ICC marked a significant step which enhanced customer centricity by driving deeper engagement, leading to greater visibility.

scores.rationale: R&D output is visible and commercially productive — 26 products by FY2030, dual-cylinder CNG, Creta EV, a localized dedicated EV, plus the HTWO hydrogen centre with IIT Madras — though core platform R&D sits with the Korean parent.
scores.quote: we recently unveiled the design of the Hyundai HTWO Innovation Centre – a state-of-the-art Research & Development hub

scores.rationale: The only inorganic move across the period was the small, simple, complementary Pune (Talegaon) plant purchase to add capacity, now producing engines and vehicles — no large or diversifying M&A.
scores.quote: last year we acquired the Pune plant. So, after the operation of this third plant, our capacity will reach 1.1 million units.

scores.rationale: Management promised a benchmarked dividend policy at IPO and delivered a coherent 31.4% payout (INR 21/share) by FY26, but there are no buybacks or valuation-sensitive distribution.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR 21 per share for fiscal '26, which translates to a payout ratio of 31.4%

scores.rationale: This is a capital-heavy three-plant automaker whose new capacity immediately depressed returns via depreciation, labour and factory overheads — the opposite of an asset-light model.
scores.quote: with the start of production at Pune plant, obviously, we are looking at some incremental costs, especially in terms of depreciation, labor costs and factory overheads

scores.rationale: Domestic volumes fell for five of six quarters and management conceded share loss in Vahan data, framing the new Venue only as the point at which they stop losing share.
scores.quote: we believe very strongly that this is the time when we will start, kind of, not losing market share

scores.rationale: Exports grew 13% then 21.5% and finished FY26 up 16.4% versus 7-8% guidance, with diversification into Africa, Mexico and Latin America offsetting Red Sea/Middle East disruption and HMIL made global manufacturer for the new Venue.
scores.quote: This enabled us to register a growth of 16.4%, significantly outperforming our initial guidance of 7% to 8%.

scores.rationale: With volumes flat-to-down, growth and margins came almost entirely from mix and price — SUV penetration to a record 71%, CNG 13%→18%, rising sunroof/ADAS trims, and repeated calibrated price increases while refusing the industry price war.
scores.quote: Post-GST, some OEMs cut the price over and above the GST cut. We refrained from doing that.

scores.rationale: The company traversed a clear cyclical trough (June 2025 lowest TIV in 30 months) into a GST 2.0-led upturn, ending with record Q4 domestic volumes and 8-10% FY27 guidance, so the cycle turn is now partly behind rather than ahead.
scores.quote: June was the lowest TIV in the last 30 months... we have every reason to believe that the worst is behind us

scores.rationale: The Indian PV market has genuine secular drivers — SUVization, rural penetration rising to 24%, early-stage electrification and the parent calling India its global strategy — though the period itself showed the market is cyclical, not steadily expanding.
scores.quote: India is not just important to Hyundai's Global Strategy, India is Hyundai's Global Strategy.

scores.rationale: Growth is fully organic and counter-cyclical — commissioning the Pune plant and committing record capex during the industry's worst demand phase — while holding discounting discipline and refusing to chase volume.
scores.quote: Right from the IPO time, we have maintained that we believe in quality of sales. We believe in the balance between volume and profit.

scores.rationale: Thirty years of operations, Creta holding the No.1 mid-SUV position every year since 2015, a published 2030 roadmap of 26 products, and the independence to abstain from a sector-wide price war evidence long-term tenacity.
scores.quote: the Hyundai CRETA continues to lead from the front, maintaining its undisputed No.1 position in the country every completed year since its launch

scores.rationale: Commentary is professional and substance-heavy rather than personality-driven, but the company is a high-profile recent IPO with an Investor Day headlined by the Global CEO and a marquee ICC cricket sponsorship, so it is hardly out of the limelight.
scores.quote: Our Global CEO's participation reinforced HMC's unwavering confidence in India's potential

scores.rationale: Top Employer recognition, a three-year union wage settlement described as an industry benchmark, and a demonstrated internal pipeline — COO Tarun Garg elevated to MD & CEO by FY26 — show systematic talent development.
scores.quote: we concluded the wage settlement agreement with the recognized Union for the period 2024–2027 which sets a new benchmark in the automotive industry

scores.rationale: Management gives quantified margin bridges (bps by driver), discloses discount levels, separates one-offs, and openly admits bad news such as market-share loss and persisting commodity headwinds.
scores.quote: near-term, the commodity headwinds are expected to continue. I think we need to admit that.

scores.rationale: Genuine skill is visible in localization (78%→82%), mix and export execution, but much of the good news came from exogenous factors — GST 2.0, parent product/technology and export tailwinds — while the Q4 margin drop to 10.4% shows results are not purely management-driven.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 10.4% as compared to 14.1% in Q4 financial year '25

scores.rationale: Creta owns a monopoly-like position in the customer's mind, with the segment itself named after the product, though this is a single-model franchise rather than a company-wide position.
scores.quote: the mid-size SUV segment is now often referred to as the "CRETA segment" in the country

scores.rationale: Passenger vehicles carry negligible switching costs and no regional exclusivity — buyers moved on price and GST-driven affordability, and Hyundai openly lost share during a weak model cycle.
scores.quote: we have seen some dip in market share, at least in the Vahan data

scores.rationale: The Indian PV market is crowded and price-competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, with rivals passing through and exceeding GST cuts and heavy discounting forcing margin pressure.
scores.quote: the industry has been giving further price cuts over and above the GST cuts

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour in the sector is irrational — an explicit price war that Hyundai had to consciously abstain from — and discounts rose to defend volumes, indicating weak competitive discipline.
scores.quote: if you would have seen like the competition where there was a lot of price war happening, we were able to not join that price war

scores.rationale: There are structurally declining hatchback/sedan-heavy players whose customers are shifting to SUVs, but over this period Hyundai was the donator rather than the recipient of share.
scores.quote: Hatchback continued to witness decline in line with industry trend

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — a recent large IPO, an Investor Day with the Global CEO, an ICC sponsorship and coverage by Citi, Nomura, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan.
scores.quote: we are pleased to announce that HMI will be hosting its first ever Investor Day on the 15th of October 2025

scores.rationale: The brand supports aspirational, feature-led pricing (sunroof, ADAS, premium editions) and enough pricing power to avoid the price war, but auto gross margins and 3.2%-of-ASP discounts fall well short of true intangible-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: sunroof penetration in first half of last year '23-24 was 47.4%. It has moved to 53%... The ADAS has moved up from 3.3% to 14.4%

scores.rationale: Trust and reliability are central to the proposition — a 30-year household brand, decade-long Creta leadership and a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating on the new Venue — though customers still respond strongly to price and GST cuts.
scores.quote: the all-new Venue has secured 5-star safety rating under Bharat NCAP testing

scores.rationale: Deliberate accessibility investment — white-space outlet additions lifting rural penetration to a record ~24% and 100 dealerships fitted with 60kW DC fast chargers — though reach still trails the market leader.
scores.quote: we continue to unlock white spaces by expanding our network through strategic outlet additions... highest-ever rural penetration of 23%

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail and the benefit set is correctly matched to it — aspirational features, design awards, safety ratings and brand engagement rather than TCO/corporate lock-in.
scores.quote: we are adding more and more value to the customer so that this effort towards ASP increase continues

scores.rationale: A credible multi-powertrain edge (dual-cylinder CNG driving penetration from 11.4% to 18%, ADAS democratization, EV localization, hydrogen and an AI roadmap) that comfortably clears CAFE, but the underlying technology is largely sourced from the parent.
scores.quote: quarter one CAFE, our target was 117.286. Actual is 112.856. So, we have achieved CAFE very comfortably

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing across a two-sided network; growth comes from plants, products and dealer additions, and the EV charging tie-up is an outsourced third-party arrangement.
scores.quote: By engaging in a strategic partnership with a local charge point operator, we are moving towards strengthening HMIL's EV charging network

scores.rationale: Distribution is expanding methodically into rural white spaces and delivering record penetration, but it is a competitive dealer network that rivals — notably the far larger market leader — can and do match.
scores.quote: Our focused efforts in terms of channel expansion and deeper market penetration... reaching a record high of nearly 24%

scores.rationale: As an asset-light AMC, growth investment is in distribution/geographic footprint rather than plant — GIFT City retail FME branch, DIFC Dubai office, 300+ towns — and incremental returns are very high (ROE ~86-88%), though absolute capex is small and undisclosed.
scores.quote: We have established retail FME branch presence in GIFT City... We have established presence in DIFC Dubai and have received requisite approval to commence operations.

scores.rationale: A dedicated Chief Marketing and Digital Business Officer and ongoing investment in the Choti SIP/daily SIP initiative show promotional intent, but no A&P quantum, efficiency or brand-equity evidence is given.
scores.quote: We are investing in it through various partners... it's a very nascent and initial trend, but we are continuing to invest in it.

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but consistent product innovation (four iSIF strategies launched within two quarters, balanced advantage category creation, GIFT City inbound fund) and a proprietary AI investment platform show reinvestment that is already yielding new products and customers.
scores.quote: There are seven investment strategies permitted, of which we have launched four investment strategies.

scores.rationale: The only deal is a small, simple bolt-on — transfer of investment management rights for certain ICICI Venture AIFs, explicitly complementary to the existing alternates bouquet — but it is a related-party transfer and post-deal margin impact is not yet demonstrable (alternates are only ~8.5% of net revenue).
scores.quote: the product bouquet that we get from Venture is totally complementary to what we already have in the alternate

scores.rationale: Large, regular dividends (INR14.85 interim and INR12.4 final per share) consistent with an asset-light, near-zero-reinvestment model, but no buyback and no articulated distribution policy or valuation discipline was discussed.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors have declared a final dividend of INR12.4 per share

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-light economics — 85.8% ROE for FY26 on INR11 trillion of AUM with only 3,585 employees, and operating margin rising to 37.6 bps from 35.9 bps — combined with a #1 equity market share moat.
scores.quote: The return on equity for the year ended March 2026 is at 85.8%.

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of share capture — equity share up to 14.2% at Mar-26, net flow share exceeding AUM share, and 7 of 10 new industry customers in Q1FY27 — but as the #1 equity AMC and #2 overall the remaining runway to gain share is limited.
scores.quote: Notably in this quarter, we added every seven of 10 new customers from the industry.

scores.rationale: Credible, capital-light expansion into GIFT City (first inbound fund launched and gaining traction) and DIFC Dubai with a dedicated team, plus 300+ domestic towns, though management refuses to size the opportunity and results are not yet material.
scores.quote: we have launched our first offering in GIFT City, the ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund... it is encouraging to see that the fund is gaining traction

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely volume/AUM- and mark-to-market-led while realisation is flat-to-falling — equity margin slipped from 67 to 66 bps and SEBI's TER slab cut plus fast-growing 9-12 bps passives dilute mix; pricing is regulated, not a lever.
scores.quote: our margins on an annualized basis stands at 66 basis points for equity... 12 basis points for passives

scores.rationale: The company was reporting through a genuine cyclical trough — 18 months of subdued equity returns and a 14.5% Nifty fall in Q4FY26 — followed by an identifiable upturn with small-caps +24% and flows rebounding 26% MoM in June 2026.
scores.quote: it is now 18 months where the equity markets are subdued, but the flows are on

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — industry AUM tripled in five years to INR83 lakh crore, unique investors up 12-13% YoY to 6.2 crore, and SIP contributions rising through a market drawdown — driven by financialisation of Indian savings.
scores.quote: mutual fund industry has seen a robust growth over the last five years with the industry AUM growing threefold

scores.rationale: Growth is organic and self-funded with no leverage discussed, the only inorganic step is a small complementary AIF rights transfer, and management resists chasing euphoric flows, preferring skeptical buyers.
scores.quote: I always like an environment where the customer is slightly asking more questions before investing... It is not happening based on euphoria.

scores.rationale: Nimesh Shah, MD since well before listing, consistently frames new businesses on a multi-year horizon and points to pioneering balanced advantage funds as a long-held conviction rather than a fashion.
scores.quote: This -- one should see this as a long-term, this one. I am not looking at it as a short-term 1 or 2 years. Let us show performance for 2, 3 years first.

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly declines to publicise targets or hype new launches (SIF, Dubai, GIFT City) and defers to results over promotion, an understated posture in its first year as a listed company.
scores.quote: We are not putting any number out as to what is the number that we are going to raise from it. Let us see what is the response to those products from the market.

scores.rationale: Evidence of talent investment and decentralised empowerment — headcount grew to 3,585, a sizeable ESOP/ESU grant (INR1.2-1.3 billion) vesting over three years, and branch expansion decisions delegated to regional heads — though no explicit succession or leadership-pipeline discussion.
scores.quote: the expansion happens at his discretion at the ground level... All these decisions are taken at a very regional level.

scores.rationale: Management is straightforward about what it does not know — refusing to quantify Dubai or SIF, admitting TER impact is still being worked out, disclosing ESOP P&L drag by year, and calling Choti SIP viability too early to judge — but stops short of discussing any mistakes.
scores.quote: The large size fund might have a bigger impact as compared to the smaller size fund. We are working to see how all of this would work out

scores.rationale: Reported 86-88% ROE and 20%+ growth are substantially a function of a tripling industry and mark-to-market, and management itself concedes it is a passenger on industry flows, so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: the way we look at business is what is the industry doing and what of the industry is coming to us as ICICI Prudential?

scores.rationale: A near-monopoly mindshare in the hybrid/balanced-advantage niche it created — 26.6-26.7% market share, roughly double its overall share — positions it as the default 'defensive' AMC in investors' minds.
scores.quote: the largest market share of 26.7%... So we have always advocated that if you cannot take volatility, you should mix equity and debt

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real but modest — sticky SIP/STP books (INR4,872 crore monthly) with capital-gains tax and exit-load friction, and flows that held through an 18-month drawdown — yet investors can and do redirect SIPs across fund houses.
scores.quote: Monthly SIP inflows remained largely stable throughout Q1 despite volatile market conditions demonstrating the resilience and stickiness of retail investor participation.

scores.rationale: The industry is concentrated at the top (ICICI Pru is #2 at 13.4%) but there are 40+ AMCs, pricing is set by the regulator rather than the players, and end customers face no negotiating friction in moving money.
scores.quote: maintaining our position as the second largest AMC with a market share of 13.4%

scores.rationale: Pricing is neither rational nor defended by the industry — SEBI cut TER slabs, exit loads and brokerage limits effective April 2026, and the fastest-growing passive segment earns only 9-12 bps, indicating structural fee erosion rather than pricing discipline.
scores.quote: One is with respect to the exit load, the 5 basis point. The second one is with respect to the cut in the expenses. And the third are the rationalization of the brokerage limit

scores.rationale: The company consistently takes share from weaker AMCs — its equity AUM grew 2% QoQ against an industry decline in Q4FY26 and 19.8% YoY versus industry, and it captured 70% of new industry customers in Q1FY27.
scores.quote: we outperformed the industry growth rate by 3.6% recording a growth of 19.8%

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a newly listed, second-largest AMC holding the #1 equity share, covered by mainstream media on quarterly calls, in a sector actively attracting new capital and entrants.
scores.quote: A warm welcome to our first earnings conference call as a listed company.

scores.rationale: The brand carries a distinct 'defensive AMC' image that supports demand precisely when markets are uncertain, and equity realisation has held near 66-67 bps with gross-margin-like operating margins expanding, though pricing is ultimately capped by SEBI.
scores.quote: And our AMC has been always positioned as a relatively defensive AMC.

scores.rationale: The proposition sold is certainty and risk control rather than the lowest fee — repeated emphasis on risk-adjusted returns and volatility-calibrated product laddering — and flows stayed with the fund house through an 18-month drawdown.
scores.quote: These market positions serve as a testament to our ongoing commitment to achieving risk-adjusted returns for our customers.

scores.rationale: Strong accessibility across a balanced multi-channel footprint — 300+ towns, 95.7% of purchases digital, an AI natural-language search handling 5 million queries and AI answering 60% of email queries — with no single-channel dependence.
scores.quote: 95.7% of our total mutual fund purchase transactions were executed across digital platforms

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to a predominantly retail base — 1.73 crore unique customers served with trust, brand and systematic-investing habit rather than institutional price negotiation — while the institutional debt book proved fickle, redeeming 6% sequentially.
scores.quote: we would continue to focus on retail growth specifically through systematic transactions

scores.rationale: A credible, multi-front AI/digital build across customer experience, operations and investment management, but it is applied efficiency rather than a deep proprietary edge rivals cannot replicate, and no R&D intensity is disclosed.
scores.quote: our goal is frictionless. Today, a customer can use our natural language search engine on our website, which has already processed over 5 million queries.

scores.rationale: Scale brings distributor and customer breadth but nothing self-reinforcing is described — the flywheel cited is past performance attracting flows, not a two-sided network that strengthens with each participant.
scores.quote: if you're managing money properly and if your customers have made returns out of your funds, they do invest again in the same funds

scores.rationale: A genuinely hard-to-replicate reach — a deliberately diversified mix (MFDs 36.2%, national distributors 15.9%, banks 18.4%, direct 29.5%) across 300+ towns with only 7.7% dependence on parent ICICI Bank, producing net flow share above AUM share.
scores.quote: MFDs accounts for 36.2%, national distributors accounts for 15.9%, ICICI Bank share at 7.7%, other banks contributing 10.7%, and direct representing 29.5%

scores.rationale: Sustained growth-oriented spend on branches (6,587 in Jun-2024 to 7,511 by Mar-2026, 528 added in the last 12 months), technology (8.5% of opex in FY2022 rising to ~11% in 9M-FY2026) and distribution, with standalone RoE still ~15.5% and RoA 2.3%.
scores.quote: We will continue to make investments in technology, people, distribution and building our brand.

scores.rationale: Brand building is repeatedly named as an investment priority across all four calls but is never quantified or linked to measurable brand equity or sales outcomes.
scores.quote: building our brand... upholds the values of brand ICICI

scores.rationale: Technology spend rising from ~8.5% to ~11% of opex has produced a steady stream of new platforms that demonstrably acquire customers and volumes (7.3 million iMobile Pay activations by non-ICICI holders, 120,000 non-ICICI InstaBIZ registrations, SmartLock, OneSCF, 20+ industry STACKs), though it is process/product tech rather than proprietary R&D.
scores.quote: The Bank has launched an industry-first initiative 'SmartLock'... The technology expenses were about 11% of our operating expenses

scores.rationale: No acquisition is discussed in any of the excerpts; subsidiaries are referenced only for results reporting.

A coherent, stated distribution philosophy ('Return of Capital' added as a guiding principle) with a Rs 12/share FY2026 dividend and capital kept strong at 16.35% CET-1, but no buyback and therefore no evidence of valuation-timed repurchase discipline.
scores.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of ■12 per share for FY2026... The principles of "Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank", "One Bank, One Team" and "Return of Capital" will guide our operations.

scores.rationale: A bank is structurally the opposite of asset-light — returns come from a leveraged Rs 3.4 lakh crore net-worth balance sheet earning a ~4.3% NIM and 2.3% RoA — though a genuine low-cost deposit moat partly offsets the capital intensity.
scores.quote: At March 31, 2026, the Bank had net worth of about ■3.4 lakh crore... Return on average assets and standalone RoE would have been 2.3% and 15.5%

scores.rationale: Explicit share-gain ambition backed by above-system growth in chosen segments over the period (business banking +44.7% in FY23, +35.6% in FY25, +24.4% in FY26; total loans +15.8% in FY26), though deposit growth decelerated to 9-11% and cards shrank, so share capture is segment-selective rather than broad.
scores.quote: we see many opportunities to drive risk calibrated profitable growth and grow market share across key segments

scores.rationale: The international book was deliberately shrunk from 5.1% of loans (Jun-2022) to 2.4% (Dec-2025) with non-India corporate exposure run down, so geographic expansion is domestic branch densification plus a nascent NRI app rather than a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: The overseas loan portfolio was 2.4% of the overall loan book at December 31, 2025... We have also launched iMobile Global, a unified banking app for NRI customers.

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/balance-sheet led while price is competed away — NIM fell from 4.78% (Q1-FY24) to 4.30-4.32%, management concedes mortgage price competition and says pricing must be found within competition, with revenue and profit growth in single digits in FY2026.
scores.quote: No, it is a competitive environment and within the competition, you have to find the right price.

scores.rationale: The bank appears past the trough of the rate/margin cycle — NIM stabilised at 4.30% then ticked to 4.32%, provisions collapsed to Rs 96 crore in Q4-FY2026, and loan growth re-accelerated from 11.5% to 15.8% year-on-year with management flagging sustained momentum.
scores.quote: certainly there has been a pickup in momentum. And we see that momentum sustaining into the fourth q[uarter]

scores.rationale: Indian credit demand is a secularly expanding end market, which management ties directly to economic activity, and the bank has compounded loans through the whole 2022-2026 window despite rate and geopolitical shocks.
scores.quote: the advances reflect the strong momentum of economic activity in the country which has been supported by policy measures and a fairly stable policy rate

scores.rationale: Four years of purely organic, risk-calibrated growth with counter-cyclical buffers built ahead of need (contingency provisions raised from Rs 85bn to Rs 131bn and deliberately not utilised even in a weak quarter), CET-1 held at 16%+, and non-India corporate risk run down.
scores.quote: We have also not utilised the contingency provisions... we are very careful about our asset quality

scores.rationale: The identical strategic framework — risk-calibrated core operating profit, 360-degree customer, ecosystems and micro-markets — is repeated verbatim from Jul-2022 to Apr-2026 and management explicitly refuses to chase growth targets or forecast, sticking to the framework through the margin downcycle.
scores.quote: Mahrukh, we don't target any particular level of loan growth

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key, process-driven commentary with an explicit humility value, no personality-led narrative across four years, and off-topic publicity questions politely declined.
scores.quote: We focus on building a culture where every employee in the Bank serves customers with humility

scores.rationale: Recurring evidence of systematic talent investment — reorganisation into city business heads, cross-functional skilling, ESOPs granted to all employees, ~7,250 net hires in a year — and a stable named leadership bench (Batra, Rakesh, Ajay, Anindya, Abhinek) present on calls throughout.
scores.quote: We have also focused on strengthening the workforce by skilling and providing cross-functional opportunities.

scores.rationale: Generally high disclosure quality — they voluntarily normalise for one-offs (AIF release, KCC seasonality, the Rs 12.83bn RBI provision) and size the affected agri portfolio at Rs 200-250bn — but they declined to explain what was actually non-compliant and deflected the Iran-payments question, so ownership of the lapse is incomplete.
scores.quote: those are really observations made by the regulator as part of its inspection process. So, we wouldn't want to go into those details

scores.rationale: Caution is warranted: FY2026 profit growth was single-digit and Q4 PAT was flattered by provisions falling ~90% to Rs 96 crore on written-off-account recoveries rather than core earnings, and an RBI supervisory finding surfaced, so recent results reflect cycle and provision release as much as durable skill.
scores.quote: Provisions (excluding provision for tax) were ■96 crore in Q4-2026... certain corporate recoveries which have come from written-off accounts

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position is evidenced; the bank competes for the same customers as peers and its aspiration is to be the customer's chosen provider rather than an unavoidable one.
scores.quote: We aim to be the trusted financial services provider of choice for our customers

scores.rationale: Real switching-cost lock-in is pursued through primary-banker status and embedded corporate rails (current accounts, OneSCF/CorpConnect supply-chain platforms, API-based collections), reflected in average current account deposits growing consistently.
scores.quote: we are just focussed on money in the Bank... try to become the primary banker, and try to get a good share of customer's wallet

scores.rationale: Indian banking is concentrated among a few large players, but the calls repeatedly describe two-sided price competition in deposits, mortgages and corporate lending, so end-customer negotiating power is real and pricing is not oligopolistic.
scores.quote: there is a price competition the other way and we are seeing fair amount of competition particularly on the corporate side

scores.rationale: Bank licensing, capital and now heavy compliance costs (rising PSL certificate costs, LCR rules, RBI supervisory reviews) are formidable entry barriers with no new entrants mentioned in four years, but pricing rationality is imperfect given aggressive mortgage and corporate price competition.
scores.quote: the cost of PSL compliance has been going up. We do meet a part of our PSL obligations by buying the priority sector lending certificates, and the cost of those has steadily gone up

scores.rationale: Management asserts share-gain runway across key segments but never identifies weaker competitors ceding ground, and its own deposit growth of 9-11% suggests it is also losing ground on funding.
scores.quote: we see many opportunities to drive risk calibrated profitable growth and grow market share across key segments

scores.rationale: Brand ICICI is invoked as a value system rather than a pricing lever, and the admission that price must be found within competition shows image does not confer pricing power in a commoditised product.
scores.quote: it is a competitive environment and within the competition, you have to find the right price

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty — safety, liquidity, provisioning and operational resilience — and it converts into a funding cost advantage, which is the purest form of trust pricing for a bank.
scores.quote: Our cost of deposits continues to be among the lowest in the system.

scores.rationale: Accessibility is exceptional and still compounding — 7,511 branches and 12,087 ATMs at Mar-2026 after adding 528 branches in a year, alongside iMobile/InstaBIZ/Money2India digital reach and micro-market/city-business-head coverage that puts relationship managers close to customers.
scores.quote: The Bank opened 126 branches during Q4-2026 and 528 branches in the last 12 months and had a network of 7,511 branches and 12,087 ATMs

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — convenience and trust for the ~42-46% retail book, and TCO/workflow lock-in for corporates via supply-chain and API platforms — all organised under an explicit 360-degree total-relationship model.
scores.quote: we look at customers on a 360-degree angle and a total relationship value

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-product digital depth funded by rising tech intensity (8.5% to ~11% of opex) with measurable customer benefit — end-to-end digital sanctions, 71% of trade transactions digital, industry-first features — but it is deployment strength rather than a defensible proprietary technology edge over peers.
scores.quote: About 71% of trade transactions were done digitally in Q1-2025.

scores.rationale: Real but modest two-sided effects exist where platforms are opened to non-customers and to corporate ecosystems — 7.3 million iMobile Pay activations by non-ICICI holders, 120,000 non-ICICI InstaBIZ registrations, and supply-chain platforms linking corporates with their vendors and dealers.
scores.quote: a one-stop solution... providing corporate customers, their vendors and dealers... We have seen about 120,000 registrations from non-ICICI Bank account holders on InstaBIZ

scores.rationale: Distribution is the strongest and most durable advantage — a 7,511-branch, 12,087-ATM physical network expanding by ~500 branches a year, layered with digital platforms and micro-market/ecosystem coverage that only two or three rivals in India can approach.
scores.quote: our focus on customer 360 degree, extensive franchise and collaboration within the organisation, backed by our focus on enhancing delivery systems

scores.rationale: Insurance is asset-light so 'capex' shows up as distribution and technology build-out — sustained hiring of health agency managers (750→1,101) and in-house platform builds like IL OneForce, which have translated into measurable returns (retail health up 51.1% in FY2026, 2x agent activation).
scores.quote: IL OneForce is an enterprise productivity platform, which has been in operation for over a year and is used by over 10,000 sales employees

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend, brand campaigns, or A&P efficiency anywhere in the excerpts.

No formal R&D line, but consistent product/technology innovation is evidenced — telematics 'Pay as You Drive' products from the sandbox era, long-term retail health products (long-term share of new business 28.5%→42.1%→53.4%), and an AI/technology chief in senior management.
scores.quote: This performance has been driven by ongoing product innovation and sustained investment in strengthening our retail health distribution franchise.

scores.rationale: The only M&A is the pre-period Bharti AXA merger, whose distribution synergies were realised (non-ICICI Bank banca +65.1%), but it was a large, not bolt-on, deal and no further acquisitions have occurred across the five years.
scores.quote: the new Bancassurance tie ups that we've got through the merger with Bharti AXA), has grown really well

scores.rationale: A steady, rising dividend policy (₹11 FY2024 → ₹12.50 FY2025 → ₹13.50 FY2026) alongside solvency comfortably above regulation, but no buybacks and no explicit valuation-linked distribution framework.
scores.quote: The overall dividend for FY2026, including the proposed final dividend is ₹13.50 per share. Last year, the overall dividend was ₹12.50 per share.

scores.rationale: Asset-light float model with investment leverage of ~3.5–4.2x and a 10-year average ROE of 19.1% versus industry 4.0%, though the underwriting moat is only partial (combined ratio still ~102-103%).
scores.quote: average Return on Equity of 19.1% over the 10-year period, which would compare favourably with the industry average (ROE) of 4.0%

scores.rationale: Consistent outperformance in chosen retail segments — retail health share 3.3%→4.1%→4.5% and health growth 20.0% vs industry 15.4% — but overall FY2026 GDPI growth of 7.0% lagged the industry's 9.2% as commercial lines were ceded on pricing discipline.
scores.quote: our market share has improved to 4.5% in Q1FY2027 from 3.5% in Q1FY2026

scores.rationale: Business is entirely India-domestic; an 'International' title appears in the leadership roster but no geographic expansion strategy, results, or plans are discussed.

Pricing power is weak and largely outside management control — motor TP rates are regulator-set and lag inflation, commercial lines saw fire de-grow 27.8% on price cuts, so growth is driven by volume/mix shift into retail health rather than price.
scores.quote: the rise is not commensurate with the loss experience and inflation that the industry has envisaged in this segment

scores.rationale: Mixed cycle position — motor has clear tailwinds post-GST rationalisation with a needed TP rate hike ahead, but commercial/fire is in a soft-pricing downcycle with April 2026 renewals at discounts and no visible turn.
scores.quote: an upward revision of Motor TP premium rates becomes both necessary and urgent in order to restore premium adequacy

scores.rationale: Indian general insurance is a structurally under-penetrated market with health the fastest-growing segment for five straight years and regulatory reforms (Use & File, EOM, Public Insurance Registry) actively expanding the addressable market.
scores.quote: The Health segment, including Mass Health, grew by 15.4% for FY2026, which makes it the fastest growing segment for the last 5 years

scores.rationale: Repeatedly walked away from unprofitable growth — capping crop exposure, de-growing commercial lines 13.8% amid price wars, holding solvency at ~2.6-2.7x versus a 1.5x requirement, with no leverage-funded M&A.
scores.quote: we witnessed a de-growth of 13.8% for the period ended Q1FY2027 in this segment

scores.rationale: Multi-year investments were pre-announced and then executed through the cycle — health agency build-out from 2022, a five-year digital team build before joining Policy Bazaar, and a 10-year average combined ratio of 102.9% vs industry 115.3%.
scores.quote: We are also build teams almost 5 years back that we have created virtual an organization an organization with an intense focus to drive our digital business.

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently process- and metric-led with no personality promotion; the smooth Dasgupta→Mantri MD transition and expansion of the named leadership bench point to institution-over-individual framing.
scores.quote: Our 'One IL, One Team' philosophy continues to foster collaboration and operational excellence

scores.rationale: Systematic talent build across the period — ~1,100 health agency managers hired, senior leaders added (Anand Singhi, Priya Deshmukh) with internal role rotation, 15,000+ employees onto a single performance platform, and explicit commitment to nurturing and retention.
scores.quote: talent acquisition, nurturing and retention

scores.rationale: Consistently quantifies bad news and its own underperformance without spin — flagging the ₹1.65bn Supreme Court TP hit, the ₹0.63bn fire losses, the 46% PAT decline, and openly stating growth below industry.
scores.quote: The Company reported a growth of 7.0% in Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI), for FY2026 compared to the industry growth of 9.2%

scores.rationale: Results survive a skill-vs-luck test — the motor combined-ratio gap versus industry widened from 10.3% in FY2020 to 21.4% in FY2026 through varied conditions, though a share of profit comes from investment income and the parent-bank distribution advantage rather than pure underwriting skill.
scores.quote: this differential outperformance between the Industry and ICICI Lombard Combined Ratios for Motor insurance stood at 10.3% in FY2020 which has further widened to 21.4% in FY2026

scores.rationale: Holds named leadership niches in Liability, Marine Cargo and Engineering and a 64% EV two-wheeler share, but these are leading positions in contestable tender/price-driven lines rather than genuine monopoly-like ownership of the customer's mind.
scores.quote: We continued to maintain our leadership position in the Liability and Marine Cargo lines of business for the FY2026.

scores.rationale: Switching costs are modest — annual renewals and aggregator platforms make comparison easy — though long-term policies (53.4% of new retail health) and advance premium build some lock-in.
scores.quote: our contribution from long term book in new retail health business continues to gain traction and stood at 53.4% for Q1FY2027

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and irrational rather than a stable oligopoly — industry combined ratio deteriorated to 119.3% with fire de-growing 27.8% on rate cuts, and corporate customers hold clear negotiating power.
scores.quote: The Commercial segment reported a de-growth of 8.6% in Q1 FY2027, driven by significant pricing pressure, particularly in the Fire insurance business.

scores.rationale: Regulatory capital creates some barrier, but pricing is demonstrably irrational with sharp discount wars in fire and motor, and IRDAI's Use & File and distribution reforms are lowering entry friction.
scores.quote: the April renewal cycle witnessed exceptional competitive pricing, with rate reductions being the sharpest at the beginning of the quarter

scores.rationale: A large pool of loss-making competitors is available to take share from — industry combined ratio of 119.3% versus the company's 103.4% and industry ROE of 4.0% versus 19.1%, plus peers struggling to meet EOM limits.
scores.quote: roughly about half of the market slightly in excess of half of the market are within the threshold

scores.rationale: This is the largest private general insurer in India, listed, widely covered by brokerages and mainstream media with separate media and investor calls each quarter — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: reinforcing our leadership stance as the largest private sector general insurance player in the country

scores.rationale: The ICICI brand supports trust and retention, but there is no evidence of price premium from image — motor and fire are priced competitively and margins are thin at ~102-103% combined ratio.
scores.quote: Amidst competitive pressure, we continue to drive profitable growth through prudent underwriting and judicious risk selection

scores.rationale: The core proposition is demonstrable claims certainty — 98.8-99.0% of retail health claims paid within 30 days versus an industry 82.1%, health claims NPS of 73 and motor 69 — exactly the reliability-over-price benefit.
scores.quote: 99.9%, with the corresponding number for the industry being 82.1%

scores.rationale: Deep, multi-channel accessibility — 94,000+ agents, banca via ICICI Bank plus acquired partners, aggregators, a 22.1mn-download app handling 67-82% of claim intimations, and PPN garages servicing 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims.
scores.quote: Our 'IL TakeCare' app... achieved 21.0 million downloads as at March 31, 2026

scores.rationale: Correctly matches benefits to segment — service/assurance and app convenience for retail health and motor, TCO and risk-governance discipline for corporates — and is deliberately rotating mix toward the stickier retail and SME side (SME 28.4%→33.6%).
scores.quote: our proportion of SME business, in the commercial lines segment, has increased to 33.6% in Q1FY2027 from 28.4% in Q1FY2026

scores.rationale: Real, in-house-built technology depth — a Chief Enterprise AI & Technology role, IL OneForce, Account Aggregator adoption in motor claims, and 69% digital service engagements — but it is operational efficiency technology rather than a proprietary, hard-to-replicate multi-product edge.
scores.quote: ICICI Lombard has started the use of the Account Aggregator framework in our motor claims process

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is described; the app and PPN garage network are distribution/service assets, and no self-reinforcing scale effect is claimed or evidenced.

Distribution and service reach is the clearest durable advantage — 94,559 agents growing, ICICI Bank plus Bharti AXA-acquired banca partners, a PPN network handling 75.6% of non-OEM claims, and an IL Sahayak on-ground claims force, in a business where service at claim time is decisive.
scores.quote: Our Preferred Partner Network (PPN) serviced 75.6% of our non-OEM claims for Q1 FY2027

scores.rationale: Investment is directed at growth capacity (agency branches, digitalisation, AI/ML, brand) rather than maintenance, and it has lifted savings cost-to-premium ratios, though incremental returns are modest with FY2026 APE up only 2.2% and RoEV at 11.9%.
scores.quote: We will continue to invest in creating capacity, greater digitalisation, and improving brand awareness in order to deliver sustainable VNB growth.

scores.rationale: A&P is mentioned only as a generic line item ('improving brand awareness') with no disclosure of spend, brand-equity metrics or measured sales lift across the 18 calls.
scores.quote: greater digitalisation, and improving brand awareness

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but consistent product/process innovation (trail-commission ULIP, GPP Flexi with Benefit Enhancer, high-sum-assured ULIP, AI-led underwriting) has repeatedly translated into channel growth — offset by the industry-first 100% premium-back annuity that later caused a ₹2.64bn negative persistency variance.
scores.quote: we have also experimented with a trail-based commission on the ULIP platform where again we have seen acceptance by distributors

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in five years; the only corporate action is a divestment — the 100% sale of the pension fund subsidiary for a ₹1.14bn gain — so the parameter is neutral rather than positive.
scores.quote: a gain of ■ 1.14 billion realised from sale of 100% equity shareholding in ICICI Pension Fund Management Company

scores.rationale: Only routine dividend approval is referenced; no buybacks, no valuation-linked repurchase discipline and no articulated distribution policy anywhere in the calls.
