scores.quote: we have leveraged our brand equity to drive a 2% price increase in May 2022

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or innovation metric is discussed in any excerpt; technology is bought in (Continua+ from Sacmi Italy) rather than developed.

Bolt-ons are small, complementary and cheap — South Asian Ceramics bought at ~Rs.120cr EV versus Rs.120cr and 24 months to build greenfield, plus Keronite in Morbi and buyout of the 15% bathware minority for Rs.50cr — but acquirees were loss-making and one subsidiary later produced a fraud.
scores.quote: If we put the individual plant of this capacity anywhere in India will cost you about 100 to 120 Crores... Plus there is also a time lag of 24 months

scores.rationale: A stated, consistently applied 40-50% payout policy funded after internal-accrual capex, with dividends likely to rise as capex stops; no buybacks executed.
scores.quote: 40% to 50% of the earnings is a dividend policy

scores.rationale: Asset intensity is moderated by ~27-28% outsourced volumes and tight working capital (51 days at Mar-26), but tile manufacturing remains capital-heavy and the moat protecting it is a brand, not a structural barrier.
scores.quote: today as Kajaria, we are outsourcing to the extent of almost 27%, 28% of the materials from Morbi

scores.rationale: Long runway acknowledged by management despite being the largest player, with a history of outgrowing a flat industry — though FY26 volumes went flat during the unification disruption before recovering to +11% in Q4.
scores.quote: despite the number one company, we are -- our market share is very less

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic depth (tier-2/3 penetration, South plants to cut transit time) plus one small Nepal JV; the brand does not travel internationally as exports are explicitly not a focus.
scores.quote: At Kajaria, we don't export much. Our main focus is the domestic market

scores.rationale: Growth has been volume-led with realization falling ~9% from Rs.401/sqm in Q3FY23 to Rs.365/sqm, discounts given to clear SKUs, and the FY26 price hike was purely gas cost pass-through rather than pricing power.
scores.quote: prices of tiles are not increasing in the market with so many players there

scores.rationale: The company sits at an identifiable cyclical inflection — industry exports fell 20% and Morbi capacity shut on a gas shock, leaving Kajaria's multi-locational plants at full utilisation with an upturn beginning January 2026.
scores.quote: it's a very, very positive scenario for the so-called organized players who have multi-locational plants going forward for the whole of '26-'27

scores.rationale: End market benefits from durable drivers — GDP-linked tile demand, a Rs.10 lakh crore five-year urban housing programme, and GST-driven formalisation pushing tier-2/3 dealers toward branded players.
scores.quote: the Finance Minister has announced a Rs. 10 lakh crore budget for urban housing for the next 5 years

scores.rationale: Capex funded entirely from internal accruals, no large or transformational M&A, net cash balance sheet, and capacity added counter-cyclically while Morbi was shutting down.
scores.quote: We are not going to do a big thing... we don't see major capex in next 1 or 2 years

scores.rationale: A 35-year owner-operated arc from 4x8 inch tiles to 4x8 foot slabs, and a willingness to accept three flat quarters of self-inflicted disruption to push the Kajaria 2.0 dealer unification through.
scores.quote: When we started the journey 33 years back we started with the manufacture of 4 inch by 8 inch tiles and now we are making four feet by 8 feet tiles slab

scores.rationale: Consistently plain, operational calls with no celebrity positioning, and an explicit withdrawal from guidance-giving rather than headline-chasing targets.
scores.quote: my request will be going forward not to give any guidance, and we perform and prove to you people that we are doing a good job as a team

scores.rationale: Leadership is family succession (two sons and now grandson Kartik heading adhesives) rather than an internal pipeline, though FY26 shows a shift to external professionalisation with 3-4 C-level hires and a bathware consultant.
scores.quote: we are hiring good people. We are hiring at least 3 to 4 C-level people

scores.rationale: Blunt refusal to give margin guidance rather than a soft promise, open admission that past guidance failed, proactive disclosure of a subsidiary fraud with an E&Y forensic audit and signing-authority changes, and self-correction of a presentation error on the call.
scores.quote: guidance, as you are aware, I have always given, right? It didn't work out

scores.rationale: The striking FY26 Q4 result (EBITDA 19.2% vs 10.0%, PAT 3x) is substantially attributable to an external Morbi gas shock and competitor shutdowns rather than demonstrated skill, so results should not be read as evidence of a step-change in capability.
scores.quote: there has been a huge distraction at Morbi players in terms of cost, labour and cash flow. As a result, Kajaria and other players who have multi locational plants will have a great advantage

scores.rationale: Brand occupies a leading position in the customer's mind and shelf display creates some stickiness, but management itself concedes share is small in a market with hundreds of competing plants — no monopoly-like position.
scores.quote: In our industry, what is visible is sold

scores.rationale: Some switching friction exists via dealer display investment and regional plant proximity cutting transit time from Morbi, but the FY26 dealer churn during unification shows the lock-in is weak.
scores.quote: we've been churning a lot of dealers... lot of tail end dealers are going out

scores.rationale: The industry is deeply fragmented rather than an oligopoly — 500-600 Morbi plants alongside organised players Kajaria, Somany and Johnson, with dealers able to switch suppliers.
scores.quote: Out of 500, 600 plants, which people say in the investing community... not more than 150

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low (a plant costs only ~Rs.100-120cr) and pricing has been chronically irrational, with realizations falling ~9% over three years and Morbi historically cutting prices until a gas shock forced a hike.
scores.quote: As we are all aware, Morbi has always reduced the prices, reduced the prices

scores.rationale: An abundant supply of weak donators — Morbi plants shutting on gas costs and export collapse, plus GST formalisation pushing smaller-town dealers to tie up with branded manufacturers.
scores.quote: If the exports don't work, they shut down their plants

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed market leader with every major brokerage on the call (Jefferies, UBS, HDFC, JM, Nuvama, Equirus), the opposite of an ignored niche.
Gross margin near 38.5% and one brand-led 2% hike show some image-based pricing, but sustained realization decline and discounting to clear SKUs indicate the intangible premium is thin.
scores.quote: we gave some discount in order to reduce our SKUs

scores.rationale: Post-GST, smaller dealers actively seek branded, reliable supply over tax-arbitrage unorganised product, and buyers accept a price gap because displayed branded material is what sells.
scores.quote: now they say that we want to join whether it is Kajaria, Somani, Johnson we have to tie up with the company

scores.rationale: Strong and widening access — ~1,700 operating dealers with 380 exclusive showrooms, multi-locational plants cutting delivery time in the South, and a new dedicated architect/interior-designer and government sales team.
scores.quote: we are putting a major thrust on the architect and interior designer community

scores.rationale: Predominantly retail-through-dealer where the brand/display intangible does work, with corporate and institutional channels (architects, government) only now being built out, so the benefit-customer match is incomplete.
scores.quote: Government is another sector that we are working on as well where we have a strong government team

scores.rationale: Process technology is purchased off the shelf from equipment vendors and available to any competitor with capital, with no proprietary R&D or multi-product tech edge cited anywhere.
scores.quote: This plant has the most advanced technology Continua+ from Sacmi Italy

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described or implied anywhere in the calls.

Multi-locational plants plus a large exclusive-showroom dealer network give reach that Morbi single-site players cannot match, proven when Kajaria serviced demand at full capacity while competitors were shut.
scores.quote: Kajaria and other players who have multi locational plants will have a great advantage

scores.rationale: Sustained high growth capex — 129 showrooms launched in FY26 and 150 planned for FY27 plus US/UK pilots — increasingly funded by franchise partners' capital while own debt fell, implying rising incremental returns.
scores.quote: During the last financial year, we launched 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere formats... the franchisee partners will put the capex fit out also

scores.rationale: A&P is a disciplined ~1.8-2% of sales, raised counter-cyclically to defend and gain share in volatile gold-price periods, and it visibly translates into sector-leading SSSG and >35% new-customer share, though it cost PBT margin in some quarters.
scores.quote: Advertisement spends during the recently-concluded quarter has been higher to mitigate the impact of volatile gold prices and to drive market share in certain new markets

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or programme is discussed anywhere in the calls for this jewellery retailer.

The only M&A is the small, complementary Candere online bolt-on, taken to 100% ownership in FY25 and turned PAT-positive by FY26 with 160% revenue growth — a bolt-on whose economics improved post-deal, though it took years of losses to get there.
scores.quote: Candere turned PAT positive from the second half of FY 2026

scores.rationale: A stated dividend policy at ~20% of net profit (INR257 crore for FY26) alongside systematic debt paydown is a coherent distribution policy, but there is no buyback discipline demonstrated at low valuations.
scores.quote: In line with our announced dividend policy, Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of approximately INR257 crores, payout of around 20% of the net profit

scores.rationale: Jewellery retail is inherently inventory-heavy with stock turns of only ~2-2.5x, though the shift to franchisee-funded (FOCO) stores and gold metal loans moves the model progressively asset-lighter.
scores.quote: with the stock turn of around 2 and 2.5 in the first three years

scores.rationale: Consistent, multi-year share capture with a long runway: >35% new customers, non-South mix rising 44%→49%, and SSSG described as top-of-street versus listed peers with explicit gains from unorganized players.
scores.quote: your same-store growth performance, which has been absolutely top of the street versus being listed -- other listed players

scores.rationale: A methodical, well-executed multi-year geographic push — franchise pilots in 2022 scaled to nationwide non-South expansion, plus Middle East, and first UK/US showrooms — with the non-South revenue share proving the execution.
scores.quote: Our share of revenue from the non-South market is now at 49%, up from 44% in the prior year

scores.rationale: Mix is genuinely improving (rising studded share, 18/14/9-karat introduction, higher-margin non-South mix) and gold-price inflation lifts realisation, but much of the growth is volume from ~130-150 new stores a year rather than pricing power.
scores.quote: studded has an organic growth also these days... it becomes actually relatively easier for us to upsell also during high gold prices

scores.rationale: The company is riding near a cyclical peak rather than a bottom — gold prices have roughly doubled, FY26 was an exceptional year for the whole sector, and management concedes an unusually high base ahead.
scores.quote: given '26 was such an exceptional year for us and the entire jewellery space

scores.rationale: The end market is in permanent secular expansion via the unorganized-to-organized shift, reinforced by tightening hallmarking compliance and structural wedding demand.
scores.quote: when you come to non-south, yes, the unorganized to organized shift is more aggressive there, because there is more vacuum from unorganized players

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, deleveraging non-GML debt from INR1,300 crore to INR300 crore over three years while self-funding expansion from operating cash flow, and no large acquisitions across the five years.
scores.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have reduced the non-GML in India from INR1,300 crores to INR300 crores

scores.rationale: The franchise strategy announced as a six-store pilot in 2022 was deliberately paced, then scaled across four years, with management explicitly prioritising partner quality over store count — long-term vision executed with independence from quarterly pressure.
scores.quote: our objective is to create a good base of franchisee partners rather than only opening stores

scores.rationale: Management refuses to engage with share-price commentary and redirects to execution, and calls are substance-heavy, though a promoter-family brand built on heavy celebrity advertising is not truly low-profile.
scores.quote: our job is to keep focused on execution and delivering numbers on the ground and rest will not be our criteria to comment on

scores.rationale: Essentially no discussion of systematic talent development or a leadership pipeline beyond generic praise for the team, despite a professional CEO/CFO layer being in place alongside the promoter.
scores.quote: Our team also have been doing a good job

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly owns misses and quantifies bad news without prompting — the missed PBT target from overspending on marketing, the INR120-130 crore custom-duty inventory hit, and a budgeting error on advance tax — and declines to guide where uncertain.
scores.quote: There were some estimate which we did for the full year, we couldn't budgeted correctly

scores.rationale: Results must be discounted for a large exogenous tailwind — a near-100% rise in gold prices and a sector-wide exceptional year — though genuine skill shows in SSSG outperformance versus listed peers and share taken from stumbling competitors.
scores.quote: the gold price is almost risen by, I would say, almost near 100%

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position: the company must actively raise marketing spend to defend regions against regional players, indicating a contested rather than owned place in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: competition in the local -- by the local players. Regional players were very high in certain markets, so we do not want to lose market share

scores.rationale: Only modest lock-in exists through gold savings schemes at a stable 18-20% of revenue and old-gold exchange, but customers face no real switching cost in jewellery retail.
scores.quote: gold saving scheme usually is in the range of 18% to 20%, which remains the same

scores.rationale: The industry is highly fragmented — a large unorganized segment plus numerous regional and listed branded players — which is the opposite of a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: we have still got a majority or a good quotient of non-south -- what do you call, unorganized players in south also

scores.rationale: Inventory intensity is a real capital barrier and Kalyan avoids discount wars and refuses to chase lab-grown pricing, but heavy competitive activity on installment and exchange schemes plus new LGD entrants signal only moderate rationality.
scores.quote: players are pushing on installment schemes as well as gold exchange programs

scores.rationale: Explicitly identified weak donors — a vacuum of unorganized players and named strategic missteps by two South competitors producing above-normal SSSG for Kalyan.
scores.quote: there has been a strategic misstep taken by two players in South, especially in Tamil Nadu where we actually are getting higher than usual SSSG

scores.rationale: This is a heavily-covered listed large-cap with an advertising-led national brand and a crowded analyst following, the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Consolidated revenue... INR10,343 crores, a growth of 42%

scores.rationale: Brand trust supports steady demand and a rising studded/premium mix, but gold-price transparency keeps gross margins structurally thin (EBITDA ~8%) so pricing power from image is limited.
scores.quote: we are still at 7.9% with the recovery which will happen

scores.rationale: The proposition is certainty of purity and fair dealing — management even declines to sell lab-grown diamonds to avoid a price crash betraying customer trust, and welcomes tighter hallmarking enforcement.
scores.quote: customer is buying those diamonds because they trust Kalyan as a brand. So if the price goes down, they will feel very offended

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the core advantage — 129 showrooms added in one year with 150 more planned, 110 omnichannel Candere stores, plus savings schemes and store-level promotions that create direct customer intimacy.
scores.quote: we plan to open 150 showrooms across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand

scores.rationale: The customer base is almost purely retail and the benefit mix is correctly matched — trust, assurance and accessibility rather than corporate TCO — with corporate/bullion sales deliberately negligible.
scores.quote: we usually do not push coins, and we don't even sell bullion

scores.rationale: No technology or product-engineering advantage is discussed; software mentions relate only to Candere's e-commerce platform upgrade.
Management describes a store-density visibility loop that an analyst labelled a network effect, but it is brand awareness scaling with footprint rather than a self-reinforcing two-sided network.
scores.quote: More number of showrooms, more expansion, thereby meaning more visibility for Kalyan and thereby helping generate more footfalls and revenue

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the primary moat — a nationwide own-plus-franchise showroom network expanding at 130-150 stores a year across India, Middle East, UK and US, with franchisee demand strong enough that partners queue for multiple stores.
scores.quote: our franchisee have the financial ability to take multiple showrooms, and we give them only one store and ask them to start the journey with Kalyan

scores.rationale: Growth capex (Vizag, Jainpur, Hosur) was built out when utilisation was only 65%, and by Mar 2026 management says no significant capital investment is needed at all — capacity ahead of demand with revenue near flat implies poor incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: the capacity utilization was 65% and our expansion project at Vizag and Ja inpur w ere on track

scores.rationale: A&P was stepped up hard (ad spend +20% in a quarter with 1.7% topline growth, Asia Cup/World Cup, Ghar Ki Raunak, jingle refresh) and has preserved brand equity rank, but has not converted into sales growth over the period.
scores.quote: So we have incre ased the ad expenditure in this quarter by around 20%

scores.rationale: R&D output is consistent and cumulative — Paint+ range now >10% of decorative, 20+ launches in FY25, 11 in FY26, plus industrial firsts (monocoat PU matt, low-bake CED, fluoropolymer) — though it has yet to translate into decorative revenue growth.
scores.quote: Paint+ group of products, which we had launched. Today, their contribution to overall decorative business is greater than 10%

scores.rationale: Only small complementary bolt-ons (Nerofix, Perma) in the fast-growing construction chemicals adjacency, with no large or transformative deals; post-deal margin impact is not disclosed.
scores.quote: In this space, we have made two acquisitions: one is Nerofix , and the other is Perma.

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy in any of the calls.

Asset-heavy manufacturing footprint (eight plants, 6.16 lakh KL capacity) running at 65% utilisation with flat-to-negative revenue means low and deteriorating asset turn, and the decorative moat is visibly being contested.
scores.quote: Our capacity is approximately 6.16 lakh KL per year.

scores.rationale: Share is gained in industrial/auto but decorative share is flat at best and the company has slipped to overall No.3 in India, so runway exists but capture is not being demonstrated where it matters most.
scores.quote: in case of decorative, it will be about same market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic and defensive rather than a premium brand travelling — deliberate over-indexing on North/East zones and selected towns, explicitly framed as a temporary 2–3 year approach, with no overseas expansion.
scores.quote: we clearly over -index in markets where we are already strong

scores.rationale: Mix is genuinely premiumising (Paint+, premium salience rising) but there is no pricing contribution at all — value and volume growth are identical, and putty pricing is being lost outright.
scores.quote: our volume and value gap is nil. We're exactly at same level

scores.rationale: The company appears past the trough: competitive intensity has stopped rising, decorative recovery visible since October, and auto is running ~20% on GST 2.0 with OEM capacity set to double by 2030.
scores.quote: competitive intensity has stabilized , and we are entering the next phase, we expect to start seeing a recovery

scores.rationale: End markets are in clear secular expansion — ~10% industry growth on a large base, construction chemicals with ~3x penetration headroom, auto capacity doubling by 2030, plus infrastructure-led high-end coatings demand.
scores.quote: only three out of ten homes, institutions, or buildings currently use construction chemicals, which implies nearly three times growth potential

scores.rationale: Stewardship is organic and disciplined — exited low-profit performance-coating business, refused to chase irrational putty pricing at the cost of reported growth, and kept M&A to two small bolt-ons.
scores.quote: we are clear in mind that we have to strike a right balance between the growth, profitability and sustainable growth

scores.rationale: The same strategic agenda (Paint+, premiumisation, projects, new businesses, services) has been pursued consistently across three years and two MDs, with stated milestones eventually hit, though delivery has been slower than promised.
scores.quote: Over the last 3 years, we have navigated challenges, taken some bold steps and made some strategic choices that are now bearing fruit.

scores.rationale: Management is low-key and substance-oriented — calls are led by functional detail and product technology rather than personality, and the MD declines to speculate publicly about rivals' ownership changes.
scores.quote: I don't have much comment as of now because at the end of the day, whether the business is in one hand, the other hand

scores.rationale: Some systematic development is evidenced — Great Place to Work certification, a formal employee innovation programme, and 200–300 technically competent people deployed on customer lines — but no explicit succession/pipeline disclosure.
scores.quote: more than 200 –300 technically competent people deployed on customer lines and field operations

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly owns shortfalls unprompted — delayed influencer initiatives, missed targets, admitted competitive impact, apologised for a service failure on the call — rather than spinning weak numbers.
scores.quote: Initially, we were a little slowed on this initiative. We were not on target.

scores.rationale: The narrative is consistently more confident than the arithmetic — nine-month PBT down 4% and decorative flat-to-negative while every segment is described as performing 'better relatively' — and the industrial strength leans heavily on the Japanese parent's technology rather than demonstrable local skill.
scores.quote: most of these segments, probably whatever results we have seen so far, our performance is better relatively

scores.rationale: In automotive OEM coatings the company holds a 50%+ share with entrenched line presence, a genuine mini-monopoly position, though nothing comparable exists in decorative.
scores.quote: Overall, I would say we are at 50% plus as far as auto is concerned.

scores.rationale: Industrial customers are locked in by approvals, on-line technical support and qualification cycles that management says take years to replicate, creating real switching costs.
scores.quote: This is not a business that can be entered easily, as it is p erformance -driven rather than purely price -driven.

scores.rationale: The former big-four oligopoly has been broken by Grasim's entry and JSW's acquisition of Akzo, with smaller entrants capturing part of industry growth, while large auto OEM customers hold strong negotiating power.
scores.quote: a part of that growth is being captured by smaller players who have recently entered the market

scores.rationale: Decorative barriers have visibly failed — well-capitalised new entrants arrived, pricing in putty turned irrational and competitors are pushing free material and heavy spend, so pricing discipline has broken down even if industrial remains protected.
scores.quote: on putty, as we were saying earlier, so pricing definitely is a challenge in the marketplace

scores.rationale: There are weak bottom-of-pyramid players to take from in industrial, but in decorative Kansai is closer to being the donator — share is being 'realigned at each counter' and it has slipped to No.3 nationally.
scores.quote: to some extent, the redistribution of the market is happening in terms of the market share

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — Indian paints is a magnet for large capital, with a conglomerate entering and JSW buying Akzo specifically to target second or third place.
scores.quote: They have expressed ambitions to aim for second or third place in India.

scores.rationale: Real brand assets exist (No.2 brand equity index, a three-decade jingle) but they are not converting into pricing power — zero price-led growth, gross margin flat, and putty realisations falling.
scores.quote: We proudly hold the position of a second most recognized brand in terms of the brand equity index nationwide.

scores.rationale: Industrial customers explicitly buy reliability and continuity of supply, validated by an unblemished supply/quality record and quality awards from Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Suzuki Motorcycle and TAFE.
scores.quote: we have not faced situations where customers have suffered due to Nerolac■s supply or quality issues

scores.rationale: Access and intimacy are being built aggressively — 3,500 dealers added, 600+ specialty stores, ~85% CCD machine coverage, projects teams in 80+ towns, and a services business now >5% of decorative — although reach still trails the market leader.
scores.quote: We have been able to add 3,500 dealers in our network as on December '25.

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched for corporate customers — TCO/reliability plus approval-based lock-in in auto and performance coatings — while the retail intangible proposition is comparatively weak, leaving the match only partially complete.
scores.quote: in industrial coatings, success is not only about having a ready -made business. It also requires a complete supply chain and va lue chain setup

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product technology edge sourced from the Japanese parent and global network — BTX-free monocoats, low-bake CED, fluoropolymer and anticarbonation coatings — but it is concentrated in industrial and only now being extended to decorative.
scores.quote: Our spirit of innovation is deeply rooted in advanced Japanese technology, which has been the driving force behind our industrial business.

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the calls; the painter/architect programmes are conventional influencer loyalty schemes, not network effects.

In industrial the service reach is hard to match — eight plants plus 200–300 technicians embedded on customer lines where continuous line support is vital — even though decorative distribution is clearly behind the market leader.
scores.quote: We have eight manufacturing locations and more than 200 –300 technically competent people deployed on customer lines

scores.rationale: Steady, self-funded growth investment in branches, lite branches, sales channels and digital platforms while ROA rose from ~1.16% to 2.11%, indicating high incremental returns, though the absolute capex intensity is modest and branch rollout slips on execution.
scores.quote: we have planned for opening 50 branches during the first half of the year, so we will be completing 25 branches before the end of this quarter

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any of the excerpts.

No formal R&D line, but consistent product/platform development has yielded measurable customer traction — DLite app with 2.5mn MAU, 24 new CASA variants, GST surrogate, LAMF, credit cards, API-first transaction banking.
scores.quote: the rating for this app is 4.8 in Google Play... 2.5 million monthly active users for our DLite app

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were undertaken or discussed across the 17 calls; growth is entirely organic.
Coherent and disciplined distribution — 130% dividend maintained plus a 1:5 bonus, funded by internal accruals with explicitly no need for dilutive capital raise, but no buyback programme.
scores.quote: we have declared a dividend of 130% as declared last year... There may not be any need to raise money in financial year '26-'27

scores.rationale: Bank balance sheets are inherently asset-heavy, and while returns are excellent (ROA 2.11%, NIM 4.26%), there is no structural moat protecting the spread — management concedes it must give up price to retain customers.
scores.quote: The ROA for the quarter stands at 2.11%

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway and demonstrated capture — guidance of 1-2% above system credit growth, mortgage volumes +56% y/y, retail jewel loans +61%, NTB disbursement growth 25%.
scores.quote: our guidance for credit growth of 1% or 2% over the industry growth will continue

scores.rationale: Credible but incremental expansion beyond the Tamil Nadu home base via institutional/state-government tie-ups, a Hyderabad retail branch and NEO's 40 locations; no overseas presence and it explicitly cannot offer GIFT City/leverage products.
scores.quote: The bank is strengthening its presence outside Tamil Nadu by partnering with institutional clients and state government bodies

scores.rationale: Mix shift genuinely drove profitability (corporate 45%→14%, RAM at 86%, fixed-rate book 23%→34% preserving NIM through 125bps of repo cuts), but pricing power is absent and management is now conceding price to retain relationships.
scores.quote: we must take a strategic bet on preserving relationships over margins

scores.rationale: The bank is at a benign cyclical peak, not a trough — GNPA 0.74%, credit cost 0.33%, with management flagging geopolitical risk and taking a one-time INR163cr prudential provision, implying credit costs can only normalise upward.
scores.quote: We have provided prudentially INR163 crores... towards sectors identified that may get affected due to ongoing geopolitical tensions

scores.rationale: Indian credit penetration, MSME formalisation and digital banking are secularly expanding end-markets, evidenced by sustained 15-16% total business growth and 18% system credit growth cited by management.
scores.quote: system has moved much early... the system level growth itself has moved from last quarter to now around 18% types

scores.rationale: Purely organic, no M&A, deliberate shrinking of low-yield corporate and co-lending books, conscious moderation of Q4 growth and bulk deposits, counter-cyclical prudential provisioning and a 18.61% CRAR with no equity raise needed.
scores.quote: We had deliberately reduced the book as it was not ROA accretive... we would keep this co-lending as secondary to our organic growth

scores.rationale: A multi-year restructuring executed with consistency across all 17 calls — ROA from 0.19% (Dec-2020) to 2.11%, GNPA 3.97%→0.74%, corporate mix 45%→14% — with guidance repeatedly met or beaten.
scores.quote: our performance has consistently surpassed our guidance across 3 key metrics, growth, profitability and asset quality

scores.rationale: Understated, operationally focused commentary from a low-profile regional bank, including an unprompted apology for a technical glitch and no self-promotion beyond factual metrics.
scores.quote: First of all, sincere apologies from our side. There is a technical glitch

scores.rationale: Leadership depth has been built largely by lateral hiring rather than internal pipeline (Consumer Banking head resigned and was replaced externally; national sales managers recruited from market), though one internal elevation to Executive Director occurred and analysts have explicitly flagged key-man risk.
scores.quote: Mr. Dolphy Jose - Chief General Manager looking after Consumer Banking resigned during the month of June and we have already recruited Mr. S T Gopal

scores.rationale: Consistently granular and self-critical disclosure — line-by-line bridges of opex and fee income declines, explicit acknowledgement of past corporate-lending mistakes, and voluntary warnings against extrapolating a strong quarter.
scores.quote: Just as a word of caution, YTD growth, this first quarter growth should not be considered as an indicator for the full year growth

scores.rationale: Record profits are genuinely skill-driven in part (mix shift, underwriting), but are also flattered by an exceptionally benign credit cycle and lumpy one-offs (write-off recoveries, tax-refund interest, SR recoveries) that management itself strips out.
scores.quote: there cannot be any sort of a uniformity in the write-off recovery because many external factors are involved

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in any product or customer's mind — accounts are routinely lost to rivals on price across LAP, housing and commercial.
scores.quote: allowed a few accounts to be taken over by others due to lower pricing

scores.rationale: Some regional stickiness and relationship lock-in — 72% of deposits from retail households and 69% of CASA growth from existing customers — but switching costs are demonstrably low on the asset side.
scores.quote: Retail households continue to be the backbone of our deposit franchise, contributing to 72% of our total deposits

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented rather than oligopolistic, and customers clearly hold negotiating power — both borrowers and depositors move on price.
scores.quote: there is some sort of a pricing pressure from other competitors also... those cases you may have to give some sort of a concession

scores.rationale: Although licensing limits entry, pricing behaviour is irrational in KVB's core segments, with margin-destroying competition in LAP, housing and MSME forcing the bank to cede business or margin.
scores.quote: LAP segment is experiencing strong pricing competition, making both customer retention and new acquisition a bit challenging

scores.rationale: Weaker incumbents exist to take share from, evidenced by the deliberate win-back campaign reclaiming customers lost to other banks and strong new-to-bank acquisition.
scores.quote: on a win back we had a campaign wherein our branches started calling them... two years, three years back they were dealing with us

scores.rationale: A century-old mid-sized Tamil Nadu bank operating in unglamorous jewel-loan and small-ticket MSME niches that larger capital largely ignores, with sales-heavy grassroots hiring.
scores.quote: The jewel loans portfolio encompassing all verticals accounts for 30% of the bank's overall portfolio

scores.rationale: No image- or brand-driven pricing power; the bank is a price taker that must sacrifice yield to hold customers, with NIM guided down to 3.7-3.8%.
scores.quote: even for the retention of existing customers somewhere it is becoming necessity for us to compromise on the margins

scores.rationale: A long-established franchise where trust and relationship continuity anchor a granular, sticky retail deposit base, with management explicitly prioritising relationships over price.
scores.quote: It is literally homecoming for them

scores.rationale: Competes explicitly on service turnaround and accessibility rather than price, backed by feet-on-street sales teams, 175 mortgage-focused branches, an integrated open-market channel and a well-rated digital app.
scores.quote: the jewel loan rather than the product and pricing, the major thing is the delivery... how fast you will be able to deliver

scores.rationale: Benefit type is sensibly matched — service/convenience and trust for retail households and jewel-loan borrowers, and TCO/transaction-banking lock-in via API-first cash management for MSME and corporate clients.
scores.quote: The Transaction Banking Group... providing API first real-time banking capabilities for corporates and MSME clients

scores.rationale: Competent, steadily improving digital stack (98% digital transactions, digital lending platform, transaction banking APIs) but table-stakes rather than a differentiated multi-product technology edge versus larger banks.
scores.quote: The share of digital transaction stands at 98%

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing two-sided network; the only adjacent effort — merchant ecosystem expansion — is aspirational and the BNPL partnership actually contracted after a partner management change.
scores.quote: expanding merchant ecosystems through expedited merchant acquisition

scores.rationale: A dense Tamil Nadu branch franchise combined with dedicated non-branch channels (business banking units, corporate banking units, open market channel, DSAs, relationship managers) that regional rivals struggle to match, though it is not a national advantage.
scores.quote: bank has established 15 business banking units across the country... and 9 corporate banking units... bank has set up a non-branch distribution unit, NEO

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly growth-oriented (Chamarajanagar, Hyderabad smart-meter plant, Sanand OSAT, INR1,500 crore HDI PCB at Chennai) with large claimed revenue potential, but incremental returns are still unproven given repeated execution delays and a stretched working-capital cycle.
scores.quote: business potential of about INR15,000 crores for the group from the customers from our current investment of INR1,500 crores in the HDI PCB manufacturing operations

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand-promotion spend across the calls; as a B2B EMS/ODM the topic is genuinely absent.
R&D/NPD ambition is stated as a forward target rather than a demonstrated track record of new-product yield.
scores.quote: our goal is to steadily increase the contribution of NPD -led and value -added solutions to nearly 30% of the tot al revenue in the coming years

scores.rationale: Iskraemeco was claimed margin-accretive but metering revenue has stagnated (~INR300-600 crore, 'growth has not come in metering segment') and brought long-dated annuity receivables that management is still trying to discount away, while August Electronics added a further cross-border integration.
scores.quote: we have identified a bank with whom we will do funding that is funding the annuities payments, which are sitting in other noncurrent assets

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed in any excerpt; capital has been raised and reinvested rather than distributed.

scores.quote: working capital days stood at around 122 days in FY '26

scores.rationale: Clear runway and evidence of capture — import substitution/China+1 wins, a stated goal of becoming India's largest smart-meter EMS, and 33-37% revenue growth off a small base.

scores.rationale: Genuine international footprint (24 countries) plus the August Electronics platform is opening high-margin North American work, though it is acquisition-led rather than organic brand travel.
scores.quote: Growth from the North American market through August Electronics integration is steadily building

scores.quote: an EBITDA margin of 15.9%, an expansion of 190 basis points year -on-year

scores.rationale: Not positioned at a cycle bottom — the company is riding an expansion phase and is currently being hurt by project deferrals, geopolitical disruption and an EV OEM collapse rather than anticipating an upturn.
scores.quote: one of the largest electric vehicle OEM manufacturers has completely dropped by about 90% of the revenue

scores.rationale: End markets — Indian electronics manufacturing, semiconductors/OSAT, smart metering (110 million meters still to be awarded), EV and defence — are in clear secular expansion backed by government policy.
scores.quote: already 11 crores meters have been awarded and ano ther 11 crores meters yet to be awarded

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (D/E 0.2) but stewardship is not organic-focused: two acquisitions plus simultaneous entry into OSAT and HDI PCB while the core EMS business missed its own execution targets.
scores.quote: broader operational complexities associated with managing the core EM S business amid global uncertainties, while simultaneously scaling new strategic platforms such as OSAT and PCB

scores.rationale: Founder-led since 1988 with a multi-year backward-integration vision that has actually been carried through to an operational OSAT plant and FSA approval despite delays.
scores.quote: Our semiconductor journey has moved decisively from intent to execution

scores.rationale: Management is highly visible — PM-inaugurated facility, television appearances reaffirming guidance late in a quarter that ultimately missed badly.
scores.quote: the management comes on the television and holds on to the guidance

scores.rationale: Stated commitment to a leadership pipeline and a strengthened board, offset by repeated top-management churn (MD changes, CEO/MD reshuffles, restructuring) that signals an unsettled bench.
scores.quote: There has been some top management restructuring and role realignment in this phase

scores.rationale: Management does eventually own the misses explicitly and apologises, but candor is retrospective — guidance was reaffirmed publicly weeks before a INR900 crore shortfall was disclosed.
scores.quote: we sincerely understand and appreciate that the guidance what we have given, we could not meet

scores.rationale: The narrative (semiconductors, PM inauguration, $1 billion FY28 target) has consistently run ahead of delivered results, so headline growth risks being mistaken for execution skill.
scores.quote: certain areas where market expectations moved ahead of actual delivery

scores.rationale: Kaynes explicitly has no branded product and remains an EMS/ODM contract manufacturer, even licensing the Iskraemeco brand rather than owning mindshare.
scores.quote: We don't have a Kaynes branded product

scores.rationale: High-mix, high-complexity, safety-critical programmes with long qualification cycles create real switching costs, reinforced by non-cancellable order books.
scores.quote: It's not very easy to shift these businesses, and it's very difficult to d evelop these businesses

scores.rationale: Smart metering has roughly five significant device players, but Indian EMS more broadly is fragmented and Kaynes' large AMISP/OEM customers hold clear negotiating power over timing and pricing.
scores.quote: there are about four, five major players in the device a rea

scores.rationale: Policy incentives are drawing abundant capital and entrants into ESDM, and Kaynes itself notes competitive churn, with customers able to defer or cut volumes at will.
scores.quote: I think that is something which is going to help all industry players in this sector

scores.rationale: Weak or disqualified competitors and displaced imports provide a pool of share to take, particularly in Kavach and China-substitution work.
scores.quote: many Kavach businesses are getting disqualified

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a heavily covered listed name in India's hottest capital-attracting sector, with brokerage-hosted calls, high investor expectations and a prime-ministerial plant inauguration.
scores.quote: the inauguration of the OSAT facility at Sanand by our honorable Prime Minister

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are contract-manufacturing thin (15-16% EBITDA, 10% PAT) and mix-driven rather than brand-driven.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin of 15.8% for FY '26

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and quality assurance in safety-critical and regulated applications, and Kaynes deliberately runs excess inventory to guarantee delivery over efficiency.
scores.quote: we make sure that we give priority for execution of orders rather than just efficiency alone, because the customers depend on us to deliver

scores.rationale: Deep design-stage engagement and a co-development model with 300+ active customers gives real customer intimacy, though not a distribution-style reach.
scores.quote: This requires us to closely work with our customers right from the early design and development stages

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate/institutional and the pitch is correctly built on reliability, qualification lock-in and TCO rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: almost close to 300 -plus active customers

scores.rationale: Technology depth is being acquired and built (OSAT, HDI PCB, Iskraemeco metering IP) but the company is still transitioning from service provider to design owner, with the brand and much IP not its own.
scores.quote: accelerate the transition from a traditional EMS -led o rganization to a differentiated ESDM and product -driven enterprise

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the calls.
The calls discuss backward integration and manufacturing capacity, not any distribution or service-reach advantage.

Consistent growth capex across cables/conductors and tower capacity (Dubai, Jaipur, Jabalpur, Butibori, Brazil) with the cables business claimed to earn very high returns, though group-level ROIC stays thin at ~2.6% PAT margin.
scores.quote: Following successful capacity enhancements at our plants in Dubai, Jaipur and Jabalpur, the expansion of our Butibori facility in Nagpur is expected to be completed by March '26

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any excerpt; the business is tender-driven B2B EPC.

Some new-product development in cables (signalling cables, jumper dropper wire, elastomeric, E-Beam) but core technology in areas like Kavach is sourced from third-party vendors rather than developed in-house.
scores.quote: we have a tie -up with one of the three approved vendors and we will continue with them

scores.rationale: No new bolt-ons in the period, but the legacy SAE Brazil acquisition was a persistent drag requiring loss funding and high-cost debt repayment over years, and management signalled openness to inorganic moves.
scores.quote: we have been losing m oney in SA E Brazil, that requires some funding to be done

scores.rationale: A modest, steady dividend (₹5.50/share in FY26) with no buybacks and no articulated distribution framework, understandable given net debt of ₹6,722 crores.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors have decided to recommend a dividend of up to 275%, that is INR5.50 per equity share

scores.rationale: Asset turn is depressed by chronic working-capital intensity — net debt including acceptances roughly doubled from ₹3,418 crores (Jun-22) to ₹6,806 crores (Dec-25) — with no moat protecting returns.
scores.quote: our net debt, including acceptances , stand at INR6,806 crores as on 31st December vis -a-vis INR5,57 4 crores

scores.rationale: Demonstrated share capture in T&D — PGCIL award for maximum circuit-km added in FY24, record order intake of ₹25,280 crores in FY26 and expanding private/TBCB client base.
scores.quote: KEC received an award for executing the maximum circuit kilometer addition transmission line in India for FY '24 from PGCIL

scores.rationale: Credible, executed international expansion — Middle East ~27% of order book, first 380kV GIS in Saudi, revival in Africa/CIS, Australia tower supply and GCC entry in oil & gas, with international T&D inflows up 35%.
scores.quote: with order exceeding INR 11,300 crores, representing a robust growth of over 35%

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/order-book led in a competitively bid business with EBITDA margins stuck around 7%; mix improvement (T&D share, larger orders, cables) is real but secondary and margin guidance was cut mid-year.

scores.rationale: The Indian T&D capex cycle is in a clear multi-year upturn that KEC is levered to, though the company is already well into the upswing rather than at the bottom.
scores.quote: there is a heightened policy and execution focus on strengthening transmission infrastructure... a robust multiyear pipeline

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — non-fossil target raised from 500GW by 2030 to 900GW by 2035, record peak power demand, grid congestion and data-centre/AI-driven demand in the US.
scores.quote: the government has enhanced its non -fossil fuel capacity target from 500 gigawatt by 2030 to 900 gigawatt by 2035

scores.rationale: Organic focus and no big M&A are positives, but repeated promises of working-capital and debt improvement from FY23 onwards were not delivered — debt roughly doubled over the four years.
scores.quote: Q3 onwards, we are very confident that the working cap ital will start showing improvement

scores.rationale: Kejriwal's stable multi-year tenure shows tenacious execution of a stated strategy — SAE turned from heavy losses to ₹1,800 crores of profitable revenue, and railways was deliberately shrunk to fix cash flows.
scores.quote: it's a very conscious decision to degrow the business for a couple of years till we get out of the old projects

scores.rationale: Some people investment is visible — a transformation program with a global consultant and an 85% 'Happiness Quotient' — but senior capability in Civil was bought in externally rather than grown, and there is no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline.
scores.quote: we have further strengthened organizational capabilities in Civil business through strategic hiri ng at senior leadership levels

scores.rationale: Consistently candid across four years — admits underinvestment and below-market margins in cables, flags misses openly, and declines to project confidence it does not have.
scores.quote: our cable margins are at least 200 to 300 bas is points lower than the market... I think we have been a little bit underinvested in this busin ess

scores.rationale: Stripping the strong order-book narrative away, results are ordinary — 2.6% PAT margin and rising debt — with much of the growth attributable to a government-driven transmission capex cycle rather than firm-specific skill.
scores.quote: Operating PAT margins have also increased by 30 basis points to 2.6%

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere; work is won project-by-project through open competitive tendering with no aftermarket annuity.
scores.quote: In some tenders, we have seen 13, in one of them, I saw, 41 bids coming in

scores.rationale: Clients re-tender every project with essentially no switching costs, and even large data-centre opportunities are split across multiple contractors.

scores.rationale: Only a handful of players can execute 765kV/HVDC work, but the end customers (PGCIL, state utilities, large private developers) hold clear negotiating power through L1 bidding.
scores.quote: several large intrastate transmission projects, earlier executed by state utilities, have transitioned to the TBCB route driving heightened participation from private developers

scores.rationale: Pre-qualifications create some barrier in HVDC/EHV, but civil, water and domestic oil & gas see heavy entry and price competition forcing KEC to withdraw from segments.
scores.quote: the business continues to strategically focus on expanding its global footprint

scores.rationale: Structural shift of intrastate projects to TBCB and supply-constrained/weaker regional contractors leave share available, which KEC is capturing with private clients.
scores.quote: we continue to scale up our presence with private sector clients and have secured orders of INR 3,600 crores from private players and SEBs

scores.rationale: KEC is a widely covered listed EPC major with a heavily analyst-followed quarterly call and a capital-attracting end market, the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Balasubramanian from Arihant Capital

scores.rationale: No image or taste-based pricing power — margins are set by commodity costs and competitive bidding, with EBITDA around 7% and roughly half the order book on fixed price.
scores.quote: roughly I'll say 50% or so would be on fixed and the balance would be on variable

scores.rationale: Execution track record and pre-qualifications do buy credibility for complex 765kV/HVDC and Kavach work, but selection still runs through lowest-price tendering.

scores.quote: This strategy of backward integration is helping us make cables business a strategic enabler for our railways business

scores.rationale: Customers are governments, utilities and corporates where TCO and reliability matter, but KEC has no switching-cost lock-in and remains exposed to slow-paying state clients such as in water projects.
scores.quote: We continue to adopt a calibrated approach to execution in Water projects given the current payment scenario

scores.rationale: Capability in HVDC, GIS and digital construction tools is real but largely licensed or partner-dependent, with no disclosed R&D intensity to sustain a technology edge.
scores.quote: we have a tie -up with one of the three approved vendors

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model strengthens with scale in a self-reinforcing two-sided way; each project stands alone.

A genuinely hard-to-replicate global execution and manufacturing footprint — plants in India, Dubai, Mexico and Brazil serving India, Middle East, Africa, CIS, Americas and Australia — is a real reach advantage in T&D EPC.
scores.quote: the business has secured significant orders, especially in UAE and Africa... a large tower supply order from Australia

scores.rationale: Sustained and rising growth capex — INR397cr (FY24) to ~INR1,000cr (FY25) to INR928cr in 9M FY26 on the Sanand greenfield plus Chinchpada/Pathredi brownfields — targeted at ~3-3.5x asset turns and INR5,000-6,000cr incremental revenue, with maintenance capex only INR20-25cr a year.
scores.quote: our maintenance CAPEX in our Company is hardly 20 to 25 crore in a year... in our industry the CAPEX ratio is 1:5

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-investment budget or advertising efficiency is discussed anywhere across the calls; only a passing reference to 'brand strategy' in the dealer context.

No R&D line item is disclosed, but consistent product/qualification development shows results — electron-beam solar wire capability, 400kV National Grid UK qualification and country-specific UL/European approvals that opened new customers.
scores.quote: KEI is the only Indian company to qualify in National Grid UK framework agreement for maximum voltages up to 400 kV

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are mentioned in any of the calls — all expansion is greenfield/brownfield organic, so there is no M&A track record to score.

Asset-light economics are confirmed (1:5 capex-to-sales ratio, ~3-3.5x asset turns on Sanand, ROCE 27.4%), but the protecting moat is only moderate given metal pass-through pricing and new entrants.
scores.quote: we have ROCE 27.4% is a return on capital employed

scores.quote: our capacities in Cables was almost at the peak level. So whatever so we could not grow much in Cable segment

scores.rationale: Exports compounded from ~INR700cr guidance in FY23 to INR1,833cr in FY26 (+45%), built over years via country-specific certifications, with landmark entries into Australia 330kV, UAE 132kV, Spain, US, Caribbean and UK National Grid.
scores.quote: It is a journey it has been a journey of several years. It is not that suddenly this demand has come up.

scores.rationale: Headline growth is largely metal-price pass-through rather than pricing power (FY26: value +20.7% but net metal volume only +6.2%), though mix is genuinely improving via EHV, exports and B2C lifting EBITDA margin to 11.81%.
scores.quote: the net volume increase was 6.21%

scores.rationale: The company is mid-to-late in a strong infrastructure/power capex upcycle rather than near a cyclical bottom, with management seeing no deceleration but also no depressed base to recover from.
scores.quote: As of now, we don't see any deceleration in the demand for cables

scores.rationale: End markets — power T&D, RDSS, solar/wind, thermal, data centres, real estate and manufacturing capex — are in durable secular expansion, with management sizing the industry at ~15% annual growth.

scores.rationale: Entirely organic growth funded from operating cash with near-nil net debt (net debt INR32cr in Q1FY23, cash INR700cr vs INR134cr borrowings in FY24), no acquisitions, and capacity built ahead of the cycle.
scores.quote: whatever CAPEX requirement that fund has already been accumulated, so, there will not be any further requirement from any loan

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-year plan — 15-18% CAGR guidance from 2022, land acquisition, then Sanand delivered — plus a years-long export certification build-out, executed independently over a 50-year operating history.
scores.quote: with our experience of running a cable industry for last around 50 years, it will be ramped up very shortly

scores.rationale: Calls are dense, numbers-first and free of self-promotion, with the promoter-CMD presenting operational detail himself, though he does give occasional TV/media interviews.
scores.quote: So this is a brief summary about the results from my side.

scores.rationale: Only tactical references to hiring — deploying new manpower in the South and East and inducting manpower for the Sanand ramp-up — with no evidence of systematic talent development or a succession pipeline.
scores.quote: more and more new manpower, we are deploying in the southern part and the Eastern part of the country

scores.rationale: Management openly disclosed the six-month Sanand delay, the capacity constraint that let Havells outgrow them, and quantified the lost March exports rather than glossing over them.

scores.quote: there may be increase or decrease by 0.5% to 1%. But for a full year basis... we will improve our operating margin

scores.rationale: Multiple well-capitalised new entrants have entered the wires segment and pricing is a formulaic metal pass-through rather than a defended price point, indicating entry barriers are low in the retail-facing part of the business.
scores.quote: a few other small companies entering Wire segment

scores.rationale: Management explicitly reallocates distribution away from weaker players and relies on a fragmented tail of smaller/unorganised competitors as the source of B2C share gains.
scores.quote: we are exchanging from the weak hands to the stronger hands in the areas wherever it is

scores.rationale: The stock is heavily covered and well followed — calls hosted by Nuvama with Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, Kotak, ICICI, HSBC and Sundaram participating — so it is anything but ignored by capital.
scores.quote: the line of Pulkit Patni from Goldman Sachs

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — end-user approvals, country certifications, type tests and BIS licences are the stated reason for winning business, and time-bound projects cannot risk cheap unqualified cable.

scores.rationale: The mix is well matched — ~42% institutional sales won on approvals, price-variation clauses and reliability, and ~54% B2C sold on brand availability through dealers — with B2C rising steadily from 42% in FY23.

scores.rationale: There is a real technical edge at the top end — 400kV EHV capability, electron-beam solar wire, in-house PVC and LT XLPE compounding — but R&D intensity is not disclosed and most volume is standard LT cable and house wire.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing across a two-sided network; growth depends on added capacity, approvals and dealer count, and dealers churn 10-12% a year.
scores.quote: every year, 10% to 12% is the churning of dealers, some dealers leaves and some new are added

scores.rationale: Distribution is the strongest durable advantage — dealer count grew 1,800 to 2,125 with 25-29% B2C growth, backed by 26 stocking depots, fortnightly price resets and a multi-year overseas agent/certification network rivals would take years to replicate.
scores.quote: in last several years, we have built a strong network of agents and marketing network to promote our products in many countries

scores.rationale: Consistent growth-oriented investment in proprietary platforms (Hexagram/mPower, XAlt, data lake, mPower Wealth, GIFT City and now a Cayman Islands facility) rather than maintenance, funded from cash with historically 44-45% EBITDA margins, though recent international build-out has yet to show returns.
scores.quote: The transaction volume continues to expand, which calls obviously for significant investments into our own technological infrastructure solutions, people, business process reorchestration

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the excerpts; the business is B2B and A&P is never quantified or explained.

Product development repeatedly converts into new mandates — mPower fund accounting now used by 8 AMCs, 60% of pension fund managers and most insurers; XAlt underpins a 37-38% AIF share; mPower Wealth won five contracts within three months of launch.
scores.quote: in the month of October, we have launched mPower Wealth ... in a matter of 3 months, we signed five large contracts in wealth and marquee names such as Tata Capital, Aditya Birla Wealth

scores.rationale: Hexagram was a textbook complementary bolt-on that scaled well, but the October 2025 Ascent deal is materially larger and has diluted group profitability — margins compressed and PAT went flat — so post-deal OPM has worsened rather than improved so far.
scores.quote: margins have compressed and one would expect it to given we have added nearly -- on an annualized basis, little over $22 million of international revenue with little to no margin

scores.rationale: Distribution policy, dividends and buybacks are not discussed; the only capital-allocation reference is retaining cash for expansion.
scores.quote: We have a dry powder of almost INR570 crores sitting in cash and cash equivalents, which we will utilize as per the Board policy for business expansio

scores.rationale: Asset-light platform model — volumes grew ~28% with a net headcount reduction in FY23 and EBITDA margins ran 44-45% — protected by regulatory licensing and client switching costs, though recent capex-heavy international build has diluted returns.
scores.quote: we have seen a significant rise in the overall volumes ... it is at 28% increase in volumes across our lines of businesses ... with a net headcount reduction during this period

scores.rationale: Sustained, broad-based share capture from a non-dominant base across every line: MF AUM share 30.3%→33%, Issuer Solutions market-cap share 43%→52%, AIF 30%→38%, and pensions from 0% to over 10% in four years.
scores.quote: in a limited period of 4 years, we moved from 0% market share to now close to 10% market share, which was otherwise dominated pretty much in a monopolistic scenario prior to KFintech entering

scores.rationale: Credible, multi-year, executed geographic expansion — >50% AMC share in Malaysia, wins in Philippines/Thailand, BlackRock Aladdin marquee-administrator status, and now 18 countries with organic international revenue still growing 32% year-on-year.
scores.quote: Even if you exclude Ascent, just the KFin's organic business has grown over 32%

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/AUM-led while pricing and mix are actively negative — April 2025 price discounts plus an adverse shift into low-yield passives meant 21% AUM growth translated into only ~11% revenue growth.
scores.quote: our AUM has grown in line with the industry at about 21%, but that, of course, did not necessarily translate into revenues as they grown only about a little over 11%. Reasons we all know part of that was the pricing discounts

scores.rationale: The business is levered to capital-market cycles and is currently at a trough — mark-to-market erosion, IPO issuance withheld, 2 million folios lost — with identifiable upturn triggers (Jio IPO pipeline, ETF-mix reversal, crypto fund recovery).
scores.quote: Many primary issuance have been withheld in the context of where the market is

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — Indian financialization of savings, demat accounts up 17% off a 25 crore base, SIP compounding, plus a $70 trillion US alternatives market barely tapped.
scores.quote: U.S. alone is a $70 trillion alternatives and public market funds ... We haven't even scratched the surface

scores.rationale: Balance sheet is prudent (cash-positive, no leverage flagged) and investment continues through a weak market, but the Ascent deal was a sizeable, margin-dilutive acquisition rather than the small bolt-on discipline the parameter rewards.
scores.quote: we have acquired Ascent Fund Solutions in the month of October ... with little to no margin given the very early stage of the entity

scores.rationale: A three-axis diversification strategy articulated five years ago has been delivered against scepticism — non-MF revenue now ~40% of the total — with tenacious multi-year pursuits like the 18-month BlackRock Aladdin qualification.
scores.quote: four years back, when this strategy was unveiled, there was a fair amount of skepticism ... but lo and behold, in a matter of four years, a near 40% of the revenue comes from businesses which are beyond

scores.rationale: Calls are substantive and operationally detailed, but the CEO's framing is consistently superlative and self-promotional ('stellar', 'superlative', 'very, very excited'), so this is neither celebrity-driven nor notably low-profile.
scores.quote: Ascent, our acquisition that happened in the October of the previous year, continues its stellar performance

scores.rationale: Talent retention and capability-building are stated priorities and the senior bench has been broadened (Murarka moving from IR to International CFO/M&A, Gattani taking IR), but no systematic development programme or succession pipeline is described.
scores.quote: none of this is truly possible without retaining strong talent ... KFin Tech continues to invest in talent both in terms of additional new account as well as in terms of retention of key personnel

scores.rationale: Management volunteers unflattering facts — losing Navi to CAMS, price discounts, equity share slippage, folio erosion, Ascent's zero margin — and explains causes, though it habitually wraps them in optimistic 'in spite and despite' framing.
scores.quote: We have had a terrific quarter ... one of our erstwhile client Navi has chosen to partner with CAMS

scores.rationale: Much of the headline growth is market beta (AUM mark-to-market), and management itself concedes client AMC performance is outside its control, so skill is only partly separable — though share gains during a down market do provide some independent evidence.
scores.quote: winning the mandate is important, providing technological edge for our clients to grow faster is all that we have in our controllables and the rest is something that is dependent on how clients perform

scores.rationale: Near-universal touchpoint with Indian financial investors and a licensed position as one of only three CRAs and two MF RTAs gives quasi-monopoly standing in several niches, though it is the number-two, not the mind-share leader, in the core MF book.
scores.quote: Nearly every individual in India who has invested in a financial asset class has some connection with KFin Technologies

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real — transitions take two to three quarters of complex migration work — creating captive, sticky mandates, but clients do occasionally move (Navi to CAMS; PNB to KFin), so lock-in is strong rather than absolute.
scores.quote: it takes roughly about 2 to 3 quarters depending upon the size and complexity of the contract for us to be able to transition it

scores.rationale: The Indian MF RTA market is a duopoly rather than a stable oligopoly, and large AMC customers demonstrably hold negotiating power — KFin conceded price discounts in April 2025 that materially depressed revenue yield.
scores.quote: part of that was the pricing discounts that were given in the month of April 2025

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are extremely high (regulatory licences, only two MF RTAs, three CRAs, no new entrants mentioned in 17 calls), but pricing rationality is imperfect given the FY26 discount round.
scores.quote: we have secured the license to become the second central record keeping agent for National Pension System

scores.rationale: Clear weak incumbents to feed on — the pension market leader is ceding share as KFin grows 3-3.5x industry, and international markets offer sub-scale boutique administrators, with the third CRA left 'fairly distant'.
scores.quote: that basically explains in terms of the superior technology solutions and the market share we are taking away from the current market leader and keeping a very distant third

scores.rationale: Far from obscure — a listed, heavily analyst-covered company hosting quarterly calls via Kotak and IIFL, with private-equity and bank shareholders and a widely discussed India-financialization narrative.
scores.quote: Kotak Mahindra Bank acquiring sub-10% stake in us and of course the December of 29 of the previous year, momentous day for KFin Tech when the Company got successfully listed

scores.rationale: High gross margins and steady, sticky demand from the compounding SIP book, but there is no image- or taste-driven pricing power — the company competes partly on being the cheaper option and had to grant discounts.
scores.quote: our contribution directly to help our clients grow in the form of technological solutions and the other value-added solutions we're able to provide at extremely compelling cost propositions

scores.rationale: Clients buy regulatory certainty and operational reliability — evidenced by the emphasis on cybersecurity scores, ESG ratings and the multi-year trust-building required to be admitted to BlackRock's marquee administrator list.
scores.quote: It is a very complex process to be identified as one of the global marquee providers

scores.rationale: Direct client intimacy and a widening sales footprint — 'feet on street' across 18 countries now driving cross-sell of pensions and wealth into Ascent's client base — supports a genuine access advantage.
scores.quote: the feet on street that our subsidiary has across 18 countries is proving to be invaluable in terms of, one, securing RFPs

scores.rationale: Customers are corporates (AMCs, listed issuers, banks, insurers) and the offer is correctly matched to them — cost/TCO propositions plus deep operational switching-cost lock-in and multi-product cross-sell, not retail intangibles.
scores.quote: 26 out of 46 asset management companies are KFin Tech's clients ... We crossed 10,500 total corporate client as of 31st March

scores.rationale: A deep, multi-product proprietary stack (mPower TA+FA, XAlt, data lake, mobility, mPower Wealth) is the stated reason for win rates in India, GIFT City and abroad, and is uniquely integrated versus competitors.
scores.quote: we continue to be probably the only player in the country who have a proprietary fit-for-purpose platform, a fully integrated transfer agency and fund administration together

scores.rationale: There are useful ecosystem spillovers — a custodian/trustee client channelling its AMCs to KFin, and the BlackRock Aladdin partner network — but no genuine self-reinforcing two-sided network that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: the contracts which that entity will get from other asset management companies will also be our clients

scores.rationale: Distribution and service reach is broad and hard to replicate — largest registrar by folios in India, ~225 million folios, 10,500 corporate clients, ~500 international clients across 18 countries — in a business where servicing capability is decisive.
scores.quote: KFin Tech has close to 225 million folios which makes KFin Tech amongst the largest registrars in this world

scores.rationale: Very high and rising growth capex — 7 new hospitals launched in 2025, 800-bed Kondapur flagship, Thane, Chennai lease — but incremental ROIC is so far negative, with new units eroding INR 32 crores of EBITDA in Q4 FY26 and group margin falling from 26.6% to 21.1%.
scores.quote: the EBITDA erosion is to the extent of about INR 32 crores

scores.rationale: A&P appears as episodic awareness events (mass BP screening, World Cancer Day with a film star, Guinness-record breast cancer camp) with no disclosed spend or demonstrated link to sales; brand-building is real but unquantified.
scores.quote: accomplished 2,04,000 numbers, more than double our expectations due to vigorous campaigning

scores.rationale: No true R&D; spend is on procuring frontier equipment and hosting academic events, which does seed new clinical programs but is purchased rather than developed capability.
scores.quote: Launch of India's first Tulsa Pro for Prostate Cancer care treatment

scores.rationale: Sunshine was a complementary bolt-on in the home market bought at a low valuation whose margin was lifted from 17.8% toward ~26% over two years, and future deals are explicitly small (400-500 beds), though the fix took longer than promised.
scores.quote: Sunshine Hospitals which is operating at 17.8% EBITDA margin

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend discussion across five years; the capital action is the opposite — a INR 1,500 crore dilutive QIP to retire debt after the share price and earnings weakened (FY26 EPS down 37%).
scores.quote: we are planning for a QIP in a month or two

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy: greenfield hospitals funded 60-65% by debt taking 3-5 years to commission, net debt built from a net-cash position in FY23 to ~INR 3,000 crores by FY26 with returns still ahead.
scores.quote: right now, we have a debt of almost INR 3,000 plus crores

scores.rationale: Small national share with real runway and demonstrated capture in new micro-markets — Mahadevapura reached INR 17 crores/month within 8-9 months with visibility to INR 25-30 crores — though the core Telangana cluster is already mature at 5-10% growth.
scores.quote: We are doing an average of INR 17 crores a month based on Q4 numbers

scores.rationale: Credible multi-state expansion from two states to 25 hospitals across five states plus Chennai, with Nagpur/Nashik turning EBITDA-positive faster than guided, but execution has slipped on insurance empanelment and Bangalore losses (Electronic City INR 25 crores in one quarter).
scores.quote: We now have 25 hospitals across 5 states

scores.rationale: FY26 ARPOB rose 14% and ARPP 11.4% on genuine case-mix upgrade (transplants, onco, payer-mix shift away from Aarogyasri), though volumes also grew 15% so growth is mix-and-volume rather than mix-led alone.
scores.quote: it's a little bit of everything, case mix, pricing and the payer mix

scores.rationale: Calls contain no discussion of an end-market cycle; hospital demand is presented as non-cyclical, and the only trough discussed is the company's own new-unit J-curve.

Indian private healthcare is in secular expansion — rising insurance penetration, government health allocation, and tertiary care migrating into tier-2/3 towns — but the mature home cluster's high-single-digit growth caps how much of that KIMS captures organically.
scores.quote: excellent medical care and latest technology is now available at tier 2 and 3 centres wherever KIMS is there

scores.rationale: Leverage moved from net cash of INR 196 crores in FY23 to over INR 3,000 crores of debt plus a INR 1,500 crore QIP, and guidance flipped within a month from 'debt has peaked, no new expansion' to fresh acquisitions and greenfields.
scores.quote: the idea is we retire some debt and use the cash flow to do more greenfield projects

scores.rationale: Founder-led for 20+ years with willingness to absorb multi-year losses and long gestation — Nagpur was turned around after 'a lot of problems' and greenfields are underwritten on 3-5 year horizons — though independence is untested against the current balance-sheet strain.
scores.quote: greenfield expansion, which will anyways take three to five years before they get commissioned

scores.rationale: Opening remarks routinely feature patriotic and political commentary, celebrity chief guests, and record-chasing publicity rather than substance-first reporting.
scores.quote: KIMS Usha Lakshmi Breast unit got 2 Guiness book of world record for largest breast cancer awareness program

scores.rationale: Systematic clinical talent building — named specialty leaders, academic masterclasses, a dedicated Bangalore cluster CEO, and near-zero doctor attrition in the most contested market — offset by heavy churn in the CFO and board/chairman ranks over FY22-FY25.
scores.quote: there has not been any doctor attrition in KIMS Kondapur. We just lost 1 doctor among the 100 doctors

scores.rationale: Consistently quantifies one-offs and discloses unit-level losses without prompting, and openly owns misjudgements such as underestimating insurance empanelment timelines and being unable to explain the April 2022 volume lull.
scores.quote: what we underestimated is the time it takes to now get insurance empanelments vis-a-vis how it was before

scores.rationale: The assessment survives the halo test because separately disclosed cluster data shows mature units still earning ~29% EBITDA while headline margin collapsed to 19.9%, isolating operating skill from the expansion drag rather than relying on flattering aggregates.
scores.quote: almost 28.5% or 29% of EBITDA margin from matured unit we continue to maintain

scores.rationale: Holds a referral-monopoly position in specific quaternary niches in its region — 100 heart-lung transplants in a year, South India's first Gamma Knife, first Tulsa Pro in India — which competitors cannot quickly replicate.
scores.quote: Launch of South India's first Gamma Knife for brain tumours

scores.rationale: In AP/Telangana tier-2/3 towns KIMS is effectively the only tertiary provider, creating a regional near-monopoly, though patient switching costs are low and metro markets are fully contested.
