scores.rationale: There are visibly weaker players ceding ground — AmbitionBox overtook the category leader in reviews, 99acres has been taking supply and traffic share month after month, and Jeevansathi has overtaken rivals in Hindi markets — though the donors (Magicbricks/Housing, Shaadi/BharatMatrimony) remain well-funded.
scores.quote: Ambition Box... grew handsomely to overtake our sort of the leading competitor in its space

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a widely-tracked large-cap internet name with heavy sell-side coverage, a celebrated founder and adjacent markets that have repeatedly attracted large pools of competing capital.
scores.quote: there's a lot of new money which is coming to the space

scores.rationale: Brand-driven pricing power is evident in structurally higher revenue per hire in premium segments and near-100% gross margin economics, with demand steady enough that billings still grew ~10% through the worst of the hiring downcycle.
scores.quote: Revenue per hire is structurally higher in this segment and we see further headroom for improvement

scores.rationale: Customers buy outcome certainty — curated, verified candidate flow and reduced time-to-hire — which management argues becomes more valuable, not less, as AI floods the market with low-signal applications.
scores.quote: potentially increasing the relevance of specialized curated platforms like Naukri

scores.rationale: Deliberate build-out of physical sales coverage from ~70 towards 100 cities plus intra-city office density gives direct customer intimacy with SMEs, complemented by a self-serve online channel that took the B2C online revenue mix from 27% to 53%.
scores.quote: Our goal is to get to 100 cities in a couple of years. We perhaps are already in more than 70 cities.

scores.rationale: The benefit types are correctly matched — corporate B2B customers are sold reliability, workflow lock-in and data products (AI-Rex, Talent Pulse), while retail jobseekers and matrimony/education users are sold brand, image and convenience via Naukri 360 and Jeevansathi.
scores.quote: paid users as a percentage of the monthly active user base have also risen from 1.2% to 2.2% over the last 15 months

scores.rationale: The edge is real but is data-led rather than patent-led — proprietary two-sided behavioural data feeding matching engines, with AI now delivering measurable internal efficiency and new products across all four verticals.
scores.quote: These efforts have already delivered 15-30% efficiency gains across various parts of our businesses.

scores.rationale: A textbook self-reinforcing two-sided network that has strengthened over the period — Naukri resumes 100m to 115m against 120,000+ recruiters, and 99acres converting supply share gains into traffic share gains into response growth.
scores.quote: it strengthens the case for platforms like ours with our proprietary datasets, two-side network effects, and deep domain context

scores.rationale: A feet-on-street sales network no digital rival in India matches, deliberately deepened during the downturn to reach SMEs in tier-2/3 cities where service and hand-holding are essential to selling the product.
scores.quote: cities for example in NCR where we used to have 3 offices earlier... now we have 6 offices to service our customers better and to grow coverage

scores.rationale: Large and rising growth capex across Zambia thermal Phase 2 ($400m), 100MW solar ($90m), avocado ($55m) and Kawambwa sugar ($100m), but incremental returns look pedestrian (solar payback 10-12 years, avocado peak revenue only $22m and not before ~2032), so the scale is there without demonstrated high incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: For the 300-megawatt expansion thermal plant, total capex outlay is $400 million. And for the 100-megawatt solar plant, capex outlay is $90 million.

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the calls; the businesses are commodity power, alloys and coal sold on contracts.
No R&D spend or R&D-driven product pipeline is discussed anywhere; mineral exploration in Ivory Coast and lithium is prospecting, not R&D.

Growth has been greenfield rather than acquisitive, with only tiny speculative resource-licence purchases (Ivory Coast manganese, lithium) and no bolt-on of an already-strong business whose OPM improved post-deal.
scores.quote: Currently, exploration is on in Ivory Coast... How much have we invested in Ivory Coast so far? Less than a million dollars.

scores.rationale: Distribution improved over the period (record INR8.50 dividend in FY26, $50m buyback) but the buyback was inside a wholly-owned subsidiary rather than at listed-company level, and management deflected repeated shareholder pressure for years while cash piled up, so policy is improving but not yet coherent or valuation-driven.
scores.quote: Nava Global bought back the shares. Nava still remains the 100% owner.

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-heavy — $400m of capex for $180-200m of annual revenue on Phase 2 and $90m for $15-16m from solar — implying asset turns well below 1x with no offsetting moat.
scores.quote: On the 300-megawatt thermal power plant in case of full year operations, the expected revenue is $180 million to $200 million

scores.rationale: Maamba is capturing share as Zambian hydro falters, but the metals division is losing ground to dumped domestic material and Indian merchant power realisations are falling, so there is no consistent share-capture trajectory.
scores.quote: we are seeing a lot of that material being dumped in the domestic market, which is essentially causing the prices to come down

scores.rationale: Zambia has been executed credibly over the period — debt fully repaid, ~100% plant availability, Phase 2 PPA signed and construction underway, plus new Zambian solar, sugar and avocado ventures — though this is asset expansion rather than a brand that travels.
scores.quote: The Maamba Energy Limited power plant operated at near perfect 100% plant availability

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/capacity and commodity-cycle led with prices moving against them — Phase 2 tariff is below Phase 1 (9.7c vs 10.3c), Indian exchange power down 12% YoY and ferro alloy realisations falling.
scores.quote: If you look at the exchange pricing itself, I think there's been a drop of about 12% year-on-year.

scores.rationale: Ferro alloys look near a cyclical trough with an 8% QoQ price uptick and safeguard duties, but domestic power realisations are simultaneously falling, so there is no single identifiable bottom-of-cycle position.
scores.quote: there's been an improvement of pricing by about 8%

scores.rationale: Zambian electricity demand is structurally short as a ~95% hydro system suffers drought and diversifies toward thermal and solar baseload, which is a genuine secular end-market expansion for MEL.
scores.quote: initially, Zambia was almost 95% hydro when we came into the picture with thermal

scores.rationale: Management deleveraged to debt-free at standalone, kept Zambian debt non-recourse, funded Phase 2 equity out of arrears rather than parent cash, and grew organically without large acquisitions.
scores.quote: The debt has been completely repaid both by Nava, Maamba Energy and also Nava Bharat Energy. That's why there is no interest cost.

scores.rationale: Over four years they renegotiated the ZESCO tariff, pursued arbitration and ground $563m of receivables down to $30.5m while restructuring debt and starting Phase 2 — a long, independent, tenacious execution.
scores.quote: The outstanding amount as of now is $563 million... The arrears amount that is yet to be paid is about $30.5 million.

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, sparsely attended and factual, management refuses to speculate publicly on land values or arbitration, and there is no promotional posturing.
scores.quote: No, I'm not going to speculate on the valuation of the land right now.

scores.rationale: Key roles are concentrated in the promoter family (Ashwin and Nikhil Devineni) with CFO turnover and no discussion of a systematic talent pipeline; the only people-related disclosure is ESOPs and wage hikes as a cost line.
scores.quote: This is partly on account of ESOPs we are giving to employees, to some extent on account of the labor code

scores.rationale: Management explains adverse items directly — the deferred tax hit, ferro alloy dumping pressure, declining domestic power prices — and admits when it cannot commit to numbers, though capital-allocation intentions stay deliberately vague.
scores.quote: profitability was impacted by a certain accounting-led tax adjustments at MEL

scores.rationale: Record profits are largely attributable to arbitration/arrears recovery, upstream dividends, buyback proceeds and a Singareni coal price cut rather than repeatable operating skill, so headline results overstate underlying franchise quality.
scores.quote: The growth was primarily supported by healthy upstream dividend flows from our overseas investments and buyback proceeds received during the year.

scores.rationale: Maamba is effectively Zambia's only large thermal baseload with a captive mine-to-mouth coal supply and a 20-year PPA, giving it a monopoly-like position in the utility's supply mix.
scores.quote: We have our own captive mine there, right? So, it's a mine-to-mouth power plant.

scores.rationale: The Zambian asset is a regional quasi-monopoly with high switching costs — ZESCO cannot replace dispatchable baseload when hydro fails — evidenced by it signing a second 20-year PPA for Phase 2.
scores.quote: The PPA is for a term of 20-years and the offtake starts post COD

scores.rationale: The core customer is a single state utility with overwhelming negotiating power — it forced the tariff down from 11.57 to 9.06 cents and withheld hundreds of millions for years — while ferro alloys is fragmented and price-taking.
scores.quote: it was about 11.57, and then the new tariff is 9.06

scores.rationale: New entrants have appeared on both sides — competing coal mines around Maamba triggering a price war and multiple new Zambian solar plants — while ferro alloy pricing is being wrecked by dumping.
scores.quote: we have started to see more competition with new mines opening around us by different players. So, there was a certain level of a price war going on.

scores.rationale: Underperforming Zambian hydro cedes generation share to Maamba, but in metals Nava is on the receiving end of stronger dumped supply, so donators exist in one segment and Nava is the donor in the other.
scores.quote: right now Zambia is going through big power crisis, as the hydros are working at suboptimal plant load factors

scores.rationale: A Hyderabad-listed mid-cap operating a Zambian mine-mouth power complex, avocado plantation and Kawambwa sugar project is exactly the kind of unglamorous, hard-to-replicate niche that mainstream capital ignores.
scores.quote: steady execution of the Kawambwa Sugar project

scores.rationale: Products are undifferentiated commodities — silico manganese, merchant power, thermal coal — with realisations set by exchanges and dumping, so there is no image- or taste-based pricing power despite optically high gross margins.
scores.quote: the prices, which you're seeing in quarter 1 have tapered down in quarter 2

scores.rationale: Customers do buy reliability: ZESCO contracts for dependable baseload at 97-100% availability when hydro fails, and Japanese mills take 40% of alloy output on annual contracts for supply certainty.
scores.quote: we have a long-term arrangement, a yearly contract with the two major Japanese mills, which essentially accounts for 40% of our production

scores.rationale: There is physical proximity advantage in the mine-to-mouth structure and local Zambian coal customer base, but no evidence of superior distribution access or a strong sales organisation.
scores.quote: No, we have a large customer base. Our sales for our coal business is fairly healthy

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/state (ZESCO, steel mills, cement plants) and management has matched it with the right instruments — 20-year PPAs, five-year bilateral power contracts and annual/quarterly fixed-price alloy contracts that lock in offtake.
scores.quote: we have engaged into a long-term 5-year period bilateral contract with Tamil Nadu for our 60-megawatt IPP plant in Odisha

scores.rationale: Across 16 calls there is no technology differentiation discussed — the assets are standard thermal, solar and submerged-arc furnace capacity, and the only 'product diversification' cited (ferro silicon) was later abandoned.
scores.quote: We've actually discontinued ferro silicon, because the market for silico manganese is more favorable at the moment.

scores.rationale: The business model — bulk power sold to one utility, coal to local industrials, alloys to steel mills — has no two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic of any kind.
scores.quote: It's the Southern African power pool members which other countries and companies can buy power based on their requirements.

scores.rationale: Output is sold through exchanges, tenders and a handful of bulk contracts rather than any proprietary reach, and the company has repeatedly been hostage to third-party logistics and fuel supply (Singareni coal diversion).
scores.quote: when tariffs go high, they divert almost all the coal to government power plants and give us nothing

scores.rationale: Sustained large greenfield/brownfield growth capex (Rs 540cr agro-specialty, Rs 450cr AHF, Rs 288cr cGMP-4, R32 doublings, Chemours, MPP debottlenecking) executed on announced timelines and now converting into revenue with ROCE at 21% and EBITDA more than doubling in FY26.
scores.quote: Execution of Wave-1 projects AHF, cGMP4 concluded and commissioned during the quarter... Wave-2 projects, namely the MPP debottlenecking, the R32 expansion, HFC expansion and the Chemours project are on track

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the calls; the B2B model makes it immaterial.

R&D spend (Surat R&D/pilot-plant upgradation) consistently converts into commercialised molecules — ~13 new molecules in FY26 plus named agro wins with Rs 40-50cr and Rs 20-30cr peak revenue potential and advanced-materials/semiconductor programs.
scores.quote: we have continued to strengthen our product pipeline in specialty chemical vertical by leveraging on our newly established R&D center at Surat. We have added a new molecule at Surat for global agro major with a peak annual revenue potential around Rs. 40 to Rs. 50 crore

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed in any of the excerpts; growth is entirely organic capex and partnerships.
A regular, earnings-linked dividend (Rs 8.6/share final, 430% of face value) alongside a near-zero-debt balance sheet, but no buyback discipline or articulated distribution policy is evidenced.
scores.quote: the Board in today's meeting has declared a final dividend of INR8.6 per equity share, 430% of the face value

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-heavy — multi-hundred-crore plants (AHF Rs 450cr, agro Rs 540cr, cGMP-4 Rs 288cr) against Rs 3,314cr revenue, with depreciation from new capex visibly depressing PAT in the ramp years — though a moat and improving working capital partly offset.
scores.quote: This reflects higher depreciation costs associated with commissioning of new CAPEXs

scores.rationale: Clear share capture as global innovators de-risk from China, evidenced by moving from transactional supply to technology partner, R32 quota-backed capacity, and sole-site status for the Chemours product.
scores.quote: we are the only manufacturing site for Chemours given the nature of the product

scores.rationale: Export/customer-geography widening is real (Japanese patented agro product, UK/EU/US big-pharma CDMO wins, export R32/R22) but this is customer expansion from Indian sites rather than a geographic footprint build-out.
scores.quote: we have also signed the supply agreement for a patented agro product catering to the Japanese market

scores.rationale: Management explicitly attributes FY26's ~990bps margin gain 70% to new capacity/volume and only 30% to pricing actions, so growth is volume-led, though genuine pricing power and a richer CDMO/specialty mix are demonstrated.
scores.quote: you will see 70% of that for Navin is coming from our capacities coming on the ground, our volumes going up and 30% is coming from affirmative actions on pricing

scores.rationale: The company invested through the FY24-25 agrochem destocking trough and is now riding the refrigerant/agro upturn, but the cyclical upswing is already substantially in the numbers rather than ahead.
scores.quote: There is a slow sort of reset happening. You're seeing some indication of volume recovery

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — low-GWP refrigerant transition, crop-protection yield demand, pharma CDMO outsourcing, and the emerging semiconductor/electronic-chemicals value chain.
scores.quote: increasing adoption of low GWP refrigerants and export opportunities

scores.rationale: Entirely organic growth with no M&A, counter-cyclical capex through the agrochem downturn, and leverage reduced from 0.38x to effectively nil while funding a large capex program.
scores.quote: As of 31 March 2026, our net debt to equity stood at 0.01x negligible, while both ROE and ROCE improved at 20% and 21%

scores.rationale: Long-dated projects have been delivered against commitments (Honeywell greenfield completed through three COVID waves, cGMP-4 and AHF commissioned on stated timelines), though MD/CFO turnover mid-period tempers the continuity of that vision.
scores.quote: We have managed to successfully complete this large and complex project through three tough phases of COVID-19 pandemic

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and understated, with the promoter chairman crediting teams rather than himself and management declining to hype product-level opportunity sizes.
scores.quote: Typically, we don't like to talk about the opportunity size on a product basis

scores.rationale: There is a formal talent program and successful re-hiring of former insiders, but the MD and CFO roles were both filled externally rather than from an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: we've actually just recently ran internally it is called a STAR program, Special Talent Recognition program

scores.rationale: Management set and then met explicit expectations (flagging a soft H1 / stronger H2 well in advance), quantified margin drivers between volume, pricing and currency, and declined to speculate rather than spin — though it deflects some pointed pricing questions.
scores.quote: if you refer to our discussions even in the last call, we had said that FY 25 is going to be a story of two halves... So I think it's playing out as anticipated to be honest

scores.rationale: FY26's doubling of profits owes materially to a favourable refrigerant pricing cycle and currency tailwind alongside genuine execution, and management's own decomposition confirms the result is not purely skill.
scores.quote: there is a currency tailwind. If you analyze the currency tailwind with the inflation figures... a lot of this is a wash

scores.rationale: Selective monopoly-like positions exist — sole global manufacturing site for a Chemours AI-datacentre product and quota-protected R22/R32 rights — but not across the portfolio.
scores.quote: your right to win comes from the quota that you have. And that's exactly what we've always been saying

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real via multi-year MSAs, dedicated plants and lengthy pharma validation cycles that lock customers in once qualified.
scores.quote: a pre-validation has been completed. Usually, this takes about 6 months before you get into the next stage of development or the validation

scores.rationale: Complex HF/fluorination chemistry and the Kigali quota regime leave few credible Indian players, and customers are large innovators who nonetheless need an alternate-to-China partner rather than the cheapest bid.
scores.quote: these global majors wants to keep the alternate supply chain on where they consider Navin in the fluorochemical as one of the partner

scores.rationale: Quota rules cap new refrigerant capacity and chemistry complexity deters entrants, but management itself acknowledges new fluorination players catching up and aggressive Chinese price cutting in agro.
scores.quote: the Chinese competition is really going very aggressive in the price reduction

scores.rationale: Share is being donated less by weak rivals than by geopolitical de-risking away from Chinese suppliers, which nonetheless hands Navin volume with global majors.
scores.quote: our strategy of working closely with the global innovators, is paying off

scores.rationale: Navin is a widely followed large-cap specialty chemical name with heavy sell-side and institutional coverage on every call, and its niches (refrigerants, semis chemicals) attract policy attention and new capital.
scores.quote: we are eyeing a capacity now in excess or 1,20,00 metric tons in India

scores.rationale: Margins are high (32.6% FY26 EBITDA) and pricing can be passed through, but this stems from process capability and contract structure rather than brand image or taste appeal.
scores.quote: we've also been able to pass on a lot of these back to the customers

scores.rationale: The core customer proposition is supply certainty and qualified reliability — global majors pay to keep a validated non-China fluorochemicals partner and bind pricing in long-term contracts.
scores.quote: the pricing structure under which we have entered into understanding with them, it is not going to hit our bottomline

scores.rationale: Relationship depth and business-development reach are stressed, but there is no evidence of a distinctive accessibility or service-proximity advantage over rivals.
scores.quote: The idea of showing this is showing the pipeline, showing the breadth of our business development efforts

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate (top-five global agro innovators, big pharma, Honeywell, Chemours) and the benefit offered — reliability, TCO through route optimisation, and validation-based lock-in — matches that type precisely.
scores.quote: we continuously work with our customers to look at new ways and new routes, new chemistries to produce the same outcome more efficiently... and thereby help them remain competitive

scores.rationale: A deep, escalating fluorination capability stack (helix to HF to complex chemistries) spanning HPP, specialty, CDMO and now high-purity electronic gases, evidenced by stabilising a licensed plant in four weeks versus a three-to-six-month expectation.
scores.quote: What our technology supplier expected us to do in three to six months, the team has really achieved in the record time

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or self-reinforcing platform dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.
Sales are direct B2B contracts with a handful of global accounts; no distribution or service-reach advantage is discussed.

The core digital businesses are deliberately capex-light (esports capex expensed as opex), but the offline arm shows genuine, rising growth capex with excellent incremental returns — Funky Monkey centres at 1-2 per month with sub-one-year breakeven and 35-40% steady-state margins, plus the Smaaash 2.0 rebuild.
scores.quote: These centers have a breakeven period of less than one year. So we can continue to see rapid growth over there.

scores.rationale: A&P is performance user-acquisition rather than brand-building, but it is run with explicit capital-allocation discipline (100% payback in two years, CAC cut from $37.5 to $35.8 while scaling spend) and finally delivered Kiddopia's return to subscriber growth in Q3/Q4 FY26 after years of stagnation.
scores.quote: we usually follow a policy where we want to earn back 100% in two years period of whatever capital we invest in user acquisition

scores.rationale: Development spend does produce a steady flow of new titles (Curve's 6+ releases, Roblox/Animal Jam, narrative IPs, AI tooling), but long-run efficiency is unproven — Curve's revenue was flat year-on-year and NODWIN admits a 60% culling rate on new IPs.
scores.quote: We have a 60% culling rate in IPs that you would test in the first year to second year gestation.

scores.rationale: M&A is the central strategy with real wins (Pro Football Network doubled and turned profitable, Curve, Fusebox) and group gaming margins expanding to 24.7%, but deals are neither small nor uniformly complementary and two have been written off — Freaks4U impaired and INR50 crore of OML/NH7 goodwill written off.
scores.quote: Freaks 4U was always a trap like it was something that we made a mistake

scores.rationale: There is no buyback or dividend policy in evidence across the four years; the company has instead been a serial issuer, raising INR950 crores of equity in FY24 alone, with 'value unlock' framed as selling non-core stakes to redeploy internally rather than returning cash.
scores.quote: we have arisen successfully between the parent entity and our subsidiaries INR 950 crores of equity capital marking our largest fundraise to date

scores.rationale: The business is genuinely asset-light (no capex in esports, mobile/PC publishing), but the required protecting moat is absent — Sportskeeda's revenue fell 38% on a Google core update and Kiddopia was hostage to Apple's IDFA change.
scores.quote: we do not do Capex in this business at all. And everything is treated as an Op ex.

scores.rationale: Nazara is small in a vast market with clear runway and shows real share capture in places (NODWIN top-three globally in esports, gaming revenue +107% in FY26, Human Fall Flat 58m lifetime units), though it is simultaneously losing share in Sportskeeda and adtech.
scores.quote: it is the reason why we are such a dominant in the world and one of the top three companies in the world

scores.rationale: Expansion into the US and Europe has been credible and largely well-executed (Curve in the UK, Fusebox, Bluetile, Pro Football Network, Starladder in Budapest), tempered by the openly admitted failure of the German Freaks4U build-out.
scores.quote: this attempt that we had done to go ahead and build a European business in Germany sp ecifically that didn't work out

scores.rationale: Growth has been consciously mix- and price-led — Kiddopia's subscription price raised to $8.99 with ARPU rising to $7.45, adtech deliberately shedding low-margin managed services, and gaming's share of EBITDA rising from 56% to 90%.
scores.quote: Gaming contribution to EBITDA increased from 56% in FY '25 to 90% in FY '26

scores.rationale: Cyclical elements exist and were navigated (the FY24 media-rights trough from the OTT funding crunch, the GST shock to real-money gaming), but management does not position the company at an identifiable cycle bottom with a defined upturn.
scores.quote: The OT T players, given the start up funding crunch have struggled to raise capital and therefore have kind of slowed down media spends

scores.rationale: The end markets — global gaming, digital advertising, and especially Indian gaming where India is #1 in downloads but outside the top 10 in monetisation — are in clear secular expansion with a long monetisation runway.
scores.quote: Indian gaming today, if you look globally, in ter ms of number of downloads on mobile phones is Number 1 on Google Play... However, we are not even in the top 10 on monetization.

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (net cash ~INR1,450 crores) and there is counter-cyclical buying, but stewardship is the opposite of organic-and-no-big-M&A — a continuous acquisition programme culminating in Bluetile/BestPlay, 'our largest acquisition to date', funded by heavy equity dilution.
scores.quote: FY26 also included our largest acquisition to date of Blue tile and BestPlay

scores.rationale: The founder has run a consistent multi-year strategy with independence and visible tenacity — persisting with Kiddopia through several years of subscriber decline until the COE-led turnaround, and NODWIN's stated three-year IP gestation and ten-year-old IP portfolio.
scores.quote: Kiddopia returned to subscriber growth in Q3 FY '26 after several quarters

scores.rationale: Calls are substantive and delegated to operating CEOs rather than personality-driven, but the company leans on promotional framing (a heavily amplified AI theme, 'building something phenomenal and everlasting') and is a high-visibility listed gaming name.
scores.quote: AI, of course, is a very big theme for us, not just a narrative but a very important aspect of what we are doing today.

scores.rationale: There is a deep operating bench — a dozen subsidiary CEOs presenting, founders retained post-acquisition (Amis, Dinsey, Stauffer, Rathee), and institutionalised Centers of Excellence led by senior hires — though the parent has seen CEO/COO churn (Manish Agarwal, Sudhir Kamath).
scores.quote: Most of the Centers of Excellence are led by very senior people with a lot of in -depth experience at scale

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly owns errors and bad news in plain language — naming Freaks4U a mistake, writing off INR50 crores of goodwill on an IP that missed projections, conceding Sportskeeda has not recovered, and explaining margin dips as deliberate spend rather than dressing them up.
scores.quote: we will continue to optimize costs... Well, I think we have yet not seen the kind of recovery we want to see over there.

scores.rationale: Headline results are hard to attribute to operating skill because consolidation and deconsolidation drive the optics — FY26 gaming revenue 'growth' of 107% is acquisition-fed while consolidated revenue rose only 13%, and Q3 margin expansion was flattered by removing NODWIN.
scores.quote: revenues of INR406 crore, which were lower by 24.1%, primarily due to the deconsolidation of our NODWIN Esports business. However, our EBITDA came in at INR67.8 crore, which was up 29.4%

scores.rationale: Several assets hold genuine mind-share leadership in their niches — NODWIN's dominance of Indian esports plus Comic Con India, and evergreen catalogue titles like Human Fall Flat — even if none is a monopoly in the strict sense.
scores.quote: Human Fall Flat with lifetime sales of 58 million units remains a long tail seller

scores.rationale: Switching costs for consumers are minimal and demonstrably so — Kiddopia runs roughly 7% monthly churn and users move freely between apps, with no captive aftermarket or regional lock-in.
scores.quote: we ha ve seen elevated levels of churn, about 7% monthly churn

scores.rationale: The end markets are fragmented and crowded rather than a stable oligopoly, with management itself naming multiple well-funded competitors in the casual gaming vertical alone.
scores.quote: we can see other competitors, such as Triple Dot, which has been valued at over a billion. We also have Easy brain, which was acquired by M iniclip

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is dictated by external gatekeepers rather than industry rationality — Apple's policy change reset the whole category's economics, Google's core update gutted Sportskeeda traffic, and user-acquisition costs are bid up competitively.
scores.quote: the entire industry has faced the brunt of increased consumer acquisition cost, which has kind of put a margin pressure

scores.rationale: Weak and distressed sellers are abundant and Nazara has repeatedly bought from them — Curve came from a parent that had stopped investing, and the wider market (e.g. Embracer divesting Easybrain) is shedding assets Nazara can absorb cheaply.
scores.quote: before Nazara acquired Curve Games, under the previous parent, Curve Gam es, for the last two years, ha d not been signing a lot of games

scores.rationale: Certain assets sit in genuinely unglamorous, under-covered niches (Pro Football Network, PrimeTimer, Funky Monkey family centres), but Nazara itself is a widely-followed listed gaming stock that actively courts capital and global M&A visibility.
scores.quote: participating in a strong manner in, for example, game developer conference in the US, which is the largest gaming conference in the world and making our name out there

scores.rationale: Owned IP does confer some taste-driven pricing power and high gross margins — PC/console publishing at 39% EBITDA margin and gaming at 24.7% — but Kiddopia's pricing was explicitly the lowest in its category and demand proved far from steady.
scores.quote: FY '26 revenue of INR 261 crores and EBITDA of INR 101 crores at 39% EBITDA margin

scores.rationale: Assurance plays only a minor role — Datawrkz's retained-client base and NODWIN's reliability as a tournament operator for sponsors suggest some trust-based stickiness, but the consumer businesses sell entertainment, not certainty.
scores.quote: out of the total revenue, 67% of revenue is from retained cli ents

scores.rationale: Access to customers runs through third-party gatekeepers (Apple, Google, Steam, Roblox) rather than proprietary reach, though the expanding Funky Monkey centre network provides genuine local accessibility.
scores.quote: we expanded footprint through four new Funky Monkey centers in the quarter

scores.rationale: The mix is coherently retail-led with entertainment/intangible benefits, but the corporate-facing pieces (adtech, sponsorship, media rights) lack the TCO-and-switching-cost lock-in the framework wants, as the media-rights 'glass ceiling' showed.
scores.quote: we will breakthrough this glass ceiling of where the media rights are at this point of time

scores.rationale: There is a real and deepening capability layer — AI applied across creative, UA, ad monetisation and data segmentation, plus Bluetile's AI-native development — but it is applied tooling rather than a proprietary, defensible multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: we are able to really scale our operations by applying AI to each individual department that we have across all the different functions

scores.rationale: Network effects are aspirational rather than demonstrated — the 2022 plan to 'create a network effect' via real-money-gaming consolidation never materialised, and the newer 'rewarded engagement network' and ecosystem stakes are too early to judge.
scores.quote: this is a consolidation play for us in really money gaming, to do scale, to c reate a network effect

scores.rationale: The group has built genuine multi-platform publishing and distribution reach — mobile, PC/console via Curve, offline centres, plus COEs in user acquisition that acquired studios plug into — which is a real, if not unmatchable, advantage.
scores.quote: Every gaming IP we own and increasingly every IP we acquire plugs into the sam e system.

scores.rationale: As an asset-light PMC there is essentially no plant capex; the only growth investment is a small opportunistic land book (39 acres/INR652cr, plus the long-litigated 21-acre Ghitorni parcel) whose high claimed returns remain unrealised after years of delay.
scores.quote: It is our land. So, investment has already made in lands. So, now only we have to take the profit by putting construction.

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-building or marketing investment is discussed in any of the calls; the only 'marketing fee' referenced is 1% revenue NBCC earns from clients, not spend.
scores.quote: we are getting 8% PMC- 1% marketing fee

scores.rationale: R&D is never mentioned across the 15 calls; the only technology reference is a client's 'innovative building technology' grain-storage MoU.
No acquisitions occur in the period — subsidiaries HSCC/HSCL/NSL are pre-existing government transfers and new activity is limited to MoUs, not deals.
scores.quote: NBCC has signing MoU with BHEL for land monetization

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed; the only dividend mentioned is one received from subsidiaries into standalone other income.
scores.quote: approximately INR42 crores is from dividend from our subsidiaries

scores.rationale: The model is genuinely asset-light and capital-efficient — INR12,000cr+ revenue on a tiny asset base with large net cash and construction outsourced to contractors — but the moat is a government mandate rather than a company-owned protection.
scores.quote: we are not executing the project, we hire outside agency

scores.rationale: Order book compounded from INR56,000cr consolidated (Aug 2022) to INR1,27,000-1,28,000cr (FY26) with new mandates spanning DDA, MAHAPREIT, J&K, RIICO, Mumbai Port Trust and court-awarded Supertech, showing continuing capture of new client pools rather than saturation.
scores.quote: NBCC's standalone order book is standing INR 1,12,000 crores, and consolidated order book INR 1,27,000 crores

scores.rationale: Expansion is announced far faster than it is executed — Dubai subsidiary (2024), Africa/Arabian countries, Australia and UAE MoUs produced no disclosed revenue, and even domestic out-of-Delhi wins (Kerala, MAHAPREIT, J&K) remain unstarted years later.
scores.quote: NBCC is planning to start real estate venture in Dubai through wholly-owned subsidiary in Dubai... No. We don't have any land.

scores.rationale: Growth is almost entirely volume/execution-led at an administered fee (8% PMC + 1% marketing), with margin moving only on project mix and real-estate sales, and falling immediately when that mix reverses.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin for quarter-to-quarter have reduced slightly because of lower contribution from our real estate projects and lower marketing fees

scores.rationale: Demand is driven by government budget and approval cycles rather than an identifiable industrial cycle bottom; management cites approval and election-code delays, not a cyclical upturn.
scores.quote: what are the approvals which are pending for redevelopment from the PSUs for this fiscal year that has been halted because of the election period?

scores.rationale: Redevelopment/monetisation of idle government and PSU land is a genuinely long-lived secular pool that management has repeatedly re-stocked from over five years, though realisation depends on state approvals.
scores.quote: various PSUs that have land parcel or they have their old colonies, township colonies. All of them are going to redevelop.

scores.rationale: Balance sheet discipline is real — no debt at NBCC level, clients carry the borrowing, and no acquisitions — but this is partly a statutory constraint, and it sits alongside scattered diversification talk into highways, railways, metro, renewables and Dubai real estate.
scores.quote: NBCC cannot take loan as Land belong to client... we are the project management consultant for them.

scores.rationale: Leadership turned over twice in the window (Gupta to Mahadevaswamy) and targets are handed down by the ministry rather than self-set, while the flagship promise to finish Amrapali 'on or before 31st March 2025' slipped to June 2026.
scores.quote: we are a Govt. Company/CPSE and we are bound by a target set by the administrative Ministry so every year, we should give a minimum growth of 20%

scores.rationale: The management style is bureaucratic rather than celebrity-driven, but the commentary leans heavily on ministerial and Presidential inaugurations and headline national projects.
scores.quote: The inauguration of IIM Sambalpur by Honorable Prime Minister, Honorable President of India inaugurated NBCC built wooden replica of historic flag post

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline appears in any call; the only staffing reference is overheads being fixed salaries.
scores.quote: we have fixed expenditure that is our overheads that is salaries only

scores.rationale: There is real candor in taking the full INR110cr Gurgaon 37D loss upfront and openly naming order-to-execution conversion as the core weakness, but this is offset by repeatedly deferred guidance and refusals to quantify pending wins as 'price sensitive'.
scores.quote: Yes, you are right, the conversion of order book to execution, that is a challenge.

scores.rationale: The headline results owe more to conferred mandates — court-appointed Amrapali and Supertech work, ministry-allotted GPRA colonies — than to demonstrated operating skill, since the self-directed items (Dubai, Jaipur/Coimbatore real estate, MAHAPREIT, J&K) have consistently stalled.
scores.quote: Supreme Court of India has upheld the NCLAT order appointing NBCC to complete Supertech projects

scores.rationale: NBCC has become the default national solution for stalled housing and government colony redevelopment, a position validated by the judiciary itself.
scores.quote: court verdict shows about believing NBCC's capability and delivering stress real estate projects... 'no courts shall interfere with the implementation of this decision'

scores.rationale: It holds an effective regional lock on central Delhi GPRA redevelopment and repeat mandates from the same client pool (DDA, MCD, PWD, MoHUA), though the tie is administrative preference rather than contractual switching cost.
scores.quote: DDA is going to give 2 more colonies to us for redevelopment. MCD, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, PWD.

scores.rationale: The CPSE construction-consultancy field is a stable small group, but the end customer is the government itself, which sets the fee and the growth target, leaving NBCC with no negotiating power.
scores.quote: we are bound by a target set by the administrative Ministry

scores.rationale: Navratna CPSE status and nomination-based awards keep new entrants out and the fee is administered rather than bid down in discount wars, with the 8%+1% structure unchanged across the whole period.
scores.quote: Otherwise, we are getting 1% marketing fee. There is no reduction in marketing fee.

scores.rationale: Failed private developers are a continuous source of transferred work — Amrapali (38,000 units) and now Supertech (~50,000 units) both landed with NBCC after the incumbents collapsed.
scores.quote: The project comprises of approximately 50,000 units, of which 40,000 units already sold

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — nationally publicised projects, ministerial inaugurations, Supreme Court coverage and investors openly discussing a INR1 lakh crore market cap.
scores.quote: I see that this company could be more than a 1 lakh crore market cap company over the next couple of years

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are structurally thin at ~6% EBITDA and set by an administered fee rather than by what the brand can command.
scores.quote: EBITDA will be in the vicinity of 6% to 6.5%

scores.rationale: Customers and courts select NBCC for certainty of completion on complex distressed projects rather than on price, which is the clearest genuine customer benefit in the record.
scores.quote: demonstrates NBCC's capability to solve the country's complex problems and contribute towards nation building

scores.rationale: It maintains direct, pan-India institutional access to ministries, PSUs and state governments and converts that intimacy into MoUs and nominated orders, though not through a conventional sales force.
scores.quote: We have given the presentation to DDA also, Delhi Development Authority. So, two projects will come within this week only.

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely institutional/government and is served with reliability as promised, but there is no lock-in or TCO premium — the client dictates fee, funding and timing.
scores.quote: It is the state government project... So getting approval is taking some time.

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology or R&D intensity exists; the actual construction is subcontracted and the differentiator is a government mandate, not engineering depth.
scores.quote: while we are not executing the project, we hire outside agency

scores.rationale: No two-sided platform or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls; the business is discrete project mandates.
Reach is broad — pan-India via HSCC/HSCL/NSL plus Maldives, Mauritius and Africa — but it is not a service network rivals cannot replicate, and reach has repeatedly failed to convert to execution.
scores.quote: out of INR1,26,000 crore... INR50,000 crores is actually not moving nothing has started over there

scores.rationale: Capex rose sharply from ~Rs.250 crore budgeted in FY25 to Rs.912 crore incurred in FY26 (incl. Rs.320 crore TBM in CWIP), yet revenue fell 9% and standalone EBITDA slipped to 8.44%, so the incremental return on this equipment spend is poor rather than high.
scores.quote: we have incurred a capex of INR344 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR912 crores we have incurred in the current year, which includes a capital work in progress for TBM about INR320 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend anywhere across the calls — as a government/institutional EPC contractor the topic never arises.
R&D spend, product development or innovation pipeline is never discussed in any of the excerpts.

No bolt-on acquisitions at all; the M&A record visible is unwinding past diversification — divesting NCC Vizag Urban in tranches, reducing group-company exposure, and fully impairing the Oman investment.
scores.quote: the impairment is done in the case of an investment at Oman ... we have made an impairment of INR21.3 crores as an exceptional item

scores.rationale: Buybacks and dividend policy are never discussed; the only capital-structure event mentioned is promoters subscribing to warrants (an inflow, not a distribution), so there is no basis to judge distribution discipline.
scores.quote: promoters have brought in INR106 crore towards subscription of warrants issued to them

scores.rationale: Although fixed-asset light, the business is heavily working-capital consuming with 119 working-capital days, unbilled revenue at 44% of turnover and debtors at 87 days in Q3 FY26, and there is no moat protecting returns.
scores.quote: working capital ... stands at INR 6,036 crores, which is 37% of the turnover. And in terms of working capital days, it is 119 days

scores.rationale: Order book compounded from Rs.40,616 crore (Aug 2022) to a record Rs.83,004 crore with FY26 inflows of Rs.31,884 crore, evidence of continued share capture in a fragmented industry — though revenue conversion is lagging.
scores.quote: Our consolidated order book as of 31st March '26, stood at INR 83,004 crores, which is about 16% increase over the last year, and highest in the company's history

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic state-hopping (AP, Bihar, UP, Maharashtra) driven by budget allocations rather than a travelling brand, while the international footprint has been written down to zero.
scores.quote: With this, the international outstanding, whatever is there, that completely impaired

scores.rationale: Growth is purely order-volume driven on competitively bid fixed-price contracts with no pricing power — margins have drifted down from 9.51% (Q1 FY23) to 8.44% standalone in Q4 FY26 as input costs rose.
scores.quote: EBITDA levels remained at 9.51% ... Slight dip in EBITDA margins is on account of increased material cost

scores.rationale: FY26 looks like a cyclical trough — 9% revenue decline on client payment delays — with an identifiable upturn: record 4x book-to-bill backlog, JJM collections resuming (Rs.1,000 crore in Q4) and a Rs.67,670 crore FY27 JJM budget provision.
scores.quote: they have created INR 17,000 crores provision to be released in the next 2 months ... For the next year also ... a budget of INR 67,670 crores

scores.rationale: The end market — Indian public infrastructure — is in a multi-year secular expansion with repeated budget thrust cited (Gati Shakti, Rs.26,000 crore infra and Rs.22,000 crore Bihar allocations, Rs.15,000 crore Amaravati), though it depends on government fiscal priority rather than private demand.
scores.quote: in the Union budget is a special allocation of funds given by Rs. 26,000 crores for infra development and Rs. 22,000 crores funds for Bihar state

scores.rationale: Growth has been organic with no large acquisitions, leverage kept modest (D/E 0.30x at FY26-end), group-company exposure steadily reduced and non-core real estate divested — though debt did spike to Rs.2,980 crore mid-FY26.
scores.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.30x at the end of Q4 FY26 as against 0.40 at the end of Q3 FY26

scores.rationale: The company has shown tenacity across a full cycle — surviving the 2019 AP order cancellations, patiently pursuing revival of abandoned Amaravati orders, and continuing to bid selectively through the FY26 downturn.
scores.quote: We will continue to bid depending on the risk/reward equation. In fact, we have already bagged a few projects in this financial year as well

scores.rationale: Calls are run by finance and IR professionals rather than a celebrity promoter-CEO, the tone is workmanlike and data-heavy, and the promoter family MDs stepped back from board roles in FY2023.
scores.quote: MANAGEMENT: MR. R.S. RAJU – DIRECTOR PROJECTS ... MR. SANJAY PUSARLA – EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT

scores.rationale: No talent-development or succession discussion in four years of calls, against visible churn — three Managing Directors and the Chairman exited around FY2023 and the Company Secretary changed twice within FY26 (Srinivasa Murthy to Sisir K Mishra to A Karthik).
scores.quote: For NCC Limited A Karthik Company Secretary

scores.rationale: Disclosure of balance-sheet data is granular and forthcoming, but guidance credibility has broken down — FY26 guidance was formally withdrawn, FY27 guidance refused, and management deflected direct questions to external variables while an analyst openly pushed back.
scores.quote: We have formally withdrawn -- that is no guidance as we speak for FY '26

scores.rationale: Stripping out the halo, the strong FY23-FY25 numbers track government capex and AP political change rather than durable operating skill, and the moment client payments slowed the same management delivered a 9% revenue decline and margin compression.
scores.quote: unless the payments are forthcoming on time, unless all the ROWs, every permit, everything is in place, there is little that we could do

scores.rationale: NCC occupies no monopoly-like position in any customer's mind — it is one of many L1 bidders across buildings, water, roads, mining and T&D, with no aftermarket or service annuity beyond small O&M tails.
scores.quote: the order book continues to be well diversified with Buildings accounting for approximately 31%; Transportation, 22%; Electrical T&D, 18%

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs — each project is separately tendered and clients can and do cancel or abandon awarded work, as the AP government did in 2019.
scores.quote: In 2019, the government has cancelled certain orders. And at the same time, they abandoned certain orders

scores.rationale: The industry is fragmented and the end customer holds all the negotiating power, dictating pricing, billing protocols, work priorities and payment timing, as seen with UP JJM, AP and the Maharashtra smart-meter reprioritisation.
scores.quote: Now the client changed, priorities changed that one and they given priority to install the meters at the offices rather than at the total remote villages

scores.rationale: Prequalification and bonding create some barrier, but awards are lowest-bid tenders and pricing is not rational enough to protect returns — margins guided at 9.5-10% have drifted to ~8.4-9% despite a record backlog.
scores.quote: we achieved an EBITDA of 8.44% for Q4 FY26 as against 9.21% of the corresponding quarter of the previous year

scores.rationale: Rather than harvesting weak rivals, NCC is currently the laggard — analysts contrast its soft inflows and withdrawn guidance with peers like L&T and Kalpataru who continue to guide and execute.
scores.quote: L&T is the largest infra company despite having a huge exports order, they have given a guidance. Kalpataru yesterday gave guidance, other infra companies are giving guidance

scores.rationale: NCC is anything but under the radar — it is covered and questioned quarter after quarter by DAM, JM, ICICI, Dolat, Nuvama, HDFC, Centrum, Phillip and Anand Rathi.
scores.quote: The next question comes from the line of Shravan Shah with Dolat Capital

scores.rationale: There is no image or taste premium — single-digit EBITDA margins (8-9.5%) on cost-plus-style construction, with material inflation passed through only via contract clauses rather than brand pricing power.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin approximately at 9%, remaining consistent with the company's margin profile

scores.rationale: Scale and a 30-year track record do buy prequalification for complex work such as tunnels, coastal roads and TBM-based projects, but selection remains price-led tendering so trust is not decisive over price.
scores.quote: including those projects -- large projects like tunnel project and coastal road project. There also, we have got all the clearances

scores.rationale: Access is via public tendering rather than customer intimacy or a sales force; NCC is repeatedly at the mercy of client billing and clearance processes rather than enjoying privileged access.
scores.quote: For every village Gram Panchayat, we need to submit a separate bill

scores.rationale: The customer base is almost entirely government and PSU clients where NCC has no lock-in and bears the payment risk, evidenced by Rs.3,015 crore stuck in UP JJM receivables and years of AP dues chasing.
scores.quote: the receivables have come down to INR3,015 crores, which includes groundwater, surface water, trade receivables and unbilled revenue

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology or R&D intensity is claimed; capability upgrades come from buying equipment such as the TBM held in CWIP, which any competitor can also purchase.
scores.quote: we have a CWIP that is a capex incurred on TBM kept under CWIP as the machine is yet to be put to use

scores.rationale: The business model is project-by-project contracting with no two-sided platform or self-reinforcing effect — scale in one state confers nothing on the next tender.

Pan-India execution capacity across seven verticals and ~150-160 concurrent projects is a real scale asset, but it is matched or exceeded by L&T and other large contractors, so it is not a reach rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: We have about 150, 160-odd projects. We have to close each of the projects

scores.rationale: Overwhelmingly growth (not maintenance) capex — Rs 150cr Dahej in FY23 scaling to Rs 1,500cr battery materials, Pakhajan Phase 2 at Rs 1,367cr with claimed 18-20% ROCE — but repeated cost revisions, delayed commissioning and still-negligible battery revenue keep incremental ROIC unproven.
scores.quote: the revised cost for Pakhajan Phase 2 stands at INR 1,367 crore... even after the revised capex... we should be targeting 18% to 20% ROCE

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the calls — it is a B2B specialty chemicals model sold via technical qualification, not brand marketing.

R&D shows real output — jointly developed multiple electrolyte recipes, new flavours/fragrance, semiconductor and specialty-polymer CSM molecules, and lithium recycling — but no R&D spend is disclosed and the core battery salt technology is licensed from Japanese partners rather than developed in-house.
scores.quote: we have jointly developed and exchanged multiple recipes of electrolytes with different lithium salt combinations

scores.rationale: BuLi Chemicals was a small, complementary bolt-on (organolithium) that reached full capacity, turned profitable and enabled lithium recycling back into the base business — exactly the bolt-on pattern, though it was a turnaround rather than an already-strong acquiree.
scores.quote: In case of organic, the main contributor is going to be the BuLi Chem... now we are almost running at full capacity... last two quarters BuLi Chemicals has been making profits

scores.rationale: Distribution is token (Rs 1/share final dividend) while the company is a serial issuer of equity — Rs 161cr promoter preferential allotment and a proposed Rs 600cr QIP — the opposite of buybacks at low valuations.
scores.quote: the Board has approved raising of INR 600 crore through an issue of eligible securities via a QIP

scores.rationale: The business is decidedly asset-heavy — roughly Rs 3,000cr of capex being deployed against FY26 revenue of Rs 862cr, net debt of Rs 1,295cr and a 120-140 day working capital cycle — so high asset turn is absent even if a moat exists.
scores.quote: consolidated total debt reached INR 1,330 crore in FY26, bringing the net debt to INR 1,295 crore

scores.rationale: Large runway with demonstrated capture — 60-75% of India's specialty lithium carbonate imports, ~25% of a quarter's revenue from brand-new customers, and four international salt approvals plus sole giga-scale local supply chain — but battery share is still at the qualification stage (Rs 36cr FY26 revenue).
scores.quote: we were importing close to around 60% to 75% of the lithium carbonate, which was getting imported into India for such specialty application

scores.rationale: Credible export expansion — US electrolyte makers completing site audits, four international salt approvals, Japanese customers and non-FEOC global demand — though exports fell to 26% of mix and international commercial supply has not yet started.
scores.quote: final site audits for multiple US-based electrolyte makers have also been completed and are currently awaiting final commercial clearances

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with raw material prices a pure pass-through, and management refuses to count price in guidance — the opposite of pricing/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: Most of this is basically by volume. There was hardly any impact of may be 2% or 3% which was because of value

scores.rationale: The company sits near a cyclical trough — persistent chemical overcapacity and weak demand — with lithium prices recovering off abnormally low levels, an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: the abnormally low prices are gone. Now it is closer... USD20 plus minus USD5 as a long-term stable price

scores.rationale: The battery materials end-market is in clear secular expansion, with Indian demand projected from 33 GWh to 92 GWh by 2027 and over 200 GWh by 2032, plus a policy-driven global shift to non-FEOC supply chains.
scores.quote: domestic battery demand is projected to surge from already 33 gigawatt hours last year to 92 gigawatt hours by 2027, eventually reaching more than 200 gigawatt hour by 2032

scores.rationale: Leverage is far from prudent — net debt of Rs 1,295cr against Rs 137cr FY26 EBITDA, finance costs up 64% YoY, followed by dilutive equity raises and a Rs 250cr+ capex overrun on the battery project.
scores.quote: Finance cost stood at INR 20.8 crore, up 64%. The increase in finance cost reflects the higher debt drawdown to fund the ongoing CAPEX

scores.rationale: Management has pursued the lithium-battery thesis consistently since FY23 and executed through a plant fire, insurance disputes and a demand downcycle, though the strategy leans heavily on Mitsubishi/Morita rather than standing fully independent.
scores.quote: we are committed to making long-term investment to secure our future growth and success

scores.rationale: Communication is technical and substance-led from a low-profile promoter family (Kanani), with no self-promotion or celebrity positioning across 20 calls.
scores.quote: I will be honest. The first six months, the approvals have taken longer time for the new site

scores.rationale: Only generic team praise appears, and the CFO role was filled by an external hire rather than an internal successor, with no evidence of a systematic talent pipeline.
scores.quote: we have appointed Mr. Gopikrishnan Sarathy as the Chief Financial Officer

scores.rationale: Management owns misses plainly — cutting FY25 battery guidance from Rs 75-100cr to Rs 50-75cr, admitting delays and explicitly saying it got the prior year wrong and is now building in buffer — though the pattern of repeated guidance revision limits the grade.
scores.quote: currently what we have done is that we kept some buffer because last year we had gone wrong

scores.rationale: The compelling EV/non-FEOC narrative outruns the actual results — FY26 PAT of just Rs 29cr on Rs 862cr revenue with rising debt and repeated timeline slippage — so the story, not demonstrated skill, is doing most of the work.
scores.quote: For FY26, revenue stood at INR 862 crore, registering a growth of 11% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased to INR 137 crore and PAT stood at INR 29 crore

scores.rationale: Neogen holds a monopoly-like position in the Indian customer's mind for specialty lithium salts — the only giga-scale local supply chain and 60-75% of specialty lithium carbonate imports — built on decades of batch-consistency credibility.
scores.quote: Neogen with its customers remains currently the only giga-scale example where the local supply chain has been established

scores.rationale: Real switching costs exist via multi-year customer qualification, plant audits and long-term formula-based contracts that took OEMs years to grant.
scores.quote: all the four customers have audited and approved Neogen facility... we have a five-year contract with a pharma customer

scores.rationale: This is not a stable oligopoly with captive customers — Chinese salt prices have run 20-50% below Neogen's formula price, forcing special discounted pricing to win trial volumes.
scores.quote: we still have a 20%/30% decrease... the current China spot prices are lower than the formula price

scores.rationale: Genuine entry barriers exist (lithium sourcing relationships, OEM approvals, no international player has localised) but pricing is far from rational, with persistent Chinese undercutting and other Indian electrolyte announcements.
scores.quote: some other Indian companies at least for electrolyte have already made some announcements

scores.rationale: Chinese suppliers holding ~95% of the electrolyte salt market are being forced to donate share by FEOC/PAP rules and customer de-risking, though they are strong rather than weak competitors.
scores.quote: 95% of it coming from China is something which we are not comfortable with

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — the EV battery thesis draws Kotak, HDFC, Axis, Avendus and JM Financial to the calls, and capital is actively flooding the ACC/PLI ecosystem.
scores.quote: the allocation of 10 gigawatt hour ACC PLI re-bidding tranche and Government's proposed PLI scheme for battery components

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power — lithium and bromine are explicit pass-throughs, EBITDA margin sits in a narrow 17-19% band, and management concedes price increases must be justified by global input costs.
scores.quote: for us, lithium is a pass-through, for both, salt as well as electrolyte customers

scores.rationale: Assurance is the core of the franchise — customers who cannot even test the impurity profile buy Neogen for batch-to-batch consistency and supply security, and explicitly told management they will pay formula prices above China spot for a non-China backup.
scores.quote: they want Neogen Chemicals as the reliability component is very high, because sometimes they are not even able to test the specifications fully

scores.rationale: Proximity to Indian giga-factories plus a business development team that hosts customers for on-site inspections gives genuine accessibility advantage over imported supply.
scores.quote: Our business development team has been actively engaged with domestic and international customers, hosting them for onsite inspections and approval visits

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/OEM and the benefit offered matches it correctly — reliability, TCO through formula pricing versus volatile spot, and qualification-based lock-in rather than brand appeal.
scores.quote: if they look at last four years, with the formula pricing which we have, they would still have been better off than buying in the spot market from China

scores.rationale: There is real homegrown process chemistry and multi-stage synthesis depth built over three decades, but the decisive battery salt/electrolyte technology is licensed from Mitsubishi and Morita rather than owned.
scores.quote: we have Japanese partners and internationally there is no dependency on China for Neogen in terms of technology as well as we had our own homegrown technology also

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the calls — the model is bilateral supply contracts with individual OEMs.
There is a locational supply-chain advantage as the only local giga-scale supplier, but no distribution or service network that rivals cannot replicate is described.
scores.quote: Neogen with its customers remains currently the only giga-scale example where the local supply chain has been established

scores.rationale: Capex intensity rose from 1.8% of sales in CY2015 to 7.7% in FY2023-24 with ~INR 5,800 Cr invested 2020-2025, a 10th factory in Odisha and >35% capacity added for Maggi/coffee/chocolate — clearly growth, not maintenance, and defended counter-cyclically.
scores.quote: invested between 2020 and 2025, we would be investing almost INR 5,800 Crores... capex levels you can see goes up from 1.8% in the calendar year 2015 to 7.7% in the financial year ending 2023-2024

scores.rationale: A&P has been redirected to digital (51% of media spend, +126% since 2020) and shows up as measurable brand equity — Maggi household penetration up 50% and coffee up 130% between 2016 and 2024.
scores.quote: since 2020, a 126% increase in the total digital media spend... 50% increase in the number of households that consume MAGGI

scores.rationale: Innovation is consistent (100+ new products in 5 years, 5.6% of sales from post-2015 launches, world-class Purina/Nestlé R&D access), but the R&D centre sits in a Nestlé SA subsidiary rather than the listed entity, so the efficiency is partly borrowed.
scores.quote: Over 100 new products have been launched in the last 5 years

scores.rationale: The only deal is a small, complementary bolt-on — the Purina petcare business (INR ~46 cr sales) bought from the parent with executive directors abstaining from the vote — synergistic with Nestlé's distribution, though it is a related-party purchase of a sub-scale asset.
scores.quote: all the executive directors, me and my two colleagues... have abstained from voting on this proposition completely

scores.rationale: Beyond a stock split that widened the shareholder base from ~170,000 to 547,000, the excerpts are silent on dividend policy or buybacks.
scores.quote: We split the shares and the shareholding went from 170,000 to 547,000 plus

scores.rationale: The model remains relatively asset-light for its scale with a strong brand/distribution moat protecting returns, but capex intensity quadrupling to 7.7% of sales and nine-going-on-ten factories mean asset turns are being diluted near-term.
scores.quote: nine factories going on to the tenth one

scores.rationale: Evidence of share capture (highest outlet addition among F&B peers in 2024, growth ahead of peer organic growth) but runway is limited by already-dominant positions in 8 of 10 categories.
scores.quote: the maximum number of outlets close to 5% of outlets have been added and is the highest gain amongst peers in 2024

scores.rationale: Well-executed domestic geographic expansion via the RUrban strategy (70,000-80,000 of a targeted 120,000 villages covered, double-digit growth in town class 1/2 and villages) plus Nespresso boutique rollout, though this is within-India rather than a brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: the objective of this Company is to cover a hundred and twenty thousand villages with more than 2000 population. We have covered 70,000 – 80,000 of these villages

scores.rationale: Management explicitly and repeatedly subordinates pricing to volume/penetration — pricing was deliberately held below cost inflation (6.3% price vs 15% commodity inflation) — which is the opposite of pricing/mix-led growth, only partly offset by a 16% CAGR premium portfolio.
scores.quote: we sell cases, we sell eaches, we sell packs, we do not sell rupees, we get rupees

scores.rationale: The FY25 commentary places the business near the trough of a consumption/commodity-inflation cycle with an identifiable upturn ahead, echoing the 5X commodity inflation shock of 2022 now normalising.
scores.quote: this is probably coming out of a curve and getting into a better curve as we move ahead

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — branded packaged F&B is only ~$40bn of an ~$800bn food market, per-capita packaged consumption is 3-4x lower than Philippines/Malaysia, and ~60 million households join the consuming class by 2030.
scores.quote: If you look at the branded packaged F&B, it is about $40 billion... the play between $40 billion and $800 billion is still allowing us tremendous room

scores.rationale: Organic, core-focused strategy with no large M&A, capacity added counter-cyclically through a consumption slowdown, and deliberate refusal to take indiscriminate price increases to protect margins.
scores.quote: We would not put that up ladies and gentlemen unless we were confident about the future... We do not get cowed down by a year or two years of blip

scores.rationale: Demonstrated tenacity over a 9-year arc — rebuilding a million lost outlets after the Maggi crisis and holding one penetration-led strategy across cycles — though strategic direction is set globally by the parent, limiting true independence.
scores.quote: during the MAGGI crisis, we lost a million outlets. We were down from 5 to 4 and we had to rebuild the whole distribution back again

scores.rationale: Professed humility and no results-brandishing sit alongside a highly visible, theatrical CMD persona and heavily narrated investor meets, so the evidence cuts both ways.
scores.quote: Nestlé is never used to be known for brandishing its results and wearing it on its sleeve

scores.rationale: Talent is treated as a core 'P' with future-ready people plans and an orderly, pre-announced CMD succession, but the successor was brought in from outside rather than from an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: I also have the privilege today like all good succession plannings to introduce my successor Manish Tiwari

scores.rationale: Management publicly reversed and explained its own 2018 petcare thesis, admits mistakes and lays out challenges rather than a rosy picture across all four calls.
scores.quote: a hallmark of trust and transparency of organization is the capability and the shedding of its ego to revisit the assumptions of its original business case

scores.rationale: The narrative is persuasive and self-referential, and much of the delivered result rests on inherited global brands, parent R&D and legacy category dominance rather than provable local skill, so results and skill are hard to separate from the transcripts alone.
scores.quote: in eight out of the 10 categories, Nestlé is a market leader

scores.rationale: Several brands occupy monopoly-like positions in the consumer's mind — Maggi at 4.5 billion serves in 52% of households, Nescafé, Milkmaid at 156 years — giving category-defining mindshare.
scores.quote: MAGGI with four-and-a-half billion serves is by far the biggest

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs or captive aftermarket in packaged food; management itself concedes credible regional competitors are taking their shot at the core.
scores.quote: There is still competition out there which we are cognizant of... what are you doing with regional competition?

scores.rationale: Categories are concentrated with Nestlé leading 8 of 10 and end customers are atomised retail consumers with no negotiating power, though the structure is loosening as new local entrants arrive.
scores.quote: in eight out of the 10 categories, Nestlé is a market leader

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour is rational (price taken well below input inflation, no discount war), but management openly flags an entrepreneurial wave of new food entrants, so entry barriers are not high.
scores.quote: Imagine if there are 200 more of these unicorns that enter the food space

scores.rationale: The large donator pool is loose/unbranded food — a $760bn gap between total and branded packaged F&B that uptrades into packaged first — rather than identified weak branded rivals.
scores.quote: Packaged food is the first food of choice when you uptrade from loose or from unbranded

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an under-the-radar niche: a 113-year-old, ~$23-24bn market cap company with 547,000 shareholders and packed hybrid analyst meets.
scores.quote: today enjoy the market capitalization of almost 23 to 24 billion dollars

scores.rationale: Decades-old brands command image- and taste-based pricing power with a premium portfolio compounding at 16% CAGR and an INR 7,500 Cr premiumisation runway, supporting high gross margins.
scores.quote: The overall premiumisation opportunity we see in our categories is roughly 7,500 Crores. Today the growth of this portfolio is about 16% on a CAGR basis since 2015

scores.rationale: Nutrition and infant/toddler products are bought on trust and label credibility rather than price, and management treats trustworthiness as the core asset rebuilt after the Maggi crisis.
scores.quote: ensure that their child gets not only the best tasting products, but most importantly the cleanest products and the most nutritious products

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a primary weapon — 5.3 million outlets, 10,000+ distributors, 940+ one-Nestlé kiosks and an explicit RUrban push into villages, backed by e-commerce and quick commerce.
scores.quote: Our 10,000 plus distributors and re-distributors... 5.3 million outlets in terms of total reach

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail households and the benefit set is correctly matched to it — brand image, taste, nutrition trust and penetration into two of three Indian households.
scores.quote: our Nestlé product reaches two out of three households in India. It reaches 80% of the urban households

scores.rationale: There is real applied food-science depth accessed via the Nestlé R&D Centre and Purina's 90 years and 500+ scientists, but it is parent-owned capability in a low-R&D-intensity category rather than a proprietary multi-product tech edge in the listed entity.
scores.quote: Purina has invested for about 90 years an army of over 500 scientists, nutritionists and pioneered some of the firsts in the category

scores.rationale: Nothing in the four calls describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the model is classic brand-plus-distribution FMCG where scale advantages come from reach, not user interaction.
scores.quote: penetration-led, volume-led growth strategy is what our simple strategy is

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the clearest structural advantage — 5.3 million outlets, the highest outlet addition among peers in 2024, rural electrification/roads leveraged into RUrban reach, and a bespoke 46-town pet-specialty network.
scores.quote: Pet Speciality Distribution network has been built in 46 towns... 50 distributors... 185 suppliers spread all across the country

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly capex-light — management says the existing plant supports Rs 2,500-3,000 crore of revenue and guides only routine Rs 20-25 crore capex for FY27 — so incremental ROIC is very high but there is no rising growth capex programme to score positively.
scores.quote: up till 2,500 crores to 3,000 crores we our manufacturing facility is almost all very very sufficient. We don't need to really invest into CAPEX

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the twelve calls; the business sells via tenders and direct enterprise engagement.

Sustained in-house R&D has repeatedly converted into new product lines (Intel-licensed architectures, ARM/RISC systems, switches, 5G ORAN, NVIDIA GB200-based AI systems) and drove the AI segment from ~7% of revenue to 43.4% with 459.6% growth in FY26.
scores.quote: This growth was a result of years of focused in-house R&D, enabling us to design and manufacture some of the world's most powerful latest generation AI systems

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were discussed or executed in any of the calls.
First meaningful distribution is a modest Rs 3 per share dividend recommended in FY26 with no buyback or articulated distribution policy — capital is retained for working capital and growth.
scores.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of INR3 per share, subject to shareholders' approval.

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-light: gross fixed asset turnover of 33.2x, ROCE 37.5% and ROE 32.9% with zero net debt, protected by its position as the only domestic full-stack high-end computing OEM.
scores.quote: The gross fixed asset turnover ratio stood at 33.2x as on 31st March 2026... zero-net-debt company

scores.rationale: Still a small player against global OEMs with a long runway, and it has demonstrably captured share — revenue up from ~Rs 60 crore a quarter in FY24 to Rs 21,836 million for FY26 (+90%), aided by DGFT import restrictions and Make-in-India preference.
scores.quote: reaffirming its position as India's largest OEM in high-end computing solutions

scores.rationale: Exports were built from nothing to ~8-11% of revenue with international HFT and enterprise customers (Tower Research, Societe Generale) at domestic-equivalent margins, but the expansion is still early and capped by management's own guidance.
scores.quote: export contributed around 7.9% for the 9-month period financial year '25 revenue

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/order-driven rather than price-led — management deliberately prices modestly, EBITDA margin has stayed pinned at 13-14% through 90% revenue growth, and the large strategic AI order was taken at 200 bps lower PBT.
scores.quote: we will be about 200 basis points lower at the PBT level on the strategic order

scores.rationale: The company is riding an AI/memory-price boom at what looks like a cycle peak, not a trough — global component shortages and surging prices are already present and management sees the surge lasting only 18-24 months.
scores.quote: it seems like it will go on for at least the next 18 to 24 months

scores.rationale: End market is in genuine secular expansion — sovereign AI compute, the India AI Mission, and a national data-centre build-out from ~1.5 GW to a planned 9 GW by 2030.
scores.quote: The build-out of indigenous AI compute is no longer aspirational. It is a strategic national imperative

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no acquisitions, zero net debt and net free cash of Rs 833 million, and capex kept to routine levels even while revenue grew 90%.
scores.quote: Our balance sheet strength is reflected by us being a zero-net-debt company.
