scores.quote: Our digitalization journey, including the IIT policy would take us around another INR500 crores

scores.rationale: The M&A programme is the opposite of small complementary bolt-ons: a 10-mineral overseas diversification mandate spanning exploration-stage lithium to operating coking coal, an explicit willingness to overpay, and the first offshore deal (Legacy gold/iron ore) posting losses in year one.
scores.quote: I don't mind paying much more because the way the steelmaking is going to grow in India

scores.rationale: With ~INR8,000-9,000cr net cash the company gave no coherent distribution rationale and refused the buyback question outright, later redirecting the cash into a INR50,000cr capex programme.
scores.quote: We can't answer your question ... I can't answer this at this point of time.

scores.rationale: Historically very asset-light for a miner — ~INR31,000cr revenue on a gross block an analyst put at only INR5,000-6,000cr, with 42% standalone iron-ore EBITDA protected by the Bailadila deposits — though the INR50,000cr build-out will lower turns.
scores.quote: If I look at the current gross block it's about -- should be about INR5,000, INR6,000 crores

scores.rationale: Volumes moved from ~40mt (FY23) to 53mt (FY26) with new mines (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) opening, and management sees a growing addressable market rather than dominance, though guidance is repeatedly missed (55.4mt target vs 53mt delivered).
scores.quote: the size of the cake is increasing. And I think everybody can take a larger piece, including us

scores.rationale: New domestic geography was genuinely delivered (Jharkhand coal mine opened), but the international leg is a year of repeated unclosed promises with the first overseas asset, Legacy, having made losses.
scores.quote: this year we hope to acquire a couple of assets abroad as well

scores.rationale: Growth is almost entirely volume-led while pricing is sluggish and blended EBITDA fell from 42% to 33%; the mix upgrades (DRI-grade pellets, branded blended ore) remain promises rather than delivered margin.
scores.quote: despite slightly sluggish prices, we've been able to achieve a PAT, an 11% growth in PAT

scores.rationale: The calls show a full cycle traverse — a 2023 trough with recovery, then sluggish FY26 prices — but management never positions the company near an identifiable cyclical bottom with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: we are seeing a pickup in national prices

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — customers doubling pellet/steel capacity, and management sizing Indian coking coal imports rising from 55-60mt to 150-160mt on blast-furnace additions.
scores.quote: India is -- which imports around 55 million, 60 million tons is likely to go up to 150 million to 160 million tons

scores.rationale: Stewardship has drifted from organic focus to self-described hyper-aggressive expansion across 10 minerals plus overseas M&A, while carrying INR7,800cr of receivables from two related state entities and funding a loss-making steel plant.
scores.quote: a company which is on hyper aggressive expansion mode

scores.rationale: The long-term 100mt vision is real, but strategy is set with the government rather than independently — the mineral portfolio is mandated, a 10% steel-plant stake was taken at the government's instruction, and RINL is supplied on credit for reasons that are not purely commercial.
scores.quote: in consultation with the ministry, we've made a very clear-cut policy that we'll be looking at 10 minerals only

scores.rationale: Tone is mostly workmanlike and occasionally self-deprecating on capacity questions, but is offset by promotional framing of results as 'spectacularly good', a 'watershed year' and a 'game changer'.
scores.quote: No let us learn to walk then we'll run.

scores.rationale: No talent-development or succession system is described; the only people evidence is a bulk recruitment of 800 workers delaying third-shift working and 43-45 days of production lost to industrial action.
scores.quote: We did lose around 43 or 44 days of production due to industrial issues

scores.rationale: Disclosure is unusually granular and self-critical — royalty mechanics, the INR282cr forest-land hit, Legacy's first-year losses, the Nagarnar mill breakdown, and mine-wise volume bridges — even if repeated target misses are always attributed to external causes.
scores.quote: any first year mining project will not make profit, where we had made some losses

scores.rationale: The 42% iron-ore EBITDA derives from the Bailadila ore body and statutory position rather than demonstrated managerial skill, and once results are separated from the asset the record shows missed volume targets, missed capex guidance and slipping projects like the KK line doubling.
scores.quote: If we take the iron ore business standalone, our EBITDA is still at 42%

scores.rationale: NMDC holds a near-monopoly position for high-grade Bailadila lump/fines with captive-like dependence from Nagarnar and RINL, whose 7-8mt offtake cannot be interrupted without immediate consequence.
scores.quote: Nagarnar still plan doesn't have a dedicated iron ore mine. So it is entirely, it will be entirely sourcing entirely from NMDC

scores.rationale: The position is regionally protected by logistics rather than product — a new competitor only touches the ~4mt Raipur market while NMDC's rail/port access locks in Vizag and the West Coast.
scores.quote: But Raipur for us accounts for around 4 million tons of ore only ... our access to the other markets, whether it is at Vizag or West Coast, we have an advantage

scores.rationale: The customer base is highly concentrated (~70% from three large steel clients) and those customers are integrating backwards into captive mines, so end-customer negotiating power is high rather than absent.
scores.quote: 70% of patent revenue comes from 3 major clients ... yes, they have their own mines

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are formidable — clearances, forest diversion and Section 5/7/9/11 sequences meant Deposit 4 took 50 years to open — and NMDC prices at or slightly above domestic peers rather than discounting.
scores.quote: after 50 years, we've been opened, been able to open an iron ore mine, that is Deposit 4

scores.rationale: Weak players exist in the ecosystem (RINL's distress, a stagnant secondary/lump segment), but the competitive newcomer named is Lloyds Metals expanding capacity, so there is no clear pool of donators being taken from.
scores.quote: We don't see too much of an enhancement in capacity there

scores.rationale: NMDC is the opposite of under-the-radar — a flagship PSU moving to Maharatna status, covered on these calls by Kotak, ICICI, Motilal, Ambit, DSP and Goldman Sachs.
scores.quote: we are all now ready for the Maharatna status of this company

scores.rationale: Margins are genuinely high (42% iron-ore EBITDA) but that is ore-body economics, not image-based pricing power; realisations track export/domestic benchmarks and the brand premium is admittedly something India has never had.
scores.quote: we are at par or blended cost this is with at par or even at a slightly premium on most of the other domestic suppliers

scores.rationale: Customers buy assured, fungible supply — NMDC keeps supplying RINL despite unpaid receivables because continuity matters more than price to both sides, and the blending-yard plan is explicitly about consistent quality.
scores.quote: that is one company we cannot afford not to supply

scores.rationale: A deliberate, consultant-backed shift from mine-head selling to stockyards, blending yards and slurry pipelines brings the product closer to customers, though most of this infrastructure is still years from commissioning.
scores.quote: we will end mine head sale and start selling from blending yard and stockyard

scores.rationale: The customer set is entirely corporate and the benefits offered (reliability, logistics, TCO) are correctly matched, but lock-in has not translated into commercial power — it has instead produced INR7,800cr of receivables and credit provisions.
scores.quote: we are seeing a very sharp increase in receivables this year to almost INR7,800 crores

scores.rationale: No technology differentiation is claimed anywhere across four years; process capability is bought in (L&T for the pipeline and pellet plant, BCG/McKinsey/Deloitte for distribution design) rather than developed.
scores.quote: we had BCG and , McKinsey and Deloitte all three going on the question of our distribution network

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the ten calls.

The evacuation and distribution network — KK line doubling, 20-26 rakes/day, slurry pipelines, RWLS, and the strategically located 1,100-acre Gangavaram port parcel — is a reach rivals cannot replicate, discounted only by chronic delays (KK doubling still incomplete after three-plus years).
scores.quote: the capacity of course will increase to around 40 million ton immediately once it is done from the present 28 to 30

scores.rationale: Growth capex is large and rising (group ₹49,068 cr in FY26 vs ₹44,636 cr FY25; standalone ₹28,462 cr vs ₹22,965 cr) with 34-37 GW under construction and a ₹16.8 lakh crore 10-year plan, but returns are regulated cost-plus rather than high incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: In FY26, we have incurred a group capex of INR49,068 crores as compared to INR44,636 crores in the previous year

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand-promotion spend across the calls; only CSR and sports sponsorship are mentioned, which is not A&P for demand generation.

Real innovation effort exists (green hydrogen blending, green methanol, AUSC JV with BHEL, vanadium redox flow, carbon capture) but four years on these remain pilots/hubs with no disclosed R&D spend or commercial revenue yield.
scores.quote: work has commenced at Pudimadaka green hydrogen hub for development of green methanol and sustainable aviation fuel

scores.rationale: M&A is small and complementary (1,350 MW Sinnar with MAHAGENCO, more state/PSU plants under discussion) but the acquiree is a stranded/distressed asset rather than an already-strong business, and no post-deal OPM improvement is yet shown.
scores.quote: This also includes the acquisition of the 1,350 MW Sinnar Thermal Power Station in partnership with MAHAGENCO

scores.rationale: A coherent, steadily rising dividend policy sustained for 33 consecutive years (₹9/share in FY26, ₹5.50 interim + ₹3.50 final) explicitly maintained alongside heavy capex, though there are no valuation-sensitive buybacks and the policy follows DIPAM guidelines rather than management discretion.
scores.quote: This is going to be 33rd consecutive years of the dividend distribution, and this has been steadily going up

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy: group gross property, plant and equipment of ₹4,70,618 crore against group income of ₹1,89,799 crore in FY26 — an asset turn well below 0.5x, the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: gross property, plant and machinery as on 31st March 2026 on group level has increased from INR4,04,210 crores to INR4,70,618 crores

scores.rationale: NTPC is already the dominant generator at ~24% of national generation and management frames the goal as maintaining, not gaining, share — leaving little runway for share capture.
scores.quote: there is no reason that we will be left behind to maintain our market share of around 25%

scores.rationale: Expansion is essentially pan-India already (Khavda, Rajasthan, Patratu, Lara, nuclear site studies in 8+ states) with only legacy international exposure via the Bangladesh Maitree project; there is no premium brand travelling into new markets.
scores.quote: 30 locations across India are being explored... MP, Gujarat, Odisha, UP, Bihar, Maharashtra has given consent for preliminary studies

scores.rationale: Growth is purely volume/capacity-led under CERC cost-plus regulated tariffs with no pricing power — FY26 total income actually fell 2.69% on weaker demand despite record capacity addition.
scores.quote: the total income is INR 1,69,725 crores as compared to INR 1,74,414 crores in the previous year, a decline by 2.69%... due to the lesser demand

scores.rationale: Management correctly called the end of the supply overhang in Aug 2022 and the cycle has since turned up (peak demand 271 GW, PLF back near 77-80%), but NTPC is now mid-cycle rather than near the bottom, and FY26 generation actually dipped to 432.2 BU from 438.7 BU.
scores.quote: The period of the low dispatch of the power and the supply overhang in the country seems to be over

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear multi-decade secular expansion — India's electricity requirement projected from 1,708 BU in FY26 to 8,100 BU by FY50, with peak demand from 245 GW to 750 GW.
scores.quote: India's electricity requirement is projected to grow from 1,708 billion units in FY26 to 8,100 billion units by FY50

scores.rationale: Predominantly organic growth with prudent leverage (weighted average borrowing cost cut to 5.98% from 6.61%, sovereign-level rating, receivable days down to 15) and counter-cyclical thermal investment when the sector was shunning coal, with only small bolt-on M&A.
scores.quote: The weighted average interest rate on borrowings during FY26 stood at 5.98% compared to 6.61% in FY25... Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-year vision has actually been delivered — captive coal ramped from 14 MMT (FY22) to 47.88 MMT (FY26), capacity from 69 GW to 90+ GW, nuclear moved from a 2022 talking point to AERB excavation consent at Mahi Banswara — though as a PSU its agenda is heavily set by Government of India targets.
scores.quote: our coal production last year, it was around 35 million tons... increased to 47.88 million metric ton

scores.rationale: Calls are heavy on award-touting and personality framing rather than substance-only communication, with repeated 'visionary leadership' language and celebration of individual executive awards.
scores.quote: I would like to congratulate Srinivasan, sir, for being conferred with the Dealmaker CFO of the Year Award

scores.rationale: Systematic, externally validated talent development with an unusually deep internal pipeline — every functional director (Sundaram 1988, Srivastava 1988, Ravindra Kumar 1989) rose from executive trainee inside NTPC, backed by a dedicated Director (HR) and reskilling programs.
scores.quote: seventh time, we have received ATD BEST Award, which is international award, which showcases our excellence in the talent development, NTPC is also certified as the Top Employer 2024

scores.rationale: Communication is detailed and quantitative, including unflattering facts such as the revenue decline, NGEL curtailment of 314 MUs plus 135 MUs TRAS loss, and adjusted (vs headline) PAT, though management deflects on selected topics and rarely explicitly owns mistakes.
scores.quote: NGEL experienced a curtailment of 314 MUs during the year... besides the TRAS loss, which we can say is 135 MUs

scores.rationale: Much of the apparent excellence is structural rather than managerial — regulated cost-plus returns, LPSC rules that fixed sector-wide receivables, pithead locations, and government-allocated 26 GW of thermal — so results should not be read as evidence of superior skill.
scores.quote: LPSC is helping almost every generator now... it is decided that in addition to the renewable energy, we will require some of the thermal capacity also... out of that 80 gigawatt, NTPC will invest in 26 gigawatt

scores.rationale: NTPC has scale leadership (24% of generation from 17% of capacity) and merit-order priority from low energy charges, but it competes with state gencos and IPPs on dispatch and holds no monopoly in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: NTPC Group generates 24% of the nation's electricity with a 17% share of installed capacity

scores.rationale: Long-term regulated PPAs with state discoms plus CERC cost-plus tariffs create captive, high-switching-cost offtake — including new co-located BESS executed under cost-plus mode — though this is regulatory rather than a market-earned monopoly.
scores.quote: Work in respect of 5 GWh BESS capacity at NTPC's existing thermal power stations is being executed under cost-plus mode

scores.rationale: Generation includes many state gencos and private IPPs rather than a tight oligopoly, and the end customer's negotiating power is neutralized by the regulator rather than by industry structure.
scores.quote: NTPC coal station achieved a PLF of 72.04% against rest of India average of 63.20%

scores.rationale: Barriers are formidable (capital, land, coal linkage, environmental and AERB clearances) and pricing is regulated so no discount wars occur, with stable Government of India ownership — but capacity is added by policy fiat, so supply is not always rational.
scores.quote: the additional coal capacity requirement till 2036 is projected to be 86 GW, of which 68 GW is in pipeline

scores.rationale: Weak state-sector competitors are visible donators — NTPC's coal PLF of 72.04% versus rest-of-India 63.20%, and it is directly absorbing distressed assets such as Sinnar and negotiating further state/PSU plant acquisitions.
scores.quote: there are some discussions which are going on with the different states, some PSU, to explore the possibility to acquire some additional plants

scores.rationale: NTPC is the opposite of under-the-radar — India's largest power producer, covered by brokerages hosting its calls, heavily rated by ESG agencies, and central to national policy.
scores.quote: NTPC, the largest power generator in the country is the mainstay in meeting the nation's energy needs

scores.rationale: Electricity is a pure commodity sold at regulator-determined cost-plus tariffs with zero image- or taste-driven pricing power; revenue fell when demand softened.
scores.quote: the new CERC norms for the next 5 years have come in effect... will be able to help to maintain our profitability and cash flows

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and baseload certainty — NTPC consistently outperforms all-India availability and PLF, holds ~18 days of coal stock, and management positions the entire franchise around energy security.
scores.quote: We continue to set benchmarks in operational excellence, consistently outperforming the all-India average in both availability factor and plant load factor

scores.rationale: Pan-India presence, pithead plant locations and the NVVN trading arm give reach and lower delivered cost, but this is grid-based commodity supply, not superior accessibility or customer intimacy through a sales force.
scores.quote: Our added strength being the proximity of our power stations to coal mines, resulting in lower energy charges and competitiveness

scores.rationale: The customer base is institutional (state discoms) and the benefit offered correctly matches — lowest-cost reliable baseload with long-term PPA lock-in — evidenced by 100%+ realization of billed dues and receivable days down to 15.
scores.quote: Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days as on 31st March '26 compared to 29 days for the previous year

scores.rationale: NTPC deploys advanced technology (first supercritical at Sipat, AUSC JV with BHEL, FGD, flexibilization, green hydrogen blending) but it is licensed or vendor-partnered rather than proprietary, with no disclosed R&D intensity or technology-derived pricing advantage.
scores.quote: One is advanced ultra-supercritical along with BHEL in a joint venture as a development project

scores.rationale: There is no two-sided network — output is fungible electrons delivered onto a common grid, and additional scale brings no self-reinforcing customer benefit.
scores.quote: NTPC Group generation stood at 432.2 billion units in FY26 as compared to 438.7 billion units in FY25

scores.rationale: Its pan-India fleet spread reduces execution and operating risk, but NTPC does not own distribution and dispatch is decided by grid merit order, so there is no service-reach advantage rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: we have a pan-India presence, which helps us to mitigate several operational risks associated with operating within a limited geography

scores.rationale: Growth investment is in RMs, offshore offices and an enterprise tech/AI stack rather than physical capex, and it has been consistently funded while ROE held at ~32% and profits compounded ~45% CAGR over three years.
scores.quote: we have added around 270+ RMs. So, that's the cost which is coming in, but that's a good cost to invest

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the calls.

Proprietary product/tech development (NUWAI training AI, portfolio solutions, Agentic AI, multicurrency reporting, Virasat estate planning) has translated into measurable output, with per-RM revenue up 25% in Wealth and 10-15% in Private.
scores.quote: we've seen about a 25% per RM revenue jump in this segment. And I think a large portion also comes through the usage of AI

scores.rationale: Management states openness to bolt-on M&A in alternates and offshore but has executed nothing over the period, so there is intent without a track record to judge.
scores.quote: We are also looking at potential M&A opportunities in this segment... the primary interest is in alternates

scores.rationale: A stated and consistently applied dividend policy of roughly half of profits, though there is no buyback discipline or valuation-linked distribution to assess.
scores.quote: we have again declared a dividend of INR14 for H2 FY '26 that takes it to roughly 50% of our profit being paid as dividend which is consistent with our dividend distribution policy

scores.rationale: Asset-light fee/annuity model delivering consistent ~32% ROE with cost-to-income falling from 65% to 54%, deliberately calibrated for capital efficiency, though the moat protecting it is only moderate.
scores.quote: Our ROE for the quarter is 32%... it is being consistent at 32% for 9 months as well

scores.rationale: Clear runway in an early-stage organized wealth industry with demonstrated share capture — 22% of incremental AIF/PMS registrations, IB share up 18% to 19% — but institutional equities share has been flat and capital markets moderated.
scores.quote: our market share happens to be 22% of all incremental AIF and PMS registration

scores.rationale: Offshore expansion was promised and delivered on schedule — DIFC live in FY25 with breakeven guided at 6-9 months and achieved, Singapore following, plus GIFT City and new domestic locations in Jaipur, Surat and Kanpur.
scores.quote: The Dubai office has already broken even, and we expect Singapore to follow in the next maybe 2 quarters

scores.rationale: Growth is genuinely mix-led toward higher-quality annuity revenue (MPIS to 60% of Wealth revenue, ARR to 60% of Private) but pricing is flat-to-compressing with blended retention around 90bps.
scores.quote: ARR assets about INR54,000 crores and yields are nearly between 0.85%-1%... on an average, we should end up somewhere around 90-95 basis points

scores.rationale: The capital markets segment is at a cyclical low after FY26 volume declines and IB/IE moderation, with management pointing to policy-supported recovery ahead, though a large part of the group remains market-linked rather than counter-cyclically positioned.
scores.quote: equity cash ADT declining by about 6% and futures ADT declining 14%... domestic growth, as there is consensus, now should begin to recover

scores.rationale: Organized wealth management in India is in early innings of a multi-year financialization trend, evidenced by client assets compounding from INR2.9 lakh crore to INR4.5-4.6 lakh crore across the period.
scores.quote: organized wealth management represents a multiyear structural opportunity. We still believe that the industry is in early stages

scores.rationale: Consistently organic growth with deliberate capital discipline — shrinking the loan book to fix ROE before regrowing it, and explicitly refusing to overpay for RM capacity when competitors were bidding up talent.
scores.quote: we deliberately calibrated our loan book because we wanted to make it undergo a change such that it becomes a reasonable ROE business... we prefer to not be mindless in adding RMs because of the price point

scores.rationale: A decade-long thesis on the affluent/HNI gap left by conflicted banks, executed through demerger from Edelweiss into an independent governance, brand and rating framework, then into the multi-year One Nuvama synergy program.
scores.quote: Our initial focus subsequent to demerger was to ensure a smooth transition and establishing ourselves as an independent company with our own governance framework, brand, rating and operating system

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and business-focused with no promotional or celebrity framing, and management explicitly cautions against the hype cycle in its own industry rather than participating in it.
scores.quote: a large number of new players are making lofty promises to RMs of future valuations, which seem extremely stratospheric to us

scores.rationale: Systematic capacity building — proprietary AI-based training, deliberate seniorization of the RM base, and a transparent long-term compensation philosophy — but senior leadership gaps have been filled largely by external hires (CIOs, CBO) rather than an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: We have created a product called NUWAI. It is an AI-based training solution... we have a stated compensation philosophy... extremely transparent and aligned with long-term value creation

scores.rationale: Repeatedly volunteers granular, unflattering detail — decomposing an NII shortfall into its INR4 crore and INR2-3 crore causes, flagging an INR11 crore one-time labour-code hit, disclosing the loss of a large asset services client, and correcting its own misstatement in the transcript.
scores.quote: there is an INR 10 crores gap. Out of this, INR 4 crores comes from there and given the volatility in the quarter, there was some INR 2-3 crores cost on the MLD hedging side

scores.rationale: Much of the FY24-FY25 profit surge coincided with a bull market, but FY26 provides a partial separation of skill from beta: profits still grew despite flat indices, yield compression and the loss of a large client.
scores.quote: despite the headwinds, index not doing anything, volatility in the market, yield compression, loss of big clients, yet there is a near 15% profit growth

scores.rationale: Custody and clearing is a licence-restricted niche where Nuvama is one of only three non-bank holders and claims a dominant position in its chosen FPI/HFT segment, though this is only one segment of the group.
scores.quote: We are one of the few, actually one of the three non-banks which have the license to offer custody services. So, it's actually a very prized asset

scores.rationale: Asset services assets are described as sticky with operational lock-in being deepened via RTA and trustee backward integration, but the loss of a single large client in Q1 FY26 shows switching costs are real yet not absolute.
scores.quote: assets are more sticky and less volatile to move... we are going to add RTA services... so that it becomes a one-stop shop

scores.rationale: The wealth industry is fragmenting rather than consolidating into a stable oligopoly, with traditional brokers and PE-backed platforms now competing down from ultra-HNI into HNI and affluent segments.
scores.quote: the competitive intensity is growing... we are also seeing several private equity-backed platforms that are aggressively building teams

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and behaviour is irrational at the margin — new entrants are flooding in and bidding for RMs with equity promises management itself calls stratospheric, while PE interest in the sector is at an all-time high.
scores.quote: private equity interest in the industry is all-time high

scores.rationale: There is an identifiable weak tail — conflicted bank channels, subscale single-product platforms and small AMCs being sold — from which a full-stack platform can take share.
scores.quote: a few scale players with fully diversified multiproduct platforms will scale as long-term leaders, and there'll be a long tail

scores.rationale: The opposite of an ignored niche: a listed company in a sector attracting record private equity capital and aggressive new entrants.
scores.quote: private equity interest in the industry is all-time high... there are early signs of consolidation

scores.rationale: There is some brand-led retention with blended ARR yields holding near 90bps, but management concedes fee levels drift and growth depends on product innovation rather than image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: yields are nearly between 0.85%-1%, this quarter being 1%... quarter-to-quarter 10-15 basis points can move

scores.rationale: The proposition is built on unbiased, trusted advice for HNI clients and on infrastructure-grade reliability in asset services, where management stresses that one bad outcome compounds for years.
scores.quote: they need unbiased advice from their wealth managers... I don't think that this business one should rush in because one bad performance here can have years of negative impact

scores.rationale: A deliberately built full-wallet, one-stop platform across wealth, lending, asset management, IB and custody, delivered through ~1,200+ RMs, 65-70 locations and an external wealth-manager channel — the explicit source of its client and RM intimacy.
scores.quote: the benefits of the value proposition built around the exhaustive platform, which can basically service the full wallet of the client

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched by customer type — advisory intimacy and estate/legacy solutions for HNI/UHNI individuals, and operational lock-in via bundled custody, clearing, RTA and trusteeship for institutional PMS/AIF and FPI clients.
scores.quote: backward integration of our RTA and trustee services will help us increase the market share here

scores.rationale: A credible, multi-product proprietary tech stack (portfolio solutions, NUWAI, Agentic AI, industry-first multicurrency reporting) with demonstrated productivity payoff, though it is an efficiency edge rather than a defensible deep technology moat.
scores.quote: We've also launched an industry-first multicurrency module on portfolio reporting

scores.rationale: Genuine cross-segment reinforcement — IB and IE relationships convert into wealth clients, and platform scale/placement capability attracts product manufacturers, which in turn attracts RMs — but it is an ecosystem flywheel rather than a true two-sided network.
scores.quote: in FY 22-23, more than 30% of the relevant investment banking clients which we onboarded became wealth management clients

scores.rationale: Distribution reach and placement capability is management's stated competitive currency, giving it first call on new product manufacturers and syndication flow that smaller rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: your distribution capability, your reach, your placement capability because that has become a big attraction of getting new product manufacturers to come to you

scores.rationale: After three years of deliberately deferring expansion to pay down debt (FY23–FY25), growth capex has stepped up sharply and is executing on/ahead of schedule (Vadraj Kutch/Surat, 4 MTPA East debottlenecking, Sachana terminal), though incremental ROIC is unproven and the assets are capital-heavy.
scores.quote: we have inaugurated 2 million tons per annum of grinding capacity at Surat on 11th July 2026, ahead of schedule

scores.rationale: A&P is modest but visibly productive — campaigns behind Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto UNO coincided with premium mix rising from 34% (Q1FY23) to 43% (FY26) and each new brand scaling to 1 mt annualised.
scores.quote: both these brands have become a 1 million ton brand now

scores.rationale: No disclosed R&D intensity, but a consistent stream of differentiated launches (patented microfiber cement, India's first hydrophobic concrete, Ecodure thermal-insulated concrete) that feed the premium mix.
scores.quote: the only patented product with unique microfiber technology

scores.rationale: Vadraj is the opposite of a small bolt-on of an already-strong acquiree — a distressed insolvency asset requiring multi-year refurbishment of clinker and grinding units before it earns anything, following the earlier debt-laden NU Vista integration.
scores.quote: The clinker unit and grinding units are planned to be commissioned in phases between Q3 FY '27 and Q1 FY '28

scores.rationale: Across the excerpts management discusses only debt repayment and reinvestment; buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy are never mentioned.

Classic asset-heavy cement economics — ~Rs.4,000-5,300 crore net debt and large clinker/grinding/siding capex against ~Rs.2,600 crore quarterly revenue, with no moat protecting returns (prices at multi-year lows).
scores.quote: our net debt, as we entered June 30th, was 4,358 crores

scores.rationale: Runway exists as a ~5th-tier player, but volumes were flat for years under a deliberate value-over-volume stance and management concedes it is only "more or less equal" to East peers, with genuine share gain only now via Gujarat entry.
scores.quote: we are more or less equal to all our peers in the eastern region

scores.rationale: First-ever move outside East/North executed credibly — Surat grinding unit commissioned ahead of schedule, Kutch clinker on track and a Gujarat bulk terminal planned — though the West market is contested and returns are unproven.
scores.quote: signifying our first-ever capacity expansion in the Western region

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly attributed to price, premium mix and geo-mix rather than volume (realization +Rs.320 QoQ on only 5% volume growth), though much of the price action was cost pass-through in a weak price cycle.
scores.quote: three reasons: one is price, second is premium, third geo-mix

scores.rationale: The company passed through a clear pricing trough in FY24–FY25 and is now on an upturn with record FY26 volume/EBITDA and a visible government capex step-up ahead, though fuel and packing cost inflation is a fresh headwind.
scores.quote: central government capex for FY '27 is planned to grow by 20% and state government capex to grow by 15%

scores.rationale: Indian cement is a genuinely secular end market — low per-capita consumption, PMAY housing and infrastructure — repeated consistently from 2022 to 2026, but demand has been lumpy (election, weather, degrowth quarters) rather than smoothly expanding.
scores.quote: world's second largest cement market, with a low per capita consumption, providing significant headroom for growth

scores.rationale: Multi-year deleveraging was promised and delivered (net debt 6,885 → ~4,030 crore) with expansion explicitly gated on hitting the debt target, offset by the choice to make a large distressed acquisition rather than pure organic growth.
scores.quote: the plan for Nuvoco is to kick start new investment movement we hit a range of 3,500, 4,000 crores

scores.rationale: Management restated the same sequenced plan — pare debt to Rs.3,500–4,000 crore, then expand — across four years and then executed it, including commissioning Surat ahead of schedule.
scores.quote: we have not changed anything from what we mentioned in the last earnings call

scores.rationale: Calls are run by IR and the MD/CFO with granular operational detail and no promotional or personality-driven framing; commentary sticks to fuel mix, sidings and gypsum sourcing.
scores.quote: our teams did a wonderful job by curtailing the use of petcoke in North from excess of 50% to about 42%

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly credits manufacturing and procurement teams and has a stable MD/CFO pair since FY23, but there is no evidence of systematic talent development or a described leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: I think our purchase team did a wonderful job

scores.rationale: Communication is unusually granular and self-critical — quantifying the SAP-migration volume loss, breaking realization vs cost bridges rupee-by-rupee, and hitting a self-issued fuel guidance range — though the East expansion slippage was framed defensively as "no delay".
scores.quote: we had a disruption of close to six days in the month of April

scores.rationale: Record FY26 results owe as much to the cement price/demand cycle turning and fuel cost deflation (Rs.2.74 → Rs.1.44/Mcal) as to management skill, so the operating outperformance should be discounted rather than taken at face value.
scores.quote: peaked at Q3 FY'23 at Rs.2.74 and then now it's been tapering down to Rs.1.57

scores.rationale: Cement is a substitutable commodity with no aftermarket or mind-share monopoly; even the premium brands compete on price in a market management calls extremely competitive.
scores.quote: East is extremely competitive as we speak

scores.rationale: There is regional density in the East (70%+ of sales, leadership in Bihar/Jharkhand/Bengal) which confers some freight-based local advantage, but essentially zero customer switching costs.
scores.quote: close to about 70 plus percentage sales which happens through east market

scores.rationale: The East market behaves as a fragmented, price-competitive market rather than a stable oligopoly, with prices at multi-year lows and rollbacks of attempted hikes.
scores.quote: prices in Calcutta and Patna are at multi-year lows

scores.rationale: Pricing has been irrational for extended stretches — hikes rolled back within weeks in FY23 and a year-long downward price trajectory in FY25 — indicating weak discipline despite capital-intensity barriers.
scores.quote: the industry has experienced a downward trajectory in prices, which is not a positive sign

scores.rationale: Weak players clearly exist to take share from — Nuvoco's own western entry came by acquiring the insolvent Vadraj assets, and its cost position (lowest-quartile fuel cost) lets it outlast sub-scale rivals in downturns.
scores.quote: Nuvoco's power and fuel cost continues to be amongst the lowest in the industry

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed midcap with questions from Nomura, Citi, HSBC, Kotak, Axis, ICICI and Ambit on every call — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the line of Siddharth Mehrotra from Kotak Securities

scores.rationale: Premium branding does deliver measurable pricing benefit — realization fell only Rs.90/t YoY versus Rs.250–390 for peers and premium mix reached 43% — but absolute gross margins remain commodity-grade.
scores.quote: our realization per ton has dropped by Rs.90.00 ... all the majors have dropped realization to the tune of Rs.250 to Rs.390

scores.rationale: Quality/technical assurance is sold through patented and specialty products, but the customer base repeatedly proves price-led — hikes are rolled back and volumes shift on realization, so trust does not override price.
scores.quote: India's first-ever hydrophobic concrete that repels water

scores.rationale: Real investment in accessibility and reach — 56 RMX plants, railway sidings at Sonadih/Jajpur/Kutch, a 1.5 mtpa Gujarat bulk terminal and a trade/individual-home-builder-centric channel.
scores.quote: It will serve as a strategic distribution hub to expand our reach across the Gujarat market

scores.rationale: The benefit-to-customer match is coherent: branded premium products (Concreto, Duraguard Microfiber, UNO) aimed at retail individual home builders, with a separate non-trade channel priced distinctly.
scores.quote: we are a individual trade-centric player, and that's where the improvement will happen

scores.rationale: There is a modest, real product-technology edge — a patented microfiber cement, hydrophobic and thermal-insulated concretes, plus best-in-class WHR/AFR/fuel-blending know-how — but it is not deep enough to be non-replicable across a multi-product platform.
scores.quote: all our factories have WHR, we have maximum percentage of blended cement, all our factories have got AFR consumption

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is two-sided or self-reinforcing with scale; demand is transactional bagged cement sold through dealers.

Distribution reach is solid and improving (rail sidings eliminating road clinker movement, RMX network, new Gujarat hub) but is not beyond the reach of far larger rivals, and rake availability remains an external constraint.
scores.quote: entire quarter, we have not moved clinker by road and everything has happened by rake

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex — stores 112 (FY23) to 313 (FY26), warehouses 18 to 44 with 2.5x capacity — delivered alongside rising returns, with ROCE at 21.2% and revenue doubling on a largely unchanged capital base.
scores.quote: return on capital employed also now stands at a healthy 21.2%... capital employed in the business, which hasn't grown that much and all of the revenue growth has come on the back of already existing capital employed

scores.rationale: A&P is treated as brand-building capex (content IPs, Nykaaland with 30,000 paying attendees, 100,000+ influencer affiliate network built over a decade) and is demonstrably efficient — visits, transacting customers and EBITDA margin all rose together.
scores.quote: the growth on revenue is coming alongside an improvement in the marketing efficiencies at all levels of the funnel

scores.rationale: No disclosed R&D line, but consistent tech/product investment (personalization, Nykaa Play, AI skin scan, derma recommendation engine) and own-brand product innovation have produced measurable commercial results.
scores.quote: we have created an online experience that includes an AI-powered skin scan

scores.rationale: Only small complementary bolt-ons (Dot & Key, Earth Rhythm) with outstanding post-deal outcomes — Dot & Key grew 13x in three years to INR 1,790 crores GMV and House of Nykaa saw large EBITDA expansion.
scores.quote: 2 successful acquisitions of both Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm behind us. Dot & Key has grown 13x over this last 3-year period

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy anywhere in the available call excerpts.

Capital efficiency is improving (ROCE 21.2%, revenue growth on existing capital employed), but the model is inventory-, warehouse- and store-heavy (44 warehouses, 1.5m sq ft, 313 stores), so it is efficient rather than genuinely asset-light.
scores.quote: We've been quite prudent on the amount of capital employed in the business, which hasn't grown that much

scores.rationale: Clear, quantified share capture in a market where it is far from dominant overall — prestige fragrance share up 300bps to ~13%, Korean beauty +58%, dermacosmetics +40%, all against a large unorganized/offline TAM.
scores.quote: our market share in the fragrance category... roughly 13% in FY '24, and this has been a 300 basis point improvement over FY '23

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is real but still small — Nysaa GCC platform, Kay Beauty into the UK via Space NK, and own brands in UAE/US/Mauritius — alongside domestic city expansion to 99 cities.
scores.quote: we spoke about the launch of Kay Beauty in the U.K and we continue to strengthen our partnership with Space NK

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume/customer-led (orders 36m to 66m, transacting customers doubled FY23–FY26) with a genuine but secondary mix tailwind from premiumization, luxury and own brands; AOVs have historically been broadly flat.
scores.quote: these customers placed about 66 million orders this fiscal versus 36 million orders in FY '23

scores.rationale: Not a cyclical business and no cycle-bottom positioning claimed; the only cyclicality referenced was a temporary industry discounting cycle in FY25 that has since normalised.
scores.quote: this trend started about a year ago and we are now at the end of the cycle

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — an underpenetrated Indian beauty market with premiumization, formalisation of unorganized retail, and stated TAMs of $15bn online BPC, $14bn organized offline and $15bn unorganized.
scores.quote: India being a market that still is highly underpenetrated when it comes to beauty consumption... how much headroom we have to grow

scores.rationale: Capital discipline has improved markedly (prudent capital employed, fashion losses narrowed from -5.4% to -2.0% of NSV, EBITDA 5.0% to 7.5%) with only tiny acquisitions, though the multiple simultaneous new-business bets temper the score.
scores.quote: our EBITDA has improved from 5.0% to 7.5%. Our PAT has improved from 0.4% to 2.0%

scores.rationale: Founder-led execution of a consistent long-horizon strategy — the content-to-commerce playbook and affiliate network built over ten years, a decade-long L'Oreal relationship and a six-year Charlotte Tilbury exclusive — sustained through a difficult post-IPO period.
scores.quote: we've been speaking about the content to commerce playbook since the very beginning of the journey as a company

scores.rationale: Management is highly visible and celebrity-adjacent — a famous founder with both children as executive directors, celebrity ambassadors, and a ticketed consumer festival — the opposite of low-profile stewardship.
scores.quote: we did host Nykaaland, the third addition of Nykaaland this quarter... we had 30,000 customers who actually bought tickets

scores.rationale: Professional CEOs have been added for each vertical (Distribution, Fashion, CFO), but the top roles remain within the promoter family and there has been visible churn in the CFO and Fashion-CEO seats across the period.
scores.quote: MR. ABHIJEET DABAS – EXECUTIVE VICE PRESIDENT, NYKAA FASHION.COM

scores.rationale: Management explains variances candidly — the GMV vs net-revenue gap from industry discounting, restructuring costs, subdued fashion quarters and one-off labor-code charges — though the tone leans heavily on 'highest ever' framing and adjusted metrics.
scores.quote: This PAT number is after adjusting for onetime impact of a new labor code... the number would have been at INR 78 crores

scores.rationale: The operating improvement is real and quantified (EBITDA margin 4% in Q1FY23 to 8.4% in Q4FY26), but it comes off a very low base and is presented with superlative-heavy commentary, so results should be credited only partly to durable skill.
scores.quote: one of the highest EBITDA margin ever, not just in the last 14 quarters, but ever

scores.rationale: Nykaa occupies a near-monopoly position in the Indian consumer's and global brand-owner's mind for prestige beauty — chosen as exclusive India launch partner by Chanel, La Prairie, SK-II, La Roche-Posay and others.
scores.quote: Nykaa partnered with Chanel, La Prairie and SK-II to be the retail partner of choice for these ultra-luxury beauty brands when it came time for their India launch

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real on the brand side — full-stack operation of Kiehl's, Nike and Foot Locker India businesses plus importer-of-record status for 40+ brands makes Nykaa hard to displace — though consumer-side switching remains easy.
scores.quote: more than 40 international brands have trusted us with their brands in the country

scores.rationale: The structure is contested rather than a stable oligopoly — own brands compete on Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit, and quick-commerce entrants forced Nykaa to build its own 30-minute offering.
scores.quote: It's the number one sunscreen brand across Nykaa, Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are moderate and pricing rationality has been breached — an industry-wide discounting cycle depressed net revenue relative to GMV through FY24-25, and new quick-commerce and specialty-retail entrants keep arriving.
scores.quote: the industry has seen higher discounts from various brands that are traded on our platform

scores.rationale: A large pool of weak competitors exists — a $15bn unorganized retail TAM plus fragmented general trade being converted through the Superstore's 485,000 retailers and House of Nykaa's GT doors.
scores.quote: $15 billion TAM of unorganized retail in beauty, all of that is addressed by us

scores.rationale: Nykaa is one of India's most closely watched listed consumer-tech names with a celebrity founder and quarterly analyst scrutiny — the antithesis of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Nykaa has actually India's largest network of influencers and content creators today

scores.rationale: Beauty carries strong image/aspiration pull and gross margin is high and rising (45.4% of net revenue), but industry-wide discounting shows pricing power is not absolute.
scores.quote: gross profit has come out at INR 1,203 crores, which is 45.4%... One of the highest gross margin ever

scores.rationale: Trust and authenticity are the core purchase driver in Indian beauty and both consumers and global brand owners buy that certainty from Nykaa, which is repeatedly chosen as launch and distribution partner of record.
scores.quote: Nykaa continues to remain the trusted partner for all of the iconic beauty groups globally

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine differentiator — order-to-delivery cut from four days to 2.2 days across 19,000 pincodes, ~50% of orders same/next day, Nykaa Now at 30 minutes to 2 hours, plus 313 stores and hyperlocal-enabled retail.
scores.quote: the average order to delivery time line on our platform across all 19,000 pincodes... is now 2.2 days

scores.rationale: The benefit set is well matched on both sides — content, experience and image for retail consumers, and reliability plus deep switching-cost lock-in (full-stack D2C, store operation, exclusivity) for corporate brand customers.
scores.quote: we are also now building and operating their exclusive brand stores in the country. And this is a first for them, not just in India, but in the APAC region

scores.rationale: Meaningful but not deep technology edge — cohort-based personalization, recommendation widgets, live commerce and an AI skin scan improve conversion, yet none is a defensible multi-product technical barrier.
scores.quote: customers who showed a propensity to buy luxury products, get shown a higher share of luxury brands on their home feed

scores.rationale: A genuine three-sided flywheel exists between 52 million customers, 6,700+ brands and 100,000+ influencers, with management citing store-to-ecommerce network effects, though it is reinforcing rather than fully self-locking.
scores.quote: not just in terms of the revenue that it's driving, but also in terms of the network effects that it's having on our e-commerce business

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the standout asset rivals cannot easily replicate — the country's largest beauty specialty store network (313 stores, 99 cities), 44 warehouses, Superstore reaching 485,000 retailers and 150,000 GT doors for own brands.
scores.quote: we do have the largest network of beauty specialty stores in the country... we sit at about 313 stores

scores.rationale: Sustained, large growth capex across new townships, malls, offices and hotels (Sky City mall ~1.1m sq ft leasable, Commerz III to 98% occupancy, Thane Garden City, Ritz-Carlton) funded largely from internal accruals with 43-65% project margins, with land mostly acquired without large upfront cash.
scores.quote: most of our land parcels do not require us to pay cash up front... everything else is linked to revenue generated

scores.rationale: Deliberate, campaign-led marketing that builds brand pull (pre-launch advertising build-up, 30-day EOI campaigns, ready experience centres and show apartments) and translates into demand, though spend is never quantified.
scores.quote: We had taken interest letters almost three weeks in advance. So we had actually mopped the entire market... a nice campaign built over 30 days

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or product-development pipeline in the technical sense is discussed anywhere in the calls.

Deals are bolt-on land/asset acquisitions complementary to the core (Nirmal Lifestyle Realty, Horizon Hotel via NCLT, Alibaug JDA, SRA redevelopments) rather than corporate empire-building, and the acquired Gurugram land produced an ~Rs.8,000 crore first-phase launch — but acquirees are distressed, not already-strong businesses.
scores.quote: we have just concluded a transaction by acquiring Nirmal Lifestyle Realty Private Limited and entered into a joint development agreement for 81 acres at Alibaug

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed; the only capital-structure item mentioned is an enabling QIP resolution to raise, not return, capital.
scores.quote: we do have an enabling resolution, which allows us to do anything that we want in terms of a particular value

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy — large land bank, multi-year capital lock-up and a growing annuity portfolio — with management itself conceding the capital cycle is long and returns unexceptional, though the brand moat is genuine.
scores.quote: our capital cycle is such that it continues to be stuck for much longer... the end effect of this margin, the return you get is still not that great

scores.rationale: Small share of a highly fragmented market with demonstrated capture — repeated micro-market dominance in Goregaon/Borivali plus a debut NCR launch that sold ~1.4m sq ft in one phase, and management asserts share resilience in downturns via flight to quality.
scores.quote: whenever there is any correction or any sort of tension in the market, the flight is always towards quality

scores.rationale: Credible, executed expansion from a Goregaon/Worli base into Thane, Mulund, Alibaug and then NCR, where the Three Sixty North debut was an outright success and management is now scaling BD into Noida/Gurgaon.
scores.quote: We've started our journey outside MMR with our project in NCR by launching Three Sixty North. This marks an important milestone

scores.rationale: Growth is meaningfully price- and mix-led (20% price hikes in Goregaon, repricing in Borivali/Thane, shift to higher floors and Rs.12-60 crore ticket sizes), but the step-changes in bookings still come from large new-launch volume.
scores.quote: we've increased price in Thane. We've increased price in Borivali. We've increased price in Goregaon by 20%, and yet there doesn't seem to be [resistance]

scores.rationale: The company sits well into an upcycle rather than near a trough — record prices, three years of strong demand, with visible late-cycle strain in Worli luxury off-take and 2-3% input cost inflation eroding contingencies.
scores.quote: Three Sixty West, FY26 where you sold 10 units versus 17 in FY25. So, clearly there is some slowdown in the Worli luxury market

scores.rationale: Genuine secular tailwinds — rising consumption per square foot, infrastructure build-out (metro, coastal road, Thane-Borivali link) and consolidation toward branded developers — though the underlying housing market remains cyclical.
scores.quote: consumption for person -- per square foot has gone up, and that really is the delta... a family of 4 want to buy a much bigger house

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage and self-funded, opportunistic counter-cyclical land buying with cash recycled from ready inventory, though BD intensity is very high and includes NCLT-route corporate acquisitions.
scores.quote: we are opportunistic, if we see good land at any point in time, be it a bad market or a good market, we go and buy that

scores.rationale: Consistent long-horizon behaviour across the 3-year window — 15-20 year township build-outs, refusal to launch before the product meets internal standards, and patient sequencing of Borivali/Goregaon phases over 40 years in the business.
scores.quote: until unless something comes to a level where we are excited and bring it to the people, we don't really launch

scores.rationale: Mixed: professes to let work speak and keeps calls to a tight 30 minutes, but the promoter gives media interviews on ambitions and makes superlative claims about his own projects.
scores.quote: It's probably... the best project in the city or the country or whatever one can say

scores.rationale: Little evidence of systematic talent development; the CEO layer has churned (Basav Mukherjee exited FY2024, three CEOs appointed FY2026) and capability is credited mainly to outsourced contractors, though scaling capacity is claimed.
scores.quote: the way we've built our entire team of contractors who we outsource is really solid

scores.rationale: Generally candid on costs and errors — quantifies 2-3% cost inflation, admits contingencies are eroding, owns communication failures and omissions — but deflects repeatedly on 360 West timelines, GDV and litigation.
scores.quote: a lot of people didn't understand our strategy or probably we did a bad job in explaining

scores.rationale: Results are real but materially aided by a strong Mumbai upcycle and secondary-market price inflation the company did not create, and repeated slippage between BD promises and launches (guided launches for years before they materialised) tempers the skill attribution.
scores.quote: we didn't see much growth... last year was more of a sustenance, I would say, where you were just releasing additional towers

scores.rationale: Owns effective micro-market monopolies — a self-contained integrated ecosystem at Garden City and sole remaining inventory holder at Three Sixty West — but this is project-level, not category-level.
scores.quote: within Three Sixty, we are reasonably, I can say, monopoly now

scores.rationale: Regional/micro-market lock-in from irreplaceable land parcels and self-built infrastructure (mall-to-metro connectivity, school, hotel) that competitors in the same catchment cannot replicate, though homebuyers face no switching costs.
scores.quote: literally, nobody will be able to offer what we are doing within our own bubble

scores.rationale: MMR residential is fragmented and competitive, with peers actively entering the market and supply within the same micro-markets directly diluting sales.
scores.quote: some of your peers doing some amazing business development activities in MMR, some are coming into MMR

scores.rationale: High approval/land barriers in MMR and rational pricing behaviour — the company raises rather than discounts prices, follows secondary-market benchmarks, and promoter ownership is stable — but new competition is entering.
scores.quote: our strategy is always to be proactive when it comes to pricing... there's no knee-jerk reaction on increasing a price

scores.rationale: Ample weak competitors to take from — the erstwhile Worli partner's fire sale, Nirmal Lifestyle's NCLT insolvency, the distressed IREO Gurugram asset — all converted into Oberoi land and share.
scores.quote: our partner did a fire sale and exited in March... We have also received approval from NCLT for our resolution plan

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a large listed developer covered by HSBC, CLSA, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Kotak, Nomura and others, operating in the most-watched real estate market in India.
scores.quote: everybody knows we are coming, I feel, you know, we are in for some exciting time there

scores.rationale: Powerful brand-derived pricing power — top-of-mind status with buyers, resale trading 20-25% above launch prices, and project gross margins of 43-65% sustained for years.
scores.quote: we have become a strong brand. When people decide to buy a house, we are on top of their mind

scores.rationale: Customers buy delivery certainty over price — flight to quality in downturns, preference for ready/near-ready Oberoi product, and NCR buyers refusing refunds even amid litigation.
scores.quote: we have customers who refuse to take refund of the deposit... They want to wait if there is any cancellation

scores.rationale: Strong direct-selling and customer-intimacy infrastructure — ready experience centres and show apartments, pre-launch EOI mopping of the market, and physical convenience designed into products.
scores.quote: walk out of the apartment, walk through the mall and straight away go into the metro station directly without even putting your feet on the road

scores.rationale: Benefit types are well matched — image and lifestyle intangibles for retail homebuyers, and reliability/Grade-A assurance for corporate tenants, evidenced by 98-100% office occupancy with marquee names.
scores.quote: Commerz III continues to scale up strongly, attracting marquee tenants... with an occupancy reaching 98%

scores.rationale: No technology edge or R&D intensity; the only differentiator claimed is construction speed and design execution via outsourced contractors, which is operational rather than proprietary.
scores.quote: we were able to do almost, 38 and 40 slabs a year... we have cracked the code as far as volume and quality is concerned

scores.rationale: No two-sided network; the closest analogue is a mall/township ecosystem whose benefits are localised to a catchment and do not compound with company scale.
scores.quote: We are planning a mall there. We are planning an international school there... we will create an ecosystem of itself

scores.rationale: Distribution is neither an advantage nor a handicap — sales are direct and project-led with no rival-proof reach, though the irreplaceable land bank and integrated locations substitute partly for it.
scores.quote: we have probably the best land parcel one could have got in Thane

scores.rationale: Sustained, rising growth capex — NRL 3→9 MMTPA expansion (~INR28,000 cr, INR19,000 cr already spent by FY25), pipeline expansions and drilling ramp from 36 wells (FY20) to 74–75+ (FY26) — but returns are exposed to administered prices and windfall levies rather than demonstrably high incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: this cost for this NRL is -- this is INR28,000 crores. Currently, the physical progress is 65%

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend across any of the calls.

Some innovation output (2G bamboo ethanol yielding green furfural/acetic acid/biochar, Drive 2.0 digital initiatives, deeper 5,500m+ seismic-led drilling) but no disclosed R&D intensity and offshore capability is bought in via TotalEnergies rather than developed in-house.
scores.quote: we have got Total Energy which is an international oil company, as our Technology Service Agreement partner

scores.rationale: Inorganic exposure is the opposite of small complementary bolt-ons — a large debt-funded Mozambique LNG stake that sat under force majeure until Nov 2025 with first gas pushed to 2028-29, plus Russian assets, driving INR11,330 crore of standalone debt.
scores.quote: effective November 2025, the force majeure which was there earlier in Mozambique project has been removed... two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA getting commissioned end 2028 or early 2029

scores.rationale: Dividends are steady and were deliberately held flat at INR11.5/share through a crude downcycle, showing some policy consistency, but there are no buybacks and distribution is effectively a CPSE payout convention rather than valuation-disciplined capital return.
scores.quote: this year we announced a dividend, which is precisely the same that we had announced last year, i.e. Rs. 11.5 per share

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy model — INR28,000 crore refinery expansion, multi-year pipeline builds and 75 wells a year against ~INR9,000 crore quarterly consolidated revenue — the antithesis of asset-light.
scores.quote: Roughly about INR19,000 crores has already invested

scores.rationale: Growth comes from its own reserve base and government-allotted OALP/DSF acreage rather than any evidence of taking share from competitors, though it remains far smaller than ONGC.
scores.quote: we have already acquired on 25 numbers of OLAP blocks where we are yet to achieve any area result till now

scores.rationale: Credible, visible expansion beyond the Assam home base into Rajasthan (now 1,000 bopd), KG, Mahanadi, Andaman and Kerala-Konkan offshore, plus CGD areas in Kolhapur and Ambala-Kurukshetra, though execution timelines have been long.
scores.quote: three offshore drilling operations are currently underway... we are drilling a deepest well, 6,000 meter... Kerala Konkan

scores.rationale: Growth is purely volume/wells-led while price is exogenous and falling — crude realization dropped from $79.35 to $65.73 per barrel over nine months and gas sits at an administered ~$6.5-6.65/MMBtu.
scores.quote: 17.16% decline in the crude oil price realization is the major driver in decline of our operating revenues

scores.rationale: Crude has softened from $78 to $69 and SAED/windfall levies have compressed margins, so the company sits low in the cycle, but management identifies no upturn catalyst and explicitly declines to forecast prices.
scores.quote: recent macro environment has once again underscored how dynamic the energy landscape can be shaped by geopolitics, supply discipline and the transition

scores.rationale: The Indian energy end-market is in genuine secular expansion, reinforced by the LPG-to-PNG migration push and CGD build-out targets (CNG 80→500 stations, PNG 73,300→1.4mn by 2030-35), tempered by long-run fossil transition risk.
scores.quote: India's hunger for energy. Therefore, the energy demand... continues to grow strongly

scores.rationale: Mostly organic drilling-led growth with moderate leverage and continued investment through the downcycle, but the large debt-funded Mozambique exposure and INR28,000 crore refinery bet cut against conservative stewardship.
scores.quote: on a stand-alone basis, the debt is INR11,330 crores, which is primarily, that is debt the company has taken for Mozambique project

scores.rationale: The 4 MMT oil / 5 BCM gas ambition has been pursued tenaciously since 2022 with record drilling, but it has slipped repeatedly from FY25 to FY27+ and strategy is heavily steered by government programmes (Samudra Manthan, PM-inaugurated projects) rather than independent capital allocation.
scores.quote: this year 3.2, next year 3.6 and next year 4.1... that is the target as of now

scores.rationale: Low-key, technocratic CPSE management that speaks in operational specifics; the CMD only appeared on an earnings call for the first time in Feb 2026 after nearly four years in post.
scores.quote: a special welcome to Dr. Ranjit Rath for the first time I think he is on the call

scores.rationale: Leadership continuity is poor — every Managing Director listed exited in FY2023 and the Director HR was simultaneously carrying additional charge of Director Finance — indicating government-appointment churn rather than a managed internal pipeline.
scores.quote: MR. ASHOK DAS -- DIRECTOR, HR & ADDITIONAL CHARGE OF DIRECTOR (FINANCE)

scores.rationale: Management discloses bad news specifically and quantifies it — the economic blockade production loss, gas offtaker shutdowns, well write-offs and the GST-on-royalty provisioning — and refuses to over-promise on numbers it cannot support.
scores.quote: we lost an opportunity of about 0.1 million metric ton of crude oil and about 0.3 million BCM of natural gas

scores.rationale: Reported profits swing chiefly on exogenous factors — crude realization, SAED/windfall tax and NRL's GRM moving from -$15.59 to +$16.27 per barrel — so strong headline results should not be read as evidence of managerial skill.
scores.quote: The decline in PAT is mainly on account of increase in SAED and other statutory levies

scores.rationale: OIL is effectively the sole gas supplier in the North East, feeding Numaligarh Refinery, Namrup power, BVFCL and the region's CGD entities off its own fields and dedicated lines.
scores.quote: the northeastern region will get saturated and the CGD entities will now also get fed through NRL being a reseller

scores.rationale: A genuine regional monopoly with physical switching costs — dedicated Duliajan-Numaligarh and Numaligarh-Siliguri pipelines, plus CGD licences covering all of Arunachal, Nagaland, north bank Assam and Guwahati, leave captive customers no alternative supplier.
scores.quote: in northeast Oil India has got through its subsidiaries and JVs, the entire Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, six districts of Tripura, entire north bank of Assam

scores.rationale: Although Indian upstream is a two-player state oligopoly, the negotiating power sits entirely with the counterparty — the government sets APM gas prices and imposed an opaque, fortnightly-revised windfall levy the company could not even explain.
scores.quote: We are not aware of any formula. This is the numbers which have been declared

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are very high (licensing rounds, PNGRB authorisations, multi-year capital cycles) and there is no discounting behaviour since prices are administered, with permanently stable government ownership.
scores.quote: the feeder line needs authorization of the government... after the PNGRB approval is done, it takes 18 months' time

scores.rationale: There are no weak rivals to harvest — incremental volumes come from OIL's own workovers, deeper wells and newly bid acreage, not from displacing anyone.
scores.quote: we drilled 61 wells... this year, we have already completed 62 wells

scores.rationale: A listed Maharatna CPSE covered by ICICI, Emkay, Ambit, Spark and others, subject to windfall taxation, Supreme Court litigation and PM-level project inaugurations — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the Honorable PM inaugurated one of our flagship initiative, which is 2G ethanol

scores.rationale: Pure commodity with zero image-based pricing power; realizations are set by Brent-linked and administered formulas and margins collapse when prices fall.
scores.quote: average price realization for Q3 FY '26 was $62.84 per barrel vis a vis $73.8 per barrel in Q3 of FY '25

scores.rationale: Customers do rely on OIL for regional supply security, but the dependence runs the wrong way — production is throttled by customers' shutdowns and evacuation constraints rather than OIL commanding a trust premium.
scores.quote: The gas sales have experienced minimum de-growth driven by reduced offtake from major customers such as Namrup Power Plant, BVFCL

scores.rationale: Physical proximity and captive last-mile access are real advantages — gas produced next to NRL and North East consumers, plus an expanding CGD footprint of 80+ CNG stations targeting 500 by 2030-35.
scores.quote: till now we have got about 80 plus CNG stations and about 73,300 PNG stations

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/industrial (refinery, power, fertiliser) with pipeline-based switching costs, an appropriate match, but pricing is administered so the lock-in yields no TCO-based pricing premium.
scores.quote: there will be an additional gas requirement for that... close to 2 MMSCMD for expanded capability

scores.rationale: Technical capability is improving (5,500m+ deep wells, 23-day Rajasthan drilling, deeper-horizon seismic imaging) but the frontier offshore capability is licensed from TotalEnergies and deepwater exploration is to be government-funded, indicating no proprietary tech edge.
scores.quote: the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing two-sided network exists; the gas grid is capital infrastructure whose value depends on third-party pipeline commissioning and offtaker availability, not on user-driven scale effects.
scores.quote: once the Indradhanush Gas Grid is completed in the entire North East

scores.rationale: Owned and JV evacuation infrastructure across the North East — the expanded Numaligarh-Siliguri (1.72→5.5 MMTPA) and Duliajan-Numaligarh (1→2.5 MMTPA) lines, the Duliajan feeder authorisation and IGGL hookup — is reach no rival can replicate in that region.
scores.quote: the Numaligarh-Siliguri pipeline capacity expansion... is already commissioned. It was inaugurated by the Honorable Prime Minister

scores.rationale: Growth capex has been very large (~₹5,300 cr into manufacturing, cells and R&D, 1mn unit auto capacity and 6 GWh cells) but incremental ROIC is deeply negative — FY26 revenue was only ₹2,253 cr on 173,794 deliveries against an asset base sized for ₹15,000-20,000 cr.
scores.quote: we have invested approximately ₹5,300 crores across manufacturing, battery innovation and R&D... the asset base can support approximately 15,000 to 20,000 crores of annual revenue

scores.rationale: The company deliberately spends nothing on marketing and still shows leading brand recall/Google search share, but the same brand lost trust through the service crisis, so A&P is neither a value-creating nor value-destroying lever here.
scores.quote: our business model does not have any spends on marketing, etc., so that also benefits when we think of operating costs

scores.rationale: R&D has repeatedly converted into shipped product — Gen2→Gen3 platform, in-house motor/ABS/electronics, rare-earth-free motor and the 4680 Bharat cell with 70+ patents — with gross margins moving from ~10% to 38.5%, though returns are still unproven at the P&L level.
scores.quote: over three generations, our gross margins went up from 10 percent to 35 percent now and our product quality improved meaningfully

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed anywhere across the nine calls; the entire strategy is organic vertical integration.

There is no dividend or buyback policy; the company is instead refinancing pre-IPO debt via fresh NCDs and planning further equity dilution at the cell entity, i.e. capital absorption rather than distribution.
scores.quote: expanding that 6 to 20 GWh by next year, but only by raising capital separately at the cell entity

scores.rationale: The business is extremely asset-heavy — ~₹5,300 cr invested and a 1mn-unit/6 GWh footprint generating just ₹2,253 cr FY26 revenue (asset turn well under 0.5x) — with no moat that has protected volumes.
scores.quote: The heavy Capex phase, which we have been investing so far, is behind us now. Our current footprint supports 1 million vehicles and 6 gigawatt hour of cell capacity

scores.rationale: Share collapsed from 48.6% of Indian e-2W in Q1 FY25 to a position where quarterly deliveries fell to 32,680 and management asks investors to ignore share, with only a partial recent rebound.
scores.quote: we don't worry about short-term market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is purely domestic regional recovery (north/east strong, regaining south/west) with global energy-storage ambitions still aspirational, so there is no executed geographic expansion to credit.
scores.quote: We are very strong in the north and east, which is actually a growing EV market, and we are gaining back our position in the south and west

scores.rationale: ASPs have been flat and mix shifted toward mass-market S1X/Roadster X; all margin gain came from cost-out and vertical integration, not pricing, and recent gross margin was even spent on growth.
scores.quote: if you see our ASPs are flat, but our gross profit per vehicle is continuing to grow

scores.rationale: The company is arguably past the trough — EV penetration growth slowed and industry volumes fell 22%, yet its own registrations rose 20% MoM with inventory down to 3-4 days and an order backlog, pointing to an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: April registrations were up 20% month-on-month, while the broader E two-wheeler industry declined by more than 22%

scores.rationale: End markets — ICE-to-EV two-wheeler conversion (motorcycles two-thirds of the market, still tiny EV penetration) plus domestic cell manufacturing and grid storage — are in genuine secular expansion backed by policy tailwinds.
scores.quote: mobility moving from ICE to EV and energy moving from imported fuels to locally made batteries

scores.rationale: Focus is organic with no M&A, but capacity and store network were built far ahead of demand (OpEx ₹844 cr/qtr peak cut to ₹428 cr, mass exits) and funded with SBI term loans and NCD refinancing — expansionary rather than prudent.
scores.quote: Consolidated quarterly OPECs, including leases, reduced from ₹840 crores at peak expansion to ₹484 crores

scores.rationale: The founder has pursued a decade-long vertical-integration thesis independently and actually delivered the only operational Indian gigafactory and in-house cell/motor/ABS stack despite heavy criticism.
scores.quote: only Indian company to have operationalized the Gigafactory

scores.rationale: This is a celebrity-founder company built on Independence Day launch events, social-media buzz and the highest search-brand profile in Indian EV — the opposite of low-profile.
scores.quote: you can see Ola is by far the highest search brand in the EV space in India

scores.rationale: Evidence points to churn rather than pipeline: CFO replaced (Harish Abichandani → Deepak Rastogi) and large severance-driven employee costs from exits during the Q3 FY26 reset.
scores.quote: the one-off employee costs will be largely linked to the exits

scores.rationale: Management explicitly owned the service failure and its brand-trust damage, disclosed segment and cash-flow detail, and published shareholder letters — though prior breakeven and volume guidance (3.25-3.75 lakh FY26 vs 1.74 lakh actual) was badly missed.
scores.quote: we do have a service challenge which we are working through that has impacted brand trust and hence sales are down

scores.rationale: The narrative is heavily self-congratulatory — claims of insurmountable leads and industry-best everything — even as volumes fell ~75% and the company remains loss-making, making results hard to separate from storytelling.
scores.quote: they are so far ahead of competition that I don't feel it's so easy for anybody to catch up

scores.rationale: Far from owning the customer's mind or the aftermarket, its service/aftermarket franchise was the very thing that drove customers away, with backlogs of 14 days before remediation.
scores.quote: we identified gaps in service execution... service backlogs have reduced nearly 50% from 14 days to around 7-8 days

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs — prospective buyers simply held back over service noise and share moved to rivals, demonstrating a fully contestable customer base.
scores.quote: the prospective customers who are holding back due to the brand noise around service

scores.rationale: The Indian e-2W market is fragmented and consolidating among many players with retail customers who are highly price-sensitive, giving no oligopolistic pricing protection.
scores.quote: industry is steady and consolidating and there will be another growth phase in the near future

scores.rationale: ICE incumbents and EV startups continue to enter, and the company itself admits ploughing gross margin into aggressive growth — a discounting posture rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: some of this gross margin in the last month or two we've invested into aggressive growth

scores.rationale: There are weak donors available — ICE two-wheelers losing share structurally, and in electric motorcycles Ola already holds 50%+ against a nascent, thin competitive field.
scores.quote: Ola now has 50% market share in electric motorcycles, and bikes contributed 15% of April gross orders
