scores.quote: margin pressure is in one particular segment, which is, say, carbon steel line pipes, and that too water

scores.rationale: Three consecutive record years to FY24 owed much to the oil, gas and water capex cycle, and the sharp FY26 reversal confirms results are cycle-driven; skill shows only in holding EBITDA percentage flat on much lower volumes.
scores.quote: our continued focus on operational efficiency, cost optimization and improved product mix with higher value-added products ensured that there was no negative impact on the EBITDA margins

scores.rationale: Genuine approval-based near-monopoly niches — sole Indian nuclear-approved spool facility for NPCIL and first Indian supplier of hydrogen-compliant pipe — though these are small parts of group revenue.
scores.quote: the only nuclear approved facility from India for Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited

scores.rationale: Customer approvals (Aramco LSAW, ADNOC, NPCIL, API monogram) create real qualification-based switching costs that take years to replicate, but orders are still won tender by tender rather than locked in.
scores.quote: Our Kutch plant received the API monogram certification from American Petroleum Institute

scores.rationale: Not a stable oligopoly — competitive intensity is rising as carbon steel players enter stainless, and end customers are PSUs, governments and Aramco/ADNOC who tender and hold strong negotiating power.
scores.quote: a lot of carbon steel players plus other players, the competition intensity in stainless steel or carbon steel is increasing

scores.rationale: Mixed picture: excess domestic stainless capacity and pricing pressure in water line pipes indicate weak barriers in the commodity end, while the extruded high-value segment sees only one new entrant expected.
scores.quote: our focus remains on high value-added extruded products, where only one new player is supposed to come

scores.rationale: Weaker rivals exist to take share from — new domestic capacity is concentrated in lower-grade pierced seamless that Ratnamani does not compete in, and imports of large-diameter product have been displaced by its own extrusion.
scores.quote: most of the capacity is for the pierced seamless products. So which market as it is, Ratnamani is not catering to

scores.rationale: The niches are specialised but the company is a well-covered listed midcap with brokerage-hosted quarterly calls and multiple analysts, and rivals are actively adding capacity in its segments.
scores.quote: hosted by Monarch Networth Capital Limited

scores.rationale: Pricing is tender- and steel-price-linked rather than image-driven, though the value-added range (Rs. 300 to Rs. 5,000 per kg) supports a defensible 16-18% EBITDA band rather than commodity economics.
scores.quote: We have a product range which starts at Rs. 300 a kg, goes up to Rs. 5,000 a kg in Stainless Steel

scores.rationale: Customers in refineries, gas transmission and nuclear buy certified reliability where failure is catastrophic, and the company competes on approvals and benchmark quality — but it still wins through competitive tenders where price matters.
scores.quote: best in segment facilities with benchmark qualities

scores.rationale: Deliberate moves toward customer proximity — a European stock-and-sale subsidiary and a Saudi plant to serve GCC customers locally — though this is early-stage rather than an established access advantage.
scores.quote: this particular subsidiary was, say, trade and stock was only for stainless-steel products

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to a corporate/institutional base — Aramco, ADNOC, IOCL, NPCIL, SKF/Schaeffler — where the sell is qualification, reliability and approval-driven lock-in rather than brand intangibles.
scores.quote: Abu Dhabi, which is customers like ADNOC or contractors who are working for ADNOC

scores.rationale: A real multi-product process edge — extrusion press for 8-10 inch and heavy-wall product, 150 mm thickness circulars, 18-metre spiral, clad and hydrogen-compliant pipe — though it is process/qualification depth rather than proprietary high-R&D-intensity technology.
scores.quote: expansion project of circulars of pipes for higher diameter and 18 meters in length having thickness up to 150 mm

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.
Sales are project- and tender-based with no distribution or service-reach advantage claimed; the only network build-out is a small Swiss stocking entity and a planned Saudi facility.
scores.quote: it is not a stock and sale item for us

scores.rationale: Capex is modest and majority maintenance, with management explicitly disavowing major growth investment.
scores.quote: Rs. 175 to 200 crores of CAPEX, of which let's say 55%-60% is a maintenance CAPEX

scores.rationale: Consistent A&P spend (KBC wardrobe partner, cinema/cricket, new CMO from HUL) but apparel EBITDA margins stayed thin at ~5% and marketing is admitted to be fragmented, so brand-equity payback is unproven.
scores.quote: move forward from fragmented marketing to a more connected omnichannel system

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but sustained product innovation (techno-series, Super 120s/140s, linen, AI-inspired lines) is visibly converting into ASP and mix gains.
scores.quote: Average selling price increases by about INR 26 per meter, reflecting the growing contribution of premium and technical fabrics

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed across the seven calls; growth is organic and via new in-house brands.
No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is mentioned in any excerpt.
Mixed: owned suiting/shirting/garmenting factories are asset-heavy with working capital at 77–90 days, offset by an asset-light franchise retail model and improved utilisation.
scores.quote: Shorter format stores, an asset-light franchise-led model, and capital partnering enable us to grow efficiently

scores.rationale: Explicit, repeated evidence of share capture from imported fabrics and in Tier 2/3, with the trade channel outgrowing the industry.
scores.quote: Industry growth remains amid single digits, while... the Raymond Lifestyle trade channel is growing in double digits

scores.rationale: Deliberate Tier 2/3 domestic push plus export de-risking from the US to UK/EU/APAC and Ethiopia, with Q4 garmenting up 38% validating the pivot.
scores.quote: we have reduced our dependency on the US market from about 50% to 35%

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly attributes growth to volume first, with premiumization/mix a secondary (though improving) contributor.
scores.quote: a year-on-year growth of 18%, mainly driven by improved business performance in the Branded Textile and Branded Apparel segment led by volume growth

scores.rationale: The FY25 trough (demand-hit quarters, Q1FY25 EBITDA of only Rs 89 cr) has clearly inflected into a discretionary-consumption upturn aided by tax/GST relief and heavy wedding dates.
scores.quote: FY26 has been a year of recovery for Raymond Lifestyle

scores.rationale: End market benefits from durable formalization, unbranded-to-branded conversion and Tier 2/3 income growth.
scores.quote: clear structural shifts, premiumization of the demand, continued formalization post-GST and strong price inelastic consumption around weddings

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, no M&A, calibrated capex and a balance sheet taken to net cash, with unprofitable stores exited rather than defended.
scores.quote: We remain debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crores

scores.rationale: Trajectory shows repeated strategy resets — the 200-store/18-month and Ethnix Rs 300–350 cr ambitions gave way to closures, and the new team is outsourcing strategy to consultants rather than executing a settled long-term vision.
scores.quote: we are also employing one of the big consultancy firms to build a three-year strategy for us

scores.rationale: A promoter-chairman-led, celebrity-brand house with high-visibility media platforms (KBC, cinema campaigns) rather than substance-over-profile management.
scores.quote: we have been selected as the official wardrobe partner for this season's highly popular quiz show, Kaun Banega Crorepati

scores.rationale: Favourable workforce metrics, but the entire senior bench — CEO, CFO, Group CFO, CMO — was hired externally within months, indicating no internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: recent appointment of Rakesh Tiwary as Group CFO, Prasad as Lifestyle CFO, and myself as the CEO, and I just introduced Kalpana as the new CMO

scores.rationale: Management discloses adverse items plainly (one-time subsidy in the base, loss-making emerging businesses, Ethnix being a four-year journey) and the new CEO openly declined to answer rather than bluff.
scores.quote: I have just done four days of office here

scores.rationale: Record FY26 results lean heavily on external tailwinds (income-tax/GST relief, dense wedding dates, weak base) and cost actions like store closures, so skill is not cleanly separable from cycle.
scores.quote: the tax benefit... to the tune of INR1 lakh crore, as well as the GST benefit... people have more money to spend

scores.rationale: Raymond holds a near-monopoly position in the customer's mind for worsted suiting and wedding occasion wear, especially in smaller towns.
scores.quote: in Tier 3 and Tier 4, Raymond still stands a very big brand for them

scores.rationale: The proprietary TRS fabric-plus-stitching channel is a genuine structural quirk, but it creates habit rather than real switching costs for customers.
scores.quote: that is a very unique model which we have through the TRS

scores.rationale: Branded worsted suiting is concentrated in Raymond's favour, but apparel and ethnic wear are crowded and the market is described as roughly half unbranded.
scores.quote: This market is roughly around 50-50 branded and unbranded today

scores.rationale: Low entry barriers in apparel/ethnics with multiple new industrial-house entrants and imported competition, plus routine end-of-season discounting.
scores.quote: other competitive brands like Tasva which many, many industrial houses they have started

scores.rationale: A large unbranded and imported-fabric pool is being displaced, though the Ethnix store closures show some of that share is harder to take than assumed.
scores.quote: some of the Italian products... imported products were in the counters, which we have been able to replace with our products

scores.rationale: A century-old iconic listed brand with broad analyst coverage and mass-media presence is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: an iconic brand that boasts of legacy spanning over a century

scores.rationale: Brand image supports premiumization and price-inelastic occasion demand, with gross margins around 44% and successful super-premium launches.
scores.quote: strong price inelastic consumption around weddings and occasions

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly trust and authenticity rather than price, particularly for high-stakes wedding purchases.
scores.quote: Raymond stands for a very trustworthy brand

scores.rationale: Unmatched physical reach with cross-sell of fabric and apparel plus stitching service creates real customer accessibility.
scores.quote: the spread is to the tune of more than 1,000 stores over 600 cities, which sell our apparel

scores.rationale: Benefit mix is well matched — image/trust intangibles for retail consumers, and design/innovation-led supply for B2B fabric buyers driving repeat demand.
scores.quote: we have been able to innovate some of the products, designs, which are liked by the B2B players

scores.rationale: Functional fabric innovation exists but is incremental finishing technology, not a deep multi-product tech edge backed by R&D intensity.
scores.quote: These fabrics offer features such as stretch, wrinkle-resistant and stain-resistant

scores.rationale: The business model is a linear brand-manufacture-retail chain with no two-sided network described anywhere in the calls.
The TRS network across 600+ towns, layered with EBO, MBO, LFS and online, is a reach management credibly claims no rival possesses, and it combines retail with stitching service.
scores.quote: We have the TRS, which if you see practically in the industry, not many would have this kind of a channel

scores.rationale: Growth capex is genuinely high and sustained (328 stores in Aug-2022 to ~600 by Mar-2026, 351 cafés, kiosks in all stores), but incremental returns are weak — ADS fell from INR131K in Jul-2022 to INR117K in Q3FY26 and company EBITDA is still only ~5.8%.
scores.quote: we ended December 31 with 577 restaurants... ADS was 117K

scores.rationale: Heavy A&P (Hrithik Roshan year-long contract, Korean LTO campaigns, celebration meals) does move traffic, but much of the spend is value/discount-led and the brand equity accrues to the franchisor, not RBA.
scores.quote: we saw about 20% growth in dine-in traffic over pre-campaign period

scores.rationale: No formal R&D, but a food-technology team and in-house engineering deliver tangible product and cost outcomes (menu re-engineering, BK Pizza Puff, an in-house-designed broiler halving utility use).
scores.quote: this was designed in-house along with our vendor partner in the U.S. by Nitin and his team

scores.rationale: The 2022 Indonesia acquisition and the 300-store Popeyes master franchise were large, cross-border and value-destroying — 46 stores closed, sustained EBITDA losses, and by FY26 Popeyes is explicitly being pushed out of the portfolio.
scores.quote: it has to be part of someone else's portfolio, not ours

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback across the period; instead the company is issuing INR900 crores of equity plus INR700 crores of warrants at INR70/share alongside a promoter change, i.e. dilution rather than distribution.
scores.quote: INR900 crores, and we'll be simultaneously issuing warrants... at a price of INR70 per share

scores.rationale: Company-owned restaurant model is capital-heavy (600 stores, leases, kiosks, cafés) generating only INR2,271 crores revenue at 5.8% company EBITDA, with no protective moat around the assets.
scores.quote: total revenue of INR2,271 crores for the full year, with the restaurant EBITDA of 11.6%

scores.rationale: Far from dominant with ~600 stores in 107 cities and demonstrable share capture — 11-12 consecutive quarters of positive SSSG and traffic in a demand environment management itself calls tough.
scores.quote: This is the 11th consecutive quarter that we are reporting positive sales

scores.rationale: Domestic city expansion is credible (107 cities, ~10 new cities a year), but the flagship international expansion into Indonesia has required store closures, G&A cuts and four years of losses, and Popeyes there is being written off.
scores.quote: We have closed about 46 restaurants that were nonprofitable

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly traffic/volume-led on a value platform (2 for INR50 to 2 for INR79/99) with ADS lower in FY26 than FY23; the premium King's Collection mix layer is only a recent addition.
scores.quote: Value has always been the mainstay of our strategy... 2for79 and 2for99

scores.rationale: The QSR cycle is at a trough that management repeatedly flags, yet SSSG is inflecting upward (4.5% in Q3FY26 to 6.3% in Q4FY26, best in 12 quarters), suggesting positioning near the bottom with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: 6.3% SSSG growth, which is the highest that we have achieved in the last 12 quarters

scores.rationale: Indian QSR is a structurally under-penetrated, young-demographic end market that supports 60-80 store additions a year plus new day-parts (café, breakfast, snacking).
scores.quote: guidance range of 60 to 80 new restaurants every year

scores.rationale: Cost discipline is real (G&A down, store rationalisation, utility savings), but stewardship was undermined by a big cross-border acquisition plus a second brand launch that never earned its keep, ending in a control sale.
scores.quote: we are challenged over there with the Popeyes business

scores.rationale: The same CEO has run a consistent 10+ year playbook (value ladder, then core/premium, then digital) and hit the FY29 gross-margin target three years early while methodically grinding out the Indonesia turnaround.
scores.quote: We've reached that more than 3 years ahead of schedule

scores.rationale: Calls are operationally detailed and management credits named team members rather than themselves, but the company leans heavily on celebrity-led publicity and high-visibility promotion.
scores.quote: thanks to all the hard work of the entire team sitting here around me

scores.rationale: Systematic people investment is visible — a Chief People Officer, Great Place to Work certification, and internal promotion of an 8-year veteran to run a new country brand.
scores.quote: We were certified as a great place to work

scores.rationale: Management openly names its failures and conscious trade-offs — deteriorating Popeyes losses, Indonesia's geopolitical hit, and a deliberate decision to hold margins flat to chase traffic.
scores.quote: it's a challenging business. It continues to be one of the big concern areas for us

scores.rationale: Results are modest enough (5.8% company EBITDA, flat ADS) that little halo exists; the verifiable skill is cost/supply-chain execution rather than superior economics, and much of the sales narrative depends on external conditions.
scores.quote: We've got to 5.8% in FY26

scores.rationale: No monopoly position in India — the brand competes head-on in burgers and must buy trial with value pricing; the only claimed mind-share leadership is in loss-making Indonesia.
scores.quote: Burger King Indonesia stands number 1 in burgers in that country

scores.rationale: QSR customers face zero switching costs and no captive aftermarket; retention is being attempted through CRM and app offers rather than any structural lock-in.
scores.quote: building loyalty over time

scores.rationale: The Indian QSR market is fragmented and contested across burgers, pizza and chicken, with delivery aggregators holding real negotiating leverage over margins.
scores.quote: working very, very strongly with the aggregators

scores.rationale: Low entry barriers and evident discount-driven competition, particularly on delivery, where profitability had to be reclaimed by cutting discounts rather than through industry-wide pricing rationality.
scores.quote: on delivery, we have reduced discounts significantly

scores.rationale: Positive SSSG through a slow market hints at share coming from weaker operators, but no specific weak competitor is identified in the calls.
scores.quote: to be positive in a market scenario, which is challenging

scores.rationale: A listed, analyst-covered company running celebrity national campaigns and now attracting a INR1,600 crore control investment is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we've just entered into a definitive agreement with Inspira Global Group

scores.rationale: Gross margin near 70% and genuine taste/brand credentials with young consumers, but pricing power is limited — growth depends on INR79/INR99 value constructs and ADS has not risen.
scores.quote: we've been able to take the trajectory of gross margins at 70%

scores.rationale: Purchase is driven by price and taste promotions rather than certainty; quality systems exist but the stated fulcrum of the strategy is value, not trust-based premium.
scores.quote: value... is fulcrum for the Burger King brand across the world that we believe in driving trials

scores.rationale: Convenience is the strongest customer benefit — ~43% delivery mix, café and breakfast day-parts, self-ordering kiosks and table ordering, with 91-92% of orders digital and direct app relationships.
scores.quote: 91% of all our orders are now digital

scores.rationale: Correctly a retail-facing business building intangibles through brand, festivals and CRM, but the dominant lever deployed is price-led value rather than durable intangible pull.
scores.quote: This helps us build a very strong emotional connect with our consumers

scores.rationale: Useful but replicable technology — own app stack, self-ordering kiosks, table ordering and an in-house broiler design — with no deep, multi-product technical edge.
scores.quote: launched our own stack for BK app, self-ordering kiosks and table ordering

scores.rationale: No two-sided network; the app is a one-way CRM/acquisition channel and the company is dependent on third-party aggregator networks it does not own.
scores.quote: Right now, the focus is on acquisition and some bits of engagement

scores.rationale: A real and improving footprint plus cluster-based supply chain that lifted gross margin over 2%, but ~600 stores is well short of a reach rivals cannot match in Indian QSR.
scores.quote: We've always worked on a strong cluster strategy to develop our overall supply chain strategy

scores.rationale: Real growth investment is visible — 18 new branches in Q3 FY26, tech refresh, GIFT City, in-house collections build — but incremental returns are poor (PAT of just INR214 crores and a 1% ROA still only an aspiration), so growth spend is not yet earning high incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: we accelerated branch expansion by adding 18 branches and we will sustain this momentum

scores.rationale: Brand spend appears only as a future intention funded by the Emirates NBD infusion, with no evidence of A&P building durable brand equity or pricing power today.
scores.quote: invest meaningfully in technology, brand and distribution

scores.rationale: Product/tech development is incremental digital work — a unified mobile app, the Suvidha JLG app and a core tech refresh — useful but not a consistent engine of differentiated new products.
scores.quote: recent digital initiatives including the launch of our unified mobile app for all the customers and Suvid ha app for our J LG customers

scores.rationale: Rather than small complementary bolt-ons, the bank sold 60% control to Emirates NBD for ~USD 3 billion with an India-branch amalgamation, and management explicitly keeps inorganic deals open — the opposite of disciplined bolt-on M&A.
scores.quote: Emirates NBD... will invest approximately US $3 billion through a preferential issue... to acquire a 60% stake in RBL

scores.rationale: There is no buyback or dividend policy discussed; instead a massively dilutive preferential issue taking net worth to ~INR44,500 crores at a price near the market, with capital deployment plans still undecided at Board level.
scores.quote: we have drawn a broad strategic points for deployment of that, and it is being discussed at the Board level

scores.rationale: Balance-sheet-heavy model with cost-to-income of 66-72% and NIM compressing from 4.9% to 4.5% before recovering to 4.63%, and no protective moat — returns depend on leverage, not asset efficiency.
scores.quote: cost -to-income ratio as a consequence is 66.3% versus 70.7% last quarter

scores.rationale: As a small bank there is genuine runway, and it is visibly capturing share in chosen segments — commercial banking +30% Y-o-Y and secured retail +25% Y-o-Y — though headline advances growth of 9-14% is near system growth because unsecured shrank.
scores.quote: commercial banking business grew 30% Y -o-Y

scores.rationale: Measured expansion into new domestic geographies plus GIFT City and the India-Middle East corridor opened by Emirates NBD, but it is simultaneously retreating from fringe card geographies, so execution is selective rather than a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: along with the selective expansion into the new geographies

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and mix-driven in the wrong direction: yields fell ~50bps sequentially and mix shifted deliberately to lower-yielding secured products, with the bank a price-taker paying ~1% more than large peers for deposits.
scores.quote: our yield on advances was lower by 50 basis points sequentially

scores.rationale: The bank is credibly past the bottom of the MFI/unsecured credit cycle — early-bucket collection efficiency at 99.5%, JLG slippages down to INR130 crores, and margins confirmed to have bottomed in Q1 FY26 — with cards recovery still two quarters out.
scores.quote: the early bucket collection efficiency is 99.5%. This is as good as one has got in this segment for a long time

scores.rationale: Underlying end markets — granular retail deposits, affordable housing, small business/LAP and MSME credit in India — are in secular expansion, evidenced by 21% 3-year CAGR in sub-INR3 crore term deposits and 34% growth in business plus housing loans.
scores.quote: Term deposits below INR3 crores have grown at a CAGR of 21% over the past 3 years

scores.rationale: Genuine discipline on risk — aggressive provisioning, CGFMU cover on 80%+ of standard JLG, deliberate shrinking of unsecured — is offset by ceding control to a foreign buyer and explicitly leaving inorganic acquisitions on the table.
scores.quote: we don't rule out the opportunity for the inorganic, which we'll keep looking at it

scores.rationale: Management has tenaciously executed a consistent multi-year plan (the 'four Cs', granular deposits from ~43% to 51.5%), but independence was surrendered in the ENBD deal, justified by an admitted desire not to remain mid-sized.
scores.quote: Given an opportunity, nobody would like to be a small midsized bank forever

scores.rationale: Calls are technical and detail-led rather than promotional, but the ENBD announcement was framed in celebratory 'historic/landmark' language, so substance and showmanship are mixed.
scores.quote: Yesterday was a landmark day for RBL Bank. We announced a histori c strategic transaction

scores.rationale: Some capability building is evident — in-house migration of card collections and added relationship and credit teams — but there is no articulated talent-development system, and the MD is an external appointee after Ahuja's 2022 exit.
scores.quote: driven by calibrated investments in relationship s and credit teams across existing markets

scores.rationale: Management discloses granular segment slippages, admits card stress persisting longer than guided and names its own underwriting as a cause, though repeated 'normalization in two quarters' timelines have slipped across the five calls.
scores.quote: There are certain pockets of the portfolio, which are exhibiting weakness... it's a combination of what underwriting, we had a reasonable jump in growth of cards post -COVID

scores.rationale: The improvement narrative is confident while reported outcomes stay weak (PAT of INR33 crores, INR200 crores, INR214 crores across the period) and the biggest step-up comes from an external capital injection rather than demonstrated operating skill.
scores.quote: our net profit for the quarter was INR214 crores

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere in the mind of the customer; even in cards the bank is a marginal player rebuilding after losing its Bajaj sourcing partnership.
scores.quote: post cessation of our new sourcing through our Bajaj partnership

scores.rationale: There are no meaningful switching costs — management concedes multiproduct lock-in is still an aspiration and card relationships are largely single-product today.
scores.quote: we want to progressively move towards multiproduct customer consumption on this rather than a single product busine ss

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented and price-competitive with depositors holding the power, forcing RBL to pay above large peers for funding.
scores.quote: the environment of deposits remains fairly co mpetitive

scores.rationale: Licensing is a barrier but pricing is anything but rational — deposit rate wars leave RBL ~1% above large private banks on cost of deposits, and ownership itself has just changed hands.
scores.quote: if you look at our cost of deposits, I would say, give or take, we are maybe 1% or so higher than, let's say, the large priv ate sector banks

scores.rationale: Over this period RBL was itself the share donator in unsecured retail, with cards and JLG degrowing for six to seven quarters while stronger banks took share.
scores.quote: The cards in force grew sequentially after 6 to 7 quarters of reduction

scores.rationale: The bank is intensively covered by global and domestic brokers (JPMorgan, Citi, IIFL, Motilal Oswal) and is now the subject of a headline USD 3 billion control transaction — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Harsh Modi from JPMorgan

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power: the bank pays up for deposits, absorbed 100bps of repo cuts on assets, and competes on rate rather than brand.
scores.quote: the bank has absorbed 100 bps of repo rate cut done until June 2025

scores.rationale: Customers are not paying a trust premium; management is explicitly trying to narrow the cost-of-deposit gap versus larger peers, implying price rather than assurance drives acquisition.
scores.quote: building granular liabilities with a narrower cost of deposit gap versus larger peers

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is the bank's most credible customer benefit — 562 branches plus RFL business-correspondent touchpoints now sourcing over 60% of retail asset leads and all organic gold loans.
scores.quote: With over 60% of the leads now sourced from the branches. In fact, our entire organic gold business originates through branches

scores.rationale: The bank serves both retail and corporate but matches neither benefit type well — cross-sell intensity and analytics-based multiproduct underwriting are stated priorities still in progress rather than achieved lock-in.
scores.quote: The sustained efforts to deepen the customer relationship and cross -sell intensity

scores.rationale: Technology is a catch-up exercise — a core tech refresh to fix stability and grievance handling, with management conceding technology disruptions will keep recurring — not a multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: we embark on a tech refresh to strengthen our core and simplify the front -end experience

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network exists; the business is single-product relationships that management hopes to bundle over time, and cards weakened precisely because customers lacked a transactional relationship.
scores.quote: one of the risk mitigants in this business is actually to have a more transactional relationship beyond cards with the custom er

scores.rationale: A real but sub-scale distribution asset — 562 branches plus the RFL BC network being repurposed for affordable housing and micro-LAP — useful for sourcing yet far from a reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: Our 562 -branch network, together with the e xtensive touchpoints of our subsidiary RFL, remains central to this growth

scores.rationale: For a lender, growth 'capex' is balance-sheet deployment: AUM compounded from INR3.85 lakh cr (FY23) to INR5.85 lakh cr with record disbursements and ROE of ~22%, though growth has decelerated from 17% to a guided 11-12%.
scores.quote: REC recorded its highest ever half-yearly disbursements of Rs. 1,15,470 crores in this half year, which is a growth of 27%

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the excerpts.
No R&D spend or product-development pipeline discussed; only a passing mention of a generative-AI implementation award.
No acquisitions are discussed across the 11 calls; growth is entirely organic lending plus an MoU, which is not M&A.
Consistent, rising dividends (INR18/share FY25, two INR4.60 interims in FY26) plus bonus issues show a coherent policy, but there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked discipline described.
scores.quote: we have been continuously rewarding our shareholders with timely dividends and bonus shares issuance

scores.rationale: A lender is structurally asset-heavy — INR5.85 lakh cr of loan assets funded by INR5.08 lakh cr of borrowings at 6.07x gearing — so returns come from leverage and spread, not asset turnover.
scores.quote: the debt-equity ratio or the gearing ratio of the company has improved to 6.07x

scores.rationale: REC already claims 20-25% share of Indian power financing yet the addressable pool (INR46 lakh cr over 4-5 years) is expanding far faster than its book, and it targets 30-40% of the new 74 GW thermal opportunity.
scores.quote: out of every four bulbs glowing in India, one is financed by REC, which is an indicator of a roughly 20% to 25% market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is sectoral (renewables, infra, logistics, shipping) and domestic only — RDSS covers 19 of 34 states — with no international or genuinely new geographic footprint claimed.
scores.quote: we are the national implementing agency for the RDSS program. We are operating in 19 states out of 34 states

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/book-led; yields rose only modestly (9.82%→10.08%) and management has repeatedly said it will concede price for credit quality and in renewables.
scores.quote: if you want to have good projects in hand, better good entities, strong entities we need to moderate our margins

scores.rationale: The power-capex cycle is in a clear upturn with DISCOM health improving (AT&C losses to 16.3%, ACS-ARR gap narrowing) and a thermal restart, but REC is mid-cycle rather than at the bottom.
scores.quote: the high AT&C losses of previous years have come down to 16.3%. Almost 40 out of 63 utilities saw an improvement

scores.rationale: The end market is in durable secular expansion — 500 GW non-fossil target, per-capita consumption at one-third the world average, and an estimated INR46 lakh cr of sector investment over 4-5 years — a theme reiterated consistently from Feb 2023 through Nov 2025.
scores.quote: We estimate that almost Rs. 46 lakh crores will be required over the next four or five years towards the entire power sector

scores.rationale: Growth is organic with no acquisitions, capital adequacy is 23.74% against a 15% requirement and NPAs have fallen steadily, though diversification into infra was launched before the appraisal capability existed.
scores.quote: The capital adequacy ratio is sitting comfortably at 23.74%, as against the RBI requirement of 15%

scores.rationale: The INR10 lakh cr by 2030 goal has been articulated and tracked consistently for years, but leadership is government-appointed IAS officers (three chairmen in five years) operating explicitly under ministry direction, which limits independence.
scores.quote: thank the Honourable Secretary of Power as well as our Honourable Minister of Power for constantly guiding us

scores.rationale: Management is low-key bureaucratic rather than celebrity-driven, but the calls devote significant time to award-listing self-promotion.
scores.quote: we have been getting various awards in almost all the fields... So you name it, we have it

scores.rationale: There is an in-house training institute (RECIPMT), but for the new infrastructure vertical capability was bought in via fixed-tenure external consultants rather than developed internally, and the top job is filled by external government appointment.
scores.quote: We are hiring outside consultants or we are hiring them within the company? Management: Both options. We are taking them for fixed tenure.

scores.rationale: Disclosure is specific and self-corrective — they volunteered that headline 7% loan growth would have been ~16% ex-prepayments, named the CHF-dollar hedge as the source of the INR576 cr derivative loss, and disclosed the Andhra Pradesh SMA slippage unprompted.
scores.quote: Had this pre-payment not been received, the growth in the loan book would have been almost around 16% on a year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: Strong reported outcomes (22% ROE, falling NPAs, sovereign-parity AAA funding) derive largely from state ownership, nodal-agency mandates and sovereign-linked cost of funds rather than demonstrable managerial skill, so the results should not be read as evidence of edge.
scores.quote: Internationally, we are at par with the sovereign ratings of India by both Moody's and Fitch

scores.rationale: REC holds government-conferred exclusive roles — sole implementing agency for PM Surya Ghar and national implementing agency for RDSS — which function as a mandated monopoly in those niches.
scores.quote: In PM Surya Ghar Bijli Yojana, we are the single implementing agency for the entire, for the very ambitious program

scores.rationale: Nodal-agency status confers some captivity, but switching costs are visibly low — borrowers prepaid INR49,000 cr in one half-year, largely refinancing or repaying from accruals.
scores.quote: We have received pre-payments of almost Rs. 49,000 crores. That is $6 billion.

scores.rationale: Beyond REC/PFC/IREDA the field is open to all banks and NBFCs and borrowers (state utilities, NTPC) can and do negotiate or seek cheaper funding, so end-customer negotiating power is real.
scores.quote: All banks are there; all institutions are there... otherwise infra all banks, all NBFCs are active

scores.rationale: The AAA rating and low cost of funds are genuine barriers, but pricing rationality is weak — renewables lending is openly described as competitive with sub-2.5% spreads and margins are conceded to win quality assets.
scores.quote: Renewable is quite competitive because we also want to encourage renewable

scores.rationale: Rather than facing weak rivals, REC is the one ceding business — it stands aside where borrowers have cheaper funding and loses book to large-scale prepayments.
scores.quote: When they do it on a standalone basis we are not financing because they have the cheaper source of financing available

scores.rationale: REC is a Maharatna PSU with a $70bn book, quarterly sell-side coverage from CLSA/DSP/Emkay/MOFSL and heavy award publicity — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Being a Maharatna company, we are strategically placed in Indian power and infrastructure and logistics sector

scores.rationale: The product is undifferentiated credit with a ~2.9% spread and no image-driven pricing power; management explicitly trades margin for asset quality.
scores.quote: It is a tradeoff always between credit quality and margins

scores.rationale: Borrowers value certainty and speed of execution — REC can underwrite an entire project alone without consortium friction and won a hospital deal outright simply by moving first.
scores.quote: REC provides a good comfort to a borrower because we can take total project, there will not be any problem in the consortium

scores.rationale: A 20+ regional and state office network plus nodal-agency machinery gives direct reach to state utilities and even retail rooftop-solar beneficiaries at scale.
scores.quote: roughly 56 lakh customers have already applied... we have disbursed close to INR8,500 crores to these beneficiaries

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate/state entities and REC correctly leads with reliability and single-window certainty, but the lock-in half of the corporate formula is missing given INR49,000 cr of prepayments.
scores.quote: Our primary borrowers are the state governments, the state electricity boards, the state power utilities

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge is claimed; the only technology references are an implementation award and an ISO risk-management certificate, neither of which confers a customer benefit rivals cannot copy.
scores.quote: technology awards for generative AI implementation

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts.

The pan-India office network combined with nodal-agency status for national schemes gives origination and last-mile implementation reach that private lenders cannot replicate, evidenced by 17 lakh rooftop-solar households and RDSS coverage across 19 states.
scores.quote: we are very, very happy that so far roughly 17 lakh households have been covered under the rooftop solar scheme

scores.rationale: Growth investment is real but platform/capability-led rather than heavy fixed capex, and it is being made while ROCE stays at 22%.
scores.quote: ROCE was at 22% despite the investments we are making in the growth areas

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.
Not classical R&D, but sustained platform build-out (Cloud Quarks 2.0, AI lab, AI Exchange marketplace) is converting into new products and partner reach.
scores.quote: Our next version of Cloud Quarks platform, we call it 2.0 internally, has been rolled out this quarter... We have launched an AI Exchange, which is like a marketplace with over 200 AI agents

scores.rationale: The Arena/Turkey acquisition destroyed value — years of losses, exit costs and finally a trade-name impairment hitting group PAT by INR75.2 crores.
scores.quote: an impairment of the trade name classified as an intangible asset arising from its investment in its subsidiary in Turkey Arena... The impact on the group PAT after minority interest is INR75.2 crores

scores.rationale: A coherent, explained payout policy (30% of profits) balanced against growth capital needs, though no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution discipline is evidenced.
scores.quote: INR 6 per share of dividend for the year ended 31st March 2026, which is 30% of profits... We have additional capital needs for growth opportunities

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-light with best-in-class working capital (25-30 days) and 22% ROCE, but the underlying moat protecting those returns is thin given gross-margin erosion.
scores.quote: we achieved one of the best-in-class working capital of 25 days

scores.rationale: Consistently gaining share — #1 in India and MEA, top-10 globally and out-growing almost all peers, with fresh runway upcountry and in security where they admit lagging.
scores.quote: there's only one distributor that will be faster than us in terms of growth. We're growing 20% year-on-year... We grew 45% in the up-country part of the business

scores.rationale: Repeated, executed country additions (Bahrain, Jordan, then ASEAN, CIS, South Africa) focused on the high-margin SSG vertical, tempered by the failed Turkey expansion.
scores.quote: our geographical expansions in the recent period are all focused on SSG, be it ASEAN countries, be it CIS countries, even South Africa

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/ASP pass-through rather than own pricing power, with gross margins in structural decline; only the SSG mix shift is a positive offset.
scores.quote: because of higher ASPs, not units, because of the price rise... the mobility business, which traditionally gives a lower margin

scores.rationale: Position in the cycle is ambiguous — component shortage and price rises are boosting revenue now but management explicitly refuses to call the direction.
scores.quote: We also don't know how long this demand cycle will last and when the price increases will stop... We cannot call it right now.

scores.rationale: The cloud/software/security end market is in clear secular expansion with a TAM tripling, and Redington's SSG share of revenue has risen from 12% to 17% in two years.
scores.quote: It's $515 billion for 2025... growing very rapidly towards $1.7 trillion

scores.rationale: Consistent capital discipline across four years — clean balance sheet, rigorous working-capital control, walking away from unprofitable deals — though the Turkey acquisition remains a lapse.
scores.quote: the deals which were not coming at any reasonable terms, I mean we had let it go... we have a clean balance sheet, if I may say

scores.rationale: They invested in cloud/SSG ahead of the market and stayed with it until it became a $2.2bn, 17%-of-revenue vertical, though heavy MD/CEO churn over FY22-26 dilutes continuity.
scores.quote: we have literally put the cart before the horse. We invested in this business way ahead of the market

scores.rationale: Communication across all calls is operational and metric-led with no personality promotion; leaders present business detail rather than themselves.
scores.quote: Our performance was driven by resilience and defined by discipline.

scores.rationale: Explicit emphasis on human capital plus visible internal bench (India CEO, global SSG head, CTO, AI head all presenting) and structured skilling via an academy and AI learning centres.
scores.quote: Redington strength lies in the human capital, partners and vendors... our own academy, which is the training and skill building programs

scores.rationale: Repeatedly volunteers bad news and errors unprompted — margin decline, KSA provisions, Turkey losses, being caught off guard, and even correcting their own IR's growth figure live on the call.
scores.quote: we were caught a bit off guard because despite the inflationary and the interest rate environment, the market demand was not softening... Just now Palak said 37%. I just want to correct that

scores.rationale: Strong headline growth is largely industry tailwind, OEM launches and price inflation on a 1.3% PAT margin, so results should not be read as evidence of exceptional skill beyond genuine working-capital execution.
scores.quote: full year PAT growth excluding exceptional items, was 17% and PAT margin at 1.3%

scores.rationale: No monopoly in the end customer's mind — the brand belongs to the OEM and Redington is an interchangeable intermediary whose route-to-market the vendors control.
scores.quote: it was Apple and Dell and Lenovo and Acer and everybody makes changes to the GTM

scores.rationale: Some emerging lock-in via the partner platform and subscription renewals, but the core hardware relationship is admittedly transactional with no switching costs.
scores.quote: unlike in the hardware business where the relationship is more transactional... the transaction gets consummated closed

scores.rationale: Distribution is a consolidated top-10 structure where Redington is #1 in its markets, but bargaining power sits with the OEM vendors above and large-deal customers below.
scores.quote: We are number 8 globally, but we are number 1 in India and number 1 in Middle East, Africa

scores.rationale: Pricing is not rational for the distributor — gross margins have declined steadily for years and large deals are consistently taken at sub-normal margins.
scores.quote: there are some large deals where it may not come at the normal -- within margins

scores.rationale: Hardware-only distributors are shrinking while Redington grows 20%, and several listed peers are being out-grown, providing share to take.
scores.quote: globally for all distribution, hardware has actually declined and are a little bit flat

scores.rationale: Not an ignored niche — it is the #1 ranked distributor in India, holds investor days and courts sell-side coverage, but nor is it a crowded glamour sector.
scores.quote: Redington continue to be the number 1 IT distributor in India for 2023-24

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power whatsoever — gross margins are wafer-thin and structurally eroding, with PAT at ~1.3% of sales.
scores.quote: Is there a pressure on the margin? Definitely, yes.

scores.rationale: Partners and vendors buy continuity, credit and availability, demonstrated by maintaining supply through the West Asia conflict and data-centre attacks.
scores.quote: our teams on the ground demonstrated strong resilience, ensuring business continuity after multiple data center attacks

scores.rationale: Reach and channel intimacy are the genuine differentiator — tens of thousands of transacting partners, upcountry penetration growing 45%, and platform-led ordering at scale.
scores.quote: more than 11000 partners are transacting every month now... we generate more than three lakh invoices every quarter

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to a corporate/channel customer base by selling reliability, credit and now annuity subscriptions, with 74% recurring revenue creating some stickiness.
scores.quote: About 74 percentage of our last year revenue is recurring

scores.rationale: Building proprietary platforms (Cloud Quarks, AI Exchange, AI lab) but the underlying technology is resold from OEMs and R&D intensity is not a stated differentiator.
scores.quote: We found an AI lab or capability center at Chennai headquarters

scores.rationale: A genuine emerging two-sided platform connecting OEMs/ISVs to resellers and customers, though it is early and revenue from it has not yet started.
scores.quote: a marketplace with over 200 AI agents that brings ISVs and AI innovators and our customers through our partner ecosystem together

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the durable moat — #1 in India and MEA across 40-odd countries with warehouse, credit and service infrastructure rivals cannot replicate quickly.
scores.quote: Redington continues to be in the top 10 despite not playing in U.S., Europe and China, the 3 biggest markets

scores.rationale: Expansion capex exists (stores in Tier 2/3, warehouses going from two to seven and then nine) with a stated return hurdle, but the model is deliberately capital-light with outsourced manufacturing and the incremental returns are muddied — ~90 new stores in Q2 FY26 produced only ~15% revenue growth with flat margins.
scores.quote: Every location we open has to clear our return thresholds from day one.

scores.rationale: Management claims marketing drove acquisition and repeat rates and cites the RedTape 10K Run, yet in the same call reduced marketing spend is listed as a source of EBITDA expansion, and the permanent 70–80% discount undercuts brand-equity building.
scores.quote: Our marketing investments in the brand have driven measurable improvement in both new customer acquisition and repeat purchase rates.

scores.rationale: No R&D function is discussed; the only development evidence is design cadence and material upgrades (EVA to ETPU, premium leather, ~50 new footwear styles a month) with a six-month design-to-production cycle.
scores.quote: we introduce almost 50 new styles of footwear every month

scores.rationale: Management explicitly rules out acquisitions and builds brands in-house (Ozark, Bond Street, Mode), so there is no M&A track record to judge either favourably or unfavourably.
scores.quote: we are not in the business of acquiring brands or taking over brands

scores.rationale: A final dividend of INR2 per INR2 share was recommended but no buyback and no articulated distribution policy, and it comes while working capital debt and inventory are still being normalised.
scores.quote: the Board has recommended a final INR2 per equity share on the face value of INR2

scores.rationale: Despite the 'capital light' outsourced model, the balance sheet is inventory-heavy at ~175 days (peak 250) with pressured operating cash flow and working-capital borrowings, and the discount-led positioning provides no protecting moat.
scores.quote: we have 175 days of inventory on sales... we had reached a high of 250 days plus also

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway (513 stores in a 140-crore-population country) and real share capture evidence — 17.8% Q4 SSSG and 19.6% FY26 revenue growth against a footwear sector described as broadly pessimistic.
scores.quote: Our SSSG, which is the same-store sales growth was 17.8% in Q4

scores.rationale: Credible, well-executed domestic expansion out of a North India base into South, West and East and into ~300 cities, though the export/UK leg is tentative and explicitly de-prioritised.
scores.quote: primarily our stores are currently based out of North India. We are now increasing our store count in South, West and East India

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led — a GST-cut volume catalyst passed straight to consumers as deeper discounts (70% to 74–80% off) with no MRP hikes taken despite raw-material pressure; only modest ASP/mix uplift from premium launches offsets this.
scores.quote: before the GST drop, we were offering 70% off. And post the GST drop, we did a 74% to 76% and in some cases we even went up to 80%

scores.rationale: The company entered FY26 near a sector trough — muted footwear trends, BIS disruption and the Bangladesh turmoil hitting the prior year — with an identifiable GST-and-wedding-season upturn that materialised in H2 FY26.
scores.quote: the entire space is sharing a very pessimistic kind of an outlook... Now, GST reduction has happened. Now, trends are expected to improve

scores.rationale: The end market is in genuine secular expansion — unorganised-to-organised shift in footwear and apparel, deep underpenetration, and rising discretionary consumption in Tier 2/3 towns where most stores sit.
scores.quote: the structural shift from unorganized to organized retail in both footwear and apparel continues to work in our favour

scores.rationale: Strictly organic growth with no M&A and an asset-light vendor model, and debt was cut by ~INR200 crores with INR175 crores operating cash flow, though the inventory build-up to 250 days and reliance on working-capital debt show imperfect discipline.
scores.quote: debt outstanding has considerably gone down by INR200 crores

scores.rationale: A multi-brand architecture built in-house over years is now delivering, alongside a deliberate 20-year view of Indian consumption and a stated professionalisation of the family business.
scores.quote: the multi-brand architecture we have built over the years is genuinely starting to work for us

scores.rationale: Promoters stay off the calls and professionals front them, but the commentary carries promotional flourishes ('most powerful brands this country has seen', 'Good would be an understatement') rather than plain substance.
scores.quote: Ultimately, we are moving from a family-run business to a professionally managed organization.

scores.rationale: People are named as one of three investment priorities and the business is professionalising, but no talent-development system or succession pipeline is described, and the five-year history shows churn (a chairman and an MD exited, two CFOs in FY26).
scores.quote: we have been investing behind three brands; brand, people and technology

scores.rationale: Disclosure is weak and often garbled — nonsensical revenue history (INR1,831 crores in 2024 then INR218 crores in 2025), inconsistent store counts (513 exclusive stores in Q2 vs 223 showrooms at year-end), no segment margins or volume data, no inventory provisioning, and repeated deferrals on lease liability and payable days.
scores.quote: The payable days has dropped, no? Okay. Okay. I will get back to you.

scores.rationale: Headline results lean heavily on non-operating and one-off factors — a GST cut, and INR133 crores of 'other income' from e-commerce rebates and claims against INR244 crores PAT, with a prior-year restatement — so the outcome is not cleanly attributable to management skill.
scores.quote: the basic component of that is the discount, rebate and discount, which you get from the e-commerce platforms... around the INR133 crores this year

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind — management concedes it competes head-on with international and domestic brands, and the offer is anchored on price rather than a must-have status.
scores.quote: given the rising competition from both domestic and global footwear brands

scores.rationale: Discretionary consumer footwear and apparel with zero switching costs and no captive aftermarket; ~30% of sales sit on third-party marketplaces where the customer relationship is shared.
scores.quote: It is primarily through the Flipkart's and Myntra's of the world.

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented between a large unorganised base and many branded players, and the end customer holds the power — as does the marketplace channel that unilaterally changed billing and rebate structures mid-year.
scores.quote: they had changed some accounting mid of the year, wherein, the rebates were being given and it was being adjusted against the top-line

scores.rationale: Pricing is structurally irrational — a permanent 70–80% off model deepened after the GST cut — and entry barriers are low, with peers claiming 100%+ growth in sneakers and building world-class uppers capacity.
scores.quote: we are a brand, which offers discounts all year long. We don't sell anything on MRP.

scores.rationale: Weak incumbents and a large unorganised base are available to take share from, with the listed footwear peer set described as posting muted trends while RedTape outperformed.
scores.quote: over the last couple of years, the trends have been very muted. But encouragingly, your company's performance has been relatively better.

scores.rationale: The Tier 2/3 niche is unglamorous, but the company is not ignored by capital — calls are hosted by Nuvama and EY with IIFL, Emkay and ICICI Prudential AMC participating.
scores.quote: Next question is from the line of Manasvi Shah from ICICI Prudential AMC

scores.rationale: Pricing power is largely absent — MRPs are inflated purely to be discounted, no price hikes were taken despite raw-material pressure, and gross margin fell to 43.4%.
scores.quote: As of today, we are not increasing any MRPs or nothing. We are doing nothing of that sort.

scores.rationale: There is some trust-led brand extension into accessories on 30 years of equity, but price and discount remain the explicit purchase driver rather than assurance.
scores.quote: The consumer who already trusts RedTape for footwear does not need a lot of convincing to pick up a bag

scores.rationale: Genuine accessibility advantage — 623 retail touchpoints across 300+ cities plus company-run marketplace warehouses expanded from two to seven (going to nine) to sit closer to quick-commerce customers.
scores.quote: we have opened some new online warehouses in Ludhiana, Hyderabad, Howrah... because in this world of quick commerce... you have to be closer to the customers

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail, where the framework requires intangible/image benefits, yet the company deliberately supplies price and discount as its core proposition rather than aspiration.
scores.quote: Indian consumer loves discounts and we are giving them that.

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge — manufacturing is outsourced to contract vendors, tech investment is ERP/systems (SAP), while a competitor is cited as building best-in-world uppers capacity.
scores.quote: Since the introduction of SAP, we have seen improvements in the overall reporting systems.

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing network exists; the network effects in the online channel belong to Flipkart and Myntra, with RedTape merely renting traffic in exchange for rebates.
scores.quote: the brands, which bring more traffic to their website, they usually offer a special rebate

scores.rationale: Reach is a real relative strength — 623 retail touchpoints across 328 cities, seven owned marketplace warehouses running B2C directly, and enough channel pull that platforms grant special rebates.
scores.quote: We run our own marketplace warehouses. We have seven warehouses in India

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex — owned ash fleet expansion (39 to ~119 trucks), EV fleet from 479 toward 2,000, Silvassa wind plant — with depreciation explicitly tied to capacity build, but incremental returns were poor in mobility (-50% margins) and power trading before the refocus onto high-margin ash.
scores.quote: Depreciation increase is aligned with the capacity expansion and asset capitalization, positioning us for higher throughput in the coming quarters

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the eight calls beyond a fleet rebranding from Refex eVeelz to Refex Mobility.

Only product/technology adoption is discussed (5.3 MW turbine platform with LIDAR, ALMM approval, localization in progress) with no R&D spend, pipeline or efficiency metrics disclosed for the core ash business.
scores.quote: all our machines contain LIDAR, which actually detects the direction of the wind

scores.rationale: The airport-taxi acquisition was of a company that had won a tender but could not execute it (a weak acquiree), and post-deal the mobility vertical ran at -50% margins and is now being demerged out — the opposite of a bolt-on that lifts OPM.
scores.quote: It was a tender which they had won and they were not able to execute. So we acquired this to execute this project.

scores.rationale: A modest INR0.50 dividend was reinstated in Q1 FY26 after being skipped to fund growth — a coherent if unremarkable policy — with no buybacks, while promoter share pledging triggered a margin call that the company had to fund.
scores.quote: the Board has declared a dividend of INR0.50 per share... barring last year when we prioritized reinvestment into growth initiatives

scores.rationale: Ash handling turns ~INR2,000 crores of revenue but the model is asset-heavy and financing-dependent (owned truck fleets, EVs on books accruing EMIs before deployment, a new wind factory, refinancing to cut borrowing cost) with no durable moat protecting the returns.
scores.quote: Green Mobility requires a lot of time for stabilization and deployment of vehicle from the time we own the vehicle, while our EMIs get calculated from the day we acquire the vehicle

scores.rationale: Revenue of ~INR2,000 crores sits against a stated INR68,000–75,000 crore TAM that is 99% unorganized and regional, and Refex has compounded ~20% for six years, grown ash 28% in FY26 and now operates 41–42 plants across 15 states — large runway plus demonstrated capture.
scores.quote: we are the only company who operates in 41 thermal power plants or 42 thermal power plants in about 15 states in the country

scores.rationale: Credible domestic multi-state expansion (from a handful of states to 15, plus mobility launches in Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune, Hyderabad), though entirely India-only with no premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: currently our presence is there in the 15 states in India

scores.rationale: FY26 growth was explicitly mix-led — revenue fell as low-margin trading was exited while EBITDA rose 68% and margin went from 10.4% to 20.1% — but underlying ash growth is tonnage-driven (70,000 to 90,000 tpd) with only 40–60% cost pass-through.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin has improved current quarter at 20.1% compared to the previous 10.4%... supported by improved business mix

scores.rationale: The trough was visible and identifiable — a 45% coal-price collapse and then an extraordinary early monsoon that cut Q1/Q2 FY26 volumes — with a clear upturn ahead in post-monsoon recovery and 50 GW of new thermal capacity, and Q3/Q4 FY26 delivered the rebound.
scores.quote: revenue increased by Rs.160 Crores, rising from Rs.123 Crores in Q2 to Rs.583 Crores in Q3

scores.rationale: Ash disposal is compliance-driven and structurally expanding — 340 million tonnes generated annually plus a INR50,000–55,000 crore legacy pond backlog and new thermal build-out — though the end market is ultimately tethered to coal generation.
scores.quote: Every year 340 million of ash gets generated... there is a Rs.50,000 to Rs.55,000 Crores of the legacy ash which is accumulated

scores.rationale: Capital was scattered across four unrelated verticals (refrigerants, power trading, EV mobility, wind turbines), two of which were wound down and one demerged after an investor publicly called out the capital allocation, alongside promoter share pledging that hit a margin call.
scores.quote: It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir. Why don't you focus on coal business and go one by one later on?

scores.rationale: Management built ash handling from a 2018 standing start into the largest organized national player at ~20% CAGR, systematically pioneering road/highway ash use and nationwide compliance systems, and then had the tenacity to kill revenue-generating but unprofitable verticals.
scores.quote: We have been growing at almost about 19 -- 20% CAGR for the last 6 years

scores.rationale: Management is generally low-key on small broker-hosted calls, but the December 2025 income-tax search on the office and the MD's house drew press coverage requiring public rebuttal, and the CMD is praised as an aggressive entrepreneur rather than a quiet operator.
scores.quote: we had an income tax search on 9th of December in our office premises and my house and the senior executive

scores.rationale: Headcount was scaled 70% for project readiness and leadership was strengthened, but the key appointment was an external hire (Anirudh Arun as mobility CEO) with no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline.
scores.quote: we have appointed Mr. Anirudh Arun as our CEO for the Green Mobility vertical

scores.rationale: They openly quantified the -50% mobility margin, conceded the capital-allocation criticism, disclosed the IT search unprompted and explained the loss-making exits — but they also over-promised wind revenue that slipped and had to walk back a 90,000 tpd guidance interpretation.
scores.quote: Point well taken, we will try and assess how to rework on these businesses to ensure that we remake them profitable, sir.

scores.rationale: The headline FY26 profit surge (PAT INR247 crores vs INR184 crores, EBITDA +68%) came largely from pruning loss-making revenue rather than proven operating skill, and sits alongside missed wind timelines, a pledged-share margin call and an unresolved tax search — so results should not be read as durable managerial edge.
scores.quote: the moderation was largely attributed to the plant transitions and restructuring within the certain businesses

scores.rationale: Refex holds a near-unique position as the only nationwide organized ash handler solving the power plants' compliance-penalty problem, which functions as a mini-monopoly in the customer's mind, though contracts still go through tenders.
scores.quote: We ensured 100% compliances for thermal power plants... We have solved that problem of the IPPs and power plants.

scores.rationale: Rivals are single-plant regional operators while Refex offers multi-plant, multi-state coverage with multi-year contracts (e.g. a three-year APGENCO order) and embedded tracking systems, creating real if not absolute switching friction.
scores.quote: Most of the players or 99% of the players are regional and 1 plant player.

scores.rationale: This is a fragmented, unorganized, tender-driven market rather than a stable oligopoly, and the end customers are NTPC and large IPPs who hold clear negotiating power — evidenced by only partial diesel-cost pass-through.
scores.quote: All our contract has the escalation clause, but not completely, it will be recoverable. There will be 40% to 60%

scores.rationale: Management itself flags new competition entering a low-barrier, truck-and-tender business, and promoter shares are pledged rather than held in stable unencumbered ownership.
scores.quote: Competition is also coming up. There is a big market is there.

scores.rationale: An overwhelmingly unorganized competitor base of local single-plant vendors that repeatedly fails on compliance is precisely the pool of weak donators Refex converts into share, and management identifies only one meaningful organized rival.
scores.quote: When they work with local vendors or local people, there's always been an issue of compliances.

scores.rationale: Ash disposal is an unglamorous, traditionally unorganized niche that listed capital has largely ignored — the company is still misclassified by the exchanges as an industrial-gases business — though the wind venture pushes it toward a more crowded narrative.
scores.quote: the company is continued to be classified under industrial gases as per the stock exchanges

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; segment margins are thin (ash and coal handling ~11.77%) with cost of goods at 79–81% of revenue, and the exited refrigerant business ran at 0.9% margin.
scores.quote: The margin for coal and ash handling is roughly about 11.77%. Refrigerant gas has been 0.9%.

scores.rationale: Customers are buying regulatory certainty — avoidance of pollution penalties via 100% compliance, GPS-tracked fleets and documented disposal — which is exactly assurance-type value, but price is still contested through tenders and partial escalation clauses.
scores.quote: Ash is a polluting product. If these are not having right compliances, the thermal power plants end up paying the penalty.

scores.rationale: Nationwide single-vendor coverage across 42 plants in 15 states plus centralized GPS/data platforms gives customers accessibility no regional operator can match, and the team reports winning new orders weekly.
scores.quote: Every week, we have keep on getting new order.

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/PSU (NTPC, APGENCO, IPPs) and the pitch is correctly matched to it — compliance reliability, technology and multi-year contracts — though lock-in is limited and the 90–110 day working capital cycle reflects customer bargaining strength.
scores.quote: most of our customers are NTPC. So generally, the average working capital cycle is about 90 to 110 days

scores.rationale: Technology is applied rather than proprietary — third-party GPS/telematics from Loconav and TATA Fleet Edge in ash, and a licensed 5.3 MW turbine platform still undergoing localization in wind — with no disclosed R&D intensity.
scores.quote: we rely on centralized GPS tracking, partnering with reputable service providers like Loconav, TATA Fleet Edge, and iAlert

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the eight calls.

A nationwide fleet and site presence across 42 thermal plants in 15 states — versus rivals confined to a single plant — is a service-reach advantage in a business where on-site execution and compliance are vital.
scores.quote: we could say that we are the only company who operates in 41 thermal power plants or 42 thermal power plants in about 15 states

scores.rationale: Capex has continued (₹140cr FY23 doubling Sparx capacity, ₹100cr FY25, ₹130cr FY26, ₹180-200cr planned FY27) but is explicitly maintenance/mould/office-led with no capacity expansion, while revenue fell from ₹2,790cr FY25 to ₹2,702cr FY26 and higher depreciation hit PAT — i.e. poor incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: there is no big capacity expansion, but a good amount will be spent on the molds

scores.rationale: A&P is run pro-cyclically as a cost lever — cut from ~4% to 3% of sales precisely when demand was weak and unorganized players were taking share, and redirected into short-term trade schemes rather than brand equity.
scores.quote: we have just reduced the advertisement expenses in this period as compared to last year

scores.rationale: No R&D disclosure at all; product work is incremental design/portfolio tinkering (new designs, Urban Basic, athleisure, premium PU) that has failed to move the mix — closed footwear stuck at 20% of sales for years.
scores.quote: Even last year, full year, it was 80 -20% only. And now also it is 80- 20%.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions, bolt-ons or inorganic activity are discussed in any of the calls.
No discussion of buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy across the excerpts; only that the company is net debt free with a growing treasury.

Asset-heavy in-house manufacturing with a 6-month imported raw-material supply chain and 75 days finished inventory, and turns deteriorating — capex and depreciation rose while revenue fell, with higher depreciation explicitly cited as hitting profitability.
scores.quote: Higher depre ciation in the quarter has impacted the profitability of the company.

scores.rationale: Runway exists but delivery has been the opposite — share lost in FY23 on price hikes, lost again in FY25 to unorganized entrants, with eight straight quarters of volume decline before the GST-driven Q4 FY26 rebound.
scores.quote: there is a mushrooming of local players, the unorganized players, new and new unorganized players have also come into the play

scores.rationale: Purely domestic and still North/East-skewed; expansion is a nascent 100-store EBO plan identifying gaps in West with South only aspirational, and the 2022 export ambition was never followed through.
scores.quote: Like earlier, it was basically North and East based. Now we have identified some gaps in West.

scores.rationale: Price increases are cost-push pass-throughs (15-18% in FY26 for polymer and Haryana wage inflation) that have historically destroyed volume, while mix premiumisation has not moved in four years.
scores.quote: we have taken 2 to 3 price increase in the market... roughly around 15% to 18% is the increase

scores.rationale: Clearly emerging from a cyclical trough — eight quarters of volume decline followed by GST 2.0 (12%→5%) restoring competitiveness against the unorganized sector and a return to 8.1% revenue and 20.4% PAT growth in Q4 FY26.
scores.quote: this is the first quarter after the 8 quarters where you have seen an increase in volumes

scores.rationale: The end market benefits from durable formalisation tailwinds — BIS/QCO quality norms and the GST cut structurally favour compliant organized players in a large, under-penetrated Indian mass footwear market.
scores.quote: The rollout of GST 2.0, which reduced tax rate on footwear priced below INR2,500 to 5% has strengthened our competitiveness versus the unorganized sector

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, net debt free with positive operating cash flow and no M&A across the period, though the A&P cut in the downturn is pro-cyclical rather than counter-cyclical investment.
scores.quote: Our company continues to be net debt free and supported by posi tive cash flow from operations.

scores.rationale: Management held a long-term quality/BIS-compliance line and refused to dilute prices in FY25 despite share loss, but tenacity is undercut by strategic oscillation between the FY23 aggressive price cut and the FY25 margin-first stance.
scores.quote: there was a pressure on us to reduce the prices which we have not

scores.rationale: Promoter-family management communicates in plain operational detail on broker-hosted calls with no celebrity positioning or grand vision statements, often deferring to the CFO for opening remarks.
scores.quote: Status quo. Our prices were more because we revised the prices in January.

scores.rationale: Consistently candid — quantifies its own decline quarter by quarter, admits temporary market-share loss, and voluntarily discloses that gross-margin optics were partly an inventory accounting effect.
scores.quote: that is the accounting part. You can see there is an increase of inventory of around INR 47 crores in this, that includes a conv ersion cost also. That's why that margin looks better.

scores.rationale: Relaxo's compounder reputation is not supported by the last four years of delivery — revenue in FY26 (₹2,702cr) is barely above FY23 levels and EBITDA margin fell from ~16% to 13.8%, so results reflect the cycle and GST rather than demonstrated skill.
scores.quote: For FY26, revenue from operations stood at INR 2,702 crores as compared to INR 2,790 crores in FY25

scores.rationale: No monopoly in the customer's mind — mass consumers abandoned the brand for cheaper alternatives within a quarter of price increases, twice in four years.
scores.quote: for our mass customers, they started s hifting to cheaper products, never mind the quality

scores.rationale: Zero switching costs and no captive aftermarket; demand shifted instantly to local players on price and only returned when the GST cut restored price parity.
scores.quote: because of lower raw material prices , a lot of new competitors have come in

scores.rationale: The industry is highly fragmented rather than an oligopoly, with a large unorganized segment plus organized rivals (Walkaroo, Aqualite, Bata, Campus) and end customers holding full price-based bargaining power.
scores.quote: are we facing pressure from organized players as well like Walkaroo and Aqualite who have also become aggressive

scores.rationale: Barriers are minimal — small manufacturers are exempt from quality norms and enter freely whenever polymer prices fall, and competition is fought via aggressive price corrections and trade schemes.
scores.quote: all small manufacturers, th ey are exempt from Quality Control standards... they can cause unethical competition

scores.rationale: Weak, sub-scale unorganized players are the obvious donator pool and GST 2.0 plus BIS compliance now tilts the field toward Relaxo, though it has been the donator rather than the taker for most of the period.
scores.quote: now after GST being again rationalized from 12% to 5%, now we are more competitive in the market, and we will gain market share

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar — calls are hosted by Motilal Oswal and IIFL with active coverage from Ambit, Elara, ICICI, JM, Emkay, PhillipCapital and others quarter after quarter.
scores.quote: hosted by IIFL Capital Services Limited

scores.rationale: Little image-based pricing power in the mass segment — every price increase triggered volume loss and downtrading, forcing an aggressive 15-20% price correction in FY23 to stay relevant.
scores.quote: The price correction has been around 15% to 20%

scores.rationale: There is a genuine quality/durability proposition backed by full BIS/QCO compliance that management believes wins long term, but customers repeatedly chose price over that assurance.
scores.quote: cheaper product can never cre ate a future. Future is always for the quality products

scores.rationale: Real accessibility advantage and improving customer intimacy — retailer base grew from 55,000 to 70,000, distributors from 550 to 630, and the Relaxo Parivaar app now drives 60% of secondary sales with 20% secondary growth.
scores.quote: we have introduced RPA, which is Relaxo Parivaar app, and we are seeing there is a 20% growth happening at secondary level

scores.rationale: Customer base is price-sensitive mass retail (>90% of portfolio below ₹1,000, 70% men's) where the required intangible pull is precisely what the brand lacks, as demonstrated by repeated downtrading.
scores.quote: more than 90%, it is less than INR 1,000

scores.rationale: No technology edge or R&D intensity is claimed anywhere; the product is commodity polymer moulded footwear whose economics are driven by EVA/PVC price swings and mould spend.
scores.quote: our total consumption of this polymer is around 1 ,000 tonnes a month

scores.rationale: No network dynamics exist in the model — growth requires manually adding distributors and retailers one by one rather than any self-reinforcing effect.
scores.quote: We keep on adding distributors. So it is a continuous process.

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the company's most durable asset — 70,000 retailers, 630 distributors, digitised last-mile via the retail app, plus growing e-commerce, LFR and a planned 100 EBOs.
scores.quote: if you see 2 years back, we were at 55,0 00. Now we are at 70,000 retailers.

scores.rationale: Consistently large growth capex (Rs 32,000–39,000 cr per quarter across 5G, retail, new energy, data centres) fully funded by cash profits, but incremental returns are visibly lagging as capitalisation crushed Jio PAT to Rs 764 cr.
