scores.quote: we hardly have any loan on our books. So, our gearing is very, very low

scores.rationale: Multi-year tenacity is well evidenced: the SKS resolution was pursued through NCLT, NCLAT and the Supreme Court from 2023 to 2026, while Rehar hydro was delivered ahead of its March 2025 schedule and coal-mine approvals have been ground out block by block over five years.
scores.quote: Construction work at 25 megawatt Rehar Hydro Power project is progressing as per schedule. We expect to complete the project before end of FY 2024-25.

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, operationally detailed and free of self-promotion, run by a Raipur-based promoter family that declines to comment on subjudice matters and refuses forward guidance.
scores.quote: Matter is subjudice. We don't want to comment on judicial process.

scores.rationale: Senior roles across the group are held by family members (Pankaj, Manish, Neeraj Sarda) with no discussion of a talent-development system, though the board was strengthened with credible outside independent directors.
scores.quote: we have appointed 2 more prominent persons as Independent Directors... Mr. Rajeev Sharma is ex-CMD of PFC

scores.rationale: Management explains misses with specific, unflattering detail (three named causes for the weak Q3), provides prudently for disputed transmission charges, admits Indonesian mine problems and refuses to guide in a cyclical industry — though it repeatedly deflects requests for segment-level profitability.
scores.quote: we are in the cyclical industry so generally we don't give advance guidance

scores.rationale: Separating skill from luck gives a mixed read — the PLF turnaround at SKS and ahead-of-schedule hydro commissioning are real operating skill, but the FY26 profit surge leans heavily on an above-average monsoon and commodity/power price swings the company does not control.
scores.quote: hydropower generation grew by 32% year-on-year, to 482 million units, supported by above average monsoon

scores.rationale: Products are undifferentiated commodities — billets, wire rod, pellets, silico-manganese, electricity sold on IEX — with no monopoly-like hold on any customer's mind or aftermarket.
scores.quote: The weighted average price of power on IEX for the quarter fell to INR3.89 per unit

scores.rationale: There is no switching-cost lock-in, but there is contracted regional captivity of a sort: a 40-year PPA with the Chhattisgarh discom at a fixed INR7.42/unit plus 200MW medium-term and 100MW long-term offtake on the IPP.
scores.quote: we have signed a 40-year power purchase agreement with Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Company Limited. The tariff has been fixed at INR7.42 per unit

scores.rationale: Secondary steel and ferro alloys are fragmented and contestable — capacity is expanding on both primary and secondary sides and Chinese/Vietnamese/Korean imports set the price ceiling after antidumping duties lapsed — leaving the company with no pricing authority over customers.
scores.quote: India remained a net importer of steel despite imposition of antidumping duty on certain steel products

scores.rationale: Barriers are high on the mining and hydro side (coal block auctions, forest and environment clearances taking 24+ months) but low in steel and ferro alloys where prices are set by imports and fragmented new capacity, so the picture is genuinely mixed.
scores.quote: Approval processes for the Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga, and Sinduri Coal Mines are ongoing

scores.rationale: The company has repeatedly acquired assets from failed or weak operators — SKS Power out of insolvency, a JV to reopen SECL's Bartunga Hill mine — and continues to shop the NCLT pipeline.
scores.quote: we are looking at a couple of assets in the NCLT

scores.rationale: It is a low-profile Raipur mid-cap operating in unglamorous niches — small hydro, underground coal, silico-manganese — whose calls are attended largely by individual investors and small brokerages.
scores.quote: we have a pipeline of three small hydropower projects of 25 megawatt each

scores.rationale: There is zero image- or taste-driven pricing power; realisations are set entirely by exchange and commodity markets, with steel at a five-year low and IEX power falling from INR3.79 to INR3.33 per unit.
scores.quote: Power prices on the exchange moderated with IEX average prices at around INR3.33 per unit compared to INR3.79 per unit last year

scores.rationale: The only reliability-based demand is contracted power offtake where discoms buy supply certainty, but this is regulated/tendered rather than trust-based pricing power; the metals customers buy purely on price.
scores.quote: we have secured 200 megawatt of medium-term and 100 megawatt of long-term offtake to our IPP providing stability to cash flows

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, sales force, dealer network or customer intimacy in any of the calls.

The customer base is entirely corporate/institutional (steel buyers, discoms, ferro alloy exporters) which fits a TCO/reliability model, but only the long-dated PPAs deliver any lock-in — the metals side has none.
scores.quote: We have focused more on domestic market for sale of ferro alloys due to better realization

scores.rationale: There is no proprietary technology edge; the technical agenda is standard efficiency upkeep — replacing TG sets, a washery, solar for captive cost saving — with no R&D intensity mentioned in five years of calls.
scores.quote: The company has placed order for replacement of existing 30-megawatt TG set with new energy-efficient TG set to save energy

scores.rationale: The business is a vertically integrated commodity producer selling coal, steel, ferro alloys and electricity into open markets and PPAs — there is no two-sided platform or any effect that strengthens with user scale.
scores.quote: steady execution across our integrated Energy plus Minerals platform

scores.rationale: Logistics investment is real but defensive rather than rival-beating — a railway siding at the coal mine, a jetty in Indonesia, grid connectivity for solar — serving own cost efficiency rather than an unmatched service reach.
scores.quote: We are also taking steps for setting up railway siding and loading infrastructure in the coal mine for movement of coal through rail for cost-effective movements

scores.rationale: Large, deliberately step-function growth investment in new music IP (₹1,000cr over 3 years, ₹235-300cr/yr) with a stated 5-year payback and 55-75 years of returns, but incremental returns have so far only 'just about matched' the charge-off and music growth slipped to 18%, so the ROIC proof is still pending.
scores.quote: over the next 3 years, we will be investing over INR1,000 crores in new music content... we maintain our guidance of a 5-year payback period

scores.rationale: A&P is treated like an investment (20% of each content deal, expensed immediately) and is demonstrably effective — the Dhurandhar album was pushed with Pocket Aces' digital muscle to sustain 6mn daily streams five months post-release — though it builds song/artist equity more than a durable corporate brand.
scores.quote: we went all out building them further using our digital marketing muscle. The Pocket Aces digital footprint played a massive role here

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but consistent capability-building — predictive data modelling to select which films' music to buy, GenAI video tooling that cut catalogue video turnaround from 10-15 days to under 3, and a new AI efficiency team — with visible output in hit rates.
scores.quote: use of generative AI video generation tools for these older songs has helped us drastically reduce both time and cost

scores.rationale: Deal-making is complementary and increasingly well-structured (Bhansali stake priced off future performance, Nav Haryanvi, ₹105cr of small catalogue bolt-ons), but Pocket Aces took roughly three years to move from a ₹10cr loss to mere breakeven, so post-deal margin improvement has been slow.
scores.quote: for us to get this company from a INR 10 crores loss into now a breakeven has been a successful journey

scores.rationale: The excerpts contain no discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy — only capital raising (₹750cr, QIP) and reinvestment.

The core music licensing business is asset-light with an irreplaceable IP moat and the events vertical recycles capital 6-8 times a year for triple-digit IRRs, though the current heavy content-capitalisation phase is temporarily depressing turns.
scores.quote: very little capital gets locked in events business, and that also for a very short duration, which results in a very high IRR

scores.rationale: Clear runway as the #2 label with an explicit target of 25-30% of all new Indian releases, and real capture — #1 in Bhojpuri, Gujarati and Haryanvi, global #1/#2/#3 YouTube videos — but Punjabi has failed twice and share commentary stays unquantified.
scores.quote: the year to start the process of moving Saregama from being the no. 2 label to the no. 1 label of the country

scores.rationale: Systematic language-market expansion (Bhojpuri, Gujarati, Punjabi, Kannada, Chhattisgarhi, Odia) plus diaspora live touring in Canada, USA and UAE, with local-language teams empowered rather than Mumbai-led — though Punjabi is a confessed miss.
scores.quote: people sitting in Mumbai are not taking decisions of what content to acquire in the Bengali or other regional languages

scores.rationale: The structural mix upgrade from free ad-supported to paid subscription streaming, plus catalogue described as an inflation-linked asset that rises as platforms raise prices, gives a genuine price/mix engine alongside volume of new releases.
scores.quote: Music catalogue globally is increasingly being treated as an infrastructure-like inflation-linked asset

scores.rationale: The business has just cleared its self-inflicted trough — the Airtel Wynk denominator drag and content-release phasing — with H1 growth of 8% versus H2 of 26%, an identifiable upturn as FY27's delayed big albums release.
scores.quote: H1 has seen a growth of 8%, while H2 has seen a growth of 26%

scores.rationale: India is under 2% of the $32bn global recorded music market with 18% of world population and under 3% paid streaming penetration versus 57% in the US, giving decades of secular expansion via subscriber, ARPU and format growth simultaneously.
scores.quote: the paid streaming penetration is 67% in Sweden, 57% in U.S... versus less than 3% in India

scores.rationale: Funding is from internal accruals and existing QIP money with no new raise, cash reserves are healthy, they invested counter-cyclically through a profit plateau and walked away from an overpriced Dhurandhar 2 — offset slightly by a widening M&A footprint (Pocket Aces, Bhansali).
scores.quote: the acquisition team stood its ground and refused to buy the album because of the pricing

scores.rationale: A decade-long rebuild since 2015 executed with explicit willingness to depress near-term profits for a 30-40 year horizon, refusing the easy option of harvesting the catalogue despite visible shareholder pressure.
scores.quote: Today, it's very easy for us to take the decision that we should reduce our new content investment significantly... We have taken a conscious call that we will not do that

scores.rationale: Management is process-focused and describes building verticals 'quietly', but the company operates in a celebrity Bollywood ecosystem under the high-profile Sanjiv Goenka/RPSG group with a very visible MD on every call.
scores.quote: While global majors are today talking about expanding artist brands beyond streaming, we have been quietly building it over the last 3-4 years

scores.rationale: Evidence of deliberate capability building — regional-language acquisition teams, a data analytics function, an AI efficiency team headed by an internal senior tech person, and claimed 'professional managerial depth' — but no explicit succession or leadership-pipeline disclosure.
scores.quote: we have recently launched a dedicated AI efficiency team headed by a very senior tech person from the company

scores.rationale: Repeatedly owns misses — twice-failed Punjabi strategy, lower-than-planned content spend, the 44% video decline, Carvaan scale-down — and when an analyst demanded rolling 12-month ex-events disclosure the MD accepted it on the call and committed to publish it.
scores.quote: I'll be honest and confess that our strategy never worked out

scores.rationale: Much of the reported success is skill-independent legacy catalogue economics plus a favourable streaming cycle, and guidance has repeatedly reset downward (30% consolidated CAGR, then 25-26% music, then 21-23%, then 18-19%), so results should be discounted for narrative polish.
scores.quote: This year, the number may be closer to 18%, 19%, but next year onwards, we should be back to 21% to 23%

scores.rationale: The 180,000-song legacy catalogue (Lata, Kishore) is non-substitutable and owns a monopoly-like place in the Indian listener's mind, but the company is only #2 in the overall market and must buy new content competitively.
scores.quote: We at Saregama with 180,000 song catalogue growing at 5,500 new releases per year

scores.rationale: Every platform must license every catalogue since a listener wants a specific song, making Saregama's IP a must-carry irrespective of platform consolidation, plus effective regional monopolies in Bhojpuri and Haryanvi.
scores.quote: consolidation does not affect us because the customer is going to listen to a song. It does not matter to us whether the customer is listening... on platform A or platform B

scores.rationale: Indian recorded music is a concentrated label oligopoly and Saregama has deliberately avoided dependence on any single platform customer, with minimum guarantees now routinely exceeded — though the buyers (Spotify, YouTube, Meta) are themselves powerful global players.
scores.quote: We have very consciously worked in a fashion that there is no overdependence on any one player

scores.rationale: Pricing for new content is visibly irrational — producers demanded prices breaking the five-year payback on Dhurandhar 2, Punjabi is 'very expensive' — and global institutional capital (Bain, Apollo, KKR) is entering catalogue buying, raising asset prices.
scores.quote: institutional capital from the likes of Bain or Apollo, KKR is now flowing into this space

scores.rationale: Some weak players have exited or been absorbed (Airtel Wynk shut down, Nav Haryanvi's ex-promoters became partners), but the main rivals are strong labels and Saregama itself concedes losing the Punjabi market twice.
scores.quote: That's the time Airtel Wynk shut their operations

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a listed Bollywood-adjacent business with brokerage-hosted calls, an aggressive analyst following, and global private capital now actively competing for the same music-catalogue asset class.
scores.quote: institutional capital from the likes of Bain or Apollo, KKR is now flowing into this space through various kinds of JVs and direct catalogue purchases

scores.rationale: Music is a pure taste/emotion good with very high structural margins (music vertical EBITDA guided at 60-65%) and authenticated human-created IP argued to become more premium in an AI world, though per-stream realisation is set by platforms rather than by Saregama.
scores.quote: our annual EBITDA guidance for this vertical being anything between 60-65%

scores.rationale: There is an assurance element in guaranteeing itself and its platform partners a reliable pipeline of A/B+ Hindi film music through the Bhansali tie-up, but customers buy specific songs on price-per-stream terms rather than paying up for Saregama's reliability.
scores.quote: Saregama secures our A and B+ Hindi film music album requirement for the next 24 to 30 months

scores.rationale: Direct-to-consumer reach is being deliberately narrowed (Carvaan pulled back to e-commerce and modern trade, physical retail exited), with the new direct channels — live events, brand partnerships — still small and unproven.
scores.quote: we have rolled out a new retail strategy whereby we'll be selling this product only from e-commerce and modern trade stores

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is correctly matched — B2B platforms get guaranteed, predictably-priced must-have catalogue, while retail consumers get nostalgia and experience products (Carvaan, Carvaan Live, diaspora tours) aimed at high-spending superfans.
scores.quote: Carvaan Live and our diaspora focused tours in America target exactly this audience segment... willing to pay a premium for curated experience

scores.rationale: Technology is applied and useful (acquisition data models, GenAI video production, AI process efficiency) but it is licensed third-party tooling rather than a deep proprietary multi-product edge, and management explicitly has committed no significant capital to AI.
scores.quote: we are watching this space carefully and have not committed any significant capital to it at this moment

scores.rationale: A genuine self-reinforcing loop exists — content makes artists big, big artists draw brand and live money and better content deals, and the 400mn-follower artist footprint plus 650mn-user reach compounds — though it is an owned-audience flywheel rather than a true two-sided network.
scores.quote: we are taking bets both on the content and the artist that is making the content

scores.rationale: The Pocket Aces-powered digital marketing reach is a rival-hard-to-match promotion machine that management credits for the industry's best hit rate at controlled marketing cost, though physical distribution is being wound down.
scores.quote: we are the most effective marketing machinery in there on the digital side... we are able to drive bigger number of hits on the music side in spite of having marketing costs which are under control

scores.rationale: Branch network (the NBFC equivalent of growth capex) rose from 135 to 256 over the period — 46 added in FY26 versus 25 guided — while returns improved (ROA 4.31%→4.53%, ROTE 10.77%→14.73%) and opex/AUM fell 161bps against 150bps promised, with further expansion explicitly gated on branch-level profitability.
scores.quote: Last year, we grew our branches by 46 instead of the guidance of 25... Cumulatively, against the 150 basis points promised, we delivered a 161-basis point reduction

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the calls.

No formal R&D line, but consistent in-house technology build — proprietary LOS/origination workflow, a multilingual rated personal-discussion app, PD/LGD model refresh on own data, branch risk-rating — that is yielding measurable underwriting and cost efficiency.
scores.quote: there is an app which we have which we are using, wherein the customer PDs are done through this app, and it is a multilingual app wherein there is a nudge to the credit manager

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed across the 14 calls; the only reference is legacy goodwill adjusted out of tangible net worth.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed in any excerpt; capital is retained (CRAR 32-38%) to fund growth.

This is a balance-sheet lender, structurally asset-heavy — AUM of INR 11,922 crores funded by INR 3,613 crores of equity plus borrowings, with returns of only ~4.5% on average assets, the opposite of an asset-light model.
scores.quote: our total AUM for June 2026 is at INR 11,922 crores... return on average AUM is 4.53%

scores.rationale: With an INR 4 lakh crore addressable market and presence in only a quarter of districts in its 15 operating states, an INR 11,922 crore book compounding 27-29% represents genuine share capture from a tiny base.
scores.quote: we are currently present in only one-fourth of the districts within operating states, which provides us with a significant runway for expansion

scores.rationale: Credible, disciplined domestic expansion — evenly spread across North/West/South with no state above 17-18%, now entering a deliberate 'phase two' of deepening in proven states after validating unit economics — though it is purely within India, not a premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: our second phase starts where we will now deepen our presence in each of these operating states

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and distribution-led with flat-to-lower yields (17.81%→17.61%→17.9%, guided range 17.50-17.75%), management explicitly disclaiming pricing power; the modest yield uplift came from gold mix, and spread gains came from falling funding costs, not price.
scores.quote: Lending is a commodity business, and we are all price takers, not price setters.

scores.rationale: The company is positioned into a deteriorating credit cycle, not near its bottom — credit cost rose from 0.80% to 1.45%, Stage 2 ECL was lifted from 6% to 16%, login-to-disbursal fell from 42% to 34%, and management flags household DSR at ~14% with inflation, rate and oil headwinds ahead.
scores.quote: The sub-10 lakh segment in particular is showing signs of leveraged stress and warrants close monitoring.

scores.rationale: The end market — under-penetrated small-business credit in small-town India — is in secular expansion, with an INR 4 lakh crore TAM 'continuing to expand', three-quarters of customers borrowing against property for the first time, and an ongoing unorganized-to-organized shift.
scores.quote: almost 3/4 of our customers borrow for the first time... a lot of unorganized form of finance is going to move to an organized form of finance

scores.rationale: Purely organic, two-product focus with no M&A and refusal of new products, very low leverage (1.9x D/E, CRAR 33%), counter-cyclical tightening of underwriting screens three to four quarters ahead of the industry, exit from unsecured lending, and provisioning at 2x regulatory minimum.
scores.quote: We have the distribution and gunpowder to push the pedal right now, but we'd rather scale this the right way than rush it.

scores.rationale: Guidance of 5-7% QoQ growth, 50bps annual opex reduction and 80-100bps credit cost was set at IPO and delivered for 12+ consecutive quarters, and management held a contrarian view on the credit cycle well before consensus.
scores.quote: When we called it out, we were the canary in the coal mine, a lone voice.

scores.rationale: Commentary is substantive and execution-focused, but opening remarks are notably literary and personality-forward (Munger, Carl Richards, CSR 'four pillars', badminton metaphors) from a well-known ex-bank CEO, so this is not a low-profile, understated management style.
scores.quote: I have gained from Charlie Munger's "Latticework of Mental Models"

scores.rationale: Clean internal succession executed — Mahesh Dayani rose from Chief Business Officer to MD & CEO and Sanket Agrawal from Chief Strategy Officer to CFO, with Dhru moving to Executive Vice-Chairman — alongside systematic frontline development via rated personal discussions used to target credit-manager training and deliberate hiring of first-time formal-sector employees.
scores.quote: the quality of the personal discussions helps us to gauge wherever we need trainings for the credit managers because all these PDs are rated

scores.rationale: Consistently quantifies delivery against promises, discloses adverse items unprompted (interest reversal on NPAs, ECL model re-cut, falling conversion rates, self-deprecating admission of past inefficiency), and openly owns errors.
scores.quote: I guess we've made enough mistakes, and I think probably we've got a little wiser in the second phase

scores.rationale: Skill is real (opex down 161bps, consistent guidance delivery), but a material part of the improving spread came from exogenous repo cuts (cost of funds down 90bps YoY) while credit cost nearly doubled and Stage 2 ECL went 6%→16%, so eloquent commentary and headline ROE gains should not be read as pure execution.
scores.quote: our cost of borrowing has come down by about 90 basis points year on year... Aided by the transmission of repo rate cuts

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position — small-ticket LAP and gold loans are contested products where competitors actively undercut on price and loan amount, and management describes itself as a price taker.
scores.quote: a few birds strayed on the badminton court, by which I mean competitors showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts

scores.rationale: Borrowers face low switching costs — customers are refinanceable against the same property and management concedes it has to walk away when rivals offer better terms; there is no captive aftermarket or regional exclusivity.
scores.quote: We were deliberate about pricing through the quarter, which meant walking away from some business rather than chasing it at any cost.

scores.rationale: The small-ticket MSME lending market is fragmented across banks, NBFCs and unorganized lenders, with customers able to source multiple loans against the same property — the borrower-overleverage problem management repeatedly cites is itself proof of many competing suppliers.
scores.quote: a certain segment of customers has got overfunded by the industry and those are the problems that are coming home to roost

scores.rationale: Barriers are modest and pricing discipline across the industry is poor — the segment was collectively over-funded, competitors offer 'generous loan amounts', and a regulatory circular alone reset co-origination from ~20% to 10%, showing exposure rather than protection.
scores.quote: the regulator's circular mandating banks not to accept collateral security for MSME customers within the 20 lakh ticket size had a direct bearing on our co-origination

scores.rationale: Ample weak donors exist — unorganized moneylenders funding first-time property borrowers, plus stressed lenders in the over-leveraged sub-10 lakh space that SBFC is deliberately stepping back from, leaving room to take quality share as they retrench.
scores.quote: a lot of unorganized form of finance is going to move to an organized form of finance

scores.rationale: The small-town micro-enterprise niche is genuinely unglamorous and under-served by the mainstream, yet the segment has clearly attracted heavy competing capital — evidenced by industry over-funding of these very borrowers — so it is not ignored by capital.
scores.quote: One that is being chased by multiple financials with open cheque books and the other that still continues to borrow at high rates of interest.

scores.rationale: Yields are high (17.9%) but management explicitly denies any brand or image-based pricing power, describing lending as a commodity and pegging yields to a target spread rather than to customer willingness to pay a premium.
scores.quote: we in our model have baked in a spread of 9% since last one year... Lending is a commodity business

scores.rationale: Customers — largely first-time property borrowers — buy access and certainty of getting a loan at rates near 18%, indicating price is secondary to reliable availability, and the model deliberately preserves in-person assessment as the trust-building step.
scores.quote: What doesn't move digitally is ensuring that the personal discussion with the customer or originating the customer... We would like to have in touch and feel of the customers

scores.rationale: Convenience and proximity are the core proposition — 256 direct-model branches taking credit into small towns with localized underwriting, in-house sourcing and digitized servicing, explicitly framed as making loans easy where customers are.
scores.quote: our promise of making loans easy for small businesses in small towns of India is a journey that's just begun

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail/micro-enterprise and the benefit offered is correctly matched to it — accessibility, local relationship and speed rather than corporate TCO arguments — though the relationship lacks retail intangible pricing power or lock-in.
scores.quote: We are financing bread and butter businesses, we are not financing manufacturing... These are trade and services, basic B2C businesses.

scores.rationale: Technology is competent and in-house (origination platform, digitized workflow, PD app, branch risk-rating, analytics-led ECL) but is process efficiency rather than a deep multi-product edge delivering a superior customer benefit, and R&D intensity is not called out.
scores.quote: It is in-house and core origination platform which we have created, it is a complete end to end workflow

scores.rationale: The business model has no two-sided or self-reinforcing network — it is a direct, branch-by-branch secured lending model where each new market must be built and paid for individually.
scores.quote: We are largely a direct model, we will continue to be a direct model in all the states that we operate in.

scores.rationale: Physical distribution plus local underwriting is the genuine competitive asset — 256 branches across 15 states built over eight years with heavy upfront state/regional cost now sweating into falling opex — but branch networks are replicable by well-capitalized rivals, so the moat is real yet not unmatched.
scores.quote: the heavy lifting on the high costs have already been done... you were laying distribution across the country in each of those states, which is extremely expensive

scores.rationale: Investment is in digital/AI platforms (Sprint, instant issuance on YONO) rather than disclosed growth capex with measurable incremental ROIC, and returns have fallen (ROE 30.8% in Q1FY23 to ~16.5% in Q1FY27).
scores.quote: Technology investments in artificial intelligence and machine learning are playing a key role in transforming our product development and service delivery.

scores.rationale: Sustained, award-winning brand and offer-led marketing (Apple offer advertised across airports/TV/print/social, Abby and ET brand awards) that visibly supports spends share gains to 19.5%.
scores.quote: This offer is being extensively advertised across Airports, Television, Print Ads, and social media.

scores.rationale: No R&D function as such; analytics/AI-ML work does yield new products (MILES card, Sprint onboarding, scorecards) but efficiency is not demonstrated in returns.
scores.quote: we enhanced data-driven customer engagement capabilities, helping enhance customer lifetime value

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed in any of the 17 calls — growth is entirely organic through co-brand partnerships, so there is no M&A record to judge.
Only a small interim dividend is declared with no buyback or articulated distribution policy, while capital is retained at a 25.6% CAR for growth.
scores.quote: This financial year, we also declared an interim dividend of INR2.50 per equity share, enhancing shareholder value.

scores.rationale: As a monoline lender it is balance-sheet heavy (INR58,269 cr receivables funded by borrowings) though revenue-to-assets is high at ~16% portfolio yield; returns are moderate with ROA 3.9% and no strong protecting moat on the asset base.
scores.quote: the receivables have increased to INR58,269 crores... With portfolio yield at 16% for the quarter

scores.rationale: CIF share has been flat at ~18.5% for four years but spends share recovered from 15.9% in Q1FY25 to 19.5% in Q1FY27 with the industry's highest net card adds, showing real recapture.
scores.quote: our spend market share has grown to 19.5% versus 18.1% in FY26

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-only into Tier 2/3 cities via RuPay-UPI acceptance, credible but incremental and with no international travel of the brand.
scores.quote: expand our reach in potential growth markets, including Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, along with the metros

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/spend-led with adverse mix — management explicitly declined to raise the 3.5% revolver rate, the high-yield revolver mix has a downward bias, and low-margin corporate spends worsened cost-to-income.
scores.quote: we would not like to take at this point of time, take action in terms of increasing the interest rate

scores.rationale: The unsecured credit cycle has clearly turned — gross credit cost fell from 8.5% (Q1FY25) to 6.5% with GNPA at 2.04% and six straight quarters of falling delinquencies — placing the company just past the trough with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: Our gross credit cost has improved by 116 basis points quarter -over-quarter and 301 basis points year -over-year to 6.5%

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — cards in force grew from ~75mn to 121mn over the period, spends to INR23.62 trillion, with digital transactions up 11x from 2021 to 2025.
scores.quote: India now has 121 million credit cards in circulation. Looking ahead, the industry is projected to grow consistently over the next decade.

scores.rationale: Entirely organic, no M&A, strong capital buffer (CAR 25.5–25.6%) and a willingness to shrink acquisition and cut 5 lakh customers' limits during the stress cycle, though the tightening was reactive rather than counter-cyclical.
scores.quote: during last three months we have reduced limits across 5 lakhs , in comparison to the 5 -lakh done over the previous full financial year

scores.rationale: Leadership is deputed from and rotates rapidly with the parent bank — three MDs (Amara, Chakravorty, Pande) and four chairmen in five years — which undermines independence and long-horizon ownership.
scores.quote: Managing Director: Abhijit Chakravorty (FY2024, exited)

scores.rationale: Commentary is institutional and metric-driven with no promoter/CEO personality cult; the MD speaks on behalf of the board and team rather than herself.
scores.quote: On behalf of the Board and Management of SBI Cards, I would like to welcome and thank you for joining us today.

scores.rationale: There is culture investment (Great Place To Work certification, employee upskilling) but the top leadership pipeline is imported from SBI on deputation rather than developed internally.
scores.quote: SBI Card has been certified a s a 'Great Place To Work' for March'22 -March'23

scores.rationale: Management disclosed the credit-cost deterioration early and explained the root cause (customer over-leveraging across all cohorts) without spin, guided that costs would stay elevated, and then delivered in line with what it had said.
scores.quote: customers obtained multiple trade lines from other lenders after taking a card, and this overleveraging has impacted their repayment capacity

scores.rationale: Strong headline results owe more to the parent's distribution and the industry credit cycle than to distinctive management skill — the same team's ROE fell from 30.8% to ~15% as the cycle turned against them.
scores.quote: ROAE is over 30.8%, which is higher by 1217 bps as compared to over 18.7% for Q1 FY22

scores.rationale: It is the number-two issuer in a contested market with no monopoly in the customer's mind — customers routinely hold multiple competing cards and are cross-sold by rival issuers.
scores.quote: It's normally the existing customers, credit-tested customers who are getting new cards issued by another new issuer.

scores.rationale: Switching costs are minimal — cardholders stack trade lines from several lenders and attrition must be actively fought through engagement programmes rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: we have been working very extensively on customer engagement which has also benefited us in terms of ensuring that the customers are retained

scores.rationale: The issuing industry is a concentrated few-large-bank oligopoly whose members responded rationally in unison to RBI's capital tightening, though retail customers retain choice among issuers.
scores.quote: after last September, October, RBI's decision of increasing capital adequacy , there were players who were not looking at some of these metrics. Now all the large banks and all the large institutions look at that

scores.rationale: Regulatory licensing and capital rules limit new entrants and pricing is disciplined (no rate war), but economics are exposed to regulator-set interchange/MDR and reward-led competition constrains pricing freedom.
scores.quote: The regulatory environment has also evolved significantly, with increased emphasis on responsible lending, customer suitability, digital resilience, cyberse curity and customer protection.

scores.rationale: Rival issuers pulled back after asset-quality problems, and SBI Card used the period to take the industry's highest net card additions and lift spends share.
scores.quote: SBI Card has made a net card addition of INR4.84 lakhs, which is highest in the industry for the quarter

scores.rationale: This is a widely-followed listed large cap covered every quarter by CLSA, HSBC, DSP, Nuvama, Equirus and global funds — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Abhishek Murarka from HSBC

scores.rationale: The brand wins recognition and supports engagement, but pricing power is weak — management ruled out raising the 42% APR and defends economics through fees and installments instead.
scores.quote: we are already at 3.5% pe r month, which is almost 42% APR. So, increasing that is not a good idea.

scores.rationale: The SBI parentage sells trust and reliability in payments, which management positions as the core of the customer relationship alongside rewards.
scores.quote: credit cards deepen customer relationships through credit access, flexibility, rewards and trust

scores.rationale: Access is a genuine strength — instant issuance on SBI's YONO and net banking, digital Sprint onboarding, and a top-rated app give direct, frictionless customer reach.
scores.quote: We have gone live with Our Instant card issuance journey on SBI's digital platforms, such as YONO and Internet Banking.

scores.rationale: The retail book is well matched with rewards/offers, but the corporate book is a low-margin pass-back business with no switching-cost lock-in that has structurally raised the cost-to-income ratio.
scores.quote: There's normally a passback involved in the corporate spend on account of which the cost goes higher... the margins are comparatively thinner

scores.rationale: AI/ML, scorecards and digital onboarding are competent and improving but are industry table-stakes, not a deep multi-product technology edge over rival issuers.
scores.quote: Continue to invest in next -generation digital capabilities to elevate and simplify customer journey

scores.rationale: The two-sided payment network belongs to Visa/Mastercard/NPCI-UPI, not to the issuer — SBI Card is a beneficiary of RuPay-UPI acceptance rather than an owner of the network.
scores.quote: the ability to use RuPay credit cards through QR-based UPI acceptance terminals is gaining traction

scores.rationale: The Banca channel gives access to the parent bank's unmatched branch and customer base, consistently sourcing ~42-46% of new accounts and uniquely enabling new-to-credit customers rivals cannot underwrite.
scores.quote: we also have a strong Banca channel where we have visibility over customers who may be new to credit or new to credit card

scores.rationale: Genuine growth spend on distribution infrastructure — 120 new branches in FY26 plus 100+ over three years and 1.2 lakh gross agent additions — with visible payback in agency APE growth of 15-20% and rising agent productivity, though it is opex-like rather than high-ROIC hard capex.
scores.quote: We opened 120 new branches this year. This expansion is aligned with our vision to create infrastructure that supports the long-term development of our agency channel.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend, its quantum, or its returns across any of the excerpted calls; brand is referenced only in passing through digital differentiation.

Product development functions as R&D and has repeatedly converted into business — Smart Platina Plus drove 621% non-par growth in FY23, and the FY26 par launches produced 133% individual APE growth — but no disclosed spend or efficiency metric.
scores.quote: This year, we launched new products in the par category and we got very good customer response in this category. That has resulted in a very robust growth in the par segment

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed anywhere in the four years of excerpts; growth is entirely organic and via distribution tie-ups, so there is no M&A record to judge.
Buybacks, dividends and distribution policy are never raised by management or analysts in the excerpted calls.

Capital-efficient model with sector-leading cost ratios (opex 6.1%, described as the lowest-cost operator) and 19.7% return on embedded value, though solvency drifted from 2.21 to 1.90 and Q1 FY27 opex re-inflated to 7.7%.
scores.quote: SBI Life being the lowest cost operator... we will be the least affected Company

scores.rationale: Already the dominant private player, and share has flattened rather than expanded — private individual NBP share peaked at 25.9% (Q1 FY25) and IRP private share sits at 22.2% in Q1 FY27 — even though the 3-year CAGR beats the industry.
scores.quote: It grew by 12.9%, 3-year CAGR, outperforming the industry average of 8.5%.

scores.rationale: Expansion is purely domestic branch and RRB/partner-bank reach with no international footprint or premium brand travelling abroad; the 120-branch build is distribution deepening within India.
scores.quote: With a view to broaden our reach, SBI Life has tied up with Paschim Banga Gramin Bank a leading RRB in West Bengal.

scores.rationale: Management has explicitly steered growth through product mix rather than price — non-par/par/protection share up, ULIP down from 70% to 61%, lifting ex-GST VoNB margin 150bps to 29% — but pricing power is limited (rates kept 'very competitive', GST absorbed rather than repriced).
scores.quote: our focus has been to improve the product mix in favor of non-ULIP products also... this is our effort to improve the profitability of the company

scores.rationale: The business is exposed to equity-market and regulatory cycles (ULIP mix swings, COVID cohort persistency dip, GST drag) and management claims only a margin trough, not a positioning near a broader cycle bottom.
scores.quote: on the margin front, we have definitely seen the bottom in the first quarter itself

scores.rationale: Indian life insurance is a structurally under-penetrated market with regulatory tailwinds (GST exemption, 'insurance for all'), and the company has compounded APE at ~13-14% and AUM from INR2.6trn to INR5.2trn over the four years of calls.
scores.quote: The long-term outlook for the Indian life insurance industry remains encouraging, supported by strong economic fundamentals, a favorable regulatory environment and increasing digital adoption.

scores.rationale: Consistently organic — no acquisitions across four years, solvency held well above the 1.50 requirement, prudent voluntary pandemic reserving, refusal to raise commissions to buy growth, and counter-cyclical multi-year investment in the agency channel.
scores.quote: As of now we are not planning any commission structure change for our corporate agents or for our individual agents and the rate structure will continue to be the same.

scores.rationale: The multi-year Agency 2.0 → Agency Next build and the deliberate two-to-three year product-mix diversification were both stated and then delivered, but independence is constrained by SBI parentage and MD churn (Sharma to Jhingran).
scores.quote: company has been focusing for last 3 years in strengthening our agency channel... this has resulted good growth in agency

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key, process-focused commentary with an explicit refusal to manage to short-term optics, and no promotional or celebrity framing in any call.
scores.quote: we do not pay much attention to month-to-month and we like to keep our focus on our yearly goals and midterm goals

scores.rationale: Strong systematic development of the distribution force (agent count 1.62 lakh to 2.57 lakh, productivity up 27%, gross adds of 1.2 lakh) but senior leadership is deputed from the SBI parent with MD turnover, so there is no evidenced internal executive pipeline.
scores.quote: we have made impressive strides in agent activation, agency channel productivity and onboarding of new agents

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly owns shortfalls plainly — admitting protection growth missed intent, that margin landed at the low end of guidance, disclosing GST and labour-code impacts both with and without adjustment, and refusing to predict COVID reserve releases.
scores.quote: the main thing is our protection has not grown to the extent we wanted. That is one of the key reasons why our margin has gone down.

scores.rationale: Results are materially attributable to the captive SBI branch network (60% of APE) and the industry's structural tailwind rather than demonstrably distinctive management skill, so headline growth should not be read as evidence of an exceptional operating team.
scores.quote: the bancassurance business of SBI and RRBs contribute 60% of the total APE business

scores.rationale: Effectively the sole life insurer inside the SBI ecosystem, giving a monopoly-like claim on India's largest bank's customer base, but this is a borrowed rather than self-created position and is exposed to open-architecture policy risk.
scores.quote: there was a media interview by the Department of Financial Services Secretary, where he yet again raised the topic of banks should be open architecture

scores.rationale: The captive banca arrangement with SBI and RRBs plus 60,000 CIFs functions as a channel monopoly with high switching friction for the distributor, though management gave no reassuring answer on the open-architecture threat beyond citing longevity.
scores.quote: With the strength of more than 60,000 CIFs, the bancassurance business of SBI and RRBs contributes 47% to the total APE

scores.rationale: Indian life insurance has LIC plus more than 20 private insurers with the leader holding only ~22% private share, and customers demonstrably shift between ULIP, par and non-par on returns, so end-customer negotiating power is real.
scores.quote: that was basically I think was being driven by more demand of ULIP products in the market depending on the returns that are being generated through ULIPs

scores.rationale: Regulatory capital and licensing barriers are high, ownership is stable under SBI, and management declined to compete on commissions or reprice after regulatory changes — but rate competition is acknowledged ('very competitive rates') and regulation repeatedly resets the economics.
scores.quote: we will be the least affected Company. As of now we are not planning any commission structure change

scores.rationale: The company has consistently grown ahead of the industry (12.9% vs 8.5% three-year CAGR) implying weaker incumbents ceding ground, though no specific weak competitor is identified and its own private share has not expanded.
scores.quote: It grew by 12.9%, 3-year CAGR, outperforming the industry average of 8.5%.

scores.rationale: This is a large-cap, heavily analyst-covered listed insurer with questions from Jefferies, Nomura, JP Morgan, CLSA and Emkay on every call — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Our next question comes from the line of Supratim Datta from Jefferies.

scores.rationale: The SBI name confers genuine trust that supports steady demand and stable ~26-29% VoNB margins, but the company positions on competitive pricing and absorbed both a yield drop and the GST hit rather than passing them to customers, indicating limited pricing power.
scores.quote: for a specific period in non-PAR savings, the impact of yield movement was absorbed by the Company instead of being passed on to the customers

scores.rationale: Customers are buying certainty and the metrics back it — 99.4% death claim settlement, a 0.02% misselling ratio described as among the lowest in the private industry, and an industry-first internal ombudsman appointment.
scores.quote: Our misselling ratio stands at 0.02%, which is one of the lowest in the private industry

scores.rationale: Access is exceptional and improving — SBI branch reach with 60,000 CIFs, 2.57 lakh+ agents, YONO three-click issuance, 99.9% digital proposal submission and 67% automated underwriting.
scores.quote: we are going to offer a product very soon on the digital platform of State Bank of India, that is YONO, and this will be a simpler product with three click kind of issuance

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — trust and convenience for the retail majority, and TCO/relationship-based lock-in for corporate business via credit life and group term written off the SBI lending book — though the lumpy group book dilutes margins.
scores.quote: we had a higher share of group business in the first quarter. That has affected margin overall

scores.rationale: Technology is a real efficiency edge — automated underwriting rose from 40% to 67% and digital submission to 99.9%, supporting the lowest cost ratios — but it is process digitisation, not a deep multi-product proprietary tech advantage.
scores.quote: 99.9% of the individual proposals being submitted digitally. 67% of the individual proposals are processed through automated underwriting.

scores.rationale: The business model is distribution- and balance-sheet-led with no two-sided network described in any call; scale brings cost efficiency, not self-reinforcing network value.
scores.quote: we are focused to strike optimum balance among various distribution channels

scores.rationale: Distribution is the core moat and is being widened — the captive SBI/RRB branch network plus 2.57 lakh agents, 120 new branches, non-SBI banks growing 22-31% and other channels up 160% — reach no private rival can replicate.
scores.quote: The other channels, the direct channel, corporate agents, other banks, brokers, online and web aggregators grew by 160% and contributed 28% of total APE.

scores.rationale: As a bank its 'capex' is technology/franchise investment, and management shows sustained, rising growth-oriented spend (new YONO, 10,000 Seva Sarathis, transaction banking hubs, Analytics 2.0) alongside ROA >1% and ROE ~18-21%, though returns on that spend are not separately disclosed.
scores.quote: our strategy is anchored around a long -term horizon with continuous investments in people, processes, products and technology

scores.rationale: The only A&P-type discussion is transactional customer-acquisition cost (DSA/home-loan sourcing, PSLC premia) rather than durable brand-equity building, so spend appears functional not brand-accretive.
scores.quote: when it comes to various acquisition expense, it is essentially on account of the home loans as one and also the PSLC certificates

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but a consistent multi-year product-development cadence (YONO 2.0 in 2022 → 8 crore users 2024 → new YONO with 4 crore registrations in three months by FY26, plus CHAKRA and Analytics 2.0) shows repeatable output from development spend.
scores.quote: the strong adoption of a new YONO, crossing 4 crore registration within three months of launch and bringing total users above 10 crores

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed anywhere in the excerpts; the only inorganic item is a divestment gain on Yes Bank shares, which is not a bolt-on acquisition record to judge.
Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are never discussed; capital talk is confined to CET-1 accretion and funding credit growth.

Structurally asset-heavy: a Rs 76 trillion balance sheet generating a ~1% ROA means very low asset turn, and returns depend on leverage rather than asset-light economics, even though the franchise moat is real.
scores.quote: Our ability to maintain an ROA greater than 1% at scale puts us in a top league of global financial institutions

scores.rationale: Demonstrated multi-decade share capture in deposits and credit growth consistently above system, but runway is limited by already-dominant position (savings balances 3x the next largest bank).
scores.quote: on the savings bank, our market share is 26.27 %. In 2004, it used to be 20.2 %, in 2014, it used to be 22.3 %. We have always gained market share while others have lost

scores.rationale: Foreign operations have compounded credibly across the whole period — 22% advance growth in FY23, 14% in FY25, 20% in FY26 — though in dollar terms growth is far more modest (8%) and it is wholesale syndicated/trade lending rather than a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: Our foreign offices have continued to perform well with growth in advances at 20% year -on-year. In dollar terms, it is 8%

scores.rationale: Growth is clearly volume-led — 15-17% loan book growth against a NIM that is guided flat-to-down at ~3% and compressed on rate cuts, so pricing is a headwind rather than the growth driver.
scores.quote: We are sticking to our NIM of more than 3% for the full year

scores.rationale: The bank sits near the favourable top of the credit cycle rather than the bottom — NPAs at two-decade lows and credit cost at 0.29% leave little cyclical upside and an ECL transition plus rate-cut margin pressure ahead.
scores.quote: The NPAs continue to be at its lowest level in over two decades

scores.rationale: Indian credit is in secular expansion (system credit 16% in FY26, Viksit Bharat capex thrust) which supports the asset side, but management itself flags financialization of household savings as a structural drag on the deposit franchise.
scores.quote: we remain mindful of structural shifts in the financial system, particularly the increasing financialization of household savings

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, no acquisitions, deliberate refusal to chase high-cost bulk deposits, and counter-cyclical buffer provisions of ~Rs 30,642 crore held beyond IRAC requirements.
scores.quote: we have not gone aggressive on the differential interest rate or high -cost deposits

scores.rationale: A stated multi-year repositioning (Project Saral, Analytics 2.0, YONOisation) has been executed consistently across two chairmen, though as a government-majority PSU its independence is inherently constrained and it aligns strategy to state objectives.
scores.quote: our FY26 performance reflects a consistency born out of a calibrated multi -year shift in ho w we run the bank

scores.rationale: Communication is institutional and substance-led — Setty deflects praise onto levers and process rather than personality — although a state-owned systemic bank can never be genuinely low-profile.
scores.quote: The profitability in Q3 has come from many levers. I did mention in Q1 and Q2 that both on the growth side as well as on the profitability side, SBI has many levers

scores.rationale: Internal pipeline is demonstrably strong — Setty rose from MD to Chairman and the MD bench is filled internally each cycle — with repeated emphasis on training and upskilling, though disclosure is generic.
scores.quote: Our people remain central to this jo urney, supported through focused training, continuous upskilling and an inclusive work culture

scores.rationale: Management gives explicit numeric guidance, is held to it, openly admits when its own internal call was wrong, and refuses to give a flattering ECL number rather than guessing.
scores.quote: Our internal guidance which has gone wrong earlier, we felt that the bond yields probably would be moving up to 6.75

scores.rationale: Record profits are materially aided by a benign credit cycle, one-offs (Rs 2,200 crore SBI MF special dividend, Yes Bank stake gain, Rs 769-1,000 crore tax-refund interest) and sovereign franchise advantage, so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: the one item which is a special dividend we have received, around Rs. 2,200 crores from SBI Mutual Fund

scores.rationale: Near-monopoly mindshare in government and defence banking gives a captive, low-risk retail lending pool that private rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: 95% is g iven to the customers who are maintaining the salary accounts... almost about 85% would be for the government employees only, that is defense and government employees

scores.rationale: Salary-account and savings-balance stickiness creates real switching costs — the bank cut savings rates to 2.5% and still grew savings 10.6% and current accounts double-digit.
scores.quote: We got the full benefit of Savings Bank reduction in interest rate to 2.5

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented and price-competitive on both deposits and floating-rate lending, with management repeatedly citing competitive pressure and NIM being dictated by repo pass-through rather than industry rationality.
scores.quote: with CASA ratio at 39.13% despite very competitive market environment

scores.rationale: Licensing makes new entry near-impossible and SBI shows pricing rationality (declining to use its own repo-linked formula to cut savings rates, avoiding high-cost bulk deposits), though deposit competition still forces rate concessions.
scores.quote: because we value our franchisee that is why we do not use this formula to the disadvantage of people

scores.rationale: Weaker peers have consistently ceded deposit share to SBI over two decades, giving an identifiable pool of donators.
scores.quote: We have always gained market share while others have lost

scores.rationale: SBI is India's largest and most systemically visible bank, covered by every major broker on quarterly analyst meets with live webcasts — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the outstanding balance in our savings bank accounts are three times the next highest, next largest bank

scores.rationale: There is franchise/trust value but no image-based pricing power in the P&L — NIM is capped at ~3% and margin is set by repo pass-through, not brand.
scores.quote: the impact of 25 basis point rate cut which is reflected in the EBLR portfolio

scores.rationale: Depositors accept a 2.5% savings rate and still add balances because they are buying sovereign-backed safety, and asset quality at two-decade lows reinforces the certainty proposition.
scores.quote: a 39.46% CASA ratio, which is an improvement of 33 basis points quarter -on-quarter, sustains our low -cost funding advantage

scores.rationale: Unmatched accessibility across physical and digital channels — ~60,000 savings accounts opened daily, 10 crore YONO users, 66% of new accounts digital, plus 500 dedicated current-account RMs, 60 transaction hubs and 10,000 branch floor coordinators.
scores.quote: we are opening almost 60,000 odd savings bank accounts daily and out of th ese, about 34-40 thousand accounts are getting opened through YONO

scores.rationale: Benefits are reasonably matched to customer type — trust/convenience and salary lock-in for retail, and dedicated hubs, relationship managers and trade/LC services for corporates — with corporate credit rebounding to double digits.
scores.quote: 60 odd transaction banking hubs we have already created and we are having 500 odd relationship managers only for mobilizing current account

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-year digital build (YONO, analytics-underwritten lending of Rs 25,438 crore in a quarter, Analytics 2.0, AI in credit and risk) is impressive for scale, but it is catch-up-to-parity technology rather than a proprietary edge over private-sector rivals.
scores.quote: Data and AI are becoming central to decision -making across credit, risk and customer engagement

scores.rationale: YONO's marketplace partners hint at platform effects but the evidence shows a scale distribution channel, not a self-reinforcing two-sided network.
scores.quote: We have now more than 100 online marketplace partners for YONO

scores.rationale: The combination of the largest branch/service footprint, 10 crore digital users and foreign offices gives a reach no rival can replicate, evidenced by savings balances three times the next largest bank.
scores.quote: the outstanding balance in our savings bank accounts are three times the next highest, next largest bank

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex (~INR 500-691 cr/yr, 8.6% of sales) on capacity, e-axle localization and 80% localization levels, but management has been moderating spend for two years and shifting emphasis to 'capex efficiency', with capex down to 3.1% of sales in Q1 CY26.
scores.quote: our capex investments stand at INR 691 crores

scores.rationale: Only promotional activity disclosed is the REPXPERT mechanic-engagement vans, which were themselves suspended for two years before being revived, with no A&P spend or brand-equity metrics given.
scores.quote: after a gap of two years, we revived the use of the REPXPERT vans

scores.rationale: Consistent new-product output — customer award for 'excellence in new product development', hydraulic cam phasers, overrunning alternator pulley, insulation-coated railway bearings, linear guides — though no R&D spend or efficiency data is disclosed and much technology originates with the parent.
scores.quote: award given to us by Voith Turbo Private Limited for excellence in new product development

scores.rationale: The single acquisition (Koovers, INR 142.4 cr, cash-funded, complementary bolt-on) targeted a loss-making startup that, nearly three years on, still runs -13.4% EBITDA and dilutes consolidated margin (19.3% standalone vs 19.1% consolidated), against repeated promises of imminent breakeven.
scores.quote: it has registered an EBITDA of minus 13.4%

scores.rationale: A clearly stated and honoured 30-50% payout policy with a rising dividend (INR 28 vs INR 26) even in a weak year, though there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution discipline.
scores.quote: we have stayed our commitment and the course of announcing dividend payout ratio between 30% and 50%

scores.rationale: This is a capital-intensive bearings/precision-components manufacturer running capex at 8-9% of sales and working capital near 18-20% of sales, so asset-light it is not, though the moat and margins (19% EBITDA) are protective.
scores.quote: Keeping the capex as a percentage of sales at 8.6%

scores.rationale: Automotive Technologies grew 30.8-33% against underlying auto production of ~15%, with the analyst explicitly noting wallet-share/content-per-vehicle gains, and localization rising to 80% displacing imports.
scores.quote: growth at 31%... underlying automotive production growth, which is at 15%, there has been a strong outperformance

scores.rationale: Exports (largely intercompany to the Schaeffler group) rebounded to 32.5% and 24% growth and 16-17% of sales, plus a planned pan-India rollout of the South-India-only Koovers platform, but this is group-directed sourcing rather than an independent premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: Exports also posted very robust numbers, as you can see, 32.5% compared to last year

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and new-business-win-led, while pricing power is visibly weak — input, LPG, freight and FX costs hit the bottom line and remain uncompensated by customers still 'in discussions'.
scores.quote: our input costs have gone up, which is yet to be compensated by the customers

scores.rationale: Several end-segments turned up from troughs across the period — commercial vehicles moved from -4.8% to 'a big jump', wind saw 'strong resurgence', tractors and exports recovered — indicating a mid-recovery rather than peak position.
scores.quote: Commercial vehicles still remain muted, as you can see, (-4.8%)

scores.rationale: Multiple secular end-markets: a car parc heading to ~60-69mn vehicles with aftermarket up 75% by 2030, B2B e-commerce at 30% CAGR, hybrids/e-mobility, renewables and railways/metro infrastructure.
scores.quote: will lead to a 75% increase of the automotive aftermarket business by the year 2030

scores.rationale: Organic focus with only one small cash-funded bolt-on, no debt discussion or leverage stress, and capex deliberately calibrated to demand while maintaining investment through the downturn.
scores.quote: this acquisition is fully funded by own cash generation

scores.rationale: Multi-year tenacity on localization (to 80%) and e-axle localization despite customers not yet launching, and persistence with Koovers through losses — but as a subsidiary of Schaeffler AG with 16-17% intercompany exports, genuine independence is limited.
scores.quote: we are staying the course when it comes to our investment plans towards localizing the product here in India

scores.rationale: Presentations are consistently framed around customers and operating data rather than personalities or promotion, opening every call with customer awards rather than management achievement.
scores.quote: why are we here? We are here because of our customers

scores.rationale: Beyond a stable long-tenured MD/CEO, a CFO succession (Satish Patel to Hardevi Vazirani) and mechanic upskilling via REPXPERT, there is no disclosure of a systematic talent-development or leadership-pipeline programme.
scores.quote: to upskill them in terms of training

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly names its own shortfalls — working capital, free cash flow, earnings quality, Koovers losses — rather than glossing them, though the recurring 'we will break even in the near future' on Koovers has gone undelivered for three years.
scores.quote: earnings quality definitely could have been better

scores.rationale: The strong CY26 numbers coincide with broad sectoral tailwinds (GST 2.0, 15% auto production growth, infra-led cement/steel/coal growth) that management itself credits, so results should not be read purely as management skill.
scores.quote: thanks to the steps taken by the government in last year pertaining to the GST 2.0

scores.rationale: Niche near-exclusive positions exist in specific applications — first-ever Indian Railways/metro recognition for insulation-coated bearings and zero-PPM status at Toyota — but the company is one of several global bearing majors, not a monopolist.
scores.quote: for the first time, we have been awarded as a very valued supplier for the Indian Railways

scores.rationale: Designed-in transmission components (clutches, cam phasers, planetary gear shafts) create high OEM switching costs, supported by long-standing customer associations and a captive aftermarket via Vehicle Lifetime Solutions.
scores.quote: Escorts Kubota as a special category award that has been given for our long association

scores.rationale: Bearings and driveline components is a concentrated global oligopoly with high technical barriers, but end customers retain real negotiating power, as shown by uncompensated input-cost increases and customer-driven cost-reduction programmes.
scores.quote: recognizing us for focused development and cost reduction activities

scores.rationale: High capital and qualification barriers (zero-defect OEM approvals, multi-year design-in) and stable MNC parent ownership, though pricing is not fully rational given customer-mandated cost reduction and the company's own 'recalibration' of unprofitable industrial volume.
scores.quote: Bearings and Industrial Solutions, on the other hand, we did some recalibration here

scores.rationale: Share is being taken from imports through localization to 80% and from the fragmented unorganized aftermarket via the digital platform and workshop network.
scores.quote: we have also increased our localization levels, and our localization levels have reached up to 80%

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar: a large listed entity with quarterly calls covered by multiple institutional houses (Nuvama, Equirus, JM Financial, Alchemy Capital).
scores.quote: the line of Raghunandhan from Nuvama Research

scores.rationale: Gross margin improvement is a recurring EBITDA driver, but demand is industrial/derived rather than image-driven and pricing power is demonstrably limited by pending cost pass-throughs.
scores.quote: the gross margin improvement brought in about INR 147 crores

scores.rationale: Customers repeatedly buy certainty rather than price — awards for zero-PPM quality from Toyota, resilient supply chain from Daimler, and reliability for railway and wind generator applications.
scores.quote: the zero PPM award for quality that we have received from one of the most stringent quality demanding customers

scores.rationale: Deep on-the-ground access via distributor network, REPXPERT vans covering 8,000 km of workshops, and the Koovers platform's 7,000 workshops across 125+ towns.
scores.quote: a deeper robust distributor network, along with technical engagement

scores.rationale: The mix is correctly matched — OEM/industrial customers (≈88% of sales) are served with reliability, TCO and design-in lock-in, while the retail aftermarket is served through brand and workshop intimacy.
scores.quote: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, 12% and our exports, which is at about 17%

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-platform technical breadth across ICE, hybrid and e-mobility with differentiated products, but the underlying technology is largely transferred from the German parent rather than generated by high local R&D intensity.
scores.quote: whether it is the ICE engine or the hybrid technology or even in the e-mobility, we have our portfolio is pretty active

scores.rationale: The Koovers B2B marketplace is the only network-effect asset and, after three years of ownership, remains sub-scale and loss-making rather than self-reinforcing.
scores.quote: EBITDA still, we are in the negative here as the focus is on scaling up the operations

scores.rationale: A layered reach — distributor shelves, REPXPERT technical service vans, and a digital platform with 7,000 workshops and 1.8 million SKUs — in a market where service and availability are decisive.
scores.quote: With 7,000 workshops, 1.8 million SKUs and being present in 125-plus towns

scores.rationale: Evidence of growth-oriented capex — two new customer-experience/digital labs built into the Vadodara plants, localization of the GMSeT gas-insulated range and the Trihal dry-type transformer line being brought to Baroda, plus 1 MW on-site solar — though absolute capex is never quantified or separated from maintenance.
scores.quote: these are part of two manufacturing setups, which we have in Vadodara... So these are the two setups, which we have made in last year

scores.rationale: Consistent brand-building spend through industry events (SWICON after a 10-year gap, Bharat E Summit, a self-organised Innovation Summit with 5,000+ attendees and 40+ CEOs) that visibly converts into customer engagement, but no disclosed A&P quantum or efficiency metric.
scores.quote: an Innovation Summit which we as a company organized... about 5,000-plus attendees came. 40-plus CEO level people came in

scores.rationale: A steady cadence of new offers — the GMSeT modular digital switchgear made fully in India, Trihal dry-type transformer, One Digital Grid AI tool, energy-storage solution and the Golden-Peacock-winning EcoStruxure XR Operator Advisor — yields real orders, but the underlying technology is largely the parent's global R&D rather than own-spend R&D.
scores.quote: GMSeT, which is a primary distribution gas-based equipment, which is made fully in India. It has got all the global technologies of Schneider Electric sitting inside

scores.rationale: The company itself has made no acquisitions across the five years — the group's L&T E&A deal was explicitly housed in a different entity — so there is no M&A execution record to reward or penalise.
scores.quote: The L&T business acquisition has taken place in other entity, not in this entity

scores.rationale: Across all excerpts there is no discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy; free cash was used to repay intercompany borrowing instead.

Revenue scaled from ~INR1,777cr to a quarter crossing INR1,000cr with fixed costs leveraged, free cash generated and debt repaid from the same asset base, indicating rising asset turns on a moderately asset-light manufacturing footprint protected by brand and installed base.
scores.quote: We continue to leverage our fixed cost, which is employee cost, other expense and depreciation... has reduced from the like-to-like last year's 9 month

scores.rationale: Order and sales growth (orders +26.9% FY24, +37% 9M FY26, backlog +50%) runs far above the 6–13% end-market CAGRs management itself cites, and wins span new accounts in semicon fabs, data centres and TBCB utility tenders — implying share capture with runway left.
scores.quote: we have an order backlog growth around more than 50%, and we have order backlog of INR 1,700 crores

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely within India (Bihar, Odisha, Gujarat, metros); no export or overseas market strategy of its own is described, with worldwide Trihal volumes belonging to the parent.
scores.quote: we have actually supplied close to 170,000 units worldwide across 100 countries. And that is what we are going to bring in Baroda

scores.rationale: Margin expansion is repeatedly attributed to mix improvement and selective order-taking alongside raw-material normalisation, but management concedes pricing is constrained in a competitive market and much of the growth is volume-led.
scores.quote: GM improvement has happened due to raw material cost normalization and better mix

scores.rationale: The company sits early in an India capex upcycle — government capex up ~11% to INR12.2 lakh crore, central utility outlays up 20% for FY27, repo cuts and PLI — which management frames as an inflection point, though raw-material inflation is a live headwind.
scores.quote: we are at the right inflection point to actually capture the growth coming in this industry

scores.rationale: End markets are in clear secular expansion — 500 GW renewables, data-centre IT load going from ~1.5 GW to 7–8 GW by 2030, EV penetration to 30%, semiconductor fabs and battery storage scaling ~200x — all electro-intensive segments the company directly serves.
scores.quote: we are at roughly about 1.7 gigawatts of IT commission load, which we see that in next 5 years down the line, this will go up to at least 4x

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, selective order intake on terms and cash, historic bad-debt problems fixed, free cash generated and intercompany borrowing repaid — a consistent counter to the leverage-and-acquire pattern.
scores.quote: We remain cautious in terms of order booking with respect to the terms & condition, payment, timelines and all to ensure that our margins and cash is secured

scores.rationale: A multi-year turnaround from losses to record revenue and profit was executed patiently across two MD regimes, but strategic independence is limited since technology, software licences and brand come from the French parent.
scores.quote: The actions were continuing and it has been a slow and steady progress... our focus has always been on improving the terms and conditions, picking up the right orders, and securing cash

scores.rationale: Communication is technically substantive but calls are laced with award-touting and superlatives (LinkedIn top employer, Golden Peacock, FICCI, 'India is shining', 'stellar performance'), so the low-profile test is only partly met.
scores.quote: this is the first time a quarter we crossed INR 1,000 crores. It's a stellar performance

scores.rationale: There is culture and employer-brand evidence (LinkedIn top company two years running, six core values, 20% gender diversity, ITI skill centres) but no described internal leadership pipeline, and MD/CFO seats turned over repeatedly across FY22–FY26.
scores.quote: Schneider in India, has actually been rated as top companies by LinkedIn to work in, and this has happened second year in a row

scores.rationale: Management corrects itself mid-call, explains provisions, the gratuity labour-code one-off and the Vivad se Vishwas base effect, and names headwinds like 30% copper/aluminium inflation, though it declines segment-level disclosure.

scores.rationale: Part of the improvement is genuine management work (bad-debt control, mix, cost leverage) but a large share is tailwind — raw-material normalisation and a government-funded capex cycle — so results should not be read as pure skill.
scores.quote: The margin has come predominantly from the gross margin improvement due to raw material cost normalization and better mix

scores.rationale: The installed base generates captive aftermarket pull-through — repeat defence submarine service orders, modernisation of existing sites and subscription maintenance contracts — a monopoly-like position on its own equipment.

scores.rationale: Switching costs arise from EcoStruxure software licences, SCADA/digital layers embedded on supplied equipment and modernisation of the company's own installed base, which locks customers into the upgrade path.
scores.quote: we are modernizing at many places by uplifting the technology with the present installed base has

scores.rationale: MV switchgear and transformers in India is contested by global majors and domestic players, with large utility and industrial buyers procuring through competitive tenders (TBCB), so the end customer retains negotiating power.
scores.quote: The margin improvement comes from pricing but it is always a competitive market

scores.rationale: Technical qualification for GIS, 765 kV panels and digital substations is a real barrier, but management repeatedly flags competitive pricing and margin defence rather than industry pricing rationality.
scores.quote: we are prescribed in the TBCB tenders, and we actually got 765 kV modernization and digitalization win

scores.rationale: The excerpts never identify weaker competitors losing ground; competitive discussion is limited to generic references to a competitive market.
This is a listed arm of a global brand with regular broker-hosted calls, flagship industry events, high-profile awards and heavy investor attention — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we had about 1,000-plus booth visiters, which comprised about 300-plus customers

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 37.1% and a premium Schneider brand give some image-led pricing power, but demand is capex-linked and raw-material inflation is only partly passed through.
scores.quote: At the gross margin level, we are 37.1%, which is up by 4.4 points

scores.rationale: The core value proposition is certainty — uptime, predictive maintenance, safety and reliability in mission-critical power distribution for data centres, metros, defence and DISCOMs — where trust clearly outweighs price.
scores.quote: how can you make those informations available to our users... with which they can maintain the minimum downtime of the assets they have

scores.rationale: Access is strengthened by a dual direct-plus-partner model with distributors and panel builders and by in-plant demonstration labs that bring customers into the factory, though no distinct accessibility edge over rivals is quantified.
