scores.rationale: Key senior roles were filled externally (MD Akhoury hired in, a senior IT head brought in, a Senior Advisor fronting calls in the MD's absence) with no evidence presented of a systematic internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we have a very strong IT team now headed by a very senior person on digital and IT intervention

scores.rationale: Management pre-warns of bad quarters, quantifies one-off cost overruns, admits dissatisfaction with utilization and that the 80mt target may be deferred, and checks itself against prior public statements — though it deflects some realization and UAE data requests to email.
scores.quote: I have no qualms in saying that Q2 and Q3 may not be very good... We are not happy with our current capacity utilization

scores.rationale: The record separates cleanly into demonstrable skill (lowest fuel cost at INR1.56/kcal vs peers' 1.80, 61% green power, highest peer-group EBITDA/ton) versus cycle-driven outcomes management itself disclaims control over.
scores.quote: our EBITDA per ton of cement for the year '25, '26 is by far the highest in the peer group

scores.rationale: No monopoly in the customer's mind — the product is a commodity that had to be sold at a INR30/bag discount to the leader, now still INR15/bag below, with no aftermarket or service annuity.
scores.quote: We had a large divergence between our sales price and sales price of competitors like UltraTech

scores.rationale: Even in its home North region Shree faces two powerful entrenched rivals and had to cede volume, and cement carries no switching costs for the buyer.
scores.quote: North had some constraints because I had 2 very powerful competitors sitting there, which is UltraTech and Ambuja

scores.rationale: The industry is consolidating toward a few large pan-India players with improving pricing discipline, but chronic overcapacity (mid-50s utilization) and multiple regional players leave price-setting power weak.
scores.quote: Pricing is a function of demand. If the demand does not revive, the pricing power will not be there with the industry

scores.rationale: Limestone reserves and capital intensity deter new entrants and incumbents are now slowing expansion, but the recent past featured unrelenting capacity addition and price discounting that destroyed realizations.
scores.quote: capacity increase is unrelenting and utilizations for the industry is not really going up

scores.rationale: Weaker regional peers visibly shed volume in downturns while Shree held or gained, giving an identifiable pool of share to capture.
scores.quote: Ramco lost 21% in quantity, 16% was lost by Dalmia, UltraTech lost 9%. We gained 1%

scores.rationale: Shree is India's third-largest cement group, covered by Morgan Stanley, CLSA, HSBC, Kotak, Nomura and others on every call — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: increased to 69.3 million tons, strengthening its position as India's third largest cement group

scores.rationale: The brand carries no price premium — it trades at a persistent discount to the leader and margins come from lowest-cost fuel and power rather than image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: we have narrowed the gap from about INR30 a bag to about INR15 a bag

scores.rationale: Some reliability positioning via the 'Solid Ghar' campaign and Bangur Concrete's testing facilities and technical manpower, but pricing discussion shows price, not trust, drives the sale.
scores.quote: Bangur concrete units are fully equipped to manufacture all types of special concretes, offering advanced testing facilities, best technical manpower

scores.rationale: Aggressive proximity build-out — RMC plants from 19 to 26 to a planned 45-55 across 50 cities, plus railway sidings and lead-distance management — improves customer access and go-to-market intimacy.
scores.quote: we have 19 commercial RMC plants. We intend to take it to 45 within next 6 to 8 months

scores.rationale: Mostly retail/trade sales (65%, down from 78-80%) which fits an intangibles play, yet the brand delivers no price premium, while the growing non-trade share brings neither TCO lock-in nor switching costs.
scores.quote: the trade sale is 65%

scores.rationale: Real process advantages (multi-fuel burners, waste-heat recovery, 61% green power, 1GW captive capacity) lower cost but are replicable engineering choices, not a deep multi-product technology edge backed by R&D intensity.
scores.quote: nothing stops me from changing from coal to petcoke or petcoke to coal. I have multi-fuel burners

scores.rationale: The described business — commodity cement sold through trade channels and captive RMC plants — has no two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic; scale brings cost, not network, benefits.
scores.quote: all my RMC plants will be using my cement and it will aid the cement quantity and capacity utilization

scores.rationale: A widening physical reach — pan-India plants across North/East/South, 26-36 RMC plants scaling to 50+, and new railway sidings — builds genuine last-mile reach, though it remains behind UltraTech's 25-year-old RMC network.
scores.quote: we are earnestly working on railway sidings... We expect to close the year with about 50 to 55 RMC plants

scores.rationale: FY26 saw ~INR 200 crores of capacity-expansion capex across Pithampur Phase 3, Ghaziabad, Pathredi, the new Coimbatore motor plant and Takahata Neemrana, alongside a piston-line asset purchase, while ROCE stayed high (23.8% at FY23) and margins were maintained.
scores.quote: we have invested close to INR 200 crores in capacity expansion across various business lines

scores.rationale: No A&P spend is ever discussed; the only brand-building evidence is aftermarket touch-point expansion improving visibility for the SPR/Usha brands.
scores.quote: we have over 1,200 touch points now and all the touch points have actually improved our visibility in the market

scores.rationale: The DSIR-recognised technology centre has produced hydrogen, flex-fuel and CNG piston solutions in advanced field trials, ring coatings for Euro-6, and ICAT/PM E-drive-approved localised motors, but hydrogen and hybrid programmes are only expected to fructify around 2029-30.
scores.quote: hydrogen pistons... There are at least 3 customers with whom our product is under advanced field trials

scores.rationale: The bolt-ons (EMFi, Takahata, TGPEL, Karna, Sunbeam lines) are complementary and management claims a repeatable post-deal playbook, but Antolin at EUR159 million (~INR 16,700 million) is a large deal into an acquiree whose margins are below standalone and still needs fixing.
scores.quote: The transaction was completed in the first week of January 2026 at an enterprise value of EUR159 million

scores.rationale: A consistent, disciplined dividend policy (INR5 interim plus INR5 final in FY26, 50% of face value each) and a long bonus history, though there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution logic.
scores.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR5 per share... In addition to the interim dividend of INR5 per share already paid

scores.rationale: The business is capital-intensive with multiple plants and continuous capacity capex, so asset turn is unremarkable even though returns (ROCE 23.8%) and fungible lines help utilisation.
scores.quote: Our manufacturing lines are fungible which means that we can produce the respective products on ear-marked lines based on changes in demand

scores.rationale: Consistent outperformance of end markets across years (9MFY25 income +15.3% vs ~6% market; Q3FY26 +21% vs 17% industry production) plus aftermarket penetration, though the company is already the leading domestic piston/ring player which limits runway in the legacy core.
scores.quote: we are continuing to outperform all the end segments of the auto industry in this quarter as well

scores.rationale: Exports reach 45 countries but have been under sustained pressure through the period, and the expansion actually being executed is domestic distribution (Assam to Kerala) rather than credible new-geography growth.
scores.quote: our exports continue to face some pressure given the geopolitical tensions, high volatility in the freight rates, high energy costs especially in Europe

scores.rationale: Margin gains came from a five-year exit of low-margin 'leakers and bleeders' (mix), but headline FY26 growth was clearly volume/industry-led and commodity pricing is a pass-through rather than pricing power.
scores.quote: 100% of the commodity changes are backed up by the customers, and we go back to our customers and claim

scores.rationale: The company is positioned near a cyclical peak, not a trough — record industry volumes on GST 2.0, rate cuts and the strongest festive season, with management expecting to keep 'breaking records'.
scores.quote: the auto industry witnessed a very strong operating environment and reported record production and sales volumes during the quarter

scores.rationale: Indian auto components is a secularly expanding end market and diversification has taken powertrain-agnostic products to ~35% of revenue, but the legacy ICE core faces a long-term EV transition management can only argue will 'coexist'.
scores.quote: the overall sales revenue of the powertrain-agnostic products would increase to over 35% of the consolidated revenue

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (D/E 0.24, debt-free cash-free deal) and portfolio pruning has been disciplined, but the strategy is explicitly acquisition-led with five deals in five years including one large one, which cuts against organic focus and 'no big M&A'.
scores.quote: thanks to the number of M&As that we have done over the last 5 years. We have a set kind of a rule book

scores.rationale: A multi-year strategy communicated and then delivered — EBITDA margin lifted from 12.4% (FY20) to ~22-23%, the five-year bleeder exit completed, and the Coimbatore EV plant inaugurated exactly as previously committed.
scores.quote: in November 2025, as committed earlier, we have inaugurated the state-of-the-art world-class facility at Coimbatore

scores.rationale: A 60-year-old company that only held its maiden investor call in April 2024, refuses to name competitors and declines forward guidance, though the FY26 rebranding and record-milestone framing is somewhat more promotional.
scores.quote: No, we don't name our competitors, sorry.

scores.rationale: Explicit systems for identifying and nurturing talent with a stated succession pipeline and 30-year veterans, and above-minimum pay insulated the company from the Noida/Haryana labour disruption.
scores.quote: our investment in cultivating a strong leadership pipeline ensures a sustainable succession plan

scores.rationale: Management discloses adverse items plainly — export weakness, the INR 252 million labour-code exceptional charge, being 'priced out' of exited lines — though it withholds segment and subsidiary revenue/margin breakups.
scores.quote: there was a nonrecurring exceptional expense of Rs. 252 million pertaining to the statutory impact of the new Labour Codes

scores.rationale: Genuine skill is visible in the pre-upturn margin expansion and product-line pruning, but recent headline results lean heavily on an industry upcycle (GST 2.0, rate cuts, festive season) and acquired revenue, so the record numbers should not all be credited to management.
scores.quote: This growth has been driven by various macroeconomic factors like the implementation of GST 2.0 reforms

scores.rationale: The SPR/Usha aftermarket brands and packaged engine-repair kits (pistons plus con rods, valve seats and guides) create a preferred position in the mechanic's mind, though competitors clearly exist and have undercut them on some lines.
scores.quote: we have started combining all those and trying to give this as a package

scores.rationale: Engine-critical parts are designed into OEM programmes years ahead (hybrid programmes for 2029-30) on relationships spanning decades, creating real switching costs, alongside a captive engine-repair aftermarket.
scores.quote: we are working on programs which are going to see the light of the day maybe in 2029, 2030

scores.rationale: The piston/ring segment is concentrated with few credible players, but the customers are large OEMs holding clear negotiating power — pricing is formula-driven and the company has been undercut out of some product lines.
scores.quote: for areas where we were getting priced out because of our competition being on a much lower price targets, we decided to actually exit those businesses

scores.rationale: Technology collaborations, DSIR/ICAT approvals and OEM qualification are real entry barriers, but management's own account of being priced out of businesses shows pricing is not fully rational across the segment.
scores.quote: our competition being on a much lower price targets

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are exiting and handing over capacity — Craftsman's Sunbeam sold its piston manufacturing lines to SPRL, and Grupo Antolin sold its three Indian entities outright.
scores.quote: signing of an asset purchase agreement with Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions... to acquire piston manufacturing lines

scores.rationale: A humble, unglamorous engine-components niche that went five decades without an investor call, though listing-driven visibility and the rebrand are gradually ending the obscurity.
scores.quote: welcome to the Maiden Investor Call of Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited

scores.rationale: This is a B2B engineering supplier with commodity pass-through pricing rather than image-based pricing power; the only intangible pull is the legacy SPR/Usha brand recognition in the aftermarket.
scores.quote: Our products are marketed and distributed under our well-known renowned brands SPR and Usha

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty on engine-critical parts — decades-long OEM supply agreements, JIT assembly units, TPM certification and quality awards, with management framing its investment around consistent quality and delivery performance rather than price.
scores.quote: These initiatives are focused on improving efficiency, ensuring consistent quality and strengthening delivery performance to all our customers

scores.rationale: Deep accessibility on both sides: five (now more) assembly units co-located with OEM plants for just-in-time supply plus a new Bhora Kalan centre, and 1,200-plus aftermarket touch points from Assam to Kerala with a strengthened distribution chain.
scores.quote: we have set up five assembly units in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat where most of the OEMs have their manufacturing setups

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — reliability, localisation approvals and design-in lock-in for the corporate OEM base, and branded, packaged, widely distributed products for the retail aftermarket.
scores.quote: we are probably the only one who have been able to demonstrate the complete localization to the ICAT authorities

scores.rationale: A multi-product technology edge backed by four decades-old global collaborations and an in-house DSIR-recognised centre doing engine testing for customers, but much of the core technology is licensed from partners rather than proprietary.
scores.quote: four long-standing technology collaborations with prominent global leaders in the automotive components sector

scores.rationale: Nothing in twelve calls describes any two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the business is a linear component supplier.

A hard-to-replicate reach combining OEM-adjacent JIT assembly centres, 1,200-plus aftermarket touch points and exports to 45 countries, though rivals in the aftermarket also hold established networks.
scores.quote: we have actually strengthened our supply chain distribution channel, and we are able to cater to those demands

scores.rationale: Growth investment is in branch/network capacity and capital deployment rather than maintenance — 2,200 branches converted for gold lending and a ₹39,618 crore MUFG infusion explicitly for expansion — with incremental returns intact (NIM 9.04%, PAT +59.8% YoY), though returns on the new equity are still to be earned.
scores.quote: around 2,200 branches are made ready for gold loan activity. So we expect the portfolio to grow double in the next 3 years

scores.rationale: A&P is managed as a discretionary cost lever to flatter the cost-to-income ratio rather than as durable brand investment.
scores.quote: the current quarter, we spent less on our branding expenses and other advertisement cost

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, product-development pipeline or innovation efficiency is discussed anywhere in the excerpts.

The defining deal was a large transformational merger (STFC + Shriram City Union) rather than a small bolt-on, but it was executed smoothly and post-deal efficiency did improve (cost-to-income 27.45% in Q1FY25 to 25.48% in Q1FY27), and the non-core housing subsidiary was sensibly divested.
scores.quote: the merger of two operating compan y, that is Shriram Transport Finance and Shriram City Union Finance Limited

scores.rationale: A coherent and rising dividend policy (interim ₹4.8 + final ₹6 = ₹10.8 per ₹2 share in FY26), but capital actions have been issuance-led (MUFG preferential allotment) with no buyback at depressed valuations.
scores.quote: final dividend of INR6 per equity share ... in addition to the interim dividend of INR4.8 per equity share

scores.rationale: As a balance-sheet lender the business is structurally asset-heavy — ₹3.14 lakh crore AUM funded at 2.14–3.82x leverage — so despite a genuine niche moat, asset turn is inherently low.
scores.quote: The leverage ratio came down because of this large capital infusion, is at 2.14x versus 3.82x as of March

scores.rationale: Clear runway plus demonstrated capture: new-vehicle disbursement mix rose from ~10% to 16–17% by winning back customers previously lost to rivals, MSME targeted from 15% to 20% of book and gold from 2.5% to 5%.
scores.quote: the customers who were otherwise going out to the competition, we are able to retain and finance them

scores.rationale: Credible domestic expansion of the ex-SCUF products from a 60% South concentration into the larger non-South market on the back of the merged pan-India branch network, though it is a multi-year work-in-progress and there is no international footprint.
scores.quote: MSME book also, we ha ve been traditionally lending in the souther n market. Other markets have not really explored much

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/AUM-led while price and mix are dilutive — rate cuts are being passed to borrowers and the shift toward new-vehicle lending is guided to pull NIM from 9.04% down to ~8.5%.
scores.quote: since we are passing on the reduced cost of borrowing to the customer ... our long -term margins of 8.5%

scores.rationale: Management correctly identified the CV cycle trough in 2022 (550k units vs a 1mn peak) and rode the recovery to 10.8 lakh units in FY26, but the company now sits mid-to-late cycle with monsoon deficit and fuel risk flagged rather than near a bottom.
scores.quote: the peak sale on commercial vehicle was 1 million units ... from 1 million , it came down to 5 ,50,000 during the 2021

scores.rationale: End markets — used-vehicle finance, small-ticket MSME, gold and rural credit in an economy growing 6.6–7.8% with rising GST collections and infrastructure capex — are in secular expansion, though cyclically sensitive.
scores.quote: the budget also provides INR11.11 lakh crore s of capital expenditure to improve infrastructure

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage and liquidity discipline (3 months of liability repayment held as liquidity, leverage cut to 2.14x, borrowings repaid before growth deployment) and deliberate slowing of MSME when stress appeared, offset by one very large merger.
scores.quote: we also have reduced our MSME growth just to keep a watch on this segment, and we are very careful about it

scores.rationale: A ~50-year franchise with a multi-year merger integration seen through and consistent 15–18% growth guidance delivered across the period, though independence is now qualified by MUFG's 20% stake.
scores.quote: Shriram has been in this business for nearly 50 years

scores.rationale: Calls are substance-dense — macro data, segment disbursements, ECL PD/LGD detail — with no celebrity framing, and management explicitly refused to speculate publicly about the MUFG relationship.
scores.quote: you are already talking about something futuristic. I think this is not a very appropriate question at all

scores.rationale: Deep internal bench with orderly succession (Parag Sharma moving from CFO to MD & CEO, Sunder to JMD & CFO) and a ~76,000-strong workforce being rebuilt toward 80,000, though headcount was trimmed opportunistically to manage cost.
scores.quote: from 79,000 odd employees, we are at 76,000 employees ... we again want to increase it closer to 80,000

scores.rationale: Generally candid — owns the gold-loan slowdown causes, admits caution and past error in MSME, and acknowledges conservatism in NIM guidance — but occasionally deflects rather than engages on uncomfortable questions.
scores.quote: MSME, we have been cautious in the last 1 year. We are now pretty confident about the MSME quality

scores.rationale: Strong headline results owe materially to exogenous tailwinds — a CV upcycle, falling repo/funding costs (8.96% to 8.56%) and a large equity infusion lifting NIM — making it hard to separate skill from cycle, though credit cost held stable at ~1.66% through the period.
scores.quote: as this liquidity gets utilized into the growth, in fact, that should support the margins in the near term

scores.rationale: Occupies a niche in used-vehicle and rural small-operator lending that banks largely avoid, which historically conferred pricing power.
scores.quote: Since we are in the niche segment of lending to used vehicle and in the rural market, we have that pricing power

scores.rationale: Switching costs are weak and price-driven — customers openly moved to competitors over interest rates and are only being won back by matching them.
scores.quote: Many of our customers would have gone to the other players because we were not matching the interest rate in the past

scores.rationale: The lending market is fragmented and contested by banks, NBFCs and even pawn brokers, with borrowers demonstrably able to shop on rate.
scores.quote: temporarily customers may go into a pawn broker for raising money

scores.rationale: Real barriers exist in capital, ratings and branch/collection infrastructure, but pricing is competitive rather than rational — the company competes by matching rates and passing on funding-cost declines.
scores.quote: Today, since we have a capital and since our cost of borrowing is coming down, we are ab le to match the rates

scores.rationale: Weak or constrained competitors exist to take from — customers returning from other financiers, and unorganised pawn brokers in gold — supporting the planned doubling of the gold book.
scores.quote: we have started using many of our existing branches for gold loan ... expect the portfolio to grow double in the next 3 years

scores.rationale: This is a highly visible ₹3.14 lakh crore-AUM listed NBFC with dense analyst coverage and a landmark ₹396 billion MUFG investment — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: MUFG Bank holding 20% stake in Shriram Finance on a fully diluted basis

scores.rationale: Sustained high margins (NIM 8.6–9.0%) and stated pricing power in its niche indicate real customer stickiness, but that power is eroding as rate cuts are passed through to retain business.
scores.quote: We have the pricing power ... to pass on any increase in borrowing cost

scores.rationale: The product sells certainty to first-time and small operators — fixed contracted EMIs that never reset, in a segment where predictability of outgo matters more than headline rate.
scores.quote: it is all contract rates and also fixed EMI. So, it doesn't fluctuate ... the predictability is clear

scores.rationale: Accessibility and field intimacy are the core of the model — a ~76,000-person workforce and thousands of branches reaching rural borrowers, with service quality cited alongside price as the reason customers return.
scores.quote: not only we match the rate, we are also able to service the customer much better

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to a retail/micro-enterprise base — small-operator vehicle loans, ~₹10 lakh ticket MSME loans against property mortgage and ~₹70,000 gold tickets — with cash-flow-based underwriting and credit cost priced into the rate.
scores.quote: the credit cost is factored in our lending rates

scores.rationale: No technology platform, digital capability or R&D intensity is discussed in any substantive way across the excerpts.
The business is a one-sided balance-sheet lender with no two-sided platform dynamic — scale brings funding and distribution benefits, not self-reinforcing network value.
scores.quote: we are into extreme retail individual operator kind of lending

scores.rationale: Its pan-India branch and field-collection network is the genuine hard-to-replicate asset — enabling gold-loan rollout across 2,200 branches and MSME entry into new geographies purely off existing reach, in a segment where physical servicing and collection are decisive.
scores.quote: since we have now branch network across the country, we will be able to grow our MSME book

scores.rationale: Sustained, large, self-funded growth (not maintenance) capex — ~INR10,000 cr announced since IPO with ~INR9,580 cr still to deploy — that has demonstrably converted into volume/revenue growth (revenue INR6,000cr to INR18,552cr in 4 years) at a respectable 16% ROCE during peak capex.
scores.quote: We have announced the CAPEX of close to 10,000 crores since 2021 being an IPO year, we have already incurred a CAPEX close to 5000 crores till FY 25

scores.rationale: Tiger brand A&P with a celebrity endorser is credited with rural penetration and volume resilience versus peers, but the payoff shows up in volume rather than in durable gross-margin premium.
scores.quote: we are focusing too much on the branding having Salman Khan and getting into the penetration of the rural it really helped us to overcome this crisis

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline, or product-development programme is discussed in any of the excerpts; process/digitisation upgrades are mentioned but not framed as R&D.

Deals are distressed-asset purchases (Ramsarup, shut for years and needing consultants and monthly cash burn; Mittal Corp with carry-forward losses), i.e. the acquiree was weak rather than already strong, though they are complementary and brownfield-integrated.
scores.quote: this plant was shut down for very long at this point of time we have appointed the consultant our PUs to evaluate

scores.rationale: A stated and consistently executed 70/20/10 reinvest-reserve-distribute policy with an unbroken quarterly/annual dividend record since listing, but no buybacks and no valuation-linked discipline.
scores.quote: We reinvest 70% of our total cash generated back into the business, retain 20% as a liquidity surplus, and 10% to distribute to our steel shareholder as a dividend

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy: management itself calls it a high-capex business, with ~INR4,300 cr sitting in CWIP and INR2,700 cr more committed for plants commissioning only in 2029, so capital is tied up long before it turns.
scores.quote: At Shyam, we understand high CAPEX business and metallurgy

scores.rationale: A mid-size player in a fragmented market growing volumes far ahead of the industry (4.94 mt, +26% YoY vs 7-8% market growth) with explicit intent to convert brownfield capacity into share.
scores.quote: we are adding our existing capacity, which will help us to reduce our cost and help us to take more market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is deepening within its Eastern India home base (80% of sales within 500 km) rather than entering new geographies; only the niche aluminium foil business genuinely travels abroad with >50% exported.
scores.quote: majorly 80% of the product what we sell is within the vicinity of 500 kilometers

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume-led (FY26 volume +26% vs revenue +22%, i.e. realisation slightly negative), though a deliberate mix shift into CR coil, stainless and aluminium is now lifting blended margin.
scores.quote: The growing contribution of CR sheet, stainless, aluminium is deliberately strategic shift, one that is enhancing our blended margin profile

scores.rationale: The company was buying/building through the 2024 trough (11.2% EBITDA margin under Chinese export pressure) but by FY27 Q1 margins had already recovered to 14.9%, so the cyclical upturn is largely behind rather than ahead.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 14.9% in comparison with the 14.3% in quarter 1 of the last financial year

scores.rationale: Indian steel demand is in a durable secular expansion, with per-capita consumption far below global levels and infrastructure-led demand repeatedly quantified at 7-8% annual growth over multiple years of calls.
scores.quote: forecasting 7% to 8% increase in the demand over next few years

scores.rationale: Organic brownfield expansion funded almost entirely by internal accruals, net-cash/near-debt-free through a peak capex cycle, with a treasury of INR2,165 cr and no large transformational M&A.
scores.quote: The proposed capex will be primarily funded through internal accruals... we are almost a debt-free company

scores.rationale: A multi-year plan articulated in 2024 (multi-metal, value-added shift) has been executed step by step through a weak price cycle, culminating in Vision 2031 and revenue tripling from INR6,000 cr to INR18,500 cr in four years.
scores.quote: since IPO from INR6,000 crores revenue, in 4 years, we have marched to close to INR18,500 crores

scores.rationale: Management professes an understated style, yet the company leans on a Bollywood celebrity endorsement and its calls are hosted for and covered by Goldman Sachs, UBS and ICICI, so it is hardly under the radar.
scores.quote: We rather believe to speak less and deliver more

scores.rationale: The calls are silent on talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline; the only references to people are generic industry-level remarks about a skilled workforce and employment creation.

Financial explanations are specific and unspun on bad news (the 55% PAT fall was traced to a prior-year tax reversal, and China undercutting was named as the margin culprit), but the tone is heavily promotional and no genuine mistake is ever owned.
scores.quote: Its aggressive export strategy, coupled with steep prices undercutting amidst its own economic crisis is disturbing the global steel export dynamics

scores.rationale: Strong headline growth is largely attributable to added capacity and captive power cost (Rs.2.47/unit) plus commodity price swings rather than demonstrable pricing skill, so the record should be discounted for cycle and volume effects.
scores.quote: 82% of our power sourcing from our captive power plant at a cost of Rs.2.47 per kilowatt

scores.rationale: Products are commodity long steel, pellets, sponge iron and pig iron sold on price into an open market with no aftermarket or mindshare monopoly; management itself describes the shift away from 'commodity-focused' as an aspiration.
scores.quote: transforming Shyam Metalics from commodity-focused steel manufacturer into a diversified value-added metal conglomerate

scores.rationale: Freight economics give a genuine regional advantage in Eastern India, and in colour-coated products management claims to be one of the few Eastern-located plants serving the North East and hilly regions, though there are no customer switching costs.
scores.quote: Our plant is one of the few Eastern located plant in India where there is a good demand of color coated sheet

scores.rationale: The secondary/long steel market is fragmented and price-taking, with realisations set by imports and global spot prices rather than by a stable few-player structure.
scores.quote: The Indian steel prices remain under pressure on a higher import and comparatively weak export

scores.rationale: Pricing is irrational and externally imposed — Chinese export undercutting and cheap imports repeatedly compressed margins (11.2% in Q2 FY25), and secondary rebar prices swing sharply with no industry price discipline.
scores.quote: prices of secondary rebars have actually gone down significantly. And not only secondary, but also primary rebar

scores.rationale: The sector is littered with failed players whose assets Shyam has literally absorbed — Ramsarup (defunct for years) and Mittal Corp (loss-laden) — providing both capacity and market share to take.
scores.quote: brought forward losses arises on acquisition of Mittal Corp Limited

scores.rationale: Far from ignored: the company runs quarterly IR calls hosted by Orient Capital/MUFG/E&Y with questions from Goldman Sachs, UBS, ICICI and Kotak, and holds investor days publicising a 2031 vision.
scores.quote: the first question is from the line of Amit Dixit from Goldman Sachs

scores.rationale: The Tiger consumer brand and B2C push give some pull in rural TMT, but margins remain commodity-level (13-15% EBITDA, 6% PAT) so pricing power from image is limited.
scores.quote: our long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of around 14% to 15%

scores.rationale: Quality and structural-product superiority are asserted as a margin driver, but customers are largely price-driven B2B buyers and realisations track market prices, not trust premia.
scores.quote: Increasing awareness about our superior quality structured product will continue to drive growth and enable us to generate better margins

scores.rationale: Proximity to market (80% of sales within 500 km) plus an established Eastern distribution network is a real accessibility advantage that management leans on when launching new products.
scores.quote: We already have a vast distribution set up, specifically in the Eastern India

scores.rationale: The mix is sensibly matched — roughly 60% B2B sold on LC/advance terms with tight working capital, alongside a deliberately growing branded B2C retail segment.
scores.quote: about 60% of our revenue was generated from B2B segment. Our strategic initiative to scale our presence in B2C segment is progressing well

scores.rationale: Advantages are conventional process/energy engineering (TRT turbines, sinter plants, captive power) available to any integrated mill, with no proprietary technology or R&D intensity claimed.
scores.quote: the plant has a 18 megawatt top gas pressure recovery turbine, which contributes 10% energy recovery

scores.rationale: A commodity metals manufacturer selling through distributors and B2B contracts has no two-sided network; nothing in five years of calls suggests any self-reinforcing user dynamic.

A dense Eastern India distribution and rural retail network — repeatedly cited as the reason volumes held up when peers fell 20-25% — is a genuine reach advantage, though not one rivals structurally cannot replicate.
scores.quote: we have never seen a very big slowdown in the rural sector, we have been able to penetrate and with the enhancing of our brand values

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex — Dahod locomotive plant, Aurangabad/Sambhajinagar bogie factory, traction motors, metro investments and 25 localized factories — that has converted into revenue doubling and margin expansion over five years.
scores.quote: We moved from only looking at being an electrification and signaling business in Mobility to expanding that into rolling stock... all of this required CapEx where the kick-in now on revenues and margins will come in.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the excerpts.
No disclosed R&D spend, but the Xcelerator/industrial-AI platform and localization engineering demonstrably converted into commercial references and new offerings.
scores.quote: two years ago, when we launched this, we had 125 individual cases... we've just taken a couple of these use cases and have been able to already win 200 references

scores.rationale: Only a small complementary bolt-on (Mass-Tech in e-mobility) that visibly lifted volumes, plus disciplined portfolio pruning via the Energy demerger and low-voltage motors sale — no large risky deals.
scores.quote: since we acquired the Mass-Tech company, it is really picked up in volumes as well over there

scores.rationale: The calls discuss cash generation and demerger but never dividends, buybacks or a distribution policy.

Revenue growth (~INR 200bn on a heavily factory-based footprint of 25 plants plus new rolling-stock capacity) implies a moderately asset-heavy, project-inclusive model rather than an asset-light one, though working capital discipline is evident.
scores.quote: Today the new company Siemens Limited... has 25 factories.

scores.rationale: Share is being captured in genuinely new segments (rolling stock, e-mobility, data centres), but the company is already dominant in its core electrification niches, limiting the remaining runway there.
scores.quote: one in three automation controllers, PLCs, in the country... are from Siemens. Over 75% of utilities distribution discoms are powered by Siemens switchgear.

scores.rationale: Expansion is via exports into the parent's global network rather than own overseas markets, but it is real and scaling — a INR 18bn multi-year bogie/traction export order and ~15-30% export share.
scores.quote: We have received an 18-billion order for the supply of bogies, traction motors, and gearboxes to the parent company... Our bogie factory in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is now part of the global network of factories

scores.rationale: FY24 margin gains came partly from mix and pricing, but by FY26 growth is order/volume-led and the company could not pass through commodity and FX cost inflation, showing limited pricing power.
scores.quote: we have seen price increases for material and purchase products from suppliers, which we couldn't completely pass on to the market

scores.rationale: Private capex was muted for three years and management is now reporting the first genuine upturn across traditional verticals — a classic near-bottom-of-cycle position with the recovery just starting.
scores.quote: We do not see a slowdown in private CapEx yet... we definitely see a real pickup in the last couple of months coming out of the private sector CapEx

scores.rationale: End markets — manufacturing's rise from 15% to 25% of GDP, energy transition, railway electrification/TCAS, data centres — are in multi-decade secular expansion and Siemens is positioned in all four government thrust areas.
scores.quote: you're looking at roughly double that element... 600 billion going up to $1.2 to $1.5 trillion of CapEx that is going to be required

scores.rationale: Organic-first strategy with only a tiny bolt-on, counter-cyclical Mobility investment made while private capex was muted, positive cash from operations of INR 21.6bn and no leverage-driven expansion.
scores.quote: we also have seen progress in our cash generation and finished the year with Cash from Operations of INR 21.6 billion

scores.rationale: The Mobility vision flagged in 2022 was executed tenaciously over four years to first contractual locomotive delivery with 90% localization, though independence is qualified by heavy parent dependence on product supply and transfer pricing.
scores.quote: by 31st of March, we delivered the first contractual... delivery dates of dispatching 40 locomotives from Dahod... We have been able to deliver over 90% localization in about 2 years

scores.rationale: Presentations are substance-heavy and operationally detailed with no personality cult, though the company does publicize its sustainability rankings and is a high-profile listed name.
scores.quote: our intent today is really to answer as many questions as we can that are on your mind

scores.rationale: Talent development and leadership pipeline are never discussed; headcount appears only as a cost line.

Management quantifies bad news precisely — 290bps EBITDA decline attributed to specific silver/copper/Euro moves — and openly admits demand weakness and inability to pass on costs rather than deflecting.
scores.quote: For silver, the price per kg went up from $1,000 to $2,700, an increase of 160%... private sector CapEx has not really picked up yet to the extent that we would have liked it to

scores.rationale: The five-year 'doubled revenues, tripled margins' record coincides with a public-capex boom, one very large locomotive order and parent technology, and the FY26 margin collapse on FX/commodities shows results are materially externally driven, not pure management skill.
scores.quote: We've doubled our revenues, tripled our margins, in almost every business.

scores.rationale: Entrenched installed-base positions plus long-dated captive service annuities (35-year locomotive maintenance) create monopoly-like standing in specific niches.
scores.quote: we will be delivering 1,200 locomotives over a period of 11 years... with a maintenance period of 35 years thereafter

scores.rationale: Automation/switchgear installed bases and embedded software create real switching costs and captive aftermarket, though not a regional monopoly.
scores.quote: there is embedded software in the products that we already deliver... Over 50% of the metros in the country are electrified by Siemens

scores.rationale: The market is a concentrated few-player field, but management itself describes tender dynamics where multiple bidders compete and the customer awards on lowest price, meaning end customers retain negotiating power.
scores.quote: customers come out with a tender, you get five companies that are bidding for those businesses and the lowest party wins

scores.rationale: Technology and localization requirements are real barriers, but L1 tender pricing and the inability to pass through input costs indicate pricing is not fully rational.
scores.quote: it is not about a product at a cheapest price, it is about delivering a solution... That is changing.

scores.rationale: No competitor is named or characterized as weak anywhere in the excerpts.
The opposite of under-the-radar — a large, heavily covered listed MNC holding in-person analyst meets, publicizing ESG rankings, with a widely tracked demerger.
scores.quote: We've also been recognized right now as being a leader in the area of governance and sustainability.

scores.rationale: The Siemens brand carries weight, but gross economics are thin and pricing power failed under input inflation — material cost rose to 74% of revenue and margins fell 290bps.
scores.quote: In quarter 2, the material cost was reported as 69% of revenue. And in quarter 6, the number went up to 74%.

scores.rationale: The customer proposition is explicitly reliability, execution certainty and mission-critical outcomes (FDA-traceable pharma batches, grid stability, cybersecurity) rather than price.
scores.quote: Customers right now are looking at flexibility, are looking at quality, are looking at speed, are looking at agility.

scores.rationale: Deep vertical know-how across 23 market verticals plus a nationwide sales-office and 25-factory footprint gives strong customer intimacy and accessibility.
scores.quote: We are present in 23 market verticals. We understand the process of manufacturing.

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/government and the pitch is correctly built on TCO (energy savings, throughput) and reliability with installed-base lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: we supply the variable frequency drives giving them 20% energy savings... we were able to bring them an average energy saving of around 13%

scores.rationale: A deep, multi-product stack spanning PLCs, DCS, digital twins, industrial edge, cybersecurity and industrial AI, integrated across segments into end-to-end offerings competitors struggle to match.
scores.quote: We in Siemens are very much into industrial metaverse, into industrial AI; we're probably the only company in the world that is actually having a platform on industrial AI

scores.rationale: Siemens Xcelerator is a genuine open ecosystem of partners, developers and a growing use-case marketplace, but it is still early and supporting rather than self-reinforcing at scale.
scores.quote: We are working here with an ecosystem of partners, developers, together with our customers as well... we are increasing the number of ecosystem partners

scores.rationale: An installed base and service/manufacturing reach rivals cannot replicate — most discoms, half the metros and a third of PLCs — in businesses where service and localization are decisive.
scores.quote: Over 75% of utilities distribution discoms are powered by Siemens switchgear. Over 50% of the metros in the country are electrified by Siemens.

scores.rationale: Land/BD spend is high, rising and funded almost entirely from internal accruals (₹5.7bn in 9M FY25, ₹6.7bn in 9M FY26) building a 21mn sq ft, ₹350-400bn GDV pipeline, but reported returns remain thin (PAT of only ₹40cr on ~₹20bn revenue in 9M FY25), so incremental ROIC is not yet demonstrated.
scores.quote: bulk of the business development has happened out of internal accruals

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend, brand-building budgets or their returns in any excerpt; only aggregate 'SG&A brokerage and taxes' is mentioned without breakdown.
scores.quote: close to 25%, 27% gone into SG&A brokerage and taxes

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or programme is discussed; product initiatives cited are third-party certifications and licensed earthquake technology, not in-house R&D.
scores.quote: we have recently entered in an agreement to use advanced earthquake safety technology

scores.rationale: No corporate M&A; only small, simple, complementary bolt-ons — land parcels in core micro-markets and buying out JDA partners' shares, which directly improves project economics.
scores.quote: about 1.8 million square foot was added by taking up one of our JDA partners share in this market

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is mentioned across the calls; capital is directed to land, construction and debt reduction instead.
The company deliberately churns land into launches quickly rather than land-banking, but the model is inherently capital-heavy (owned land, 42mn sq ft of inventory) with no protective moat around it.
scores.quote: our thesis of the company has always been to do a fast churn on inventory

scores.rationale: Presales compounded ~60% over three years to ₹128bn TTM with the company positioning itself as one of few large supply creators in its micro-markets — clear share capture with plenty of runway in a fragmented NCR market.
scores.quote: we've actually seen like a good close to 60% sales CAGR over the last 3 years

scores.rationale: Strategy is explicitly geography-concentrated in Gurugram/Sohna; the Delhi opportunity is acknowledged as policy-dependent and management itself calls it premature, and the two out-of-Gurgaon townships (Daxin, City of Colors) carry lower realisations.
scores.quote: it's a little premature to say how large will it become

scores.rationale: Growth is clearly pricing- and mix-led — realisation rose ₹4,000/sf (FY21) to ₹9,800 to ₹11,700 to ₹12,700 to ₹15,200/sf (+21% YoY) on a shift to mid-income Gurgaon product, even as units sold fell from ~3,500 (9M FY25) to ~1,700 (9M FY26).
scores.quote: INR15,200 per square foot of realization is about 20% higher vis-a-vis the previous year

scores.rationale: The company sits well past the bottom of the cycle — micro-market prices are up 98-151% over five years, launch supply has more than doubled YoY, and management describes demand as post-euphoric with price growth decelerating to single digits.
scores.quote: demand is steady but not euphoric... I expect price to move up in late single digits

scores.rationale: End market has genuine secular support — urbanisation, Gurugram's population projected to 55 lakh by 2041 and real estate projected to 20% of GDP by 2047 — though housing remains a cyclical, not permanently expanding, market.
scores.quote: projected by CREDAI and CareEdge to become a INR5 trillion to INR10 trillion market by 2047

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, prudently levered growth: net debt held at ~₹10bn for 2-3 years despite a 60% sales CAGR, land bought from operating surplus, explicit net-debt-to-surplus discipline and no large acquisitions.
scores.quote: we've been in this range for the last 2 to 3 years, despite the growth being done by the company

scores.rationale: Strategy has been unchanged and repeatedly executed across ten calls — sustained supply creation in three chosen Gurugram micro-markets — though FY26 guidance (₹125bn presales vs ₹67bn at 9M) shows targets are stretched.
scores.quote: our strategy for coming years is going to remain similar to address this mid-income housing market

scores.rationale: Communication is largely operational and promoter-family run, but management devotes airtime to macro cheerleading and stock-price performance, which cuts against a pure substance-over-profile posture.
scores.quote: we have almost delivered about, you know, 50% sort of returns on the stock

scores.rationale: No talent-development or succession discussion at all, and the record shows three CFOs across FY2024-FY2025 (Gaurav Malik and Manish Garg exiting) with leadership concentrated in the Aggarwal family; execution capability is being bought in externally rather than built.
scores.quote: we've also now onboarded Bain & Company, which will further help us in improving construction-related efficiency

scores.rationale: Management consistently discloses shortfalls and rationale unprompted — guidance gaps, weather-hit completions, unsold-inventory breakdown including blocked floors, and misgivings about the quality of the order book during the boom.
scores.quote: it was a little scary because we weren't sure the quality of book which was getting created

scores.rationale: Headline presales growth is hard to separate from a market-wide Gurugram price boom (Dwarka Expressway +98%, Sohna +151%), while reported profitability has been weak (₹40cr PAT in 9M FY25, EBITDA 12% on recognised revenue) — results flatter the skill assessment.
scores.quote: the GP margin was at 27%, EBITDA was at 12%

scores.rationale: The company holds a strong position in specific micro-markets as one of few large supply creators, but faces full competition from branded NCR developers and has no aftermarket or mind-monopoly position.
scores.quote: we are amongst few large supply creators in the Sector 71 market

scores.rationale: Regional quasi-monopoly economics in chosen micro-markets via contiguous owned land (92+ acres in Sector 71, 18.5mn sq ft potential) that rivals cannot replicate there, though a home purchase carries no switching costs.
scores.quote: we have access to about 92 acres plus land, which is mostly owned by the company

scores.rationale: Gurugram residential is a fragmented, supply-competitive market — NCR launches rose 39% QoQ and more than doubled YoY — and the buyer has ample choice and negotiating power.
scores.quote: New housing launches rose by 39% over the previous quarter and more than doubled compared to the same period of last year

scores.rationale: RERA and land/approval complexity favour branded incumbents, but supply is surging and the company itself prices defensively to drive volume, indicating limited pricing rationality in the segment.
scores.quote: we try to stay as competitive on the product pricing as possible

scores.rationale: Management identifies a shortage of credible branded supply in mid-income NCR housing, implying weaker unbranded local developers from whom share can be taken.
scores.quote: which is definitely starved in terms of good quality developments and coming from branded developers

scores.rationale: The company is a recently IPO'd, brokerage-covered stock in India's most watched housing micro-market with active FII interest and IFC as a lender — the opposite of a capital-ignored niche.
scores.quote: There has been very good support from the foreign institutional investors

scores.rationale: The brand supports realisations and customer confidence and gross margins have improved to ~31% (40% in Q3 FY26), but pricing is set competitively rather than on image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: coming from a very strong brand, a very well-established company... has been giving a lot of confidence to the customers

scores.rationale: The core proposition is delivery certainty — 16mn sq ft delivered, tier-1 contractors (Ahluwalia, Capacit'e, ACC), Bain engaged for on-time completion, ISO/IGBC/EDGE certifications and earthquake-safety technology — with buyers paying for trust in completion.
scores.quote: the precise mandate, which we've given to Bain & Company... so that these projects get completed in a timely manner

scores.rationale: A strong distribution/channel network and construction-linked payment plans give direct customer access and quick sell-through (80%+ of launched GDV sold), though no unique accessibility advantage is evidenced.
scores.quote: a very well-established company with strong distribution network

scores.rationale: Customers are retail end-users and the company matches them appropriately with brand, ticket-size engineering and assurance of delivery rather than corporate TCO arguments.
scores.quote: We are now launching projects with starting apartment sizes about 1,800-odd square foot... to ensure that the ticket size remains attractive

scores.rationale: There is no proprietary technology edge; construction is outsourced to third-party contractors and safety technology is licensed in under an agreement rather than developed.
scores.quote: we recently entered in an agreement to use advanced earthquake safety technology

scores.rationale: The build-to-sell housing model described across all calls is a one-off transaction business with no two-sided platform or self-reinforcing scale effect anywhere in evidence.
scores.quote: by and large, we are sticking to a strategy of mid-income housing, working on a build-to-sell model

scores.rationale: Sustained multi-project supply across three micro-markets plus a strong broker/distribution network drives fast sell-through (80%+ of ₹234bn launched GDV sold), but this reach is replicable by other large NCR developers.
scores.quote: effectively 80% plus sales have been achieved

scores.rationale: Growth capex is large and sustained (₹8,000cr in FY22 rising to ₹7,500–8,000cr/yr in FY26) but incremental returns are poor — PAT crept from ₹970cr to ₹1,008cr while SGEL lost ₹258cr, Buxar lost ₹92cr and ₹174cr of impairments were booked.
scores.quote: for this year the total capex which we have kept is around INR7,500 crore... the revenue of SGEL was INR 510 crores... That translates to a loss of INR 258 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the excerpted calls.
No R&D spend, programme or new-product pipeline discussed in any call.
Inorganic activity is limited to greenfield JVs with state utilities (Assam APDCL, MAHAGENCO) rather than bolt-on acquisitions, so there is no acquiree-quality or post-deal OPM evidence either way.
scores.quote: formed a joint venture named SGEL Assam Renewable Energy Limited with Assam Power Distribution Company Limited for execution of 1,000 megawatt renewable energy projects

scores.rationale: A routine PSU dividend policy (₹1.50/share for FY26, interim plus final) with no buybacks, and equity issuance (SGEL QIP) was contemplated rather than capital return.
scores.quote: total dividend at the rate of 15%, Rs.1.5 per equity share... we are planning to have some QIP in the current year

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy: FY26 revenue of ₹3,545cr sits on a ~₹30,000cr debt-funded asset base, with ₹7,000cr capitalised for a single Buxar unit earning ₹522cr.
scores.quote: we are at INR30,000 crore odd total for now... The capitalized cost of Unit-1 is around 7,000 crores

scores.rationale: Installed capacity nearly doubled from 2,377 MW (FY24) to 4,196 MW (FY26) with a 3,926 MW pipeline and a 16 GW REIA award mandate, so real capacity share is being added off a small base.
scores.quote: the total installed capacity of SJVNL stands at 4196 megawatts

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-state and cross-border expansion (Bihar, Gujarat, Assam, Rajasthan, UP, Nepal) but execution has been weak — Arun-3 slipped from June 2023 to December 2028.
scores.quote: we have a plan to commission the entire plant, all the four units, by December '28

scores.rationale: Growth is purely volume/capacity-led at administered or bid-determined tariffs, and the mix is deteriorating toward ~₹2.60 solar and loss-making thermal versus high-margin regulated hydro.
scores.quote: Average tariff is around INR2.60 paisa for these all the solar grids... there is a decrease in the tariff with the subsequent bids

scores.rationale: The RE bidding cycle appears past its peak, not near a bottom — tender supply exceeds DISCOM demand and only 25–30% of awarded capacity has been tied up in PSAs.
scores.quote: there are a lot of tenders which came out simultaneously in the market. And the demand is not that much... all have almost signed 25% to 30% of their capacity

scores.rationale: The Indian power/renewables end market is in secular expansion (500 GW by 2030 target, PM-Surya Ghar), though near-term DISCOM offtake for RE is proving constrained.
scores.quote: listed as one of the Renewable Energy Implementing Agency by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy to contribute towards nation's ambitious 500 gigawatt renewable energy target by 2030

scores.rationale: Leverage has ballooned to ~₹30,000cr against a ₹3,545cr revenue base, ECB of $300m was left entirely unhedged, and repeated impairments (₹138cr FY24, ₹174cr FY26) show capital committed without return discipline.
scores.quote: It is entirely unhedged, but we are keeping a close watch on the movement of the dollar price

scores.rationale: Four chairmen in five years including three-month stopgap charges, with targets set as GoI MoU obligations rather than independently chosen — and the 12,000 MW-by-March-2026 vision delivered only 4,196 MW.
scores.quote: we are seeing the appointment of CMD not for the years like for 4 years or 5 years. It has been going on for 3 months

scores.rationale: Calls lean heavily on Prime Ministerial inaugurations, foundation stones and award citations rather than operating substance.
scores.quote: Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated Unit 1... SJVN Limited received the prestigious SCOPE Eminence Award

scores.rationale: An HR award is cited but the leadership pipeline is externally controlled and unstable — CMD posts filled by three-month additional charge pending government orders.
scores.quote: this charge has been given for the 3 months, and we are expecting within 3 months the regular appointment order will be issued from the Minister of Power

scores.rationale: Management explains impairments, PLF shortfalls and revenue misses openly and concedes analyst criticism, but has serially reiterated commissioning targets that slipped by years without owning the forecasting failure.
scores.quote: You are true, you are very true, you are very right what you are asking actually... due to one or the other reason, which is like unavoidable, which is beyond the control of the SJVNL

scores.rationale: Reported profit is driven by regulated tariff true-ups and government-allocated mandates rather than managerial skill — FY26 revenue growth came largely from a ₹679cr prior-period truing-up order while operating delivery slipped.
scores.quote: primarily driven by recognition of earlier year sales amounting to INR 679 crores pursuant to truing up tariff order

scores.rationale: Regulated hydro stations enjoy assured cost-plus offtake, but there is no monopoly in the customer's mind and no aftermarket/services franchise; DISCOMs curtail its thermal output at will.
scores.quote: there was not much demand and the power was being curtailed down by the beneficiary

scores.rationale: Long-dated 25-year PPAs and CERC cost-plus regulation on hydro create captive, locked-in offtake once a plant is built.
scores.quote: SJVN signed power purchase agreement with Punjab State Power Corporation Limited for 400-megawatt solar project for 25 years

scores.rationale: It competes with NTPC, NHPC and SECI in open competitive bidding while the end customers (DISCOMs) hold all negotiating power and simply decline to sign PSAs.
scores.quote: not only SJVNL, NHAI, SECI and NTPC. So, all have this issue that all have almost signed 25% to 30% of their capacity

scores.rationale: Solar bidding shows classic irrational price competition with tariffs falling bid after bid, and SJVN itself had to accept a ₹2.43 PPA against a ₹3+ expectation, triggering impairment.
scores.quote: there is a decrease in the, like this bid which they have, like tariff, decrease in the tariff with the subsequent bids which have come in the market

scores.rationale: Its competitors are the strongest players in the sector (NTPC, SECI, NHPC) rather than weak share-donors, and SJVN itself is the one impairing assets and slipping schedules.
scores.quote: not only SJVNL, NHAI, SECI and NTPC

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar: a listed Navratna CPSE whose projects are inaugurated by the Prime Minister and whose sector is the focus of national capital allocation.
scores.quote: Honorable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji virtually laid the foundation stone for the 200 megawatt solar power project

scores.rationale: Electricity is a pure commodity sold at regulator- or auction-set tariffs (₹2.45 CPSU cap, ₹2.88, ₹2.60 average), leaving zero image- or taste-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: that is fixed by the Government of India, that is under CPSE scheme. The maximum is INR2.45 per unit

scores.rationale: Reliability is the product, but SJVN has repeatedly failed on it — design energy shortfalls, plant shutdowns in floods, and PAF-based incentives at minus 23% for FY26 and minus 40% in Q4.
scores.quote: Then PAF, it is minus 23 and the deviation charges are minus 3%... PAF-based incentive is minus 40

scores.rationale: No accessibility or customer-intimacy advantage — offtake is bureaucratic PPA/PSA signing, and even power evacuation depends on transmission lines it cannot get built.
scores.quote: this only issue in transmission line is the land acquisition, and we are constantly in touch with the even higher offices of Nepal Ministry

scores.rationale: It sells to corporate/state DISCOM buyers where lock-in exists only via signed PPAs, but those buyers dictate configuration, curtail dispatch and refuse to sign the bulk of awarded capacity.
scores.quote: there is a possibility that all the PPAs may not be done... that configuration which was there in the tender may not be required by the DISCOM

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology — projects are executed through awarded EPC contracts and the company was even stalled by inability to source domestic solar panels.
scores.quote: SJVN also awarded an EPC contract of 1,000-megawatt solar project in Bikaner... we were facing some problem with the panels, local domestic panels

scores.rationale: A generation asset business with no two-sided network; scale brings depreciation and interest, not self-reinforcing advantage.
scores.quote: Because new projects have been commissioned, that's why the depreciation also, the finance cost has increased. However... revenue has not increased correspondingly

scores.rationale: Government-conferred channel roles (REIA mandate, PM-Surya Ghar in three states, 18 ministries) give privileged access, but this is allocated rather than built and only two transmission lines are owned.
scores.quote: SJVN has been allotted three states, namely Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Arunachal Pradesh... 18 ministries have also been allocated to us

scores.rationale: Capex has stepped up from the historical INR100-150cr/yr run-rate to a stated INR500cr programme over FY26-28 with new Haridwar and Pune lines for localisation, but incremental returns are unproven as PBT margin guidance fell to 11-12%.
scores.quote: from '26 to '28, we have around INR 500 crores investment, which will go through each year

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.
An in-house engineering centre feeds new products (Hub-3, sprockets, EV motor and insulated high-speed bearings) with design wins booked out to 2030, though R&D spend efficiency is never quantified.
scores.quote: we have an engineering center in India which is anyway working on product developments for these new product

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the excerpts; the only corporate action is a demerger, not a bolt-on purchase.
Buybacks, dividend policy and distribution philosophy are never discussed in the excerpts.

Roughly INR200cr annual capex against ~INR2,030cr automotive sales plus a meaningful traded-goods component makes it neither notably asset-light nor heavy, and the moat is being tested by new localised competitor capacity.
scores.quote: we're seeing new capacity is coming up from the competition on localizing SRB, CRBs

scores.rationale: Consistent evidence of share capture — 2-wheeler gains at Bajaj and Honda, ~50% share in EV 2-wheelers, railway class E/K approvals opening freight wagons — though FY26 aftermarket share was defended with discounts.
scores.quote: we continue to gain market share with customers like Bajaj and Honda

scores.rationale: Exports have shrunk from ~10% to ~8% of sales and management explicitly deprioritises overseas customers in favour of domestic demand, so there is no credible geographic expansion.
scores.quote: India for India, our focus is first to serve our domestic customers

scores.rationale: Growth in FY25 and FY26 was explicitly volume-led rather than price/mix-led, with aftermarket net sales falling on discounts and price pass-through lagging steel inflation.
scores.quote: Primarily quarter-on-quarter and annual growth was driven by volumes

scores.rationale: Macro indicators (IIP, PMI, auto and steel production) are improving off a soft patch and margins are at a trough, but management gives no evidence of a clear cycle bottom with an identified upturn.
scores.quote: IIP growth since last 3 quarters has been stable and was 4.1% for Q4 2026

scores.rationale: End markets include genuinely secular drivers — EV transition, renewables, railway wagon expansion and infrastructure — offset by lower bearing content per EV.
scores.quote: the number of bearings in EV are less than ICE engine

scores.rationale: Growth is organic with no acquisitions, capex is self-funded and the demerger simplifies rather than levers the business, though the split itself absorbed one-off costs and management attention.
scores.quote: we typically do about 100 to 150 Crores of capex every year

scores.rationale: The company is a Swedish-parent subsidiary whose economics are set by group transfer pricing, and the flagship localisation ambition set in 2022 was still stuck at ~40% for industrial in 2025.
scores.quote: has localization moved at the pace we would have liked to over the past few years, no

scores.rationale: Communication is technical, plain and product-focused, with no promotional or celebrity-CEO framing across four years of calls.
scores.quote: The purpose of today's call is to purely educate and bring awareness about the company's fundamental business

scores.rationale: Three managing directors and repeated CFO turnover including an interim CFO within five years signal a weak internal pipeline, and talent development is never discussed.
scores.quote: MS. AASHI ARORA – INTERIM CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

scores.rationale: Management openly admitted the localisation shortfall and gave an unusually detailed FEMA/transfer-pricing explanation of margin swings, though FY26 disclosure narrowed and leaned heavily on 'one-off' framing.
scores.quote: we cannot go and recover that by issuing a debit note to a supplier

scores.rationale: Historically flattering ~20% margins were partly an unrepeatable transfer-pricing retention rather than operating skill, and normalised guidance of 11-12% PBT reveals the gap between results and underlying capability.
scores.quote: as a company, we landed up retaining a higher margin

scores.rationale: The SKF name carries real aftermarket recall, but pricing has to be defended with discounts, which is inconsistent with a monopoly-like position in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: because of the discounts we offered to remain in the market and to beat the competition

scores.rationale: Automotive OEM designs-in create genuine switching costs with long sales cycles and an order book running to 2030.
scores.quote: it's a longer sales cycle, but the solutions are sticky

scores.rationale: Bearings is structurally a few-player industry and OEM contracts allow steel-cost pass-through, but pass-through is slow and only partially secured, showing customers retain negotiating power.
scores.quote: we have taken only from a couple of customers and similar discussions are happening

scores.rationale: Competitors are adding localised SRB/CRB capacity and SKF is discounting in the aftermarket, evidence of eroding barriers and less rational pricing.
scores.quote: do you think immediately you might see some pressure on either market share or pricing

scores.rationale: Approvals in railway freight and direct OEM onboarding let SKF take share from legacy incumbents and imports.
scores.quote: to make sure that SK bearing also get purchased along with their legacy players

scores.rationale: SKF India is a widely covered listed multinational subsidiary followed by multiple institutional analysts, the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the line of Krupashankar NJ from Avendus Spark

scores.rationale: There is some brand-based pull in the aftermarket, but gross margins have contracted and demand had to be held with discounts, so pricing power from image is limited.
scores.quote: gross margin have seen a contraction by around 600 bps Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and performance — evidenced by delivery and sustainability awards from TVS, Honda and Suzuki and premium technical bearings commanding multiples of standard pricing.
scores.quote: in recognition of the top of the line excellent delivery performance

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is a stated growth engine, with continuous onboarding of industrial part sellers and authorised distributors improving end-customer access.
scores.quote: our reach to our end customers are getting better

scores.rationale: The model correctly matches benefits — sticky, design-in reliability for OEM corporates and brand/availability for the retail aftermarket channel — spanning roughly two-thirds OE and one-fifth distribution.
scores.quote: original equipment manufacturers accounted for about two-third of our sales

scores.rationale: A multi-product technical edge in high-performance and EV-specific bearings (insulation, high-speed, hub units) delivers measurable customer benefit and forward design wins.
scores.quote: the motor bearings and also the electric insulation, high-speed bearings

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts.
An established retail and industrial distribution network gives it market access rivals cannot easily replicate, which management used to launch entirely new aftermarket product lines.
scores.quote: we already have access to the retail market where these will also get sold in addition to bearings

scores.rationale: A clearly growth-oriented INR 800 crore+ capex programme through FY30 for a new Pune plant and new DGBB/TRB channels, plus a low-cost debottlenecking that lifted capacity ~48% while cutting cost 18%, though management concedes the added depreciation will drag margins until FY30.
scores.quote: we are looking at doing a capex spend of around INR 800 crores plus, which includes a significant chunk of investment on the new Pune plant

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend anywhere in the call.

No R&D spend is disclosed, but there is repeated evidence of application engineering converting into orders — a platform-stage co-designed tractor bearing worth INR 32.5 crore, a unitized rail bearing raising axle load and service interval, and 'two or three more product lines' added per quarter.
scores.quote: almost every quarter two or three more product lines are added

scores.rationale: The only corporate action discussed is the demerger from SKF India Limited; no acquisitions are mentioned.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed on the call.

This is an asset-heavy bearings manufacturer committing INR 800 crore of plant and machinery and carrying net working capital guided at 19%-20% of sales, so the moat does not come with asset-light economics.
scores.quote: plant and machinery, plant and machinery, basically to add more capacity

scores.rationale: Management explicitly states it is re-entering wind, railway freight and agricultural tractor segments it had previously exited and is winning share on the back of localization, with wind up 91% QoQ.
scores.quote: So, we are winning more share, but if you compare it to it comes at the cost of some amount of margin

scores.rationale: Exports are only ~6% of FY26 sales and, while Europe and Southeast Asia performed well, the strategy is explicitly India-for-India localization with global markets largely served by the parent's other factories.
scores.quote: Exports also performed well, primarily exports to Europe and some Southeast Asian countries

scores.rationale: Growth was volume-led with adverse mix — lower-margin OEM sales rose from 46% to 50% and dragged PBT from 13.1% to 11.5% — while pricing actions are purely cost pass-through of FX and steel inflation, not pricing power.
scores.quote: the biggest reason was the mix change. Our OEM business grew significantly and as a result, the mix of lower margin OEM business compared to higher margin distribution business accounted for most of this drop

scores.rationale: The macro data cited — 6.5% GDP, 4.5% IIP, 6.6% construction and 9.7% iron and steel growth — points to a mid-cycle expansion already underway rather than a company positioned near a cyclical bottom.
scores.quote: construction growth was 6.6% and iron and steel production was 9.7% year-on-year

scores.rationale: Core end-markets are in secular expansion — India described as the fastest growing wind market, rail modernization toward Vande Bharat speeds, and emerging data-centre chiller/compressor demand for hybrid bearings.
scores.quote: Wind is primarily India, actually. India is now the fastest growing wind market

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth funded by internal capex with no M&A, a 2.8% QoQ working capital reduction, and the discipline to hold back shipments to distributors with overdue payments even at the cost of segment revenue.
scores.quote: we made some corrections to distributors whose payments were outstanding. So, we shifted volume from them to other distributors, but also held back on some shipments

scores.rationale: There is a clear long-horizon plan — ACES strategy through 2028, plant commissioning end-CY28, a margin roadmap to FY30 — but independence is limited given royalty/trademark payments, transfer-pricing charges and reliance on the Swedish parent's factories and technology.
scores.quote: We call our strategy, the ACES strategy, and our strategy is defined through to 2028

scores.rationale: A short, data-dense 45-minute call led by the MD and CFO with slide-by-slide operational detail and no promotional framing beyond routine credit to the team.
scores.quote: I will go through the presentation which has been shared with each one with all of you

scores.rationale: Management proactively stripped out one-off demerger costs both ways, named the exact drivers of the margin decline, disclosed the distributor receivable problem, and pushed back on an analyst's higher margin hopes rather than accepting them.
scores.quote: our aspiration is to get to 16% to 18%, but right now up to 2030... we have been conservative here in saying we are going to get to around 15%. More increase is possible, but we can't commit to it right now

scores.rationale: The assessment is not yet robust to halo — the only reported comparison is QoQ because year-on-year figures rest on extracted, assumption-laden carve-out accounts, so a single quarter's 'solid' result cannot be separated from parent brand, parent technology and demerger optics.
scores.quote: has been extracted and may involve some assumptions by the management from the financial information of SKF India Limited

scores.rationale: The higher-margin distribution/aftermarket channel (35% of FY26 sales) is the profit engine, and management explicitly frames low-margin OEM design-ins as the route to owning the subsequent aftermarket.
scores.quote: though it comes at a lower margin as you'll see in the subsequent slides, helps us in long-term aftermarket business and that will improve our margin also

scores.rationale: Designing customer-specific bearings from the platform stage and delivering integrated unitized bearing-housing-seal assemblies creates real specification lock-in and switching costs at OEMs.
scores.quote: SKF Industrial worked right from the platform design stage... and created a customer-specific offering which included our tapered roller bearings and our cylindrical roller bearings

scores.rationale: Bearings is a concentrated global industry, but management describes intense competition and difficult OEM negotiations on price, indicating end customers retain meaningful negotiating power.
scores.quote: it is a competitive environment and we do face lots of competition. So, while as the especially at the OEMs, I think the competition is intense

scores.rationale: Technical qualification barriers exist, but pricing is not comfortably rational — the company had earlier exited low-margin wind and freight rail business on affordability grounds and can only 'hope' to pass on FX and cost escalation to OEMs.
scores.quote: Obviously, with OEMs, it might be it's a little tougher, those are tougher negotiations. We are hoping to pass on most of it

scores.rationale: Share is being reclaimed mainly from imports and from the company's own prior exits via localization, with no identified weak competitor donating share.
scores.quote: there are many areas, even the agricultural tractor business, some of it was we exited and now we are getting back into it due to localization

scores.rationale: This is a newly listed arm of a well-known multinational brand, covered on the call by institutional analysts from Anand Rathi, SiMPL and Avendus Spark — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We'll take our first question from the line of Mumuksh Mandlesha from Anand Rathi Institutional Equities
