scores.rationale: Debt-averse, no large M&A, funded growth from internal accruals, and monetized every legacy asset without a haircut while peers in infra failed.
scores.quote: the company has successfully monetized its all renewable power assets and transmission assets, thereby garnering a cash surplus of INR1,500 crores and not in a single asset we had to see haircut

scores.rationale: Four decades of independent, conservative operation through a dead sector cycle, holding cash and capability until the upturn — explicitly acknowledged by long-term investors on the call.
scores.quote: you are one of the few people I know in the power sector who have generated real positive cash flow in such a troubled time

scores.rationale: Substance-oriented, conservative reputation with a small IR footprint, though the MD does volunteer bold headline aspirations (INR10,000cr topline, EPS targets) that lean promotional.
scores.quote: image of our company, Guptaji, is generally that we are conservative

scores.rationale: Deliberate capability build — Delhi office tripled, recruitment across IT/DC/transmission, upskilling and a digitization drive, plus visible succession grooming of Ankit Saraiya taking the data-centre vertical.
scores.quote: A lot of people are under recruitment on the IT side, data center side as well as on the transmission, smart metering.

scores.rationale: Delays and policy setbacks are disclosed plainly, but repeated optimistic guidance has slipped without being owned (Chennai DC from June-2023 to Aug-2025; DC revenue guided ~INR100cr then cut to ~INR25cr) and EPS targets are defended rather than reset.
scores.quote: Despite facing delays due to regulatory and permissions, approvals, et cetera, supply chain disruption, we have successfully now completed the first phase

scores.rationale: Much of the 4x revenue jump coincides with a sector-wide, policy-driven capex boom, and the newer DC bets remain unproven, so results should not be read as pure managerial skill despite the strong balance-sheet record.
scores.quote: This year it is almost double of last year and next year again it will be no less than 70%, 80% of this year

scores.rationale: Claims a leading position in high-end grid solutions but the business is won through open competitive tenders, with no monopoly in the customer's mind or captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: battery storage solutions where Techno enjoys a market-leading position

scores.rationale: TBCB transmission concessions and AMISP metering contracts create long-dated, regionally exclusive annuity positions with recurring O&M lock-in, even though the core EPC has no switching costs.
scores.quote: high-margin recurring O&M scope under TOTEX model

scores.rationale: Customers are monopsony-like utilities (PowerGrid, SEBs, state DISCOMs) awarding work on L1 competitive bidding, so the end customer holds the negotiating power.
scores.quote: We are further L1 in orders and also in advanced stage of order receipt for worth INR720 crores.

scores.rationale: Genuine qualification barriers exist in 765kV/GIS/STATCOM/HVDC work, but pricing in adjacent segments has turned irrational enough that the company is withdrawing from bidding.
scores.quote: given the recent pressure on margins in new tenders, we have adopted a selective bidding approach and are not pursuing additional projects at this stage

scores.rationale: Weak, counterparty-impaired infra peers (IL&FS-type failures) and consistently lower peer margins leave share available to a debt-free, cash-rich player.
scores.quote: Techno has been able to garner better operating margins consistently over the years in this phase compared to its peers.

scores.rationale: No longer under the radar — the company actively courted FIIs and mutual funds via a INR1,250cr QIP and operates in the most crowded themes in the market (power capex, AI data centres).
scores.quote: we are likely to go for a QIP of INR1,250 crores but mainly, we would like to engage with large FII FPIs and mutual funds

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are contractually capped in a narrow 13–15% EBITDA band typical of project EPC, and value comes from cost/schedule efficiency not brand.
scores.quote: A compressed schedule increases the productivity of the resources deployed

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty of on-time, quality delivery — 400+ projects delivered, 17 commissionings in a year, preferred-vendor status with the largest grid owners — though price is still set by competitive bidding.
scores.quote: you are a preferred supplier or vendor to Power Grid, Adani, Sterlite, IndiGrid or anybody as far as station is concerned

scores.rationale: Some deliberate reach-building (expanded Delhi office, channel partners and distribution network for data centres) but no evidence of a differentiated sales force or customer-intimacy advantage.
scores.quote: we are onboarding global channel partners for distribution and establishing an extensive distribution network within India

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to a corporate/PSU customer base — reliability and schedule certainty for utilities, plus concession-based lock-in in metering and TBCB assets.
scores.quote: They don't trust our type of firms to do jobs in time, quality jobs in time, create sustainable value accretive assets.

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product high-end engineering edge (765kV AIS/GIS, STATCOM, VSC-HVDC, BESS, high-density DC design) but it is applied engineering capability with no disclosed R&D intensity.
scores.quote: our data centers, especially the Chennai data center is natively designed for high-density power delivery on per rack basis

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business is self-reinforcing with scale — projects are won one tender at a time and the RailTel edge network is a contracted rollout, not a two-sided network.
scores.quote: We have secured a concession from RailTel to build 100 edge data centers

scores.rationale: Nationwide execution and service reach few EPC rivals match — 17 commissionings in a year, 20+ substations countrywide including extreme-altitude Ladakh sites, and 100 edge sites across Tier 2/3 India.
scores.quote: we have successfully commissioned projects at 17 locations all over the country

scores.rationale: Growth capex is real and sizeable (~$30mn consumables programme, Chile greenfield plus INR21cr extra land) but commissioning slipped from June 2025 to early Q3 FY27 while consumables revenue went flat, so incremental ROIC is unproven.
scores.quote: we have a capex plan of about $30 million overall in the consumable business segment

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the excerpts.

R&D has produced a genuine winner in DynaPrime (revenue up 157% YoY in Q1FY23, claimed segment leadership vs Metso) and continued R&D/innovation investment is cited, but spend and efficiency are never quantified.
scores.quote: We do invest into R&D and lot of proposals and products are under evaluation

scores.rationale: Tega McNally was a slow distressed turnaround (18-24 months to integrate) and Molycop is the opposite of a bolt-on — roughly 7x Tega's revenue, growing ~1-3% at ~12% EBITDA (dilutive to Tega's 22%), funded with $838mn assumed debt plus INR1,500cr parent debt and INR83.9cr of one-off costs.
scores.quote: we'll be adding close to $838 million of debt in our financial as of first of June

scores.rationale: Excerpts discuss capital raising (equity plus debt for Molycop) but are silent on dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy.

The moat is visible in a durable ~60% gross margin, but the business is not asset-light — multi-country plants, a multi-year Chile greenfield and rising inventory/FG builds keep asset turn ordinary (~1x on INR1,774cr revenue).
scores.quote: We have maintained healthy gross margin of 60% at the group level

scores.rationale: Long runway with a small base in a billion-dollar liner market and presence in all top-40 miners, and management denies share loss, but the last three years show conversions slipping rather than measurable share capture.
scores.quote: there is a huge growth prospect going there and we are in present in all the top 40 miners of the world

scores.rationale: Credible multi-region build-out — Chile plant, a six-year European contract generating ~INR10cr/month executed successfully, and advanced trials in Europe/LATAM/Australia — though the Chile commissioning has slipped repeatedly.
scores.quote: We are also making good progress in expanding across Europe, Latin America, and Australia with customer trials and negotiations at advanced stages

scores.rationale: Growth has been volume-led with pricing acting only as a lagged cost pass-through rather than pricing power; the pass-through is explicitly framed as cost recovery with a quarter's lag.
scores.quote: we take increase of around 13% to 14% of price side and the volume is about 30%

scores.rationale: Positioned ahead of an identifiable mining capex upturn — constrained copper/gold supply, record gold demand and miners ramping exploration — although the last two years have been the flattish part of the cycle for Tega.
scores.quote: This surge in outlook has prompted mining companies to ramp up exploration and production

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion on independent data: copper demand +40% by 2040 needing ~80 new mines and >$250bn investment, gold demand at record levels with ~1% supply growth, and falling ore grades mean more tonnes milled per unit metal.
scores.quote: UNCTAD projects copper demand to increase by over 40% by 2040

scores.rationale: Stewardship broke the organic/prudent-leverage test with a transformational, heavily levered acquisition roughly seven times Tega's revenue, funded by INR1,500cr new parent debt plus $838mn assumed debt and a INR2,000cr equity raise, with deleveraging pushed out 3-4 years.
scores.quote: our very primary focus will be to bring down the debt in the next 3 years to a level wherein 3x of leverage

scores.rationale: Tenacity is evident — DynaPrime scaled from a standing start, the McNally turnaround delivered PBT margin 4%→8%, and the Chile project was pushed through delays — but repeatedly reaffirming a 15% CAGR after three years of 10%/11%/flat consumables looks more stubborn than independent.
scores.quote: we remain firm on our guidance of 15% plus on a long-term basis

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key, substance-focused calls over 17 quarters — operating detail, ore-mix and logistics explanations, no celebrity positioning by the promoter-MD.

Positive signals on engagement, a dedicated CEO for Tega McNally and a 'strong talent base', but the finance seat has churned three times in five years and the company entered its largest-ever acquisition with an interim CFO.
scores.quote: MR. SHYAMA PRASAD GANGULY – INTERIM CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

scores.rationale: Disclosure is detailed and one-offs are quantified (INR6cr labour code, INR775mn Molycop costs, ~$30mn more to come), but misses are habitually explained as timing/spillover and guidance was never reset — Q3 guided ~8% consumables growth ended flat three months later.
scores.quote: It has just been a time lag where some of the volumes have moved from one quarter to the other

scores.rationale: Early margin expansion owed much to logistics normalisation, cost pass-through and quarter spillovers rather than durable skill, and an analyst's tally of 10%/11%/flat consumables against a repeated 15% promise shows results diverging from the narrative.
scores.quote: management keeps guiding 15%, but consistently, Consumable segment has been weaker

scores.rationale: DynaPrime holds a leadership niche in composite mill liners and the installed base creates an aftermarket-like consumable annuity, though Metso remains a credible global rival.
scores.quote: on some of the fronts, including DynaPrime, we are the leaders in that segment

scores.rationale: Once a mill is converted, the liner supplier is effectively locked in via the recurring spares stream, giving a captive-aftermarket character to most of consumables revenue.
scores.quote: our sustainable spares business, which is a repeat business, has come back very strong

scores.rationale: The global liner market is concentrated (Metso the principal competitor), but the end customers are large mining houses with real negotiating power — Tega can only pass costs with a quarter's lag and saw orders deferred at customers' discretion.
scores.quote: Metso is our major competitor globally

scores.rationale: Rational pricing and high entry barriers are visible in a 57-60% gross margin band held through commodity volatility with no mention of discounting or new entrants, alongside stable promoter control.
scores.quote: we generally operate in a gross margins of 57% to 60%

scores.rationale: Share is taken by converting mills off legacy metallic liners, and the acquisition of the weak McNally Sayaji equipment franchise (revenue 183→206) is share bought from a donator, but the main rival Metso is not weak.
scores.quote: some of the initiatives on conversions of new customers

scores.rationale: Mining consumables is an unglamorous, capital-light-of-attention niche that Tega has quietly compounded in, though the Molycop deal and analyst coverage now put it firmly on the radar.
Gross margin near 60% is high, but the pull is engineering performance for industrial buyers, not image or taste, and pricing follows input costs rather than brand power.
scores.quote: our gross margins remained healthy at around 60% of revenue

scores.rationale: Customers buy uptime certainty — Tega pre-built inventory and rerouted supply through COVID and the Red Sea disruption without a single supply failure, and won a six-year European contract on proven reliability.
scores.quote: we have not failed any of the supply to any of our customer worldwide

scores.rationale: Localised manufacturing beside mining regions (Chile, South Africa, India), on-site service income and a dedicated business-development function give proximity and customer intimacy rivals must ship in from afar.
scores.quote: Our localized manufacturing footprint, supportive commodity environment, strong talent base

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to a corporate customer base — TCO through lower power consumption, reliability of supply and switching-cost lock-in via the spares annuity rather than consumer-style intangibles.
scores.quote: The customer is very happy and satisfied with our progress we have done so far

scores.rationale: DynaPrime is a genuine technical edge claimed at parity or better versus Metso with quantifiable customer benefit in power and carbon reduction, but R&D intensity is never disclosed and the product portfolio is narrow.
scores.quote: our technologies and products are helping our customers on their own sustainability journey by enabling significant reductions in power consumption

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the excerpts.
Multi-continent manufacturing and service reach into mine sites — where liner installation and service income matter — is a real advantage, now materially widened by Molycop's global footprint.
scores.quote: expanded geographic reach

scores.rationale: Large growth capex and capacity build-out were made ahead of demand, but incremental returns have been deeply negative — FY26 revenue fell to INR1,103 crores with a PAT loss of INR909 crores and net debt of INR3,531 crores.
scores.quote: we also made major capital investments in R&D and manufacturing operations

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend anywhere in the calls; the business is tender/OEM driven.

R&D is sustained and does yield a steady stream of new products and patents (676 filed, 371 granted; 5G Massive MIMO, C+L WDM, DCI, 4G/5G core), but efficiency is poor as the spend has not yet converted into profitable revenue.
scores.quote: We filed 63 patents in Q4, bringing the cumulative count to 676

scores.rationale: Saankhya Labs was a small, complementary bolt-on (5G radios, satcom, semiconductor PLI) that was cleanly merged, but margins deteriorated rather than improved post-deal.
scores.quote: 63.43% shares of Saankhya Labs have been acquired

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed in any call; the company has been a net raiser of capital (Panatone warrant conversion of INR712.5 crores) rather than a distributor.
Extremely asset- and working-capital-heavy: FY26 revenue of INR1,103 crores against inventory of INR2,438 crores and receivables of INR3,258 crores, funded by INR4,035 crores of gross borrowings.
scores.quote: your inventory is almost twice the amount of orders in hand

scores.rationale: Small base with real runway and demonstrated share capture in BharatNet Phase III and indigenous routers, though wireless share gains outside BSNL remain at trial stage.
scores.quote: we are the largest supplier in terms of number of circles for BharatNet Phase III

scores.rationale: Credible international push via Telecom Egypt, NEC and Rakuten partnerships and wins in Africa, Europe and the Americas, but execution is slow with international still only ~12-15% of revenue.
scores.quote: we are seeing increasing engagements with international customers... through partnerships with NEC and Rakuten

scores.rationale: Growth is project/volume-led with no pricing power — fixed-price rupee tenders left the company unable to pass through component cost inflation, and it is still renegotiating merely to protect margins.
scores.quote: fixed price in India we do not have any opportunity to increase the prices to our customers

scores.rationale: The company is at a clear cyclical trough after the one-off BSNL spike, with an identifiable upturn ahead in the delayed 18,000-site add-on PO and AI-driven network build-outs.
scores.quote: AI is going to drive a network infrastructure build super-cycle

scores.rationale: End markets — broadband, optical transport, data-centre interconnect and 5G — are in secular expansion driven by data and AI traffic, though telecom equipment capex remains lumpy and tender-dependent.
scores.quote: by 2033, AI traffic is predicted to be more than 60% of the total network

scores.rationale: Leverage ballooned to INR4,035 crores gross debt while inventory of INR2,438 crores was built and held for years against a purchase order that never arrived, and investment was not trimmed despite a INR909 crore loss.
scores.quote: we had not cut down on the investments during the year

scores.rationale: Persistent multi-year execution of an indigenous 4G/5G stack culminating in a live 100,000-site BSNL network shows genuine tenacity and long-horizon vision, albeit heavily dependent on state policy.
scores.quote: The BSNL 4G/5G network went live across 100,000 sites

scores.rationale: Management courts visibility — product launches by the Prime Minister and Minister of Communications, award announcements and Gartner/Omdia citations feature prominently in every call.
scores.quote: we also won the prestigious Golden Peacock Awards for our 5G RAN solutions

scores.rationale: Internal bench is used for succession (Arnob Roy to MD/CEO, Preetham Uthaiah to COO, AVS Prasad to CFO) and headcount grew 42% in FY24, but a CEO resignation left the seat vacant for three-plus quarters alongside CFO and board churn.
scores.quote: it's been about three quarters since Mr. Anand Athreya resigned from his post as CEO

scores.rationale: Management openly names what went wrong — supply-chain misjudgement, the BSNL delay, missed FY24-level revenue guidance — and apologises for operational slips, though it deflects on timelines to profitability.
scores.quote: The part that has not played out to expectation was the BSNL expansions

scores.rationale: The FY24 record year (INR2,471 crores, 343% Q4 growth) was a single government-mandated BSNL project rather than repeatable skill, as the collapse to INR1,103 crores and a INR909 crore loss two years later demonstrates.
scores.quote: the BSNL project last year was a huge sharp spike in our business

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position — the company competes head-on with global RAN and optical majors and describes itself as a newcomer in wireless.
scores.quote: this is a long cycle and we are a new player in this market

scores.rationale: The large installed base (100,000 BSNL sites, 15,000 MAAN routers, BharatNet circles) creates genuine expansion/switching-cost stickiness, but that lock-in has not translated into pricing power or timely follow-on orders.
scores.quote: we have a delay in the receipt of this PO

scores.rationale: End customers hold overwhelming negotiating power — a handful of government agencies and Tier-1 telcos buying through fixed-price tenders, with a single delayed BSNL PO able to halve company revenue.
scores.quote: tender deals which were rupee denominated in fixed price

scores.rationale: Technology barriers are real but the company faces entrenched global OEMs in price-competitive tender processes where it cannot pass through cost inflation.
scores.quote: our gross margins have definitely been adversely impacted

scores.rationale: Clear share donators exist in the form of high-risk vendors being ripped out of Western networks and legacy SONET/SDH utility equipment being replaced.
scores.quote: a large replacement market of replacing high-risk vendor equipment in EU and the U.S.

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar: a flagship Atmanirbhar national champion with PLI incentives, ministerial launches and heavy analyst and press coverage.
scores.quote: the Department of Telecom announced a variant of the PLI scheme

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are squeezed by component costs and fixed-price contracts, and the company has posted cumulative losses over five years.
scores.quote: in the last five years, we have not made any positive bottom line cumulatively

scores.rationale: Reliability credibility built on the BSNL rollout is demonstrably what opens doors — global partners and international customers came because of proven large-scale execution.
scores.quote: based on the credibility of our performance in BSNL, that's where we got a lot of international partnerships

scores.rationale: The end-to-end portfolio under a single network management system offers a one-stop convenience, but international reach depends on partners (TCS, NEC, Rakuten) rather than an owned sales/service network.
scores.quote: a unique advantage of being able to build complete end-to-end network for any customer

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate/government where price and tender terms dominate; the company has not converted reliability into TCO-based pricing power or contractual lock-in.
scores.quote: India once again dominated our business, 88% was from India

scores.rationale: A genuinely deep, multi-product indigenous technology stack with high R&D intensity — 676 patents, 150+ 3GPP contributions, 5G-Advanced/6G standards-essential filings and C+L band 76 Tbps WDM.
scores.quote: more than 150 contributions to the evolving 3GPP standards

scores.rationale: A hardware equipment vendor with no two-sided network — value comes from projects and partnerships, and nothing in the calls suggests self-reinforcing scale benefits.
Distribution is a weakness rather than a moat: it reaches large customers through intermediaries (TCS for BSNL, NEC/Rakuten internationally) and international revenue remains a small slice.
scores.quote: our immediate customer is TCS, which is a private entity

scores.quote: customers trust us to manage biomass better than anybody else

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power; margins are structurally thin (projects 5-8%, products aspiring to 10%) and repeatedly compressed by raw-material swings.
scores.quote: our projects business historically has been 5% to 6%... maybe you could increase the profitability out there to give more of a range of 5% to 8%

scores.rationale: The clearest strength — customers pay a premium for engineering certainty and execution reliability, giving Thermax a 'last look' and a 2-3 paise price premium in solar despite no technology edge.
scores.quote: customers to prefer to have some peace of mind, and they will come back and at least give us the last look

scores.rationale: Deliberate multi-year build of customer intimacy and service accessibility through H/H-live, AMCs and rapid spares, from a low base of installed-base visibility.
scores.quote: focus really deeply on the services part of our portfolio - bring digital in... have AMC capability, rapid spare parts

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate/industrial and the benefit offered is correctly reliability and execution certainty rather than brand imagery, matching benefit type to customer.
scores.quote: the customer has a preference that Thermax just from as a partner of trust would be the one that they would look to work with

scores.rationale: Management explicitly disclaims proprietary technology, and even in water it concedes the edge is missing and still an aspiration.
scores.quote: In our water business, we are not always having that technology edge, and our ask is to build a technology edge in water

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the calls.

Service reach matters in this business and is being rebuilt digitally, but the admission that distributor-sold units and two-thirds of the installed base were untracked shows no rival-proof distribution advantage today.
scores.quote: they were sold through distributors so who that the distributors sell it to, when were the spare parts provided... lot of that information we did not have

scores.rationale: Sustained growth investment is real and expanding — Sterling went from ~30 resorts (2022) to 50 (2024) to 77 across 63 destinations (2026) — but it is deliberately asset-light/managed rather than heavy owned capex, with returns showing up as record EBITDA and 52% cash growth.
scores.quote: Our network expanded to 75 resorts with 3,705 keys as on December 31st... we are at 77 hotels and resorts across 63 destinations

scores.rationale: A&P is mentioned as ongoing brand and marketing investment leveraging Thomas Cook/SOTC brand recall, but spend is never quantified nor linked to measurable brand-equity or sales payback.
scores.quote: continue our investments in marketing through digital and print medium

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but consistent technology/product development across all 16 calls has yielded shippable products with measurable pull-through — VKYC, TCPay, TACY, Rahi and Sterling ONE, which alone contributed over INR1,000 million to 9M FY26 revenue.
scores.quote: Sterling ONE, our proprietary distribution platform... has contributed over INR1,000 million this financial year nine months to the top line

scores.rationale: Over the five years the group did no material acquisitions and instead simplified — merging dormant subsidiaries and demerging the resort business — so there is neither a bolt-on track record to reward nor empire-building to penalise.
scores.quote: the Board has granted in-principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts

scores.rationale: The only distribution-adjacent actions discussed are face-value consolidation and the demerger framed as value unlock; no buyback programme, dividend policy or valuation-linked capital-return discipline is articulated across the 16 calls.
scores.quote: The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries... improves our Earnings Per Share

scores.rationale: The model is genuinely asset-light and float-funded — INR16 billion of prepaid-card float financing operations and Sterling expanding debt-free on an asset-right model — though the moat protecting those returns is thin, with travel EBIT margins of only 3.3%.
scores.quote: Our float as we speak, stands at about INR 16 billion on a total prepaid card load volumes of USD 764 million

scores.rationale: Repeated, quantified share capture against a shrinking industry: RBI LRS data showed education down 22% and travel forex down 3% while the company grew those same segments 17% and 13% respectively.
scores.quote: Despite the contraction in the overall student education segment, we gained market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is broad and executed — Cyprus office opened, DMS units across Asia, Africa, US and Middle East, Sterling into 63 destinations, Blinkit into 12 cities — but returns are uneven, with Desert Adventures down 50% in Q4 FY26.
scores.quote: the commencement of our air and hotel operations from our TCI-Euro office in Cyprus

scores.rationale: Group growth is volume/inventory-led with an adverse mix shift from high-value long-haul to cheaper short-haul, partially offset by genuine pricing at Sterling where ARR rose 12% and RevPAR 16%.
scores.quote: a 23% increase on our short haul on a 9-month basis versus a 5% increase in long haul

scores.rationale: The business is visibly near a cyclical trough — FY26 EBT fell 14% on Pahalgam, Operation Sindoor and the US-Iran-Israel conflict — but management itself describes forward bookings as softening, so the upturn is probable rather than identifiable.
scores.quote: our EBT was impacted by the geopolitical crisis and was 14% lower than last year

scores.rationale: Indian outbound and domestic travel is in secular expansion with policy tailwinds, including TCS on overseas packages cut to a flat 2% and structurally domestic-led tourism demand.
scores.quote: Travel and tourism remains structurally very strong with demand being overwhelmingly domestic in nature

scores.rationale: Prudent stewardship is evident — zero debt and INR3.4 billion cash at Sterling, no large acquisitions, and counter-cyclical resort building through the downturn — though the legacy Quess mark-to-market holding lingered as a non-core distraction.
scores.quote: Our cash reserve stands close to INR 3,400 million, while continuing to maintain a completely debt-free balance sheet

scores.rationale: Management pursued a multi-year transformation with independence, notably sunsetting Sterling's cash-generative membership sales in favour of a hospitality model and sustaining it to a 25th consecutive profitable quarter.
scores.quote: having completely sunset the acquisition of long-term membership products from July 2023

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and delivered by a stable, low-profile team; there is no celebrity positioning or personality-led narrative across the five years.
scores.quote: I just want to assure you that in terms of margins, we have stable margins

scores.rationale: Talent is treated as a lead investment ahead of growth — leadership hiring in advance of the 1,000-key expansion and continued leadership-depth investment — supported by internal succession from Iyer as CEO to MD.
scores.quote: it was necessary to start investing in leadership and manpower in advance, which is what has happened in Q1

scores.rationale: Management guides explicitly and then scores itself against those guides, and discloses bad news promptly, including a USD 0.5 million doubtful-debt provision from a customer's bankruptcy and admitting a margin concession under competitive pressure.
scores.quote: we thought it's only prudent that we take this provision for doubtful debt at one go

scores.rationale: Results are heavily driven by exogenous swings — post-COVID rebound then geopolitical shocks — so the halo risk is real, though the share gains against declining LRS industry data provide some genuine skill signal independent of the cycle.
scores.quote: 2026 did not play out in a normal operating environment

scores.rationale: The company holds strong brand recall and a leading forex-specialist position in study-abroad, but nothing approaching monopoly ownership of the customer's mind, and it competes openly with OTAs, banks and agents.
scores.quote: we are now taking an industry-leading position there, as India FOREX specialists

scores.rationale: Corporate travel and forex programmes carry some embedded switching costs across 8,000 corporate clients and 1,100 forex corporates, but pricing power is weak — travel EBIT margin is just 3.3% — indicating no captive economics.
scores.quote: we have about 8,000 corporate clients with digital adoption of over 30%

scores.rationale: The end markets are fragmented and price-competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, with the company forced into tactical margin concessions in the Middle East against competitive intensity.
scores.quote: faced stiff competitive intensity and muted demand... we had to make a tactical progress in terms of our margin

scores.rationale: Travel distribution has low entry barriers and visible price competition, with input costs and pricing set by airlines and hotels rather than the operator — airfares surging 30-50% on westbound routes with no ability to pass through.
scores.quote: We are seeing airfares surge by 30% to 50% on most westbound routes

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are visibly exiting or shrinking — a large European travel operator declared bankruptcy — and the company grew retail forex 25% while the industry contracted, indicating share flowing from weaker hands.
scores.quote: the sudden declaration of bankruptcy by a large European travel unit called FTI

scores.rationale: This is a well-known listed legacy brand with regular sell-side hosted calls from IIFL, Systematix and 360 ONE, so it is neither obscure nor ignored by capital.
scores.quote: hosted by IIFL Securities Limited

scores.rationale: Brand trust is real and repeatedly invoked, but it does not convert into high gross margins — forex gross margin is 1.5% and travel EBIT 3.3% — so image-based pricing power is limited.
scores.quote: Gross margins for the business improved from 1.35% to 1.5%

scores.rationale: The proposition is increasingly built on certainty rather than price, with new protection products explicitly sold as peace of mind, including an industry-first visa rejection cover.
scores.quote: TravSure, a pioneering travel protection initiative designed to... provide customers with greater confidence and peace of mind

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the clearest differentiator — omnichannel access, Tier 2/3 last-mile outlets, airport counters, app and WhatsApp, plus quick-commerce forex card delivery via Blinkit now in 12 cities.
scores.quote: Our reach via quick commerce, which is Blinkit... increasing our digital distribution network to 12 cities

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched to each customer set — convenience and brand for retail forex and holidays, and reliability plus programme lock-in for the corporate travel and MICE book of 1,100 forex corporates.
scores.quote: we cater to about 1,100 corporates spanning across large, mid-sized and SME customers

scores.rationale: There is a consistent multi-product technology build — VKYC, TCPay, AI agents TACY and Rahi, Sterling ONE — with measurable adoption (23% digital, app bookings up 4.9x), but the stack is replicable rather than a deep proprietary edge.
scores.quote: Bookings on our app, which is TCPay, saw a 4.9x increase in transaction

scores.rationale: Across all 16 calls there is no evidence of a two-sided self-reinforcing network; growth comes from added outlets, resorts and accounts, which scale linearly rather than compounding.
scores.quote: Distribution footprint for the foreign exchange business expanded by 7 outlets during the year

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the group's strongest and hardest-to-replicate asset — franchise and airport counters, 800 education counsellors, NBFC tie-ups, quick-commerce delivery, 77 resorts and destination-management units across continents.
scores.quote: Our relationships with over 800 marquee education counsellors across the country gave us a genuine on-the-ground advantage

scores.rationale: Five years of sustained growth capex (labs 17→44, ₹250cr+ invested) has come with sharply rising returns, ROCE going from 15% in FY23 to 34% in FY26, i.e. genuinely incremental capacity, not maintenance.
scores.quote: we have achieved all this while continuing to invest in our business INR 250 crores plus of capex investments... Return on capital employed has also improved from 15% in FY 23 to 34% in FY 26

scores.rationale: A&P is real and brand-building — rebranding in FY23, brand architecture (Aarogyam/Jaanch/Her Check), and a national ambassador in FY26 — with Jaanch growing 66% y-o-y, but spend is modest and the positioning remains price-led rather than premium.
scores.quote: we onboarded Madhuri Dixit as the brand ambassador for Thyrocare, which is an important step in strengthening brand recall and consumer trust at a national level

scores.rationale: There is no classical R&D, but consistent menu/platform development has yielded a ~5x test menu and new revenue lines (allergy, NIPT/genomics, histopathology), plus real-world data studies — productive, though largely built on bought-in platforms.
scores.quote: Our test menu has increased nearly fivefold to more than 1,375 tests

scores.rationale: M&A has been small, complementary bolt-ons (Polo Labs for weak North India presence, Think Health for at-home ECG) rather than transformational deals, and group margins expanded from 23% to 32% over the period, though acquiree quality and standalone returns were never quantified.
scores.quote: Polo Labs is a pathology diagnostic company based out of Punjab... This will allow us to expand our footprint in North India, where we have been weak

scores.rationale: Distribution is conservative and coherent — zero debt, ₹230cr+ net cash and a ₹7/share final dividend funded by ₹213cr operating cash flow — but there is no buyback or articulated valuation-linked capital return policy.
scores.quote: Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 7 per equity share... net cash and investment of INR230 crores plus and zero debt

scores.rationale: The model is structurally asset-light — third-party franchisee collection points and a hub-and-spoke lab network drive 34% ROCE and 74% gross margins — but the protecting moat is scale/cost rather than anything competitors cannot replicate.
scores.quote: our hub-and-spoke model ensures strong economics, allowing incremental volumes to flow into existing infrastructure, driving better utilization and operating leverage

scores.rationale: Clear, sustained share capture from a small base in a highly fragmented market: franchisees 2,700→11,700 in five years, tests +23% in FY26 and pathology +26% in Q1 FY27, explicitly ahead of industry.
scores.quote: our active franchise network has grown to over 11,700, a fourfold increase versus when we took over... this volume is higher than some of our biggest competitors combined

scores.rationale: Domestic expansion is well executed (pin codes 3,500 to a lab within 150km of anywhere in India, North India filled via Polo Labs) and Tanzania is growing fast, but international remains a trivial base rather than a proven premium-brand travel story.
scores.quote: our Tanzania operations, though small in base but has also grown by 75% for us year-on-year

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led by design — Q1 FY27 revenue +26% against test volume +28% — with the company explicitly committed to being the lowest-price option; mix (Jaanch, specialty) helps margins but is only ~2% of pathology revenue.
scores.quote: We will continue to remain an affordable option to all patients... All our efforts on our value proposition is towards ensuring low cost to the patient

scores.rationale: The cycle referenced is the one-off COVID collapse and recovery (FY21 trough, degrowth of 20%) which has already fully played out by FY26, leaving no identifiable cyclical upturn ahead.
scores.quote: during FY21, our pathology business, excluding COVID, hit an all-time low of 304, a degrowth of 20% versus the previous year

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — preventive/diagnostic testing moving to the centre of care in an underpenetrated India, plus a nascent genomics opportunity — and management has consistently framed and invested against this.
scores.quote: diagnostics is no longer a back-end support function. It is central to clinical decision-making and increasingly to preventive health management

scores.rationale: Prudent balance sheet (zero debt, net cash), organic-first growth with only small bolt-ons, counter-cyclical rebuilding of the franchise base through the FY22–23 trough, and willingness to shrink loss-making radiology centres; tempered by being a subsidiary of a leveraged parent with related-party API business.
scores.quote: in radiology... we undertook some strategic consolidation of centers during the year. While this has temporary impact on the growth, the overall financial performance has improved with a stronger bottom line

scores.rationale: Rahul Guha has run the same eight-point/three-pillar strategy unchanged across all 17 calls and delivered a four-year rebuild from a 5% three-year CAGR to 20%+ growth, though independence is qualified by API Holdings ownership and early reliance on group channels.
scores.quote: in a three-year CAGR it is only 5% growth. I look it as an opportunity rather than a headwind

scores.rationale: Communication is substance-heavy on operating metrics, but the FY26–27 calls lead with award recitations, a Great Place to Work badge and a celebrity ambassador, and every call opens with a signature Gandhi/Mandela quote — more self-promotional than low-profile.
scores.quote: We were recognized at the 4th National Diagnostic Forum & Awards by Voice of Healthcare with two prestigious awards

scores.rationale: There is an ESOP retention program, a built-out senior team and a Great Place to Work certification, but the five-year record shows heavy churn rather than an internal pipeline — three CFOs (Salvi, Jagnani, Gupta) and two Chief Commercial Officers over the period.
scores.quote: the ESOP program... This initiative implemented at group level aim to retain the talent within Thyrocare

scores.rationale: Consistently owns weakness and quantifies it — accepted the 5% three-year CAGR critique in 2022, admitted North India was weak, flagged radiology decline, and explicitly sized the ₹4cr one-off inflating the prior-year partnership base rather than hiding behind the optics.
scores.quote: The extent of the one-off was approximately INR4 crores in Q4 FY '25. And normalizing for that, the partnership segment still grew at 32%

scores.rationale: The turnaround is verifiable in hard, skill-attributable metrics (ROCE 15%→34%, complaints down to 3.06/mn, TAT 3.43 hrs, NABL 100% of own labs) rather than just headline growth, though part of the growth flatters off a COVID-depressed FY21 base.
scores.quote: significant progress on our quality metrics, with complaints reducing to 3.06 per million tests, thus sustaining a Six Sigma level of performance

scores.rationale: Thyrocare is the largest-volume B2B pathology player but holds no monopoly-like position in the customer's mind — it wins on price and turnaround in a market with several national and many local alternatives.
scores.quote: we continue to actually have one of the lowest prices as a B2B player in the country

scores.rationale: Some lock-in exists through API integrations with healthtech/insurance partners and the slab-based franchisee pricing that rewards volume loyalty, but franchisees demonstrably switch away and back on price, as the FY22 channel-partner loss and recovery showed.
scores.quote: channel partners are coming back, channel partners are increasing their share of wallet with us

scores.rationale: Indian diagnostics is fragmented, not an oligopoly — the company itself flags aggressive new entrants in wellness and unbranded B2B competitors, and franchisee customers negotiate hard on price.
scores.quote: in the B2B space I would say there I have been new entrance in the last I would say two years

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is not rational — new entrants have arrived repeatedly and Thyrocare's own strategy is to be the lowest-price provider, while it also had to normalize aggressive insurance-segment pricing after buying traction.
scores.quote: This year, we have normalized our pricing into the insurance segment, and therefore, the growth has been slower in this segment

scores.rationale: The donor pool is enormous and structurally weak — only 2% of Indian labs are NABL accredited, so a vast unorganized standalone-lab base is losing share to accredited, faster-TAT chains, which is exactly the share Thyrocare has been taking.
scores.quote: only 2% of NABL Labs in India, 2% of labs in India are NABL credit

scores.rationale: This is a well-covered listed diagnostics name that actively courts visibility with awards, a celebrity ambassador and a segment (preventive/genomics diagnostics) attracting substantial competing capital — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We received the India's most trusted customer-focused diagnostic brand 2026 award at the pride of Healthcare Excellence Award and Summit 2026

scores.rationale: Gross margin is high and rising (74.7%, +113bps) with demonstrable brand trust among doctors and steady non-discretionary demand, but the brand is deliberately built on affordability so pricing power from image is deliberately unmonetized.
scores.quote: 9 out of 10 doctors trust Thyrocare reports and confidently recommend our services to their patients

scores.rationale: Assurance is the core proposition being built — 100% NABL-accredited own labs, MD pathologist review of every report, Six Sigma complaint rates and 3.37-hour TAT — but the pitch pairs trust with low cost rather than making price secondary.
scores.quote: Diagnostics is fundamentally a trust business... accuracy and quality. This continues to be non-negotiable for us

scores.rationale: Access and intimacy are the standout advantage: 11,700 collection points, the largest phlebotomy network at 99% arrival adherence, a lab within 150km of anywhere in India, plus structured field teams and franchisee meets.
scores.quote: If you drop a pin anywhere in India, you will find a Thyrocare pathology lab within 150 kilometers

scores.rationale: The benefit match is sensible — retail gets branded packages (Aarogyam, Jaanch), while corporate/institutional buyers get TCO, one-stop capability and API integration lock-in — though the retail-facing intangible is thin because the end patient is reached through franchisees.
scores.quote: our API-based integration are also enabling partners to expand diagnostics offering across multiple cities seamlessly, which is strengthening our positioning as a preferred B2B partner

scores.rationale: Technology is applied well for logistics, automation and TAT, but the differentiating platforms are purchased third-party systems (Phadia, BioFire, NGS) with no proprietary tech edge or meaningful R&D intensity.
scores.quote: the addition of Phadia-based allergy testing platform and other 20-plus specialized tests, including histopathology, a new HPLC platform

scores.rationale: There is a scale/density flywheel — more volume into hub labs improves utilisation and TAT, which attracts more franchisees — but it is operating leverage, not a self-reinforcing two-sided network.
scores.quote: allowing incremental volumes to flow into existing infrastructure, driving better utilisation and operating leverage as the network scales

scores.rationale: The distribution and logistics backbone is the genuine moat in a business where turnaround time is decisive: 44 labs, 11,700 franchisees and 2,100 phlebotomists delivering 3.37-hour lab TAT nationally, a reach rivals cannot quickly replicate.
scores.quote: Our home collection network stands at 2,000 phlebotomists, probably the largest phlebotomy network in India with exceptional service levels

scores.rationale: The Prag Distillery expansion from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases was executed and commissioned for ~INR 59 crore with ~INR 10 crore per annum of bottling savings (a very high incremental return), but guided capex thereafter reverts to maintenance-only levels of ~INR 25 crore per year.
scores.quote: This expansion entailed an investment of around INR 59 crore, which has been fully invested... TI expects savings in bottling costs to the tune of INR 10 crore per annum

scores.rationale: Management deliberately invested to build brandy's low share of voice ('A Warm Welcome') and plans to revamp A&SP on the under-invested Imperial Blue, with Mansion House crossing 10 million cases as evidence of durable brand equity, though at times margin expansion came from cutting S&D rather than investing.
scores.quote: we feel that IB is a slightly underinvested brand for the last 4 - 5 years. We will look at revamping our investments in A&SP across markets

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but a consistent new-product pipeline has delivered commercially — Flandy (India's first premium flavoured brandy), Monarch Legacy luxury brandy, Mansion House Whisky and Seven Islands Pure Malt — with management still describing a live NPD pipeline.
scores.quote: we launched our luxury whisky, Seven Islands Pure Malt whisky in the state of Maharashtra and certain export markets

scores.rationale: The INR 3,442 crore Imperial Blue purchase is the opposite of a small bolt-on — it is transformative, funded by INR 2,100 crore of new debt, and the acquiree was a weakening asset (low-to-mid single digit FY26 volume degrowth, 11.7% steady-state margin below TI's ~15%), so post-deal consolidated OPM was diluted rather than improved.
scores.quote: the steady-state margin of Imperial Blue before acquisition, which is around 11.7%... assuming 13% as the combined business

scores.rationale: Distribution policy is thin and dilution-heavy: repeated preferential issues (INR 311 crore, then INR 2,093 crore) with no rights issue for retail holders, no buybacks, and only a token first dividend of INR 1 per share in FY26.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors have recommended a dividend of INR 1 per share for FY25-'26

scores.rationale: The model is deliberately asset-light — 16 of 20 units are contractual and only INR 59 crore of owned capacity was added even at 20 million cases — combined with a genuine brandy brand moat, though the new IB debt load weighs on returns.
scores.quote: Our manufacturing footprint extends to 12 states through 20 units, 4 owned and 16 on contractual arrangements

scores.rationale: Share gains have been consistent across the whole period from a non-dominant base — brandy share from ~14-15% to 20%, Telangana 6.8% to 7.4%, southern IMFL 5.8% to 6.2%, and post-IB close to 40% of P&A in South India.
scores.quote: TI market share as percentage of overall IMFL in its key southern states has now increased to 6.2% in Q3 from 5.8%

scores.rationale: Expansion has been real and executed — from a 14-state, South-concentrated brandy player to pan-India via Imperial Blue, plus Assam whisky, exports to Middle East/Africa/SE Asia and Monarch in international markets — though the pan-India leap was bought rather than built.
scores.quote: we are now truly a pan-India and pan-category P&A focused player

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led rather than price/mix-led: NSR ex-IB rose only 2.6-4% while volumes grew 14-17%, and the company was forced into an ~INR 200 per case price cut in Andhra Pradesh, with revenue guided at only 150-200 bps above volume growth.
scores.quote: The price correction in Andhra blended level on a state basis would be around Rs. 200, reduction

scores.rationale: Alcobev demand is not presented as cyclical; the swing factors are regulatory (Karnataka excise cut, AP route-to-market change, Maharashtra MML shrinking the prestige segment 25%, Telangana receivable delays) and cut in both directions with no identifiable cycle bottom.
scores.quote: we have seen the segment as a whole has de-grown by 25%-odd

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — roughly 10 million legal-drinking-age consumers added annually, premiumization across categories, a growing cocktail culture, and a stated 200 million+ case addressable opportunity.
scores.quote: 10 million legal drinking age people get added in India every year

scores.rationale: Stewardship was exemplary through the deleveraging phase (gross debt from ~INR 1,200 crore in 2019 to INR 45 crore with net cash by Q3 FY25) but was then reversed by a very large debt-and-equity-funded acquisition taking gross debt to INR 2,295 crore, the opposite of the 'organic focus, no big M&A' criterion.
scores.quote: our aggregate gross debt now stands at Rs.45 crore with net cash balance of Rs.31 crore

scores.rationale: A 1933-founded family business took a near-insolvent balance sheet to net cash over six years, patiently built brandy category leadership others ignored, then independently executed a transformative acquisition — a long arc of stated intent followed by delivery.
scores.quote: We have reduced our gross debt from a peak of almost INR1,200 crores in March 2019 to INR239 crores as of June 2023

scores.rationale: Calls are substance-led and operationally detailed with no celebrity positioning, and management explicitly declines to talk about stock price, redirecting to operating performance.
scores.quote: I will not comment upon the performance from a stock market perspective, what we can speak about is the operational and business performance

scores.rationale: Talent was scaled aggressively (350 to 850 employees, senior leader onboarding, Big 4 and HR consultants for integration) but this was bought-in external hiring rather than an internal pipeline, and the CFO seat churned through four occupants in five years with a family member now heading the luxury business.
scores.quote: having increased our workforce from around 350 employees to 850 employees as of March

scores.rationale: Management explains bad news with specifics and owns it — the AP repricing and RTM volume hit, IB degrowth in FY26, April disruption post-TSMA exit, and a proactive explanation of the revenue-presentation change and exactly which line items it flatters.
scores.quote: This change will have a negative impact on reported revenue and gross margins, but will have a positive impact on EBITDA margins and PAT margins

scores.rationale: Results are partly flattered by factors outside management skill — government subsidy income materially inflating EBITDA and a Karnataka excise duty cut driving 20%+ volume growth — although management does candidly attribute the Karnataka gain to the government rather than itself.
scores.quote: this was on account only of the excise duty reduction. There was no reduction in ex-factory or EDP price of the company

scores.rationale: Mansion House is the largest-selling brandy in India and TI owns the category's mindspace, including being the only flavoured brandy player in Asia, giving a quasi-monopoly position within brandy though not in whisky.
scores.quote: Yes, we are the only ones in Asia, I believe in this particular product category

scores.rationale: State-level excise licensing, registered labels and route-to-market structures create defensible regional positions — visible in the ~40% South India P&A share and in the fact that even transferring IB's own labels required a multi-quarter TSMA arrangement — but consumers face no switching cost.
scores.quote: we had taken TSMA support services from Pernod Ricard, while the labels under TI name were being registered

scores.rationale: IMFL is a consolidated oligopoly and the retail consumer has no negotiating power, but the actual customer in TI's core southern states is the state corporation, which demonstrably does have power — forcing price corrections in AP and stretching receivables in Telangana.
scores.quote: it has been a matter of concern in terms of the increased receivables, which we are having from the government

scores.rationale: Licensing and label registration keep new entrants rare and ownership stable, but pricing rationality is imperfect — TI had to cut prices to match competition in Andhra, and a new state-created MML category shrank its Maharashtra prestige segment by 25%.
scores.quote: the one-time price correction which we had to do in line with competition that has already been effected

scores.rationale: TI's growth has come squarely from under-investing rivals — the brandy category was starved of marketing by incumbents, and Imperial Blue itself was a brand its multinational owner had left underinvested for four to five years before selling it.
scores.quote: there has been very little investments made by industry players in the Brandy category

scores.rationale: Brandy was a neglected, low-prestige niche that larger players and capital ignored, which is precisely where TI built leadership, though the Imperial Blue deal has now moved the company firmly into the spotlight.
scores.quote: its share of voice is very low in comparison to other IMFL categories

scores.rationale: Brand pull is demonstrable — secondary volumes grew 8% in Andhra even while primaries de-grew during the RTM transition — with gross margins around 50% and a successful premium/luxury ladder from Flandy to Monarch.
scores.quote: Despite degrowth in primary volumes, secondary volumes in Andhra Pradesh grew at 8%, indicating strong brand equity for our products

scores.rationale: Reliability/trust is a secondary rather than primary purchase driver here, and when a shareholder challenged IB's blend quality management could only fall back on legacy and volumes rather than a demonstrable assurance proposition.
scores.quote: the IB brand has a 30-year legacy and is the 3rd largest selling whisky in India

scores.rationale: Distribution reach and availability are explicitly the company's chosen route to consumer access, used to launch Mansion House Whisky in Assam and to carry Spaceman's gin and vodka, now extended to a 200 million+ case opportunity.
scores.quote: the distribution network now gives us access to 200 million+ cases opportunity in the Indian Alcobev market

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail consumers and the benefit set is correctly matched to them — image, aspiration and price laddering aimed at a younger legal-drinking-age cohort rather than TCO arguments.
scores.quote: our aim is to make brandy more aspirational and youthful; and Flandy is a step in that direction

scores.rationale: There is no technology edge or R&D intensity in this business; management itself identifies distribution, packaging and communication — not technology — as the differentiators, and declines to name any proprietary advantage.
scores.quote: I think distribution is a key part, right, in today's times... so is the packaging around it, and the communication that goes around it

scores.rationale: Twelve calls contain no discussion of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic; the scale benefits described are distribution and procurement scale, not network effects.

Distribution is the company's clearest and most durable advantage — deep southern reach that it monetises by carrying third-party brands, now extended pan-India through Imperial Blue and repeatedly named by management as the key moat.
scores.quote: given our distribution strengths in southern India as well as in East, we do believe that there is a decent play. Distribution will play a very important role

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex (Nasik CRSS, Phaltan, large-diameter tube line, ~Rs.300-350cr core capex for FY27) with capacity kept 2-3 years ahead and core ROIC of 44-49%, though a parallel Rs.500-750cr of parent capital is flowing into loss-making EV.
scores.quote: capex in our core business will be around Rs.300 Crores to Rs.350 Crores range... we are running at 80% to 85% capacity utilization

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend anywhere across the five calls.

Product development is continuous (indigenised microcontrollers, swap technology, new tube grades, new medical products) but efficiency is poor — the three-wheeler needed a re-engineered variant after 'product concerns' and TI Medical/CDMO products slipped by quarters to 18 months.
scores.quote: There have been, there were some product concerns which we have now put it together

scores.rationale: Recent deals are genuinely small and complementary (Medicura IV-cannula asset purchase, taking over the body-in-white supplier's facility) and cheaply bought, but the acquiree was a non-operating asset rather than an already-strong business, and management concedes the target pool is thin.
scores.quote: It was maybe we got at an attractive price. The company was not in operation.

scores.rationale: A stable, repeated but modest dividend (Rs.2 interim + Rs.1.50 final in both FY25 and FY26) with no buybacks and no articulated payout policy, while free cash is redirected to subsidiaries.
scores.quote: The Board has declared and paid an interim dividend of Rs.2 per share in February 2026... recommended a final dividend of Rs.1.50 per share

scores.rationale: ROIC held at 44-49% through the period with free cash flow rising to 100% of PAT, and the moat rests on long OEM approval cycles, though tube-making is capital-intensive rather than asset-light.

scores.rationale: Share is described as intact-to-marginally-better in tubes and chains but the company is already at ~50% in industrial chains with little runway, while EV share is going backwards (M&HCV from 50%+ to 'over 40%', three-wheelers ceded to incumbents).
scores.quote: our market share is intact, rather, it is a marginal improvement... we do almost maybe let us say close to 50% share in that

scores.rationale: Exports have been stuck at ~15% of sales for years, the US is shut out by Section 232's 50% duty, Europe is weak, and management explicitly concedes the export lever failed.
scores.quote: export growth has not been to the level we wanted... export as a lever has not played out

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with no pricing benefit — commodity inflation is merely passed through with a one-to-two quarter lag — with only the bicycle premiumisation providing any mix gain.
scores.quote: there are no major price movements in the Q4. So, you can consider whatever is the sales growth shown in the Q4, it is in line with the volume growth

scores.rationale: Post-GST-cut auto demand inflected upward through FY26 with double-digit engineering volume growth, and the depressed railway/MFPD business plus a Rs.1,000cr seven-year contract represents a trough yet to turn, though commodity and fuel inflation now loom.
scores.quote: after that we see a really uptick in demand... October as well as November, both seems to be very very strong months

scores.rationale: Core auto-component and tube demand is cyclical, but the electrification thesis, Vande Bharat railway coaches, medical devices and CDMO give genuine secular end-market exposure, even if monetisation is delayed.
scores.quote: all of the IC components and IC products in these businesses are going to get replaced over time

scores.rationale: Strong cash discipline in the core (FCF at 100% of PAT, no large M&A, TI2 now closed to further bets) is offset by years of diversification into loss-making adjacencies with a further Rs.500-750cr of parent money committed after Rs.412cr of FY25 EV losses.
scores.quote: it will definitely be at least Rs.500 Crores and it could be so my sense is the range is Rs.500 Crores to Rs.750 Crores... From the parent balance sheet

scores.rationale: Management sticks to a decade-long thesis independently — doubling down on EV despite losses, keeping capacity two-to-three years ahead of demand, and persisting through an 18-month CDMO permitting delay — although tenacity here is not yet distinguishable from stubbornness.
scores.quote: now is the time to double down on that business. It is not the time to kind of back off

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, numbers-first and free of promotion, with management repeatedly refusing to give flattering forward numbers because past estimates were wrong.
scores.quote: honestly, I have given an estimate in the past and I have been wrong. So, I would rather kind of err on the side of caution here

scores.rationale: A clean promoter-to-professional MD handover, stable long-tenured division heads presenting on every call, and deliberate leadership hiring for CG Power services indicate a working pipeline.
scores.quote: from the time you took over from the professional manager and then handed over the baton to another professional manager... we are now in the process of recruiting one or two key people

scores.rationale: Unusually direct ownership of mistakes across the period — admitting EV misjudgement, wrong capital estimates, and repeated slippage in railways, medical certification and CDMO without spin.
scores.quote: I made some mistakes, kind of I have not perhaps performed as well as we could have in certain segments... TI2 is taking longer than I thought it would

scores.rationale: The assessment survives halo-stripping because management itself separates results from skill — core engineering delivered on stated plans (capacity, domestic growth) while the same team openly reports the TI2 failures rather than letting consolidated CG Power profits paper over them.
scores.quote: where we thought exports would kind of drive it, actually, we have seen the opposite

scores.rationale: Roughly half of the Rs.900cr industrial chain market and a commanding early lead in heavy electric trucks (172 of 206 industry deployments in FY25) show monopoly-like niches, though the EV lead is already eroding.
scores.quote: out of 206 trucks 172 trucks were deployed by IPL Tech

scores.rationale: OEM qualification cycles create real switching costs that kept US business sticky even through a 50% tariff, and every new plant needs a multi-month customer approval cycle that equally protects the incumbent.
scores.quote: wherever we are supplying to the OEMs, which maybe approval process is also quite longer, and that is how it gives you advantage in this kind of a time, where the business is sticky

scores.rationale: Tubes and chains are concentrated, but the end customers are large auto OEMs and Indian Railways who clearly hold negotiating power — railway tenders were taken up and then judged unprofitable, and one Korean OEM's fortunes swing the MFPD segment.
scores.quote: the railways, where maybe we have not got the profitability in the tender business

scores.rationale: Approval-based barriers protect the legacy tube and chain business, but the new segments show the opposite — seven to eight entrants in heavy electric trucks within two years and rising three-wheeler competitive intensity.
scores.quote: there are about seven to eight players who are now active in the market

scores.rationale: Little evidence of weak rivals to feed on — share is held rather than taken in chains, and in EV the competitors named are strong incumbents (Mahindra, Ashok Leyland, Volvo, Eicher) who have been taking share from TI, not donating it.
scores.quote: where we made mistakes and where the incumbents have now taken the lead has been in the three-wheeler side

scores.rationale: This is contract-priced B2B metal forming with no image-based pricing power — margins sit near 12% PBIT and input costs are recovered from customers with a lag rather than through brand pull.
scores.quote: commodity price increase, we get it from our customers because we have contracts in place, which comes with sometimes a one or two quarter lag

scores.rationale: Customers buy qualified, approved reliability — long approval cycles, prototype validation for Vande Bharat coaches, and repeat truck orders driven by demonstrated field performance rather than price.
scores.quote: in terms of product performance, what we have demonstrated to the customer, our existing customer satisfaction and the repeat orders which we are getting

scores.rationale: Distribution is being built rather than owned — the EV dealer plan of 120 three-wheeler and 25 SCV/tractor dealerships was still incomplete a year after being set out, with trucks sold direct.
scores.quote: we are 85 dealers who are fully operational as of today... the plan is to go upwards of 120 dealership for FY26

scores.rationale: The benefit mix fits the customer base well: corporate/OEM buyers are locked in by approval-based switching costs, and the EV truck pitch is explicitly a TCO argument to fleet operators.
scores.quote: the customer takes the GST as the input credit... from a total cost of ownership perspective

scores.rationale: There is real engineering capability (in-house microcontrollers, battery swap, cold-rolled strips, large-diameter tubes) but no evidence of high R&D intensity or a durable multi-product edge, and management is candidly unsure whether its swap technology will even prevail.
scores.quote: We are well on our way to indigenize majority of the microcontrollers within ourselves... So the judgment is still not out

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is discussed anywhere in the five calls.

Distribution reach is a work in progress rather than an unmatched asset — dealer counts are still being built out in EV and the company had to take over a supplier's plant to fix its own supply chain.
scores.quote: we have taken over that particular facility of the supplier

scores.rationale: Capex has scaled from ~INR175cr (FY25) to INR370cr (FY26) with roughly half explicitly toward value-added capacity (composite cylinders, IBC, recycling, US plant) and ROCE climbed 14%→18.9% over four years, though a large maintenance/re-engineering component remains and the 20% ROCE target was missed.
scores.quote: Total capex incurred during FY '26 was INR370 crore s, which includes INR198 crores towards regular and maintenance... and INR172 crores towards value -added products

scores.rationale: No advertising or brand-promotion spend is discussed across the calls; the business is ~92% B2B with formula-based pricing.

A steady pipeline of internally developed products has repeatedly reached commercialization — Type IV CNG cascades, LPG, oxygen cylinders (approved and commercialised), 6/9kg composite fire extinguishers (April 2026), hydrogen drone cylinders, 250L CNG, and TBS/E-rickshaw batteries developed on a INR5-7cr spend against ~INR100cr potential.
scores.quote: both the products of 6 kg and 9 kg is ready, and that will be the commercialization will take place from April 2026

scores.rationale: Two small bolt-ons (Ebullient Packaging, Systoverse) are only named in passing with no rationale, price or post-deal margin evidence, while the earlier Middle East 50% disinvestment dragged on for years — so complementarity is plausible but unproven.
scores.quote: There are other acquisition updates which have also been communicated. Regarding Ebullient Packaging Private Limited and S ystoverse Private Limited

scores.rationale: Dividend has been paid for 30 years with payout nudged to 15.8% from 14.6%, but the buyback floated in 2022 never materialised and the company instead issued INR800cr of QIP equity (INR460cr still parked in FDs), so the policy is consistent but modest and dilutive.
scores.quote: The company has been paying dividend consistently for the last 30 years and has increased the dividend payout in this year to 15.8%

scores.rationale: This is a capital- and working-capital-heavy manufacturer — ~100-day working capital cycle (down from 120), heavy multi-plant brownfield/greenfield spend, and ROCE only now nearing 19% — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: the working capital cycle time was 120 days, which is now reduced to almost 98 to 99 days

scores.rationale: It is winning share in the newer composite categories (CNG cascade +22-23%, value-added share 22%→29-30%) but is already the leading Indian and top-3 global player in its 75% core packaging business, limiting runway there.
scores.quote: we are, of course, the leading player in this country and with our presence in about 11 countries globally. We are there in the top 3

scores.rationale: Overseas is ~35% of sales across 10-11 countries and now growing faster than India (13% vs 11%), with a fifth US plant in Georgia operational and Saudi Dammam planned, executed as local-for-local manufacturing that neutralised tariffs.
scores.quote: we have a manufacturing location in U.S.A. and supplying for the local in U.S.A. So tariff has not affected any of our revenue

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led with pricing a pure pass-through (FY26 volume +13.5% vs revenue +12%; 9M FY26 volume +15% vs revenue +11%), and the only positive lever is mix from value-added products rising to 29-30%.
scores.quote: Volume increased 15%... The gap is primarily due to lower of the raw materi al cost

scores.rationale: Earnings swing with polymer/oil prices and geopolitical shocks, but management describes no cycle-bottom positioning — pass-through contracts are used to neutralise rather than ride the cycle.
scores.quote: price revisions are implemented through mutually agreed monthly or quarterly mechanisms

scores.rationale: Core end markets are in secular expansion — CNG cascade rollout, LPG composite conversion, hydrogen, PE pipes for water/gas infrastructure, and mandated PCR recycling — all of which management has capacity in place to serve.
scores.quote: As industries globally transition towards cleaner, safer and more sustainable energy and packaging solutions, we believe our company is exceptionally well positioned

scores.rationale: Leverage has been cut hard (debt INR647cr→INR266cr, net debt down INR409cr in FY26), growth is organic with non-core assets liquidated to fund it, but debt-free timelines have slipped repeatedly (2.5 years promised in 2024, still 12-18 months away in 2026) and INR460cr of QIP money sits idle.
scores.quote: the total debt as of -- in the 9 months ended stood only INR266 crores as against INR647 crores

scores.rationale: A multi-year composite-cylinder thesis has been pursued through election delays, the Ukraine war and Middle East disruption, with the Daman-to-Morai consolidation finally commissioned as promised and a four-year ROCE ladder (14→16→18→20%) publicly tracked.
scores.quote: in the last 4 years working on the deduction only, 14% to 16% achieved, 16% to 18% achieved

scores.rationale: Calls are hosted by small brokerages, run by long-serving operating executives (Vageria, Thyagarajan, technical director Naveen Jain) who talk about mould consolidation and power tariffs rather than personal profile.
scores.quote: consolidation manufacturing unit and brownfield expans ion that will continue

scores.rationale: Talent is mentioned only as a cost/location variable in plant consolidation; there is no discussion of systematic development or a leadership pipeline.

Disclosure is granular and self-marking — capex split, debt, QIP utilisation under a monitoring agency, and an explicit admission that FY26 ROCE of 18.9% fell short of the 20% target — though delayed projects are usually attributed to external events rather than owned.
scores.quote: FY '26 ROCE is 18.9% versus 20% target, reflecting short -term impact of QIP -led automation investments

scores.rationale: Record FY26 numbers owe much to pass-through pricing, capacity utilisation and falling finance cost rather than durable pricing power, and guidance has a long habit of running ahead of delivery (2022's 'debt-free in 2.5 years', repeated cylinder-line delays), so the results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: PAT growth minimum 21%, may exceed further because as the interest cost is further reduced

scores.rationale: In Type IV composite cylinders the company holds a near-unique domestic position with PESO/CPRI approvals and OMC acceptance, giving it a de facto monopoly-like standing in that niche, though its 75% packaging base has no such position.
scores.quote: Composites, of course, we are #1 with very broad presence in terms of Composite Cylinders in LPG, CNG and even entering hydrogen

scores.rationale: Packaging is a logistics-bound regional business where being co-located with chemical clusters (Chiplun, Silvassa, Georgia USA) creates local captive advantage, but there is little evidence of aftermarket lock-in.
