scores.rationale: New well-capitalised entrants and an active discount war in the fastest-growing segment, with management openly willing to price irrationally, indicate weak entry barriers and poor pricing rationality there even if the core is benign.
scores.quote: if we have to be irrational from time to time, we should be willing to be irrational as well

scores.rationale: A vast unorganized offline supply base is the donor pool — professionals earning ₹15,000-17,000 offline can be pulled onto the platform — but in InstaHelp the competitors are well-funded rather than weak.
scores.quote: to be able to get supply side from offline, where they are making around ■15,000 to ■17,000

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure: a headline IPO covered by Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Kotak, JM and BofA, with competitors raising capital specifically to attack the niche.
scores.quote: both your competitors raise money. In pockets, one could see competition getting irrational

scores.rationale: The brand commands a quality/trust premium (4.8 average rating, 83% of NTV from retained users) and a healthy take rate, but current pricing power is diluted by discounting in the growth segment.
scores.quote: our customer experience remains best-in-class with an average rating of 4.8 out of 5 across categories

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty in an unorganized market — selection, training, SOPs, 100% AI-audited proof of work — with management defining the category as a business of trust rather than price.
scores.quote: It's a service where the quality of the service professional, the training, the effort that you put into selection, onboarding, the details that you go in into SOPs, etc. These are the things that matter

scores.rationale: Densification has enabled UC Instant delivering core services in 30-60 minutes with app-owned customer intimacy across 60+ categories and 47 cities, an accessibility advantage rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: we've rolled out UC Instant, which is basically getting all our core services... between 30 to 60 minutes, so users don't have to wait and plan anymore

scores.rationale: Customers are retail households and the benefit stack is correctly matched — trust, ratings, brand and instant convenience — with repeat behaviour confirming fit (83% of NTV from retained users).
scores.quote: 83% of NTV now comes from retained users, a number that has only moved in one direction

scores.rationale: A real applied-AI layer across quality audit, partner support (55% automated), demand forecasting, fraud and code generation plus in-house Native product engineering, but this is operating leverage rather than a defensible multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: 55% of all partner support queries are now handled effectively through AI... more than 90% of our code is being shipped, by GenAI

scores.rationale: A measurable self-reinforcing two-sided density flywheel — utilisation rising 59→83→89 monetized hours, lowering cost to serve and fulfilment time, which in turn lifts demand — has driven four consecutive quarters of growth acceleration.
scores.quote: once you cross threshold density in a category in a micro-market... service professionals start getting utilized much better. Consequently, their earnings go up, and the cost to serve for the entire business comes down

scores.rationale: A trained service network spanning 60+ categories, 47 cities and hundreds of micro-markets is the reach rivals cannot replicate, and it is what makes the Native hardware business work where servicing is vital.
scores.quote: Native's strong performance has been underpinned by good product design, strong consumer proposition, and also the dependable Urban Company service network

scores.rationale: Sustained brownfield growth capex (INR 245cr FY25, INR 198cr FY26, INR 300cr planned over next 2 years) aimed at capacity plus value-added capability, with ROCE improving to 20.6%, though the volume payback has been slower than promised.
scores.quote: In next 2 years, we intend to spend close to INR 300 crore to increase our manufacturing capacity for elevator ropes

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.

A Global Development Center and customer-embedded R&D teams have produced identifiable new products (Ocean Fibre synthetic slings cash-positive in year one, GALSTAR, plasticated LRPC), though scale contribution is still nascent.
scores.quote: Our R&D teams are working closely with these customers to develop customized solutions enabling us to participate in more specialized and higher value requirements

scores.rationale: No acquisitions executed over the period despite opportunities in a distressed European market; management has only recently begun 'evaluating selective... inorganic opportunities', so there is no track record to score either way.
scores.quote: we are also evaluating selective organic and inorganic opportunities in markets where our footprint is still limited

scores.rationale: Dividends are paid and were called attractive by an analyst, but there is no buyback programme and no articulated distribution policy discussed on any call.
scores.quote: Congratulations to the management on delivering a strong set of results along with an attractive dividend payout

scores.rationale: This is a capital- and working-capital-heavy steel converter — ~194 net working capital days on INR 3,691cr revenue with large plant capex — so despite a decent 20.6% ROCE it is far from asset-light.
scores.quote: net working capital days improved to 194 days from 199 days last year and ROCE improved to 20.6%

scores.rationale: Long runway outside India (US share sub-5%, Europe ~8-9% versus 65-70% at home) with concrete capture evidence in elevator/crane/mining ropes and premium European OEMs, though overall rope volumes grew only ~5%.
scores.quote: still our market share in the U.S. is sub 5%. So, there is tremendous opportunity for growth

scores.rationale: Credible multi-year expansion — Saudi rigging built to ~60 new customers, US topline share up 7%→9%, international revenue to 57% — though Saudi ramp lagged the 4,000t target and the Middle East hit a war-driven setback.
scores.quote: Since starting our Rigging business there, we have added around 60 new customers

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly mix- and realization-led rather than volume-led: EBITDA/ton rose from ~INR 30,100 to ~INR 34,100 and margins from 17.2% to 19.1% while rope volumes grew only ~5%, and management deliberately walks away from low-value GP rope tonnage.
scores.quote: tonnage growth is not always linear, but we do have better quality of revenue with stronger realizations and healthier margins

scores.rationale: Several end-markets are at or near cyclical troughs with identifiable upturns ahead — Middle East demand depressed by conflict with reconstruction optionality, plus an oil-and-offshore energy-security tailwind.
scores.quote: Volumes in the Middle East came in below normal levels... More countries are prioritizing energy security and that is driving demand that we are well positioned to capture

scores.rationale: Core end-markets — Indian infrastructure, ports, Tier-2/3 city elevators, mining and offshore energy — are in durable secular expansion, though wire rope demand ultimately tracks industrial capex rather than a pure secular category.
scores.quote: the continued growth in infrastructure activity, port expansion and advancement of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities is expected to drive demand

scores.rationale: Consistently organic and prudent across the period: net debt of INR 124cr in FY24 taken to net cash of INR 332cr by FY26, capex funded from internal accruals, no acquisitions, and capex only 'where demand visibility is clear'.
scores.quote: we closed the year with a consolidated net cash position of INR 332 crore and with standalone operations now entirely debt free

scores.rationale: The multi-year 'One Usha Martin' restructuring, Ranchi expansion and long OEM qualification programmes were pursued through weak cycles and are now visibly in the numbers, though volume guidance (e.g. 15% growth in FY24) repeatedly proved optimistic.
scores.quote: Our 'One Usha Martin' program is now showing up clearly in the numbers. Fixed employee costs came down 3% and administrative expenses declined by over 7%

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and metric-driven with no personality promotion, and the company runs a deliberately unglamorous industrial niche.
scores.quote: I will begin with a summary of the quarter and then share our perspective on the drivers behind the performance

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development or leadership pipeline; workforce mentions are limited to redundancy provisions and Wage Code costs.

Management quantifies shortfalls and one-offs rather than burying them (INR 4cr redundancy, INR 13cr Wage Code, the 900t Middle East volume miss) and openly explains the deliberate choice to forgo GP rope tonnage, though it has been slow to concede repeated volume-guidance misses.
scores.quote: the rope volumes came in lower than our expectations... that did have an impact of about 900 ton or so for this particular quarter

scores.rationale: Margin and cash improvements are genuinely attributable to identifiable management actions (mix shift, One Usha Martin cost cuts, deleveraging), but stagnant rope volumes and steel-price pass-through mean results should not be read as unqualified skill.
scores.quote: for the last few years, I think our volume in Wire Rope is almost stagnant

scores.rationale: Dominant domestic position (~65-70% share) and an entrenched place in specialised applications backed by field-performance references and aftermarket rigging services, though it is not monopoly-like in export markets.
scores.quote: we already have 65% to 70% market share

scores.rationale: Long OEM qualification cycles and rigging/value-added services create genuine switching costs and recurring, sticky demand once approvals are secured.
scores.quote: customer qualification cycles are longer, but once established, they tend to be more stable and recurring

scores.rationale: The industry is fragmented and price-competitive at the low end — Asian pricing pressure in US general-purpose ropes and margin pressure from European competitors — so no stable oligopoly protects pricing.
scores.quote: we are seeing some competition in the US market particularly and also some pricing pressure from other Asian manufacturers

scores.rationale: Approval-gated, engineering-heavy value-added segments create real entry barriers and management refuses to fight on price, but the commodity GP rope and LRPC segments remain exposed to discounting.
scores.quote: it is not that we are losing on price to competition. It is a deliberate policy that if I have orders of the higher value-added products, we focus on servicing those customers

scores.rationale: Weak European rope makers in recession and the absence of US domestic capacity provide identifiable share donors that Usha Martin has been converting into orders.
scores.quote: Right now, Europe is going through a recession and many companies are going through a difficult period. I think there are big opportunities for us... to gain market share

scores.rationale: Specialty wire rope is an unglamorous, capital-light-attention niche with an under-covered mid-cap profile that attracts little competitive capital.
scores.quote: As a Specialty Wire Rope Solutions provider with a substantial presence in International markets

scores.rationale: Demonstrated pricing power — full pass-through of rising steel and gas costs with margins still expanding to 21.6% — driven by engineering reputation and the Brunton Shaw brand rather than commodity positioning.
scores.quote: we have been able to pass on the increase for the wire segment, LRPC segment... we have been able to expand our margins even in this situation where prices have been increasing

scores.rationale: Core value-added segments (mining, elevator, crane, oil and offshore) are safety-critical purchases where customers buy proven reliability and field-performance track record, explicitly not price.
scores.quote: higher traction in elevator ropes, crane ropes and oil and offshore ropes, where requirements are more engineering-driven and less price led

scores.rationale: Dedicated rigging shops across Europe, Middle East and Southeast Asia plus direct India-to-Europe supply improve service levels and deepen customer intimacy, deliberately increasing stickiness.
scores.quote: Focus on value-added services for customers through our dedicated rigging shops in Europe, Middle East, Southeast Asia, thereby also improving customer stickiness and margins

scores.rationale: The customer base is overwhelmingly corporate/OEM and the benefit offered matches it — reliability, engineering support and approval-based lock-in rather than consumer-style intangibles.
scores.quote: we are also working on more OEM approvals in the value-added segment, which is our focus, for example, in elevators, cranes

scores.rationale: Genuine engineering depth across multiple products — large-diameter offshore ropes, the record single-reel Oceanmax project, synthetic Ocean Fibre, GALSTAR, plasticated LRPC — although R&D intensity is never quantified and the edge is process rather than proprietary IP.
scores.quote: we executed a landmark Oceanmax project at our Ranchi facility, including the largest single reel rope production ever undertaken

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the business model.

A genuinely global service and distribution footprint — manufacturing in India, UK and Thailand, rigging shops across three regions, 57% international revenue and channel partner networks in India — in a category where service matters, though European and American rivals have comparable reach.
scores.quote: International revenues now account for 57% of total topline, up from 55% last year

scores.rationale: Real growth investment in branches, UFCs and cloud/IT is happening but incremental returns are not yet visible — core PAT is roughly flat while costs rise.
scores.quote: since we have expanded close to around 90 UFCs in the last one and a half years, that has obviously increased our costs

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P (investor awareness programmes, Dainik Jagran, a Google partnership reaching 10 crore individuals) has not converted into sales, with gross-sales share falling from 7.79% in FY24 to 6.1% in FY26.
scores.quote: our digital marketing partnership with Google has expanded us to reach over 10 crore s unique individuals over the past nine months

scores.rationale: Product/research investment is deliberate and steady (smart beta, Balanced Advantage, Multicap, G-Sec ETFs, expanded equity research), but the payoff in AUM per launch is modest.
scores.quote: Our product development philosophy has always centred on delivering differentiated investment solutions rather than simply expanding the number of schemes.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across any of the twelve calls — growth is entirely organic and de novo (Paris, GIFT City, US registration), so there is no M&A record to judge.
A coherent, disciplined and explicitly repeatable distribution policy — Rs 40/share dividend at a ~95% payout — though there are no opportunistic buybacks at low valuations.
scores.quote: we have been maintaining a very healthy pay-out ratio of the profit in excess of 95%. I think hopefully that will continue.

scores.rationale: The AMC model is genuinely asset-light with high core margins (core EBITDA Rs 171cr on Rs 308cr standalone core revenue in Q1FY27), but the protecting moat is weak given continuous yield and share erosion.
scores.quote: The core EBITDA stood at Rs 171 crores for the first quarter of FY26 -27

scores.rationale: Runway exists (only ~5-6% share, not dominant) but the four-year trajectory is share loss — gross-sales share 7.79% FY24 to 6.1% FY26, and equity QAAUM +5.46% vs industry AUM +12.6%.
scores.quote: market share of 5.5% of the gross sales of the industry during this quarter and market share of 6.1% of the gross sales for the financial year FY26

scores.rationale: Domestic tier-2/3 expansion has been executed at net-zero incremental cost, but the international build-out (Paris, SEC registration, GIFT City) has coincided with UTI International AUM roughly halving from Rs 27,645cr in FY24 to Rs 14,027cr in Q1FY27.
scores.quote: expanded our geographic presence in a calibrated manner while maintaining net zero incremental costs

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led into low-yield passives (index/ETF QAAUM +24.86% vs equity +5.46%, at ~8bps vs 72-73bps) with management guiding to structural yield dilution since 2022, though recent TER cuts were passed on without margin loss.
scores.quote: we may see some bit of dilu tion in the management yield number going forward

scores.rationale: Earnings are market-beta linked and the company is describing a resilient, high-level market after a multi-year surge, not a position near a cyclical bottom with an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: The year FY25 -26 has been a year of resilience in investor behavior, even as markets have witnessed volatility.

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — industry AAUM from Rs 37.7 lakh crore (Jun 2022) to Rs 84.2 lakh crore (Jun 2026), folios to ~28 crore, and monthly SIPs of Rs 32,087 crore.
scores.quote: the financialization of savings is clearly sustaining momentum

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, no leverage or M&A, headcount cut from 1,402 to 1,248 via VRS, supervisory ratio improved 1:1 to 1:5, and continued investment in branches/tech through a weak share period.
scores.quote: Our total employee strength, which stood at 1,402 employees as of March 2024, is now at 1,248 as of March 2026.

scores.rationale: A long-horizon plan exists (Mission 2031) and institutional mandates were re-won for a third consecutive EPFO term, but four years of stated market-share ambition have produced share loss and repeated MD/CEO turnover.
scores.quote: our Mission 2031 strategy, to transform UTI AMC into a larger, more competitive, technology -enabled... organi sation

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently low-key and operational — no celebrity framing, with even the new CEO deflecting credit to the platform and team rather than himself.
scores.quote: I would like to take a moment to thank UTI Shareholders, Board and Trustees for the confidence and trust they have reposed in me

scores.rationale: Systematic workforce renewal and an internal succession — frontline average age down 41 to 36, Gen Z from 5% to 38% of staff, and a CEO promoted after nearly a decade inside the firm.
scores.quote: the average age of the team has dropped from 41 years in FY21 to 36 years in FY26. And Gen Z now makes up 38% of the workforce

scores.rationale: Management quantifies one-offs and adverse drivers unprompted (VRS/family pension Rs 130cr, labour code Rs 4cr, commission over-estimation, yield dilution) and gives forward cost run-rate guidance, though it occasionally labels rising costs as 'investment' and declines some data requests.
scores.quote: there is a one -off on account of VR S and family pension. The total quantum of that is close to around Rs. 130 crores

scores.rationale: Headline results flatter the operator — FY24 PAT rose 75% on a 35% industry AUM surge while core PAT rose only 8%, and consolidated normalized core PAT actually fell from Rs 492cr (FY25) to Rs 452cr (FY26), so skill is hard to separate from market beta.
scores.quote: the consolidated net profit was ■ 766 crore , Higher by 75% YoY... the consolidated core PAT was ■ 345 crore , up by 8% YoY

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind — UTI is a mid-single-digit share player in a crowded 40-plus AMC market and its gross-sales share keeps slipping.
scores.quote: UTI was able to capture a market share of 5.5% of the gross sales of the industry during this quarter

scores.rationale: Some captive/sticky elements exist (5-year EPFO and CMPFO mandates, sticky SIP book of 29.53 lakh folios), but the Rs 3.16 lakh crore PMS outflow on an EPFO mandate revision shows how little lock-in there really is.
scores.quote: The implementation of the revised EPFO mandate and consequent transfer of assets led to a decline of Rs 3,16,000 crores in the PMS AUM

scores.rationale: The pension/PMS side is a licensed near-oligopoly (one of two CMPFO managers, 24% of NPS AUM), but the end customer holds the negotiating power through open competitive bidding, and the mutual fund side is fragmented.
scores.quote: both the EPFO and CMPFO concluded the process of appointing new portfolio managers through an open bidding system

scores.rationale: Pricing is structurally irrational and regulator-driven — NFO price distortion, 50-85% of fees surrendered to distributors, TER/exit-load cuts and persistent yield dilution across the four years.
scores.quote: the industry had witnessed lesser NFOs where the pricing structure get s distorted

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified to take share from; on the evidence UTI has itself been the donator, with equity AUM growing at less than half the industry rate.
scores.quote: Our equity quarterly average AUM for March 2026 stood at Rs. 95,824 crores, rising by 5.46%

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered listed AMC in India's most fashionable financial-services niche, fielding questions from ICICI Prudential, Investec, Centrum, B&K and Equirus — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Uday Pai from Investec.

scores.rationale: The 60-year-old UTI brand and high structural gross margins are real, but there is no pricing power — TER changes are passed straight through and yields have compressed from ~41bps toward the low 70s on equity.
scores.quote: whatever the impact of the TER changes has been there, we have passed on the impact to all our intermediaries

scores.rationale: Institutions buy UTI for reliability, evidenced by a third consecutive EPFO term, a second consecutive CMPFO term, a clean credit book and low tracking difference in passives.
scores.quote: For the third consecutive term, UTI AMC was selected as one of the portfolio managers for EPFO.

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — presence in 699 districts, ~270 branches skewed to B30, plus AI contact centre, WhatsApp payments and eight-language communication.
scores.quote: the breadth of our distribution franchise with presence in 699 district s across India

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is reasonably matched: convenience and vernacular digital access for the 1.42 crore retail folio base, and reliability/track-record for corporate mandates (EPFO, CMPFO, NPS).
scores.quote: We added approximately 3.89 lakh folios, taking our total live folio base to 1.42 crore s.

scores.rationale: Credible, measurable tech execution — VAANI automating ~60% of inbound calls, first Indian AMC with in-app WhatsApp payments, 31% lower cost per transaction — though these are replicable rather than a deep proprietary edge.
scores.quote: a 234% increase in revenue, 33% increase in transactions, and a 31% reduction in cost per transaction

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing two-sided network is evidenced; scale in AUM has not compounded into share, as AUM growth trailed the industry despite a far larger asset base.
scores.quote: our mutual fund franchise continued to strengthen with quarterly average AUM reaching Rs 3,92,691 crores

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is management's most defensible asset — 21-23% of AUM from B30 versus 16-18% for the industry, 108 of 167 UFCs in B30 in 2022 and ~90 UFCs added since — but it has not yet been converted into share gains.
scores.quote: 23.3% of our Monthly Average AUM for June 2022 came from B30 cities while the industry stood at 16.6%

scores.rationale: Large, rising greenfield growth capex (Rs 300cr Dadri cell line delivered in six months under a Rs 400cr budget, Rs 272cr Ratlam, Rs 350cr TOPCon planned) that coincided with revenue +72.3% and EBITDA margin expanding 16.1%→18.5%, indicating healthy incremental returns rather than maintenance spend.
scores.quote: we had targeted total budget of solar cell line was around Rs. 400 crores, while we completed this line in around Rs. 300 crores

scores.rationale: A&P is limited to a newly signed cricketer brand ambassador with no spend disclosure or track record of durable equity, while management itself attributes demand to word-of-mouth and service rather than advertising.
scores.quote: we are also delighted to welcome Surya Kumar Yadav as our brand ambassador for Fujiyama Solar

scores.rationale: R&D is described only qualitatively (500+ SKUs, service-engineer feedback loops, three years of AI in the sales network) with no R&D spend, pipeline or efficiency evidence, and the cell technology chosen was the older Mono-PERC rather than a proprietary edge.
scores.quote: we are adopting AI in our sales network. We have been working on AI for 3 years

scores.rationale: No acquisitions, bolt-ons or inorganic transactions are mentioned anywhere across the three calls.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed; the company is in a capital-absorbing phase using IPO proceeds for debt repayment and capex.

Asset turn is deteriorating as the model becomes capital-heavier — total assets more than doubled to Rs 23,436mn against 72% revenue growth, ROCE fell from ~40% to ~25% on lower asset turnover, and working capital days rose from 71 to 83 — offset by a genuine distribution/service moat.
scores.quote: the growth that we achieved in the ROCE and ROE in the past, is due to the higher asset turnover

scores.rationale: A small player with large runway growing far above the 40-45% industry CAGR (revenue +72.3%, 400,000+ households added, channel base to 8,900), with half its geography untapped and the new DCR cell line opening the previously inaccessible subsidy segment.
scores.quote: 50% of our area is untapped

scores.rationale: Credible, well-executed domestic expansion — new distributors/dealers/Shoppes each quarter, entry into Tier 1 via on-grid, and a stated plan to double channel partners across India — but purely within India with no international/premium-brand travel evidence.
scores.quote: if we go for fully operational all over the India, then we are expecting double channel partners in next three years

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-driven with flat realisations, and management confirms all input cost movements are passed straight through rather than retained as price.
scores.quote: Yes, volume increase, sir.

scores.rationale: No identifiable cycle-bottom positioning; the only cyclical references are an industry-wide module oversupply (which they consume captively) and a one-off GST-cut demand pause, neither framed as an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: oversupply of modules is coming

scores.rationale: End market is in clear secular expansion — India's 300GW-by-2030 target, ~25GW of untapped PM Surya Ghar opportunity, rising grid instability and a 40-45% projected rooftop CAGR.
scores.quote: With over 7 million installations still untapped under PM Surya Ghar Yojana, this represents close to 25 gigawatt of incremental opportunity

scores.rationale: Entirely organic growth with no M&A, deleveraging post-IPO to 0.25x net debt/equity and capex delivered under budget, tempered by a short listed track record and a rising inventory/working-capital build.
scores.quote: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.25 as of March 2026 compared to 0.85 in FY25

scores.rationale: Thirty-year operating history in which they created the off-grid rooftop category themselves from 2008 inverter-plus-solar-charge-controller education, and deliberately cede AMC economics to dealers to build multi-decade channel loyalty.
scores.quote: We have started the whole market from zero

scores.rationale: Promoter-managers speak plainly and operationally, decline to give bold guidance and avoid self-promotion, though the company has begun buying visibility through a celebrity endorsement post-listing.
scores.quote: Historically, if we see, we have grown year on year and we will try better and better every time.

scores.rationale: Decent employee orientation — 600+ field service engineers, hiring ahead of new capacity, and redeploying Bawal staff after the fire — but no systematic talent development programme or internal leadership pipeline is described.
scores.quote: the company is facilitating to transfer the employees to other manufacturing facilities to ensure the continuity of employment

scores.rationale: Generally candid: they admitted the GST-cut sales were permanently lost, disclosed BIS seizures, the Bawal fire and the Ratlam inverter/battery line delays, and refused to quantify cell-line savings before ramp-up — though they withhold segment-wise revenue splits.
scores.quote: What happens is that the sale that is lost, is lost.

scores.rationale: Results are heavily tailwind-driven — management itself concedes the growth came from a market expanded by government awareness rather than share capture — and the first-post-IPO glow of 72% growth sits against falling ROCE, volume-only growth and inventory build.
scores.quote: market share did not increase, the market increased

scores.rationale: Brand trust with ~1 million customers in specific rural/Tier 2-3 pockets, but no monopoly-like position and the aftermarket/service annuity is deliberately handed to dealers rather than captured.
scores.quote: we tell our dealer-distributor that you pay less attention to earning on the service

scores.rationale: System-level lock-in exists because customers buy inverter, battery and panel as one matched package from the same brand, creating modest switching costs reinforced by the local dealer relationship.
scores.quote: the customer wants the battery and panel of the same company for which we take solar inverter

scores.rationale: The rooftop market is fragmented and attracting many new entrants including large groups like Tata Power, with no stable oligopoly structure.
scores.quote: there are so many players who have announced or forayed into rooftop solar market

scores.rationale: Low entry barriers with heavy capacity addition and module oversupply industry-wide, and management openly welcomes all comers rather than pointing to any structural deterrent.
scores.quote: There are a lot of opportunities, everyone is welcome.

scores.rationale: Weak/unequipped competitors exist — the DCR cell demand-supply gap and looming ALMM 2 mandate leave rivals without domestic cell capacity, from whom Fujiyama's new captive cell lines can take subsidy-segment share.
scores.quote: DCR cells are very, the demand and supply gap is very high

scores.rationale: The off-grid backup niche in towns and villages is genuinely under-served by subsidy-focused on-grid players, but the solar sector overall is a magnet for capital and the company has just IPO'd and signed a celebrity ambassador.
scores.quote: Our major sale is, sir, in towns and villages

scores.rationale: Positioning is value-for-money rather than image-led, with all raw-material price moves passed through to customers and mid-teens-to-18% EBITDA margins, indicating functional rather than intangible pricing power.
scores.quote: we ensure that we look at value for money for the customer

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and backup certainty for an unreliable grid, and management attributes repeat purchase to on-time service and trust rather than price, backed by 600+ field service engineers.
scores.quote: When people are happy with services, they tell other people.

scores.rationale: Exceptional last-mile access — 8,900+ channel partners, exclusive Shoppe outlets handling sizing/installation/financing, 500 SKUs stocked and a 24-hour dispatch commitment.
scores.quote: as soon as the order comes, we immediately have the complete target of dispatching it within 24 hours

scores.rationale: Over 90% retail B2C, correctly matched with local dealer intimacy, service assurance and financing support rather than corporate TCO selling, though the retail hook is service reliability more than brand intangibles.
scores.quote: Our B2C business remains the core driver of scale, contributing over 90% of revenue in H1 FY26

scores.rationale: Real breadth in power electronics with 500+ SKUs, but the cell technology chosen was trailing-edge Mono-PERC selected for speed and cost while peers move to TOPCon, and no R&D intensity is disclosed.
scores.quote: if we go for Mono-PERC, we can complete the line within six months

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network exists; the business is a conventional one-way channel-push model through distributors, dealers and Shoppes.
scores.quote: our major business is channel driven we have business with distributors, dealers and shoppers

scores.rationale: The clearest moat: 8,900+ channel partners plus 600+ service engineers feeding R&D, exclusive Shoppes and 24-hour dispatch in a category where after-sales service drives repeat purchase, built over decades and explicitly hard to replicate.
scores.quote: our total channel partners network has crossed 8,900 as on March 2026

scores.rationale: Almost all capex is growth capex — 74 stores in FY25, 136 in FY26 and 170-200 guided for FY27 at ~Rs. 2.6-2.8 cr per store — funded largely by internal accruals while ROE rose from 10.7% (FY24) to 26% (FY26), indicating high incremental returns.
scores.quote: During FY '26, we added 136 stores... ROE continues to improve and now stands at 26% compared to 23.2% in FY '25 and around 10.7% in FY '24

scores.rationale: A&P is deliberately kept below 1% of sales with most 'marketing' being customer gifts/discounts booked in COGS, so brand equity is built by price-value rather than by durable advertising investment.
scores.quote: So, it's less than 1% of total sales... Because we have understood that the product is the best brand ambassad[or]

scores.rationale: No R&D line exists, but there is an analogous and improving product-design capability — own-design merchandise rising from 35-40% toward a targeted 60% by summer 2026 and 80% by 2027 — with no disclosed efficiency metrics to judge it.
scores.quote: Our own design products contributed about 35% to 40% this year and we target it to reach around 60% by the summer of 2026 and 80% by 2027

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with no acquisitions in the period; the only corporate action is an internal simplification — shutting three manufacturing units and merging the subsidiary into the standalone retail entity.
scores.quote: because now, we have shut down three manufacturing units... we are going to merge both the entities now

scores.rationale: There is no dividend or buyback policy discussed; capital flowed the other way with a Rs. 400 crore QIP raised at peak valuations after a 60%+ growth run, and management flags further debt or equity for expansion.
scores.quote: The company successfully raised approximately Rs. 400 crores through a QIP with marquee investors

scores.rationale: Asset turn is genuinely high and improving — leased stores, sales rising to Rs. 1,200 psf/month in mature stores, inventory down to ~90 days and ROE at 26% — but the moat protecting it is thin given competition at nearly every location.
scores.quote: our older stores this year have already touched Rs. 1,200 per square feet of sales

scores.rationale: With only 325-350 stores against a fragmented unorganized base and much larger rivals, V2 has enormous runway and is demonstrably capturing share, growing 63% in FY26 versus a far slower market.
scores.quote: The 60% year-on-year revenue growth for the 4th Quarter significantly outpaces the broader market

scores.rationale: Disciplined, data-led entry into seven new states in FY26 (Punjab, Rajasthan, Bengal, AP, Karnataka, Gujarat, Maharashtra) using a 4-5 store pilot before scaling, with new-state stores performing at par with the new-store average and negligible added logistics cost.
scores.quote: Whenever we enter a new state, we open about 4 to 5 stores there just to get a lot of data points... we had entered Karnataka, and now we have almost 15 to 16 stores there

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume and new-store led (47-53% volume growth, ASP still ~Rs. 300) with gross margin deliberately capped and price increases only passed through on input costs; the only mix gain is the rising full-price share.
scores.quote: we pass on all the benefits from our own production as well as private labels to the customers... we are targeting a gross margin percentage ranging from 27% to 29%

scores.rationale: Management describes a two-to-three year damp consumption cycle with GST cuts and government stimulus as an identifiable upturn ahead, though near-term demand has also been hit by war-related disruption.
scores.quote: with the GST trickle down effect and government trying to ramp up consumption, because it has been a little damp for the last two years to three years

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — the unorganized-to-organized shift in Indian apparel retail, with organized retail guided to compound at 9-10% against 5-6% GDP over two decades.
scores.quote: India is poised to grow at 5%-6% GDP in the next 20 years and if you look at organized retail, it is poised to grow at 9%-10%

scores.rationale: Consistent organic focus, store-level EBITDA gating before expansion, low debt with expansion funded by internal accruals, no acquisitions, and exit from non-core manufacturing to concentrate on retail.
scores.quote: we don't want to chase just growth by compromising on profitability... not even a single store is EBITDA negative on a YTD level with the corporate cost

scores.rationale: A promoter team that rebuilt after the earlier Vishal Mega Mart failure has delivered against guidance for three straight years and explicitly frames current investment against a 20-year horizon, refusing to be swayed by short-term shocks.
scores.quote: what we are building today is not for the near term. We are building for our 20-year vision

scores.rationale: Communication is substance-heavy and metric-driven, but the CEO is openly the single public face, gives TV interviews and courted marquee QIP investors, so the company is no longer low-profile.
scores.quote: you seem to be a one man show... it's just that I have been the face of the investors and the community

scores.rationale: There is a data-driven review and appraisal culture with roughly six senior leaders of 10+ years tenure and vendor capability-building, but the pipeline is asserted rather than demonstrated and the earlier CEO hire (Manshu Tandon) did not last.
scores.quote: there would be at least six people who would be able to take the call if I am not available. And most of them have been with us for a journey of more than I think 10 years now

scores.rationale: Disclosure is unusually clear and self-correcting: reported versus Durga-Puja-normalized SSSG both given, pre-IndAS numbers volunteered for comparability, the audit qualification resolved via a write-off, and past mistakes at the prior venture openly owned.
scores.quote: Reported SSSG for Q3 stood at 2% and normalized SSSG adjusted for the Durga Puja shift stood at 12.8%

scores.rationale: Spectacular headline results make halo risk high — management itself cannot separate its own execution from a booming market, and the promoter's prior retail bankruptcy plus a share pledge argue for discounting the narrative.
scores.quote: now it's very hard to differentiate how much of that is because of our own strengths or the work that we have put or how much of that is the overall market growing

scores.rationale: V2 holds no monopoly-like position in the customer's mind or in any aftermarket; it competes as one of several value-fashion chains and concedes leadership only in a narrow Rs. 300 ASP price band.
scores.quote: there is competition from each space, I would say, whether it's Vishal, V-Mart, Zudio

scores.rationale: There are effectively no switching costs in value apparel and almost no protected regional pockets — fewer than 20 of 304 stores face no organized competition, and management treats competition as a permanent given.
scores.quote: out of 304 stores that we have now, there would be less than 20 stores where we do not have any organized competition. Because competition has become the new reality

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly, with unorganized mom-and-pop stores plus Zudio, Vishal, V-Mart, Style Baazar and Trend all competing, and management expects room for five or six national players.
scores.quote: in India the market is big enough to easily accommodate five-six big national players

scores.rationale: Barriers to entry in value apparel retail are low and rivals keep expanding, though pricing behaviour is relatively rational — V2 sells ~90% at full price and competes on cost structure rather than discount wars.
scores.quote: full price sales contributing 92%, which reflects the strength of our proposition and reduced dependence on discounting

scores.rationale: A large pool of weak donors exists in the unorganized mom-and-pop trade whose share is migrating to organized retail, and V2's per-square-foot sales run 25-30% ahead of its nearest organized competitor.
scores.quote: the shift from unorganized to organized retail is accelerating... our per square feet sales are at least 25% to 30% higher than our nearest competition

scores.rationale: The company is no longer under the radar — a Rs. 400 crore QIP with marquee investors, dense sell-side coverage on calls and TV appearances mean capital and competitors are fully aware of the niche.
scores.quote: The company successfully raised approximately Rs. 400 crores through a QIP with marquee investors

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly cheapest-at-quality rather than image-driven, with gross margin deliberately capped at 28-30% and all input-cost inflation passed through rather than captured as premium.
scores.quote: we give maximum value to the customer. So, in a sense that means that we are the cheapest in that quality benchmark

scores.rationale: Private-label brand building aims at quality consistency and size standardization that customers can trust, but price remains the primary purchase driver rather than secondary to trust.
scores.quote: customers have size standardization, and they have that trust, so that whatever product they're buying of that brand will be of a certain quality

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the core customer benefit — 350+ stores pushed into underserved rural and Tier-2/3 markets with localized assortments, backed by a direct 8 crore customer database reached via WhatsApp/RCS/SMS.
scores.quote: we have a database of about 8 crore customers and we do reach them through WhatsApp, RCS, and SMS

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and is served with value and variety rather than the intangible/aspirational benefits the framework prefers for retail buyers, giving a partial rather than strong match.
scores.quote: V2 stands for value and variety... we have almost 2X the number of options offered to the consumers

scores.rationale: There is real and increasing investment in analytics-driven merchandising, supply chain systems and data-based reviews, but this is operational tooling rather than a deep, multi-product technology edge over rivals.
scores.quote: Our ongoing investments in analytics-driven merchandising, supply chain responsiveness, and operational discipline

scores.rationale: The model has no two-sided network — the 8 crore customer database is a one-way outreach list with no loyalty programme, and value to each shopper does not increase with other shoppers.
scores.quote: We don't have a loyalty program per se, but we have a database of about 8 crore customers

scores.rationale: A steadily strengthening zonal warehouse and supply chain network — vendor on-time delivery lifted from 40% to 70-75%, safety stock cut, negligible logistics cost into new states — but it is a scaling advantage, not one rivals like Trent or Vishal cannot match.
scores.quote: earlier our on-time delivery used to be just 40% and it has now increased to around 70% to 75%

scores.rationale: Growth spend is almost entirely opex (airtime, digital marketing) rather than capex, and management explicitly describes the manufacturing model as low-capex with spare capacity, so there is little rising growth capex to judge even though ROCE has recovered to 24%.
scores.quote: Jewelry manufacturing is a low capex model, to increase the production capacity for future growth, we can do that with very little capex

scores.rationale: Content/broadcasting and digital marketing spend compounded at ~23% against ~12% revenue growth, rising from 11% of sales in FY20 to 20% and staying there, with management conceding no leverage from the line — spend that has diluted returns more than it has built durable brand equity.
scores.quote: the CAGR growth in this line item is 23% whereas our revenues have only grown by half of that like 12%

scores.rationale: No R&D programme, spend or product-pipeline-from-R&D is discussed across the calls; technology commentary is limited to adopting AI tools in workflows.

Ideal World and Mindful Souls were small, complementary bolt-ons integrated into VGL's supply chain, and both moved to profitability with Ideal World compounding double-digit growth and lifting UK EBITDA by 220bps.
scores.quote: Ideal World continued to be strong momentum with a healthy double-digit growth of 15%... Overall, U.K. EBITDA improved substantially by 220 basis points

scores.rationale: A consistent Rs.1.5/quarter dividend (Rs.6 for FY26, ~37% of FCF) shows a steady policy, but with the stock down from ~1,000 to ~230 management gave no commitment on buybacks when an investor asked.
scores.quote: our stock price is down really from the peak from 1,000 to 230-odd. We would request the management to go for a buyback

scores.rationale: Asset-light model (low-capex manufacturing, net cash Rs.296cr, ROCE 24%, record FCF Rs.272cr) but the protecting moat is modest, since demand falls away when metal prices rise.
scores.quote: ROCE improved to 24% and ROE to 15%, reflecting much better profitability and disciplined capital allocation

scores.rationale: Runway exists as a small player in large Western markets, but there is little evidence of actual share capture — unique customers were roughly flat (706k, +2%) and volumes fell 9-10% YoY with US up only 1% and UK negative.
scores.quote: volumes have declined across the board in both TV and digital by about 9% to 10% Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: Germany was executed to breakeven and Ideal World scaled well, but breakeven slipped repeatedly from the FY24 guidance to full-year FY26, a four-year drag on group margin, and India entry remains deferred.
scores.quote: Germany, we have already guided breakeven in H2 of FY24 ... The Germany business achieved EBITDA breakeven for FY '26

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely price/mix-led — ASPs up ($32 to $38 digital), lab-grown diamonds at 11% of retail at $250 ASP, in-house brands past 50% — though the volume decline partly reflects weak demand rather than pure pricing power.
scores.quote: volume has a degrowth, but the realization is pretty good with the lab-grown products

scores.rationale: The business is operating through a trough of soft discretionary spending and spiking metal prices, with identifiable upturn levers named (India-UK/EU FTAs, easing US-China tariffs) and margins already inflecting off the low.
scores.quote: The India, U.K. and India EU free trade agreements... all create a favorable environment for a vertically integrated retailers like us

scores.rationale: Digital/social commerce is a genuine secular tailwind (digital now 44% of B2C, targeting 50%), but roughly 56-58% of sales still sit on structurally declining TV home shopping with cord-cutting.
scores.quote: Digital contribution stood at around 44% of B2C sales for the year

scores.rationale: Consistently net cash (Rs.158cr in FY25 to Rs.296cr in FY26), only small bolt-on acquisitions, and continued investment through the downturn in Germany, OTA and digital.
scores.quote: Net cash position stood at INR296 crores as of 31st March 2026

scores.rationale: Twenty-five years listed with a consistent 4R framework, persistence through four years of German losses to breakeven, and long-dated commitments like 1 million meals a day by FY40 — though repeated mid-teens growth/margin promises went unmet for years.
scores.quote: we have achieved the milestone of completing 25 years of public listing

scores.rationale: Low-profile Jaipur-based promoter management running plain, numbers-first calls with no celebrity positioning, focused on operating metrics and ESG substance.
scores.quote: The number of customers, repeat purchase, the retention rate and the reach, therefore, are the b

scores.rationale: Group-wide Great Place to Work certification and process/AI-led productivity gains sit against very heavy senior churn — five MDs exited across FY21-FY25 plus CFO and IR head changes — suggesting a thin internal pipeline.
scores.quote: all our group entities across India, U.S., U.K., Germany and China are now Great Place to Work certified

scores.rationale: Disclosure is detailed and management answers hostile questions on cost lines directly and enhanced segmental reporting, but repeated resets of guidance (mid-teens growth and mid-teens EBITDA, Germany breakeven) are re-issued rather than owned as misses.
scores.quote: we reiterate our previously provided guidance of mid-single-digit revenue growth, while maintaining mid-teens revenue growth in the long run

scores.rationale: Little halo risk to strip away — EBITDA margin fell from ~14-15% to 7% and has only recovered to 10.8%, and recent gains are traceable to cost cuts, mix and the Germany turnaround rather than to demonstrated pricing skill.
scores.quote: our margin is steadily improving from 7% to 11% from FY '23 to '26

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind or in aftermarket; it is a deep-discount value retailer competing for discretionary spend that customers freely defer.
scores.quote: consumer confidence compelled the consumers to defer discretionary purchases

scores.rationale: There are no switching costs or captive aftermarket — retention is only ~38-40% and customers migrate freely to Meta, TikTok, Apple and Google-discovered alternatives.
scores.quote: Customers are increasingly discovering, evaluating and purchasing through platforms like Meta, Apple, TikTok and Google

scores.rationale: VGL is a small value player in fragmented Western e-commerce/TV retail, not a member of a stable oligopoly, and the retail customer has unlimited alternatives.
scores.quote: the retail landscape continued to shift rapidly towards digital-first customer discovery

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low in discount jewelry e-commerce and pricing power sits with counterparties — VGL had to exit two broadcast services over airtime price negotiation and pays up for better channel positions.
scores.quote: 2 broadcast services we had, we exited them because there were some price negotiation could not be completed

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are available to take share from — VGL bought the distressed Ideal World UK channel and has grown it 12-15% while turning it profitable on VGL's supply chain.
scores.quote: Ideal World continues to deliver strong revenue growth, supported by a wider assortment of products and in-house sourcing capabilities

scores.rationale: A humble, unglamorous niche — deep-discount gemstone jewelry sold on low-power OTA antenna channels — that large capital largely ignores, giving VGL room to buy airtime and assets cheaply.
scores.quote: getting such opportunities in OTA households is not very easy and it comes with a time

scores.rationale: Gross margins of 63-66% are genuinely high and in-house brands now exceed 50% of B2C sales, but the proposition is explicitly deep-discount value rather than image, and demand is not steady — it drops when metal prices rise.
scores.quote: our deep discounts and value positioning worked well in various kinds of economic cycles

scores.rationale: Some reliability benefit from vertical integration and product availability when rivals faced supply constraints, but price, not trust, is the core purchase driver for these customers.
scores.quote: It is helping us with increased product availability, while many other retailers battle with supply chain constraints

scores.rationale: Strong accessibility and direct customer intimacy — 127mn TV households plus web, apps, OTT, social and marketplaces, with Budget Pay EMI at ~38% of B2C revenue driving stickier omni-channel customers.
scores.quote: Budget Pay option allowing customers to purchase products on EMI basis, has proven valuable and contributing 38% of our B2C revenue

scores.rationale: Purely retail customers served with discount/value and convenience rather than the intangible brand pull the framework prefers for retail, though the in-house brand push to 50% is a partial move in that direction.
scores.quote: our in-house brands have crossed 50% of our B2C sales, a year ahead of our earlier target

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge — AI use is generic adoption of third-party tools for marketing, HR productivity and content, with no R&D intensity behind it.
scores.quote: we expanded the use of AI across customer engagement, marketing optimization, analytics, content creation, merchandising and operational workflows

scores.rationale: The model is one-sided retail with no self-reinforcing network; if anything, VGL depends on third-party platforms' networks (Meta, TikTok) for customer acquisition.
scores.quote: paid social media emerging as one of the most important channel for customer acquisition

scores.rationale: A distribution and sourcing footprint rivals would struggle to replicate — 127mn TV households across three countries plus OTA/OTT/digital, backed by owned manufacturing and supply relationships in 30 countries.
scores.quote: Our vertically integrated supply chain network spanning 30 countries is the backbone of our business and a key differentiator

scores.rationale: Capex was deliberately held far below depreciation for years while deleveraging (FY24 ~INR200cr vs INR380cr depreciation), but is now stepping up to INR450-500cr on the back of the highest-ever order book, with reported ROCE of 24-29%.
scores.quote: The CapEx, I think overall will be at least to the tune of between INR 450-500 crores, is what we see as the overall CapEx for this year.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand-promotion spend across the calls; Varroc is a B2B OEM supplier.

R&D repeatedly converts into commercialised products and new order wins — EFI developed in record time, traction motors/controllers industrialised first-time-right, 130+ patents, and EV-linked wins now 65-75% of intake.
scores.quote: In the 9 months, we filed close to 15 patents, taking the tally to 130 plus.

scores.rationale: No bolt-on acquisitions in the period — capital action has been divestment (VLS 4-wheeler lighting sold in 2022, Italian forging business now being shopped) and an internal subsidiary merger, so the parameter is neutral rather than demonstrated.
scores.quote: Separately, we are also looking out for suitable opportunities to find a proper buyer.

scores.rationale: Distribution has only just restarted after deleveraging — dividend raised from 100% to 150% of face value in FY26 — with no buyback programme or articulated long-run distribution policy.
scores.quote: the board of directors have recommended a 150% of the face value as dividend for financial year 2026

scores.rationale: Management explicitly runs an asset-sweating model — capex below depreciation, orders taken to fill existing capacity, ROCE 24.4% in FY26 — but the underlying moat is thin given 46% Bajaj dependence.
scores.quote: All these business wins helps us to fill the existing capacity and sweat our assets even more.

scores.rationale: India operations outgrew the industry for several years (FY24 +14.5% vs industry) and EV content is compounding at ~50%, though Q3FY26 India growth of 12.3% lagged industry growth of 15-20% on ICE mix.
scores.quote: our India operations continued to outperform the industry growth with a growth of over 14.5%

scores.rationale: Overseas expansion has been the chronic problem — Europe 4W lighting divested in 2022, Romania electronics and Italian forging still not at EBITDA breakeven four years later, with turnaround repeatedly pushed out to H2FY27.
scores.quote: Only in Romania we have significant challenge, and we should reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4... Italian forging business... may take maybe one more year

scores.rationale: There is no pricing power — raw-material moves are simply passed through to OEMs with a quarter's lag — so growth comes from volume plus a genuinely improving mix (EV content, 4W lighting, higher per-vehicle value).
scores.quote: there could be in some of the cases, there would be probably a lag of at least a quarter, but we are expecting to be compensated in full

scores.rationale: The Indian auto cycle Varroc rides is currently mid-to-strong rather than near a bottom (all segments growing double digits post-GST cut), while only the overseas piece is at a cyclical trough with a stated upturn ahead.
scores.quote: two-wheelers grew by 20.7%, three-wheelers grew by 32.4%, passenger vehicles grew by 11.3%

scores.rationale: Electrification is a genuine secular driver for Varroc's content per vehicle — EV-model revenue rose from 5.3% of sales in FY24 to ~13-14% in FY26 growing ~50% y/y, with 65% of record FY26 order intake EV-linked.
scores.quote: The revenue from EV models continues to be at around 13%, which again grew by 39% if you take full year.

scores.rationale: Delivered on the promised balance-sheet repair — net debt cut from ~INR2,700cr in FY23 to ~INR495cr with D/E 0.27, no big M&A, capex restraint and a VRS with a 4-year payback — though the 12% EBITDA promise made in 2022 is still unmet at 9.4% consolidated.
scores.quote: the net debt to equity ratio improved to 0.63 from 1.27... net debt to EBITDA also improved to 1.29

scores.rationale: Promoter-controlled management has stuck tenaciously with a multi-year plan — exit non-core Europe, deleverage, rebuild through EV/electronics wins — and is still funding the overseas turnaround rather than abandoning it.
scores.quote: we continue to strengthen our company for long-term growth and performance by taking appropriate decisions and meticulously executing them

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and unpromotional, run by the CFO and IR with detailed segment numbers and no celebrity framing or grand vision-selling.
scores.quote: My suggestion is, don't look at it on quarterly basis because there are several things which we accounted for on a full year basis

scores.rationale: Leadership pipeline is family succession (Arjun and Dhruv Jain installed as CEOs of the two business units) alongside churn of professional MDs/chairmen (Limaye, Kathuria exited FY25) and a 400-person VRS, with no evidence of systematic talent development.
scores.quote: MR. ARJUN JAIN – WHOLE-TIME DIRECTOR AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, BUSINESS UNIT 1 / MR. DHRUV JAIN – WHOLE-TIME DIRECTOR AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, BUSINESS UNIT 2

scores.rationale: Management volunteers bad news and quantifies one-offs — a provision against a defaulting EV customer, VRS and labour-code charges, and an unprompted admission that India growth lagged the industry on ICE mix.
scores.quote: I would say it's a combination of weaker performance on ICE versus EV for us. And also, I would say, driven really by mix and model changeovers.

scores.rationale: The optics of a strong turnaround should be discounted: most of the PBT improvement came from divesting the loss-making Europe business, interest-cost reduction and a buoyant Indian 2W cycle rather than demonstrated pricing or competitive skill.
scores.quote: significant PBT growth was also enabled by the interest cost reduction over a period of time and also strict capital controls

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like mindshare; the closest thing is a fast-growing, better-margin aftermarket business at ~10% of revenue, which is helpful but not dominant.
scores.quote: The aftermarket business... is paying a much faster growth and the profitability margins there is also pretty good. So that has now reached almost 10% of revenue

scores.rationale: Deep incumbency at Bajaj creates some stickiness and fast win-to-SOP capability, but the concentration runs against Varroc — the OEM holds the leverage, not the supplier.
scores.quote: Bajaj adds up to 46%

scores.rationale: Auto components is a fragmented supplier market where the end customer (OEM) sets terms — Varroc must wait a quarter for cost recovery and management concedes each OEM dictates its own recovery method.
scores.quote: Every OEM honestly operates differently. The method of recovery in every OEM will be different.

scores.rationale: Barriers are modest in polymers and lamps though higher in EV powertrain electronics; pricing is rational only in that it is OEM-administered cost pass-through, and overseas customer concentration has repeatedly exposed the business.
scores.quote: the Overseas Electronics, Lighting and the Forging business continues to face challenges due to customer concentration

scores.rationale: Varroc is visibly taking programmes off incumbents — 4W lighting from an incumbent OEM's supplier in India, headlamps for Thailand and high-voltage PCBA in Romania from global EV players — indicating weaker rivals to feed on.
scores.quote: the 4-Wheeler Lighting business for our Indian operations, from an incumbent OEM for its upcoming EV vehicle

scores.rationale: Not under the radar — the company is covered and hosted by multiple institutional brokers (Ambit, Investec, ICICI, Equirus) with active buy-side participation on every call.
scores.quote: hosted by Investec Capital Services

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power; gross margin swings with commodities and forex and is recovered only by negotiated pass-through, which management confirms drove the Q3FY26 gross-margin decline.
scores.quote: on the raw material, there's definitely a level of topic with respect to certain commodities and also FOREX, but those are largely passed through

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and speed of industrialisation — EFI delivered in record time, traction motors industrialised first-time-right, and management positions the company as a dependable global partner able to ramp win-to-SOP quickly.
scores.quote: our strength really is the ability to ramp from business win to SOP very quickly

scores.rationale: Proximity manufacturing to anchor customers plus a faster-growing, higher-margin aftermarket channel at ~10% of revenue gives real accessibility and customer intimacy, though it is not a decisive advantage.
scores.quote: The aftermarket business... has now reached almost 10% of revenue of continued operations, which is a good sign.

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/OEM, and Varroc matches it on engineering reliability and TCO, but without meaningful switching-cost lock-in given cost pass-through terms and 46% dependence on one buyer.
scores.quote: we continue to leverage our strong customer relationships, technology capabilities and expanding product portfolio

scores.rationale: A real multi-product technical edge is emerging — traction motors and controllers worth INR15,000+ per vehicle, EFI, HV PCBA for a global EV OEM, 130+ patents and separately reported R&D spend — though it is not yet reflected in pricing power.
scores.quote: we started mass production for both traction motor and traction controllers for our anchor customer. And the value of these two products put together is more than Rs. 15,000 per vehicle.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls bears on two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamics; the business model has no such mechanism discussed.

Distribution reach is ordinary for the sector — an aftermarket channel and a plant footprint across India, Romania, Italy, Vietnam and Thailand — with no evidence of service reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: our two-wheeler lighting business abroad, which has got plants in Italy primarily and Vietnam

scores.rationale: Sustained, large growth capex — greenfield plants in Bihar/Jammu (2022), Supa/Gorakhpur/Khordha/DRC (2024), and four more in CY2025 — running at near-full utilisation and funded while turning India net-debt-free with an AAA upgrade, indicating high incremental returns.
scores.quote: During CY 2025, we capitalized new CAPEX of ~Rs. 45,000 million

scores.rationale: Across all excerpts management discusses discounts, chilling equipment and outlet expansion but never A&P spend or brand-building investment, which sits with franchisor PepsiCo.

No R&D line or spend is discussed; innovation shown is packaging/formulation work (light-weighting, sugar reduction) and PepsiCo-owned launches such as Sting Classic and Ad-Rush rather than proprietary R&D output.
scores.quote: focus on reducing sugar content and the lightweighting packaging material

scores.rationale: BevCo (2024), Twizza and Crickley Dairy (2026) are complementary bottling/route-to-market bolt-ons in an existing region with a clear margin-improvement thesis, but they are not small relative to earnings and post-deal OPM gains remain unproven.
scores.quote: the focus is also on increasing the share of PepsiCo brands , which is a better contributor to top line and bottom line

scores.rationale: A consistent but token dividend policy (Rs. 0.50/share, ~Rs. 1,691 million) with no buybacks; cash is deliberately retained for capex and acquisitions.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, Rs. 0.50 per share

scores.rationale: The model is heavily asset-intensive — Rs. 45,000 million of plants in one year, 13+ backward-integrated factories, a million visi-coolers — so despite the protective PepsiCo franchise moat it is the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: capital work in progress and capital advances stood at the ap proximate level of Rs. 5,400 million

scores.rationale: Long runway from a low base — underpenetrated Indian territories acquired from PepsiCo and 1.8% PepsiCo share in South Africa — with a demonstrated capture record (Zimbabwe) and 300,000-500,000 new outlets added annually.
scores.quote: PepsiCo's market share is very meagre at 1.8% ... in Zimbabwe , but as we've mentioned in past calls, we achieved 71% market share

scores.rationale: Well-executed multi-year expansion across India's weak territories plus Morocco, Zimbabwe, Zambia, DRC and South Africa, with international volumes growing 21.4% in Q1 CY2026 and a repeatable playbook.
scores.quote: volume growth of 14.4% in India and 21.4% in international territories

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led with negative pricing/mix in India — realisation fell 4% in Q4 CY2025 and 1.5% in Q1 CY2026 on pack upsizing and Rs. 10 price points — and full-year CY2025 realisation rose just 0.5%.
scores.quote: In India, realization per case declined by a marginal 1.5%, primarily due to volume growth initiatives such as upsizing of packs

scores.rationale: The weather cycle bottomed in CY2025 (2.2% India volume growth, 'worst year') with a visible upturn already delivering 14.4% India volume growth in Q1 CY2026 against a soft base.
scores.quote: such a bad year, which was the worst year we have ever seen in the last few years in our industry

scores.rationale: Indian beverage consumption is in secular expansion off a low per-capita base, driven by demographics, incomes, urbanisation and a market-wide cold-chain build-out of ~1 million coolers a year.
scores.quote: we are very bullish on the Indian market, and we believe th e growth should continue in double-digits for the next 5-10 years at least

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage discipline (debt repaid from cash flows and QIP, India net debt-free, CRISIL AAA) and counter-cyclical investment through COVID, offset by a steady stream of overseas acquisitions rather than a purely organic focus.
scores.quote: the India business continued to remain net debt -free with free cash of ~Rs. 12,250 million ... CRISIL upgraded the company's long -term credit rating to AAA/stable

scores.rationale: Demonstrated tenacity and long-horizon thinking — investing through two washed-out COVID seasons, judging performance annually not quarterly, and a 30-year volume record — though strategic independence is bounded by the PepsiCo franchise relationship.
scores.quote: We have a history of consistent volume growth in the past 30 years, which is paramount for us.

scores.rationale: Calls are operational and substance-led, management declines to speculate about competitors or its own market share, and it withholds data it deems competitively sensitive rather than publicising it.
scores.quote: We would not like to comment on whether we have gained market share or lost market share

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline across any excerpt; the only people-related mentions are BevCo ESOPs and labour-code costs.

Candid about a bad season, negative realisation and discounting pressure, but persistently sandbags margin guidance (22-23% against a delivered 26%) and has withdrawn distribution disclosure, which analysts openly pushed back on.
scores.quote: But now we are at 26%. And frankly, no one takes that 22% - 23% number seriously.

scores.rationale: Headline results are materially aided by factors outside management skill — heat waves, election demand, low bases, PET price falls and an exclusive franchise — so execution quality cannot be cleanly separated from tailwinds.
scores.quote: The reason for this is, heat wave, elections , low base from the last year

scores.rationale: Exclusive PepsiCo bottling rights confer a monopoly on Pepsi-brand supply within each licensed territory, extended by dedicated Sting-only outlets and owned chilling assets in the trade.
scores.quote: 400,000 outlets additional got added because of our energy drink Sting and they are right now buying only Sting from us

scores.rationale: The franchise creates genuine regional exclusivity, and company-owned visi-coolers at over a million outlets create physical shelf lock-in, though retailers still stock rival colas alongside.
scores.quote: our exclusive customers and our visi-coolers, which is close to a million plus in the market

scores.rationale: Indian CSD is a concentrated few-player market but stability has weakened with Reliance's Campa entering and industry-wide discounting, and the end customer (retail trade) can switch.
scores.quote: there is Campa in the market , they are growing the volumes in the market , and even Coke is growing

scores.rationale: A well-capitalised new entrant has arrived and capacity additions triggered a discounting war in CY2025, evidencing weak entry barriers and periods of irrational pricing.
scores.quote: the discounting in the market has been much higher ... people end up discounting and throwing the kitchen sink

scores.rationale: Weak franchisees and low-share incumbents were a real donor pool historically (territories acquired from PepsiCo, sub-2% PepsiCo share in South Africa), but in India the current narrative is market expansion against strengthening rivals rather than taking share from weak players.
scores.quote: All the weak territories we had acquired from PepsiCo as well as the other franchisees are now showing results

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar — the calls are attended by Jefferies, CLSA, Kotak, JP Morgan, IIFL, Nuvama and Emkay, and the category is attracting large new capital from Reliance.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Vivek Maheshwari from Jefferies.

scores.rationale: Gross margins are high (~55%) on the strength of the Pepsi/Sting image, but realised pricing power is weak — the company is upsizing packs and adding Rs. 10 entry points rather than taking price, and the brand equity belongs to PepsiCo.
scores.quote: Our gross margin for the full year remained largely stable at 55.2%

scores.rationale: There is some reliability-based value for retailers — six months of international inventory cover and no stock-outs in peak season — but the consumer buys on impulse and price, not on assurance, and water is explicitly a commodity.
scores.quote: Water is like a commodity , you can increase your sales as much as you want by offering discount s

scores.rationale: Convenience is the core benefit and the company's defining strength: 3 million-plus outlets, over a million visi-coolers, and 300,000-500,000 new outlets added every year putting chilled product within reach.
scores.quote: we are expanding at about 300,000 - 400,000 outlets every year. Hopefully this year we might expand half a million outlets

scores.rationale: The retail-consumer benefit set is correctly matched on availability and price points, and the retailer relationship is locked in through company-owned coolers, but the intangible/brand half of the retail equation is owned by the franchisor.
scores.quote: We do not give visi -coolers to everyone.

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge is claimed; advantages cited are scale, backward integration and plant cost-efficiency, with product IP resting with PepsiCo.
scores.quote: the new plants are much more cost -effective and large r, with much higher production levels

scores.rationale: The business shows no two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic; scale benefits come from route density and manufacturing leverage, not network effects.
scores.quote: whoever does a good go -to-market and whoever can expand his distribution will win the game

scores.rationale: Distribution and cold-chain reach is the durable, hard-to-replicate advantage — millions of outlets, company chilling infrastructure, and route expansion that management itself names as the decider of the category.
scores.quote: our wide distribution reach, strengthened execution, and continued investments in manufacturing capability and chilling infrastructure

scores.rationale: Sustained and rising growth capex ($3bn over 2 years in FY23, an $8bn programme announced in FY25, ₹14,918 cr delivered in FY26) funded from internal accruals with group ROCE of ~32%, though returns are commodity-price dependent rather than proven incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: During the year, we deployed INR15,000 crores of growth capital in line with guidance... Our return on capital employed stood for the year at 32%

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across any of the fifteen calls.
No R&D spend, intensity or pipeline is disclosed; technical work discussed is field/process engineering (ASP injection, debottlenecking), not an R&D programme.

Bolt-ons have been complementary and value-accretive — FACOR production doubled since acquisition, Athena gave captive power security, and Incab was bought for downstream synergies — though Athena/Meenakshi power are sizeable rather than small.
scores.quote: At FACOR ferro chrome, we have already doubled our production since acquisition

scores.rationale: Distributions are large but structurally driven by the parent's debt-servicing need (brand fee plus dividend upstreaming to VRL), with no buybacks, and the FY26 policy change from rule-based to discretionary weakens the framework.
scores.quote: So with 4% to 5% dividend and the routine brand fee, VRL can be managed

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy: smelters, refineries, mines and power plants with a stated ~$50bn replacement cost and multi-billion-dollar annual capex against ~$20bn revenue.
scores.quote: the replacement cost of our assets today across aluminium, zinc, oil, gas, iron ore, steel, et cetera, is the replacement cost is in excess of $50 billion

scores.rationale: Genuine runway and evidence of capacity share capture — global leader in wire rod, moving to second largest billet producer, India's largest private oil producer, largest ferro alloys ambition — though in price-taking commodities.
scores.quote: We are already the global leader in wire rod production... making us the second largest producer of billets in the world

scores.rationale: Real international footprint being built out — Gamsberg (South Africa) volumes up 39% YoY with Phase 2 ~94% complete, Liberia iron ore restarted with a 3 Mtpa concentrator, Fujairah copper rods — but Liberia's 30 Mt ambition has repeatedly slipped since 2022.
scores.quote: Gamsberg volumes rising 39% year-on-year, driven by higher throughput, stable ore delivery, and improved feed grade

scores.rationale: Growth is led by volume and exogenous LME/price moves rather than company pricing power, with only mix (90% value-added products, low-carbon brands) as a partial offset.
scores.quote: Our quarterly revenue grew 29% year-on-year to INR 51,524 crores, supported by positive prices, exchange rate, and sustained growth

scores.rationale: The company is now near a cyclical peak, not a bottom — record FY26 EBITDA of ₹56,000 cr with LME moving from $2,600 to $3,100 and margins at an all-time-high 44%.
scores.quote: the LME was closer to 2,600, now 2,800, and as we speak, it is closer to 3,100

scores.rationale: Core products (zinc, silver, aluminium, critical minerals) sit in secularly expanding energy-transition and electrification end-markets, and the company has won 18 critical-mineral/gold/manganese exploration blocks.
scores.quote: we are positioning ourselves to meet India's rising need for critical minerals powering the growth of AI, data infrastructure, and advanced technologies

scores.rationale: Leverage has been reduced substantially (net debt/EBITDA 1.9x to 0.95x) but the group remains structurally levered at the promoter holdco ($4.7bn at VRL) which drives cash extraction and stake sales, alongside continued acquisitions and a QIP.
scores.quote: now that we still have about USD 4.7 billion of debt at VRL, what are the modes of addressing that debt?

scores.rationale: Multi-year projects promised in 2022-24 were actually commissioned by FY26 (Lanjigarh Train 2, BALCO 435kt smelter, Debari roaster, Meenakshi/Athena power) and the demerger was pushed through NCLT over several years, but independence is constrained by parent-company obligations.
scores.quote: the year marked successful commissioning of various multi-year projects, setting us up on a trajectory of multi-year growth

scores.rationale: Communication is markedly promotional and self-celebratory — superlatives, 'trophy assets', TSR-versus-index boasting — under a high-profile promoter chairman.
scores.quote: Our assets are also quite unparalleled... ESL, one of our trophy assets

scores.rationale: A deep expat/specialist bench is claimed, but senior churn is heavy across the period — Group CEO moved from Duggal to Navin Agarwal's oversight to Deshnee Naidoo, and business CEOs changed repeatedly — indicating hiring more than an internal pipeline.
