scores.quote: the Bank reported Gross NPA and Net NPA ratio of 1.3% and 0.2%, respectively, the lowest ever that we have seen in the last 24 quarters

scores.rationale: Indian credit and deposits are in secular expansion and management repeatedly cites resilient domestic demand, 37 straight months of manufacturing expansion and rising system loan growth as the backdrop.
scores.quote: India remains comparatively resilient, supported by steady domestic demand and a stable financial system.

scores.rationale: Consistent organic, liability-led discipline across the period — no acquisitions, deliberate slowdown of unsecured retail in FY25, calibrated growth, PSL compliance and a stated refusal to chase assets without deposits.
scores.quote: The idea is never to really aggressively pursue Assets in the absence of a Deposit construct.

scores.rationale: Tenacity is evident in a multi-year turnaround delivered largely as guided, but independence is absent — the Bank operated under a government/RBI reconstruction scheme, saw its entire FY22–FY24 board exit, and the MD role passed to an SBI veteran under SMBC's control.
scores.quote: Over the past several years, he led YES Bank through a multi -year and truly unique transformation.

scores.rationale: Management consistently refuses to discuss the share price or stake-sale speculation and restricts calls to reported results, a substance-over-publicity posture maintained across MD transitions.
scores.quote: I think we don't comment in terms of the movement on the stock prices.

scores.rationale: Strong workplace credentials (Great Place to Work four years running, top-25 BFSI) and internal elevation of Rajan Pental and Manish Jain to ED, but the leadership bench is repeatedly filled externally — retail assets, collections, financial markets, CRO and the MD all hired in.
scores.quote: YES Bank also has been recognized as a Great Place to Work for the fourth consecutive year.

scores.rationale: Management quantifies drags and one-offs rather than hiding them — the 70bp RIDF margin drag, SR book value vs face value vs fair value, the one-off INR 119 crore tax-refund interest, and early admission of unsecured delinquency and deliberate growth calibration.
scores.quote: We've been consistently saying that there are early signs of delinquency on the unsecured side. In fact, we've also consciously slowed down on some of these products

scores.rationale: The improvement narrative is hard to separate from external rescue and a collapsed base — reconstruction backed by GoI/RBI/SBI, capital from SMBC/Advent, and profits historically flattered by SR/treasury gains (SR gains fell from INR 338 crore to INR 86 crore YoY) while ROE is still only 8.3%.
scores.quote: the strong support of the Government of India, the Reserve Bank of India and the State Bank and other banks who got in together to bring in the reconstruction

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind; the only differentiated niche claimed is digital-payments plumbing, while core deposits and lending are openly commoditized and price-competed.
scores.quote: our modern technology platform, the leadership in digital payments ecosystem

scores.rationale: Some genuine stickiness is being built through primary banking relationships, transaction banking, CMS and cross-sell, but retail customers demonstrably shop across banks and there is no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: enabled us to capture higher primary banking share from our target customer segments

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented across PSU, private, small-finance banks and NBFCs, and the Bank repeatedly cites industry-wide deposit competition as the binding constraint — customers hold the negotiating power on price.
scores.quote: In a system where Deposits are the binding constraint

scores.rationale: Licensing is a barrier but pricing is not rational — persistent deposit-rate competition, guidance-limiting spread compression, and the Bank's own ownership has churned repeatedly (reconstruction, SBI, then SMBC and Advent).
scores.quote: Despite adverse interest rate environment and elevated competitive intensity in Deposits

scores.rationale: Weaker rivals exist and the Bank has demonstrably captured share from them in deposits/CASA over four to six quarters at a time, particularly among branch-led retail depositors.
scores.quote: this outperformance is not just recent but has been persistent over the last four to six quarters

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — one of India's most-watched stocks with retail investors questioning the share price on calls, heavy analyst coverage, and constant media speculation about stake sales.
scores.quote: Despite all the good performance showing by YES Bank, there is no significant growth in the YES Bank share price.

scores.rationale: Brand equity was destroyed in 2020 and is described as being rebuilt gradually rather than commanding a premium; the Bank pays up for deposits and runs the peer group's lowest NIM at 2.7%, i.e. no image-based pricing power.
scores.quote: the YES Bank ’s brand remained relevant and trust was rebuilt gradually through steady execution

scores.rationale: Reliability is the product and trust is being re-earned through independent validation (Moody's Ba1, CARE AA+, ICRA AA, S&P BB+, PCR 81.9%), but ratings remain below the top private peers so price is still not secondary for customers.
scores.quote: Moody's upgraded our issu er rating to Ba1.

scores.rationale: Real progress in digital onboarding, embedded banking and branch addition, offset by a shareholder pointing out concrete service gaps versus SBI and IDFC First on basic transaction cut-offs.
scores.quote: our Bank's cut -off time for filling IPOs is 3:30 PM, whereas IDFC Bank gives it until 4:30 PM

scores.rationale: The mix is being managed sensibly — retail/branch-led deposits near 60% for granularity and corporate served via forex, trade and CMS cross-sell — but neither retail intangibles nor corporate switching-cost lock-in is strong enough to defend pricing.
scores.quote: driving higher penetration of forex, trade and CMS flows within our Corporate relationships

scores.rationale: A consistent, credible edge in digital payments and fintech/e-commerce partnerships across the whole period — from CA growth driven by digital solutioning in FY23 to embedded-banking capability cited as a core strength in FY26.
scores.quote: our modern technology platform, the leadership in digital payments ecosystem we have and collaborative embedded bankin g capabilities

scores.rationale: The fintech/e-commerce payments franchise brings scale flows and sticky current accounts, but the Bank is a plumbing provider inside someone else's network rather than the owner of a self-reinforcing two-sided one.
scores.quote: Average daily current accounts have actually grown 50 % Y-o-Y, mainly on account of our digital solutioning to the e -commerce and fin tech players

scores.rationale: Branch and RM reach is improving and now supplies close to 60% of deposits, but at 82 branches added a year the network is far smaller than SBI/HDFC-class rivals and is not a reach competitors cannot match.
scores.quote: Retail and Branch -led Deposits now comprise close to 60% of our Total Deposits

scores.rationale: Capitalised development spend is rising and explicitly tied to new products rather than maintenance, and new products (Zoyer/BROME/Fleet) are visibly monetising, though returns are muted by negative operating cash flow.
scores.quote: capitalized development costs have nearly doubled from INR30 crores in H1 to INR56 crores in H2 FY26... we capitalize only those costs, which are related to new product development. Any maintenance work is not capitalized

scores.rationale: A&P exists (higher sales and marketing costs, a cricket brand ambassador, ad awards) but is asserted rather than evidenced as durable brand equity in a B2B business.
scores.quote: our investment in Ayush Mhatre, taking him as a brand ambassador has proven to be one of the best choices we have made

scores.rationale: R&D has consistently produced new revenue-generating products (Zoyer from April 2024, BROME, Fleet, Smart EPP) and measurable development-cycle gains, but SaaS/platform fees remain only ~2% of revenue so R&D efficiency in monetisation terms is unproven.
scores.quote: to develop and deploy a new product feature traditionally took us about 75-plus days. Now the same can be rolled out... in less than 30 days

scores.rationale: Bolt-ons are small, complementary and two have scaled sharply post-deal (86400 INR17cr FY24 to INR74cr FY26; GreenEdge INR36.5cr to INR103.7cr), offset by TaxSpanner underdelivery, an abandoned EffiaSoft deal and a restructured DICE price.
scores.quote: revenues grew from about INR34 crores in 2025 to INR74 crores in FY26, represented a remarkable year-on-year growth of 118%

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback across the period; the company is a net issuer, raising INR595 crores of QIP equity for inorganic expansion and earmarking further primary infusions.
scores.quote: in December 2024 we successfully completed the QIP of INR 595 crores... The fundraise is in line with our growth strategy of inorganic expansion

scores.rationale: The model is nominally asset-light software-plus-cards with high revenue per asset, but working capital absorbs the growth (OCF only turned near-breakeven in FY26) and the moat protecting those returns is thin, as 3-4% Propel gross margins show.
scores.quote: we are just about minus INR6 crores on negative cash flow, and we will look forward to improving it to a positive cash flow in the coming quarters

scores.rationale: A small player in a large market with sustained 40-70% growth, customers rising from ~1,800 to 3,900 and users to 3.9 million, plus claimed segment leadership in city-gas fleet cards — clear runway and evidence of capture.
scores.quote: we have gained market leadership in the CGD space with our fleet program solution... We now serve more than 3,900 corporate customers

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is repeatedly announced (GIFT City, UAE/Abu Dhabi, US) but slipping with no revenue yet — the US launch alone has been pushed from June 2026 to financial year-end.
scores.quote: We are on track to kick start our U.S. operations by financial year-end. Earlier, we had thought that we will do it by June 2026

scores.rationale: Growth is almost entirely volume/gross-accounted transaction throughput with deteriorating mix — low-margin Propel Points dominate revenue and its margin fell from 10% to 4%, while high-margin SaaS fees are just 2.2% of revenue.
scores.quote: our Propel margins have declined from 10% to 4%... our SaaS platform contributes to around 2.2% of our overall revenue

scores.rationale: No discussion of cyclical positioning; the only cyclicality mentioned is intra-year seasonality of H2 versus H1, not an industry cycle.
The end market — digitisation of corporate spend, UPI and card payments in India — is in secular expansion, reinforced by tax rules extending employee benefits to the new regime.
scores.quote: employee tax benefits have been extended to the new tax regime, which is a huge kicker to us... Globally, spend management is growing at a breakneck speed

scores.rationale: Stewardship leans acquisitive rather than organic — a INR595cr QIP explicitly for inorganic growth, five targets evaluated at once, five deals pursued and one abandoned — alongside years of negative operating cash flow while headline PAT grew.
scores.quote: we are currently evaluating five targets in the spend management and adjacent space... Out of this, two are at advanced stages

scores.rationale: Consistent multi-year platform strategy with a stable stated long-horizon target and delivery of successive product launches, though guidance is revised often and the $1bn/14-15% ambition remains distant.
scores.quote: we would be in the adjusted EBITDA of about 14% to 15% in about 5 to 7 years is what we have guided, along with $1 billion of revenue

scores.rationale: Management is markedly promotional — calls routinely enumerate awards and the Chairman and CEO publicly congratulate each other on personal accolades.
scores.quote: I would like to take a moment to congratulate our CEO and MD – Mr. Avinash Godkhindi, who has been recognized with "India's Most Influential CEO Award"

scores.rationale: There is senior hiring and talent absorption (a veteran banker as director, 100+ AI engineers via DICE) and an employer-brand award, but no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline — indeed the CFO left with only an interim replacement.
scores.quote: the Board has approved the appointment of Mr. Rajesh as Interim CFO till the time a new Chief Financial Officer is appointed

scores.rationale: Management quantifies one-offs, concedes underperformance at TaxSpanner and that margin expansion was never linear, and disclosed walking away from EffiaSoft — though the answer on the platform-fee jump was thin.
scores.quote: while we are not very stoked about the performance through the financial -- last financial year, we have taken the following calculated steps

scores.rationale: Headline results are flattered by gross-basis Propel accounting and heavy award-citation while unit economics (3-6% Propel gross margin) and cash conversion lagged, so results should not be read as proof of skill.
scores.quote: the margins are now about at 3%... And we know that this business requires a lot of capital

scores.rationale: Only a narrow claimed leadership in one niche (city gas distribution fleet cards); elsewhere Zaggle is one of several vendors with no monopoly-like grip on the customer's mind.
scores.quote: we have gained market leadership in the CGD space with our fleet program solution

scores.rationale: Deep API/HRMS/ERP integration and single sign-on create real switching costs, reflected in sub-2% churn and steady cross-sell into installed accounts.
scores.quote: there is a complete API integration with their HRMS system... churn rate, which is currently less than 2% for us today

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and contested with corporate buyers holding clear negotiating power, evident in wafer-thin Propel take rates that management cannot lift as promised.
scores.quote: in Q2 we have sort of indicated that... the margins should recover... but that hasn't happened

scores.rationale: Low structural barriers in Indian spend management, with pricing rationality poor — gross margins on the largest revenue line fell rather than held.
scores.quote: our Propel margins have declined from 10% to 4%, like 10% in Q4 FY25 to 4% in Q4 FY26

scores.rationale: Much of the share being taken is from manual, cash-based and offline legacy processes rather than strong incumbents, which management explicitly targets.
scores.quote: While competitors remain tethered to outdated offline workflows, we look to leverage AI automation to capture market share

scores.rationale: The company is highly visible and actively courts attention — IPO, QIP, celebrity brand ambassador, award publicity — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: India brought home the U19 World Cup... when he raised his bat, the Zaggle sticker was right there for everybody to see

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; the dominant revenue line earns mid-single-digit gross margins and pricing is set by interchange and merchant commissions, not brand.
scores.quote: even at 192 crores of kind of revenues, we are earning about 6% of gross profit on this business

scores.rationale: Corporates buy compliance, control and reliability — security certifications, bank/network backing and multi-year partnerships underpin trust-led selling and sub-2% churn.
scores.quote: our commitment to providing a secure platform to their users and we have demonstrated this through various certifications such as GDPR, ISO 27001, PCI DSS

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly convenience — one platform bundling software, cards, travel booking, bill payment and reconciliation — with demonstrated account intimacy through cross-sell into existing clients.
scores.quote: we were able to cross-sell to multiple customers, including House of Hiranandani, CK Birla Healthcare and HT Media

scores.rationale: The benefit type matches the buyer: corporates get TCO/compliance savings with integration lock-in, and the new retail pillar targets a captive salaried base already on the platform.
scores.quote: ZAG.money establishes our 4th monetization pillar, a captive high-intent base of 3.7 million salaried users

scores.rationale: A genuinely multi-product stack with AI/agentic development, but customers pay overwhelmingly for transactions rather than software, suggesting the tech edge is not the source of monetisable differentiation.
scores.quote: our core monetization is driven majorly by transaction-based revenues, which is program fees and Propel Points

scores.rationale: There is an ecosystem of corporates, banks, networks and merchants, but nothing presented shows it becoming self-reinforcing with scale — growth still comes from selling each client individually.
scores.quote: Historically, our growth has been fuelled by 3 distinct pillars: enterprise clients, banking and network partners along with the merchant ecosystem

scores.rationale: Distribution is a real edge — multiple bank tie-ups plus long-dated network agreements where Visa/Mastercard actively channel corporate customers to Zaggle, supplemented by HRMS and travel partners.
scores.quote: Mastercard will recommend our software platform and card solutions to their corporate customers and other entities like banks and fintechs

scores.rationale: Capex has been shrinking for years and the one major growth investment (Bengaluru tech centre) was written down and its staff made redundant, indicating poor incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: our capitalization has not been very high... certain investments which we had done earlier in tech centre in Bengaluru, which was amortized

scores.rationale: Marketing is defended as non-discretionary and rose 44% in Q4FY26, but management frames it as efficiency-seeking maintenance spend rather than durable brand equity building, and ad revenue kept declining.
scores.quote: how do we make our marketing more efficient rather than cutting back

scores.rationale: The 2022 technology and innovation centre was largely dismantled by 2024 with staff called redundant, and new capability is now bought in via a VFX stake rather than developed internally.
scores.quote: A large part of the churn has happened in the tech centre... we think they have become a bit redundant

scores.rationale: The transformational Sony merger pursued for years collapsed, and the recent bolt-ons (Phantom Digital ₹116cr, CORE ₹20cr) are small but unproven, funded from an FCCB raise whose deployment plan was still 'work in progress'.
scores.quote: an investment of up to INR116 crores was also approved... in Phantom Digital Effects Limited

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed anywhere across the calls; instead the company raised dilutive FCCB capital while sitting on ₹27.6bn cash with no articulated distribution framework.
scores.quote: this fundraise was undertaken to ensure availability of funds which can act as a growth capital

scores.rationale: The business carries a very heavy ₹67.6bn content inventory against declining revenue, and required accelerated amortization plus a ₹4,084mn impairment — asset-heavy without a protecting moat.
scores.quote: content inventory advances and deposits as of March '26 stood at INR67.6 billion

scores.rationale: Viewership share recovered from 16.1% in Q1FY23 to 17.4-17.5% with Marathi at 33.6% and Bangla leadership regained, though it took four years versus the 2022 promise and has not yet converted into ad revenue.
scores.quote: we gained 60 basis points year-on-year, taking our network share to 17.5%

scores.rationale: Expansion is language-market deepening within India (7-language ZEE5 packs, south/east strength) rather than credible new geographies; no international growth story is presented.
scores.quote: with the 7 language packs, which was rolled out in quarter 2

scores.rationale: Digital growth of 71-73% was explicitly pricing- and mix-led (ZEE5 hikes from Rs 499 to 699, revised telco pricing, NTO 3.0 on linear subscription) rather than volume-driven.
scores.quote: a revised pricing strategy on our digital entertainment platform, ZEE5, has resulted in a 73% year-on-year increase in our digital revenue

scores.rationale: Ad revenue is clearly depressed (down 9-12% YoY) which could mark a cyclical trough, but management has predicted an H2 recovery in nearly every call since 2022 without it arriving, so no upturn is identifiable.
scores.quote: we should start to kind of see an inflection point over the next few quarters

scores.rationale: The core linear TV and GEC advertising market is stagnant-to-declining with FMCG spends shrinking, and the growing digital segment is fiercely contested rather than a protected secular tailwind.
scores.quote: advertising revenues were up 6% quarter-on-quarter and though they are down 9% year-on-year

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage and a strong ₹27.6bn net cash position and cost frugality sit alongside a failed mega-merger and an FCCB raise made before any deployment plan existed.
scores.quote: very soon we will be ready with our deployment plans also. We have a broad sense of it, but just some more work is left

scores.rationale: Management delivered the promised ZEE5 EBITDA breakeven exactly as guided, but the 2022 pledge that 'this year is the year where you'll see the market share returning back' took four years and ad revenue is still contracting.
scores.quote: that was the target, which is what we had said at the start of the year to breakeven by FY '26 end

scores.rationale: The promoter-CEO is a high-profile media figure entangled in a public merger collapse and Star arbitration, and repeatedly joined or skipped calls around other commitments rather than presenting a low-key substance-first posture.
scores.quote: Our CEO, Mr. Punit Goenka is currently in the U.S. and due to unavoidable last-minute exigencies, he is unable to join the call today

scores.rationale: Management does own operational failures directly ('sheer implementation issues', 'people issues') but withholds material specifics such as ILT20 cost, headcount and arbitration status, and repeatedly deferred recovery promises.
scores.quote: It's just a matter of sheer implementation issues Abneesh. We've not had as successful run this time around

scores.rationale: With four years of falling ad revenue and a collapsed merger there is little halo to separate from skill; the ZEE5 turnaround is real but was achieved mainly through cost cutting and one-off syndication/telco deals rather than demonstrated operating excellence.
scores.quote: The revenue growth was aided by syndication revenues and revised pricing agreement with a telco player

scores.rationale: ZEE is a perennial 'strong number 2' nationally with genuine regional dominance only in Marathi and Bangla, so no monopoly-like position in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: We continue to maintain our position as India's strong number 2 TV entertainment network

scores.rationale: Regional language leadership (Marathi 33.6%, Bangla leadership) gives quasi-regional strength, but viewers and advertisers face zero switching costs and can move channels freely.
scores.quote: For Zee Marathi, the new content slate has resonated strongly... enabling us to achieve a market share of 33.6%

scores.rationale: The industry consolidated into a dominant Star-Jio entity leaving ZEE structurally sub-scale, and the end customer (FMCG advertisers) demonstrably holds the negotiating power by pulling spends at will.
scores.quote: consolidation is happening between the two large players... how do you see costing pressure? How do you see pricing pressure?

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low with deep-pocketed OTT and sports entrants bidding up content, and management itself concedes competitive intensity is fierce while ad pricing stays under pressure.
scores.quote: given competition is quite fierce

scores.rationale: ZEE has taken some viewership share in the south and east, but the main competitor is a strengthened merged giant rather than weak donators, and the share gains are not converting to revenue.
scores.quote: ZEE remained the fastest-growing network in the south with a share of 17.7%

scores.rationale: ZEEL is a heavily covered large-cap under constant analyst, regulatory (TRAI/NTO, SEBI) and litigation scrutiny — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the next hearing will be somewhere in July

scores.rationale: The Zee brand supports successful ZEE5 subscription price hikes and strong GEC engagement, but it commands no pricing power with advertisers, who buy on reach-per-rupee.
scores.quote: TV continues to remain a powerful proposition for brands, providing massive reach at the most competitive price point

scores.rationale: Advertisers buy cheap reach rather than certainty, and revenue swings with FMCG budget cycles, elections, sports and geopolitics — evidence that price, not trust, governs the purchase.
scores.quote: March was severely impacted with the ongoing Middle East conflict where advertisers have held back their spends

scores.rationale: Omnichannel accessibility is genuinely strong — 800mn monthly unique reach across platforms, 740mn weekly linear reach, telco distribution deals — and management is investing in the sales force.
scores.quote: ZEE's monthly unique reach has crossed 800 million across platforms

scores.rationale: The corporate customer base (FMCG advertisers) has no switching costs or TCO lock-in and cuts spend at will, while the retail subscriber relationship is largely intermediated by telcos and DTH operators.
scores.quote: our business is largely dependent on FMCG because we are an FMCG-driven company from the advertising point of view

scores.rationale: The in-house tech centre was wound down as redundant, amortization is running off with minimal new capitalization, and VFX capability is being bought rather than built.
scores.quote: We can always keep trying to outsource it. But we believe that having it internally could be far more beneficial

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing dynamic exists; ZEE5's scale must be repurchased each quarter through content spend and marketing, and subscribers churn with content slates and telco deals.
scores.quote: revised pricing agreement with a telco player during this quarter

scores.rationale: Reach across linear, digital, telco tie-ups and YouTube is genuinely broad and hard to replicate — 28bn weekly impressions, 740mn weekly reach and 176mn music subscribers.
scores.quote: weekly impressions of above 28 billion and a weekly reach exceeding 740 million

scores.rationale: Capex commentary is about shrinking, not growing, the asset base — leases resized/terminated across India and the US with depreciation guided down, and the only expansion cited in four years is one Belgrade delivery centre.
scores.quote: we have resized multiple facilities which we have across India and across U.S.

scores.rationale: No A&P or brand-spend discussion appears anywhere in the eleven calls.

No disclosed R&D line, but sustained capability investment produced named proprietary offerings (ZenseAI, Agentic foundry, ZenseAI.Guidewire) that management credits for the $210M mega-deal win and 20% AI-influenced order book.
scores.quote: one of the reasons for our large deal win was our AI solutioning

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were made in the period — only a settlement of legacy deal adjustments — with M&A evaluated but held to an accretion test, so there is discipline but no track record to score.
scores.quote: Do we evaluate M&A situations? Yes, very actively, but we are very mindful in terms of how they will be accretive

scores.rationale: Dividend policy is coherent and rising (450% of face value FY24 to 750% FY26) but no buybacks were executed despite cash equal to ~18-19% of market cap, so distribution lags cash generation.
scores.quote: our total dividend for the year adds up to 750% of face value

scores.rationale: The model is genuinely asset-light with strong working capital (DSO 71 days), but the required protecting moat is absent and $319.5M of idle cash depresses effective asset turn.
scores.quote: Cash, including investments stood at USD 319.5 million

scores.rationale: Revenue crawled from $591M (FY24) to $644M (FY26) with TMT declining eleven straight quarters and accounts lost in vendor consolidation; the single mega-deal win is the only clear share capture.
scores.quote: we have been at the wrong end of consolidation

scores.rationale: Geographic footprint is stable rather than expanding — one new nearshore centre in Serbia and a recovery (not extension) in EU/South Africa — with no evidence of a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: We opened a delivery centre in Belgrade, Serbia

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with adverse mix — onsite-to-offshore shift suppresses revenue per unit of work — while AI is deflating pricing on renewals.
scores.quote: a majority of AI spend is being repurposed from existing engagements... creating pressure on renewals and pricing

scores.rationale: The sector downcycle is well advanced but management identifies no upturn — TMT guided to keep declining, competitive intensity rising, and FY27 made contingent on one deal.
scores.quote: TMT will remain under pressure for next few quarters

scores.rationale: AI adoption is a genuine secular shift the company is positioned for, but management concedes it is cannibalising existing service revenue rather than expanding the pool.
scores.quote: enterprises are prioritizing cost optimization and vendor consolidation over discretionary spend

scores.rationale: Four years of purely organic focus, no acquisitions, net cash of $319.5M with no leverage, and repeated refusal to buy revenue at the expense of profitability.
scores.quote: we will not be indiscriminately buying revenues

scores.rationale: Tandon delivered on the multi-year internal agenda he set in Jan 2023 — EBITDA 11.3% to 17.8%, attrition 22.8% to 9.5%, CSAT 53 to record highs — but the growth half of the promise has not been delivered in over three years.
scores.quote: margins are a function of internal efficiencies more than external markets

scores.rationale: Consistently low-key, substance-first tone, including an explicit refusal to inflate AI metrics the way peers inflated 'digital'.
scores.quote: I don't want this to treat AI like people used to treat digital, but suddenly 100% of their revenues became digital overnight

scores.rationale: Systematic talent machinery — 98.6% learning coverage, Ignite AI Academy reaching 85% of the workforce, five straight quarters of sub-10% attrition — plus a smooth internal CFO succession from Zute to Bhandari.
scores.quote: This is the fifth successive quarter where our voluntary attrition has been below 10%

scores.rationale: Margin bridges are quantified basis point by basis point, one-offs are volunteered, and management owns unflattering facts — budgeting for continued decline in the top TMT account and admitting the inherited business was near-staffing.
scores.quote: we have not taken any growth in that account. We have, in fact, budgeted for continuous decline

scores.rationale: Strong headline profit growth (PAT +13.6%, EPS more than doubled in FY24) is substantially attributable to cost levers, currency and offshore mix rather than demand-side skill, and flat dollar revenue keeps the halo in check.
scores.quote: Positive forex impact of 0.7%, Improved offshore effort mix by 1.4%, Leave utilization benefit of 1.0%

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere — the company is displaced from accounts during consolidation and is itself one of many bidders on every deal.
scores.quote: we have been consolidated out of a couple of accounts

scores.rationale: Relationships are sticky enough to produce top-quartile CSAT, but switching costs are demonstrably weak given account losses to consolidation and pricing pressure on renewals.
scores.quote: creating pressure on renewals and pricing

scores.rationale: The structure is fragmented and worsening, with Tier-1s now bidding for deals they previously ignored and clients holding clear negotiating power.
scores.quote: we are seeing Tier 1s competing for deals, which a few months back, they wouldn't even look at

scores.rationale: Management describes escalating competitive intensity and price pressure with no entry barrier protecting the mid-cap position.
scores.quote: the competitive intensity is going up tremendously

scores.rationale: Weak incumbents do exist — Zensar displaced a Tier-1 on the mega deal — but the company simultaneously donates share elsewhere, netting out roughly neutral.
scores.quote: we have replaced one of the Tier 1 incumbents

scores.rationale: Management is humble and low-profile, but the niche is anything but ignored — Tier-1 competitors are crowding into precisely its deal sizes.
scores.quote: almost everywhere, we are encountering a Tier 1 in our competitive set

scores.rationale: Gross margin of ~33.7% is modest and there is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; realised pricing is being pushed down by AI-led repricing and offshore shift.
scores.quote: Gross profit improved to 33.7%

scores.rationale: The clearest customer strength: record client-experience scores (53 to top-3 in industry, +470bps in FY26) alongside delivery-excellence positioning, though it has not yet converted into pricing power.
scores.quote: Our annual customer satisfaction score improved by 470 bps to its highest ever level, positioning Zensar in the top 3 of industry CSAT

scores.rationale: Access is being built — nearshore Serbia centre, ongoing sales investment — but analysts repeatedly question sales proactiveness and large-deal reach was long a work in progress.
scores.quote: we continue to invest in augmenting capabilities, specifically around AI and sales

scores.rationale: The corporate-customer playbook is correctly matched — TCO, reliability, outcome-based delivery — but the lock-in half of the requirement is missing given consolidation losses.
scores.quote: enable measurable business outcomes

scores.rationale: A credible multi-offering AI stack (ZenseAI, Agentic foundry, physical AI lab for a Fortune 50 client) exists, but it is capability-building on partner technology rather than a defensible proprietary edge, and it has not lifted revenue growth above ~3%.
scores.quote: We have established a physical AI lab for a Fortune 50 client

scores.rationale: The business is linear project- and relationship-based services with no two-sided platform; management itself characterises the inherited model as near-staffing.
scores.quote: What we inherited was really a slightly more advanced form of a staf[fing]

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is a known gap — a large-deal engine was still being built years into the tenure and Tier-1 rivals now contest every pursuit.
scores.quote: creation of a large deal effort on a consistent basis is a work in progress

scores.rationale: Capex talk is growth-oriented (US manufacturing build-out, supply-chain ramp, HyperStrike mass-production capacity) but figures and incremental ROIC are never quantified, and FY26 revenue fell 29% against the build-out.
scores.quote: this will involve setting up of manufacturing facility also, at least therefore to qualify as a Make in America it has to be 51%

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend beyond incidental defence-expo participation (ITSEC Orlando, North Tech Prayagraj); nothing to judge as brand-building outlay.

R&D is the core engine and has consistently converted into commercialised products across the period — anti-drone systems, Barbarik/RCWS, anti-drone simulator, Vrishabh UGV, 30mm ammunition, HyperStrike — with management committing to a structurally elevated R&D base.
scores.quote: we expect to make higher investments in R&D going forward, which will be reflected in an elevated cost base... this is a structural commitment that we will continue

scores.rationale: Bolt-ons are small and complementary (AI Turing, ARI, ANAWAVE) and are visibly producing product, but the Rs.1,000 Cr QIP earmarked for acquisitions and willingness to go larger tempers the 'small and simple' test.
scores.quote: our acquisition with AI Turing is playing out very well... A typical size we are looking at is between Rs.100 to 300 Crores

scores.rationale: ESOPs are funded by market purchases rather than fresh issue (shareholder-friendly), but the company raised Rs.1,000 Cr via QIP and articulates no buyback or dividend policy, so there is no coherent distribution framework.
scores.quote: we are actually buying from the cash that we have from the market and giving it to them. So, that was the existing share holders proportion of ownership does not get diluted

scores.rationale: The business is genuinely asset-light and IP-led with ~73% gross margins and a moat, but asset turn is deteriorating — FY26 revenue down 29%, working capital stretched to 257 days and Rs.1,217 Cr of idle cash.
scores.quote: our bill of materials goes somewhere between 20% to 35%... the remaining 65% to 80% on an average they reflect the IP content

scores.rationale: Zen is already dominant in Indian Army simulators (limiting runway there) but has real un-captured share in Navy, Air Force and exports, and won ~Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders post Op Sindoor.
scores.quote: as far as the army and naval market in which we are dominant these are very big

scores.rationale: US/EU expansion has been promised since Nov 2024 with little delivered — management now concedes no breakthrough for a year or two and can only bid as a subcontractor — while established Middle East/Africa/CIS exports continue.
scores.quote: as of now, I think a year or two, there is no big news from US as such or the EU but maybe third year onwards something may happen

scores.rationale: Growth is order-volume driven, and the strategic pitch is explicitly lower price points (cheaper-than-Shahed interceptors, cheaper CIWS), with mix and geography repeatedly cited as margin drags.
scores.quote: at a much lower price point can be pushed to the armed forces

scores.rationale: The company sits near the trough of its own order/execution cycle — FY26 revenue down 29% on delayed inflows — with an identifiable upturn from a Rs.1,239 Cr book, a Rs.177.5 Cr MoD order and Rs.2,500 Cr targeted by FY27-end.
scores.quote: the revenue trajectory in FY2026 has been impacted by the timing of order inflows with the bulk of the orders received over the past several months scheduled for execution from FY2027 onwards

scores.rationale: End markets — military training simulation and counter-drone — are in secular expansion driven by Ukraine, Armenia-Azerbaijan and Israel-Iran wars plus the Indian IDDM/Atmanirbhar procurement shift.
scores.quote: the sudden non-existence of war prior to 2020, to now Armenia-Azerbaijan, Ukraine-Russia, Israel-Iran, all these wars have really changed the dynamics very, very well

scores.rationale: Debt-free with Rs.1,217 Cr cash, self-funded R&D and promoters with net worth in the stock, though the Rs.1,000 Cr QIP raised explicitly for acquisitions sits against the pure organic-focus test.
scores.quote: the group remains debt free... if we do a bad decision, it is the promoters who suffer the most almost all of our net worth is in these shares

scores.rationale: Three decades of self-funded, independently-developed IP — refusing DRDO co-development funding and building capability over four-to-five year horizons — with sustained investment through the FY26 revenue trough.
scores.quote: privately self-funded independent R&D companies, innovation and R&D companies, should actually be treated much, much better than people who are just co-developing with DRDO

scores.rationale: Not a celebrity-CEO setup, but the CMD's commentary is markedly promotional — repeated 'best in the world' claims, political commentary on Trump and Musk — which cuts against substance-over-showmanship.
scores.quote: We think that the products that we have are absolutely world class. They are the best in the world.

scores.rationale: Systematic elements exist — market-purchased ESOPs, high-end technical recruitment, performance incentives and capable subsidiary leadership under Commodore Ahluwalia — but the CFO and chairman/MD seats have churned repeatedly over FY21-FY26.
scores.quote: Zen's employees were underappreciated and to correct that we started giving ESOPs to them this year

scores.rationale: Candour is consistently high: a five-factor bridge for the FY26 margin miss, disclosure of the fire loss and provision reversals that flattered a prior quarter, admission of missed guidance and of failed R&D projects.
scores.quote: last year when we projected Rs.450 Crores, we fell short by Rs.20 Crores and we achieved only Rs.430 Crores

scores.rationale: Stripping the halo off the FY23-25 boom, results tracked a government order cycle rather than repeatable skill — the promised 50% three-year CAGR reversed into a 29% FY26 decline and the 35% EBITDA guidance was missed for consecutive quarters.
scores.quote: we will have an average CAGR of 50% over the next three years and we are confident

scores.rationale: Zen holds a near-default position in the Indian Army's mind for training simulators plus a captive AMC franchise (Rs.318.4 Cr AMC order book), though the customer is a single sovereign buyer.
scores.quote: consolidated order book stood at Rs.1239 Crores... comprising an equipment order book of Rs.920.6 Crores and an AMC order book of Rs.318.4 Crores

scores.rationale: Installed simulators generate a locked-in annuity at 8-11% of equipment value with the OEM holding the IP, and the fresh Rs.177.5 Cr order is an upgrade of Zen's own installed base — real switching costs.
scores.quote: they start generating revenues anywhere between 8% to 11% depending on what the AMC is

scores.rationale: The supplier set is narrow, but the end customer is a government monopsony that dictates timing and tender terms, and competitors are visibly closing in on anti-drone and interceptor drones.
scores.quote: frequency dominance is one of the biggest challenges that we are seeing worldwide is that a catch-up game that the other vendors are playing with Zen

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are genuine — multi-year capability development, weapon and ammunition licences, IDDM preference and stable promoter ownership — but the drone segment is drawing new entrants such as Paras.
scores.quote: when you develop a product after four or five years of hard work, that is a capability development. It is not a product

scores.rationale: Foreign OEMs are the donors: Zen competes mainly against overseas suppliers whose share the IDDM/indigenisation policy shift is actively transferring to indigenous designers.
scores.quote: because our competition is from foreign overseas companies mostly we get a good margin on this

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — Indian defence is the most crowded theme in the market, the QIP was five-times subscribed and management courts high-visibility launches and expos.
scores.quote: we have raised through a QIP Rs.1000 Crores it was subscribed more than five times

scores.rationale: Gross margin is high at ~73% from IP content rather than image-based pricing power, and demand is anything but steady — revenue swung from +200% growth to a 29% decline on tender timing.
scores.quote: our gross margin for the quarter stood at 72.9%, broadly consistent both sequentially and year-on-year

scores.rationale: The customer buys proven reliability — battle-proven status after Op Sindoor drove ~Rs.800 Cr of orders and demonstrable training outcomes are the sales argument — though L1 tendering keeps price relevant.
scores.quote: the government itself, as you have seen, that they almost placed Rs.800 Crores worth of anti-drone orders on us postop Sindoor

scores.rationale: Zen maintains direct, continuous engagement with the armed forces, briefing them on its development roadmap ahead of other stakeholders — genuine customer intimacy in a relationship-driven market.
scores.quote: we do continuously keep telling our customers what exactly we are developing and what is the future development path and they do know what we have developed much in advance

scores.rationale: The benefit set is correctly matched to an institutional buyer: total-cost and reliability arguments (ammunition and range savings, compressed training time) plus AMC-based lock-in rather than retail-style intangibles.
scores.quote: We have seen Agniveers 100-week training program was shrunk to 30 weeks after using our simulators

scores.rationale: A deep, self-funded, multi-product technology edge — 70MHz-12GHz frequency dominance, indigenised 20km radar, AI-native systems, >85% indigenous UGV content — built entirely in-house.
scores.quote: we have preemptively made the product with wider frequency dominance with 70 megahertz or 12 gigahertz

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere across the calls; the business is a direct product supplier to sovereign buyers.
Domestic reach and AMC service coverage of its installed base are solid, but internationally Zen has no distribution of its own and must ride prime contractors to access the US market.
scores.quote: we are not eligible to be directly bidding, so we are trying to be a subcontractor and try to get into those markets

scores.rationale: Sustained multi-year growth capex — the greenfield Oragadam multi-divisional plant approved in FY23 and repeatedly ramped with new lines (e-compressor, hydraulic ESC, ASP cartridges, crankshaft machining, vacuum pump) plus assembly upgrades at Jamshedpur/Lucknow/Pantnagar — accompanied by EBITDA rising from 15.0% (Q1FY23) to 20% (Q3FY26) and record FY26 revenue of INR 4,302 cr, indicating growth (not maintenance) spend earning good incremental returns.
scores.quote: the investment approval for the Oragadam site is obtained, and the construction activities are under way

scores.rationale: A&P is not a meaningful lever for this B2B component supplier; the only promotional spend referenced is trade-level channel/merchandising work rather than brand-equity building.
scores.quote: Spark merchandising program, especially in door control retrofit ASP

scores.rationale: R&D consistently converts into new products and customers across all 16 quarters — ESC, ADAS, AMT, ECAS, e-compressor, Actuator 4.0, exhaust brake assembly — backed by a new electronics testing lab, an IIT Madras MoU, and engineering service exports growing 11–22% that monetise the R&D base.
scores.quote: the company inaugurated an Electronics Testing lab and design office... These new facilities will enhance our capabilities and accelerate product development

scores.rationale: No acquisitions by the company are discussed anywhere in the excerpts; the only M&A reference is the parent ZF's ADAS divestment to Harman, which management clarified does not involve this entity.
scores.quote: the announced transfer of certain advanced driver assistance system ADAS activity applies exclusively to its ADAS division portfolio... does not pertain to ADAS portfolio of ZF CVS division

scores.rationale: Distribution is limited to a modest final dividend and a first-ever 5:1 bonus issue — a cosmetic, liquidity-oriented action rather than value-accretive buybacks at low valuations, so the policy is conservative but not disciplined capital return.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors has approved the issuance of bonus equity shares in the ratio of 5:1... aimed at rewarding our shareholders and enhancing market liquidity

scores.rationale: The business is capital-intensive rather than asset-light — a greenfield plant plus assembly lines across five-plus sites and continuous new-line commissioning — though this is offset by a strong regulatory/technology moat; no asset-turn metrics are disclosed to support a positive score.
scores.quote: New lines for crank shaft machining, ASP cartridges, vacuum pump have been successfully commissioned

scores.rationale: Clear, repeated evidence of share capture (Q3 FY26 sales +28.1% vs 20.6% industry; FY26 OE sales +17.6% vs 16.6% industry; ESC and e-compressor gains at independent bus makers), but the company is already the incumbent leader in CV braking, limiting the runway.
scores.quote: CV more than 6 tonne production recorded a growth of 20.6%, while our overall sales rose by 28.1%... enabled us to outperform the market by 7.5%

scores.rationale: Genuine export build-out with new global OEM wins (Volvo, DAF, Daimler, BMW) and India positioned as ZF's engineering hub, but goods exports fell 11.1% in FY26 on US tariffs, so execution has been credible yet the geographic leg is currently a drag.
scores.quote: company reported export revenue of INR 1,025 crores in financial year '25-'26, reflecting a decline of 11.1% year-on-year

scores.rationale: Growth is driven mainly by volume and regulation-led content/mix (ESC, EBS, AMT, e-compressor raising value per vehicle) with only modest explicit pricing actions, so mix helps but pricing is a secondary lever.
scores.quote: An overall price rise of INR 7 crores is what we have seen in this quarter compared to the previous year's quarter

scores.rationale: The CV cycle bottomed in FY25 (Q1 FY25 production -3.5%) and has already rebounded sharply by FY26 (Q4 production +26.9%, record 151,000 units), so the company sits post-upturn rather than near a cycle bottom, with replacement demand as remaining runway.
scores.quote: production reaching a record 151,000 vehicles in quarter as compared to 119,000 of previous year same quarter, reflecting a growth of 26.9%

scores.rationale: End market is in permanent secular expansion via safety-regulation mandates (ESC from Sept 2025, AIS-113 trailer, upcoming ADAS/AEBS), electrification of buses and trucks, and rising content per vehicle — all recurring themes from 2022 through 2026.
scores.quote: a sharp rise in ESC penetration driven by updated regulations effective September 2025

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no acquisitions, no leverage stress, and counter-cyclical capacity building — Oragadam was constructed and ramped through the FY25 CV slowdown, ahead of the FY26 upturn it now serves.
scores.quote: we are advancing strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening our competitiveness and delivering long-term value

scores.rationale: Long-horizon execution is evident — multi-year localization of ESC/ECAS, patient Oragadam ramp, IIT Madras collaboration — but as a ZF Group subsidiary strategic direction and portfolio decisions are set by the parent, limiting genuine independence.
scores.quote: increasing penetration of ESG is driving our focus on localization efforts to enhance and sustain market share across all customer segments

scores.rationale: Consistently low-profile, engineering-led communication across all 16 calls — dense operational and product detail, no personality promotion, and even the MD and operations-head successions were reported in a single matter-of-fact paragraph.
scores.quote: Mr. M.S. Ravi Kumar retired as Regional Operating Officer of CVS India after 39 years of service. He was succeeded by Mr. G. Mukund, who joins us from VECV Limited

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building is real — R&D headcount added, TEI/Kaizen award participation, NAPS trainees, an OMA maturity assessment framed as building a learning organization — but the senior operations succession was filled externally rather than from the internal pipeline.
scores.quote: This achievement reflects our dedication to building a learning organization and driving cultural transformation through qualifications and capability growth

scores.rationale: Communication is structured and reasonably candid — degrowth quarters, export declines, Red Sea logistics, and Q4 margin compression are all named with their drivers — though the tone stays scripted and mistakes are attributed largely to external factors rather than owned.
scores.quote: we've had significant challenges on increased supply, coupled with the war life situation in the Middle East. And therefore, we have some increases on the cost side

scores.rationale: Separating skill from tailwind is difficult here — record FY26 results coincide with GST-driven CV upcycle, government safety mandates and parent-supplied technology, though consistent above-market outperformance suggests some genuine execution capability.
scores.quote: FY '25-'26 sales was driven by sharp industry rebound after GST rate cuts

scores.rationale: The company holds a leadership position in CV braking systems that it explicitly aims to sustain, with an entrenched aftermarket/OES and retrofitment franchise built on its own installed base.
scores.quote: We aim to sustain our leadership position in braking system by strengthening our market share in ESC across OEMs ahead of upcoming truck regulation

scores.rationale: Safety-critical, homologated braking systems designed into OEM platforms create high switching costs, and the installed BS-VI vehicle park feeds a captive OES/retrofit aftermarket, though no explicit lock-in economics are disclosed.
scores.quote: greater uplift from OES-driven requirement, primarily due to replacement demand arising from BS-VI vehicles park expansion

scores.rationale: CV air-braking in India is a concentrated few-player market with no competitive pricing pressure discussed and the company able to reset prices on low-margin products, but its customers are a handful of large OEMs with real negotiating power.
scores.quote: profitability improvement actions, including price resetting of low-margin products

scores.rationale: Barriers are high — homologated safety electronics, deep localization, capital-intensive plants and OEM co-development — and pricing behaviour is rational with cost pass-throughs negotiated rather than discounted, under stable ZF Group ownership.
scores.quote: One prestigious new product development excellence award from major OEMs for significant contribution of ZF towards launch of Advanced Electronic Braking System

scores.rationale: Share gains are documented but competitors are never named or characterised anywhere in the calls, so there is no evidence of identifiable weak players from whom share is being taken.
scores.quote: increased market share among independent bus manufacturer for e-compressor and EBS system

scores.rationale: The business is a niche B2B braking supplier, but it is a listed entity with regular sell-side-hosted calls (Spark, Anand Rathi, B&K, 360 ONE) and carries the global ZF brand, so it is not off the radar of capital.
scores.quote: hosted by Batlivala & Karani Securities India Private Limited

scores.rationale: Demand is functional and regulation-driven rather than image- or taste-based; margins are healthy (20% EBITDA) but pricing power derives from engineering content and mandates, not brand intangibles.
scores.quote: achieving an EBITDA margin of 20% on total sales

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty in safety-critical systems — braking, stability control, ADAS — where reliability and regulatory compliance dominate price, evidenced by OEM excellence awards and service-reliability-led aftermarket growth.
scores.quote: This strengthened infrastructure continued meaningful to overall aftermarket growth by improving reach, responsiveness and service reliability

scores.rationale: Deep and widening direct reach — thousands of retailers, distributors and fleets covered by the aftermarket team, plus 51 new distributor branches and 14 new service centres in FY26 alone, extending into B and C class cities.
scores.quote: extensive aftermarket team outreach covering 6,000-plus retailers, 4,000-plus distributors, 1,800-plus fleets and 200-plus workshops

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate (OEMs and fleets) and the benefit mix is correctly matched — reliability, TCO and regulatory compliance plus design-in switching costs — with fleet-level TCO explicitly cited as a demand driver.
scores.quote: replacement demand for aging fleets driven by need for improved efficiency and lower total cost of ownership

scores.rationale: A deep, multi-product technology edge spanning ABS/EBS, ESC, ADAS, AMT, telematics and EV aggregates, sustained by heavy in-house engineering and access to ZF Group platforms, delivering measurable safety and efficiency benefits to customers.
scores.quote: With over five decades of experience in pioneering active safety technologies for CVs, ZF was the first to market 'ESCsmart™'

scores.rationale: The digital/telematics business gathers fleet data at scale but is a subscription service without a genuine self-reinforcing two-sided network; value does not compound with each additional participant.
scores.quote: managing around 90K active connections

scores.rationale: Distribution and service reach are hard to replicate — plants co-located near OEM hubs (Jamshedpur, Lucknow, Pantnagar) for delivery responsiveness, plus a continually expanded authorised service-centre and distributor network in a market where service is vital.
scores.quote: the expansion of our service footprint through 7 new authorized service centers, enhanced network accessibility and customer support

scores.rationale: Sustained growth-oriented capacity build — new SEZ oral solid and injectable sites, a US biologics manufacturing facility for the Agenus CDMO, and a new dialyzer membrane plant — funded while EBITDA margin rose from 20.5% to 31.2%, implying high incremental returns.
scores.quote: in nephrology, we are establishing a high-end dialyzer membrane facility to address the global rising demand

scores.rationale: Consumer Wellness brand spend has translated into durable brand equity and pricing power (Glucon-D, Nycil, Everyuth growth plus 377bps gross margin expansion on calibrated price increases), though A&P efficiency is never quantified.
scores.quote: gross margin expansion with an improvement of 377 basis points ... driven by calibrated price increase taken earlier

scores.rationale: R&D held at a disciplined 7.5-8% of revenue for years and has visibly converted into output — Desidustat approved in China, Saroglitazar heading to USFDA NDA, world-first Nivolumab biosimilar, Aflibercept, semaglutide pen and 25-35 US launches a year.
scores.quote: we launched the world's first biosimilar of Nivolumab under the brand name Tishtha

scores.rationale: Deals have been frequent and value-accretive with margins still at record highs and leverage at 0.5x, but Amplitude Surgical (a new MedTech vertical), Comfort Click and the proposed Assertio buy are diversifying platform acquisitions rather than small complementary bolt-ons.
scores.quote: We acquired the French orthopedic firm, Amplitude Surgical, and entered the nephrology and cardiovascular devices space

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy anywhere in the excerpts.

Business is manufacturing-heavy across multiple new plants (SEZ sites, US biologics facility, dialyzer plant) so it is not asset-light, though rising margins and a net-cash-to-0.5x-levered balance sheet show capital is being turned productively.
scores.quote: We have put up a new oral solid dosage facility in the Ahmedabad SEZ (SEZ 2) to cater to the requirements of the US market

scores.rationale: Consistent, multi-year share capture: India branded has outpaced IPM for many consecutive quarters with a 200-400bps outperformance target, US base business gained volume share against peers seeing declines, and it is now a top-3 US generic player.
scores.quote: our branded formulation business ... a robust 14% year-on-year growth outperforming the market growth for yet another quarter

scores.rationale: Credible and well-executed expansion — UK operations started FY24, France/Spain retail build-out, WeightWorld into Poland/Finland/Portugal, and international formulations growing 38-45% YoY with management noting new markets beat expectations on both revenue and margin.
scores.quote: all the new markets that we entered like UK and some of the markets in EM, all of them have significantly tracked better than expectations, both on revenue and margins

scores.rationale: Mix is improving strongly (chronic to 46.3%, pivot to specialty/rare disease/505(b)(2)), but headline growth is repeatedly attributed to volume expansion while US pricing erodes, so growth is volume-and-mix rather than price-led.
scores.quote: The base US business continued to grow driven by sustained volume expansion and new products launched over the last 12 months

scores.rationale: The company is at a cyclical high, not a bottom — record-ever margins of 31.2% with management already guiding FY27 down to 'in excess of 24%' on Revlimid, Mirabegron and Asacol competition rolling off.
scores.quote: FY27, looking at competition, also Revlimid competition, Mirabegron competition, expenses related to Saro launch, we are expecting margins in excess of 24%

scores.rationale: Core end markets — Indian chronic therapies, rare disease, biosimilars and the VMS/wellness segment — are in secular expansion, though a large US generics base faces structural price deflation.
scores.quote: It significantly strengthens our presence in the high growth VMS segment, covering adult nutrition, pediatric wellness and animal health

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudently managed at 0.5x net debt/EBITDA and the organic base still compounds in double digits, but the framework's 'no big M&A' test is failed by a rapid FY25-26 deal spree spanning consumer, MedTech, US biologics plants and Assertio.
scores.quote: we kept our net debt to EBITDA ratio comfortably within the benchmark levels, even as we pursued several inorganic growth opportunities

scores.rationale: Decade-long, independently funded NCE programs have been pursued with tenacity across the whole period — Saroglitazar tracked from Phase 2b in 2022 to a US NDA filing in 2026, and Desidustat from licensing in 2020 to Chinese approval.
scores.quote: Our Desidustat tablets, which we licensed to China Medical Systems Holdings in 2020, has now received approval from the Chinese regulator

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently run by the same low-profile team with operational detail rather than personality, and management repeatedly refuses to grandstand on pending litigation or unapproved products.
scores.quote: the trial is just about to start, it will be better to not comment on that outcome right now

scores.rationale: Explicit people-investment philosophy with external workplace validation, and continuity in the senior bench (Nayak, Bothra, Garg through all 17 calls) alongside an orderly CFO transition, though no formal succession pipeline is described.
scores.quote: Our philosophy to invest in people to build the businesses has received external validation as well

scores.rationale: Guidance is specific, deliberately conservative and repeatedly met or beaten (20%+ FY23 margin, 27.5% FY24, high-teens FY27), assumptions are stated openly, and weaknesses like the three-year European struggle are acknowledged rather than glossed over.
scores.quote: Europe, which was going through a challenge for us in the last 3 years, in the last year and this year have done meaningfully better

scores.rationale: Results are genuinely strong but a material slice of the FY24-26 margin surge came from limited-window exclusivities (Revlimid, Asacol, Mirabegron) and acquired revenue, so skill is only partly separable — the ex-acquisition double-digit base growth is the honest evidence of skill.
scores.quote: Even after adjusting for acquisitions, the base business grew in double digits

scores.rationale: The Sentynl rare-disease portfolio holds literal single-product monopolies in the patient's mind — Zycubo is the only approved Menkes therapy, Nulibry the only MoCD Type A therapy, Zokinvy the only Progeria therapy.
scores.quote: Zycubo has become the first and only therapy approved for the treatment of Menkes disease

scores.rationale: Orphan designations and first-to-market biosimilar positions create de facto exclusivity windows and semi-exclusive positions in emerging markets, but the bulk generics business carries essentially no switching costs.
scores.quote: where we are many times semi exclusive or exclusive because of the technology, we are seeing good traction

scores.rationale: US generics — roughly half of revenue — is a fragmented market with concentrated buying consortia, evidenced by continual price erosion and multiple entrants eroding key products.
scores.quote: There was a price erosion of the impact of 2.5% which was offset by new launches

scores.rationale: The core generics markets show low entry barriers and unavoidable price competition, with management routinely modelling new competitors into guidance for Asacol, Revlimid and Mirabegron.
scores.quote: to be on the conservative side, it is always prudent to assume we will see competition

scores.rationale: Zydus repeatedly took volume share in the US base portfolio in quarters when peers reported sequential declines, and consistently gains rank against weaker players in Indian therapies.
scores.quote: most of the other companies have reported a sequential decline with double-digit erosion in the base business

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered large-cap tracked by Macquarie, Nomura and a full sell-side roster, and its chosen growth areas (biosimilars, GLP-1s, oncology) are the most capital-crowded niches in pharma, not ignored ones.
scores.quote: Hi, this is Kunal from Macquarie

scores.rationale: Marquee consumer brands and pillar Indian formulation brands support price increases and category leadership with expanding gross margins, though pricing power is brand/prescription-based rather than aspirational.
scores.quote: we retained leadership position across most product categories that we operate in

scores.rationale: The stated US customer proposition is reliability — compliant facilities, agile supply and execution certainty — reinforced by a clean run of EIRs at SEZ, Jarod and the oncology injectable sites.
scores.quote: a network of regulatory compliant manufacturing facilities, an agile supply chain and an efficient cost management

scores.rationale: Deep Indian field reach is being extended beyond the prescription through patient support programs and value-added services, and Comfort Click adds a direct digital-first consumer channel.
scores.quote: our engagement extends well beyond the point of prescription. Through patient support programs and value-added services

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched — intangible brand pull for Indian retail consumers and doctors, reliability/TCO for US institutional buyers — but the US relationship remains price-driven with limited lock-in.
scores.quote: This will be driven by large product portfolio, strong customer relationships

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-modality technical depth (NCEs, complex injectables, biosimilar ADCs, a CE-marked surgical robot) backed by 8% R&D intensity, but much of the revenue base is still commodity generics where the tech edge does not price.
scores.quote: we achieved an important milestone with the CE mark approval for our proprietary Andy robotic surgical system

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the excerpts.

Distribution is a real asset — a top-3 US generic footprint, deep Indian coverage, and acquisitions bought explicitly for channel access such as Assertio's Medicare Part B oncology relationships — but it is matched by several large Indian peers.
scores.quote: By leveraging Assertio's deep oncology relationships and the strong share in Medicare Part B accounts

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly confirms capex is maintenance-only at INR30-35 crore with no growth capex programme; expansion has come via acquisitions, not organic asset creation.
scores.quote: Currently, the capex is the maintenance line capex... in the range of INR30 crores, INR35 crores... no large capex that we envisage.

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P (celebrity campaigns, 360-degree media, reinvestment of gross-margin gains) has translated into measurable share gains in scrubs and peel-offs, though the same spend has not arrested Complan's decline.
scores.quote: We reinvested some part of our gross margin expansion into brand building, as a result of which advertisement expenses grew by 19.1%

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-year innovation cadence (Immuno-Gro, Sugar Free Green/Gold Plus, D'lite, Recharge hydration, RTD, wafer bars, Nutralite Professional variants) with an explicit target for new-product revenue share.
scores.quote: our wish list is go up to 6% to 8% of our revenue could come in products from products launched in 36 months

scores.rationale: RiteBite went from breakeven to near double-digit EBITDA and doubled its pre-deal growth while Comfort Click is cash-EPS accretive and margin-accretive, but Comfort Click is a large, debt-funded, cross-border deal rather than a small simple bolt-on.
scores.quote: EBITDA improving from breakeven at acquisition to levels approaching double-digit margins

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy across the excerpts; capital was directed to debt repayment and then acquisitions.

Operations are genuinely asset-light (maintenance-only capex, plant closure, hub-and-spoke outsourcing), but the balance sheet is now loaded with acquired brand intangibles carrying ~INR472mn quarterly amortisation, diluting returns on the enlarged asset base.
scores.quote: Amortization of acquired brands resulted in higher depreciation and amortization charges, about INR472 million for the quarter 3

scores.rationale: Clear share capture in Everyuth scrub (+373bps to 46.2%) and peel-off (+200bps to 78.2%) and sweeteners (+80bps), but several positions are already dominant (Sugar Free 95.9%) leaving limited runway, and Complan slid from 4.8% to 4.3%.
scores.quote: Everyuth scrub has maintained its leadership position with a market share of 46.2%... an increase of 373 basis points

scores.rationale: Credible, executed international expansion — Comfort Click into Poland/Finland/Portugal/UAE and Boots.com, RiteBite into 9 countries in year one — with international like-to-like growth of 29.5% in FY26.
scores.quote: The international business, including Comfort Click business, delivered a like-to-like growth of 29.5%

scores.rationale: Growth has been overwhelmingly volume-led rather than price/mix-led (17.1% of 20% growth was volume in Q1FY25; 10.3% of 17.8% in Q1FY23), with Nutralite value trailing volume on market-driven prices.
scores.quote: consolidated net sales growth of 20% on a year-on-year basis, of which 17.1% is due to volume

scores.rationale: The cyclicality here is weather/seasonal rather than an industrial cycle; the seasonal portfolio fell 18.8% in FY26 on a poor summer, creating a weak base but with no identifiable structural upturn management will commit to.
scores.quote: the seasonal brands declined by 18.8%... it was less than expected and the temperatures were lower than normal

scores.rationale: Core exposures — European VMS (€11bn+), protein snacking, better-for-you sweeteners and quick commerce — are in secular expansion, offset by the structurally declining health-food-drinks category where Complan sits.
scores.quote: it's a large 11 - more than €11 billion market in Europe for VMS. Market is shifting towards online space

scores.rationale: After fully deleveraging in FY25 they immediately re-levered for a large overseas acquisition that pushed the company into reported net losses, the opposite of the organic-focus/no-big-M&A test.
scores.quote: the acquisition was funded through a low-cost bridge loan at 5% with the related interest expense... amounting to approximately INR371 million for the quarter 3

scores.rationale: Multi-year consistency of strategy — Transformation 2.0 footprint rationalisation, patient category development in scrubs, and Sugar Free Green's 20 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth — shows tenacity in chosen niches.
scores.quote: Sugar Free Green delivered 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth

scores.rationale: The same small management team (Arora, Parikh, Patel) presents substance-heavy operational detail call after call without self-promotion, keeping celebrity to brand endorsement rather than management persona.
scores.quote: MANAGEMENT: MR. TARUN ARORA – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER... MR. UMESH PARIKH – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

scores.rationale: Repeated Great Place to Work certification and dedicated capability-building teams (separate B2B/B2C Nutralite teams, a dedicated RiteBite team) indicate systematic talent investment, though no explicit succession pipeline is disclosed.
scores.quote: certified as a Great Place to Work for the fourth consecutive year, reflecting its continued commitment to talent development

scores.rationale: They candidly own competitive misses ('slow to respond', 'only a small 5% player') and explain one-offs, but the 17-18% EBITDA aspiration promised for 'the next couple of years' in 2024 was still unmet and simply re-promised in 2026, and segmental disclosure requests have been deferred repeatedly.
scores.quote: The shift that we have been slow to respond to has been the low-priced pouches, which is almost like a price war

scores.rationale: Headline FY26 growth of 46.4% is almost entirely acquisition-driven — the domestic base business grew just 2.4% and margins remain far below the long-stated aspiration — so results should not be read as evidence of operating skill.
scores.quote: For financial year '26, net sales registered growth of 46.4%... while the domestic business grew by 2.4%

scores.rationale: Several brands hold monopoly-like positions in the consumer's mind — Sugar Free at 95.9%, Everyuth peel-off at 78.2%, Glucon-D at ~60%, and Cuticolor as the No.1 doctor-prescribed hair colour.
scores.quote: The Sugar Free brand maintained its dominant position in the sugar substitute market with a commanding market share of 95.9%

scores.rationale: These are FMCG categories with essentially no switching costs or captive aftermarket — consumers down-trade freely to cheaper pouches and sachets, as Complan's erosion demonstrates.
scores.quote: the health food drinks category saw a continued slowdown, which is further compounded by down-trading to LUPs and lower-priced pouch packs

scores.rationale: Structure is mixed: near-duopoly leadership in glucose powder and prickly heat powder, but a distant No.4 in nutrition drinks and No.5 with 6.6% in fragmented facial cleansing, and only 8-10% share in European VMS.
scores.quote: Everyuth brand holds fifth position with a 6.6% market share in the overall facial cleansing segment level

scores.rationale: Leadership has been durably held for years in sweeteners and glucose without discounting, but the nutrition-drinks category shows outright irrational pricing behaviour and the online VMS space is openly crowded.
scores.quote: the low-priced pouches, which is almost like a price war and the sachets where we have been a reluctant participant because of the margin

scores.rationale: Share is being taken from weaker players in scrubs and peel-offs, and Comfort Click's 8-10% share in a fragmented European VMS market leaves ample donator base — though in nutrition drinks Zydus is itself the donator.
scores.quote: our market shares within the markets we operate, which is typically 8% to 10%, which gives us enough room for growth

scores.rationale: The company operates in small, unglamorous niches — prickly heat powder, glucose powder, peel-off masks, sugar substitutes — that large FMCG players and capital largely ignore.
scores.quote: Nycil has maintained its number one position with a market share of 34.9% in the prickly heat power category

scores.rationale: Consolidated gross margins of 66-67% and consistent brand-led share gains show real image-based pricing power, tempered by evident consumer down-trading and market-driven pricing in Nutralite.
scores.quote: on an annualized basis, you can assume it about 66%, 67% on a consolidated basis

scores.rationale: Trust and clinical endorsement are central — Cuticolor is the No.1 doctor-prescribed hair colour, Complan is medically detailed, and Comfort Click shows >50% repeat purchase and 4.6/5 ratings.
scores.quote: The brand is Number 1 doctor prescribed in the hair coloring space

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — 2.5 million outlets with an even urban/rural split, ~30% organized-channel salience, and a growing owned D2C base in Europe that deepens direct customer intimacy.
scores.quote: overall availability of Zydus Wellness products crossing 2.5 million stores with equal split between urban and rural distribution

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched to customer: intangible/brand benefits for retail consumers, and dedicated B2B teams with functional professional SKUs for institutional food-service buyers.
scores.quote: supported by strong execution from dedicated B2B and B2C teams

scores.rationale: R&D is formulation- and reformulation-led (Sucralose+Chromium, mayonnaise and bar variants) plus AI-led media targeting — useful capability but not a deep, defensible multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: We recently upgraded Sugar Free Gold to Sugar Free Gold Plus with a new formulation, Sucralose plus Chromium

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists; the D2C and marketplace businesses are transactional retail relationships with no self-reinforcing scale effect claimed anywhere in the calls.
scores.quote: Right now, the business is largely led by Marketplace Amazon and D2C

scores.rationale: Reach is a real asset — 2.5mn outlets, Nycil at 1.67mn, Everyuth expanding to 6.8 lakh outlets, plus above-market share on e-commerce and quick commerce — though it remains well short of the largest Indian FMCG networks.
scores.quote: our market shares across our e-commerce platforms that we track are also ahead of our general market share
